laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 92
AN ACT to establish a State Trade and Training School for
Negroes in the section of Kentucky , known as Normal District
No. 2 ; to create a Board of Regents for the general manage .
ment thereof ; which shall determine the requirements for
admission and graduation and the course of study for said
school ; to create a commission which shall determine the loca-
tion of said school ; and to appropriate funds for its main-
tenance .
Whereas , that district of Kentucky , known and designated as
"Normal School District No. 2 ," contains a negro population of
165,515 ; and ,
Whereas , this negro population controls and operates 284,880
acres of farm land valued at $ 7,639,487 ; and ,
Whereas , there is no school in this section of the State where
negroes may receive agricultural and mechanical training ; and
other useful trades and training .
Whereas , the cost of transporting students from this section
of Kentucky to other normal schools of the State is so great
that a large majority of negro boys and girls are unable to at-
tend school and receive the training necessary to make them
useful citizens ; therefore ,
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. There shall be established and maintained
as hereinafter provided a State Trade and Training
School for Negroes of " Normal District No. 2 " as
follows : The State and Training School for Negroes
to be located in " Normal District No. 2 " the district
of the State set apart in the Acts of 1906 establish-
ing the Western Normal School at Bowling Green ,
Kentucky .
2. The Governor of the State shall within
thirty days after this act becomes a law appoint a
commission composed of five persons , one selected
from the State at large , but no two persons from the
same county , who shall, within thirty days after
their appointment , meet at Frankfort , Kentucky , on
a date fixed by the Governor, and organize and ar-
range to receive from localities in said " Normal
District No. 2 , " desiring to secure location of said
school not to be established in said congressional
district where a State Normal School for colored
persons is already established , proposals and dona-
tions of suitable sites and other valuable consid-
erations , and shall , within ninety days after their
appointment , locate said school in " Normal School
District No. 2 , " at the place making the most ad-
All pro-vantageous offer , all things considered .
posals for sites and locations for the school shall be
in writing, shall be entered at large on the re-
cords of the commission , and the findings of the
commission , fixing the location of the school , shall
be in writing and entered at large on the records of
said commission .
§ 3. The object of the State trade and training
school for negroes shall be to train negro boys and
girls in the elementary branches , agriculture , me-
chanic arts , practical mining , carpentry , black-
smithing, shoemaking , modern housekeeping , plas-
tering , brick masonry , dressmaking , designing and
domestic science .
§ 4. There is hereby created a board of re-
gents for said State trade and training school , to be
known as " The Board of Regents for the State
Trade and Training School for Negroes . " The said
board shall have perpetual succession , with power
to contract and be contracted with , to sue and be
sued , to plead and be impleaded , to receive by any
legal mode of conveyance property of any descrip-
tion , and to have and hold and enjoy the same ; also
to make and use a corporate seal , with power to
alter the same ; to adopt by-laws , rules and regula-
tions for the government of their members , official
agents and employes ; provided , such by -laws do not
conflict with the Constitution of the United States
or with the Constitution of the State of Kentucky .
§ 5. The board of regents for said school shall
be composed of five members , including the State
Superintendent of Public Instruction , who shall be
member and chairman of said board , and shall in
clude the president of said school , who shall be mem-
ber ex-officio of said board . The other three mem-
bers of said board shall be appointed by the Gover-
nor of the State from said " Normal District No. 2 "
at large. Provided , that no more than one member
of said board shall be appointed by the Governor
shall begin on the first day of July , one thousand
nine hundred and twenty-six , and one member
thereof shall retire , as may be determined by lot , at
the end of one year thereafter ; one in two years , and
the other in three years ; they shall be subject to re-
moval by the Governor for cause , and he is author-
ized to fill all vacancies occurring by death , resigna-
tion or otherwise .
§ 6. The said board of regents shall hold its
first meeting thirty days after its appointment , the
time and place of meeting to be designated by the
Superintendent of Public Instruction who shall ad-
minister the oath of office to each member . At this
meeting the board shall appoint a secretary, treas-
urer , and such officers as it deems necessary . The
board shall not appoint one of its own members as
treasurer , and the compensation for the treasurer
shall not exceed one hundred dollars per annum .
The treasurer shall give bond such as the board
shall prescribe .
§ 7. The board of regents shall hold its regu-
lar meetings at such time and place as may be
agreed upon and , until the buildings are arranged
for and completed , and as much oftener as may be
necessary , but thereafter the regular meetings of
the board shall be held quarterly and at the said
school or office of the State Superintendent of Pub-
lic Instruction , as the board deems most expedient
for the good of the school . In the absence of a regu-
lar meeting of the board , the board may appoint one
or more of its members to act in its stead in matters
which the board shall name as expedient . Such bus-
iness as is transacted in the absence of a regular
meeting of the board shall not be considered final
until passed on in a regular meeting of the board .
8. A majority of the members of said board
shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of bus-
iness , but no appropriation of money , or any con-
tract which shall require any appropriation or dis-
bursement of money , shall be made , unless a ma-
jority of all the members of the board shall vote for
the same .
§ 9. The board of regents shall have general
control and management of said school ; shall pos-
sess full power and authority to adopt all needful
rules and regulations for the guidance and supervis-
ion of the conduct of the students of any department
thereof ; shall have power to appoint and dismiss
teachers , and shall require such reports from officers
and instructors as it deems necessary .
§ 10. The board of regents is authorized to
grant from time to time , certificates of proficiency
showing the completion of the courses pursued , and
whose moral character and disciplinary relations to
said school shall be satisfactory . And such students
as shall have completed the prescribed course , and
exhibited satisfactory evidence of ability to instruct
shall be entitled to diplomas appropriate to such
standing as the board of regents shall confer upon
them , which diplomas shall entitle them to teach in
any trades and industrial departments in both high
and normal schools of the State , and have the same
force and entitle the holder to the same privileges
as are granted to students who graduate from the
other normal schools of the State .
§ 11. No member of the board of regents shall
draw any salary for services as such , but shall re-
ceive ten cents per mile for every mile necessarily
traveled in going to and from meetings of the board ,
and other legitimate expense , to be paid out of the
contingent fund of the school .
§ 12. The board of regents shall, in a body or
in a majority of their members , visit said school and
inspect its condition , and they shall make a biennial
report to the legislature , setting forth the financial
and scholastic condition of said school , making such
suggestions as in their opinions would improve the
school , and in years in which the legislature is not
in session , they shall make their report to the Gov-
ernor.
§ 13. It shall be the duty of the treasurer of the
board of regents to receive and disburse all moneys
under the control of the board of regents and per-
form all such acts as pertain to his office , under the
direction of the board of regents and to make a re-
port of the same to the board at its quarterly meet-
ings . On or before the second Monday in January ,
one thousand nine hundred and twenty - seven , and
every two years thereafter , said treasurer shall also
report to the board of regents , to be by it transmit-
ted to the General Assembly, an itemized statement
of all receipts and expenditures for the two calendar
years preceding , showing minutely all disburse-
ments of moneys received from the State or other-
wise.
14. It shall be the duty of the secretary of
the board to keep and preserve all records , books
and papers belonging to the board . He shall keep
a record of all proceedings of the board and shall
execute all duties pertaining to his office .
$ 15 . In order to enable the board of regents to
carry into effect the provisions of this act there is
hereby appropriated out of the general fund the sum
of thirty -five thousand dollars ($35,000.00 ) condi-
tioned upon a like sum being deposited with the
Auditor of Public Accounts by interested citizens
of the Commonwealth . Fifteen thousand dollars
( $ 15,000.00 ) of which shall be an annuity . The en-
tire seventy thousand ( $ 70,000.00 ) to be appropri-
ated for the following purposes :
Fifteen thousand dollars ( $15,000.00 ) for a
recitation hall .
Fifteen thousand dollars ( $ 15,000.00 ) for an in-
dustrial building .
Fifteen thousand dollars ( $ 15,000.00 ) for a dor-
mitory .
Fifteen thousand dollars ( $ 15,000.00 ) annually
for current expenses and maintenance .
Ten thousand ( $ 10,000.00 ) for equipment .
§ 16. The money hereby appropriated for
buildings , equipment and maintenance shall be avail-
able immediately for said school upon the delivery
of a good warranty deed, conveying to the Common-
wealth the property to be donated as above provided
and its acceptance by the locating commission . The
money appropriated under this act for the buildings ,
equipment and maintenance of said school shall be
disbursed as follows , viz.:
The chairman and secretary of the board of re-
gents shall draw their warrants for the equipment ,
buildings and maintenance of said school , provided
for in this act , on the Auditor of Public Accounts ,
payable to the treasurer of the school , and upon re-
ceipt of said draft by the Auditor he shall draw his
warrants for the proper amounts upon the treasurer
of the State . The money authorized to be paid out
of the State Treasury under this act shall be paid
out of the general funds not otherwise appropriated .
Approved March 27 , 1926 .

laws.summary: This statute mandates that the fiscal court impose a capitation tax not exceeding one dollar on all legal male voters residing in the territory affected by an ad valorem tax for the county board of education. The sheriff is responsible for collecting this tax, along with other state and county revenues, and remitting it to the county treasurer, who serves as the ex-officio treasurer for the county board of education. The sheriff's commission for collecting this specific school tax is limited to one percent of the total school tax collected, and the commission is calculated proportionally based on the combined funds collected.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 172
AN ACT relating to the fiscal administration of the common
schools in each of the counties of the Commonwealth by the
county board of education ; providing for a uniform budget sys-
tem for the administration of the fiscal affairs of the common
schools in each of the counties of the Commonwealth ; prescrib-
ing the duties of the county superintendent , the county treas-
urer , county . court clerk , county tax commissioners , county at-
torney and other officers with reference thereto ; repealing sec-
tions 8 and 9, chapter 36 , Acts of 1920 , session of General As-
sembly of Commonwealth of Kentucky , enacting sections 2
and 3 of chapter 39 of the Acts of the General Assembly of
1922 , approved March 22nd , 1922 ; providing for the compensa-
tion of the treasurer and the designation by the county board
of education of depositories for school funds and the fixing of
interest rates to be charged on deposits ; and providing for
penalties for the violation of any of the provisions of this act .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
1. The fiscal affairs of the common schools
of each county of the Commonwealth of Kentucky
shall be administered by the county board of edu-
cation under a uniform budget system . The school
budgets shall provide for all the funds to be ex-
pended by the county board of education from cur-
rent revenues for each fiscal year .
All school funds from whatever source received
shall be appropriated and accounted for under the
provisions of this act .
§ 2. In the classification of expenditures for
common school purposes each separate activity of
the county board of education for which county
funds are to be expended by the county board of
education shall be construed to constitute a separate
budget unit . If any budget unit includes more than
one class of expenditures the said budget unit shall
be subdivided into budget funds so that the cost of
each separate class of expenditures for common
schools can be ascertained . The funds set apart in
the school budget for a budget unit , or any subdi-
visions thereof , shall be construed to constitute a
separate budget fund , and shall be appropriated
and accounted for separately .
It shall be the duty of the State Superintendent
of Public Instruction to furnish to each county su-
perintendent the form of a properly drawn school
budget provided for under the provisions of this
act ; and the forms of the school budgets so fur-
nished each of the county superintendents shall be
uniform . The Superintendent of Public Instruction
is given the power and authority to approve all
common school budgets as to form and arrangement
of budget units and all subdivisions thereof for the
sole and exclusive purpose of establishing and
maintaining in the common schools of each county
of the Commonwealth a uniform budget system , so
that the costs of each separate activity of the county
board of education in the maintenance of the com-
mon schools of the county can be ascertained for the
information of the people of the State .
The school budget shall provide for the follow-
ing funds : ( 1 ) " General Expense Fund ” out of
which the emergency expenses of the county board
of education may be paid . (2 ) " Sinking Fund " out
of which the bonded indebtedness of the county
board of education can be paid if such indebtedness
has been incurred by the board ; and , " Sinking
Fund to Pay Floating Indebtedness , " out of which
any floating indebtedness of the county board of
education shall be paid ; and " Interest Fund " for
the payment of the interest on all interest -bearing
school warrants .
§ 3. The county board of education shall have
the school budget prepared , and they shall file said
school budget , together with an itemized county levy
to raise each separate budget fund provided for in
the school budget in the office of the county court
clerk not less than thirty days nor more than thirty-
five days prior to the time fixed by the fiscal court
to make the county levy for the next fiscal year .
The county board of education in the prepara-
tion of the school budget shall use the forms of the
school budget furnished to them by the Superintend-
ent of Public Instruction , and the county board of
education shall have no power or authority to make
any change in the form of the school budget so fur-
nished them by the Superintendent of Public In-
struction .
The county board of education may adjourn
from time to time until the school budget has been
completed , and may hold such hearings as they may
deem necessary in the preparation of the school bud-
get .
The county board of education shall also pre-
pare and file with the fiscal court on the first day of
the term at which the school budget and itemized
county levy is to be considered by the fiscal court , a
written statement explaining their reasons for pro-
viding the budget funds contained in the school bud-
get , together with all data and records showing the
resources of the county and the needs of the common
schools , considered by them in the preparation of
the school budget for the information of the fiscal
court and the people of the county .
§ 4. The county court clerk shall immediately
upon the filing in his office of the school budget and
itemized county levy by the county board of educa-
tion endorse the same filed in his official capacity ,
and shall thereupon immediately record the same
upon the fiscal court order book . The county court
clerk shall immediately make two copies of the
school budget and one copy of the itemized county
levy , and cause a certified copy of the school budget
together with the itemized county levy to be printed
in a newspaper published in the county once a week
for a period of two weeks , before the time fixed to
adopt a school budget and a county levy for school
purposes for the next fiscal year for the information
of the people of the county . If no newspaper is pub-
lished in the county the county court clerk shall
cause same to be printed in a newspaper having gen-
eral circulation of the county , and by posting type-
written or printed copies thereof on the court house
door and at least five other places in the county for
a period of two weeks prior to the time the school
budget is to be adopted and the county levy is to be
made .
The school budget and the county levy to raise
the funds provided for therein shall be adopted at
the same term of the fiscal court at which the county
budget is adopted , and the county levy is made to
raise the funds provided for in the county budget .
§ 4. The county board of education shall hold a
meeting at their office at the county seat at the same
time the fiscal court of the county is required to
adopt the school budget and make the county levy
to raise the funds provided for therein . It shall be
the duty of the county superintendent and the mem-
bers of the county board of education , if required
by the fiscal court of the county , to appear before
the fiscal court and explain in detail any budget fund
or funds contained in the school budget for the in-
formation of the fiscal court ; and the county board
of education shall have the power at such meeting
to make any necessary changes they may deem
necessary in any budget fund or funds contained in
the school budget after the same has been considered
by the fiscal court in a joint meeting of the county
board of education and the fiscal court of the county ;
provided , however , it shall be the duty of the fiscal
court to adopt the school budget as finally submitted
$12 COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY
to them , together with the itemized county levy as
finally submitted to them by the county board of
education and it shall be the duty of the fiscal court
to make the levy therein recommended and de-
manded upon all taxable property subject to state
taxation in said county , exclusive of property in
graded school districts and cities and towns , main-
taining a separate and distinct system of common
schools .
( 2 ) It shall be the duty of the county tax com-
missioner of each county , upon blanks furnished to
him by the State Tax Commission , in making the as-
sessments for the county , to show on each assess-
ment the property subject to taxation under the pro-
visions of this act , and it shall be the duty of the
county court clerk after the Tax Commission has
made out and completed the tax assessor's books of
the county, to certify to the county superintendent
the total assessed valuation of property in the
county subject to taxation under the provisions of
this act . Upon receipt of such certificate from the
county court clerk, it shall be the duty of the county
board of education to use the same in the prepara-
tion of the school budget as provided for under the
provisions of this act .
(3 ) The school budget as required by this act
shall show the amount of money needed for supple-
menting teachers ' salaries , for permanent improve-
ments , repairs , furniture , and the maintenance and
support of schools during the succeeding school year
and also the estimated total amount that will be re-
ceived from the state and the amount that will be
needed to be raised by local taxation , which in no
event shall be less than twenty-five cents nor more
than fifty cents on each one hundred dollars ' worth
of taxable property in the territory affected by this
act .
( 4 ) At the time that the fiscal court makes the
ad valorem levy demanded by the county board of
education , it shall also impose upon all legal male
voters residing in the territory affected by the said
ad valorem tax , a capitation tax not exceeding one
dollar each . It shall be the duty of the sheriff of
the county in the same manner and at the same time
he collects other state and county revenues , to col
lect the tax imposed under the provisions of this act
and after deducting his commission for same as now
allowed by law he shall pay same to the county treas-
urer , who by virtue of his office is ex-officio treasurer
for the county board of education . Provided , how-
ever , the commission allowed the sheriff for the col-
lecting of said tax shall not exceed one per cent of
the total school tax collected .
(5 ) For the purpose of determining the sheriff's
commission for collecting the tax provided for in
this act, the tax so collected , together with the state
and county revenues collected by the sheriff , shall be
treated as one fund , and the sheriff shall deduct from
the taxes collected under the provisions of this act
his commission for collecting the same , which shall
be in proportion to his entire commission on the
combined funds referred to herein , as the school
taxes collected bear to all the taxes collected by him.
The county board of education , by an order enterd
of record on its minute books may require the sheriff
to make monthly settlements of the taxes collected
under the provisions of this act . The fiscal court
shall annually make a settlement with the sheriff for
the taxes collected under the provisions of this act
in the same manner as now provided for by law for
the settlement of state and county taxes and a copy
of said settlement must be filed with the county
board of education . The money collected by taxation
under the provisions of this act shall be appro-
priated and expended by the county board of educa-
tion in accordance with the provisions of this act .
The money raised by the levy under the provisions
of this section shall be expended in strict accordance
with the school budget .
(6 ) The county superintendent and the county
board of education shall make all reports required
by the Superintendent of Public Instruction or State
Board of Education at such times , and upon such
items , and in such forms and on such blanks that
may be prescribed by the State Board of Education
and the State Superintendent of Public Instruction .
(7) The county court clerk shall also transmit a
certified copy of the school budget to the Superin-
tendent of Public Instruction for his approval at
the same time he causes a copy thereof to be printed ,
and if approved in form the Superintendent of Pub-
lic Instruction shall so advise the county court clerk ,
and if upon examination , the Superintendent of
Public Instruction finds the school budget is not in
proper form he shall rearrange the budget units and
subdivisions thereof so that the budget will be in
conformity with the provisions of this act and shall
transmit the same to the county court clerk of the
county from which said school budget was received .
§ 5. The county board of education shall ap-
propriate and account for each budget fund con-
tained in the school budget , separately , and all ap-
propriations shall designate the budget fund from
which the appropriation is to be paid .
The county board of education shall at its first
meeting in each fiscal year enter an order on its
minute book appropriating the entire budget fund
set apart to pay interest on interest-bearing school
warrants on a certificate of the treasurer as same
become due and payable . The county court clerk
shall issue a separate school warrant for the ac-
crued interest on each separate interest-bearing
school warrant .
§ 6. The county court clerk shall by virtue of
his office be the clerk of the county board of educa-
tion and shall be the custodian of its minute books
and school warrant books . The county court clerk
shall keep in his office a record book of the county
board of education to be known as the " School
Claim Book . ”
All persons , firms or corporations having claims
against the county board of education , except for
claims for interest or principal on bonded indebted-
ness , shall make off proof of their claims against the
county board of education , attaching thereto an
itemized statement of the claim or incorporating
therein an itemized statement thereof, and setting
forth the consideration the county has received and
the manner in which the county board of education
and the county is liable for the claim . Said proof of
claim shall be signed and sworn to by the person
making same or his or her duly authorized agent .
The claim properly proven shall be filed with the
clerk of the county court, and the clerk shall endorse
thereon the date of filing same , and shall thereupon
record said claim in the school claim book and prop-
erly index the same. All claims shall be numbered
by the clerk consecutively in the order in which they
are filed . The number of the claim shall be recorded
with the claim as a part thereof.
The county board of education shall have no
power to allow any claim for a period of thirty days
from the date of the filing of the claim in the county
court clerk's office , with the exception of the claim
for salary of teachers , county superintendents and
his assistants , other employes , county officers for
services rendered to the county board of education
per diem and expenses of members of county board
of education and claims going on written contracts .
It shall be the duty of the county court clerk
to call the attention of the county attorney to the
filing of claims against the county board of educa-
tion in his office , and the county attorney is required
as a part of the duties of his office to examine each of
the claims so filed , and to file exceptions to any and
all claims which are not valid obligations against
the county .
§. 7. The county treasurer shall by virtue of
his office be the exclusive custodian of all county
school funds from whatsoever source they may be
received . He shall also be the exclusive checking
agent of the county as to all school funds , and no
bank or trust company in which county school funds
are deposited shall honor a check on the county
school funds unless the same is signed by the county
treasurer in his official capacity . All county school
funds shall be deposited in bank in the name of
County Board of Education , " subject to be
checked out by the county treasurer .
66
The county treasurer shall keep a set of books
of accounts of financial transactions of the county
board of education to be provided for under the pro-
visions of the uniform accounting law of this State
providing for uniform accounting in State and
county government .
The county treasurer shall at the beginning of
each fiscal school year credit on the budget ledger
kept by him each budget fund provided for in the
school budget for that fiscal year , and he shall ac-
count for each budget fund separately .
The county treasurer shall at each regular and
special meeting of the county board of education ,
with the exception of the first meeting thereof in
each fiscal year file with said board on the first day
of said meeting a financial statement as appears
from his budget ledger showing the balance in each
budget fund as appears from his budget ledger .
This financial statement shall be signed by the
county treasurer in his official capacity , and said
statement shall be recorded upon its minute book as
a part of the proceedings of said meeting at which
'said statement is filed .
§ 8. The county treasurer shall sign all county
school warrants issued by the county court clerk
and enter the warrant on his budget ledger as a
charge against the budget fund out of which the
warrant is payable , if there is a sufficient balance in
said budget fund out of which said warrant is pay-
able to pay the same . No county school warrant
issued by the county court clerk shall be valid unless
signed by the county treasurer as provided for
under the provisions of this act .
§ 9. The county court clerk shall immediately
after the adjournment of any regular or special
meeting of the county board of education issue
county school warrants to cover all appropriations
made by the county board of education to the per-
sons named in said appropriations . The county
court clerk shall designate in said county school
warrant the budget fund from which the warrant is
payable , together with the number of the claim and
the page of the claim book in which same is re-
corded , if the appropriation is for a claim required
to be recorded . At the time the county court clerk
issues county school warrants on appropriations
made by the county board of education he shall enter
on the margin of claim , for which the appropriation
was made , on the claim book where same is recorded
if a recordable claim , the date of the county school
warrant , serial number , to whom issued , and the
amount thereof, issued in payment of the claim .
A county school warrant shall not be construed
to be legally issued until the warrant has been
signed by the county treasurer . After the county
court clerk has issued all county school warrants
he has been directed to issue by appropriation of the
county board of education , he shall then immediately
deliver his county school warrant book to the county
treasurer .
§ 10. The county treasurer shall, upon the de-
livery to him by the county clerk of the county
school warrant book , verify each county school war-
rant issued by the county court clerk by checking the
warrant with the claim and appropriation .
County Treasurer .
The county school warrant shall have printed
thereon in the proper place the following : " Ap-
proved and entered " and the
county treasurer shall sign each warrant when he
has determined that there is sufficient funds in the
budget fund out of which it is payable and shall then
charge said warrant to the budget fund out of which
it is payable . The county treasurer shall show by
his entry on his budget ledger of warrants as a
charge against budget funds the date of the war-
rant , serial number , to whom issued and the amount
thereof , and said budget ledger shall be prepared in
form to meet these requirements .
If the county treasurer finds upon examination
of his ledger that the balance in any budget fund or
funds is insufficient to pay any county school war-
rant or warrants , issued by the county court clerk he
shall refuse to sign said warrant or warrants and
endorse across the face of each of said warrants in
red ink the following : " Void for want of funds , "
and sign said endorsement in his official capacity .
The county treasurer shall be liable on his offi-
cial bond for the amount of any county school war-
rant approved and signed by him as provided for in
this act , if there is insufficient funds in the budget
fund out of which said warrant is payable to pay the
same .
•
The county treasurer shall return the county
school warrant book to the county court clerk after
he has signed and entered the county school war-
rants issued by the clerk , or mark the warrant or
warrants so issued void as provided for under the
provisions of this act .
The county court clerk shall upon demand after
the county school warrant book has been returned to
him by the county treasurer deliver the school war-
rants to the persons entitled to receive them .
§ 11. The county treasurer shall issue his check
in payment of all county school warrants presented
for payment , if, at the time such warrant is pre-
sented for payment , he has sufficient money on hand
belonging to the budget fund out of which the war-
rant is payable .
If the county treasurer should have insufficient
funds on hand , belonging to any budget fund out of
which county school warrants are payable , at the
time the county school warrant is presented for pay-
ment , he shall fill in the following which shall be
printed on all county school warrants in the proper
place , to -wit : " Due and payable on or before

from his knowledge of the accrual of current reve-
nues for the fiscal year, and if to be paid from funds
derived from other sources , from his knowledge
when said funds may be expected to be received by
him .
§ 12. The county treasurer shall keep in his
office a record book to be known as the " Interest
Bearing School Warrant Record , " which record
shall be provided for under the provisions of the
uniform accounting law of the State. The county
treasurer shall enter all interest bearing school war-
rants upon this record before they are delivered to
the person entitled thereto , and shall be entered
upon said record under a heading which shows the
budget fund from which the school warrants so
entered are payable . The record shall show the
date of each county warrant so entered , serial num-
ber, amount , and to whom payable , and the due date
of the warrant . As interest bearing school war-
rants are paid by the county treasurer , each war-
rant so paid shall be stamped " paid " by the county
treasurer with a stamp that cuts holes through the
warrant in stamping the word " paid " thereon ; and
the county treasurer shall thereupon enter on said
record the date of payment of the school warrant ,
to whom paid and the amount paid . He shall stamp
"paid " school warrants paid by him , that have not
been made interest bearing the same as the interest
bearing school warrants and all said warrants so
stamped " paid " shall be filed as a part of the rec-
ords of his office .
§ 13. If interest bearing county school war-
rants become due and payable before the county
treasurer has sufficient funds in his hands belong-
ing to the budget fund or funds out of which such
warrants are payable , he shall certify said fact to
the county court clerk . Said certificate of the county
treasurer to the county court clerk may include as
many interest bearing school warrants as the county
treasurer is going to be unable to pay at maturity ,
and said certificate shall give the date , serial num-
ber , amount , to whom issued , and to whom payable
if the school warrant has been transferred , together
with the amount of interest due on each separate
school warrant . This certificate shall be signed by
the county treasurer in his official capacity .
The county court clerk shall immediately upon
the filing of said certificate of the county treasurer
in his office endorse the date of filing thereon and
sign said endorsement in his official capacity . The
county court clerk shall number said certificates , as
claims are required to be numbered and record the
same upon the school claim book and properly index
the same.
The county court clerk shall issue renewal war-
rants as of the date the warrants renewed are due
and payable , and said renewal warrants shall be
payable out of the same budget fund that the war-
rant of which it is a renewal was payable and the
budget fund shall be designated in the face of the re-
newal warrant . The county court clerk shall issue
said renewal warrant from the same warrant book
from which the original warrant renewed was issued
and shall endorse thereon the following : " Renewal
of school warrant No... " All interest bearing
school warrants renewed under the provisions of
this act shall be surrendered to the county treasurer
before he delivers the renewal warrant to the person
entitled thereto , and said interest bearing school
warrant so renewed shall be stamped by the county
treasurer with the word " renewed " that cuts holes
through the warrant , and the warrant so renewed
shall be filed as a part of the records of his office .
The county court clerk shall issue the renewal
warrant to the person entitled thereto as shown by
the certificate of the county treasurer . The county
court clerk shall issue school warrants for each sep-
arate interest item due and payable as shown by the
certificate of the county treasurer to the person en-
titled thereto . A school warrant for interest shall
only include interest on one warrant . The interest
warrant shall be payable out of the budget fund
known as the " interest fund , " and the county court
clerk shall designate in each warrant for interest
that it is payable out of the interest fund .
The county court clerk shall deliver the county
warrant book to the county treasurer after he has
issued the warrants required by the certificate of the
county treasurer as aforesaid ; and the county treas-
urer shall sign said warrants , and fill in due dates
and the place where payable and sign the form pro-
vided therefor to make it interest bearing .
He shall draw his check in payment of the in-
terest warrants , if he has sufficient funds on hands
belonging to the budget fund known as the interest
fund , from which to pay said warrants for interest ,
and if he does not have sufficient funds to pay said
warrants for interest, he shall make them interest
bearing, as other school warrants are made interest
bearing.
14. All school warrants issued under the
provisions of this act shall be subject to call for pay-
ment by the county treasurer , when he has sufficient
funds on hand in any budget fund to pay outstand-
ing school warrants issued and charged to that bud-
get fund or funds . The county treasurer shall make
a call for payment of interest bearing school war-
rants by serial number in the order in which they
were issued , which interest bearing warrants , in the
aggregate , do not exceed the amount of money on
hand in the budget fund from which the warrant or
warrants called for payment are payable . The call
of the county treasurer shall be printed in a news-
paper published in the county once a week for a
period of two weeks or by giving the holders of the
warrants he desires to pay a written notice of the
call , in his discretion . No interest bearing school
warrant , so called for payment , shall bear interest
after the expiration of ten days after publication
of said notice , or said written notice has been given
to the holder or holders of said warrants .
§ 15. The county treasurer shall, upon receiv-
ing county revenues from the sheriff , or tax collec-
tor for the county , distribute the money so received
to the proper budget funds . The money received by
the county treasurer from other sources for school
purposes shall also be distributed to the proper
budget funds . This record book of the county treas-
urer shall be provided for under the provisions of
the uniform accounting law of the State .
§ 16. All contracts of the county board of edu-
cation entered into for and on behalf of the county
for the expenditure of county school funds provided
for in the school budget , shall contain a provision
that the contract shall not be deemed an obligation
of the county to pay the sums stipulated in the con-
tract , until the contract has been submitted to the
county treasurer , so that the county treasurer can
determine from his budget ledger whether the sums
to be expended under the contract are within the
budget fund out of which it is payable . If the county
treasurer determines from an examination of his
budget ledger that the sum proposed to be expended
under the contract is within the budget fund out of
which it is payable , then he shall enter the sum , to be
expended under said contract , on his . budget ledger
as a charge against the budget fund out of which it
is to be paid ; and shall thereupon attach a certificate
to said contract , showing that the sum proposed to
be expended is within the budget fund from which it
is to be paid and that said contracts have been en-
tered upon his budget ledger . Said certificates shall
be signed by the county treasurer in his official ca- .
pacity .
If the budget fund out of which the sum is to be
expended under the contract , be insufficient to pay
the sum proposed to be expended under the contract ,
the county treasurer shall refuse to sign said certi-
ficate , and shall write across the face of the contract
in red ink the following : " Void for want of funds ,
and sign said endorsement in his official capacity .
17. At the close of each fiscal year the
county board of education shall use any surplus
fund or funds remaining in any budget fund paid
the deficits , if any , in any budget fund or funds .
All deficits remaining in the budget fund , if any ,
after the surplus had been applied thereto , shall be
carried over into the next fiscal year , and provided
for in the school budget for the next fiscal year .
The deficits referred to in this section shall be
construed to be a deficit in the budget fund or funds
caused by the failure of current revenues to raise
the budget fund , or funds , in which said deficit may
occur .
§ 18. All books , receipts , blanks , records ,
county school warrant books and forms , required to
be used by the county treasurer , county court clerk
or other officials in the administration of the county
schools of the county under the provisions of this
act , shall be formulated under the provisions of the
uniform accounting law and other laws of the Com-
monwealth , and shall be provided for the officials
required to administer the fiscal affairs of the com-
mon schools of the county under this act, and shall
be uniform in each county of the Commonwealth .
It shall be the duty of the State Inspector and
Examiner to install in each county of the Common-
wealth a uniform system of accounting and book-
keeping in the administration of the fiscal affairs of
the common schools of the county .
§ 19. The county treasurer shall within sixty
( 60 ) days after the close of each fiscal school year ,
make off a financial statement as of June 30th , show-
ing in detail receipts and disbursements of the
county school funds received from all sources , and
in said statement to account for each budget fund
separately . The county treasurer shall file a copy of
said statement with the Division of Inspection and
Accounting of the State Department of Education ,
another copy with the State Inspector and Exam-
iner and another copy with the county court clerk
of the county . The statement filed with the county
court clerk shall be recorded on the minute book of
the county board of education by the clerk and prop-
erly indexed .
A copy of said financial statement of the county
treasurer issued at the close of each fiscal year shall
be published in full by the county treasurer one time
in a county newspaper published in the county , and
if no newspaper is published in the county then by
posting typewritten copies thereof at the court
house door and at five other public places in the
county . The cost of said publication shall be paid
by the county board of education as other claims
are paid .
§ 20. It shall be the duty of the county board
of education of each county within sixty ( 60 ) days
after this act takes effect to enter an order or orders
on the minute book of the county board of education
designating one or more banks or trust companies
as depositories for county school funds , from what-
ever source received , and the county treasurer , as
ex-officio treasurer of the county board of education ,
shall be required to deposit all school funds in the de-
pository or depositories so designated by said order
or orders by the county board of education . The
county board of education shall enter into an agree-
ment with said depository or depositories , so desig-
nated , for the payment of interest on school funds
on deposit , on daily balances , and said interest rates
shall not be less than two ( 2 % ) per cent on daily
balances . The depository shall credit interest to
the school fund every four months and shall send
deposit slips to the county treasurer showing said
credits . The county board of education shall re-
quire the county treasurer to execute , with approved
security, the bonds now required by law to be exe-
cuted by the county treasurer , and shall perform the
duties now imposed and that may be hereafter
imposed upon him as treasurer .
$ 21. The county board of education shall
after the teachers have been employed by contract
as required by law enter an order of appropriation
of their said salary , subject , however , to the failure
of school funds to meet the salary named in the con-
tract of employment , and subject to their discharge
for cause , with direction in the order of appropria-
tion for the clerk of the county court to issue war-
rants against the appropriation upon certificates
signed by the superintendent of common schools of
the county as to amount due under their con-
tract of employment . The certificate of the county
superintendent shall be filed by the clerk and
numbered as other claims are required to be num-
bered and recorded in the school claim book and
properly indexed .
§ 22. That section 2a of chapter 39 , Acts of
1922 Session of the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky , be and the same is repealed
and re-enacted , and as re -enacted shall read as fol-
lows :
The county board of education so elected shall
have the same power , authority and jurisdiction
now conferred by law on county boards of education .
§ 23. That section 3 of chapter 39 , Acts of
1922 Session of the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky , be and the same is repealed
and re-enacted , and as re-enacted shall read as fol-
lows :
All funds and securities due and belonging to
the county board of education for the use of the pub-
lic schools of the county districts , or of any subdis-
trict thereof, shall go into the hands of the county
treasurer , ex -officio treasurer of the county board of
education , who shall , together with his sureties , be
responsible therefor , and he shall pay out said funds
as provided for under the provisions of this act .
§ 24. The county board of education shall fix
a reasonable compensation for the county treasurer
to be allowed and paid out of the school funds ; they
shall also fix a reasonable compensation for the ser-
vices of the county court clerk to be allowed and
paid out of the school funds .
§ 25. That sections 8 and 9 of chapter 36 , Acts
of 1920 , of the General Assembly of the Common-
wealth of Kentucky , be and each of said sections are
hereby repealed .
§ 26. Any appropriation by the county board
of education in excess of any budget fund shall be
illegal and void , and all members of said county
board of education voting for such illegal appropri-
ation shall be deemed guilty of violation of the pro-
visions of this act .
27. Any officer or officers violating any of
the provisions of this act shall be deemed guilty of a
misdemeanor and subject to indictment , and upon
conviction , be fined in any sum not less than fifty
( $ 50.00 ) dollars , nor more than five hundred
($500.00 ) dollars for each offense .
§ 28. If any section , provision , paragraph or
clause of this act shall be declared unconstitutional ,
the invalidity of such section , provision , paragraph
or clause shall not affect the remaining sections ,
provisions , paragraphs or clauses of this act ; and it
is declared to be the legislative intent to enact each
clause , paragraph , provision and section of this act
separately.
$ 282 . The county board of education of any
county in the Commonwealth may in its discretion ,
in lieu of issue interest bearing county school war-
rants as provided for under the provisions of this
act , anticipate the revenues for the current year and
borrow money upon the faith thereof. If the county
board of education of any county elects to borrow
money in anticipation of current revenues under the
provisions of this section , the county board of edu-
cation shall enter an order upon the minute book or
order book of said county board of education , au-
thorizing the chairman of said county board of edu-
cation and the county treasurer to negotiate said
loan or loans , on the best terms possible not in ex-
cess of six per cent per annum , and shall authorize
the chairman of the county board of education to ex-
ecute a note or notes of the county board of educa-
tion , to be signed by the chairman of said board in
his official capacity , for the purpose of borrowing
said sum or sums which is authorized by said order
or orders of the county board of education . The
notes so executed by the chairman of the county
board of education shall be negotiable and shall des-
ignate the budget fund from which they are payable .
Said note or notes may be renewed by the county
board of education , if there is insufficient money be-
longing to the budget fund on hand from which the
note or notes are payable , when they become due
and payable . The county board of education may
issue notes against one or more budget funds in
their discretion in anticipation of current revenues
for the current year . All notes so issued by the
county board of education shall be charged on the
budget ledger by the county treasurer against the
budget fund from which they are payable , and no
obligation of the county board of education issued
under this section shall be valid if in excess of the
budget fund from which it is payable , and shall not
be a valid obligation of the county board of educa-
tion unless countersigned by the county treasurer .
The signature of the county treasurer on an obliga-
tion issued under this section shall be construed to
be his certificate that the obligation is within the
budget for the current year from which it is pay-
able , and the note has been charged against the bud-
get fund on his budget ledger of which it is payable .
§ 29. The county board of education of any
county of this Commonwealth , may in their discre-
tion , in lieu of issuing interest bearing county school
warrants as provided for under the provisions of
this act , anticipate the revenues for the current year
and borrow money upon the faith thereof . If the
county board of education elects to borrow money in
anticipation of current revenues under the provis-
ions of this section , the county board of education
shall enter an order upon the order book of said
county board of education authorizing the chair-
man and county treasurer to negotiate said loan or
loans , on the best terms possible and not in excess
of six (6 % ) per cent per annum , and shall author-
ize the chairman of the county board of education
to execute a note or notes of the county board of
education , to be signed by the chairman of said
board in his official capacity , for the purpose of bor-
rowing said sum or sums of money which is author-
ized by said orders of the county board of education .
The note or notes so executed by the chairman of
the county board of education shall be negotiable
and shall designate the budget fund from which the
note or notes are payable . Said note or notes so is-
sued may be renewed by the county board of educa-
tion , if there is insufficient money belonging to the
budget fund on hand from which the notes are pay-
able when they become due and payable . The county
board of education may issue notes against one or
more budget funds in anticipation of revenue for
the current year, but no money shall be borrowed as
against school funds coming from the Common-
wealth .
All notes so issued by the county board of edu-
cation shall be countersigned by the county treas-
urer , and shall be charged on the budget ledger by
the county treasurer against the budget fund from
which they are payable , and no obligation of the
county board of education issued under the provis-
ions of this section shall be valid if in excess of the
budget fund from which it is payable , and shall not
( be) a valid obligation of the county board of educa-
tion unless countersigned by the county treasurer .
The signature of the county treasurer on an obliga-
tion issued under the provisions of this section shall
be construed to be his certificate that the obligation
is within the budget fund for the current year from
which it is payable , and that the note has been
charged against the budget fund on his ledger out of
which it is payable .
§ 30. All acts and parts of acts in conflict
herewith are hereby repealed .
Approved March 27 , 1926 .

laws.summary: This statute amends existing law regarding independent school districts. It specifies that independent school districts embracing cities of the first five classes, along with their surrounding territories, and any independent graded common school districts with a census of 250 or more white children, will be designated as independent school districts. It also sets a condition for continued operation: districts (other than those in cities of the first five classes already operating as independent districts) must maintain a census of at least 250 white children, unless the State Board of Education determines that operating as an independent district allows for a more efficient school service program.

CHAPTER 42
.
AN ACT amending Section three
(3) of Article five
(
5) of
Chapter sixty
-five
(65
) of the Acts of the General Assembly of
nineteen thirty -four ( 1934 ) , being Section four thousand three
hundred ninety -nine -three (4399-3 ) , Kentucky Statutes , Bald-
win's Kentucky Statutes Service of nineteen thirty -four ( 1934 ) ,
relating to independent school districts .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
That Section three ( 3 ) of Article five ( 5 ) of Chap-
ter sixty -five ( 65 ) of the Acts of the General As-
sembly of nineteen thirty -four ( 1934 ) being Section
four thousand three hundred ninety-nine -three
( 4399-3 ) , Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's Kentucky
Statute Service nineteen thirty -four ( 1934 ) Edi-
tion , be and the same hereby is amended by repeal-
ing said Section in its entirety and re-enacting same
so that as amended and re -enacted said Section will
read as follows , to wit :
Independent school districts . All school districts
embracing cities of the first five classes together
with the territory within their limits , including any
territory which has heretofore been added for school
purposes outside of the limits of such cities or dis-
tricts , and any territory which may be included by
any future change in the limits of such cities , and
all independent graded common school districts
having a school census enumeration of two hundred
fifty ( 250 ) or more white children shall hereafter be
known and designated as independent school dis-
tricts , provided that no such district other than cities
of the first , second , third , fourth , and fifth classes ,
operating as independent districts at the time this
Act becomes effective , shall continue to operate
when its school census enumeration of white chil-
dren falls below two hundred fifty ( 250 ) pupils un-
less it appears to the State Board of Education that
the district can maintain a more efficient program
of school service by operating as an independent
district . The State Board of Education may per-
mit an independent graded common school district
existing at the time of the passage of this Act with
a census enumeration of white children below two
hundred and fifty ( 250 ) to operate as a temporary
independent school district for four -year periods
beginning with July first ( 1 ) , nineteen thirty-four
(1934 ) , if it appears to the State Board of Educa-
tion that such district can maintain a more efficient
program of school service by operating as a tempo-
rary independent district , and the decision of the
State Board of Education shall be final ; provided ,
at the end of each four -year period the State Board
of Education may permit such independent district
to operate for an additional four -year period on the
condition that such inspection as the State Board
of Education may make shows that it is operating
a school in accordance with the school law and the
standards , rules , and regulations set up by the State
Board of Education . The State Board of Educa-
tion may by order make any temporary independ-
ent school district a part of the county district
whenever the same is (it ) not complying with the
school law and the standards , rules , and regulations
of the State Board of Education , and after it has
been given a reasonable time , to be fixed by the
State Board of Education , within which to so com-
ply . The first application of such district to operate
as a temporary independent . district shall be filed
with the State Board of Education not later than
July first ( 1 ) , nineteen thirty -four ( 1934 ) . Each
subsequent application of such independent district
to operate as a temporary independent district for
an additional four -year period shall be filed with
the State Board of Education not later than May
first ( 1 ) , of the last year of the four -year period .
Each independent school district shall maintain at
least an approved twelve -grade school service for
the white children residing in its district . Provided ,
however , any independent school district that main-
tains within the district at least an approved ten-
grade school service for the white children residing
in its district , may furnish free transportation for
white children residing within the district to attend
school in an adjoining district for completing the
eleventh and twelfth grade school work and pro-
vide by contract with an adjoining district , which
maintains at least an approved twelve -grade pro-
gram of school service , for such children procuring
eleventh and twelfth grade service in such adjoin-
ing district . Provided further that each independ-
ent school district shall provide by establishment
or by contract with another district for at least an
approved twelve -grade program of school service .
for its colored children .
All laws in conflict herewith are hereby repealed .
Approved February 25 , 1936 .

laws.summary: This act provides for the payment of tuition and fees by the Commonwealth of Kentucky for residents who are qualified to study at the University of Kentucky or other state institutions but cannot due to Section 187 of the Kentucky Constitution. These individuals are permitted to pursue such courses at educational institutions outside of the state, and their expenses will be covered. The State Superintendent of Public Instruction will ascertain and pay these tuition and fees, with the State Board of Education prescribing rules and regulations. Funds are appropriated for this purpose, with a limit of $175.00 per person per school year.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 43 .
AN ACT to provide State aid for education in certain courses
of study of State students pursuing certain courses of study
at educational institutions outside of the State for whom no
such courses are provided in the educational institutions of
the State , and prescribing the conditions under which such
State aid may be granted and authorizing and directing the
State Board of Education of Kentucky to administer pro-
visions of this Act , making an appropriation therefor and
declaring an emergency . This Act to be known as the "Ander
son -Myer State Aid Act ."
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
Section One . That pending the full develop-
ment of the educational institutions of the Common-
wealth of Kentucky , all bona fide residents of this
State at the time of making written application for
the benefits provided in this Act and have been such
residents continuously for five ( 5 ) years next pre-
ceding the time of filing said application , and who
are duly qualified for matriculation in courses of
study offered at the University of Kentucky , but
who , because of Section one hundred eighty - seven
(187 ) of the Constitution of Kentucky cannot pur-
sue such courses at the University of Kentucky or
other State institutions at which such courses are
offered , or who have otherwise qualified to pursue
such courses therein , and who are now pursuing or
may hereafter pursue such courses in educational
institutions outside of the State whereof no courses
of study are provided for such persons within this
State , shall have their tuition and fees paid at such
institutions by the Commonwealth of Kentucky .
Section Two . That such tuition and fees be as-
certained by the State Superintendent of Public
Instruction and paid upon requisition of him out of
funds not otherwise appropriated .
Section Three . That the State Board of Edu-
cation shall prescribe the rules and regulations gov-
erning the granting of State aid under this Act . In
event the funds appropriated for the purpose of
carrying out the provisions of this Act are insuf-
ficient for the purpose in any year , said Board of
Education shall have the right to prorate the same
among such persons whose applications are ap-
proved therefor pursuant to the provisions of this
Act ; and provided further , that not more than one
hundred and seventy -five ( $175.00 ) dollars shall be
allowed to any such person for the purposes and
under the provisions of this Act during any one
school year of nine ( 9 ) months .
Section Four . That for the purpose of carrying
out the provisions of this Act and for no other pur-
pose , there is hereby appropriated for the State
Board of Education of Kentucky , out of funds in
the State Treasury not otherwise appropriated the
following sums : Five thousand ( $5,000.00 ) dollars
for the fiscal year ending June thirtieth ( 30th ) one
thousand nine hundred thirty - seven , and five thou-
sand ( $5,000.00 ) dollars for the fiscal year ending
June thirtieth ( 30th ) , one thousand nine hundred
thirty -eight .
Section Five . That if any part of this Act shall
be held unconstitutional , such holding shall not in-
validate any other portion thereof .
Section Six . It being immediately necessary for
educational opportunity to certain persons of this
Commonwealth , and for the preservation of the
public peace , health and safety , an emergency is
hereby declared to exist , by reason whereof this
Act shall take effect and be in full force from and
after passage and approval . Approved February 25 .

This Act to be known as the "Ander son -Myer State Aid Act ."

six -b1 ( 1486 -b1 ) to one thousand four eighty -six b -twenty-
seven ( 1486 -b27 ) , inclusive , of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes ,
one thousand nine hundred thirty ( 1930 ) Edition . This Act to
be known as the Rives -Robinson Registration Law .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
Section One . This Act may be cited and referred
to as the " General Registration Act " . The term
"initial registration " shall refer to the general
initial registration to be held in each precinct as
provided in this Act .
Any word importing the masculine gender , when
used herein , shall extend to and be deemed to in-
clude women as well as men .
Section Two . Every citizen of the United States
not otherwise disqualified by the laws of this Com-
monwealth , who is twenty - one years of age or who
will become twenty -one years of age on or before
the next regular election to be held in November
of any year, or on or before the date of any special
election , and who will have been a resident of the
State of Kentucky one year , and of the county six
months , and of the precinct , outside the corporate
limits of a city of the first class , in such county for
sixty days next preceding such election , and who is
a registered voter , and is otherwise qualified , shall
be entitled to vote for all officers elective by the
people , and on all measures or questions submitted
for determination by the voters at any regular or
special election ; provided , however , that only per-
sons who are duly and properly registered as herein
provided shall be permitted to vote at the primary
election to be held on the first Saturday in August ,
one thousand nine hundred thirty -six ( 1936 ) , and
at all primary , general and special elections held
thereafter .
Section Three . The initial registration held
under this Act shall be at the voting precincts in
each county at the primary election to be held on
the first Saturday in August , one thousand nine
hundred thirty -six ( 1936 ) . After said initial regis-
tration , all further registration or change of regis-
tration shall be made in the manner herein pro-
vided .
Section Four . Any person possessing the quali-
fications for registration as a legal voter as set out
in Section two ( 2 ) hereof, and who fails to register
on such primary election date , may appear before
the county court clerk of the county of the residence
of such voter , between the fifteenth day of August
and the tenth day of October , and between the
fifteenth day of November and the tenth day of
July of any year ( Sundays and legal holidays ex-
cepted ) at any hour of the day the office of the
County Court Clerk may be open for business . Any
voter who wishes to change his party affiliation may
appear before the clerk between said dates of any
year, and upon his request , the clerk shall make
said change on the registration book .
Section Five . No person shall be registered who
does not personally appear before the officers on
said primary election date , or who does not per-
sonally appear before the County Court Clerk at
and within the times hereinbefore set out , except
those hereinafter provided for , and the voter , if he
be not known to the clerk, or if any bystander shall
challenge the voter's right to register , shall be
sworn by the clerk and shall answer any and all
questions asked him by the clerk or bystander ,
touching his qualifications as a voter , or his right
to be then and there registered , and on the registra-
tion book opposite the name of the voter , the clerk
shall write the words, " sworn as to qualifications " .
Any voter otherwise qualified who , on account of age,
infirmity or illness , is not able to attend the County
Clerk's office of the county of his residence during
the time between the dates above set out , may be-
tween the first and thirtieth day of September ( both
inclusive ) be registered in the following manner :
He shall present to the clerk by mail or at the hands
of some friend , his affidavit stating that his failure
to appear was due to age, infirmity , or illness , and
an affidavit of a physician or neighbor corroborating
the voter's affidavit . Upon compliance with the
foregoing the clerk shall enter his name on the regis-
tration book for the precinct of his residence , the
same as if he had registered before the clerk in
person .
If any such voter be unknown to the Clerk , or if
his right to register be challenged , it shall be the
duty of the Clerk to write opposite his name on the
registration book the word , " questioned " , and it
shall be the duty of the election officers , when said
voter applies for a ballot , if there be any doubt of
his qualification to vote , to swear said voter, who
shall, under oath , answer such questions as may be
asked him touching his qualifications .
Section Six . The Attorney General of Kentucky ,
and the two apointive members of the State Board
of Election Commissioners shall constitute a Board
to prepare proper blanks and record forms for the
registration of voters as herein provided . It shall
be the duty of said Board to have said blanks and
record forms properly prepared on or before the
tenth day of July , one thousand nine hundred thirty-
six ( 1936 ) , by which date the necessary blanks and
forms shall be in the hands of the county court
clerks of each county , for distribution to the pri-
mary election officers in each precinct of the State .
Said blanks and forms shall be printed , prepared
and furnished as other books are now printed and
prepared for the Commonwealth , and shall be paid
for out of the State Treasury . Separate card or
looseleaf registration record forms for the regis-
tration of the individual voters shall be prepared
in duplicate , upon durable paper and of convenient
size and shape as determined by the Board , the
original cards or forms being printed upon white
paper and marked " Original " , and the duplicates
printed upon paper of another color , and marked
" Copy", each of said cards or forms providing for
the entry thereon of the following information ,
signatures and affidavit of the voter :
