At the time of registering a voter , the Clerk shall
enter upon the original record form the name of the
voter and all other data and information called for
on said form ; after such entries have been made ,
the voter shall , in his own hand , write his signature
upon both the original and copy record forms . The
clerk , either at the time of registering the voter or
as soon thereafter as practicable , shall enter upon
the copy record form the name of the voter together
with all of the data and information appearing on
the original record form , so that the copy form shall
be an exact duplicate of the original , and shall at all
times keep in a safe place in his office both the
original and copy record forms except that the copy
forms shall be furnished to the election officers as
hereinafter provided .
In the event any applicant for registration states
under oath that he cannot write his name , the clerk
shall sign the registration record forms for such
person , and such person shall sign said records by
making his mark thereon and the clerk shall attest
the same .
The original and copy record forms shall be filed
in securely locked binders or card files , by pre-
cincts , in such systematic order as the Board shall
prescribe and shall constitute the precinct registers
to be used as hereinafter provided .
Section Seven . Upon each primary , special or
general election , the precinct register containing the
"copy" record forms signed by the voters , after
having been first securely locked in the binders or
containers provided therefor , shall be delivered by
the county court clerk to the precinct election clerk
of each precinct at the same time he delivers the
ballots , and the election clerk shall give the county
court clerk a receipt for same and it shall be the
duty of the precinct election clerk to produce such
precinct register so delivered to him (or see that
same is so produced ) at the proper polling place in
his precinct at the opening of the polls on such elec-
tion day. The county court clerk shall also at the
time of delivering the ballots , deliver to the pre-
cinct election clerk a complete and correct single-
spaced typewritten list , in triplicate , of all voters
then registered in said precinct and entitled to vote
in said election , giving the name and address of
each voter , each page being separately attested by
the county court clerk ; the election clerk shall , at
the opening of the polls , post one copy of the type-
written list outside the entrance to the voting place ,
and deliver one copy to the sheriff of the election .
retaining the third copy for the use of himself and
the judges of the election . At the close of the polls
the election clerk shall deposit one copy of said list
in the ballot box ; the election officers who return
the ballot boxes to the county court clerk's office
shall at the same time return said precinct register
to the county court clerk and secure a receipt
therefor .
Section Eight. If any person applying to vote at
any primary , special or general election is unknown
to the election officers , or is challenged , such person ,
before a ballot is issued to him, shall be required
to sign his name upon a comparative signature card ,
unless such person signed his registration record
by making his mark , and it shall be the duty of the
officers of election in that precinct to compare the
signature of such person with the signature of such
person in the registration record form in the pre-
cinct register. The challengers of the respective
political parties present shall also have the right to
compare said signature at the same time said com-
parison is made by the election officers . If such com-
parison of signatures shall create a doubt in the
mind of two of the election officers , as to whether
the person applying to vote is the same person as
the registrant , no ballot shall be issued to him un-
less he shall otherwise satisfactorily establish his
identity as to the registrant .
In the event any person applying to vote at any
election shall state that he cannot sign his name
as above provided , the judges of the election in that
precinct shall immediately swear such person as
to his name and his inability to write , and there-
upon the judges of election and the challengers of
the respective political parties present shall ex-
amine the registration record in the precinct regis-
ter , and if it shown by said record that the person
of that same name signed his name on the registra-
tion record, a ballot shall not be issued to the per-
son so applying , unless the inability of the person
to sign his name at the date of such election is due
to some physical disability arising subsequent to
his registration .
It shall be the duty of the election officers to make ,
keep and return to the county court clerk , a record
or record sheets to be provided in the same manner
as other election paraphernalia are provided , of
each person so sworn , and showing the disposition
made of such case.
It shall be the duty of the clerk of each precinct ,
immediately after issuing the ballot to any voter ,
at the primary election held in August , one thou-
sand nine hundred thirty -six ( 1936 ) , and at every
primary and general election held thereafter , to in-
dicate at the place provided therefor on the regis-
tration record form that such person voted at such
primary or election . The fact that any person is
registered shall constitute prima facie evidence only
of his right to vote and shall not prevent the officers
of any primary or general election from refusing
to issue him a ballot for causes and in the manner
provided by the general election laws of this State .
Section Nine . Not less than ten days prior to the
primary election held on the first Saturday in
August , one thousand nine hundred thirty -six
( 1936 ) , the county court clerk of each county shall
appoint two special deputy clerks for each precinct
in his county , who shall serve for the day of such
election only , and who shall be appointed one from
each of the two political parties , having representa-
tion on the State Board of Election Commissioners .
These appointments to be made from a list of two
or more names for each precinct submitted to the
County Court Clerk by the County Executive Com-
mittee of each of such political parties , and who
shall be sworn to faithfully perform their duties .
At the time of delivering the ballots to the clerk of
election for each precinct , the county court clerk
shall also deliver to each election clerk two precinct
registers containing , respectively , a supply of orig-
inal and " copy " registration record forms , serially
numbered and equal in number to the total number
of votes cast in that precinct at the general election
held in November , one thousand nine hundred thirty-
five ( 1935 ) , such forms being securely locked in
binders or containers provided therefor , before de-
livery by the county court clerk, who shall take re-
ceipts therefor from the clerks of election . On the
day of said primary election , each such deputy clerk
so appointed shall be present at the opening of the
polls in the precinct for which he is appointed , in the
room in which such election is to be held , and the
clerk of the election shall there deliver to such
deputy clerk the original and the " copy " precinct
registration forms received from the county court
clerk . The sheriff of the election shall provide , at a
convenient place within the voting place , a table and
)
at least three chairs for the use of the deputy clerks
and persons being registered . The deputy clerks
shall there register in the manner herein provided ,
every person who offers for registration during the
hours in which such election is held , and who has the
legal right to vote or who will have the legal right
to vote , in such precinct , at the next election to be
held therein . Every person registering shall be re-
quired to sign his name , in his own hand except as
herein after provided , upon both the original and the
"copy " registration record forms . The original
registration record form shall be entirely filled out
with the name and serial number of the person reg-
istering and all the information called for on said
form , before the signature of the registrant is made
thereon , but only the signature of the registrant and
the attestation of the deputy clerk shall be made
upon the " copy " registration record form . In the
event any applicant for registration states that he
cannot write his name , the deputy clerk , after swear-
ing the applicant to such statement , shall sign both
the original and " copy " registration record forms
for him, and such person shall sign said records by
making his mark thereon , attested by the deputy
clerk .
If the deputy clerk be in doubt as to the right of
any person to be registered , or if his right to regis-
tration be challenged by any officer of the election
or by any challenger of a political party present ,
the applicant shall be sworn by the deputy clerk
touching his right to be registered and may be inter-
rogated thereon by the deputy clerks or any officer
of the election ; not more than two citizens may also
be sworn and interrogated touching his right to
registration . The judges of the election shall de-
cide all questions relating to the qualifications of
the applicant for registration , except that in case
of a difference of opinion between the judges , the
clerk of the election shall have the deciding vote .
If any applicant whose right to be registered is
challenged is allowed to register , the word " ques-
tioned " shall be written by the deputy clerk oppo-
site his signature on both the original and the
"copy" registration record forms . At the close of
the polls at said primary election , the deputy clerks
shall endorse on reverse side of the last original
and " copy" registration record forms signed by a
registrant during such election , the notation " End
of precinct registration " , and such notation shall
be signed by the deputy clerks and by both judges
of the election . The election officers who return the
ballot boxes to the county court clerk's office shall
at the same time return said original and " copy"
registration record forms to the county court clerk ,
and secure a receipt therefor ; upon receipt of such
registration record forms from the election officers ,
the county court clerk shall promptly copy into the
"copy" registration record forms , in the corre-
sponding blanks provided therefor , all information ,
data and remarks which appear on the original
registration record forms relative to such voters .
Each deputy clerk conducting such precinct regis-
tration shall be paid as compensation for his serv-
ices , the sum of three dollars , to be paid out of the
county treasury .
Section Ten . In case a registered voter changes
his place of residence from one precinct to another
in the same county , or whenever the boundaries of
the precinct in which he is registered are changed
by law so as to remove him from that precinct , he
may appear before the county court clerk and , upon
his making oath as to such removal and indicating
the precinct into which he has moved or been trans-
ferred by such change of boundaries , the clerk shall ,
under the heading of " Remarks " on his original
and " copy " registration record forms , write the
words " Removed to ..precinct . "
(Filling in the name of the precinct to which he
has so removed ) , and shall at the same time regis-
ter such voter in the proper precinct . Such trans-
fers shall be registered only on those days when
registrations are provided for under Section four
(4) hereof.
Section Eleven . If any original or " copy " regis-
tration record form is lost or destroyed , or be-
comes so mutilated , blotted , torn or defaced or
other wise in such condition as to render it difficult ,
troublesome or unsafe to use such record , it shall
be the duty of the county court clerk to cause a
new registration record form to be made and exe-
cuted in such manner as may be necessary , con-
sistently with the provisions of this Act , the cost
thereof to be paid out of the county treasury . If
the re-registration of the voters of an entire pre-
cinct shall so become necessary , it shall be held in
the precinct at the next ensuing primary or general
election , in the same manner as the initial registra-
tion herein provided for . If such re -registration is
made necessary by the loss or destruction of regis-
tration records through the negligence or willful
misconduct of any person , such person shall be
liable to the Commonwealth for the cost of such re-
registration of any precinct , to be recovered in a
civil action in the name of the Commonwealth of
Kentucky .
Section Twelve . The following methods shall be
used to purge the registration records and keep
them corrected up to date :
(a) It shall be the duty of the Registrar of Vital
Statistics for each county to furnish to the county
court clerk of his county , at least once a month , an
official and certified report containing the names
and addresses of all persons whose death , occurring
in said county during the month immediately pre-
ceding , has been reported to said registrar ; like-
wise , it shall be the duty of each Circuit Court Clerk
to furnish to the county court clerk, at least once
a month , an official and certified report containing
the names and addresses of all persons who have ,
during the month immediately preceding , been, by
the circuit court of such county , adjudged insane
or convicted of any offense which , under the laws
of this State , operates as an exclusion from suffrage
and the offense of which such persons have been
convicted . Immediately upon receipt of such lists
of deaths , adjudications of insanity , and convic-
tions , it shall be the duty of the Clerk to mail to
every person whose name is included in any of such
lists , at the address appearing on the registration
record of such person in the office of the County
Court Clerk , stating that the registration of such
person will , unless protest is filed within five days
from and including the date of such notice , be can-
celled , and the reason therefor . If no protest is
filed within said time , the registration record of such
person shall be cancelled . If protest is filed within
said time , the Clerk shall investigate the matter and
shall not cancel such record until after the prot-
estant has been given an opportunity to be heard .
(b ) The failure of any person registered as
herein provided to vote at any primary or general
election for two consecutive years as shown by the
voting record of such person on his registration
record shall be prima facie evidence that such per-
son is no longer entitled to registration . The County
Court Clerk shall , in the month of January of each
year , cause a check of all registrations to be made
and a list prepared of all persons whose registra-
tion records indicate that such persons have failed
to vote at any primary or general election for two
consecutive years , and shall mail a notice to each
of such persons on said list , at the address of such
person appearing on the registration record , stating
that his registration will , unless protest is filed
within five days from the date of such notice , be
cancelled , and the reason therefor . If protest is
filed , said Clerk shall make an investigation , and
shall not cancel said registration if the person is
found to be legally entitled to registration . If no
protest is filed within said time , his registration
shall be cancelled , and to vote thereafter he shall be
required to register as if he had never registered .
Section Thirteen . When the county executive
committee of any political party having representa-
tion on the State Board and County Board of Elec-
tion Commissioners shall desire it , the County Board
of Election Commissioners shall appoint two offi-
cers for any precinct, whose duty it shall be to purge
the registration list in that precinct , and these offi-
cers need not reside in the precinct . If the county
committee of either of such political parties shall
desire to have the registration purged in any pre-
cinct , such committee shall file a request in writing
with the County Board of Election Commissioners
not later than two weeks before the next ensuing
primary or general election in any year ; such re-
quest shall state the name and address of each voter
whose name is challenged , and the ground upon
which challenged . It shall be the duty of the County
Board of Election Commissioners , within three
days after the filing with them of such request , to
appoint two purgation officers as aforesaid , one
from each of the political parties having represen-
tation on the State Board and County Board of
Election Commissioners , these appointments to be
made from a list of names submitted to the County
Board of Election Commissioners by the county ex-
ecutive committee of each of such political parties .
The list of challenged voters shall be turned over
to these two purgation officers , who shall be sworn
faithfully to discharge their duties as such , and
they shall meet in the precinct for which they are
to act , at some place designated and provided by
the sheriff . Said officers shall have the power to
summons and swear witnesses , and shall conduct a
hearing in the precinct at such time as they may
fix ; each voter who has been challenged shall , unless
upon investigation the purgation officers shall agree
that the challenge is unfounded and the voter law-
fully registered , be notified of the time and place of
the meeting at which the challenge against him will
be heard, such notice to be in writing and served
upon the challenged voter either by delivering or
offering , to deliver a copy of said notice to him in
person or , if said voter cannot be found at his place
of residence shown on his registration record , by
leaving a copy thereof with any person over the age
of sixteen residing in the same family with said
voter , or, if no such person be there , by affixing a
copy of said notice to the front door of such place
or residence . The person who serves such notice
shall return a copy thereof to the purgation officers ,
with an endorsement thereon stating when and how
it was served , and if a copy was not delivered to
the person to whom it was directed , the endorse-
ment must state the facts authorizing the manner
of service adopted , if the person serving the notice
be an officer , his endorsement must show his official
position ; if he be not an officer , he must make an
affidavit that his endorsement is true , that he is
over sixteen years of age , and that he is not a party
to nor interested in the proceeding . Such endorse-
ment of an officer , or such endorsement and affidavit
of one who is not an officer , shall be proof of
service .
After investigation and hearing such evidence as
may be presented , the purgation officers shall deter-
mine whether the voter is properly and legally reg-
istered ; such hearing shall be conducted in a sum-
mary manner and the officers , in their discretion,
may reasonably limit the number of witnesses tes-
tifying for either party . If the purgation officers
find that the challenged voter is not properly and
legally registered , his registration shall thereupon
be canceled by them. The failure of any voter
against whom a notice of challenge has been served
as provided herein to appear at such hearing shall
be prima facie evidence that he is not entitled to
registration , and his registration record shall be
cancelled . Appeals from the action of the purga-
tion officers may be taken in the manner hereinafter
provided . If they find that he is legally and prop-
erly registered , nothing further shall be done with
his name . The County Court Clerk shall turn the
"copy " registration record of the precinct over to
such purgation officers when they are to hold their
meetings , taking their receipt therefor , and upon
the conclusion of their meetings , the purgation offi-
cers shall return such registration record to the
County Court Clerk and take his receipt therefor .
In the event the purgation officers disagree as to
whether the registration of any person should be
canceled , they or either of them shall reduce to
writing the facts as developed and certify such
statement of facts to the County Court Clerk , who
shall forthwith assign the case of each such voter
challenged to the judge of the County Court , who
shall promptly hear the case de novo , summarily
decide the question , and endorse on the statement
Acts- 5
an order disposing of the same , returning the state-
ment with his endorsement thereon to the clerk .
The clerk , upon receipt of such certification from
such purgation officers , shall immediately issue a
notice to the challenged voter to appear before the
judge of the County Court not later than three days
after the service of such notice , which notice shall
be served by any officer authorized to serve sub-
poenas or by any person authorized by law to serve
notices .
Section Fourteen . When any person is ag-
grieved by any act of the purgation officers in
respect to his registration , or when any person or
executive committee that has challenged the regis-
tration of any voter is aggrieved by any act of the
purgation officers in respect to the registration of
such person , such person or such committee so ag-
grieved shall have the right to apply to the judge
of the County Court , with a written statement of
the act of the purgation officers and the grounds of
his , or its complaint . Before such application is
made , written notice shall have been given to the
purgation officers setting out the time and place at
which such application will be made , and the
grounds therefor , so as to give the purgation officers
a reasonable opportunity to be present at such time
and place . The judge to whom such application is
made shall , at the time fixed in the notice , or a sub-
sequent time appointed by the said judge , summa-
rily decide the question presented and endorse on
the statement of complaint an order disposing of
the same. The action of said judge in such case
shall be final and upon return of the statement of
complaint, with the order of the judge disposing of
same endorsed thereon , to the County Court Clerk ,
the clerk shall correct his record in accordance with
such order .
Section Fifteen . Any voter may, by giving five
days ' notice in writing , to any person whose name
has been registered, move the county court to strike
his name from the register , and both parties may
introduce witnesses , not exceeding two in number
on each side . Said notice must be served person-
ally . If at the hearing the court shall be of the
opinion that the person registered is not lawfully
entitled to register , it shall direct the clerk to strike
his name from the register , by inserting opposite to
it the words " Stricken off by order of the county
court." If the person upon whom notice is at-
tempted to be served cannot be found , the clerk
shall write opposite such name on the registration
book the word " doubtful " and when at an election
such person whose name is marked " doubtful "
shall offer to vote he shall be sworn , and his right
to vote investigated fully .
Section Sixteen . The Clerk shall preserve for a
period of not less than two years all cancelled
registration records in a separate file , and said
records shall be filed and arranged in alphabetical
order for the entire county according to the last
name of the person registered thereon . Said file
shall be designated the " Canceled Registration
File " . When the registration record is canceled ,
the original record and the copy thereof shall be
marked in large letters in ink " Canceled " , and
there shall also be noted thereon in ink the date of
and reason for such cancellation .
Section Seventeen . Any county court clerk or
deputy county court clerk who shall falsely or
fraudulently register the name of any person , or
permit any person to register , knowing that such
person it not entitled to register , or who shall fraud-
ulently alter, change , or make erasures in , or add
names to any registration record or who shall reg-
ןיד
ister the name of any person at any other time or
times , as fixed herein , or who shall fail or refuse to
deliver to the person entitled thereto , or to the
proper election officers , copies of the registration ,
or the copy of the records to be used in such elec-
tions as they are required to be used for , shall be
deemed guilty of a felony and , upon conviction , pun-
ished by confinement in the penitentiary for not less
than one nor more than three years , and shall there-
after be disqualified from holding any elective or
appointive office in this Commonwealth .
Section Eighteen . Any person knowingly or
fraudulently , shall cause himself to be regis-
tered in more than one precinct , or in a pre-
cinct other than that in which he is a legal voter ,
or shall register under any name than his real
name , or who shall give a false address , or who in
any manner or method shall cause himself to be
registered when he is not legally entitled to regis-
ter , or any person , or officer who knowingly or
fraudulently shall in any way aid , abet , counsel or
advise in the commission of any such act , or acts ,
shall be deemed guilty of a felony , and upon con-
viction shall be confined in the penitentiary for not
less than one year nor more than three years and
shall thereafter be disqualified from holding any
appointive office in the Commonwealth .
Section Nineteen . Any county court clerk or
election officer , or other person who shall un-
lawfully alter or change any registration book , or
fraudulently add any name thereto , or who shall
willfully secrete , suppress , mutilate or destroy , or
make , or use any false or fraudulent registration
book , shall be deemed guilty of a felony , and shall
be, upon conviction , confined in the penitentiary
for not less than one nor more than three years and
shall thereafter be disqualified from holding any
appointive office in the Commonwealth .
Section Twenty . Any person who shall at-
tempt to or forcibly prevent any person from
registering , or shall in any way unlawfully inter-
fere with any person registering , or shall prevent
or interfere with a clerk in carrying out his duties
with relation to the registration of voters , shall be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor , and shall be fined
not less than one hundred nor more than five hun-
dred dollars , or imprisonment for not less than six
months nor more than twelve months , or both , in
the discretion of the court or the jury .
Section Twenty - One . The clerk of the county
court shall permit any citizen to inspect at all
reasonable hours , or to make copies of any regis-
tration book , without any fee , and he shall also , upon
request , furnish to any person requesting same a
copy or copies of the registration book , or books ,
for which he shall receive compensation as pro-
vided in the succeeding Section .
Section Twenty -Two . The clerk for his serv-
ices in the carrying out of the provisions of
this law shall be entitled to collect the following
fees :
For original registration , except the initial reg-
istration in the precincts , two cents for each person
registered ; for copying from the original registry
into the "copy" book , or copying from the original
for the use of any person , two cents per name , in-
cluding data and remarks ; for making copies of
any registration books lost, mutiliated or destroyed ,
two cents per name , data and remarks included ; for
preparing the lists of registered voters for use of
election officers as required by Section seven (7)
hereof, two cents for each five names listed ; for all
services with relation to the purging of the regis-
tration as hereinafter required , five cents for every
name ordered stricken off, or canceled as provided
in Section twelve (12 ) hereof, all of which expenses
and fees shall be paid by the county , except where
the copying be done for an individual requesting
the copy.
Section Twenty -Three . Whenever in this Act a
duty is imposed on the county clerk, it may be per-
formed by any deputy county court clerk, who may
be subject to all penalties provided herein against
the county clerk , and for the registration held at the
primary election all penalties imposed upon the
county clerk in the violation of this law , when such
violations occur , shall be imposed upon the deputy
clerk, or the clerk of the election . All election of-
ficers shall be liable to the penalty provided in
Sections eighteen ( 18 ) and nineteen ( 19 ) hereof,
for any violation of law mentioned in such cases ,
and for any violation or refusal to permit the
deputy county court clerk to enter and remain in
the voting room, or for any interfenence of such
officer in the performance of his duties under this
law shall be punished as provided in Section twenty
( 20 ) hereof .
Nothing in this law shall be construed to prevent
any soldier, sailor , officer or employee of the United
States Government , or officer or employee of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , or any person coming
within the meaning of the word , " absent voter " ,
from registering in the manner now or as may here-
after be provided by law .
Section Twenty -Four . If any section , para-
graph , clause or separable provision of this Act
should be adjudged to be unconstitutional , such de-
cision shall not affect , or render unconstitutional
any other section , paragraph , clause or separable
provision of the Act, it being the intention of the
General Assembly in enacting this Act to enact
each section , paragraph , clause and provision sep-
arately .
Chapter sixty -four ( 64 ) of the Acts of the Gen-
eral Assembly one thousand nine hundred twenty-
four ( 1924 ) session as amended , being Sections one
thousand four hundred eighty-six b-one (1486b - 1 )
to one thousand four hundred eighty -six b-27
( 1486b -27 ) , both inclusive , of Carroll's Kentucky
Statutes , one thousand nine hundred thirty ( 1930 )
Edition , are hereby repealed . All other laws and
parts of laws relating to the registration of voters
residing outside of the corporate limits of cities of
the first class in conflict herewith are hereby re-
pealed to the extent of such conflict .
Approved February 17 , 1936 .

shall be covered into the State Treasury immedi-
ately after the close of each month through the
Department of Finance and placed to the credit of
the General Expenditure Fund , excepting those
revenues which are specifically allocated to the .
State Road Fund or the Revolving Fund which shall
be credited to their respective funds as provided for
in this Act . The fees , receipts , and/or revenue of
every officer , department , division , subdivision , com-
mission , board , institution , or agency of the State
Government shall be covered into the State Treas-
ury immediately after the close of each month , and
placed to the credit of the General Expenditure
Fund and shall be used to defray the expenses of
the State Government , and the appropriations made
from the General Expenditure Fund in this Act ,
unless otherwise specifically appropriated to one of
the professional boards , commissions , institutions ,
agencies , or subdivisions of the State Government
for Revolving Fund purposes ; such agencies shall
be only those that are listed in this Act as having
been approved for Revolving Fund Accounts .
29.
The appropriations herein made for the ordinary
recurring expenses and extraordinary expense and
capital outlay for any officer , department , board ,
commission , institution , and subdivision of the
State Government of the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky shall not be available for expenditure until
allotted as now provided by law , and such appro-
priations as are specifically made in this Act are
hereby declared to be maximum and conditional
appropriations except when the Governor deter-
mines an emergency exists in any department , board ,
commission , institution , or subdivision of the State
Government requiring an additional allotment of
funds to be made from the General Emergency Fund
hereby placed at his disposal and made a specific
appropriation to be used by him to meet existing
emergencies so determined by him . This appropri-
ation is designated under Section 4 , " EXECUTIVE
DEPARTMENT " , as Item ( d ) , Part I , for the fiscal
year ending June 30 , 1939 , and Section 4, Item ( d ) ,
Part I , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1940 , of
this Act .
Since the actual needs of each officer , department ,
board , commission , institution , or subdivision , of the
State Government can only be anticipated and not
finally determined by the Legislature , and since the
total amount of revenue accruing to the General Ex-
penditure Fund from which these appropriations are
hereby made can only be anticipated through exist-
ing law , and those that may hereafter be enacted , it
is the purpose and intention of the Legislature that
the State expenditures for each fiscal year covered
in this Act shall not exceed the total revenues accru-
ing to the General Expenditure Fund for the same
fiscal year . To carry out this provision , the inten-
tion and purpose of the Legislature , upon the de-
termination of the conditions set forth to wit : The
needs of each officer , department , board, commission ,
institution , or subdivision of the State Government ,
and the total revenue accruing to the General Ex-
penditure Fund , the condition can not be finally de-
termined until after adjournment of this session of
the Legislature , the Governor of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky is hereby authorized , empowered and
directed to ascertain the needs of each officer , depart-
ment , board, commission , institution , or subdivision
of the State Government , and to ascertain the total
revenues accruing to the General expenditure Fund
of the Commonwealth , and upon the ascertainment
of said facts , he , the Governor is hereby authorized ,
empowered , and directed by the Legislature to pre-
vent an over - draft or deficit in any fiscal year for
which appropriations are herein made , by equitably
reducing, without discrimination , the appropriations
herein made to any officer , department , board , com-
mission , institution , or subdivision of the State Gov-
ernment ; provided that the power hereby invested
and granted to the Governor shall not permit any re-
duction of the appropriation of any officer , depart-
ment , board, commission , institution or subdivision
of the State Government that will actually impair
the necessary governmental functions of any agency
whose operations and functions are determined to
be a necessary governmental function .
30.
To carry out the purpose of this Act for the bien-
nium beginning July 1 , 1938 , and ending June 30 ,
1940 , the State Budget Officer , with the approval of
the Commission of Finance , is hereby empowered
and granted the authority to make allotments and/or
reallotments from appropriations made to the vari-
ous officers , departments , boards , commissions , insti-
tutions , and subdivisions of the State Government ,
so as to prevent an over -draft , or a deficit in any
fiscal year for which appropriations are herein ,
made , and to prevent the maximum appropriation
made to any officer , department , board , commission ,
institution , or subdivision of the State Government
from being exceeded .
31 .
In enacting this Budget Appropriation Law , it is
the deliberate intention of the General Assembly to
enact each section , and each subsection thereof , as a
separate and/or specific appropriation and law , and
if any section or any subsection thereof shall be held
invalid , or unconstitutional , the decision of the
courts shall not effect or impair any of the remain-
ing sections , subsections , or provisions contained
herein .
32.
All continuing appropriations in existence at the
time of this Act are hereby discontinued and re-
pealed by this Act. All laws and parts of laws in
conflict with any of the provisions of the above enact-
ments , to the extent of such conflict , are hereby
repealed .
Approved by the Governor : January 18 , 1938 .

laws.summary: This statute establishes a County Board of Registration and Purgation in each county of the Commonwealth of Kentucky. The board is appointed by the State Board of Registration and Purgation and consists of three members. Two members are chosen from the two dominant political parties, and one is selected by the State Board. Members must be at least twenty-one years old, reside in the county, and possess the qualifications of a legal voter. The State Board can remove members at its discretion.

§ 11. Compensation of County Board . No mem-
ber of the County Board of Registration and Purga-
tion as provided for herein shall receive any com-
pensation for his service except in counties contain-
ing cities of the first class . In the counties which
do not have a city of the first class , the County
Board of Registration and Purgation shall meet not
exceeding fifteen days before any primary and not
exceeding fifteen days before any General Election .
In counties having a city of the first class the County
Board of Registration and Purgation may meet at
any time that may be necessary to perform the duties
herein imposed upon them but they shall remain in
session for the purpose of hearing challenges con-
tinuously from the date that the registration books
shall be closed before any Primary or General Elec-
tion and for their services they shall be paid the sum
of Twelve Hundred ( $ 1,200.00 ) Dollars each per an-
num to be paid by the Fiscal Court of the county of
their appointment in monthly installments .
The County Board of Registration and Purgation
as provided for under this Act may employ such
clerical , stenographic and other help as they may
deem necessary to carry out the provisions of this
Act and may purchase such supplies and equipment
as they may deem necessary and such clerical help
se employed and supplies and equipment so pur-
chased by the said County Board shall be paid for
by the Fiscal Court of the county when the costs of

may be presented , the purgation officers shall deter-
mine whether the voter is properly and legally reg-
istered ; such hearing shall be conducted in a sum-
mary manner and the officers , in their discretion ,
may reasonably limit the number of witnesses testi-

registered , his registration shall thereupon be can-
celled by them . The failure of any voter against
whom a notice of challenge has been served as pro-
vided herein to appear at such hearing shall be
prima facie evidence that he is not entitled to regis-

celled . Appeals from the action of the purgation of-

they or either of them shall reduce to writing the

or parts hereof which were not attacked or adjudged
unconstitutional , and all remaining sections shall be
enforced as if they had been enacted separately .
§ 18-A. Failure to perform duty ; penalty . Any
person who shall wilfully fail to perform any of his
duties set forth in this Act , shall be guilty of a mis-
demeanor , and , upon conviction thereof , be fined not
less than $ 10.00 dollars , nor more than $ 100.00 dol-
lars , for each offense .
§ 18 -B . Nothing contained in this Act shall in
any manner affect , change or alter the qualifications
of any voter in any election held in this state .
4
§ 19. All laws in conflict herewith are hereby
expressly repealed .
§ 20. Emergency Clause . Whereas , there are a
large number of persons registered throughout the
State under the present registration laws , and there
are a large number of voters whose names appear
in the registration lists who are not entitled to vote
in any primary , general or special election , and
whose names should be removed from the registra-
tion lists , and
WHEREAS , there is now fast approaching a pri-
mary election and in order to have an honest elec-
tion and to provide means whereby any such voters
as are entitled to vote will be permitted to vote , and
WHEREAS , it is necessary to create and provide an
effective purgation of the registration lists through-
out the entire State and in order to have said regis-
tration lists purged in time for the coming primary
election or any special election that may be held in
the State , an emergency is hereby declared to exist
and this act shall become effective immediately after
its passage and approval by the Governor .
Approved by the Governor : March 11 , 1938 .

CHAPTER 147.
AN ACT amending Chapter forty -two (42 ) of the Acts of the
General Assembly of nineteen thirty -six (1936 ) , being Section
four thousand three hundred ninety-nine -three ( 4399-3 ) , Car-
roll's Kentucky Statute , 1936 edition relating to independent
school districts .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
That Chapter forty -two ( 42 ) of the Acts of the
General Assembly of nineteen thirty six ( 1936 ) being
Section four thousand three hundred ninety -nine-
three ( 4399-3 ) , Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , 1936
Edition , be and the same hereby is amended by re-
pealing said Section in its entirety and re -enacting
same so that as amended and re - enacted said section
will read as follows , to wit :
Section 4399-3 . Independent school districts .
All school districts embracing cities of the first five
classes together with the territory within their limits ,
including any territory which has heretofore been
added for school purposes outside of the limits of
such cities or districts , and any territory which may
be included by any future change in the limits of such
cities , and all independent graded common school
districts having a school census enumeration of two
hundred ( 200 ) or more white children shall here-
after be known and designated as independent school
districts , provided that no such district other than
cities of the first , second , third , fourth , and fifth
classes , operating as independent districts at the
time this Act becomes effective , shall continue to
operate when its school census enumeration of white
children falls below two hundred ( 200 ) pupils unless
it appears to the State Board of Education that the
district can maintain a more efficient program of
school service by operating as an independent dis-
trict . The State Board of Education may permit
an independent graded common school district exist-
ing at the time of the passage of this Act with a
census enumeration of white children below two hun-
dred ( 200 ) to operate as a temporary independent
school district for one-year periods beginning with
July first ( 1 ) , nineteen thirty-eight ( 1938 ) , if it ap-
pears to the State Board of Education that such dis-
trict can maintain a more efficient program of school
service by operating as a temporary independent
district , and the decision of the State Board of Edu-
cation shall be final ; provided , at the end of each
one-year period the State Board of Education may
permit such independent district to operate for an
additional one-year period on the condition that
such inspection as the State Board of Education may
make shows that it is operating a school in accord-
ance with the school law and the standards , rules ,
and regulations set up by the State Board of Educa-
tion . The State Board of Education may by order
make any temporary independent school district a
part of the county district whenever the same is not
complying with the school law and the standards ,
rules , and regulations of the State Board of Educa-
tion , and after it has been given a reasonable time ,
to be fixed by the State Board of Education , within
which to so comply . The first application of such
district to operate as a temporary independent dis-
trict shall be filed with the State Board of Education
not later than July first ( 1 ) , nineteen thirty -eight
( 1938 ) . Each subsequent application of such inde-
pendent district to operate as a temporary inde-
pendent district for an additional one -year period
shall be filed with the State Board of Education not
later than May first ( 1 ) . Each independent school
district shall maintain at least an approved twelve-
grade school service for the white children residing
in its district . Provided , however , any independent
school district that maintains within the district at
least an approved ten -grade school service for the
white children residing in its district , may furnish
free transportation for white children residing
within the district to attend school in an adjoining
district for completing the eleventh and twelfth
grade school work and provide by contract with an
adjoining district , which maintains at least an ap-
proved twelve -grade program of school service , for
such children procuring eleventh and twelfth grade
service in such adjoining district . Provided further
that each independent school district shall provide
by establishment or by contract with another district
for at least an approved twelve -grade program of
school service for its colored children .
All laws in conflict herewith are hereby repealed .
Approved by the Governor : March 12, 1938 .

CHAPTER 275 ,
AN ACT repealing , amending and re -enacting Section 551, Ken-
tucky Statutes , relating to corporations , their management
and control , the election and qualifications of directors of
corporations.
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
That Section 551 Kentucky Statutes be repealed
and re-enacted so that when so amended and re-
enacted it will read as follows : The affairs of each
corporation shall be managed by a board of not less
than three directors , each of whom shall own in
his
right not less than three shares
ofcapital stock
;they
shall hold office until their successors are respectively
elected and qualified
, and

constitute
aquorum for the transaction
ofbusiness
.
All elections for directors shall
beby ballot
, and shall
beheld in this state
; and
,
inthe first instance
, the
directors shall
beelected
at
ameeting held before the
corporation
isauthorized
tocommence business

thereafter
atan annual meeting
ofthe stockholders
to be held on the day named in the by-laws , and which
shall not be changed within sixty days next before
the day on which the election is to be held , and notice
of any change shall be given to each stockholder
twenty days before the election is held ; and if , for
any cause , an election is not held on the day named in
the by -laws , a special meeting for that purpose shall
be called within thirty days thereafter , of which due
notice shall be given to each stockholder , in person or
by letter mailed to his last known address . A stock-
holder may vote at any meeting by proxy , in writing ,
signed by him, and attested in such manner as the
by-laws may prescribe ; and a vacancy in the board of
directors shall be filled by the board ; and the direc-
tors so appointed shall hold office until the next an-
nual election , provided that if the directors are
divided into classes in the manner set out herein , the
directors so appointed shall hold office for the re-
mainder of the term of the directors they are ap-
pointed to succeed . The directors of any corpora-
tion may, by a vote of the stockholders , be divided
into one , two or three classes , the term of office of
those of the first class to expire at the annual election
next ensuing, of the second class one year thereafter ,
of the third class two years thereafter ; and at each
annual election held after such classification , direc-
tors shall be chosen for two or three years , as the
case may be , to succeed those whose terms expire .
But each director of a banking , trust or insurance
company , or building and loan association , must own
in his own right five shares of capital stock , and a
majority of them must be residents of Kentucky
during their term of office : Provided , however , That
in the case of an insurance company , such a com-
pany may, by by-laws, require that each director own
a greater number of shares of stock than five and
may, by by-law , require that such qualifying shares
be deposited with the treasurer of the company :
Provided further , That the above -mentioned clause ,
declaring that all elections for directors shall be by
ballot , and shall be held in this state , shall not apply
to corporations created and organized for educa-
tional purposes only, and having no capital stock ,
and in which tuition to students is free .
Vetoed by the Governor : March 11, 1938.
(This bill was vetoed , but Circuit Court held veto void ; now
pending on appeal .)

PROCLAMATION
TO THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE
COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY :
WHEREAS, the disorderly condition of the finances of
certain counties of the Commonwealth of Kentucky has resulted
in impairing the credit of those counties and of other units of
the government in the Commonwealth ; and
WHEREAS, the problems raised by this chaotic condition
present issues which can be dealt with only by the General
Assembly of Kentucky ; and
WHEREAS , certain other emergencies have arisen , and
the Legislature did on March 1, 1938 , adjourn sine die without
considering them ;
NOW, THEREFORE , in order to insure proper protection
of the credit of the subdivisions of the Commonwealth , and to
provide for other aspects of orderly financing , and in order to
meet the several other emergencies , and in accordance with the
power vested in me by the Constitution of Kentucky to convene
the General Assembly into extraordinary session , as Governor of
Kentucky I do issue this my proclamation convening the Gen-
eral Assembly of Kentucky in extraordinary session at the seat
of government in Frankfort , Kentucky , at one o'clock , P. M. ,
March 2, 1938 , for the sole purpose of considering the following
subjects , to wit :
1. To pass legislation providing for the orderly financing
of county governments including (a ) rendering more effective
uniform county accounting and budgeting ; ( b ) improving local
tax adiministration ; ( c ) authorizing optional consolidation of
local government units ; ( d ) permitting the same public official
or employe to perform related functions for two or more local
government units ; ( e ) authorizing optional reorganization of
county financial administration ; and (f ) making provision for
adequate county debt administration and for state supervision
thereof , possibly providing a revolving fund of not more than
$500,000 ( no part of which shall be spent except for bonds under
a contract to resell without loss to the Commonwealth ) , pro-
vided that nothing herein shall be deemed to submit legislation
appropriating money from the state treasury, or imposing any
tax, for payment of any county debt or the interest thereon .
2. To pass an act re -creating the Kentucky Disabled Ex-
Service Men's Board .
3. To pass an act appropriating not in excess of thirty -five
thousand dollars ( $35,000.00 ) from the Road Fund for the pur-
pose of advertising the Commonwealth of Kentucky at the New
York City World's Fair.
4. To amend and reenact House Bill 526 passed by the
1936 regular session of the Kentucky Legislature known as the
Kentucky Unfair Practices Act and to provide for the creation
of a Trade Commission for the enforcement thereof.
5. To enact legislation amending and reenacting section
681c -6, Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's 1936 revision , rela
ting to fraternal benefit societies .
6. To pass an act providing for the merit system of civil
service for firemen in cities of the third , fourth and fifth classes .
7. To pass a resolution authorizing the personal repre-
sentative of Morgan Hacker to sue the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky or the State Highway Commission for a sum not to exceed
five thousand dollars ( $5,000.00 ) damages for personal injuries
resulting in the death of Morgan Hacker .
8. To pass an act making provision for teachers retire-
ment benefits effective not earlier than June 30 , 1940 .
9. To pass an act to amend and revise the Public Service
Commission Act , being Chapter 145 of the Acts of the General
Assembly of 1934 .
10. To amend and reenact section 98a -5, Carroll's Kentucky
Statutes , Baldwin's 1936 Edition .
11. To pass an act providing for redefinition of the func
tions of the Department of Revenue and for machinery for the
execution thereof-not including the organization of the Depart-
ment , the imposition of any new tax , or the repeal of any exist-
ing tax.
12. To pass an act making it illegal to sell any alcoholic
beverage on Sundays or election days .
13. To consider legislation to provide that trucks on which
a well drilling outfit is mounted shall be licensed for the same
fee as farmers ' trucks .
14. To pass an act permitting the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky to acquire the Louisville Municipal Bridge under the
Murphy Toll Bridge Act ( Section 4356s -1, Carroll's Kentucky
Statutes , Baldwin's 1936 Edition ) .
15. To pass an act amending and re-enacting section
4618-139 , Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's 1936 Edition .
You will , therefore , in accordance with this proclamation
assemble in said extraordinary session at the seat of govern .
ment at Frankfort , Kentucky , on the day and date above writ
ten to consider the subjects herein mentioned , and only such
subjects .
Given under my hand at nine o'clock , A. M. , this the sec-
ond day of March , 1938 .
By the Governor : '
A. B. CHANDLER ,

TO THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE

WHEREAS , subsequent to the issuance of the Governor's
proclamation dated March 2, 1938 , convening the General
Assembly in extraordinary session , it has become apparent
cities should be permitted to extend the merit system of civil

WHEREAS , an emergency exists in respect of the appro-
priation for the payment of county tax commissioners ; and
WHEREAS , à similar emergency exists in respect of the
appropriation for the operation of the charitable and penal insti-
tutions and for the administration of the Department of Wel-
fare ; and
WHEREAS , uncertainty respecting the legal effect of Sec-
tion 4020 , Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's 1936 Revision ,
has been brought to the attention of the Governor of the Com-
monwealth ; and
WHEREAS , inadequate provision is made for the vocational
education of white people in Eastern Kentucky ; and
WHEREAS , inadequate provision is made for the vocational
education of Negroes in Western Kentucky ; and
WHEREAS , it is necessary that some immediate action be
taken with reference to first -time offenders ; and
WHEREAS , practices constituting an emergency have arisen
injurious to both those who practice optometry and those who
are aided thereby ; and
WHEREAS , it has been called to the attention of the Gov-
ernor that the pension justly due the widows of many Con-
federate veterans is denied ; and

WHEREAS , the lack of stenographic and clerical assistance
available to county judges of this Commonwealth so retards the
execution of their functions as to cause distress ; and
WHEREAS , the assessment of taxes and the collection of
funds under the Workmen's Compensation Act is threatened ;
and
WHEREAS , this Commonwealth is being embarassed by
inability to wisely and discreetly use certain funds collected
from foreign insurance companies ; and
WHEREAS , legislation respecting building and loan asso-
ciations , rural highway funds , probation and parole officers and
water works and sewage disposal system is urgent ; and
WHEREAS , there is an opportunity to immediately reduce
the cost of maintaining the Kenova -Catlettsburg bridge ; and
WHEREAS , the authority to use tax paid crowns in lieu
of stamps in the administration of beer consumption tax is

WHEREAS , adequate high school facilities should immedi-
ately be provided for all pupils ; and
WHEREAS , the development of fruit growing should be
encouraged ; and

spirits to distillers ;
NOW , THEREFORE , in order that these emergencies may
be considered by the Extraordinary Session of the General
Assembly convened by the aforesaid proclamation , and in accord-
ance with the power vested in me by the Constitution of Ken-
tucky, I do issue this my proclamation amending the aforesaid
proclamation by revising item six thereof as detailed below and
by adding to the fifteen items therein submitted for considera-
tion the additional items which follow :
6. To pass an Act providing for the merit system of civil
service for firemen and policemen in cities of the third , fourth
and fifth class .
16. To pass an Act making an appropriation in an amount
not to exceed three hundred thousand dollars ( $300,000 ) for
the operation of the charitable and penal institutions and the
administration of the Department of Welfare including proba
tion and parole for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1938 , and
to make an appropriation not to exceed one hundred and forty-
two thousand dollars ( $142,000 ) to the Department of Revenue
for paying the various county tax commissioners of the state
as provided by law for the year ending June 30 , 1938 .
17. To pass an Act repealing , amending and re-enacting
Section 4020 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's 1936
Revision .
18. To pass an Act authorizing the purchase of properties
fo the Mayo School in Paintsville and to establish and provide
for the maintenance of a vocational school thereon , provided
the total appropriation for all such purposes shall not exceed
seventy-five thousand dollars ( $75,000 ) for the biennium begin-
ning July 1, 1938 .
19. To pass an Act repealing , amending and re -enacting
Sections 4257-59 through 4527-80 , Carroll's Kentucky Statutes ,
Baldwin's 1936 Revision , and making provision for the establish-
ment and maintenance of a Negro vocational school at Paducah ,

21. To pass an Act relating to the practice of optometry
and authorizing and vesting the regulation thereof in the Depart-
ment of Health , and expressly repealing , amending and reenact-
ing Section 2618a -6 of Carroll's Kentucky Stattues , Baldwin's

22. To pass an Act repealing , amending and re- enacting
Section 415b -6 ( 2 ) of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's
1936 Revision .
23. To pass an Act repealing , amending and re -enacting
Section 1061a -1 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's 1936
Revision , so that fiscal courts may provide judges of counties
containing cities of the first , second , third or fourth class with
a stenographer or clerk.
24. To pass an Act repealing , amending and re -enacting
Section 4968-9 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's 1936
Revision , and making other provisions for the care and man-
agement of funds of the Workmen's Compensation Board .
25. To pass an Act repealing , amending and re -enacting
Section 762b -5 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's 1936
Revision .
26. To pass an Act authorizing building and loan associa
tions to make direct reduction loans , and to regulate same , and
to define the duties of such lenders and borrowers .
27. To pass an Act repealing , amending and re-enacting
Section 331e -3 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's 1936
Revision , and to establish a merit board in counties having
cities of the first class and providing that it shall appoint pro-
bation officers , and that the court of counties having cities of
the second class may appoint probation officers ; providing for
the payment of such probation offcers from funds available to
the county , and providing that voluntary probation officers may
be appointed in other counties .
28. To consider legislation relating to the distribution of
rural highway funds , and providing that such funds may be
available for use in any county only upon condition that the
county comply with certain financial practices , and then possibly
only for the payment of county road and bridge bonds , provided
the use of said funds shall not be affected by such legislation
prior to April 1 , 1940 .
29. To pass an Act repealing , amending and re -enacting
Sections 2741 -L- 1, Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Baldwin's 1936
Revision.
30. To pass a resolution authorizing the Commissioner of
Highways to convey as an easement part of the right -of-way of
the Kenova -Catlettsburg Bridge to the City of Kenova , West
Virginia for the purpose of building flood walls thereon and
to convey all that portion of said bridge , appurtenances thereto
and right -of-way, including buildings located on such real estate ,
as are located in West Virginia to that Commonwealth .
31. To pass an Act authorizing the Commissioner of Reve
nue to collect the beer consumption tax through the medium
of tax paid crown seals rather than through the medium of
stamps now employed .

for all pupils.
33. To pass an Act to promote , develop and encourage
better methods of producing , packing and marketing fruit .

spirits in bottles to distillers and permitting distillers to pur
chase same .

TO THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE
COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY :
WHEREAS , subsequent to the issuance of the Governor's

WHEREAS , the legal status by which gifts are awarded by

and

wards of hospitals for the insane ; and

ending June 30 , 1938 , is inadequate to finance the work of that
Division , particularly the repairing of public buildings made
necessary for housing divisions of the State government under
the terms of the Governmental Reorganization Act of 1936 ; and
WHEREAS , the basis for allowing county court clerks rea-
sonable compensation for the work incident to their services
rendered in the various elections is uncertain ;
NOW , THEREFORE , in order that these emergencies may
be considered by the Extraordinary Session of the General
Assembly convened and acting pursuant to the aforesaid procla-
mations , and in accordance with the power vested in me by the
Constitution of Kentucky , I do isssue this my proclamation
amending the aforesaid proclamations by adding to the thirty-
eight items therein submitted for consideration the following
items , towit :
39. To pass an act repealing , amending and re -enacting
Section 4281b -28 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , 1936 Edition .
so as to permit the payment of income tax in three installments
without interest .
40. To pass an act relating to the awarding of gifts by
lot and repealing, amending and re -enacting Section 2573 of
Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , 1936 Edition .
41. To pass an act to enable the Department of Welfare
to receive and expend money from the United States of America
and/or any of its agencies .
42. To pass an act appropriating $38,500.00 from the Gen-
eral Expenditure Fund to the Finance Department , Division of
Purchases and Public Property for the fiscal year ending June
30, 1938 .
43. To pass an act relating to the compensation of county
court clerks for services rendered in various primary , special
and general elections .
Given under my hand at 2 o'clock P. M. this the fourth day
of April , 1938 .
By the Governor :
CHARLES D. ARNETT ,
Secretary of State .
A. B. CHANDLER ,
Governor .
PROCLAMATION
TO THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE
COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY :
WHEREAS , subsequent to the issuance of the Governor's
proclamations dated March 17 , 1938 , March 31 , 1938 , and April
4, 1938, amending the Governor's proclamation dated March 2 ,
1938, it has become apparent that the provisions of the statutes
relating to tax sales are unsatisfactory and jeopardize the
financial stability of municipalities ; and
WHEREAS , Herman Southall remains unpaid for services
rendered while representing T. Fowler Combs before the Gen-
eral Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky ;
NOW , THEREFORE , in order that these emergencies may
be considered by the Extraordinary Session of the General
Assembly convened and acting pursuant to the aforesaid procla-
mations , and in accordance with the power vested in me by
the Constitution of Kentucky , I do issue this my proclamation
amending the aforesaid proclamations by additing to the forty-
three items , to wit :
44. To pass an act repealing, amending and re -enacting
Sections 3002 and 3004 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , 1936
Edition .
45. To pass a resolution authorizing the payment to Herman
Southall of a sum of one hundred fifty dollars ($ 150.00 ) for
services in representing T. Fowler Combs before the General
Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky .
Given under my hand at 7 o'clock P. M. this the fourth day
of April , 1938 .

laws.summary: This act defines terms related to the Teachers' Retirement System, including 'Present Teacher' and 'New Teacher'. It specifically mentions the 'West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons at Frankfort, Kentucky' as an institution whose teachers engaged in classroom instruction are eligible for the state retirement system. This explicit mention of a college for 'Colored Persons' within the context of a state-wide retirement system suggests a segregated educational system, a hallmark of Jim Crow era legislation.

CHAPTER 1 .
AN ACT providing a Teachers Retirement System for the State
of Kentucky ; providing for retirement allowances for teachers
of State supported Colleges , Public Schools , (including all
elementary and secondary schools of the state ) ; providing
for disability benefits for disabled teachers of such schools ;
providing that the funds for the payment of retirement annul-
ties to teachers and for disability benefits shall be raised by
contributions from the teachers and by contributions from
the State of Kentucky from its general funds ; providing for
the repeal of Section 4506a -1 through and including Section
4506a -15 ; and providing for the administration and manage-
ment of the retirement system and all funds created for its
maintenance and support , by a Board of Trustees to be selected
under the supervision of the Superintendent of Public Instruc-
tion, by a vote of the members of the system . This Act shall
be known as the Porter -Rayburn Act .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. A state teachers ' retirement system is here-
by established for the teachers of the public schools
of the state of Kentucky for the purpose of provid-
ing retirement allowances and other benefits under
the provisions of this act . The retirement system
herein created shall be established as of July 1 , 1940 .
It shall have the powers and the privileges of a cor-
poration and shall be known as the " Teachers ' Re-
tirement System of the State of Kentucky , " and by
such name all of its business shall be transacted ,
all

and West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored
Persons at Frankfort , Kentucky , who are engaged
in actual classroom instruction , any member of a
local retirement system who becomes a member of
the state retirement system according to the pro-
visions of Section 49 of this act , and who is employed
in actual classroom instruction .
5. " Present Teacher ' shall mean any teacher as
defined in this act , ( a ) who was a teacher on or be-
fore the first day of July , 1940 , and who became a
member of the retirement system created by this
act on the date of the inauguration of the system or
within one year after said date , ( b ) any teacher who
was a member of a local teacher retirement system
in the public elementary or secondary schools of
the state on or before July 1 , 1940 , and who con-
tinued to be a member of such system until he , with
the membership of the local retirement system , be-
came a member of the state retirement system .
6. " New Teacher ' shall include any teacher not
a present teacher .
7. "Prior Service " shall mean the number of
years during which the mmeber was a teacher in the
public schools of Kentucky prior to his membership
in the state retirement system , as allowed in his
" prior service certificate ."
8. " Subsequent Service " shall mean the number
of years during which the teacher is a member of
the state retirement system .
9. "Prior Service Certificate " shall mean the
certificate issued by the board of trustees of the
state teachers ' retirement system designating the
amount of accredited service of a member prior to
his membership in the state retirement system .
10. " Annual Salary " shall mean the average an-

his services as a teacher in the public schools of
Kentucky during the five years immediately pre-
ceding retirement by reason of superannuation or
disability , except that any salary which exceeds
$2,000 in any year shall be considered as $2,000
only.

18. " Local Retirement System " shall mean any
