Frankfort Cemetery, Jefferson and Kenton County fees, and for
defraying the expenses of all other State obligations for (a)
the fiscal years ending June 30, 1941, and June 30, 1942, (b)
the fiscal years of the Department of Highways ending March
31, 1941, and March 31, 1942, and (c) certain appropriations
for the current fiscal year ending June 30, 1940; designating
the sources and funds from which said appropriations are
made, describing the manner in which they are to be paid,
providing for the payment into the State Treasury of all fees
and other miscellaneous receipts collected by all the different
officers, departments, boards, commissions, institutions and
sub-divisions of the State Government; providing for the
establishment of certain revolving funds specifically men
tioned; providing for money refunds; authorizing and empower
ing the Governor of the Commonwealth of Kentucky to limit
and restrict expenditures of money appropriated, and to reduce
or adjust each of the appropriations herein made; authorizing
the State Budget Officer, with the approval of the Commis
sioner of Finance, to make allotments and reallotments from
the appropriations made to the various officers, departments,
boards, commissions, institutions, agencies and sub-divisions
of the State Government; authorizing transfers of appropria
tions and allotments from one budget class to another budget
class within the same budget unit, and to provide for certain
appropriations to be limited to specific purposes, and barring
the use of appropriations for certain purposes; and repealing
all blanket and continuing appropriations not provided for in
this Act and appropriations made by any previous Act or Acts
of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky,
and repealing all laws or parts of laws in conflict with any
of the provisions of this Act; enacting each section and each
sub section as a separate or specific appropriation.

whether heretofore specified in this Act, of every
department, board, commission, institution, agency,
division, or subdivision of the State Government
shall be covered into the State Treasury immediately
after the close of each month through the Depart
ment of Finance and placed to the credit of the
General Expenditure Fund, excepting those
revenues which are specifically allocated to the State
Road Fund or the Revolving Fund which shall be
credited to their respective funds as provided for
in this Act. The fees, receipts, and/or revenue of
every officer, department, division, subdivision,
commission, board, institution, or agency of the
State Government shall be covered into the State
Treasury immediately after the close of each month,
and placed to the credit of the General Expenditure
Fund and shall be used to defray the expenses of
the State Government, and the appropriations
made from the General Expenditure Fund in this
Act, unless otherwise specifically appropriated to

stitutions, agencies, or subdivisions of the State
Government for Revolving Fund purposes ; such
agencies shall be only those that are listed in this
Act as having been approved for Revolving Fund
Accounts.

recurring expenses and extraordinary expense and
capital outlay for any officer, department, board,
commission, institution, and subdivision of the State
Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky
shall not be available for expenditure until allotted
as now provided by law, and such appropriations
as are specifically made in this Act are hereby de
clared to be maximum and conditional appropria
tions except when the Governor determines an
emergency exists in any department, board, com
mission, institution, or subdivision of the State
Government requiring an additional allotment of
funds to be made from the General Emergency
Fund hereby placed at his disposal and made a
specific appropriation to be used toy him to meet
existing emergencies so determined by him. This
appropriation is designated under Section 4
"EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT" Item (d) Part
One for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1941, and
Section 4, "EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT" Item
(d) Part One-A for the fiscal year ending June 30,
1942, of this Act.
Since the actual needs of each officer, department,
board, commission, institution, or subdivision of
the State Government can only be anticipated and
not finally determined by the Legislature, and since
the total amount of revenue accruing to the General
Expenditure Fund from which these appropriations
are hereby made can only be anticipated through
existing laws and those that may hereafter be
enacted, it is the purpose and intention of the
Legislature that the State expenditures for each
fiscal year covered in this Act shall not exceed the
total revenues accruing to the General Expenditure
Fund for the same fiscal year. As the conditions
cannot be finally determined until after the ad
journment of this session of the Legislature, and
as the needs of each officer, department, board,
commission, institution or subdivision of the State
Government and the total revenues accruing to the
General Fund cannot be fully determined at this
time, it is the intention and the purpose of this
Legislature that the Governor of the Common
wealth is, therefore, hereby authorized, empowered
and directed to ascertain the needs of each officer,
department, board, commission, institution, or sub
division of the State Government, and to ascertain
the total revenues accruing to the General Ex
penditure Fund of the Commonwealth, and upon
the ascertainment of said facts, he, the Governor
is hereby authorized, empowered, and directed by
the Legislature to prevent an over-draft or deficit
in any fiscal year for which appropriations are
herein made, by equitably reducing, without dis
crimination, the appropriations herein made to any
officer, department, board, commission, institution,
or subdivision of the State Government; provided
that the power hereby invested and granted to the
Governor shall not permit any reduction of the
appropriation of any officer, department, board,
commission, institution or subdivision of the State
Government that will actually impair the necessary
governmental functions of any agency whose opera
tions and functions are determined to be a neces
sary governmental function.
32.
To carry out the purpose of this Act for the
biennium beginning July 1, 1940, and ending June 30,
1942, the State Budget Officer, with the approval
of the Commissioner of Finance, is hereby em
powered and granted the authority to make allot
ments and/or reallotments from appropriations
made to the various officers, departments, boards,
commissions, institutions, and subdivisions of the
State Government, so as to prevent an over-draft,
or a deficit in any fiscal year for which appropria
tions are herein made, and to prevent the maximum
appropriation made to any officer, department,
board, commission, institution, or subdivision of the
State Government from being exceeded.
33.
Nothing in this Act shall be construed to repeal
any appropriation for the fiscal year ending June 30,
1940, which was made under the provisions of
Chapter 1, Acts of the 1938 Regular Session and of
Chapter 15, Chapter 30, and Chapter 31, Acts of
the General ASsembly, First Special Session, 1938,
and Chapter 1, Acts of the Second Special Session,
1938.
34.
In enacting this Budget Appropriation Law, it
is the deliberate intention of the General ASsembly
to enact each section, and each sub-section thereof,
as a separate and/or specific appropriation and
law; and if any section or any subsection thereof
shall be held invalid, or unconstitutional the decision
of the courts shall not affect or impair any of the
remaining sections, subsections, or provisions con
tained herein.
35.
All continuing appropriations in existence at the
time of this Act are hereby discontinued and re
pealed by this Act. All laws and parts of laws in
conflict with any of the provisions of the above
enactments, to the extent of such conflict, are
hereby repealed.
36.
Whereas, the Commonwealth has been called
upon to provide funds necessary to supplement
Federal funds for the purpose of carrying on the
receiving and distribution of Federal surplus com
modities to be distributed to the needy; and
Whereas, the appropriation made by the Gen
eral Assembly at its 1938 Regular Session for
relief of the indigent persons and other emergencies
deemed by the Governor are exhausted; and
Whereas, it is imperative that funds be made
available for the period from December 15, 1939,
to June 30, 1940, for relief and other emergencies
deemed as such by the Governor; and
Whereas, there is a need for the provisions
of other sections of this budget to become operative
at once, an emergency is hereby declared to exist,
and this Act shall become effective immediately
upon its passage and approval by the Governor.

laws.summary: This statute outlines the administration of federal grants for library service in Kentucky. It mandates that appointments to the Library Extension Division and participating libraries be based on merit and efficiency, without political consideration. Crucially, it requires the Library Extension Division to make plans to lessen inequalities of opportunity for library service and to make equitable apportionment of funds so as to provide library facilities to both the white and colored races. It also details the process of notifying the U.S. Commissioner of Education and entering into contracts for local public library service.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 106
(H. B. 386)
AN ACT relating to libraries and library service, and to the
powers, duties and functions of the Library Extension Division
of the Department of Library and Archives.
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky:
§ 1. The Library Extension Division, in addition
to the powers now vested in it by law, is hereby
authorized and empowered to receive, accept and
administer any money or moneys appropriated or
granted to
it,separate and apart from the general
fund, for providing and equalizing public library
service in Kentucky, by the federal government or
by the Commonwealth of Kentucky and any other
agencies, private and otherwise.
§ 2. The State Treasurer shall serve as trustee
of funds apportioned to the Commonwealth of Ken
tucky from any appropriations made by the federal
government, the commonwealth or any other agency
for providing and equalizing public library service
in Kentucky.
The Department of Finance shall, on the requi
sition of the Library Extension Division, authorize
the State Treasurer to make disbursement from
such funds to such libraries, cities, towns and
counties for library service as have been approved
and authorized to participate in the benefit of these
funds under the terms of the Federal Acts, and for
the payment of salaries and other expense as are
authorized herein out of the fund provided by the
federal government.
§ 3. The Library Extension Division is hereby
designated, authorized and required to cooperate,
as provided in and required by the Acts of Congress
providing federal grants to states for library
service, with the United States Commissioner of
Education in the administration of the provisions
of said Acts, employ personnel and do all things
necessary to entitle the Commonwealth of Kentucky
to receive the benefits thereof.
§ 4. All libraries, cities, towns, counties and
school districts participating in or benefiting by the
provisions of the federal grant for library service
or receiving any service from the Library Extension
Division, are hereby required to make such reports
and audits as are required to the State Treasurer,
the Library Extension Division, and fhe United
States Commissioner of Education. The State
Treasurer and Library Extension Division are
authorized and required to make such reports and
audits as may be required by the federal govern
ment and the United States Commissioner of
Education in respect to the expenditure of federal
grants and progress of library service.
§ 5. All appointments of personnel and the
tenure thereof to the Library Extension Division
and to such libraries, cities, towns, counties and
school districts participating in or benefiting by
the provisions of the federal grants for library
service shall be based on merit and efficiency
without regard to political consideration.
§ 6. The Library Extension Division shall, as
soon as possible after the passage of this Act, make
and administer plans to lessen inequalities of
opportunity for library service, for the maintenance
of a cooperative and integrated system of library
service throughout the Commonwealth, for suitable
cooperative arrangements with school systems, co
operative agricultural extension service and other
appropriate agencies, and to make equitable ap
portionment of any funds so received so as to pro
vide library facilities to both the white and colored
races.
§ 7. The Library Extension Division shall, as
soon as possible after the passage of this Act, trans
mit to the United States Commissioner of Education
official notice of acceptance of the provisions of the
aforesaid Acts of Congress and legislative enact
ment pertaining to the matters specified herein.
§ 8. The Library Extension Division may enter
into contracts with any local, state or federal
governmental agency or- authority for the purpose
of enabling the establishment and maintenance of
a local public library service upon such terms as may
be agreed upon by the several contracting parties,
subject to the statutes relating to the establishment
438 ACTS or THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY
and maintenance of libraries by the governmental
agencies or authorities with whom the contracts are
made.
The contracting parties may establish such
districts or units of library service as they may
mutually agree upon. The library service within
such districts shall be carried on according to plans
approved by the Director of Library Extension.
All libraries established under this Act shall
send such statistics and furnish such information
regarding their activities as the Director of the
Division of Library Extension may require from
time to time. Approved by the Governor March 26, 1940.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 125
(H. B. 337)
AN ACT to amend Sections 3235b-l to 3236b-18, inclusive, of Car
roll's Kentucky Statutes, 1936 Edition.
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky:
Sections 3235b-l to 3235b-18, inclusive, of Carroll's
Kentucky Statutes, 1936 edition, are hereby amended
to read as follows :
3235b-l Boards of Commissioner es for. —All public
parks which have been or may hereafter be estab
lished and maintained for the recreation, pleasure
and welfare of the white population in cities of the
second class shall be held, managed and controlled
by a board under the name and style of the "Board
of Park Commissioners ( White)
' ' of the city wherein
such parks may be located, and all public parks which
have been or may hereafter be established and
maintained for the recreation, pleasure and welfare
of the colored population in cities of the second class
shall be held, managed and controlled by a board
under the name and style of "Board of Park Com
missioners (Colored)", of the city wherein such
parks may be located. Each board of park commis
sioners shall continue and is hereby declared a body
politic and corporate under the name as herein pro
vided, with perpetual succession; and each by its
name may contract and be contracted with, sue and
be sued, have and use a corporate seal, and alter or
renew the same at pleasure.
3235b-2 Appointment and term of boards. —Each
board of park commissioners shall consist of five
members who shall be appointed by the mayor of the
city in which it is established and the term of office
shall be for five years or until their successors are
appointed and qualified, and when a vacancy occurs,
the person appointed to fill such vacancy shall hold
office until the expiration of the term of the person
whose vacancy he filled or until his successor is ap
pointed and qualified.
3235b-3 Oath of office.—The persons so appointed
as members of said boards of park commissioners
shall each, within ten days after appointment, appear
before the city clerk of his city and make and sub
scribe to an oath that he will faithfully, diligently
and to the best of his ability perform all the duties
of such park commissioner without favor or
prejudice ; that he is not subject to any of the pro
hibitions or disqualifications set out in this act; that
he will not in any manner, directly or indirectly, be
concerned in any contract, purchase, sale, salary, or
emolument of any kind connected with or growing
out of any business of said boards of park commis
sioners, or the providing, purchasing, condemning,
managing or improving of any park property; or in
supplying any labor or material, save as by the terms
of this act. Said oath shall be filed in the office of
the city clerk and shall be a public record.
3235b-4 Bond of members of board. —Each person
appointed as park commissioner as aforesaid shall
likewise, within ten days after such appointment,
execute bond in the sum of five thousand dollars
($5,000) payable to the city which he serves as park
commissioner, with good security, to be approved by
the mayor, conditioned that he will faithfully per
form all of the duties of a park commissioner of said
city as prescribed by law which said bond shall, when
approved by the mayor, be filed in the office of the
city clerk and be of public record. The expenses of
executing such bond when made by a guarantee com
pany shall be paid out of the funds available for park
purposes as are the other expenses of the board.
For any violation by the principal in such bond of
any duty as park commissioner, or any participation
by him, directly or indirectly, in any contract or sub
contract in respect to park property or the improve
ment thereof, or the furnishing of supplies of any
kind therefor, suit may be maintained upon such
boricT against the principal and sureties; such suit to
be in the name of the city and brought by the city
solicitor or attorney, or by any citizen, and any re
covery shall inure to the benefit of the fund for park
purposes.
3235b-5 Officers of boards; reports to mayor. —
The commissioners who shall be appointed and who
shall qualify as aforesaid shall, as soon as convenient
thereafter, meet and choose one of their number to
be president of their board, to serve for the term of
one year, and annually thereafter a president shall
in like manner be chosen. The duties of the president
shall be the usual duties incumbent upon such an
office and such as the board may prescribe. Each of
said boards of park commissioners shall also elect
a secretary, who may or may not be of their own
number, whose duties shall be, in addition to keeping
accurate and exact minutes of all meetings of the
board, to keep a set of books showing with accuracy
the receipts and expenditures of the board and shall
preserve on file duplicate vouchers for all expendi
tures, which books and vouchers shall at all times be
subject to the examination of the mayor, or any com
mittee of the general council authorized to make such
examination either by themselves or through expert
accountant duly chosen; and shall annually, in the
month of January, transmit to the mayor and
general council a full and detailed report and state
ment of all the acts and doings of the board for the
preceding year, together with a complete and
itemized account of all receipts and disbursements
of money, with an itemized estimate of the money
needed for park purposes. Said report and state
ment shall be published in the official newspaper of
the city in which said board is established.
3235b-6 Secretary of boards; salary.—Each board
of park commissioners may allow out of the funds
appropriated for park purposes such salary to the
secretary of the board as may be commensurate with
the work done by him not to exceed five hundred
dollars ($500.00) per annum. The members of the
boards of park commissioners shall receive no com
pensation for their services; nor shall any member
of either board hold any other office or appointment
or employment under the city, or any department of
the city, or any institution thereof. Provided, That
either of said boards may elect one of its own num
ber secretary, as provided in this act, and he may
receive the compensation provided herein for his
services as such secretary.
3235b-7 Duties and powers of boards; police power
over parks.— Each board, as constituted aforesaid,
shall have the care, management and custody of the
parks and grounds used for park purposes, the
boulevards and parkways now belonging to the city,
or to any existing board of park commissioners, or
in the control of the city, or the existing board, and
all such property as may be required for park
purposes or public squares by the city or board, the
white park board as herein constituted to have the
care, management and custody of all such public
parks which are established and maintained for the
recreation, pleasure and welfare of the white popula
tion, and the colored board as herein constituted to
have the care, management and custody of all such
public parks which are established and maintained
for the recreation, pleasure and welfare of the
colored population. Each board shall have power to
acquire and hold property for public parks and
public squares by condemnation or by contract for
the same; to accept conveyances thereof; to accept
gifts, donations or devises of land or other property
for park purposes; to lay out and improve with
walks, drives, roads, tree planting and other proper
improvements the park or parks, square or squares,
and other property held by it or acquired and
managed, and to enter into contract for same ; to pro
tect all property and improvements to
it,belonging
to or under its management or control, from injury
or decay; to adopt rules and regulations for the
reasonable and proper use for preventing injuries
to or misuse of all parks, public squares, boulevards,
driveways, walks and park property generally, and
to prevent disorder and improper conduct within the
precincts of any park or enclosure, or upon any drive,
walk or avenue under the control of said board of
park commissioners. The police power of the city
shall extend over the said park property of every
kind, as the same is or shall be acquired; and all
violations of such park rules and regulations, and
all other misdemeanors or offenses committed within
any park property or precinct, shall be punished by
the police court of the city on complaint and proceed
ing had, as provided by law, in cases of mis
demeanors and violations of city ordinances. The
said commissioners and their agents and employees
shall have power to make arrests for felonies or mis
demeanors committed within any park precinct, or
for violation of any park rules or regulations.
3235b-8 Land may be acquired. —In locating parks
and such other property as may be acquired under
this act, the boards shall have regard to the needs
of the different portions of the city and population
thereof, and the suitability of grounds for park
purposes, as well as the cost thereof. In and of all
such matters said board shall have discretion, as
also in the system of improvements of the same.
The said boards may acquire by purchase, gift or
condemnation land for parkways connecting the
parks and may improve and regulate the use of the
same.
3235b-9 Title of land acquired. —The boards shall
not be compelled to accept any gift or offer of land
which in its judgment, is unsuited for park purposes,
or the improvement of which would entail an in
judicious outlay. The title to all property acquired
under the provisions of this act or that may now be
owned and used for park purposes by any city of the
second class, shall, from and after the passage of
this act, vest in the boards of park commissioners,
and the same with all the improvements and equip
ment shall be held in strict and inviolable trust for
public park use, free from all taxation, impost or
assessment, state, county district, municipal or
otherwise.
3235b-10 Care of trees. — Said boards of park com
missioners shall have the control and management of
the planting and care of all shade trees along the
sidewalks and thoroughfares of such city, and are
hereby given the power to adopt such rules and regu
lations as may be necessary for the protection and
care of same and for the enforcement of said rules
and regulations.
3235b-1l Condemnation of land. — Whenever in the
opinion of either board, property shall be needed for
any of the purposes herein contemplated, either
within or beyond the boundaries of the city and
within the county in which such city is situated, such
board may, by resolution reciting such need, order
the condemnation of such property, and proceedings
for such condemnation shall be had in the name of
said board of park commissioners in accordance
with the provisions of section 3095, of the act for the
government of cities of the second class. If any
member of the board be the owner or interested in
any property necessary, in the opinion of the ma
jority of the other members of the board, to be taken
for park purposes, then proceeding to acquire such
property shall be by condemnation, and such facts of
ownership or interest of such member, and the
opinion of the majority of his colleagues and the
necessity for condemnation shall be fully set forth
in the petition.
3235b-12 Tax to support. —For the purpose of
providing necessary funds for the purchase, care and
improvement of all park property, and to meet the
expenses of the boards, the general council of the city
in which such boards of park commissioners has
been established in accordance with the provisions
of this act shall, in each year, levy and cause to be
collected, a tax of not exceeding five cents (5c) upon
each one hundred dollars ($100.00) of value of all
the property within the city taxable for municipal
purposes.
3235b-13 Funds; how paid out.—Two funds of
equal amount shall be set aside from the aforesaid
levy, and each shall be held by the treasurer of the
city in separate and distinct accounts, each to be
designated as a park fund, one for use by the white
park board and the other for use by the colored park
board, and said funds shall be paid out by the treas
urer only upon an order issued by said boards of
park commissioners, signed by the secretary and
countersigned by the president of the respective
board, by which such withdrawal of funds is made,
and after a bill for same has been approved by such
board at session assembled ; but in no case shall the
treasurer honor in any one year orders for a greater
sum than the amount appropriated and levied for
that year for park purposes.
3235b-14 Election to decide if bonds shall be is
sued.— For the purpose of raising money for the pur
chase or improvement of lands for park property, the
general council of the city, upon the request of either
board of park commissioners shall, by ordinance, sub
mit to the qualified voters of the city the question as
to whether the city shall issue bonds with interest
coupons attached to the amount and of the character
set forth in said ordinance ; and when such ordinance
is passed it shall, at the next November election, be
submitted to the qualified voters of the city; and, if it
receives the assent of two-thirds of those voting, the
bonds so issued shall be issued by the city and sold by
the mayor, the proceeds of said sale to be placed in
the hands of the treasurer of the city to be held by
Acts— 17
him to the credit of the park fund and paid out upon
the order of the board of park commissioners which
requested the passage of the aforesaid ordinance.
Said bonds shall not bear interest at a rate exceeding
six per cent (6%) per annum, payable semi-annually,
and shall not be sold for less than par and accrued
interest.
3235b-15 Board may borrow money. —Either board
of park commissioners shall have the power to bor
row money on the credit of the board, in anticipation
of its part of the revenue from the city for the year in
which the same is borrowed, and to pledge said
revenue for the payment of the principal and interest
of said loan : Provided, that the interest paid shall
in no case exceed six per cent \$%) for annum, and
the principal shall in no case exceed fifty per cent
(50%) of the anticipated revenue. Neither board
shall not to any extent or under any device, in one
year, anticipate or create a charge upon the income
of the future years; and no work done or improve
ments made in any one year shall be made a charge
upon the income of any future year.
3235b-16 Park policemen. — The general council of
the city may from time to time, upon application
therefor made by either board, provide by ordinance
for a special park police, the same to be under the
control of the board of park commissioners by whom
such application is made and to be paid by it.
3235b-17 "Park"; what included in.—The term
"park property" used in this act includes all parks,
squares and areas of land within the management of
the board; and all buildings, structures, improve
ments, seats, benches, fountains, walks, drives,
roads, trees, plants, herbage, flowers and other
things thereon and enclosures of the same; and all
shade trees on streets or thoroughfares, resting
places, watering stations, playgrounds necessary
and incidental to such public parks and property,
parade grounds, or the like ; and all connecting park
ways and roads or drives between parks; and all
avenues, roads, ways, drives, walks, with all trees,
shrubbery, vines, flowers and ornaments of any de
scription; and all birds, animals or curiosities or
objects of interest or instruction placed in or on any
such enclosures, ways, parkways, roads or places,
and said terms shall be liberally construed.
3235b-18 Officers of city to assist; labor and
material obtained. —In carrying out the provisions
of this act either board of park commissioners may
command the services of the city engineer and the
superintendent of public works and may employ
such labor and purchase such material as may be
necessary. All legal services or advice required by
said boards shall be rendered by the city solicitor
and city attorney and their assistants without ad
ditional Compensation. Neither approved nor vetoed.

laws.summary: This statute re-enacts and defines vagrancy for able-bodied males and females. It outlines conditions such as habitual loitering without means of support, refusal to engage in honest labor, desertion of family without support, and habitual refusal to work while loitering in public places. Penalties include fines and imprisonment, with increased penalties for subsequent offenses.

laws.full_text:
§ 2. Section 4758-1 of Carroll's Kentucky
Statutes, 1936 edition, is re-enacted to read as
follows :
4758-1. The following persons shall be deemed
to be vagrants, to-wit:
(1) Any able-bodied male person who habitually
loiters or rambles about without means to support
himself, and who has no trade, calling or profession
to make an honest livelihood;
(2) Any able-bodied male person who is without
visible means of support, and who habitually fails
or refuses to engage in honest labor for his own
support, or for the support of his family, if he has
one;
(3) Any able-bodied male person who purposely
deserts his wife or children, leaving them, or any of
them, without suitable subsistence or suitable means
of subsistence, and himself being idle and dissolute ;
(4) Any able-bodied person, male or female,
who has no visible means of support and who habit
ually refuses to work, and who habitually loiters on
the streets or public places of any village, town or
city.

ment may be both such fine or imprisonment. For
the second offense and all subsequent offenses, sixty
days' imprisonment in the workhouse, if there be

who is fined under this act shall be required to work

It grants circuit, police, quarterly, and justice courts jurisdiction over vagrancy offenses, with police, quarterly, and justice courts deemed always open for such trials. It also mandates sheriffs, constables, marshals, and policemen to watch for vagrants, warn them to leave and find work, and disperse groups of vagrants if necessary, using reasonable force.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 196
(S. B. 88)
AN ACT to repeal section 4 of 1924 House Bill No. 44, which
amended section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, 1922
edition, relating to pensions for Confederate veterans, by
amending section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, 1936
edition, to read like section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky Stat
utes, 1922 edition.
WHEREAS, House Bill No. 44 of 1924 was vetoed by the Gover
nor without stating his reasons therefor, as required by section
88 of the Constitution, and said House Bill therefore became a
law ten days after the adjournment of the 1918 Central As
sembly; and
WHEREAS, the General Assembly desires to clarify the status
of the law on the subject matter now compiled as section 415b-9
of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, 1936 edition, and the repeal of
1924 House Bill No. 44 would repeal all law compiled under
section 415b-9;
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky:
§ 1. Section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky
Statutes, 1936 edition, is amended to read as
follows :
That no person shall be entitled to the benefits
of this Act who is able to earn a support by manual
labor; or
Who is able to earn a support by reason of his or
her knowledge, art, or skill, in any profession, trade
or craft ; or
Who receives a pension from the United States
or any state or foreign government, or any other
source ; or
Who removes from this state or is absent there
from for a period of three months ; or
Who possesses property of the value of two thou
sand five hundred dollars ; or
Who possesses an income to the amount of three
hundred dollars a year; or an income equivalent to

laws.summary: This statute details appropriations for various aspects of public education in Kentucky for the year 1942. It includes funding for general school expenses, textbooks, scholarships, vocational education, and specifically allocates funds for the 'Kentucky State College for Negroes' and the 'West Kentucky Vocational Training School' for Negroes, as well as 'College Tuition for Negroes' to attend institutions outside the state. It also lists appropriations for the 'Kentucky School for the Blind - White' and 'Kentucky School for the Blind - Colored'.

CHAPTER 1
(H. B. 1 )
AN ACT appropriating money for the operation , maintenance ,
support and functioning of the State Government of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , including each of the various
officers , departments, boards, commissions , institutions , and
sub -divisions of the State Government , and the purchase of
record books as provided by Section 388 , Kentucky Statutes ,
1936 Edition , judiciary and court costs , Confederate pensions ,
the Frankfort Cemetery , Jefferson and Kenton County fees ,
and for defraying the expenses of all other State obligations
for ( a ) the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1943 , and June 30 ,
1944 , ( b ) the fiscal years of the Department of Highways
ending March 31 , 1943 , and March 31 , 1944 ; designating the
sources and funds from which said appropriations are made ,
and providing for the establishment of certain revolving
funds specifically mentioned ; providing for money refunds ;
authorizing and empowering the Commissioner of Finance
with the approval of the Governor to limit , restrict , and
supervise expenditures of all money appropriated herein and
hereafter by the General Assembly in the Regular Session
of 1942 , and to reduce or adjust each of the appropriations
in the manner herein provided ; providing for certain ap-
propriations to be limited to specific purposes , and barring
the use of appropriations for certain purposes ; repealing all
blanket and continuing appropriations not provided for in
this Act and appropriations made by any previous Act or
7
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky , and repealing all laws or parts of laws in conflict with
any of the provisions of this Act ; enacting each section and
each sub - section as a separate or specific appropriation .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
There is hereby appropriated out of the General
Expenditure Fund for the fiscal year beginning
July 1 , 1942 , and ending June 30 , 1943 , the following
sums for the following officers , departments , boards ,
commissions , institutions , and subdivisions of the
State Government , printing of County Record
Books, Judiciary and Court Costs , Confederate
Pensions , Frankfort Cemetery , Jefferson and
Kenton County Fees and any and all other agencies
of the State Government of the Commonwealth of
Kentucky subject to the provisions of the Re-
organization Act of the 1936 General Assembly , and
the Budget and Financial Administration Act of
1934 General Assembly, for which the specific ap-
propriation is herein listed , excepting those listed in
Parts Two and Three of this Budget Act, for the
following purposes :

PART TWO
REVOLVING TRUST AND AGENCY FUNDS
There is hereby appropriated to the various pro-
fessional boards or other boards , commissions ,
institutions , agencies or subdivisions of the state
Government for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1943 ,
all of the fees (which include fees for board and
room , athletics , student activities ) and rentals , ad-
mittances , sales , licenses collected by law , contribu-
tions , gifts , subventions , and other miscellaneous
receipts produced by any of the following profes-
sional boards , or other boards , commissions , institu-
tions , agencies , and subdivisions of the State
Government , except as otherwise specifically pro-
vided , for the use and benefit of each of the below-
named professional boards , or other boards , com-
missions , institutions , agencies and subdivisions of
the State Government , the receipts which are re-
ceived by each of the respective professional boards ,
or other boards , commissions , institutions , agencies
or subdivisions of the State Government ; which
receipts are placed to the credit of a Revolving Fund
(Minor Fund ) out of which shall be established
separate Revolving Fund Accounts for the use and
benefit of each separate professional Board or other
boards , commissions , institutions , agencies and/or
subdivisions of the State Government . The fund ac-
credited to each shall not exceed at any time the
amount of receipts received from the separate pro-
fessional board or other boards , commission , institu-
tion, agency , and/or subdivision of the State Govern-
ment . Withdrawal from the said Revolving Fund
by each of the said professional boards , or other
boards , commissions , institutions , agencies , and/or
subdivisions of the State Government may be made
when and if needed for ordinary recurring expenses
of operation properly approved by the Department
of Finance , Division of Accounts and Control , and
said requisitions shall not be approved unless there
is to the credit of the Revolving Fund of such pro-
fessional Board , or other board , commission , institu-
tion, agency and/or subdivision of the State Govern-
ment , a free and unencumbered sum equal to the
amount of the requisitions . The total amount any
agency may requisition from the Revolving Fund
Account through the Department of Finance , shall
not during the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1943 ,
exceed the amount placed to the credit of the Re-
volving Fund , out of which has been established a
Revolving Fund Account for each separate agency
during the fiscal year July 1 , 1942 , to June 30 , 1943 ,
inclusive , plus any balance which said professional
board, or other board , commission , institution ,
agency and/or subdivision of the State Government
may have had forwarded from the preceding year ,
on or before September 30 , of the then current fiscal
year, by the Department of Finance .

PART THREE
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHWAYS
(1 ) State Road Fund. There shall be estab-
lished for the purpose of paying all cost of operation
and maintenance of the State Highway Department
and for carrying on its activities for the fiscal year
beginning April 1 , 1942 , and ending March 31 , 1943 ,
a State Road Fund ; and there is hereby appro-
priated to the State Road Fund all the funds now
realized out of the State revenues , authorized now
by law or that may hereafter be authorized by law ,
or any additional or other revenues that may be im-
posed by law for the benefit of public roads and
all funds realized from the Motor Vehicle Registra-
tion Tax, the Gasoline Tax, and the Tax on Other
Motor Fuels , now collected by law or that may here-
after be imposed or collected by law for the benefit
of said department and its activities . Such receipts
and revenues shall constitute the State Road Fund .
There is hereby appropriated to the State High-
way Department all monies received and placed to
the credit of the State Road Fund during the fiscal
year ending March 31 , 1943 , not otherwise appro-
priated in this Act , for use and benefit of the State
Road System in construction , maintenance , and re-
pair of roads , and for all the activities and duties of
said Department, as prescribed by law.

Equipment , Maintenance and Construction . There
is hereby appropriated out of the State Highway
Road Fund for the Fiscal year ending March 31,
1943 , for ordinary recurring administrative ex-
penses of operation , including the cost of printing
Treasury checks for the department , the sum of
$600,000.00 .

be used by the Division of Rural Highways , for the
improvement , reconstruction and maintenance of
County roads and bridges which have not been ac-
cepted by the State Highway Commission for
maintenance , said appropriation to be expended in
accordance with Chapter 5 , Acts of the General As-
sembly , 1936 , the sum of $ 2,000,000.00 .

be used for Administrative purposes for the Rural
Highway Division in the Highway Department . )

as described in the general Statutes , through the
Department of Finance and placed to the credit of
the General Expenditure Fund , excepting those
revenues which are specifically allocated to the

of the State Government shall be covered into the

general Statutes , and placed to the credit of the

the appropriations made from the General Ex-

penditure Fund in this Act , unless otherwise spe-

divisions of the State Government for Revolving
Fund purposes ; such agencies shall be only those
that are listed in this Act as having been approved
for Revolving Fund Accounts .
2 .

recurring expenses and extraordinary expense and

tucky shall not be available for expenditure until
allotted as now provided by law, and such appro-
priations as specifically made in this Act are hereby
declared to be maximum and conditional appro-
priations except when the Governor determines an

mission , institution , or subdivision of the State
Government requiring an additional allotment of
funds to be made from the General Emergency
Fund hereby placed at his disposal and made a

ECUTIVE DEPARTMENT " Item (d ) 1 , Part One

4, "EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT " Item ( d) 1 ,
Part One -A for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1944 ,
of this Act .

Legislature that the State expenditures for each

the conditions can not be finally determined until

Legislature that the Commissioner of Finance , with
the advice of the Commissioner of Revenue and the
approval of the Governor of the Commonwealth ,
be and he is hereby authorized , empowered and

each officer , department , board , commission , insti-

general laws , is hereby authorized , empowered and
directed by the Legislature to prevent an overdraft

cording to need , without discrimination , the appro-
priations herein made to any officer , department ,

the State Government ; provided that the power
hereby vested shall not permit any reduction of
the appropriation of any officer , department , board ,
commission , institution or subdivision of the State
Government that will actually impair the necessary
constitutional functions of any agency whose op-
erations and functions are determined to be neces-
sary constitutional functions of government .
None of the money appropriated specifically
herein under the term " capital outlay " shall be al-
lotted or expended without the approval of the
Governor , and the Governor shall not approve the
allotment or the expenditure of any funds for capi-
tal outlay unless the total amount of revenue ac-
cruing to the General Expenditure Fund through
existing laws is sufficient to justify said expendi-
tures and unless the Governor of the Common-
wealth believes the expenditure of said fund is
feasible , taking into consideration the cost of labor
and the cost and supply of materials incident
thereto .

To carry out the purpose of this Act for the

laws.title: AN ACT relating to the transfer of prisoners confined in any of the state penal institutions or reformatories.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 31, pp. 276–277
laws.summary: This act charges the Commissioner of Welfare with classifying and segregating prisoners in state penal institutions and reformatories based on various factors including past records, rehabilitation potential, and influence on other prisoners. The Commissioner is also given the authority to transfer prisoners between institutions. The act declares an emergency and is effective upon passage.
page_titles: An Act relating to the classification and segregation of prisoners.
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 31
(S. B. 8)
AN ACT relating to the transfer of prisoners confined in any
of the state penal institutions or reformatories .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
Section 1. That the Commissioner of Welfare of
the Commonwealth of Kentucky shall be charged
with the duty of classifying all prisoners and with
the duty of segregating said prisoners in all of the
state penal institutions and reformatories accord-
ing to their past records , the probability of their
being rehabilitated , the influence such prisoners
might exert upon fellow prisoners , and for any other
purpose that the Commissioner of Welfare , in his
discretion , may deem sufficient for the discipline of
the prisoners in any institution or reformatory , and
for the rehabilitation of any of said prisoners .
Section 2. For the purposes of carrying out
Section One of this Act, the Commissioner of Wel-
fare is vested with the authority to direct and com-
pel the transfer of any prisoner from any penal
institution or reformatory , irrespective of the order
of the court committing said prisoner to any one
institution or reformatory .
Section 3. If the Kentucky Revised Statutes are
enacted at the present session of the General
Assembly , this act shall be treated as repealing KRS
198.100 and 197.060 , regardless of the date of enact-
ment or taking effect of the Kentucky Revised
Statutes .
Section 4. There being an immediate need for
the segregation of prisoners and there being an
immediate need for work to be done at the various
state institutions and properties under the control
of the Department of Welfare , an emergency is
declared to exist , and this Act shall become effective
upon its passage by the General Assembly and its
approval by the Governor .
Approved by Governor Johnson , February 21 , 1942 .

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 53, pp. 383–384
laws.summary: This act consolidates and amends sections of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes concerning public parks in second-class cities. It allows cities to appropriate funds for park purchase, care, and improvement, and to maintain them from city funds. Crucially, it mandates the annual appropriation of two separate funds for park care and maintenance, one for a 'white park board' and the other for a 'colored park board', with funds paid out only upon order from the respective boards.
key_provisions: § 1. Sections 3235b -12 and 3235b -13 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , 1936 edition , as amended by Chapter 125 of the Acts of 1940 , are consolidated into one section and amended to read as follows : 66 66 (1) The city may appropriate a sufficient sum to provide for the purchase , care and improvement of public parks , and to meet the expenses of the boards of park commissioners , and may maintain public parks out of the city funds to the same extent as it is authorized to maintain other public property . (2 ) Two funds in whatever amounts the city legislative body deems sufficient for the care and maintenance of public parks may be annually appropriated for that purpose , and each shall be held by the treasurer of the city in a separate and distinct account , one for use by the white park board and the other for use by the colored park board . The money in either fund shall be paid out by the treasurer only upon an order issued by the board of park commissioners for which the fund is appropriated , signed by its secretary and countersigned by its president, and after a bill for the withdrawal has been approved by the board at session assembled . In no event shall the treasurer honor in any one year orders for a greater sum than the amount appropriated for park purposes . "

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 87, pp. 539–540
laws.summary: This act amends a statute concerning the office of Commonwealth's Attorney in counties with a population of 150,000 or more. It acknowledges that a large portion of the population in such counties is composed of 'persons of the colored race' and states that it is essential to work in harmony with this race and employ persons of that race to work among them, without discriminating against any person because of race or previous condition of servitude. The act also addresses the increase in work and the need to increase the number of district detectives in these offices.

CHAPTER 87
(H. B. 273)
AN ACT to amend section 125b - 1 of Carroll's Kentucky
Statutes , 1936 edition , relating to the office of Common-
wealth's Attorney in counties containing a population of
one hundred and fifty thousand or more .
WHEREAS , in counties containing a population of one
hundred and fifty thousand or over , a large portion of the
population of said counties is composed of persons of the
colored race , and it is deemed essential to the general wel-
fare of said counties and people to work in harmony with
said race and to employ whenever possible persons of that
race to work among them without doing violence to , or
discriminating against , any person because of race or
previous condition of servitude , and
WHEREAS , the work in said office in said counties has
greatly increased and it becomes necessary to increase the
number of district detectives in the office of Common-
wealth's Attorney in said counties, now therefore ,
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. Section 125b - 1 of Carroll's Kentucky Stat-
utes , 1936 edition , is amended to read as follows :
In counties having a population of 150,000 or
more the Commonwealth's Attorney shall appoint
four district detectives for a term of four years ,
subject to removal at any time by the Common-
wealth's Attorney . The district detectives shall
each be paid a salary not to exceed twenty -four
hundred dollars ( $ 2400.00 ) annually for each detec-
tive, to be paid out of the county levy in equal
monthly installments .
§ 2. If the Kentucky Revised Statutes are
enacted at the present session of the General Assem-
bly, section one of this Act shall , upon the taking
effect of the Kentucky Revised Statutes , be substi-
tuted in place of subsection ( 1 ) of KRS 69.110 , and
shall thereafter be treated as an amendment to sub-
section ( 1 ) of KRS 69.110 rather than an amend-
ment to $ 125b - 1 of Carroll's Statutes .
Approved March 5 , 1942

CHAPTER 52
(S. B. 147 )
AN ACT to amend and re-enact Sections 97.470, 97.430 , Kentucky
Revised Statutes , 1942 Edition , pertaining to the Secretary

Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
That Section 97.430 of the Kentucky Revised Stat-
utes 1942 Edition , be and the same is hereby amended
and re -enacted so that when so amended and re -enact-
ed said section shall read as follows :
" 97.430 (3235b -6 ) Compensation of Secretary and
Treasurer ; members not to receive pay or hold other
office .
The secretary and treasurer of each board may re-
ceive an annual salary of not over five hundred dol-
lars , to be fixed by the board and paid out of the fund
appropriated for park purposes . The members of
the boards shall receive no compensation for their
services as members , but a member who is elected
secretary and treasurer of his board may receive the
compensation authorized by this section for his serv-
ices as such . No member of either board may hold
any office , appointment or employment under the city
or any department or institution of the city ."
Section 97.470 Kentucky Revised Statutes , 1942
Edition , is amended to read as follows :
“ 97.470 ( 3235b -12 ; 3235b -13 ) Appropriations for
park purposes ; separate funds for white and colored
park boards.

provide for the purchase , care and improvement of
public parks , and to meet the expenses of the boards
of park commissioners , and may maintain public
parks out of the city funds to the same extent as it
is authorized to maintain other public property .

lative body deems sufficient for the care and mainten-
ance of public parks may be annually appropriated

laws.title: AN ACT pertaining to registration for elections in cities of the first class, amending KRS 117.310.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 88, pp. 213–215
laws.summary: This act amends KRS 91.010 concerning voting procedures in cities of the first class. It outlines a process for voters who claim they cannot sign their name, requiring them to be sworn in. If their registration record shows they previously signed, they will not be permitted to vote unless their inability to sign is due to a physical disability acquired after registration. Election officers must record these cases.
page_titles: AN ACT pertaining to cities of the first class amending KRS 91.010.
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 88
(H. B. 103 )
AN ACT pertaining to registration for elections in cities of the
first class , amending KRS 117.310 .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
Section 1. Section 117.310 Kentucky Revised
Statutes 1942 is hereby amended and as amended
reads :
117.310 Comparison of voter's signature with reg-
istration record ; voting record .
( 1 ) Prior to every primary , special , or regular ,
election in a city of the first class , the County Clerk
shall have prepared for each precinct of the city a
Comparative Signature Book which shall be in per-
manent form and contain sufficient blank sheets of
non -detachable type to afford reasonable space for
as many signatures as there are registered voters in
the precinct . The County Clerk shall follow the in-
structions of the Board of Registration Commission-
ers with respect to the exact form and makeup of the
Comparative Signature Books and they shall be fur-
nished and paid for in the same manner as other elec-
tion paraphernalia . The County Clerk shall deliver
the Comparative Signature Books along with other
election paraphernalia to the clerks of election of the
several precincts who shall sign a receipt therefor .
Before a vote is cast by any person , at any primary ,
special , or regular , election in a city of the first class ,
he shall sign his name in the Comparative Signature
Book , unless he signed his registration record by mak-
ing his mark , and the officers of election shall compare
the signature of every such person with the signature
of that person on the registration record form in the
precinct register . The challengers of the respective
political parties present shall also have the right to
compare the signature at the time the comparison is
made by the officers of election . If the comparison
of signatures creates a doubt in the minds of two of
the election officers as to whether the person applying
to vote is the same person as the registrant , no vote
shall be cast by him unless he otherwise satisfactorily
establishes his identity as the registrant . When the
polls close , the precinct sheriff and judge of the op-
posite political faith shall forthwith convey the Com-
parative Signature Book to the place where the Coun-
ty Clerk receives other election paraphernalia . The
Board of Registration Commissioners shall have at
that place , plainly identified , a duly authorized rep-
resentative to whom the sheriff and judge aforesaid
shall deliver the Comparative Signature Book and
secure a receipt therefor . The Board shall retain the
Comparative Signature Books for such length of time ,
not less than six (6 ) months , as it deems necessary .
( 2 ) If any person applying to vote at an election
states that he cannot sign his name , the judges of
election shall immediately swear him as to his name
and his inability to write , and thereupon the judges
and the challengers of the respective political parties
shall examine the registration record in the precinct
registrar , and if it is shown by that record that the
person of that name signed his name on the registra-
tion record , said person shall not be permitted to cast
a vote , unless his inability to sign his name at the date
of the election is due to some physical disability aris-
ing subsequent to his registration . The election of-
ficers shall make and return to the board a record
sheet of each person so sworn , showing the disposi-
tion made of each case . The record sheets shall be
provided as other election paraphernalia .
( 3 ) The clerk in each precinct shall, immediately
after a person has cast his vote at every primary , spe-
cial , and regular , election , indicate at the proper place
on the registration record that such person voted at
the election .
Passed February 14 , enrolled February 18 , approved February
24 , 1944 .

Medical Association . Thereafter members shall be
appointed for terms of four years and until their suc-
cessors are appointed and have qualified . Three mem-
bers of the commission shall be appointed from the
membership of the Kentucky State Medical Associa-
tion and the other eight members shall be selected
from persons engaged in different trades , occupa-
tions and professions , in different parts of the state ,
as to give a fair representation to all classes of citi-
zens in this state .
The Commissioner of Health shall, by virtue of his
office , be a member of the commission , and said com-
mission shall elect from its membership a chairman .
4. The Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission of
Kentucky , immediately upon its appointment , shall
*
proceed to select suitable sites for the establishment
of a state tuberculosis sanatorium in each of the dis-
tricts enumerated in Section 1 of this Act except the
Second District . The commission shall have author-
ity to acquire by gift , purchase , condemnation or
otherwise such tracts of land as the commission con-
siders best suited for the purpose . The commission
shall select sites where there is an adequate municipal
water supply and where there is convenient access to
utility service and fuel . The commission may acquire
tracts of land upon which buildings are erected . If it
is necessary to acquire land by condemnation , the
procedure shall be as provided in KRS 416.120 . Title
to any real estate acquired under this section shall be
taken in the name of the Commonwealth . The com-
mission shall have authority to expend not more than
thirty thousand dollars , out of the sums appropriated
by this Act , for the acquisition of sites , except that the
Governor , in his discretion , may supplement such
amount out of any emergency fund at his disposal .
In lieu of acquiring a tract of land on which to erect
a sanatorium in any district , the commission may ,
with the approval of the Governor , acquire by gift ,
purchase or otherwise any existing hospital , institu-
tion or colony in such district that is adaptable for
sanatorium purposes and that has adequate water
and utility services , municipal or otherwise , available .
§ 5. The commission first appointed under this
Act shall submit a report to the Governor within
ninety days after the date of its appointment , except
that the Governor may extend such time if , in his
opinion , the circumstances so require . Upon receipt
of the report , the Governor shall have authority to
enter into contracts for the preparation of architec-
tural plans and for the construction of such buildings
and improvements as may be necessary to provide
adequate sanatorium facilities upon each site . In the
event available funds are not sufficient to provide for
the construction of a sanatorium on each site , the
Governor , with the approval of the Tuberculosis San-
atoria Commission , shall have power to determine
which sanatorium shall first be constructed . The plans
and contracts for the sanatoria shall provide for facil-
ities sufficient to accommodate not less than one hun-
dred patients at each sanatorium . The Governor shall
have the further power to contract for the furnishing
of utilities services to the sanatoria .
§ 6. Upon the completion of each sanatorium , the
Governor shall appoint a board of commissioners who
shall have charge of the government and operation of
the sanatorium . Each board shall consist of five mem-
bers who shall serve for terms of four years , except
that two members of the first board shall be appointed
for terms of two years , two members for terms of
three years and one member for a term of four years .
Two members of the board shall be physicians who
are members in good standing of the Kentucky State
Medical Association , and the other members shall be
representatives of different trades , occupations and
professions .
7. The board of commissioners for each sana-
torium shall be a body corporate for the benefit of the
state . All funds and property of the sanatorium shall
be under the management and control of the board of
commissioners , subject to the provisions of Chapters
12 , 41 and 45 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes . The
board may receive property by legacy , conveyance or
otherwise for the benefit of the Commonwealth , in aid
and furtherance of the objects of the sanatorium .
Any donation to a sanatorium for a specified use shall
be applied to such use and no other . The board shall
furnish to the Governor an annual report covering the
operation of the sanatorium and such other reports as
the Governor may require . All funds of the board
shall be handled as provided in Chapter 45 of the Ken-
tucky Revised Statutes .
§ 8. The board of commissioners of each sana-
torium shall employ a medical director for the sana-
torium . No person may be employed as medical
director unless his employment is approved by the
Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission of Kentucky , nor
unless he is a member in good standing of the Ken-
tucky State Medical Association , or the National Tu-
berculosis Society , and has had at least five years
clinical experience in the field of tuberculosis . The
board of commissioners of each sanatorium shall have
authority to employ such physicians , nurses and other
personnel as it deems necessary for the operation of
the sanatorium , and may regulate the terms of serv-
ice , type of duties , and fix the salaries of such person-
nel , subject in all respects to the provisions of KRS
42.110 to 42.150 . The board of commissioners for each
sanatorium shall encourage the employment of in-
mates in such a way as to contribute to their physical ,
mental and moral improvement , and may utilize the
product of their labor in the maintenance of the
sanatorium .
§ 9. (1 ) Subject to the provisions of subsections
( 2 ) , ( 3 ) and ( 4 ) of this section , the board of commis-
sioners of each sanatorium shall receive for treatment
at such sanatorium any pauper patient who is a resi-
dent of the sanatorium district sent to the sanatorium
by any county or city board of health with the ap-
proval of the county judge as to pauper status .
( 2 ) The board of commissioners shall have au-
thority to refuse to accept any patient where the
acceptance of such patient would result in an unequal
proportion of patients , according to population, from
any county in the district .
(3) The board of commissioners may accept pay-
ing patients so long as at least one-half of the accom-
modations of the sanatorium are kept available for
pauper patients desiring admission . The charge to
be made for paying patients shall be fixed by the board
subject to the approval of the Governor .
(4) Whenever the number of patients sent to a
sanatorium is greater than can be accommodated and
cared for in the sanatorium , the board shall place the
names on a waiting list and shall receive them in the
order of their application as soon as accommodations
can be provided , subject to the provisions of sub-
sections ( 2 ) and ( 3 ) of this section .
(5 ) By agreement of the boards of commissioners
of the sanatoria involved , paying patients or pauper
patients may be transferred from one sanatorium to
another in order to best accomplish the purpose of
this Act to provide sanatorium facilities for all needy
persons of this state . The terms upon which the
transfer shall be made shall be as agreed upon by the
respective boards of commissioners . In the event the
board of commissioners cannot agree , the Governor
may order a transfer in any case where he deems it
necessary for the purposes of this Act .
(6) The board of commissioners of each sana-
torium shall receive and provide adequate facilities
for the treatment of paying and pauper patients of
the negro race who are residents of the district .
§ 10. The cost of transporting paying patients
shall be paid by themselves or by their friends or
relatives . The cost of transporting paupers shall be
paid by the fiscal court of the county from which they
are committed .
Passed and enrolled March 15 , approved March 17 , 1944 .

laws.summary: This act outlines qualifications and examination procedures for classified county employment. It requires applicants to be registered voters, of sobriety and integrity, law-abiding, and able to read, write, and understand English. Examinations are to be conducted by a commission, with notice published in the largest circulation newspaper. Applicants who served in the US military during wartime and received an honorable discharge receive a five percent increase in their examination grade. The commission certifies ranked lists of applicants to the fiscal court.
