laws.title: AN ACT relating to education in fields related to health, with particular reference to the education of, and the training of nurses and doctors of the Negro race.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 112, p. 313
laws.summary: This act allows hospitals to provide instruction in nursing, medicine, surgery, or other related graduate-level courses if their governing body elects to do so. It specifically addresses the lack of accredited training facilities for Negro women in nursing and postgraduate training for Negro doctors in Kentucky, while noting that adequate provisions exist for other races. The act aims to enable such training within hospitals that accept Negro patients.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 112 (H. B. 447) AN ACT relating to education in fields related to health , with par- ticular reference to the education of , and the training of nurses and doctors of the Negro race. WHEREAS , There is no accredited public , or private , agency in Ken- tucky where Negro women may obtain training in the profession of nursing , nor are facilities for postgraduate training available to Negro doctors , and WHEREAS , there are adequate provisions for such training for mem- bers of other races within the existing facilities of accredited hos- pitals which accept Negro patients . Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Common- wealth of Kentucky : The provisions of KRS 158.020 shall not be construed to prohibit the giving of instruction in nursing , medicine , surgery , or other related courses of graduate grade or on the professional level , within any hospital , if the governing body of the hospital , by a majority vote of its members , so elects . Approved March 25 , 1948 .

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 190
(S. B. 199 ).
AN ACT relating to the state tuberculosis sanatoria , including Hazel-
wood Sanatorium ; providing for a State Tuberculosis Sanatoria
Commission and transferring to such commission certain powers and
duties now possessed by the State Board of Health , the Tuberculosis
Sanatoria Commission of Kentucky and the boards of commissioners
for individual sanitoria , and abolishing the Tuberculosis Sanatoria
Commission of Kentucky and the boards of commissioners for
individual sanatoria ; and making provisions for the management ,
operation , construction , improvement , funds , financing , properties ,
and personnel of the sanatoria , and the admission and transfer of
patients .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Common-
wealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. Section 215.072 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes
is repealed and in lieu thereof there is enacted the following
section , to be numbered KRS 215.072 :
( 1 ) There is created a commission to be known as the
State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission , and to consist of
five members . The Commissioner of Welfare shall be ex
officio a member , and the other four members shall be appoint-
ed by the Governor . The appointed members shall be appoint-
ed for terms of four years and until their successors are
appointed and have qualified , except that upon the appoint-
ment of the first members one shall be appointed for a term
of one year, one for a term of two years , one for a term of
>
three years , and one for a term of four years . The commis-
sion shall annually elect a chairman from its membership ,
for a term of one year . The commission shall meet at the call
of the chairman, or at the call of the Governor , at such time
and place as is designated in the call . The members of the
commission , other than the Commissioner of Welfare , shall
receive a per diem of ten dollars for each meeting of the com-
mission attended , and all members shall be reimbursed for
their actual and necessary expenses in attending meetings of
the commission and otherwise in performing their duties . Any
vacancy shall be filled by appointment by the Governor for
the unexpired term .
(2 ) The State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission shall
be attached to and constitute a part of the Department of
Welfare . The Department of Welfare shall furnish such secre-
tarial and clerical assistance , and office space , as may be
required by the commission .
( 3) The per diem and expenses of the members of the
State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission shall be paid out of
appropriations for the ordinary recurring expenses of opera-
tion of the state tuberculosis sanatoria .
§ 2. Section 215.076 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes
is amended to read as follows :
The State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission shall have
charge of the government and operation of the state tuber-
culosis sanatoria located in each of the six districts enumerat-
ed in KRS 215.071 , and shall have authority to prescribe rules
and regulations for that purpose . All funds and properties
of the sanatoria shall be under the management and control
of the commission , subject to the provisions of Chapters 12 ,
41 , 42 and 45 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes . The com-
mission may receive property by legacy , conveyance or other-
wise , on behalf of the Commonwealth , in aid and furtherance
of the objects of the sanatoria or of any individual sana-
torium . Any donation for a specified use shall be applied to
such use and no other . The commission shall furnish to the
Governor an annual report covering the operations of the
sanatoria , and such other reports as the Governor may re-
quire . All funds of the commission shall be handled as pro-
vided in Chapters 41 , 42 and 45 of the Kentucky Revised
Statutes .
§ 3. Section 215.077 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes
is amended to read as follows :
The State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission shall em-
ploy and fix the compensation of a medical director for each
sanatorium , and in so doing shall not be subject to any re-
striction contained in subsection ( 2 ) of KRS 12.050 . No per-
son may be employed as medical director unless he is a
member in good standing of the Kentucky State Medical
Association , or the National Tuberculosis Society , and has
had at least five years ' clinical experience in the field of
tuberculosis . The Commission shall have authority to employ
such physicians, nurses and other personnel as it deems nec-
essary for the operation of the sanatoria, and may regulate
the terms of service , type of duties , and compensation of such
personnel , subject in all respects to the provisions of KRS
42.110 to 42.150 . The commission shall encourage the employ-
ment of inmates in the sanatoria in such a way as to con-
tribute to their physical , mental and moral development , and
may utilize the product of their labor in the maintenance of
the sanatoria .
§ 4. Section 215.078 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes
is amended to read as follows :
(1 ) Subject to the provisions of subsection ( 2 ) , ( 3 ) and
(4) of this section , and subject to such regulations as the
State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission may prescribe , the
medical director of each state tuberculosis sanatorium shall
receive for treatment at such sanatorium any pauper patient
who is a resident of the sanatorium district sent to the sana-
torium by any county or city board of health with the ap-
proval , as to pauper status , of the county judge of the county
of which the patient is a resident.
(2 ) Any medical director , with the advice of the com-
mission , shall have authority to refuse to accept any patient
where the acceptance of such patient would result in an
unequal proportion of patients , according to population , from
any county in the district .
(3) Paying patients may be accepted at any sanatorium
so long as at least one-half of the accommodations of the
sanatorium are kept available for pauper patients desiring
admission . The charge to be made for paying patients shall
be fixed by the State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission
subject to the approval of the Governor .
(4 ) Whenever the number of patients seeking admission
to a sanatorium is greater than can be accommodated and
cared for in the sanatorium , the names of those applying for
admission shali be placed on a waiting list and they shall be
received in the order of their application as soon as accom-
modations can be provided , subject to the provisions of sub-
sections ( 2 ) and ( 3 ) of this section .
(5) The State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission may
provide for the transfer of paying patients or pauper patients
from one state sanitorium to another , in order to best accom-
plish the purpose of providing sanatorium facilities for all
needy persons of this state .
(6) Provisions shall be made at each sanatorium for
the receipt and furnishing of adequate facilities for the treat-
ment of paying and pauper patients of the Negro race who
are residents of the district .
§ 5. Section 215.079 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes
is amended to read as follows :
The cost of transporting paying patients to any of the
state tuberculosis sanatoria shall be paid by themselves or by
their friends or relatives . The cost of transporting pauper
patients shall be paid by the fiscal court of the county from
which they are sent .
§ 6. Section 215.070 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes
is repealed , and in lieu thereof there is enacted the following
section , to be numbered KRS 215.070 :
The title to all property situated in Jefferson County
that is used and occupied by the state tuberculosis sanatorium
in that county is hereby transferred to and shall hereafter be
vested in the Commonwealth , and the State Board of Health '
shall execute such conveyance and instruments as are neces-
sary to effectuate the record of such transfer . Such transfer
shall not affect the validity of any mortgage or bonds , hereto-
fore executed according to law, which constitute an encum-
brance upon such property , and the State Tuberculosis
Sanatoria Commission shall arrange for the payment of the
interest and principal of such mortgage or bonds out of any
funds appropriated for that purpose .
§ 7. Sections 215.010 , 215.020 , 215.030 , 215.040 , 215.050 ,
215.060 , 215.073 , 215.074 and 215.075 , and subsection ( 2 ) of
Section 215.071 , of the Kentucky Revised Statutes , are
repealed .
§ 8. Any appropriations made by the General Assembly ,
including revolving , trust or agency fund appropriations , for
the ordinary recurring expenses of operation of the state
tubeculosis sanatoria , which appropriations have been made to
or under the name of any other state agency , shall be deemed
to have been made to , and shall be available to , the State
Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission . The commission , with
the approval of the Commissioner of Finance , shall allocate
and apportion such appropriations among the various state
tuberculosis sanatoria as in its judgment will best meet the
needs and purposes of the sanatoria , except that this shall
not authorize the diversion of any appropriation made by the
General Assembly specifically for the uses and purposes of a
particular , named sanatorium .
§ 9. The repeal of KRS 215.074 , by this Act , shall not
affect the validity of any outstanding , uncompleted contract
executed under authority of that section .
Approved March 26 , 1948 .

laws.summary: This statute outlines the compensation and meeting schedules for county boards of registration and purgation. It specifies daily pay rates for board members and secretaries, with different provisions for counties with and without cities of the first class. The statute also details the number of days the board must meet, particularly around election periods, and mandates that purgation be concluded at least twenty days before any primary or general election. Meetings are to be held at the courthouse unless otherwise necessary and with proper notice. It also includes a mechanism for citizens to prefer charges against a board that fails to meet or purge adequately.

Section 30. Comparative signature books ; comparison of
voter's signature with registration record ; voting record . ( 1)
Prior to every primary , special , or regular election in a city of the
first class , the county clerk shall have prepared for each precinct
of the city a comparative signature book which shall be in
permanent form and contain sufficient blank sheets of non-
detachable type to afford reasonable space for as many signa-
tures as there are registered voters in the precinct . The county
clerk shall follow the instructions of the board of registration
commissioners with respect to the exact form and makeup of the
comparative signature books and they shall be furnished and
paid for in the same manner as other election paraphernalia . The
county clerk shall deliver the comparative signature books along
with other election paraphernalia to the clerks of election of the
several precincts who shall sign a receipt therefor . Before a
vote is cast by any person , at any primary , special , or regular
election in a city of the first class, he shall sign his name in the
comparative signature book , unless he signed his registration
record by making his mark , and the officers of election shall
compare the signature of every such person with the signature
of that person on the registration record form in the precinct
register . The challengers of the respective political parties
present shall also have the right to compare the signature at
the time the comparison is made by the officers of election . If
the comparison of signatures creates a doubt in the minds of two
of the election officers as to whether the person applying to
vote is the same person as the registrant , no vote shall be cast
by him unless he otherwise satisfactorily establishes his identity
as the registrant . When the polls close, the precinct sheriff and
judge of the opposite political faith shall forthwith convey the
comparative signature book to the place where the county clerk
receives other election paraphernalia . The board of registration
commissioners shall have at that place , plainly identified , a duly
authorized representative to whom the sheriff and judge afore-
said shall deliver the comparative signature book and secure a
receipt therefor . The board shall retain the comparative signa-
ture books for at least the next two succeeding primary and
general elections .
(2) If any person applying to vote at an election states that
he cannot sign his name , the judges of election shall immediately
swear him as to his name and his inability to write , and there-
upon the judges and the challengers of the respective political
parties shall examine the registration record in the precinct
register , and if it is shown by that record that the person of that
name signed his name on the registration record , said person
shall not be permitted to cast a vote , unless his inability to sign
his name at the date of the election is due to some physical dis-
ability arising subsequent to his registration . The election of-
ficers shall make and return to the board a record sheet of each
person so sworn , showing the disposition made of each case ,
which shall be delivered to the Commonwealth's attorney within
ten days of the election . The record sheets shall be provided
as other election paraphernalia .
(3) The clerk in each precinct shall , immediately after a
person has cast his vote at every primary , special , and regular
election , indicate at the proper place on the registration record
that such person voted at the election .

Section 46. Purgation for primary election in cities of first
class by house to house canvass . The city board of registration
of each county containing a city of the first class shall cause a
purging and correcting of the registration lists and records of
the city for primary elections upon the request in writing of the
county executive committee of either of the two political parties
having representation upon the State Board of Election Com-
missioners , or upon the request in writing of any candidate for
office in the primary . The purging and correcting shall be con-
ducted as provided in this section .
(2) The registration commissioners of the city , shall cause
to be made a house to house canvass in each precinct of the city
with respect to which a request has been made under subsection
(1) of this section . The canvass shall be made jointly by two
investigators in each precinct , who shall be appointed by the
board of registration commissioners ten days in advance of the
date specified for the commencement of the canvass . One of the
investigators shall be selected from each of the two political
parties having representation upon the State Board of Election
Commissioners . The city board of registration may remove any
investigator and appoint a substitute . The canvass shall be made
during the first two weeks of the sixty -day period next preced-
ing the date upon which the primary is to be held. The board
of registration commissioners shall prepare and furnish each in-
vestigator with a list of names and addresses of the registered
voters in the precinct which he is to investigate , arranged in
convenient order to facilitate investigation .
(3) The investigators for each precinct shall make a written
report to the board of registration commissioners not later than
the last day of the two weeks period provided for making the
canvass , giving the names and addresses of
allpersons properly
registered in the precinct who are legally entitled to vote in the
primary election to be held in that year . When the reports of
the investigators in any precinct agree that any person registered
in the precinct is not legally entitled to vote at the election to
be held in that year , the city board of registration commissioners
of the city shall remove , transfer or cancel such registration as
the case may be , so as to make the record correspond with the
report made by the investigators and to correct the registration
record to the date of the report . No change shall be made until
after notice has been mailed by the board of registration com-
missioners to the person affected , at the address appearing upon
the registration record on file in the office of the board , stating
that it is the intention of the board of registration commissioners
to change , transfer or cancel his registration unless protest is
filed within five days in the office of the board of registration
commissioners . If protest is filed, no such change shall be made
until after the protestant has been given a reasonable oppor-
tunity to be heard , at which hearing the right of the protestant
to vote shall be determined by the board of registration com-
missioners .
(4) Each investigator provided for in this section shall be
paid reasonable compensation by the board , the board to de-
termine the amount .

laws.summary: This act amends Section 145 of the Kentucky Constitution regarding voter qualifications and disenfranchisement. It outlines the general requirements for voting (age, residency) and then lists exceptions, including persons convicted of treason, felony, bribery in an election, or "such high misdemeanor as the general assembly may declare shall operate as an exclusion from the right of suffrage." It also notes that such excluded persons may be restored to civil rights by executive pardon.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 2
(S. B. 13)
AN ACT to amend and re-enact Section 145 of the Constitution of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky.
That upon the concurrence of three-fifths of all the members
elected to each House of the General Assembly, the ayes and
nays being taken thereon and entered in full in their respective
journals, Section 145 of the Constitution of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky, be amended, extended and reenacted so that as so
amended, extended and reenacted it will read as follows :
"145. QUALIFICATIONS OF VOTER. PERSONS DIS
FRANCHISED. Every citizen of the United States of the age
of eighteen years who has resided in the state one year, and in
the county six months, and the precinct in which he offers to
vote sixty days next preceding the election, shall be a voter
in said precinct and not elsewhere but the following persons
are excepted and shall not have the right to vote.
"1. Persons convicted in any court of competent jurisdic
tion of treason, or felony, or bribery in an election, or of such
high misdemeanor as the general assembly may declare shall
operate as an exclusion from the right of suffrage, but persons
hereby excluded may be restored to their civil rights by execu
tive pardon.
4 Acts of the General Assembly
"2. Persons who, at the time of the election, are in con
finement under the judgment of a court for some penal offense.
"3. Idiots and insane persons."
3. That this amendment shall be submitted to the voters of
the State for their ratification or rejection at the time and in the
manner provided for under Section 256 of the Constitution and
under the Kentucky Statutes.
Approved March 22, 1954

laws.summary: This act repeals existing powers and duties granted to separate 'Board of Park Commissioners (White)' and 'Board of Park Commissioners (Colored)' in cities of the second class, vesting all such powers and duties in the city itself. This implies the consolidation of previously segregated park management structures.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 59, pp. 224–226
laws.summary: This act outlines procedures for challenging voter registrations. It specifies that a voter's name can be challenged if they have not voted in two consecutive years. The process involves written notification to the voter, an opportunity to appear before the board to contest the challenge, and the potential for removal from registration lists if the challenge is upheld or if the voter fails to appear. Challenges must be made in writing within ten days after registration books close.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 145, pp. 634–646
laws.summary: This statute amends Section 157.360 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, which deals with the allocation of classroom units for the foundation program in school districts. It outlines how classroom units are determined based on average daily attendance for elementary, secondary, vocational, and special education, as well as for administrative and support staff. A specific provision is made for Lincoln Institute, stating that one twenty-seventh of a classroom unit shall be included for each pupil in average daily attendance at Lincoln Institute if attendance is under a written contract between the institute and the district of the pupil's legal residence.

laws.summary: This act mandates the classification and segregation of inmates in a home for delinquent children based on race, sex, and the nature of their delinquency or conviction. It also emphasizes preventing association between 'good' and 'bad' conduct children.

AN ACT relating to a city/county children's home .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
Section 1. KRS 201.010 is amended to read :
As used in this chapter unless the context otherwise requires :
( 1 ) " Home " means the institution to be established and
maintained in any county having a city of the first class , in con-
formity with the provisions of this chapter .
( 2 ) "Board " means the body created by KRS 201.020 .
[ ( 3 ) " Dependent " , "neglected " and "delinquent children "
have the same meaning as in KRS 199.010 . ]
Section 2. KRS 201.020 is amended to read:
( 1 ) In each county containing a city of the first class there
shall be a bipartisan board known as the " Board for ( name of
city ) and ( ------- ) County Children's Home ” .
( 2 ) The board shall be composed of 14 [ 10 ] members ,
at least two of whom shall be women , appointed jointly by the
Mayor of the City and the County Judge of the County . Each
member shall be at least twenty - five years of age and a bona fide
resident of the county . The members shall be appointed in
equal proportion from the two political parties casting the high-
est and next highest number of votes at the last preceding gen-
eral election in the county .
( 3 ) The members of the board shall be divided into four
groups , of which two groups shall consist of three members each
and two groups shall consist of four members each . Members
shall serve for four years each , and the terms of the members of
any one group shall expire at the end of a year which is dif-
ferent from the year in which the terms of the members of any
other group expire . Members originally appointed during the
year following the effective date hereof may be appointed for
such terms as may be necessary to effectuate the rotation pro-
vided for in the preceding sentence .
[ ( 3 ) Three members of the board shall serve for two years ,
three for three years , and four for four years each. Members ap-
pointed after the original appointments shall serve for four years
each . The board shall be continuously divided between the two
major political parties as provided in sub-section ( 2 ) of this
section . ]
(4) Vacancies in the board , whether occurring during the
term or at the close of the term of a member , shall be filled in the
manner provided in sub -section ( 2 ) of this section , within thirty
days after the vacancy occurs , and if the mayor and the county
judge fail to make the appointment within thirty days , the mem-
bers of the board may make the appointment . Whenever any
vacancy occurs , the board shall immediately certify the fact of
the vacancy and the reason therefor to the county judge and the
mayor . All members shall serve without compensation .

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 40
laws.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the operation and maintenance of two institutions specifically designated for "Colored Persons": the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons and the West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons. It outlines specific amounts for salaries, expenses, materials, repairs, boarding, rooming, athletics, student activities, and instructional equipment for both colleges. It also details how fees and other operating receipts will be handled for the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons.

laws.summary: This statute addresses the admission of Negroes to educational institutions in Kentucky. It states that Negroes will not be admitted on an equal basis with other races and that no Negro citizen will be forced to attend a segregated regional institution if an institution offering the same course of study to other races exists within the Commonwealth. It also outlines a program for medical research and education, allowing contracts with medical schools to admit residents of the Commonwealth, with specific provisions for payment and reporting. Several sections of the Kentucky Revised Statutes are repealed.

laws.summary: This statute clarifies the operational and financial separation of schools for white and colored deaf students. It mandates that these schools be maintained as distinct institutions, though under a single Board of Commissioners and superintendent. Crucially, it specifies that the school for white deaf students is entitled to all appropriations unless explicitly designated for the colored deaf school, while the colored deaf school is only entitled to appropriations where the term 'colored' is used to distinguish it. Funds for each school must be kept separate and expended accordingly.

AN ACT for the benefit of the Kentucky School for the Deaf .
[ Act March 25 , 1910. Acts 1910 , Chap . 99 , p . 276. ]
1. Appropriation . That there is hereby appropriated out of the gen-
eral revenue of the State , not otherwise appropriated , for the benefit of

1. For the erection of two fire escapes on the dormitory buildings

2. To build an addition to the shops of the manual training depart-
ment , five thousand one hundred dollars .
3. To enlarge the laundry building and for coal cellar under same,

no provision has hitherto been made by the Commonwealth , six hundred

some difficulty has arisen in construing various acts appropriating funds

SEC. 769 .
( 1 ) A lease made under the authority of this section did not relieve the lessor
from the same responsibility for the negligence of its lessee as existed under a charter
which it acquired from another railroad , although this charter was in existence before
the enactment of K. S. 573. Clinger's Admr . v . Chesapeake & O. Ry . Co. of Ky ., 128
Ky. 736 , 33 R. 86 , 109 S. W. 315 .
( 2 ) This statute does not authorize the taking of private property for private
purposes without the consent of the owner under condemnation proceedings for the
purpose of building spurs or branches . Riley v . L. H. & St. L. Ry. Co. , 142 Ky. 67,
133 S. W. 971 .
( 3 ) The words " competing or parallel " in this section do not mean " competing
and parallel ." Nor is it material in deciding whether two lines come within this
section , that through trains are not operated on one of the lines ; as a road may be
a competing road by reason of connections with another line , although it does not own
the connecting line . Com . v. L. & N. R. R. Co. and Frankfort & C. R. R. Co. , 144
Ky. 324 , 138 S. W. 291 .
185
SEC . 772b. CORPORATION LAWS .
(4 ) This section does not authorize a railroad company to construct a spur
across a sidewalk , without the consent of the city authorities . City of Covington v .
L. & N. R. Co. , 158 Ky . 136 , 164 S. W. 329 .
SEC . 772 .
( 1 ) Under this section a railroad company is required to maintain no more
convenient water closet at a station than is found in adjoining dwellings , business
houses , etc. Louisville & N. R. Co. v. Com., 131 Ky. 268 , 114 S. W. 1192 .
(2 ) This section is to be reasonably considered and a railroad company should
not be held liable for violation thereof until it is shown that it allowed a privy to
remain a nuisance . Louisville & N. R. Co. v. Com., 137 Ky . 802 , 127 S. W. 152 .
(3 ) A railroad ran only a freight train with a caboose car instead of complying
with this section and running a regular passenger train . It was indicted under K. S.
795 for violation of the separate coach law. In such a proceeding its violation of this
section can not be inquired into . Southern Ry. Co. in Ky . v. Com ., 129 Ky . 87 , 33
R. 430 , 110 S. W. 372 .
(4 ) A removal of a passenger station a distance of three hundred and seventy-
six feet was not an abandonment of the station within the meaning of this section .
Lou. & I. Ry. Co. v . Callahan , 143 Ky . 517 , 136 S. W. 1018 .
( 5 ) An indictment following substantially the language of this section was
held sufficient ; no bill of particulars could be required . L. & N. R. R. Co. v. Com .,
144 Ky. 525 , 139 S. W. 756 .
(6 ) A certain room was held not to be a waiting room. L. , H. & St. L. R. R.
Co. v. Com ., 144 Ky. 541 , 139 S. W. 776 .
(7) Certain evidence was held sufficient to preclude a peremptory instruction
on an indictment under this section . L. , H. & St. L. R. R. Co. v . Com., 144 Ky . 625 ,
139 S. W. 931 .
( 8 ) Where the depot of a railroad together with the privy in connection there-
with was destroyed by fire , and the railroad company erected a temporary depot
without having been notified so to do by the State Railroad Commission , but failed
to provide a privy in connection therewith , within a reasonable time after the erection
of the temporary depot , a conviction under Section 772 of the offense of failing to
provide such privy , will be sustained . L. & N. R. Co. v . Com., 155 Ky. 187 , 159
S. W. 701 .
(9 ) This section applies only to such depots as the railroad company has regularly
established for the convenience of the public , and has no application to places between
regular depots at which trains stop to receive and take on passengers or to offices
in cities or towns at which tickets are sold . Commonwealth v. Chesapeake & Ohio
Ry . Co. , 157 Ky. 140, 162 S. W. 783 .
( 10 ) A railroad company is not required to provide separate closets for the
sexes . If such company provides a sufficient number of closets for colored passengers
on trains , it does not discriminate against them because it provides only one closet
in the colored compartment- a half car in length- while it provides two closets in
the white car-a whole car in length . Equality of accommodations does not mean
identity of accommodations . L. & N. R. Co. v . Com., 160 Ky . 769 .
( 11 ) For form of instructions under this section, see Instructions to Juries
( Ky. ) , Sec . 825 .

laws.summary: This section of the corporation laws addresses railroad regulations, specifically concerning the carrying of passengers. Subsection (1) states that a railroad company is not required to carry a separate coach for white and colored passengers on a freight train that includes a combination car used as a caboose. Subsection (2) discusses liability for not running a regular passenger train as required by K.S. 772a, when only a freight train with a caboose is operated.

SEC. 791 .
( 1) An indictment under this section charging the defendant with operating
a railway in Kentucky "under a lease, without having the same recorded in the
office of the Secretary of State and in the County Clerk's office of B. County ," is good .
Com . v. C. & O. Ry. Co. , 24 R. 1880 , 72 S. W. 359 .
SEC . 792 .
( 1) Where two railroad companies have entered into a traffic contract that
prohibits one of them from furnishing reasonable and proper facilities to serve the
public along the road operated jointly by them, so much of the contract is in violation
of the statute and void . C. & O. Ry . Co. v. Peed , 155 Ky . 696 , 160 S. W. 472 .
SEC . 793. [ Amended . ]
This section was amended by Acts March 22 , 1910. Acts 1910 , Chap .
52 , p . 180 , by merely striking the figures " 786 " from Section 793 , as the
penalty for violating Section 786 is changed and provided in Section 786 .
( 1 ) An indictment for an offense purely statutory is sufficient if it follows the
language of the statute . Com . v. C. & O. Ry. Co. , 101 Ky . 159 , 19 R. 329 , 40 S. W. 250 .
( 2 ) The lowest fine allowed by the statute for the violation of K. S. 772 in
reference to a waiting room is $ 100.00 . L. , H. & St. L. R. R. v. Com., 144 Ky . 541 ,
139 S. W. 776 .
(3) For form of indictment under this section , see Kentucky Form Book ,
Form No. 2798 .
SEC . 794 .
(1) A reckless throwing of a stone into a railroad car is only a misdemeanor ,
unless the stone is calculated to produce great bodily harm and some person is injured
by the throwing of it . Robinson v . Com., 144 Ky . 111 , 137 S. W. 833 .
SEC . 795 .
( 1 ) A railroad company is not required to carry a separate coach for white and
colored passengers in a freight train carrying a combination car which is used as a
caboose . L. & N. R. Co. v . Com ., 117 Ky. 345 , 25 R. 1442 , 78 S. W. 167 .
(2 ) A railroad ran only a freight train with a caboose car attached instead
of complying with K. S. 772a in running a regular passenger train . In an indictment
under this section it could not be held liable for violation of K. S. 772a . Southern
Ry. Co. in Ky. v . Com., 129 Ky. 87 , 33 R. 430 , 110 S. W. 372 .
(3 ) An interurban railroad must comply with the provisions of this act and
can not evade its duty by leasing its right to a street railroad , nor can the street
railroad rely on want of authority to operate the road as a defense . The lessor could
191
SEC . 805. CORPORATION LAWS .
only be held liable if it knew when it executed the lease that the lessee would violate
the statute . Louisville Ry. Co. et al . v. Com., 130 Ky. 738 , 114 S. W. 343 ; Louisville
& Interurban R. Co. v. Com., 130 Ky. 738 , 114 S. W. 343 .
(4 ) A railroad company, which hauled a sleeper of the Pullman Company , receiv-
ing no part of the fares collected by the Pullman Company from persons riding in
the sleeper , which sleeper with its occupants was under the exclusive control of the
servants of the Pullman Company , did not thereby violate this statute , because of
hauling the sleeping car with its unseparated colored passengers and white passengers
through the State of Kentucky . Com. v. Ill . Central R. Co. , 141 Ky. 502 , 133
S. W. 1158 .
( 5 ) On the facts in this case , it was held that the conductor had not failed in
his duty under this section. Hale v . C. & O. Ry . Co. , 142 Ky. 835 , 135 S. W. 398 .
( 6 ) A young white girl was required by the conductor to ride in the coach
provided for colored passengers ; a verdict and judgment for punitive damages against
the company was sustained ; but it was held that the company would not be liable
if the conductor in good faith believed , and in the exercise of ordinary care had a right
to believe , that she was a woman of color and was not insulting to her . L. & N. R. R.
Co. v. Ritchel , 148 Ky. 701 , 147 S. W. 411 .
(7) In an indictment for violating this section conversation between the con-
ductor and a passenger which tended to show that the coach was intended for colored
people was properly rejected . C. & O. Ry . Co. v. Com., 149 Ky . 386 , 149 S. W. 826 .
(8 ) A railroad company is not required to provide separate closets for the
sexes . If such company provides a sufficient number of closets for colored passengers
on trains , it does not discriminate against them because it provides only one closet
in the colored compartment- a half car in length-while it provides two closets in
the white car- a whole car in length . Equality of accommodations does not mean
identity of accommodations . L. & N. R. Co. v. Com., 160 Ky. 769 .
(9) For form of indictment under this section , see Kentucky Form Book , Form
No. 2805 .
SEC . 796 .
A railroad company is not required to provide separate closets for the sexes . If
such company provides a sufficient number of closets for colored passengers on trains ,
it does not discriminate against them because it provides only one closet in the colored
compartment — a half car in length-while it provides two closets in the white car-a
whole car in length . Equality of accommodations does not mean identity of accommo-
dations . L. & N. R. Co. v . Com ., 160 Ky . 769 .
SEC . 799 .
(1 ) A white passenger on a railroad went into a compartment for colored
passengers and killed a colored passenger ; the conductor did not know that the white
passenger was in the colored compartment ; a porter saw the white man in the colored
compartment ; but it did not appear that it was practicable for him within a reasonable
time to notify the conductor or for the conductor if he had been so notified to eject
the white passenger before the difficulty . The railroad company was not civilly liable
for the killing . L. & N. R. Co. v. Renfro's Admr ., 142 Ky. 590 , 135 S. W. 266 .
SEC . 801 .
( 1) The fact that the only passenger train run was a freight train with a
caboose for passengers did not require separate compartments therein for whites and
negroes , in view of the express provision of this section . Southern Ry. Co. v. Com.,
129 Ky. 87 , 33 R. 430 , 110 S. W. 372 .
SEC . 805 .
A trespasser swinging off a moving train voluntarily , and so getting his foot into
an unblocked frog in the street , can not recover where the accident would not have
192
CORPORATION LAWS . SEC . 809 .
occurred , but for his violation of the statute . Louisville Bridge Company v. Siebert ,
157 Ky. 151 , 162 S. W. 804 .
SEC . 806 .
( 1) This section is not a violation of the Constitution , Sec . 10, forbidding
unreasonable searches and seizures, and its provision for the ejection of disorderly
passengers and gambling passengers is reasonable and proper . Com. v. Marcum , 135
Ky. 1, 122 S. W. 215 .
( 2 ) It is the duty of a railroad conductor to put a boisterous , profane , or obscene
passenger off the train without waiting for arrival at a station . L. & N. R. Co. v.
Setser's Admr ., 138 Ky. 476 , 128 S. W. 341 .
(3 ) A conductor on a railroad train has a right to refuse as a passenger a
person who is intoxicated ; and should such person get upon the train without the
conductor's knowledge the conductor may stop the train and put him off. C. & O.
Ry. Co. v . Selsor , 142 Ky . 163, 134 S. W. 143 .
(4 ) The mere failure of a conductor to obey the provisions of this section does
not make the railroad company liable for injury done by a riotous passenger in shooting
and killing a licensee walking along the railroad track . N. , C. & St. L. Ry. Co. v.
Lowery's Admr ., 148 Ky. 599 , 147 S. W. 19.
(5 ) In Kentucky , the conductors of passenger trains occupy a peculiar position .
In addition to the duty which they owe to the carrier , they also owe a duty to the
Commonwealth , imposed upon them by express statutory enactment ; and that duty is
one not imposed on other citizens . And in the discharge of the imposed duty no
reasonable presumption will be denied in favor of the bona fides of a conductor's acts
in respect thereof . C. & O. Ry. Co. v. Pruitt , 157 Ky. 133 , 162 S. W. 781 .
SEC . 807 .
( 1) Where malice is not shown under this section, prosecution may take place
under K. S. 1256. Com . v. Wells , 33 R. 964 , 112 S. W. 568 .
(2 ) For form of instruction under this section , see Instructions to Juries ( Ky.) ,
Sec . 828 .
(3 ) For form of indictment under this section , see Kentucky Form Book , Form
No. 2803 .
SEC . 809 .
( 1) Uncontradicted evidence that the train could not be stopped in time to
prevent striking a horse authorized the Circuit Court not to submit the issue of negli-
gence to the jury . Crawford v. Sou . Railway in Ky ., 150 Ky . 741 , 150 S. W. 990 .
( 2 ) There is no presumption of negligence where the injury is merely the result
of fright . Pickett v. Lex . & E. Ry . Co. , 153 Ky . 460 , 155 S. W. 1139 .
(3 ) The provision as to dividing the loss between the railroad and the owner
of the cattle applies where there has been no attempt on the part of the railroad
company to comply with K. S. 1789 to 1799 , inclusive ; if a railroad company attempts
to construct a right-of-way fence , its liability is to be adjudged by K. S. 1789 to
1799. Crawford v . Sou . Ry. in Kentucky , 153 Ky. 812 , 156 S. W. 861 .
(4 ) The prima facie presumption of negligence and carelessness in the injury
of cattle is not overcome without a showing that the signals of K. S. 786 have been
given . Campbell v . Mobile & Ohio Ry. Co. , 154 Ky . 582 , 157 S. W. 931 .
(5) Under this section the killing or injuring of stock by a railroad train is
presumed to have been caused by the negligence of those in charge of the train ; and
the burden of proving that such was not the case rests upon the railroad company . It
may , therefore , relieve itself of that presumption by showing by competent evidence that
its servants in charge of the train used ordinary care to avoid the killing or injuring
of the stock . C. & O. Ry. Co. v. Burton , 156 Ky. 736 , 161 S. W. 1116 .
(6 ) For form of approved instructions , with annotations , in action for stock
struck on track , see Instructions to Juries ( Ky. ) , Section 531 .
(7) 193
SEC . 818. CORPORATION LAWS .
(7 ) For form of petition for killing animals on railroad track , see Kentucky
Form Book , Form No. 2814 .
SEC . 815 .
( 1) The necessity exists under this section when there is a substantial convenience
to the public by making the road safer or better . Railroads built under this section
come within the general laws regulating railroads . Greasy Creek Mineral Co. v . Ely
Jellico Co. , 132 Ky . 692 , 116 S. W. 1189 .
(2 ) A party building a railroad under this section is not a "common carrier "
so as to make this statute unconstitutional in view of Sec . 210 of the Constitution .
A coal company can not make extortionate track charges to others , but until it
has been repaid for the cost of construction , others can not claim that track charges
contracted for are extortionate . Straight Creek Coal Mining Co. v. Straight Creek
Coal & Coke Co. , 135 Ky . 536 , 122 S. W. 842 .
(3 ) A certain joint stock company having the powers mentioned in this
section was held to be a corporation within the meaning of Constitution 203. Stearns
Coal Co. v. McPherson , 144 Ky. 730 , 139 S. W. 971 .
SEC . 816.
( 1) The fact that Section 816 Kentucky Statutes is not enforcible as a penal
statute does not deprive the Railroad Commission of jurisdiction to award reparation
for extortionate charges, the designation of sections 816 , 817 and 818 in section 829
being merely descriptive of the subjects of the Commission's Jurisdiction thereunder .
Illinois C. R. Co. v. Paducah Brewery Co. , 157 Ky . 357 , 163 S. W. 239 .

laws.summary: This section of the 1915 Supplement to the Kentucky General Assembly statutes addresses the legitimacy and inheritance rights of children, particularly in the context of marriages involving slaves prior to February 14, 1866. It clarifies that customary marriages between slaves, even without formal clerk registration, were considered valid if recognized by the couple and their children. It also explicitly states that the issue of such customary marriages, and those who continued to cohabit as man and wife after February 14, 1866, are to be held as legally married and their issue legitimate for all purposes. This Act is noted as being broader than a previous statute from 1898.

laws.full_text:
SEC. 1399a .
( 1) Where a slave took a slave girl as his wife , but they did not go before the
clerk of the court as required , but lived together for two years and had a son whom
they recognized , there was a customary valid marriage . Talbott v . Owen , 29 R. 550 ,
93 S. W. 658 .
(2 ) A son of a slave born during slavery but not the result of a customary
marriage , can not inherit from his father . Turner v. Terrill , 30 R. 89, 97 S. W. 396 .
(3 ) Where a slave was twice married , according to the custom of slaves , the
issue of each marriage is legitimate . Lindsey's Devisee v . Smith , 131 Ky . 176 , 114
S. W. 779 .
(4 ) In connection with this section consult Acts 1910 , Chap . 70 , Sec . 1, which is
Sec . 1399b of this Supplement .
SEC . 1399b .
1. Slave marriage made legitimate . That all negroes and mulattoes
who lived and cohabited together as man and wife prior to February 14,
1866 , and who so continued to live and cohabit since that time up to the
death of either or both of them , and all who are now so living and co-
habiting together , who so lived and cohabited prior to February 14 , 1866 ,
shall be taken and held in law as legally married , and their issue held
as legitimate for all purposes .
2. The customary marriages and the issue of same of negroes and
mulattoes prior to February 14 , 1866 , shall be held legitimate .
[ Act March 22 , 1910. Acts 1910 , Chap . 70 , p . 207. ]
This Act seems broader than that of March 16, 1898 known as Ky. Stats . Sec . 1399a .
Consult in connection with this Act , Ky. Stats . Sec . 1399a .
SEC . 1401 .
( 1) Weisiger v. McDonald , 116 Ky . 862 , 25 R. 1053 , 76 S. W. 1080 .
(2 ) A will provided among other things that if testator's daughter should die
leaving children , certain land devised to her should go to said children . She died
leaving a son to whom she devised the land . The son died an infant . In view of all
the provisions of the will it was held that the son took under his grandfather's will
and not under his mother's will , and that this section did not apply to the land .
Cocksey v . Hill , 106 Ky. 297 , 20 R. 1873 , 50 S. W. 235 .
( 3 ) Where an infant dies, possessed of lands devised to him by a grandparent ,
they descend as if he were an adult . Turner's Trustee v. Washburn , 25 R. 2198 , 80
S. W. 460 .
(4 ) Where a minor dies without issue leaving land inherited from her mother ,
and the relatives by her mother are her mother's sister , her mother's brother , and the
314
DESCENT LAW OF . SEC . 1403 .
child of a dead sister of her mother , each takes one -third . Carnes v. Bingham , 134
Ky . 96, 119 S. W. 738 .
(5 ) Where an infant dies owning real estate derived from one parent as provided
in this section, the whole descends to that parent or his or her kindred . Holmes v .
Lane , 136 Ky. 21 , 123 S. W. 318 .
(6) An adopted child died in infancy without issue ; the estate which he inherited
from his foster parent descended to the kindred of that parent ; they were not the
natural kindred of the adopted child . Lanferman v. Vanzile , 150 Ky. 751 , 150 S. W.
1008.
(7 ) Timber was cut under a contract that passed no title on land , one -half of
which belonged to an infant . She died in infancy unmarried and without issue . Her
right of action did not descend to her heirs ; it vested in her administrator as personal
estate. Layne v. Clark, 152 Ky. 310 , 153 S. W. 437 .
( 8 ) Where the wife devised property to the husband , but he died before her ,
their infant child took the devised estate as the devisee would have done had he
survived the testatrix , and the infant taking as devisee of his mother's will , under
the terms of Section 1401 , it descends to the heirs at law of his mother . Banks V.
Cornelison , 159 Ky. 793 , 169 S. W. 502 .
(9 ) See also Bertram v. Witherspoon's Admr ., 133 Ky. 116 , 127 S. W. 533 .
SEC . 1403 .
(1) Thompson v. Thompson , 117 Ky. 526 , 25 R. 1626 , 78 S. W. 418 ; Howland v.
Harr , 123 Ky. 732 , 30 R. 53 , 97 S. W. 358 .
(2 ) The exemption allowed under subsection 5 to the widow and infant children
does not apply to the husband and children of an intestate wife . Thaxton's Gdn . v .
Walter's Admr ., 130 Ky. 235 , 113 S. W. 118 .
(3 ) The husband became insane and died leaving no personal property , but left
two claims , the proceeds of an exchange of his real estate . These vested in the widow
immediately on his death , for herself and infant children , and she was entitled to sue
for them . Manns v. Manns , 115 S. W. 715 .
(4 ) A testator provided that all cash notes and debts owing him should go to
two grandchildren , to be shared equally with any other heir , full brother or sister to
them , the money to be held in trust and the interest used for the benefit of the children
until they should come of age . The gift was absolute so that , upon the death of one
of the grandchildren , his share passed by descent to his father and mother . Cornelison
v. Million , 124 S. W. 366 .
(5 ) Where an intestate dies possessed of property which came from his dead
mother and where his mother's sister and his two half brothers survived , his interest
in land passed to his aunt , if he was an infant when he died , otherwise , to his half
brothers . Bertram v. Witherspoon's Admr ., 138 Ky. 116, 127 S. W. 533. See also
Sec . 1401 .
(6 ) The failure of a childless widow to demand that her exemptions be set apart
to her when the appraisement is made , does not release the administrator from his
responsibility incurred to her by taking and selling the property ; it is his duty to
cause the exempt articles to be set apart to her . Chism v . Chism , 2 Ky. Opinions 461 .
(7) The husband of a deceased married woman is not entitled to the specific
articles mentioned in subsection 5 of this section . Hamilton's Admx . v. Riney , 140
Ky. 476, 131 S. W. 287 .
(8 ) A policy in the Bricklayers ' Union for $ 150.00 provided that it should be
paid to the widow or other legal representative of the deceased ; it was paid to the
administrator . A judgment awarded it to the widow as exempt from the payment of
debts . On account of the smallness of the amount no appeal lay from the judgment .
Costigan & Roll v. Sallie Gilson's Committee , 141 Ky. 377 , 132 S. W. 553 .
( 9 ) A note held by a married woman passes at her death to her personal
representative ; her husband can not, as such , sue thereon ; this was also the case
prior to 1893. Boughner v. Sharp , 144 Ky. 320 , 138 S. W. 375 .
( 10 ) This section is cited . Smith v. Perkins , 148 Ky. 387 , 146 S. W. 758 .
( 11 ) In 1876 the title of personal property of a decedent vested in his personal
representative when he qualified , and it became his duty to set aside to the widow the
exemptions ; the widow had no cause of action to recover property not thus set aside
for her . ( Subsection 5. ) Green v. Wilson , 8 Ky. Opinions 636 .
315
SEC . 1407. DESCENT LAW OF .
( 12 ) A woman died in 1858 ; her surviving husband was entitled to the interest
she had under the will of a certain decedent . ( Subsection 3. ) Armstrong v . Crutch-
field's Exrs ., 150 Ky. 641 , 150 S. W. 835 .
( 13 ) An executor who takes charge of the personal estate and pays it out to
creditors is liable to the testator's widow for her exemptions if she renounces the will
within a year . Franzell's Exr . v. Franzell , 153 Ky. 171 , 154 S. W. 912 .
( 14 ) For form of report under this section , see Kentucky Form Book , Form
No. 1527 .
( 15 ) A widow voluntarily agreeing in writing to accept the provisions of her
husband's will may thereafter within twelve months renounce the will and take under
the statute when this may be done without prejudice to any who has in good faith
acted on her acceptance of the will . Williams v. Williams , 161 Ky. 55 .
SEC . 1403. Subsec . 5. [ As re - enacted . ]
Exemptions $ 750 to widow or children . Personal property or money
on hand or in bank to the amount of $ 750 shall be exempt from distribu-
tion and sale and shall be set apart by the appraisers of the estate of an
intestate to his widow and children , or , if no widow , to his infant children
or child surviving him . The appraisers shall state in their appraise-
ment the money or the articles and value of each set apart by them to
the widow, or infants , separately to the articles appraised for sale , but
if the widow be present at the time of the appraisement , or any one
authorized by her in writing , she may make her selection out of the
property appraised to the amount of said $ 750 and said appraisers shall
so report . The provisions of this section shall apply to cases where the
husband dies testate , and the widow renounces the provisions of the will
in the time prescribed by law.
Sec . 1403 , subsec . 5 was repealed and the above subsec . 5 enacted as a substitute
by Act March 13, 1912. Acts 1912 , Chap . 72 , p . 226 .
SEC . 1404 .
( 1 ) Although a widow's husband left real estate in other states , she can not
prosecute an appeal from the order probating his will, after she has renounced the
will and elected to take under the law. Thompson v. Thompson , 134 Ky. 757 , 121
S. W. 641 .
(2 ) The provisions of this section, do not apply to the husband of a deceased
testatrix . Bottom v. Fultz , 124 Ky. 302 , 30 R. 479 , 98 S. W. 1037 .
(3 ) A creditor can not compel his debtor to elect to renounce the debtor's wife's
will , and to take the share of her property which he would have taken in case of
intestacy . Bains v. Globe Bank & Trust Co. , 136 Ky . 332 , 124 S. W. 343 .
(4 ) A widow who receives a part of her husband's estate under his will can not ,
without renouncing the provisions made for her in his will , claim dower in land as to
which he died intestate . Smith v. Perkins , 148 Ky. 387 , 146 S. W. 758 .
(5 ) The election of a wife to take under the will of her husband does not prevent
her from asserting dower in land in which he had only a defeasible fee ; he had no
right to dispose of the land by will . Landers v . Landers , 151 Ky. 206 , 151 S. W. 386 .
(6 ) Under Section 1404 , and as therein provided , the widow may relinquish what
was given her by a will and thereupon receive her dower and distributable share as
if no will had been made . Redwine's Executor v . Redwine , 160 Ky. 282 , 169 S. W. 864 .
(7 ) For form of renunciation by widow under this section, see Kentucky Form
Book , Form No. 1405 .
SEC . 1407 .
(1 ) The provisions with reference to advancements should be liberally construed .
Tye v. Tye , 24 R. 637 , 59 S. W. 718 .
316
EMBALMING AND UNDERTAKING . SEC . 1410 .
(2) To constitute an advancement , two things are necessary ; first , that the
parent or grandparent die partially intestate ; and second , that the gift be with a view
to a portion or settlement . Owsley v . Owsley , 23 R. 1194 , 77 S. W. 394 .
(3 ) A testator can specify and determine a previous advancement in his will .
Dowell v . Workman , 25 R. 1761 , 78 S. W. 857 ; Sullivan v . Sullivan , 122 Ky . 707 , 29
R. 239 , 92 S. W. 966 .
(4 ) A memorandum book kept by an intestate was competent evidence as to
advancements made to his children . Ray v. Ray's Admr ., 2 Ky . Opinions 131.
(5 ) Advancements not charged in a will can be considered only in the distribu-
tion of the undevised estate . Gulley v . Lillard's Exr ., 145 Ky. 746 , 141 S. W. 37.

SEC. 2089c .
Columbus Day made legal holiday . That the twelfth day of October
of the year 1910 , and the twelfth day of October of each year thereafter
is hereby declared a legal holiday , to be known as " Columbus Day " and
the same shall be recognized , classed and treated as other legal holidays
under the laws of this State .
[ Act March 14, 1910. Acts 1910 , Chap . 9, p . 38. ]
SEC . 2095 .
Hospitals .
( 1 ) An infant who has not previously been convicted of a felony is a first offender
within subsection 19a of this section , although he may have been previously convicted
of a misdemeanor . Henson v . Com., 148 Ky . 631 , 147 S. W. 399 .
SEC . 2095a .
Houses of Reform .
( 1) A minor convicted of a felony , which is her first offense , must be sentenced
to the House of Reform . Upon attaining her majority , if the period of her confinement
is not then exhausted , she must be transferred to the penitentiary to serve the residue
of her sentence . ( Subsection 19a . ) Washington v. Com., 143 Ky . 602 , 136 S. W. 1041 .
(2 ) If an infant defendant is convicted of felony in a Circuit Court and the
offense is his first offense , the Circuit Court may at any time thereafter during his
minority , by an order made upon motion , direct his confinement in the House of Reform
until he attains his majority , and if his term of punishment be not ended , that he
then be transferred to the penitentiary until it expires . ( Subsection 19a . ) Carrico
v. Com., 145 Ky. 641 , 140 S. W. 1036 .
(3 ) Sections 13 and 14 of this Act held void as not being expressed in the title
of the Act. Thompson v . Com., 159 Ky . 8, 166 S. W. 623 .
SEC . 2095a . Subsec . 20 .
[ By Acts 1914 , Chap . 61 , p . 154 , Chap . 118 of Acts 1910 and subsections 3, 4 and
5 of subsection 20 of Section 2095a , are repealed , and the following subsections enacted
in their stead.]
Houses of reform-white and colored children- separate apartments .
The children of white and colored races committed to said institution shall
be provided with separate apartments . [ Acts 1914 , p . 154. ]
450
HOUSES OF REFORM . SEC . 2095a .
SEC . 2095a . Subsec . 20.
1. Superintendent's duty to have inmates employed . The Superin-
tendent of the Houses of Reform shall cause the inmates to be employed at
such labor and during such hours as may be designated by the Prison
Commissioners of Kentucky , and he shall pay into the State Treasury the
proceeds of the labor of the inmates , and all other income and receipts of
the institution as they are received by him . [ Acts 1914 , p . 154. ]
SEC . 2095a . Subsec . 20 .
2. Payment of expenses- itemized accounts . The expenses of said
institution , including the salaries of all the employes , shall be paid out
of the State Treasury upon a warrant drawn by the Auditor . The Super-
intendent thereof shall , at the end of each month , certify to the Board of
Prison Commissioners all bills , accounts and other indebtednesses and
expenses of said institution on behalf of the inmates thereof incurred
during the preceding month , including the salaries of the officers and
employes thereof , and shall furnish said Board itemized statements of
all such claims , and upon approval thereof by the Board of Prison Com-
missioners , certified by the chairman thereof, the Auditor of Public Ac-
counts shall draw his warrant in favor of the claimant therefor on the
State Treasurer , and the same shall be paid . [ Acts 1914 , p . 155. ]
Under Act 1912 , Chap . 136 claimants were held entitled to interest only from June
14 , 1910 , and not from the date of the accrual of their claim , the word " items " referring
to the several claims themselves . Bosworth v. Wolfe & Son , 159 Ky. 128, 166 S. W. 796 .
SEC . 2095a . Subsec . 20.
3. Requisites before employing persons-Governor to approve . Be-
fore the Board of Prison Commissioners shall be authorized to appoint or
employ any person to be assigned to said House of Reform , they shall
present to the Governor a written statement setting forth the necessity
for the employment of such person , the duties to be performed by such
person , and the amount said person is to receive for the services to be
performed , and they shall also state whether the person so employed is to
receive board and lodging . If the Governor approves the employment ,
he shall so indicate it by his written indorsement on said statement , which
shall be filed with the Auditor of Public Accounts . [ Acts 1914 , p . 155. ]
SEC . 2095a . Subsec . 20.
4. Farm and dairy products to be used . It shall be lawful for said
Superintendent to use and apply in kind to the maintenance of the said
institution and the inmates thereof , any and all the products of the farm ,
dairy and other departments or industries of the institution . [ Acts 1914 ,
p. 155. ]

SEC. 2978b .
24. Board may borrow money . The Board shall have power to
borrow money on the credit of the Board in anticpation of the revenue
from school taxes for the fiscal year in which the same is borrowed and
to pledge said school taxes for the payment of the principal and interest
of said loan : Provided , that the interest paid shall in no case exceed six
per cent . per annum and the principal shall in no case exceed fifty per
cent . of the anticipated revenue . [Acts 1910 , p . 15. ]
SEC . 2978b .
25. Tax to be levied by General Council . To raise money for the
maintenance of the schools the General Council shall annually cause to be
levied and collected a tax of not less than thirty - six cents ( .36 ) on each
one hundred ( $ 100.00 ) dollars of property assessed for taxation for city
purposes . Upon the completion of the assessment of property for taxation ,
the amount levied as above shall annually be passed to the credit of the
school fund , upon the books of the city, and the said amount , as collected ,
shall be paid over to the Board by the Treasurer of the city , in regular
monthly installments , the first payment to be made within one week after
the collection of said amount shall have been commenced and the other
763
SEC . 2978b . MUNICIPALITIES FIRST CLASS .
payments to be made weekly thereafter in current money by the said
Treasurer as collected . [ Acts 1910 , p . 15. ]
SEC . 2978b .
26. City's portion of State funds . For the maintenance of the schools
there shall be appropriated the sum or sums which may be received from
year to year as the city's portion of the school fund of this Common-
wealth . [ Acts 1910 , p . 16. ]
SEC . 2978b .
27. Escheated property to vest in Board . So much real or mixed
property in the city which , from alienage , defect of heirs , failure of kin-
dred or other causes , shall escheat to the Commonwealth of Kentucky , shall
vest in the Board for the use and benefit of the common schools . Said
Board may , in the name of the Commonwealth , for the use and benefit
of the common schools of the city , by its President or other officers to
be designated by it, enter upon and take possission of said property or
sue for and recover the same by an action at law or in equity , and with-
out office found . The Board may sell and convey any of such property
by warranty deed or otherwise . [ Acts 1910 , p . 16. ]
SEC . 2978b .
28. Tax officers to enforce existing laws . All officers of any city
of the first class , and of the State , concerned with the assessment and
collection of taxes , fines and penalties shall perform such duties relating
to the levying and collection of school taxes and the collection of such
fines and penalties , and the payment thereof to said Board for school pur-
poses , as are now imposed by the existing laws upon such officers in
relation to the levy and collection of school taxes and the collection of
fines and penalties payable to the school funds ; and nothing in this Act ,
unless inconsistent therewith , shall be construed as repealing any existing
law providing for the assessment and collection of school taxes in such
city ; and all powers and duties conferred by existing law upon any
Board in relation thereto shall be continued in the Board created by this
Act . [ Acts 1910 , p . 16. ]
SEC . 2978b .
29. Expert accountants to be employed . At the close of each fiscal
school year the Mayor of such city shall appoint one or more expert
accountants , who shall examine the books , accounts and vouchers of the
Secretary and Treasurer , Business Director , and all other departments
of expenditures of the Board , and shall make due report thereof to the
Mayor and Board of Education of such city . All the officers and em-
ployes of the Board shall produce and submit to such accounts for exam-
ination all books , papers , documents , vouchers and accounts in their office
belonging to the same or thereto pertaining , and shall in every way assist
said accountants in their work . In the report to be made by said ac-
countants they may make any recommendation they deem proper as to the
764
MUNICIPALITIES -FIRST CLASS . SEC . 2978b .
business methods of such officers and employes . A reasonable compensa-
tion for such services shall be paid by the Board . [ Acts 1910 , p . 16. ]
SEC . 2978b .
30. Kindergarten , manual and normal departments may be estab-
lished . The Board shall have power to establish and maintain kinder-
gartens for children from four to six years of age , high schools , manual
training schools and a normal school and normal training classes for the
purposes of training teachers to fill positions in the schools of the city,
and to this end it may prescribe rules and regulations for the government
of such schools , and as in other cases it may employ the principals and
other teachers necessary for their efficient management . [Acts 1910 ,
p. 16. ]
SEC . 2978b .
31. White and colored schools to be kept separate . The Board shall
provide , maintain and support separate schools wherein all colored chil-
dren , who are bona fide residents of said city, between the ages of six
and twenty years , may be taught in like manner as herein provided for
white children . Said schools for colored children shall be entitled to
the same benefits , to be governed by the same rules and regulations , and be
subject to the same restrictions as the schools herein provided for the
white children . [Acts 1910 , p . 16. ]
SEC . 2978b .
32. The Board shall prescribe the necessary qualifications and mode
of examination for applicants for admission to the various schools , and
may furnish text books and necessary school supplies to pupils free of
charge under such rules and regulations as it may adopt . [ Acts 1910 ,
p. 16. ]
SEC . 2978b .
33. No formula of religious belief shall be taught or inculcated,
nor shall any class or any text book be used which reflects on any reli-
gious denomination . [ Acts 1910 , p . 18. ]
