CHAPTER 81 .
AN ACT to prohibitand provide penaltiesfor the manu-
facture, sale, transportation or other dispositionof
spirituous, vinous, malt or intoxicatingliquors except
for sacramental, medicinal, scientificor mechanical pur-
poses in the Commonwealth of Kentucky and to regulate
the manufacture , saleand transportationof alcohol for
non -beverage purposes thereunder.
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssembly oftheCom-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That it shallbe unlawful to manufacture
sell, barter, give away , or keep for sale, or trans-
port, spirituous, vinous, malt or intoxicatingliq-
uors except for sacramental, medicinal, scientific
or mechanical purposes in the Commonwealth of
Kentucky .
§ 2. On a firstconviction for a violationof any
provisionsof thisAct, except for the violationof
a provisionforwhich a particularpenaltyisherein
provided ,the defendant or defendants shallbe fined
not lessthan $50.00 nor more than $300.00, and
ifpersons, shallin addition, be imprisoned in the
county jailfornot lessthan thirty,nor more than
sixty days .
Upon a second convictionfora violationof any
provisionsof thisAct, except Sections11, 15 and
20 to 31, inclusive, the defendant or defendants,
if persons, shallbe confined in the penitentiary
for not less than one year , nor more than three
years, and for the third and each subsequent con-
viction, the person or personsshallbe imprisoned
in the penitentiarynot lessthan five nor more
than ten years . Ifthe defendant be a corporation,
for the second offense, a fine shall be imposed of
not lessthan $1,000.00or more than $5,000.00and
for the third and each succeeding offense, a fine
shallbe imposed in the discretionof the jury,but
not lessthan $5,000.00.
§ 3. Every personknowingly aidingor abetting
any person, firm or corporationin the violation
ofany ofthe provisionsofthisAct ,shallbe deemed
a principaland punished as such.
§ 4. No witness in a trialfor a violation of
thisAct shallbe permitted to refuseto answer any
question because the answer willincriminate him-
self,but hisevidenceshallnot be used againsthim
in any subsequent proceedings, and such witness
shallnot be prosecutedfor any offencedisclosed
in such testimony .
§ 5. The articlesenumerated in this section
shall not, after having been manufactured and
prepared for the market , be subjectto the provi-
sionsof thisAct ,includingthe provisionsrelating
to the keeping of records,the giving of notice,and
the filingof statementsin the county courtclerk's
office,ifthey correspondto the followingdescrip-
tionsand limitations,namely :
(a) Denatured alcoholor denatured rum pro-
duced and used as provided by laws and regula-
tions now or hereafter in force .
(b) Medicinal preparationsmanufactured in
accordancewith formulasprescribedby the United
States Pharmacopeia , National Formulary or the
American Instituteof Homeopathy that are unfit
for use for beverage purposes .
(c) Patented, patent and proprietarymedi-
cines that are unfit for use for beverage purposes .
(d) Toilet, medicinal, and antisepticprepara-
tions and solutions that are unfit for beverage
purposes .
(e) Flavoring extracts and syrups that are
unfit for use as a beverage , or for intoxicatingbev-
erage purposes .
(f) Vinegar and preservedsweet cider.
(g) Wine forsacramentalpurposes.
(h) Alcohol, medicated according to such for-
mulas as willrender it unfitfor beverage purposes
and which isto be sold for legitimateexternal use.
(i) Alcohol for mechanical and scientificpur-
poses ifunfitfora beverage.
(j) Any person who manufactures, purchases
or possessesany of the articlesmentioned in this
section, or preparationsfitfor beverage purposes
which are authorized to be manufactured , may be
used in the manufacture of other preparations
compounded in accordance with formula pre-
scribedby the United States Pharmacopeia , Na-
tional Formulary or the American Instituteof
Homeopathy , which preparationswhen so manu-
factured are unfit for beverage purposes , or in
the manufacture of patented, patent and proprie-
tary or other medicines, or for physicians' pre-
scriptions, which are unfit for use for beverage
purposes, may purchase and possess liquorsfor
that purpose, but he shallgive bond as provided
in Section17 to the Commonwealth of Kentucky
that such liquorsshallbe used only for the purpose
mentioned herein, and he shallkeep a record of
the amount of the liquors so manufactured each
day . Said records to be open to the inspection
of the county attorney of the county and to the
Commonwealth's attorney of the districtwherein
such person resides.
No such manufacturer shall sell, use or dispose
of any liquor otherwise than as an ingredient of
the articles authorized to be manufactured there-
from . No more alcohol shall be used in the man-
ufacture of any syrup, extract or the articles
named in paragraphs b, c and d of this section
which may be used forbeverage purposesthan the
quantity necessary for the extraction or solution
of the elements contained therein and for the
preservation of the article.
Any person who shallknowingly sellany of the
articlesmentioned in paragraphs a, b, c and d of
this sectionfor beverage purposes or any extract
or syrup for intoxicatingbeverage purposes, or
who shall sell any of the same under circum-
stances from which the seller might reasonably
deduce the intentionofthe purchaser to use them
for such purpose, or shallsellany beverage con-
taining one -half of one per centum or more of
alcoholby volume in which any extract,syrup or
other articleis used as an ingredient,shallbe sub-
ject to the penaltiesprovided in thisAct .
Nothing in thisAct shallprevent the manufac-
ture or saleof wine for sacramental purposes in
accordance with the provisionsof the National
Prohibition Act .
Alcohol for mechanical and scientificpurposes
may be secured from persons authorized to manu-
facture and sellsuch alcohol under the provi-
sions of the National Prohibition Act .
§ 6. All persons who are convicted under this
Act and receivea fineor jailsentenceas punish-
ment shallserveout the judgment at hard labor
at the rate of One Dollar per day of the unpaid
fineor jailsentence.
§ 7. No trick, device, subterfugeor pretense
shallbe allowed to evade the operation or defeat
the purpose of this law .
§ 8. Any person,firmor corporationknowingly
or intentionallyrenting,hiring,or lettingor lend-
ing any house , building, or other structure or pre-
mises, or any boat or other watercraft,aircraftor
any car, truck, wagon or other vehicle, or the ani-
mal or animals used in hauling or propellingthe
same , to another or others, for the purpose of vio-
latingany provisionsof thisAct ,shallbe considered
guilty of a nuisance and of a violationof thisAct ,
and the property so used shallbe forfeitedand
soldas ifthe unlawfulact had been committed by
him or them in person .
But nothing in this Act shall be construed so
as to make it unlawful to possess liquors in one's
privatedwellingwhile the same is occupied and
used by him as hisdwellingonly and such liquors
need not be reported, provided such liquorsare
for the use only for the personalconsumption of
the owner thereofand his family residingin such
dwelling, and for his bona fideguests when enter-
tained by him therein; and the burden of proof
shallbe upon the possessorin any actionconcern-
ing the same to prove that such liquorwas law-
fullyacquired, possessed and used .
§ 9. Whenever a nuisanceiskept,committed ,
maintained or exists as defined in this Act , the
Commonwealth's Attorney or County Attorney,
or any citizenof the county wherein such nuisance
exists, may maintain an action in equity in the
name of the Commonwealth of Kentucky upon
the relationof such attorney or citizen to forfeit
such property and to perpetuallyenjointhe said
nuisance, the person or personscommitting, con-
ducting or maintaining the same ,and the owner or
agent of the building, ground, vehicle, animal,
boat , or other water craft, aircraftin connection
with which the nuisance is committed . In such
actionthe court,or judge in vacation, shallupon
the presentationof a petitionthereforalleging
that the nuisance or commission of such nuisance
exists,or has been maintained or committed ,grant
a temporary injunction,without bond ,ifthe exist-
ence or commission of such nuisance be made to
appear to the satisfactionof the court or judge,
by evidence in the form of affidavit, depositions,
oral testimony or otherwise as the complainant
may elect. Three days'noticeshallbe given the
defendantofthehearingoftheapplication. When
an injunctionhas been granted,itshallbe binding
on the defendant throughout the Commonwealth
of Kentucky , and any violationof the provisions
of the injunctionherein provided shallbe a con-
tempt as hereinafterprovided .
§ 10. In such action evidence of the general
reputationof the place shallbe admissible. If
the complaint isfiledby a citizen, itshallnot be
dismissed, except upon a sworn statement made
by the complainant and his attorney, setting
forth the reasons why the action should be dis-
missed, and the dismissalapproved by the Com-
monwealth or County Attorney in writingor in
open court. If the court is of the opinion that
the action ought not be dismissed, it may direct
the Commonwealth or County Attorney to pros-
ecute said action to judgment ; and if the action
is continued more than one term of court, any
citizenmay be substitutedfor the complaining
party and prosecutesaidactionto judgment .
§ 11. That in case of the violationof any in-
junctiongranted under the provisionsof thisAct,
the court, or, in vacation, a judge thereof, may
summarily try and punish the offender. The pro-
ceedings shallbe commenced by filingwith the
clerkof the court an affidavit,settingout the al-
legedfactsconstitutingsuch violation,upon which
the court or judge shallcause an order of arrest
to issue, under which the defendant shall be ar-
rested. The trialmay be had upon affidavits, or
eitherparty may at any stageof the proceedings
demand the production and oral examination of
the witnesses. A party found guiltyof contempt
under the provisionsof thisaction, shallbe pun-
ished by a fineof not lessthan $200.00 nor more
than $1000.00,or imprisonment in the county jail
not lessthan three nor more than sixmonths or by
both fineand imprisonment.
§ 12. That if the existence of the nuisance be
establishedin an action as provided in thisAct ,
an order of abatement shall be entered as a part
of the judgment in the case, which order shall
direct the removal from the building or place of
all fixtures, furnitureor movable property used
in conducting the nuisance, and shallorder the
salethereof in the manner provided for the sale of
chattelsunder execution, and the effectualclosing
of the building or place against its use forany
purpose ,and so keeping itclosedfor a period of one
year , unless sooner released. If any person shall
break, enter or use a building, erectionor place
so directedto be closedhe shallbe punished as
for contempt ,as provided in the preceding section.
The sheriff shall be allowed for sales hereunder
the same fees as allowed for sales under execution .
For all other services hereunder the sheriff shall
be allowed a reasonablefee by the court, to be
taxed as a part of the costs in the action; provided
that no injunctionshallissueagainst an owner ,
nor shall an order be entered requiring that any
buildingor apartment or any place be closed or
kept closedifitappears that such owner and his
agent have in good faithendeavored to prevent
such nuisance. Nothing in this Act contained
shallauthorize any reliefrespectingany other prop-
erty than that in which a nuisance exists.
§ 13. That the proceedsofthesaleof allprop-
erty, as provided in the preceding sections, shall
be appliedfirstto the payment of the costsof the
action and abatement , the balance remaining, if
any , shall be paid to the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky and be credited to the General Expenditure
Fund .
§ 14. If the owner , agent ot lessee, of any
building, erection, place or ground or property of
any kind, against which an injunctionhas been
issued, appears and pays allcostsof the proceed-
ings and filesa bond with surety to be approved
by the clerk, qualifiedas required by Section 684
of the Civil Code of Practice, in the fullvalue of
the property to be ascertained by the court, or,
invacation,by the judge thereof,conditionedthat
he willimmediately abate said nuisance and pre-
vent the same from being maintained or kept
within a period of one year thereafter, the court,
or, in vacation, the judge, may be satisfiedof his
good faith, order the premises which have been
closed,or otherpropertyinvolved,under the order
of abatement to be released to said owner and said
order of abatement cancelled so far as the same
may relateto said property; and ifsaid bond be
given and coststhereinpaid beforejudgment and
order of abatement , the action shallbe thereby
abated as to said property . The release of the
property under the provisionsof thissectionshall
not releaseitfrom any judgment , lienor liability
to which itmay be otherwisesubjectby law.
§ 15. It shallbe the duty of every person who
proposes to manufacture or sellany liquorscom-
ing within the provisionsof thisAct , except as
provided in Section6 of thisAct, before he shall
manufacture or sellany such liquors, to filewith
the county court clerkof the county wherein he
proposes to manufacture or sellsuch liquors, his
sworn statement of intentionso to do , which shall
contain the followinginformation :
His intentionto manufacture or sellsuch liquors
and the kind thereof .
The particular place where such liquors are to
be manufactured or sold .
Ifany person shallmanufacture or sellany such
liquorsbeforethe filingof hisdeclarationof inten-
tion so to do , or before executing a bond as here-
inafterprovided, with the county court clerk, he
shall be fined not less than one hundred dollars
nor more than fivehundred dollarsor imprisoned
in the county jailnot lessthan six months nor
more than one year or both so finedand imprisoned
in the discretionof the jury and every day on
which he shallmanufacture,sellor disposeof any
such liquors, shallbe deemed a separateoffense.
No such liquors shallbe manufactured or sold
by any person at any place other than that set
out in his declaration of intention .
§ 16. Before any person shallmanufacture any
spirituous, vinous, malt or intoxicatingliquor
coming within the provisionsof thisAct , he shall
execute bond in the sum of $1,000.00with good
surety,payable to the Commonwealth ofKentucky ,
to be approved by the county court clerk; which
said bond shall be executed and filed in the office
of the county court clerkof the county in which
said liquorsare to be manufactured or sold. Said
bond shallbe conditionedthatsaidperson shallnot
manufacture, sellor dispose of such liquorsin
violationof any of the provisionsof this Act .
Upon convictionof any person of any offensepro-
vided in thisAct , the said bond shallbe forfeited
to the Commonwealth of Kentucky .
§ 17. Beforeany personotherthan a manufac-
turer shallsellor dispose of any spirituous,vinous ,
malt or intoxicatingliquor coming within the pro-
visions of this Act , he shall execute bond in the
sum of $1,000.00with good surety,payable to the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , to be approved by
the county clerk; which said bond shall be exe-
cuted and filedin the officeof the county court
clerk of the county in which said liquors are to
be sold . Said bond shall be conditioned that such
liquorswillnot be soldor disposedof in violation
of any of the provisionsof thisAct . Upon con-
victionof any such person of any offenseas provided
in this Act the said bond shall be forfeited to the
Commonwealth of Kentucky .
§ 18. All persons manufacturing any spiritu-
ous , vinous , malt or intoxicating liquor coming
within the provisionsof thisAct , except as pro-
vided inSection6 of thisAct ,shallfilein the office
of the county court clerkof the county in which
such liquorsare made , a sworn statement, show-
ing the amount , kind and qualityof the liquors
so manufactured and itslocation, and ifany has
been sold, the amount sold, the date of each sale
and the name and address of the person to whom
it has been sold. If none has been sold, the re-
port shallso state. This reportshallbe made and
filedon the firstday ofJuly and the thirty-firstday
of December of each year . Such persons so man-
ufacturingsuch liquors,except as provided in Sec-
tion6 of thisAct ,shallkeep a recordshowing the
amount , kind and quantity of such liquors,the
amount sold,the name and address of the persons
to whom any such liquors are sold, and the dates
of allsuch sales, which record shallbe open to the
inspectionof the county attorney of the county
and the Commonwealth's attorney of the district
in which such liquorsare manufactured, at all
business hours of any day .
§ 19. All persons, other than manufacturers,
who sellor dispose of any spirituous, vinous , malt
or intoxicatingliquorscoming within the provi-
sionsof thisAct , except as provided in Section6
of thisAct ,shallkeep a record,showing the amount
kind and quantity of such liquors, and the amount
sold and the name and address of the persons to
whom any such liquorsshallbe sold, or disposed
of, and the dates of allsuch salesor dispositions,
which record shall be open to the inspection of
the county attorneyof the county and the Com-
monwealth's attorney of the districtin which such
liquorsare sold,at allbusinesshours of any day .
All such personsother than manufacturers,who
sellor disposeof liquorswithin the provisionsof
thisAct ,exceptas providedinSection6 ofthisAct ,
shallfilein the officeof the county court clerkof
the county in which such liquorsare sold, or dis-
posed of,a sworn statement,showing the amount ,
kind and qualityof the liquorssold, the dates of
such sales, the amount sold, and the name and
address of the persons to whom sold. Ifnone has
been sold, the report shallso state; such reports
shallbe made and filedon March 31, June 30,
September 30 and December 31 of each year.
§ 20. Physicians may issue and pharmacists
may fillprescriptionsfor intoxicatingliquors, un-
der the restrictions of the National Federal law .
§ 21. Every physicianwho issuesprescriptions
under thisAct shallkeep duplicatesof same on
filein alphabeticalorderat hisofficefortwo years
afterthe date thereof; said prescriptionsshallbe
open to the inspectionof the county attorney of
the county and the Commonwealth's attorneyof
the district, in which such physicianresides.
§ 22. No saleor dispositionof such liquorsas
definedherein,shallbe made by any person upon
or because of any physician'sprescription, unless
such prescriptionshallstate the name and address
of the patient,the druggist or pharmacist to whom
addressed, the amount required, that the physi-
cian isin personalattendanceon saidpatient,and
the name and address of the physicianwho pre-
scribesthe liquor, and that the alcoholicprepara-
tionprescribedisnecessaryinthe propertreatment
of said ailment of said patient and the date
thereof. All such prescriptionsshallbe marked
cancelledand filedand kept by the person mak-
ing the salefor two years afterthe date of the sale
and shallat no time be refilled. Such prescrip
tionsshallbe subjectto inspectionat any business
hour of any day by the county attorney of the
county and the Commonwealth's attorney of the
districtin which such liquorsare sold. No per-
son other than a regularlicensedand practicing
physicianshallissueany such prescription.
§ 23. No prescriptionshallprovide for more
than one pint of such liquors,nor shallany physi-
cian prescribefor more than one pint of such liq-
uors to any person at any time, nor at intervals
of lessthan ten (10) days. If any person shall
procure any such liquorsupon such prescriptions
at intervalsof lessthan ten (10) days, he shallbe
finednot lessthan fiftydollars($50.00) nor more
than one hundred dollars($100.00) or imprisoned
in the county jailfor not lessthan ten (10) days
nor more than sixtydays ,or both so finedand im-
prisonedin the discretionof the jury.
§ 24. Upon the firstor second convictionof
any druggist, pharmacist or physicianfor violat-
ing any of the provisionsof thisAct , the judg-
ment of conviction,in additionto allother penal-
tiesimposed in thisAct ,may , in the discertionof
the trialcourt, provide for the suspensionof the
licenseof such physician, druggistor pharmacist,
for the periodof one year; and for the thirdcon-
viction, shallprovide for the suspension of the
licenseof such physician, druggistor pharmacist,
for the period of one year .
§ 25. Any person who shallforgea physician's
prescriptionor attempt to use such prescription
in obtaining liquorsfrom any person authorized
to sellsuch liquors,or other person, shallbe pun-
ished by confinement in the county jailnot less
than sixty days nor more than one year for such
offense .
§ 26. It shall be the duty of the Auditor to
prepare, by and with the advice of the attorney
general, allblanks and forms provided for here-
under. Upon applicationhe shall furnish any
person with a sufficientquantity of the same .
§ 27. For each manufacturer's report filed,
the County Court Clerk shallreceivea fee of one
dollar .
For each reportfiledby any person other than
a manufacturer, the County Court Clerk shallre-
ceive a fee of fiftycents.
For each declaration of intention to either man-
ufactureor sell, filedby any person, the County
Court Clerk shall receive a fee of one dollar .
All such feesshallbe paid by the person filing
such reports and declarationsof intention.
§ 28. Any personwho shallin any publicplace
or in or upon any passengercoach,streetcar,or in
or upon any vehiclecommonly used for the trans-
portation of passengers, or in or about any depot ,
platform, waiting stationor room , drink any in-
toxicatingliquorof any kind, or if any person
shallbe drunk or intoxicatedin any public or
private road or in any passenger coach , street
car, or other public place or building, or at any
publicgathering, or ifany person shallbe drunk
or intoxicatedor shalldisturb the peace of any
person, he shallbe guiltyof a misdemeanor and
upon convictionthereofshallbe punished by fine
of not lessthan $10.00or more than $100.00, or
by imprisonment for not lessthan fivedays or
more than thirtydays, or by both such fineand
imprisonment .
§ 29. Every railroadconductor is hereby au-
thorizedand empowered to exercisein every county
of thisStatethrough which the trainin charge of
such conductor passes allthe common law and
Statutory powers in their respective counties for
the purpose of enforcing the provisions of the last
preceding section, and to arrestoffendersagainst
any such provisions,and in so doing are actingfor
the State and not as employes of the railroadcom-
pany . Arrestsfor offensesagainstany such pro-
visionsmay be made by such conductor without
warrant ;and persons so arrested shallbe delivered
by him to some justiceof the peace,policejudge,
sheriff, constableor policeofficerat some station
or place within the county in which the offense
was committed ,fortrialas provided by law; pro-
vided that ifthe trainshallhave passed from the
county in which such offense was committed and
for which such arrestshallhave been made , then
such conductor shalldeliverthe person so arrested
to some officerof another county,and he shallbe
held and deliveredto some officerof the county
in which the offense was committed to be there
held for trialas provided by law. Provided that
any railroadconductor who is actuallyengaged
in the discharge of his duty and makes a legal
arrestunder the provisionsof this section, then
and in that case the railroadcompany employing
him shallnot be liablefordamages to the person
or persons for such arrest.
§ 30. Any officer, agent, or employe of the
railroadcompany ,expresscompany ,or othercom-
mon carrier, who shallknowingly carry or de-
liverany liquors, the saleof which is prohibited
by thisAct , to or for any person to be sold, bar-
tered, given away , or otherwisefurnishedin vio-
lationof thisAct,shallbe guiltyofa misdemeanor ,
Any officer,agent,or employe who shallknowingly
deliverany such liquorto any person other than
the person to whom itisconsignedand without a
written order in such instanceof the consignee
thereofshallbe guiltyof a misdemeanor ,and upon
conviction shallbe fined not lessthan $50.00 nor
more than $500.00.
§ 31. Any judge or justiceof the peace,when
affidavitsof any State or federal officerand one
other reputablecitizen, or when the affidavitsof
two reputable citizens, are filedwith him describ-
ing the premisesas nearlyas may be,where intox-
icatingliquorsare soldor suspectedof being sold
or disposed of, in violationof thisAct , may by
hiswarrant cause any house or buildingor other
placeto be searchedby nightor by day forthe de-
tectionof any intoxicatingliquorswhich are kept
there for the purpose of saleor other disposition,
in violation of this Act , and if admission be not
given on demand made ,the officeror other person
in charge of the warrant shall force an entrance
into such house , building or other place and seize
any intoxicatingliquors and arrest the keeper or
person in charge, of such house, buildingother
place or intoxicatingliquors, and carry such per-
son or personsbefore the judge or justiceof the
peace issuingthe warrant or before some other
judge or justiceof the peace to be dealt with ac-
cording to law .
§ 32. Upon convictionof the personor persons
in charge of the house,building,otherplaceor the
intoxicatingliquors,the judge,justiceof the peace
or court trying such offender or offendersshallad-
judge the intoxicatingliquorsso seizedcontraband
and confiscate the same at once unless notice of
an appeal or an appeal of the case be taken . When
notice of appeal of the case is given or an appeal
taken thejudge,justiceofthe peaceor courttrying
the case shallkeep such intoxicatingliquorsin his
possessionuntilthe case isfinallydetermined and
he shall then dispose of such intoxicatingliquors
as the finaljudge may determine. Upon final
judgment of convictionsuch liquorsshallbe either
destroyed or sold to some person authorized to use
such liquorsforlawfulpurposes and the proceeds
of such saleshallbe appliedas provided inSection
Fourteen (14) of thisAct .
§ 33. The remedies provided for in the last
two precedingsectionsshallbe in additionto and
not exclusiveof the other remedies provided by
law in this Act or otherwise .
§ 34. It shallbe the duty of the courts and
judges of thisCommonwealth and allofficersand
conservatorsof the peace to enforceallthe pro-
visions of thisAct and of the Acts of the Congress
of the United States enacted to enforce the Eight-
eenth Amendment to the United States Consti-
tution .
§ 35. Nothing in thisAct shallprevent the
manufacture, sale, transportationor deliveryof
intoxicatingliquorsby manufacturers, wholesale
druggists or retaildruggists, having permits issued
under the regulationsprovided for the enforce-
ment of the Act of Congress known as the Na-
tionalProhibitionAct, or the sale, transportation
and delivery by manufacturers or wholesale drug-
gists or retaildruggists to other manufacturers ,
wholesaledruggistsor to retaildruggists;provided
however ,that such manufacturers ,wholesale drug-
gistsand retaildruggistshave permits to sellor to
purchase under the provisionsof said National
ProhibitionAct , and have complied with allthe
provisionsof thisAct .
§ 36. All laws or partsof laws in conflictwith
thisAct are hereby repealed.
§ 37. Ifany section,paragraph,or part of this
Act shall be held to be unconstitutional, the re-
mainder of this Act shall continue effective and
enforceablenotwithstandingsuch decision.
§ 38. This Act shall take effecton and after
July 1, 1920.
Approved March 23, 1920.

CHAPTER 90 .
AN ACT relatingto vehicles; regulatingtheir use and
operation upon the public highways of this Common-
wealth; providing for the registrationand licensingof
motor vehicles; fixingthe amount of the license, and
manner of payment thereof; providing for the registra-
tionand licensingof operatorsof motor vehiclesand the
amount of such license; providing a method of registra-
tion of motor vehicles;preventingillegaltrafficin motor
vehicles;providing penalty for the violationof thisAct ,
and repealingany and allconflictinglaws.
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. (a) Definitions. Whenever and where-
ever the word "vehicle" isused in thisAct ,itshall
include all agencies for the transportationof
persons or property over and upon the public
highways of thisCommonwealth , and allvehicles
passing over or upon said highways , excepting
road rollers,and such vehiclesas travelexclusively
on rails, and whenever and wherever the word
" automobile " is used , it shall include allvehicles
that are propelledotherwise than by muscular
power , exceptingroad rollersand such vehiclesas
travel exclusivelyon rails.
(b) Whenever and wherever the word "Com-
mission" is used herein, it shall mean the State
Tax Commission , and whenever and wherever
the word "clerk" isused herein, itshallmean the
clerkof a county court.
(c) Whenever and wherever the word "chauf-
feur" isused herein,itshallmean a person whose
businessor occupation, in whole or in part, isthe
operation of an automobile for compensation,
wages or hire.
(d ) Whenever and wherever the word "manu-
facturer" is used herein, it shallmean any indi-
vidual, partnership, corporationor company en-
gaged in the business or occupation of manufactur-
ing or assembling automobiles, who will, under
normal business conditions during the year , manu-
facture or assemble as many as ten or more new
automobiles .
(e) Whenever and wherever the word "dealer"
isused herein, itshallmean any and allpersons,
partnerships, corporations, companies or agencies
engaged in the businessof purchasing, sellingor
distributingautomobiles in this Commonwealth .
(f) Whenever and wherever the word "high-
way " is used herein, it shallmean any and all
public highways , roads and passways, no matter
of what type of construction, and allboulevards,
parkways , streetsand publicalleysof any and all
incorporatedcitiesand towns,as wellas the same
in unincorporated towns and villagesof this Com-
monwealth .
(g) Whenever and wherever the word " oper-
ator" is used herein, itshallmean the person in
actual physicalcontrolof the guidance, starting
and stopping of a vehicle.
§ 2. (a) Registrationand Fees. Before the
owner of an automobile shalloperate, or be per
mitted to operate,same ,or shallpermit the opera-
tion of same upon any public highway , such
owner shallregisterwith the Commission ,through
the clerk in the county in which he resides, or in
the county in which the automobile is to be
operated,making applicationforsuch registration
to the clerkof such county on a blank to be fur-
nishedby the Commission through theclerk,which
applicationshallbe accompanied by a billof sale,
ifthe applicationbe forregistrationof a new car,
or by exhibitingthe owner's registrationreceipt,
ifsuch automobile has theretoforebeen registered,
and thereafterhe shallregisterhis automobile on
or beforethe firstday of January each and every
year. Provided, that in so far as the owner is
concerned, the registrationwith the clerk as re-
quired by law shallbe deemed to be a registration
with the Commission .
(b) Such applicationblank shallcontainblank
spacesfor,and the owner applyingforregistration
shallgive thereon, the following detailed informa-
tion: Owner's name and postofficeaddress,name
of manufacturer of the automobile ,motor number ,
car or chassisnumber , if any , model and year
number , horse power as rated by the Society of
Automobile Engineers, motive power , style, and
ifthe automobile be a truck, in additionto the
foregoing,theowner shallgivethetonnage capacity
as rated by the manufacturer. Each and every
applicationshallbe accompanied by the appro-
priatefeeand same shallbe as follows:
(c) Fees for Passenger Automobile. For each
motorcycle the registrationfee shallbe ten dollars.
Automobiles primarily designed for carrying
passengers and having provisionsfor not more
than seven passengers, including the operator,
shallbe classed as passenger automobiles , and the
annual registrationfeeforsame shallbe sixtycents
for each horse power of the vehicleregistered,to be
calculatedon the rating fixedby the Society of
Automobile Engineers .
(d ) Fees for Other Than Passenger Automo-
biles not included in subsection (c) above are
classifiedas trucks,and the annual registrationfee
shallbe as follows: Those having a capacity of
one thousand pounds or less, twenty-two dollars;
thosehaving a capacityofmore than one thousand
pounds and up to two thousand pounds , thirty
dollars; thosehaving a capacityof more than two
thousand pounds and up tothreethousand pounds ,
fortydollars;thosehaving a capacityof more than
three thousand pounds and up to four thousand
pounds , fiftydollars; those having a capacity of
more than four thousand pounds and up to five
thousand pounds , sixty dollars; those having a
capacityof more than fivethousand pounds and
up to sixthousand pounds , seventy dollars;those

and fifteenmiles an hour ,in each instance.
(7) For trucksequipped with ironor steeltires
and for trucks equipped with rubber tiresbut tow-
ing or trailingvehicleswith ironor steeltires,the
provisionsof paragraph (1), (2) and (3) above
shallgovern , except the respectivespeeds shallbe
six,eightand ten milesan hour,in each instance.
(8) Trucks with capacitiesas setout inpara-
graphs (4) and (5) pullingtrailersof such capa-
citythat the combined capacitieswould be equal
the capacitiesset out in paragraphs (5) or (6)
respectivelyshallbe governed by the provisions
of saidparagraphs (5) and (6).
(9) Nothing in the paragraph above shallap-
ply to vehiclesowned and operated by the fire,
police or hospitaldepartments of any munici-
pality.
§ 11. Right of Action Not Prejudiced.-Noth-
ing in thisAct shallbe construed as curtailingor
abridgingthe rightof any person to prosecutea
civilaction for damages by reason of injuriesto
person or property resultingfrom the negligent
use of vehicleson publichighways .
§ 12. Duty in Case ofAccident.- Any person,
who , while operatinga vehicleon a publichigh-
way , shallrun against, over, or into any other
person, vehicleor personalproperty in possession
of any other person in such manner as may injure
or damage such other person or property ,shallim-
mediately stop and ascertainthe extent of such
injury or damage and render such assistanceas
may be needed, includingthe carrying of such
person or occupants of such vehicle to the nearest
medical aid, ifsuch carryingisrequestedby the
person struck,or by any occupant ;and such opera-
tor, person or persons having or assuming author-
ityof such operator,or ownership of such vehicle,
shallgive the occupant of such vehicle, or person
struck, if requested, the registrationnumber of
such vehicle, ifany , alsothe name and addressof
the owner thereof and the names and addresses
of the occupant and operator, the total names not
to exceed fivein number , unless more be volunta-
rilygiven .
-
§ 13. Tampering With Vehicles or Parts
Thereof.- (a) No personshall,without the consent
of the owner of the person in controlthereof,tam-
per with any vehicle, or parts thereof, while the
same isstandingupon a publichighway .
(b ) Removing Parts. No person shallbreak,
injureor remove any part or partsor any acces-
soriesof any vehicle for any purpose whatsoever
against the willor without the consent of the owner
of such vehicle, whether maliciously or otherwise.
(c) Changing Motor Numbers .-No person
shallpurposely deface, change from the rightful
number , or make illegibleany motor or chassis
number of an automobile, nor shallany person
knowingly have in his possessionany automobile
having thereon or therein an altered, changed,
mutilatedor illegiblemotor number .
§ 14. Glass Throwing .-No person shallthrow
or deposit upon any public highway any glass
bottles,glass,nails,tacks,hoops,wire,cans or any
other substancelikelyto injureany person, ani-
mal or vehicle .
§ 15. Taking Vehicles Without Consent of
Owners . Any person who shallunlawfullytake,
drive or operate a vehiclewithout the knowledge
and consent of the owner shall be guilty of the
offenseof grand larceny,and punished as provided
by law in such cases.
§ 16. Revocation of Registrationand Duty of
Courts.- (a) In case the operator of a vehicle
is convictedof the violationof any of the provi-
sions of thisAct as many as four times within any
periodof six months , the commission shallforth-
with revoke the registrationreceiptof such person
ifhe be the owner or chauffeur of an automobile ,
and in case such offendingoperator isthe driver
of any other vehicle, the commission shallnotify
him that thereafterhe issubjectto the provisions
of subsection(b) hereof.
(b) Shall Not Operate. Whenever the owner
or the chauffeur of an automobile has had his reg-
istrationreceiptrevoked, as provided above, or
whenever the driverof any othervehiclehas been
notified by the commission of the violations of
thisAct , such person shallimmediately give up
registrationreceipt, number plates or badges as
the case may be,to the clerk, and such person so
notified, or whose registrationreceipt has been
revoked, shallnot operate or drive any vehicle
upon the public highways during a period of six
months after such revocation or notice; and no
clerkshallissuea registrationreceiptto any such
person untilthe expirationof such period.
(c) Duty of TrialCourt. It shallbe the duty
of every trialcourt,in every case in which a con-
victionbe had forthe violationof any of the pro-
visionsof thisAct,to transmitimmediately to the
commission, a copy of the judgment of conviction
giving the name and post officeaddress of the
person convicted.
§ 17. Duties of the Clerk. (a) It shallbe
the duty of the clerk in each county to see that
the provisionsof this Act in his county are en-
forced, and in so doing he shall:
(b ) Take allapplicationsas provided in this
Act .
(c) Issuethe receiptsprovided for in thisAct
on blanks furnished by the commission .
(d) Collectthe feesdue the State as provided
for in this Act .
(e) Distribute the registrationplates and
badges furnishedby the commission and keep a
complete record in hisofficeforthebenefitof the
publicof allsuch registrationsin his county, and
to notifythe owner or chauffeurof the receiptby
him of duplicate badges or plates.
(f) Remit and reporteach Monday to the com-
missionallmoneys collectedunder him during the
previousweek , togetherwith the duplicatesof all
receiptsissuedby him during the same period,all
checks to be made payable to the StateTreasurer.
(g) Account to the commission for allregis-
trationplates,badges and receiptforms consigned
to him , at such time or times as the commission
may direct; givethe commission timelynoticeof a
probable deficiencyof platesor other supplies.
§ 18. Dutiesofthe Commission .- (a) Itshall
be the duty of the commission to carry out the
provisionsof thisAct ,and in so doing shall:
(b) Furnish Blanks and Instructions. Pre-
pare and furnishto the clerk in each county a
good and sufficientsupply of allforms or blanks
provided for in thisAct , provided that the form
for receiptsshallbe designed for the writing of
triplicatecopies, the originalsof which, except
those to be used for duplicatesof lostreceipts,
shallbe numbered consecutivelyfor each county,
the second and thirdcopiesbearingthe same num-
ber as the original;and the colorsof allthreecop-
ies shall be different and the combination of colors
shall not be the same for consecutiveyears;
shallalsofurnisheach clerka listof horse power
ratingsof allautomobiles as determined by the
Societyof Automobile Engineers.
(c) Keep Record .-Keep a numerical record
of allregistrationnumbers issued in the State for
which they may use the second copy of receipt
forwarded by the clerkof each county,a recordof
motor numbers assigned owners under sub -section
(j) of Section 2. Also keep the copies of judg-
ments of convictions for violationsof this law , all
of which shallconstitutea public record.
(d -e) Furnish RegistrationPlates, etc. The
Commission shallfurnishto each clerkoriginally
each year upon estimate, and thereafterupon
requisitionat alltimes a sufficientsupplyof plates
for allclassesof vehiclesrequired to be registered.
Such plates shall be selected by the Commission
or some person under their direction, and shallbe
of proper and practicableform and size, and shall
contain such letteringand numbering as the com-
mission may deem to be proper, practicable and
efficientfor the intended purposes .
(f) Chauffeur Badges . Furnish a metal badge
for each chauffeur'sregistration, consecutively
numbered , with the letters"KY ." and the year
number thereon,and shallallota sufficientsupply
to the clerk in each county . Said badge shall be
of differentform or design for each year .
(g) Supply Not Later Than November 15.-
Registrationplates,badges and forms forthe suc-
ceedingyear in number equal to or greaterthan
the currentyear'sregistrationin that county shall
be delivered to the clerk in each county not later
than November fifteenth, and the commission,
with the assistanceof the clerk, shall estimate as
closelyas possiblethe increasein registrationand
make provisionthereforas soon aftersaid date
as possible.
(h) Lists. Furnish serialnumericallistsof all
registrationsand transfersto those who subscribe
for same on an annual basison multigraphed or
mimeographed sheets, beginning not later than
January fifteenth,and followedthereafterweekly.
These lists are to be furnished at a reasonable
price, but not to exceed seven and one-halfcents
per one hundred names . Separate county lists
may also be furnished subscribersin the same
manner as State Lists are furnished, the price
therefor not to exceed fifteen cents for one hun-
dred names .
(i) Dispositionof Funds . Receive allmoneys
forwarded by the clerk in each county and turn
over same to the Auditor for the benefit of the State
Road Fund ;and out of thisfund shallbe paid the
expenses of said commission incident to the en-
forcement of thisAct , said payment being made
in the manner provided by law for payment of
salariesand expenses .
(j) Settlements . Shall at the end of each fis-
calyear make a settlement of the accounts showing
the receiptsand expendituresand filesame with
the Auditor of Public Accounts for the State .
And they shallfurtherrequirean accountingfrom
the clerkin each county for allmoneys received
by him under the provisionsof thisAct ,afterthe
deduction of his fees under this Act , and for all
receipts, forms, plates and badges consigned to
him .
(k) Publication and Distributionof Act.-
Cause to be printed not lessthan one hundred
thousand copies of this Act and to distribute
through the clerkin each county a copy to each
person applyingforregistrationor transferof reg-
istration, and when such supply is exhausted,
shallcause additionalcopiesto be printed from
time to time as may be necessary.
(1) Shall assign motor number when applied
forunder Sub -section(j) of Section2,such motor
numbers to be distinctive,so as to show theirdes-
ignationby the commission.
§ 19. Arrests for Violation of Law . Any
peace officermay make arrestsfor violationor
violationsof thisAct in the following manner :
If the offensecommitted be a misdemeanor , the
peace officermay make the arrest:
(a) Without warrant if the offense be com-
mitted in his sight;
(b ) With warrant ifhe does not observe the
commission of the offense .
Ifthe offensebe a felony,the peace officermay
make the arrest without warrant if he has reason-
able grounds for believingthat an offenseamount-
ing to a felonyhas been committed .
If the arrest be for an offense amounting to a
felony, the officershallproceed with the arrested
person as in other felony cases.
If the arrest be for a misdemeanor , and the
arrest be made without warrant , the accused
may elect to be immediately taken before the
nearest court having jurisdiction, whereupon it
shall be the duty of the peace officerto so
take him . If the arrestedperson electnot to be
so taken, then it shallbe the duty of the peace
officerto require of the arrestedperson a bail
bond , in a sum not less than twice the amount
of the maximum fineprovided for the violation
of the law, and in cases where the penalty
carriesimprisonment, not lessthan ten times the
amount of the maximum fine. The condition of
the bond shallbe such that the arrestedperson
binds himself to appear in the courtof jurisdic-
tion at a time fixed in the bond , not , however , in
any caselaterthan sixdays from the day of arrest.
In case the arrestedperson failstoappear on the
day fixed,the bond shallbe forfeitedin the manner
as isprovided for the forfeitureof bonds in other
cases .
No officershallbe permittedto take a cash bond ,
but he may ,inhisjudgment ,requireor not require
surety on the bond .
The officerarresting and taking bond shall re-
port the same to the jurisdictionalcourt within
eighteen hours aftertaking such bond .
§ 20. (a) Penalties. Any person violating
the provisions,or any of them ,of Sections2,4,5,
7, 8,9, 10, 14, 16 and 17, or Sub -sections(a), (b)
or (c) of Section 3, shallbe deemed guiltyof a
misdemeanor , and upon convictionthereof shall
be punished by a fineofnot lessthan ten nor more
than one hundred dollars for each offense .
(b) Any person violatingthe provisionsof
Sections6, 12 or 13, or Sub -section(d) or (e) of
Section 3, or any of them , shallbe deemed guilty
of a misdemeanor , and upon convictionthereof
shallbe punished by a fineof not lessthan ten nor
more than two thousand dollars, or by imprison-
ment in the county jailfor not exceeding one year,
or by both such fineand imprisonment within or
to the maximum of both .
(c) The above Sub -sectionsshallnot be con-
strued in any wise as relatingto the penalty fixed
by Section15 of thisAct .
§ 21. Time Effective. This Act in allitsparts
and provisions shalltake effectas provided by the
Constitution and Laws ,except that so much there-
of as relatesto the registrationof automobiles and
chauffeurs shall not take effect and be in force un-
tilDecember 2, 1920
§ 22. Any and alllaws and parts of laws in
conflictherewith are hereby repealed
§ 23. Constitutionality. If any section, sub-
section, paragraph , sentence, clause or phrase of
this Act is for any reason held to be unconsti-
tutional or invalid, such holdings shall not affect
the validityof the remaining portionsof thisAct .
The General Assembly hereby declaresthat it
would have passed thisAct ,and each section,sub-
section, paragraph, sentence, clause or phrase
thereofirrespectiveof the fact that any one or
more othersections,sub-sections,paragraphs,sen-
tences, clauses and phrases be declared unconsti-
tutional, or invalid.
Approved March 23, 1920.

CHAPTER 94 .
AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and
maintenance of the various Departments , Boards , Com-
missions, Institutionsand Agencies of the State Govern-
ment , exceptfor the Legislativeand JudicialDepart-
ments and except for the common schools, for the fiscal
year ending June 30, 1921, and appropriatingmoney for
making permanent repairsand improvements for the
benefitof said Departments, Boards, Commissions,
Institutionsand Agencies; designating the funds and
sources from which said appropriationsare to be paid,
and prescribingthe manner in which same are to be paid.
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssembly of theCom-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That for the purpose of providing the
necessaryfunds for the payment of salaries, cost
of maintenance, operation and permanent im-
provements of each of the Departments , Boards ,
Commissions, Institutionsand Agencies of the
State Government named in this Act , for the
fiscalyear ending June 30, 1921, there is hereby
appropriatedout of the fund or funds specified
herein the various amounts herein shown .
§ 2. Out of the general expenditure fund pro-
duced by the annual levy of fifteencents, as now
provided by law,thereishereby appropriatedfor
the benefitof the Adjutant General'sDepartment
of the State for use for the fiscalyear ending June
30 , 1921 , the following sums for the following
purposes :
(a) For the payment of salariesand clerical
hire, $12,000.00.
(b) For the payment of travelingexpenses,
maintenance and operation, suppliesand repairs,
includingprintingand postage necessaryfor the
use of saidDepartment , $15,000.00.
(c) As an emergency fund for the use of said
Department , same to be expended only when an
emergency existsand upon the order and with
the approval of the Governor of the Common-
wealth ,$20,000.00.
§ 3. There is hereby appropriatedout of the
general expenditure fund ,for the use of the Attor-
ney General'sDepartment of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky for the fiscalyear ending June 30,
1921 ,the followingsums forthe following purposes :
(a) For salariesof the Attorney General,First,
Second , and Third Assistant Attorneys General
and Law Clerk,$ 14,900.00.
(b) For allstenographichelp,the salariestobe
determined by the Attorney General, $3,900.00.
(c) For necessary travelingexpenses of the
Department when engaged in the State'sbusiness,
printing,stamps and officesupplies,$1,250.00.
§ 4. There ishereby appropriatedout of the
generalexpenditurefund forthe use ofthe Depart-
ment of the Auditor of Public Accounts of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , for the fiscalyear
ending June 30, 1921, as hereinafterset out, the
followingsums for the following purposes :
(a) For salariesand clericalhire,$35,000.00.
(b) For printing, stamps and officesupplies,
$4,000.00.
§ 5. There is hereby appropriatedout of the
sums realizedfrom licenseson motor vehicles, for
the benefitof the Department of Motor Vehicles of
the Commonwealth of Kentucky , for the fiscal
year ending June 30, 1921,not exceedingone dol-
lar for each motor vehicle registered under the
provisionsof the law regulatingthe registrationof
motor vehicles in the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky ,same to be used for the payment of salaries,
clericalhire, travelingexpenses, printing, stamps,
officesupplies and licensetags.
§ 6. For the purpose of paying the expensesof
the Department of Banking of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky for the fiscalyear ending June 30,
1921, thereishereby appropriatedand ordered to
be paid out of the feesrealizedfrom an examina-
tion of sundry banks and buildingand loan asso-
ciations, as provided by law, the followingsums
for the following purposes :
(a) For the purpose of paying salaries,clerical
help, travelingexpenses, printing, stamps and
officesupplies,$35,000.00.
§ 7. There ishereby appropriatedout of the
generalexpenditurefund for the use of the State
Board of Control having charge of the charitable,
correctionaland penal institutionsof the Com-
monwealth ,forthe purpose of paying the existing
deficitand for the necessary expenditures for the
fiscalyear ending June 30, 1921, the following
amounts for the followingpurposes:
(a) For the purpose of paying the deficit
existingon the 5th day of January, 1920,incurred
in the conduct of said institutions under the con-
trolof said State Board of Control ,$206,581.68.
(b) For the purpose of paying the salaries,
clericalhire, travelingexpenses, printing, stamps
and necessarysuppliesforsaid Board of Control,
and the costof operation,maintenance, improve-
ments , repairsand alloperatingexpensesfor the
fiscalyear ending June 30, 1921, for the State
Reformatory at Frankfort , State Penitentiary at
Eddyville , Western State Hospital for the Insane
at Hopkinsville, Central State Hospital for the
Insane at Lakeland ,Eastern State Hospital for the
Insane at Lexington , Feeble-Minded Institute at
Frankfort, and the Houses of Reform , $ 1,996,-
688.00 .
§ 8. There ishereby appropriatedout of the
general expenditurefund, for the benefitof the
State Board of Election Commissioners for the
fiscalyear ending June 30, 1921, the following
sums forthe followingpurposes:
(a) For salariesand allclericalhire,$310.00.
(b ) For printing, stamps and necessary sup-
plies,$40.00.
§ 9. There is hereby appropriatedout of the
generalexpenditurefund,for the use of the State
Board of Health forthe fiscalyear ending June 30,
1921, the followingamounts to be used for the
following purposes :
(a) For the purpose of paying salaries,clerical
help,travelingexpenses,printing,stamps,supplies
and allother operatingexpenses, $76,300.00.
(b) For the payment to publichealth labora-
toriesat StateExperiment Station$18,000.00.
(c) For preventionof venerealdiseases, $27,-
000.00 .
(d) For preventionand treatmentoftrachoma,
$ 13,700.00.
§ 10. There ishereby appropriatedout of the
general expenditure fund, for the use of the
Department of Agriculture, Labor and Statistics
forthe fiscalyear ending June 30,1921,the follow-
ing amounts for the following purposes :
(a) For the purposes of paying allthe salaries
and clericalhireforsaidDepartment ,$11,700.00.
(b) For the purpose of paying the per diem ,
travelingexpenses and other expenses now allowed
by law to theStateBoard ofAgriculture,$2,700.00.
(c) For the purpose of paying allthe expenses
of the Department of Labor , under the said State
Department of Agriculture, Labor and Statistics,
as now allowed by law or as may hereafterbe
allowed by law , $ 9,000.00.
(d) For the purpose of paying allthe expenses
of the Immigration Branch (freeemployment ) of
said Department , as now allowed by law, or as
may hereafterbe allowedby law, $2,000.00.
(e) For the purposeofpaying forthestationery,
printing, officesupplies,equipment,telephoneand
telegraphbills, express, freightand hauling
chargesand postageofsaidDepartment ,$4,300.00.
(f) For the purpose of paying allthe expenses
for the fieldwork of said Department of Agricul-
ture, Labor and Statistics, now permitted and
allowedby law or as may hereafterbe authorized
by law , $ 15,000.00.
(g) For the purpose of defrayingthe expenses
of saidDepartment in collectingstatistics,as now
allowed by law or as may hereafterbe authorized
by law,$700.00.
(h ) For the purpose of paying the traveling
expenses of the Commissioner of Agriculture,
Labor and Statistics,as now authorizedby law or
as may hereafterbe authorizedby law, $1,000.00
(i) For the purposeof paying specialpremiums
which the said Department is now authorized by
law to pay , or which itmay hereafterby law be
authorizedto pay ,$4,000.00.
(j) For the purpose of creatingan emergency
and co-operativefund forthe use of said Depart-
ment , as now authorizedby law or as may here-
afterbe authorizedby law, $4,600.00,
§ 11. There ishereby appropriatedout of the
generalexpenditurefund,for the use of the State
Board of Agriculture,for the Kentucky State Fair,
forthe fiscalyear ending June 30,1921,the follow-
ing sums for the following purposes :
(a) For salaries, travelingexpenses, main-
tenance and operation,$ 10,000.00.
(b ) For premiums for the Kentucky State
Fair, $ 15,000.00.
(c) For the purpose of meeting othernecessary
expenses for the conduct of the Kentucky State
Fair, including additional premiums , all sums
realizedby the State Board of Agriculturefrom
the salesof concessions, admissions, advertising,
entry fees,stallrents,donations,exhibitors'tickets,

laws.summary: This statute requires candidates to submit an affidavit from two reputable electors of the same political party, affirming their qualifications and support for the party. This requirement can be seen as a mechanism that may have been used to restrict voting rights, particularly for Black Kentuckians, by imposing additional barriers to candidacy.

Provided, that the provisionsof Section 6 of

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 100 .
AN ACT to defineand prohibitcriminalsyndicalismand
seditionand to prohibitconduct,publications,assemblies
and the use of property for the promotion of criminal
syndicalismand sedition, prescribingthe dutiesof peace
officersand providingpenalties.
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. "Criminal syndicalism" ishereby defined
to be the act of committing , aiding or counseling
crime, physical violence, arson, destruction of
property ,intimidation,terrorism or other unlawful
acts or methods , as a means of accomplishing
politicalends , or as a means of bringing about
politicalrevolution.
§ 2. "Sedition" isdefinedto be the advocacy
or suggestionby word , act, deed or writing of
public disorder or resistanceto the Government of
the United States or of the Commonwealth of
Kentucky or of the Constitution or Laws of either
of them , or of the change or modification of the
Government of the United States or of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky , or of the Constitution
or Laws of eitherof them , by force or violence or
by means other than by the lawful means provided
by the Constitution and Laws of the United
States and of the Commonwealth of Kentucky for
such purpose
§ 3. Criminal syndicalism and sedition, as
hereby defined, are declared to be unlawful and
felonious, and are prohibited, and any person
guiltyof any or eitherof said offenses, on convic-
tion, shall be confined in the State Penitentiary at
hard labor for not more than twenty-one (21)
years or by a fineof not more than $ 10,000.00, or
both such imprisonment and fine.
§ 4. Any person who , by word of mouth or
writing, advises, counsels, advocates suggests or
teaches the duty ,necessity,propriety or expediency
of crime , criminal syndicalism, or sedition, or who
shall advise, counsel, advocate , suggest or teach
the duty , necessity, propriety or expediency of
doing any act of violence, the destruction of or
damage to any property,the bodilyinjuryto any
person or persons, or the commission of any
crime or unlawful act as a means of accomplishing
or effectingany politicalends, change or revolu-
tion; or who prints, publishes, edits, issuesor
knowingly circulates,sells,distributes,or publicly
displaysany books, pamphlets, paper, handbill,
poster, document , or written or printed matter in
any form whatsoever , containing matter advocat-
ing, advising, suggesting or teaching crime , crimi-
nal syndicalism, seditionor the doing of any act
of physicalviolence,the destructionof or damage
to any property, the injuryto any person, or the
commission of any crime or unlawful act as a
means ofaccomplishing,effectingor bringingabout
any politicalends , or change , or as a means of
accomplishing , effecting or bringing about any
politicalrevolution,or who shallattempt tojustify,
by word of mouth or writing, the commission or
the attempt tocommit any actofphysicalviolence,
the destructionof or damage to any property, the
injury of any person, or the commission of any
crime or unlawful act at any time or place with
the intentto exemplify, spread, or teach, or sug-
gest criminalsyndicalismor sedition,or organizes,
or helps to organize or become a member of, or
voluntarily assembles with , any societyor assem-
blage of persons which teaches, advocates or sug-
gests the doctrine of criminal syndicalism, or
sedition, or the necessity,proprietyor expediency
of doing any act of physicalviolenceor the com-
mission of any crime or unlawful act as a means
of accomplishing or effectingany politicalends,
change or revolution,isguiltyof a felonyand upon
convictionthereofshallbe punished by imprison-
ment in the State Penitentiary for a term of not
more than twenty -one years, or by a fine of not
more than $ 10,000.00, or by both such imprison-
ment and fine .
§ 5. The owner , lessee, agent, superintendent
or person in charge or occupation of any place,
building,room or rooms , or structure, who know-
inglypermits thereinany assembly or consort of
persons prohibitedby thisAct , or who ,afterno-
tificationby any peace officeror Commonwealth's
Attorney that the place or premises, or any part
thereof, is or are so used, permits such use to
continue, isguiltyof a misdemeanor and punish-
able upon convictionthereofby imprisonment in
the county jailfor not more than one year , or by a
fineof not more than $500.00,or by both such
imprisonment and fine.
§ 6. Any peace officerwho shallhave notice
or knowledge of any such unlawful assembly in
violation of this Act shall forthwith disperse the
same , using the power of the county and such
force as is reasonably necessary for that purpose ;
and ifany such peace officershallfailor refuse
actively to disperse such assembly forthwith, he
shall on conviction be fined one thousand dollars,
and be imprisoned in the county jailthirtydays,
shall forfeithis officeand be disqualifiedfrom
holdingany publicofficefora periodof fiveyears.
§ 7. It shallbe unlawful for any person or
persons, individuallyor collectively, to advocate,
advise, counsel, aid or otherwise promote by
writing, speaking or otherwise, the changing by
force, intimidation, violence, rebellionor insur-
rection the present form of State or Federal
Government or the Laws or Constitutions thereof ;
or by violence,force or threats to alarm or disturb
or intimidate, or attempt to alarm or disturbor
intimidate, the General Assembly of the Com
monwealth or any branch or member thereof; or
by violence, forceor threatsto alarm, disturbor
hinderor obstruct,or intimidateany officerof the
Commonwealth of Kentucky ,in the matter of his
officialaction or in the discharge of his duty ; or
attempt so to do ;or by violence,forceor threats
to resist, obstruct, or hinder any militiaman or
militaryorganizationor posse acting under the
orders of any officerof the Commonwealth of
Kentucky ,or of the United States;or to advocate ,
counsel,aid or advise,by speaking or writing,the
assassinationof any officeror officersof the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky or of the United States,
or of any person, and any person or persons violat-
ingany provisionsof thissectionshallbe punished
by confinement in the State Penitentiary for not
more than twenty-one (21) yearsor by a fineof
not more than $10,000 or both such confinement
and fine .
§ 8. If the death of any person shalloccur in
the course of, or by reason of,any violationof
this Act , or be contributed to by such violation,
the person or persons so violating this Act shall
be guilty of murder and shallbe punished by
death or by confinement in the State Penitentiary
for life.
§ 9. It shallbe unlawful for any person to
print,publish, utter,or circulateor to have in his
possessionforthe purpose of publication,uttering
or circulatingany newspaper, book , circular,
pictureor other thing which advocates, suggests,
counsels or advises forcible resistance to constituted
authority or criminal syndicalism, sedition or the
assassination of officersor other persons, or the
forcibleabolitionof government , or changing by
force or violence or direct action the form of the
Government , Constitution, or Laws of Kentucky
or of the United States, and any persons publish-
ing, uttering, circulating, or for such purposes
having in their possessionany such newspaper,
book , circular, picture or other thing, shall be
guilty of a felony and upon convictionshallbe
punished by confinement in the State Penitentiary
for not more than twenty-one (21) years or by a
fine of not more than $ 10,000, or both such im-
prisonment and fine, and any person or persons
who shallrent or furnishany building, land or
place or any machinery or printingpressfor the
printingor circulationof any such matter, shall
be guilty of a misdemeanor , and shallbe fined not
more than $1,000foreach offenseor imprisonment
in the county jailfor not more than one year ,or
shall be both so fined and imprisoned .
§ 10. It shallbe unlawful for any person, or
persons,by speech,writingor otherwise,to arouse,
inciteor fix,or attempt to arouse, inciteor fix
enmity , discord or strifeor illfeeling between
classesor persons for the purpose of inducing
public tumult or disorder in order to cause the
forcible or violent change or overthrow of the
Government of the United States,or of the Govern-
ment of the Commonwealth of Kentucky , or for
the purpose of incitingresistanceto the courts,
laws, officersor constitutedauthoritiesof the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , and it shall be
unlawful, for any such purpose,to displayin any
parade, meeting, assembly or other place any red
flag, revolutionaryinsigniaor any revolutionary
banner , flag, placard, tag, sticker, circular, device
or picture, and any person taking part in such
parade or meeting,or violatingthissection,shall
be guiltyof a felony and on convictionshallbe
punished by confinementin the State Penitentiary
for not more than twenty -one years, or by a fine
ofnot more than $10,000,or by both suchimprison-
ment and fine .
§ 11. Ifany two or more personsshallagree,
band , or confederate themselves together to do
any of the things prohibited by thisAct ,they shall
be guiltyof a felony and on convictionshallbe
punishedby confinementin the State Penitentiary
not more than twenty-one yearsor by a fineof not
more than $ 10,000,or by both such imprisonment
and fine. And in any prosecution under this Act
itshallnot be necessary to prove any overt act on
the part of the accused pursuant to any unlawful
combination or agreement .
§ 12. Any use of any buildingor structureor
premises by any person or persons in the course of
any violationof thisAct , or for any prohibited
meeting or purpose, shallconstitutea nuisance,
and may be abated as other nuisances or may be
summarily abated by any peace officerat any time
by ejectingallpersonstherefrom, seizingany in-
criminatingarticlestherein, and securelyclosing
the place and excluding allpersons therefrom until
the owner , lessee, agent , tenant or occupant shall
give bond with sufficientsurety approved by said
peace officerin the penal sum of one thousand
dollars, payable to the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky , conditioned that said premises shall not
thereafterbe used for any unlawful purpose or
by any person convicted under this Act . Any
use of leased premises in violationof thisAct shall
terminate the lease thereof, at the option of the
lessor .
§ 13. In case any sectionor part of thisAct
shallbe held unconstitutionalby any court, itis
the legislativeintention that no other part of this
Act shallbe affectedby such holding.
§ 14. In any prosecutionunder thisAct , no
witness shall be allowed to claim privilegeor
exemption on the ground that his testimony may
incriminatehim ;but saidwitnessmay be required
neverthelessto testifyfor the Commonwealth ,
but no such testimony given by any such wit-
ness shallbe used againsthim in any prosecution
except for perjury, and he shallbe discharged
from any liabilityfor any violationof thisAct
so necessarilydisclosedin histestimony And the
provisionsof Section 241, Criminal Code , shall
not apply in any such prosecution.
Approved March 23, 1920.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, ch. 101, pp. 551–552
laws.summary: This statute grants women citizens the right to vote for presidential electors, while excluding certain individuals based on criminal convictions, which historically affected Black Kentuckians disproportionately.
page_titles: Act Granting Women Citizens the Right to Vote
Amendment to Voting Rights and Child Welfare
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 101 .
AN ACT granting to women citizensthe rightto vote for
presidentialelectors, and requiring officersto perform
duties with reference thereto .
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. Every female citizenof the United States
of the age of twenty -one years, who has resided in
the State one year,and in the county sixmonths ,
and in the precinctin which she offersto vote sixty
days next preceding the election, isa voter in said
precinct and not elsewhere, in all electionsof
electorsof President and Vice -President, and shall
be entitledand allowed to vote in allsuch elections;
but the followingpersons are excepted, and shall
not have the right to vote :
(a) Personsconvictedinany courtofcompetent
jurisdictionof treason,or felony, or briberyin an
electionor of such high misdemeanor as the General
Assembly may declare, shalloperate as an exclu-
sion from the right of suffrage; but persons hereby
excluded may be restoredto theircivilrightsby
executive pardon .
(b) Persons who , at the time of the election,
are in confinement under the judgment of a court
for some penal offense.
(c) Idiotsand insanepersons.
§ 2. Separateballotsshallbe provided in each
electionprecinct throughout the State for women
in all elections of electors of President and Vice-
President, which ballotsshallbe similar to ballots
provided for male voters, and shallcontain the
names of candidatesfor presidentalelectorswho
are to be voted for, and the ballotscast by women
voters shall be canvassed with and at the same
time other ballotscast for presidentialelectors
are canvassed, and by the same officers.
Approved March 28, 1920.

CHAPTER 102 .
AN ACT to amend subsection9 of Section331e of Chapter
18 of the Kentucky Statutes, which was an act of Feb-
ruary 24, 1894, pertainingto childrendestituteor mal-
treated .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssembly oftheCom-
monwealth ofKentucky:
§ 1. That Subsection 9 of Section 331e of
chapter 18 of the Kentucky Statutesbe amended
by adding to said subsection the following:
" Provided that the statusof no child, who has
been already adopted by any person by order or
judgment of a circuitcourt having jurisdiction
under the laws of the Commonwealth relating to
adoption of children, may be affectedor changed
by any order of the county or juvenile court other-
wise having controlof the statusof the child."
So that said Subsection 9 of said Section 331e
of Chapter 18 of the Kentucky Statutes, when
amended , willread as follows:
When any childshallbe found to be dependent
or neglected within the meaning of this act, the
court may allow such child to remain in its own
home , subject to the friendlyvisitationsof a
probation officer,such child to report to the proba-
tion officeras often as may be required, and ifthe
parents, parent or guardian or person having the
custody , control or supervision of such child con-
sent thereto, or if the court shall find that the
parents, parent, guardian or person having its
custody , control or supervision are unfit or im-
proper guardians, or are unwillingor unable to
care for, protect, educate or disciplinesuch child,
and shall further find it is for the interest of such
childand forthe people of thisState that such child
be taken from the custody or control of itsparent,
parents, guardian or person having its custody,
controlor supervision, the court may cause such
childto be placedina suitablehome ,subjectto the
friendlyvisitationand supervisionof a probation
officer, or cause it to be boarded out in some
suitablefamilyhome ,in caseprovisionismade by
voluntary contribution or otherwise for the pay-
ment of the board, and subject to the friendly
visitationand supervisionof a probation officer;
or the court may commit such child to the care of
some association, societyor corporationwillingto
receiveit, embracing in its objects the care of
neglected, dependent or delinquentchildren, pro-
vided, however , that the court shall not commit
any dependent or neglected child, within the
meaning of this act, to any association, society or
corporationreceivingdelinquent children unless
suitableprovisionis made by such association,
society or corporationfor separatingdelinquent
from neglectedor dependent children. Any de-
pendent or neglectedchild committed as herein
provided shallbe committed for such time during
itsminority as the court may deem fit, and the
courtat any time thereaftermay setaside,change
or modify such order. Provided that the status
of no child, who has been alreadyadopted by any
person by order or judgment of a circuitcourt
having jurisdictionunder the laws of the Com-
monwealth relatingto adoption of children, may
be affectedor changed by any orderof the county
or juvenilecourt otherwisehaving controlof the
status of the child.
Neither approved or disapproved.

laws.title: AN ACT to repeal and re-enact Section 1112, Kentucky Statutes, relating to change of venue in criminal cases, with an emergency thereto.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, ch. 123, pp. 603–604
laws.summary: This statute allows a circuit judge to change the venue of a criminal trial if there is a state of lawlessness or a high level of prejudice against the defendant, which may prevent a fair trial. It also allows for a change of venue on the defendant's motion if they are in danger of mob violence.
page_titles: Change of Venue in Criminal Cases
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 123 .
AN ACT to repeal and re-enact Section 1112, Kentucky
Statutes, relatingto change of venue in criminalcases,
with an emergency thereto.
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssembly oftheCom-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That Section1112 of the Kentucky Stat-
utes be repealed and that there be enacted in its
stead the following:
Whenever any circuitjudge shall be satisfied
from his own knowledge and from the written
statement of the Commonwealth's Attorney of
that district that such a state of lawlessness exists
in any county of thisCommonwealth or that he
be so satisfiedthat a high state of excitement or
feelingof prejudiceexiststhereinagainstthe de-
fendant that thereisapparent danger of mob vio-
lence wherein loss of lifeor destructionof prop-
erty may occur unlawfully, that a trialin such
county cannot be fairlyand impartiallyhad or
that the officersof the court willbe prevented
from dischargingtheirduty or thatthe jurorsmay
be intimidatedor deterredfrom fairlyand impar-
tiallyrendering a verdict in the case he may order
the prosecution removed to some other county
in which a fairtrialcan be had ;and the fiscalcourt
of the county from which such removal is made
shall allow and pay the costs thereof from the
county levy .
§ 2. A change of venue may be had to some
other county when the facts exist as set out in
Section 1 of this Act on the motion of the defend-
ant by counseland his presencein court waived
when the written statement of his counsel is filed
in such case and the affidavit of the defendant filed
thereinthat he isin danger of mob violencein such
county and for that reason desiresthat a change
of venue be had to some other county and that he
thereinwaives his presence on the hearing of a
motion for a change of venue .
§ 3. Whereas , there are now pending in the
circuit courts of this Commonwealth cases in which
mob violencemay ensue by taking the defendant
into court where he has been indicted for the pur-
pose of securing a change of venue or for trialand
that it is to the best interest of the State that this
Act become a law immediately, an emergency is
declared to exist .
Neither approved nor disapproved .
