laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 159 .
That Chapter thirty-six of the Acts of one thousand
nine hundred and sixteenbe and the same ishereby repealed
and the followingisenacted in lieuthereof:
AN ACT providing for the working of prisonerswho are
confined in the prisons, on State highways and bridges,
constructed by the Department of State Roads and
Highways ;providingfor the settingapart of a fund from
the State Road Fund , to be used by the Department of
State Roads and Highways in buildingState Roads and
bridges with convict labor and to enable said Department
of State Roads and Highways to work said prisonersin
the mining , quarrying and manufacturing and prepara-
tion of material for building roads and bridges ; provid-
ing aid and assistanceto the State Highway Commission
in the construction of State roads with convict labor and
otherwise; providing for the assignment of prisonersto
do State road work and fortheirsupervisionand manage-
ment while so engaged ; providing a method of payment
for the roads so constructed out of the State road fund ,
and authorizingthe State Board of Control to provide
means of employment for convictswhile not engaged in
working on public roads and bridges, and in the manu-
facture, quarrying, mining and preparation of road
material; providingthat the State Board of Control may
leasefarms on which to work convicts, and providing
compensation for allprisonersthat may work under the
supervisionof the State Board of Control; and providing
ways and means whereby prior indebtedness of the
counties to the State for convict labor work can be
liquidated.
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssembly oftheCom-
monwealth ofKentucky:
SectionOne . Upon a demand of the State
Highway Commission ,the State Board of Control
shallassign such of the prisonersconfined in either
of the prisonsas are availablefor work on such
roads as are constructed under the direction of
the Department of State Roads and Highways .
Such prisonersmay alsobe employed in the manu-
facturing, quarrying, mining and preparationof
road and bridgematerialto be used eitherby the
Department of State Roads and Highways in the
constructionof roads and bridges, or by the State
Board of Control for such other purposes as the
saidBoard may determine. Such prisonersas are
assigned for the aforesaidwork shallwork at such
placesand such timesas shallbe designatedby the
State Highway Engineer and the work done by
them shall be performed under the direction and
according to the plans and specificationsof the
Department ofStateRoads and Highways . While
such prisonersare engaged in the work aforesaid,
the transportation, as definedbelow, care, guard-
ing, supervision, maintenance and housing shall
be under the control and direction of the said State
Board of Control. The costand expense of same
shallbe paid out of the fund accruing from the
hiringof such convictsas provided in Section 3
hereof. The transportation as above referred to
shall mean the railroad fare and incidental ex-
penses of prisoners from their respective prisons
to the county in which they shallbe employed ,and
shall also include the transportationfrom one
county to another county when saidprisonersare
so removed for the purpose of employment . The
saidboard shallprescriberulesand regulationsfor
theirsupervision, care and comfort, and to that
end the said Board is given fullpower to pre-
scribesuch rulesand regulationsas may be neces-
sary for the proper confinement, watching and
guarding of said prisonerswhile so engaged, and
the expensesthereofshallbe certifiedby the State
Board of Control to the Auditor and paid as pro-
vided for herein; provided, however , that for the
year one thousand nine hundred and twenty, not
more than fifteenper cent of the road fund for
that year shallbe expended under the provisions
of thisAct , and for the year one thousand nine
hundred and twenty -one , not more than fifteen
per cent of the road fund for that year shallbe
expended in additionto such a sum as represents
the differencebetween fifteenper cent of the road
fund for one thousand nine hundred and twenty ,
and the amount actually expended during one
thousand nine hundred and twenty, under the
provisionsof thisAct . But the saidlimitationsof
expendituresas above referredto arenot to include
expendituresfor the purchase of machinery as
provided in Section 2 hereof.
Section 2. The purchase of the necessary ma-
chinery and equipment for the constructionof
roads and bridgesor repairingmaterialfor roads
and bridgesand the purchasing of and payment
for such materialsas may be required in con-
structingroads and bridges with convict labor,
and forthe purchase of and maintenance of vehicles
to be used in transportingthe convictswhile so
engaged in such work , or for the transportation
of employees of the Department of State Roads and
Highways in the interestof any State roads,shall
be a proper charge againstthe State Road Fund ,
when so certifiedby the State Highway Engineer
and upon the approvalof the StateHighway Com-
mission, shallbe paid by the Auditor of Public
Accounts . All purchases made under the pro-
visionsof thisAct shallfirstbe advertisedby the
State Highway Commission , and contracts for
such material shall be let to the lowest and best
responsiblebidder and allbids shallbe filedin the
officeof the StateHighway Commission ,and be a
public record thereof. The amount expended
under the provisionsof thisSection shallnot exceed
ten per centum of the State Road Funds .
Section3. After July first, one thousand nine
hundred and twenty , the use of convict labor
herein provided for shallbe confinedexclusively
to the construction and maintenance of the system
of State Highways heretofore designated by the
General Assembly , and when the State Highway
Commission shallemploy any convictsin accord-
ance with Section1 hereof,they shallpay therefor
from the State road fund , the sum of one dollar
and fiftycents($1.50),per day ,per man ,foreach
convict so hired by them . The State Highway
Commission shall, at the end of each month ,
certifyto the State Board of Control and to the
Auditor of Public Accounts , the number of con-
victshired by them during such month , and the
amount of hire with which said State Board of
Control shall be credited, and with which the
State road fund shall be charged . Convicts
engaged on State road work may be employed on
an average of ten hours a day but the number of
hours per day such convicts may be required to
work in any month may vary with the seasonand
shall be under the direction of the State Board of
Control and theStateHighway Engineer.
Section 4. The State Board of Control shall
not work any convicts outside the walls of the
prison on road or bridge work who have been
sentenced to lifeimprisonment, untilthey shall
have actually served within the walls of the
prison fiveyears of such sentence, nor shallany
convict sentenced for rape, attempted rape, de-
taining a woman against her will, or who has
escaped or attempted to escape, or who has
violatedhis parole, or who has been convicted
and sentenced to the penitentiarymore than twice,
but such convicts shall serve their respective
sentenceswithinthe wallsof the prison.
Section 5. The State Board of Control shall
provide rulesand regulationswhereby each pris-
oner engaged in any kind of work shallreceivea
certainsum each day from his earnings, which
sum shallbe not lessthan five(5) cents nor more
than fifteen(15) centsper day ,the amount thereof
to be determined as may be providedby the State
Board of Control; provided, the funds thus ac-
cruing to the creditof any prisonershallbe paid
to him ,or to dependent members of hisfamily,at
such times and in such manner as the State Board
of Control may deem best,but at leasttwenty -five
per cent of such creditshallbe leftfor and paid
to the prisonerat the time of his parole or final
dischargeby the StateBoard of Control;and pro-
vided that the warden may , with the approval of
the State Board of Control by way of punishment
forviolationof rulesand of propriety,or any other
misconduct, cancelor distributeto the family of
the prisonersuch portionor such creditas he may
deem best. At the end of each month , the State
Board of Control shallcertifyto the Auditor of
PublicAccounts the amount due each prisonerfor
that month and he shall draw warrant on the State
Treasurer for the amount so certified .
Section 6. The State Board of Control are
hereby vested with fullpower and authority to
provide method and means of employing allcon-
victswho may be retainedwithin the wallsof the
prison at any time that such method or means as
may be determined or put intoeffectshallbe sub-
mitted to the Governor , who shallapprove all
plans, methods or means which may be suggested
or outlinedby saidBoard .
Section 7. The State Board of Control are
hereby empowered to lease a farm or farms or
land immediately adjoiningeitherpenitentiaryor
adjacent thereto for the working of convicts
thereon,said lease to be limited to the term of the
Governor approving same , and the said State
Board of Control, may prescribeall necessary
rulesand regulationsfor the support and mainte-
nance of prisoners while at work on such farm or
farms and the contract price of such lease shallbe
certifiedto theAuditor by saidBoard ,and paid as
other claims against the Commonwealth , but no
lease so made by said Board shall be binding or
effective until the same has been submitted to the
Governor and shallhave been approved by him .
Section8. With the approval and consent of
theStateHighway Commission ,theStateHighway
Engineer may employ such civilengineersas may
be deemed necessary to assistthe Department of
State Roads and Highways in the constructionof
roads and bridges herein provided for, and the
salaryand expensesof such engineersshallbe paid
by the Auditor out of the State road fund upon
propercertificationby theStateHighway Engineer
and the approval of the State Highway Commis-
sion .
Section9. The State Highway Engineer shall
execute a bond to the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky, in the sum of Ten Thousand Dollars
($10,000.00) for the faithfulperformance of his
dutiesand that he willdiligentlycareforany and
all property belonging to the State coming into
his hands for use in the construction of roads and
bridges, which bond shall be approved by the
Governor and filedwith the Secretary of State .
The State Highway Engineer may require any
employee in the engineeringdepartment to execute
a bond to the Commonwealth of Kentucky , in a
sum to be fixedby the engineerconditionedfor
the faithfulperformance of the duties of such
employee, which bond shallbe approved by the
engineerand filedwith the Secretaryof State.
Section10. The State Highway Commission
shallcause to be prepared a statement of costs of
any convict labor road improvements heretofore
made under the presentlaw :such statement shall
show a listof allexpendituresand the totalof
same . A copy of thisstatement shallbe presented
to the FiscalCourt of the county, in which such
convictlabor improvements have been made set-
tingforththe amount due the Stateby the county
as itsshare of the cost according to the provisions
of Chapter 36, Acts General Assembly , one
thousand nine hundred and sixteen . The State
Highway Commission shall, at the time of sub-
mitting thisstatement to the FiscalCourt, make
request upon the Fiscal Court of such county for
the immediate payment of the sum due the State
as setout in such settlement. Upon the failureor
refusalof any county to comply with the request
to reimbursethe State in a sum equal to fiftyper
centum of the totalcost of such road improvement ,
then the State Highway Commission shallthere-
upon place to the creditof the State,as reimburse-
ment to the county on any State aid road work
which has already been accepted by the State, or
may hereafterbe accepted,the totalsum paid out
by the State on convictlaborin such county. In
case the amount due any county on State Aid
road construction,islessthan the amount due the
State by the county on convictlabor road work ,
then the difference between such amounts shall
again be submitted by the State Highway Com-
mission for payment . When such payment or
payments have been made , they shallbe placed
to the creditof such county on account of convict
labor road improvements in that county .
Section11. All laws and parts of laws in con-
flictwith thisAct are hereby repealed.
Neither approved nor disapproved.

CHAPTER 162 .
AN ACT to amend and re-enact Section 4527 Kentucky
Statutes , Carroll's1918 Edition .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssembly oftheCom-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That Section 4527 Kentucky Statutes,
Carroll's1918 Edition,be,and the same is,hereby
amended and re-enacted so that said section,when
so amended and re-enacted ,willread as follows:
"Section4527. Trustees- Appointment - Term
of Office - Powers - Vacancies - Treasurer . The
State Normal School for Colored Persons (see
Section 4527a), establishedby an act of the
General Assembly ,approved May eighteenth,one
thousand eight hundred and eighty-six, shall
hereafterbe under the controland supervisionof a
board of trustees,composed of the Superintendent
of Public Instruction, who shall be ex-officio
chairman of the board , and three intelligentand
discreetpersons to be appointed by the Governor ,
subject to the approval of the Senate, who are
hereby constituteda body corporate, with power
to sue and be sued, plead and be impleaded, and
to hold in trustallfunds and propertynow owned
by saidschool,or which may hereafterbe.provided
forit,and shallbe known and designatedas "The
Board of Trustees of the Kentucky State Normal
School forColoredPersons." (See Section4527a).
Provided, that no two appointive members of
the saidboard shallbe residentsof any one county .
" The term of office for the three members
appointed by the Governor shallbegin on the first
day of July, one thousand nine hundred and
eighteen, and one member thereofshallretire, as
may be determined by lot,at the end of one year
thereafter, one in two years and the other in three
years; theirsuccessorsshallbe appointed by the
Governor for a term of threeyears;they shallbe
subjectto removal by the Governor forcause,and
he is authorizedto fillallvacanciesoccuringby
death , resignationor otherwise.
"Said board shall adopt such rules for the
government of said school not inconsistent with
law, as they deem proper, and shallsuperviseall
itsinterests,providefor allitswants,and require
formal reports of the actual condition of the school
in every regard. They shallbiennially,beginning
on the firstday of July, 1918,electsome suitable
person outsideof theirown number as treasurer,
who , before enteringon his duty , shallgive in
bond such a sum as they may prescribe,and they
shallagreewith him as to compensation;provided,
that in no case shallsuch compensation exceed
one hundred dollarsper annum ; provided,that no
member of the board of trustees of the State
Normal SchoolforColored Personsshalldraw any
salaryfor his servicesas such, but shallbe paid
theirnecessarytravelingexpenses and hotel bills
in going to and from each meeting of the board
and other legitimateexpenses, to be paid out of
any money now appropriated by the State of
Kentucky forsaidStateNormal SchoolforColored
Persons,saidexpensesto be paid afteran itemized
account is filedas is now required by law for
similarexpensesagainstthe State."
Neither approved nor disapproved.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 163 .
AN ACT to amend and re -enact Subsection 1 of Section
1137 of Kentucky Statutes (Carroll'sedition, 1915.)
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssembly oftheCom-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That Subsection1 ofSection1137 of the
Kentucky Statutes, Carroll's1915 Edition, be
amended by adding at the end of the said sub-
section the following :
"Except in cases where the accused has been
adjudged to suffera death sentence for the crime of
rape or attempted rape, in which event sentence
shallbe executed by hanging the condemned in
the county in which the crime was committed ,"
that such an execution shall be within an enclosure
to be provided by the county and admittance to
saidenclosureto be limitedto 100 persons. The
sentence to be executed by the sheriffof the county .
So that said Subsection 1 of Section 1137 of
the Kentucky Statutes (Carroll's1915 Edition),
when amended and re-enacted shall read as follows :
" That from and after the period that this law
shall take effect the mode of the execution of a
death sentencemust in every case be by causing
to pass through the body of the condemned a cur-
rent of electricityof sufficientintensityto cause
death as quickly as possible, and the application
of such current must be continued until the con-
demned is dead .
"All executionsof the death penaltyby electro-
cutionshalltake placewithinthe wallsof theState
penitentiary, hereafterindicatedby the Board of
Prison Commissioners , and in such enclosure
as will exclude public view thereof. Except in
cases where the accused has been adjudged to
suffera death sentence for the crime of rape or
attempted rape, in which event the sentence
shallbe executed by hanging the condemned in
the county in which the crime was committed .
The sentence to be executed by the sheriffof the
county ."
Neither approved nor disapproved.

laws.summary: This act outlines the powers and responsibilities of boards of trustees for common schools, including the appointment and dismissal of principals and teachers, the prescription of studies, and the admission of students. Section 4474 specifically states that 'All white children of common school age residing in any graded common school district shall have the right to attend the graded common school thereof.'
key_provisions: Section 4474. All white children of common school age residing in any graded common school district shall have the right to attend the graded common school thereof. The trustees may admit into said graded common school children who do not reside within the said district , or persons over the common school age, on such terms and conditions , and upon the payment of such tuition and other fees as they may deem proper .

Section 4476. Boards of trustees of graded com- mon school districts are hereby authorized and em- powered to levy each year not later than the last Saturday in June , a tax for establishing , maintain- ing and operating the common schools of their re- spective districts , at a rate not less than twenty -five cents ( 25c ) and not to exceed one dollar and twenty- five cents ($1.25 ) upon each one hundred dollars ($100.00 ) of taxable property within the district and owned by white persons ; and , also , a poll tax on each white male inhabitant within the district over twenty -one ( 21 ) years of age , not exceeding two dol- lars ( $2.00 ) ; and shall , also levy a sufficient amount to provide for the payment of interest and for sink- ing fund purposes for the next fiscal year, and the tax accruing from so much of said levy as is made for the payment of interest and sinking fund purposes shall be by said board of trustees at once irrevocably set aside and used for these purposes and not other- wise ; and said interest and sinking fund provisions as above provided shall include the interest and the sinking fund for the entire outstanding bonded in- debtedness of said board. The tax so imposed shall be collected on the as- sessed value of the property in the district as ascer- tained by the assessment for State and county pur- poses next preceding the collection of the tax. Said board of trustees shall elect a collector of taxes , who shall give good and sufficient bond to said

Section 4484. No new colored graded common school district shall hereafter be created or organ- ized , nor shall the boundaries of any colored graded common school district hereafter be changed except as heretofore provided in this Act. Such colored graded common school districts as are organized and established at the time this Act goes into effect shall hereafter operate under the conditions and pro- visions of this Act . Provided that no white person shall vote at any election held in a colored graded school district under the provisions of this Act ; nor shall the property of any white person be taxed to maintain any graded common school for colored chil- dren ; nor shall the property of any colored person ' be taxed for the benefit or any graded common school for white children ; nor shall any white child attend any graded common school for colored chil- dren organized under the provisions of this Act ; nor shall any colored child attend any graded com- mon school for white children .

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 8 .
AN ACT to repeal Chapter 38 of the Acts of the General As-
sembly of 1920 , relating to the election and qualification of
members of boards of trustees in graded common school dis-
tricts ; also Chapter 46 of the Acts of the General Assembly
of 1920 , relating to the establishment of independent , con-
solidated , graded and high school ; also Chapter 25 of the Acts
of the General Assembly of 1920 , relating to the condemna-
tion of land by boards of trustees of graded common school
districts ; also Section 4464 , Section 4500 , and all intervening
sections , of the Kentucky Statutes , Carroll's Edition , 1918 ,
relating to the management and control of graded common
school districts ; and in order to provide for a better system
of graded schools and to provide for a more effective manage-
ment and control of graded common schools in this Common-
wealth , be there enacted in lieu of the above , the following
sections , relating to the management and conduct of graded
common school districts .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That Chapter 38 of the Acts of the General As-
sembly of 1920 , relating to the election and qualifi-
cation of members of boards of trustees in graded
common school districts be and the same is hereby
repealed ; also Chapter 46 of the Acts of the General
Assembly of 1920 , relating to the establishment of
independent , consolidated , graded and high school ;
also Chapter 25 of the Acts of the General Assembly
of 1920 , relating to the condemnation of land by
boards of trustees of graded common school dis-
tricts ; also Section 4464 , Section 4500 , and all in-
tervening sections , of the Kentucky Statutes , Car-
roll's Edition , 1918 , relating to the management and
control of graded common school districts , be and
the same are hereby repealed ; and in lieu thereof
are now enacted the following sections to be known
and designated as :
Section 4464. Each graded common school dis-
trict organized and incorporated at the time this Act
goes into effect shall be under the management and
control of a board of trustees .
Section 4465. The board of trustees of each
graded common school district shall consist of five
(5 ) members , who shall be elected at large from the
qualified voters of the graded common school dis-
trict , as hereinafter provided for terms of three ( 3 )
years , beginning with the second Saturday of May
following their election , and shall hold office until
their succesors are elected and qualified . Members
of boards of trustees shall qualify by taking the oath
prescribed for public offices under Section 228 of
the Constitution of the State . Failure to qualify
within seven ( 7 ) days after election shall constitute
a vacancy .
Graded common school district trustees shall be
chosen solely because of their fitness and shall be
eligible for re - election unless otherwise disqualified
by the provisions of this section . No person shall
be elected to or serve on this board who is in any way
subject to its authority , and no member shall enter
into business transactions for personal gain with
this board .
Members of boards of trustees of graded common
school districts shall be elected on the first Saturday
of May in each year, the number to be elected each
year for the full term of three ( 3 ) years to be de-
termined by the number of regular vacancies to be
filled .
If at any time there should be a vacancy in said
board , the same shall be filled by election by the re-
maining members , and the person elected to fill such
vacancy shall hold office until the next regular elec-
tion of trustees when his successor shall be elected
to fill out the unexpired term .
All graded common school district elections shall
be provided for by the trustees of the district in of-
fice at the time of the particular election . The board
of trustees shall appoint the officers to hold all
elections . These officers shall take an oath to be
under the same responsibilities and subject to the
same penalties as the officers holding State or coun-
ty elections , but they shall make returns of poll
books and certify the result of the elections to the
board of trustees who shall examine and compare
the same and issue certificates to the persons found.
to be elected .
On presentation of evidence by the Superintend-
ent of Public Instruction that any member of a
board of trustees is not capable of discharging , or
is not discharging his duty, or is guilty of immoral
or disreputable conduct , the remaining members of
the board of trustees shall hear evidence in the case ,
making known to the defendant in writing the
charges against him , and give him an opportunity to
be heard in person or by counsel and to present wit-
nesses in his own defense upon not less than ten ( 10 )
days ' notice . If, after careful investigation , the
board of trustees shall find sufficient cause for re-
moval , it shall declare the office of the respective
member vacant at once and the vacancy shall be
filled as heretofore provided in this section .
Members of boards of trustees shall receive no
compensation for their services .
Section 4466. The board of trustees of a graded
common school district shall be named and styled :
" The Board of Trustees of the -Graded
Common School District , " and in that name may
sue and be sued , contract and be contracted with ,
and may acquire and hold by purchase , gift , devise
or otherwise , and dispose of and convey , any real or
personal estate , goods and chattels , necessary and
convenient for the use and purposes of such graded
common school district ; and the title of all such prop-
erty shall vest in said board of trusteees and their
successors in office , to be held sacred for the use and
benefit of said graded common school district . The
board of trustees of any graded common school dis-
trict is authorized and empowered to condemn any
land deemed necessary by said board for a site for
a graded common school , not exceeding ten ( 10 )
acres , in the manner now provided by law for con-
demning land for railroad purposes .
Section 4467. The office of the board of trustees
of each graded common school district shall be in
the principal school building of the district unless
otherwise adequately provided for . The board of
trustees shall hold its annual meeting each year in
its office on the second Saturday of May . At this
meeting the board shall each year elect one of its
members to act as president , one to act as vice pres-
ident, and one to act as secretary , and shall fix the
time and place of its regular meetings , which shall
be duly advertised . Such special meetings may be
called at such times as the duties and business of
the board may require . The rules generally adopted
by deliberative bodies for their government shall be
observed by boards of trustees , but no motion or
resolution shall be declared adopted without the con-
currence of a majority of the whole board.
The secretary of the board shall conduct all corre-
spondence of the board, issue calls for all meetings
on the order of the president, prepare the docket or
calendar of the same, keep the minutes of the pro-
ceedings , preserve in the office of the board all its
records , make all reports required of the board , re-
ceive all reports required by it, seeing that they are
in proper form , complete , and accurate , and shall
perform such other secretarial duties as may be im-
posed by the board or as may hereinafter be im-
posed by the provisions of this Act.
Section 4468. Each board of trustees shall ap-
point a treasurer , but said treasurer shall not be a
member of the board . Before entering upon his
duties , the treasurer shall file with the board a bond
to be paid for by the board in amount to be deter-
mined by it as surety for the faithful performance
of his duties . Said bond shall be guaranteed by a
personal security or a surety company authorized
to do business in the State , and made payable to the
respective board of trustees . The bond shall pro-
vide that as treasurer of the respective board he will
faithfully perform the duties of his office ; receive all
moneys to which the respective board is entitled by
the Constitution of the State , or by Statute, or
which may in any way come into its possession ; hold
all such moneys as a separate fund in his hands ;
and pay over all such moneys to such persons and in
such manner as said board may under the provis-
ions of this Act direct ; and that he will keep full and
complete accounts in such manner and make such
reports thereon as the State Board of Education
and the respective board of trustees may require ;
that he will preserve all records relating to the
transactions and duties of his office , and turn all
public school funds in hand and all accounts and rec-
ords , after due and proper audit by a competent
outside agent , if required by said board , to his suc-
cessor . The expense of such audit shall be paid by
the board of trustees .
The treasurer of the board of trustees shall pay
out school funds only on appropriate written orders
signed by the president and secretary of the respec-
tive board of trustees .
Section 4469. No new graded common school dis-
trict shall hereafter be created or organized , unless
100 pupil children reside therein .
Provided further , that no graded common school
district shall hereafter operate independent of the
county school system that has a school census of less
than seventy -five ( 75 ) census pupil children ; or that
does not maintain an elementary school with a min-
imum term of eight ( 8 ) months , and a high school
with a minimum term of eight ( 8 ) months which
meets State standards as to the number and qualifi-
cation of teachers ; but any graded common school
district may elect to pay the tuition of all pupils re-
siding in the graded school district who are eligible
and who enter any other public high school which
maintains a course of study required by law and
which has been approved by the State Board of
Education .
When the board of trustees of a graded common
school district fails to conduct and manage the
schools under its jurisdiction and authority accord-
ing to the provisions as stated in the preceding par-
agraph, the State Board of Education , after due no-
tice to the board of trustees of such failure and the
lapse of ample time for the board of trustees to
make the needed and necessary improvements in
said schools , shall declare the given graded common
school districts with existing metes and bounds ,
abolished , and shall create therefrom a subdistrict
of the given county system to be under the jurisdic-
tion of the county board of education of the county
in which the given graded common school district is
located . Record of such action shall be copied in
triplicate ; one copy shall become a part of the per-
manent records of the State Board of Education ;
one copy shall be sent to the board of trustees of
the graded common school district abolished , and
filed by said trustees among its permanent records ;
and one copy shall be sent to the county board of
education of the county in which the graded common
school district abolished is located , and shall be filed
among its permanent records .
When a graded common school district is thus
abolished and a subdistrict of the county system is
created therefrom , all property belonging to , pos-
sessed and held in the corporate name of the given
board of trustees of the graded common school dis-
trict abolished shall pass to and be possessed and
held in the corporate name of the county board of
education of the county in which the graded common
school district abolished is located . The county
board of education shall , after due and proper audit,
possess all funds on hand or to be collected , and
shall assume all responsibilities , financial or other-
wise , lawfully entered into by contract , or otherwise ,
by the board of trustees of the graded common
school district abolished .
And provided further , on petition to the graded
school board of forty per cent of the legal voters
in any graded common school district , asking that
their graded school district be made a part of the
county school system , it shall be the duty of the
graded school board to call a meeting of the board
within one week from the time the petition has been
received , and to make an order which shall be re-
corded in the minutes of the board, for holding an
election for the purpose of determining whether it
is the will of the legal voters in the graded common
school district that their graded common school dis-
trict be made a part of the county school system ,
and shall designate two citizens residing within the
graded school district to act as election officers in
said election . The election shall be held in exactly
the same manner as elections of graded school board
members are held , and at the school building ; pro-
vided that such election may not be held earlier than
twenty days from the date of such order . It shall
be the duty of the graded school board to advertise
at least ten days before said election the date and
the place and the purpose of holding such an election
by posting notices to this effect in conspicuous places
in various portions of the graded school ditsrict .
The majority of the votes cast shall determine
whether or not the graded common school district
shall be made a part of the county school system .
Section 4470. All graded common school districts
other than those in cities of the first , second , third
and fourth class , operating under special laws or
special charters , shall when this Act goes into effect
cease to operate under their respective special laws
or special charters and shall thereafter operate un-
der the provisions of this Act . Provided that boards
of trustees or other managing authorities in such
graded common school districts in office when this
Act goes into effect , in other than those in first , sec-
ond , third and fourth class cities , shall continue to
serve until the next regular election of boards of
trustees as provided in Section 4464 of this Act . Pro-
vided further , that at the first election under the
provisions of Section 4464 of this Act , one trustee
shall be elected for one year , two for two years , and
two for three years , thereafter regular election shall
be for the full term of three years .
All graded common school districts in cities of the
first , second , third and fourth class , operating under
special charters or special laws , shall when this Act
goes into effect cease to operate under their respec-
tive special laws or special charters , and shall there-
after operate under the general laws governing the
management and conduct of the common schools in
cities of their respective classes . Provided , that the
board of trustees or other managing authorities in
such graded common school districts shall serve un-
til the next regular election of members of boards of
education in first , second , third and fourth class
cities . Provided , further , that the first election in
such graded common school districts under the gen-
eral school laws governing the management and con-
duct of common schools in first , second , third and
fourth class cities shall conform to the provisions
of the respective general city school laws for the
first election of members of boards of education .
Section 4471. Boards of trustees shall , subject to
the provisions of this Act and the rules and regula-
tions of the State Board of Education , prescribe
rules and regulations for the control, government
and management of the common schools under their
jurisdiction .
Section 4472. Boards of trustees shall appoint
for the schools under their respective jurisdiction
a principal and all teachers , fix their compensation
and dismiss them for immorality , misconduct , incom-
petency , insubordination , or wilful neglect of duty.
Provided that in each case the charge be made in
writing and that the principal or teacher be given
opportunity on not less than ten ( 10 ) days ' no-
tice to be heard in person or by counsel and to pre-
sent witnesses in defense . Provided further , that
no principal or teacher shall be employed who does
not hold the kind and grade of certificate required
by law and issued by the State Board of Education .
Section 4473. Boards of trustees shall, subject to
the provisions of this Act and the rules and regula-
tions of the State Board of Education , prescribe the
studies to be taught and the course of study to be
used in the schools under their jurisdiction .
Section 4474. All white children of common
school age residing in any graded common school
district shall have the right to attend the graded
common school thereof.
The trustees may admit into said graded common
school children who do not reside within the said
district , or persons over the common school age, on
such terms and conditions , and upon the payment of
such tuition and other fees as they may deem proper .
Section 4475. Whenever it becomes desirable on
account of geographical or other conditions to es-
tablish a consolidated school , composed of a graded
common school and other adjoining common school
subdistrict or subdistricts , the board of trustees of
such graded common school shall have authority to
enter into contract with the county board of edu-
cation of the county in which said graded common
school district is located , to establish , operate and
maintain such consolidated school . The contract
when made shall be in writing , and shall stipulate
in full and complete terms , the number of years
such contract shall exist , the employment of teach-
ers , the arrangements of the course of study , and all
other arrangements necessary to the successful con-
duct of such consolidated school .
The expense of the transportation of pupils to
and from such consolidated school may be provided
for jointly by the graded common school and the
subdistrict annexed or by the subdistricts alone .
The tax for the transportation of pupils by the
subdistricts concerned shall be voted , levied and col-
lected in the same way and at the same time that
other consolidated schools vote , levy and collect a
tax for the same purpose .
Section 4476. Boards of trustees of graded com-
mon school districts are hereby authorized and em-
powered to levy each year not later than the last
Saturday in June , a tax for establishing , maintain-
ing and operating the common schools of their re-
spective districts , at a rate not less than twenty -five
cents ( 25c ) and not to exceed one dollar and twenty-
five cents ($1.25 ) upon each one hundred dollars
($100.00 ) of taxable property within the district
and owned by white persons ; and , also , a poll tax on
each white male inhabitant within the district over
twenty -one ( 21 ) years of age , not exceeding two dol-
lars ( $2.00 ) ; and shall , also levy a sufficient amount
to provide for the payment of interest and for sink-
ing fund purposes for the next fiscal year, and the
tax accruing from so much of said levy as is made for
the payment of interest and sinking fund purposes
shall be by said board of trustees at once irrevocably
set aside and used for these purposes and not other-
wise ; and said interest and sinking fund provisions
as above provided shall include the interest and the
sinking fund for the entire outstanding bonded in-
debtedness of said board.
The tax so imposed shall be collected on the as-
sessed value of the property in the district as ascer-
tained by the assessment for State and county pur-
poses next preceding the collection of the tax.
Said board of trustees shall elect a collector of
taxes , who shall give good and sufficient bond to
said board and who shall be allowed a fee not in ex-
cess of four per cent on all funds collected . Provided ,
however , that if the said board of education selects
the sheriff as the collector of taxes , it shall be his
duty to act as such collector , at same fees as above
provided .
Before entering upon his duties as collector , the
treasurer which may be elected by the board shall
give to each board of trustees a bond , in amount
agreeable to the respective board of trustees and
guaranteed by some surety company authorized to
do business in the State , or good personal security ,
for the faithful performance of his duties . Said
bond shall be paid for by the respective board of
trustees .
The treasurer as collecting officer shall settle his
accounts with the board of trustees on or before the
first Monday of January each year, and boards of
trustees may require him to settle his accounts
monthly.
Section 4477. If the tax levied under the provis-
ions of Section 4476 of this Act is not sufficient to
provide suitable grounds , buildings and equipment ,
boards of trustees are hereby authorized and em-
powered to order an election and submit to the
voters of their respective graded common school
districts the question whether or not the trustees
thereof shall issue bonds of their respective graded
common school districts , in any amount not exceed-
ing the limit provided by Sections 157 and 158 of the
present Constitution of this State , for the purpose
of providing suitable grounds , school buildings , fur-
niture and apparatus for their respective graded
common school districts ; Provided , that due notice
of said election shall be given by the trustees of
their respective districts , by written or printed
posters not less than one foot square , signed by the
trustees of their respective districts , stating the
time , place and hours of the said election , posted at
not less than six public , conspicuous places in the dis-
trict for ten days previous to the day of election , and
by one insertion thereof in the newspaper , if any ,
published in said district .
The board shall appoint two judges, a clerk and
a sheriff to hold such election , who shall be first duly
sworn before acting and shall be housekeepers and
taxpayers , resident in the district for which they
are appointed , and one of the judges shall ask of
each voter : " Are you in favor of the issue of bonds
by the trustees of the graded common schools of
this district , for the purpose of providing suitable
grounds , school buildings , furniture and apparatus
for this district " and the clerk shall record the ans-
wer " Yes " or " No " as given by the voter . If two-
thirds of the voters voting at said election vote in
favor of the issue of the bonds , then the trustees of
such graded common school may issue the bonds of
said district for an amount not exceeding the con-
stitutional limit and in conformity with the Con-
stitution of the State .
For the payment of the interest on such bonds
and for creating a sinking fund for the payment of
the principal thereof, the board of trustees of their
respective districts are authorized and empowered
to levy annually the needed tax as provided for in
Section 4476 of this Act .
Said bonds may be of any denomination , in even
hundreds , not exceeding one thousand dollars each ,
running not exceeding thirty years and bearing in-
terest not exceeding six per cent per annum , payable
annually or semi -annually as expressed in said
bonds payable to bearer with interest coupons at-
tached .
Said bonds shall be signed by the president of the
board of trustees and attested by the secretary
thereof , shall pass by delivery , and shall be redeem-
able at the option of said board .
Said bonds shall be sold by the trustees or their
authorized agent , for the highest price obtainable ,
but for not less than their face par value and ac-
crued interest , and the proceeds paid over to the
treasurer and applied to the uses and purposes for
which they were issued .
Section 4478. The Superintendent of Public In-
struction shall pay to the treasurer of each graded
common school district the pro rata portion of the
State and county school funds due the district ac-
cording to the number of pupil children therein .
Section 4479. Each board of trustees may employ
not less than one attendance officer who shall hold an
attendance officer's certificate issued by the State
Board of Education . Provided that boards of trus-
1
tees may enter into contract with county boards of
education for the employment of an attendance offi-
cer or officers who shall serve both the county and the
graded common school district , the expense of such
attendance officer or officers being pro rated accord-
ing to the number of pupil children in the county and
in the graded common school district .
Section 4480. School attendance of children of
school age in graded common school districts shall
be subject to the same requirements and provisions
as of children of school age in county school districts
as provided by law .
Section 4481. Each board of trustees shall each
year not later than the last Saturday of May pre-
pare an annual school budget on forms and blanks
prepared by the State Board of Education' and shall
submit the same to the State Board of Education for
approval .
Section 4482. Each board of trustees shall as
soon after June 30 , each year as possible have made
a complete audit of its accounts and business trans-
actions of the preceding school year either by the
Auditor of Public Accounts or by a competent out-
side auditor and shall publish the results of this
audit .
Section 4483. Boards of trustees shall make such
reports as may be required by the State Board of
Education and on such forms and blanks as may be
prescribed by the State Board of Education .
Section 4484. No new colored graded common
school district shall hereafter be created or organ-
ized , nor shall the boundaries of any colored graded
common school district hereafter be changed except
as heretofore provided in this Act. Such colored
graded common school districts as are organized
and established at the time this Act goes into effect
shall hereafter operate under the conditions and pro-
visions of this Act . Provided that no white person
shall vote at any election held in a colored graded
school district under the provisions of this Act ; nor
shall the property of any white person be taxed to
maintain any graded common school for colored chil-
dren ; nor shall the property of any colored person '
be taxed for the benefit or any graded common
school for white children ; nor shall any white child
attend any graded common school for colored chil-
dren organized under the provisions of this Act ;
nor shall any colored child attend any graded com-
mon school for white children .
§ 2. All laws and parts of laws in conflict with
this Act are hereby repealed .
Approved March 7 , 1922 .
laws.title_raw: AN ACT to repeal Chapter 38 of the Acts of the General As- sembly of 1920 , relating to the election and qualification of members of boards of trustees in graded common school dis- tricts ; also Chapter 46 of the Acts of the General Assembly of 1920 , relating to the establishment of independent , con- solidated , graded and high school ; also Chapter 25 of the Acts of the General Assembly of 1920 , relating to the condemna- tion of land by boards of trustees of graded common school districts ; also Section 4464 , Section 4500 , and all intervening sections , of the Kentucky Statutes , Carroll's Edition , 1918 , relating to the management and control of graded common school districts ; and in order to provide for a better system of graded schools and to provide for a more effective manage- ment and control of graded common schools in this Common- wealth , be there enacted in lieu of the above , the following sections , relating to the management and conduct of graded common school districts .

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 10, pp. 110–112
laws.summary: This act establishes two new normal schools for the training of white elementary teachers, one in the western part of the state and one in the eastern part. The schools will be managed by the State Board of Education and funded by the state, with a condition that significant gifts of land, buildings, or money must be received before state funds become available. The act explicitly states these schools are for 'white elementary teachers'.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 10 . AN ACT to provide for the establishment of two Normal Schools for the training of white elementary teachers , and appropriat- ing moneys for the maintenance and operation thereof. Whereas , the greatest need of common schools is trained ele- mentary teachers , and Whereas , the State Normal Schools already established can neither reach nor train all the elementary teachers needed for the common schools ; therefore , Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky : 1. That a Commission is hereby created , to be known as the State Normal School Commission , con- sisting of eight members who are citizens of the State of Kentucky and over the age of twenty -one years , to be appointed as follows : Five by the 1 Speaker of the House of Representatives and three by the Président of the Senate , which is hereby au- thorized and empowered to establish two new Nor- mal Schools for the training of white elementary teachers , one to be located in the western part of the State and one to be located in the eastern part of the State . The said Commission is hereby au- thorized to receive gifts of land , buildings or money for the establishment of these two normal schools for white elementary teachers .

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 10 .
AN ACT to provide for the establishment of two Normal Schools
for the training of white elementary teachers , and appropriat-
ing moneys for the maintenance and operation thereof.
Whereas , the greatest need of common schools is trained ele-
mentary teachers , and
Whereas , the State Normal Schools already established can
neither reach nor train all the elementary teachers needed for
the common schools ; therefore ,
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
1. That a Commission is hereby created , to be
known as the State Normal School Commission , con-
sisting of eight members who are citizens of the
State of Kentucky and over the age of twenty -one
years , to be appointed as follows : Five by the
1
Speaker of the House of Representatives and three
by the Président of the Senate , which is hereby au-
thorized and empowered to establish two new Nor-
mal Schools for the training of white elementary
teachers , one to be located in the western part of
the State and one to be located in the eastern part
of the State . The said Commission is hereby au-
thorized to receive gifts of land , buildings or money
for the establishment of these two normal schools
for white elementary teachers .
§ 2. The management and control of these two
normal schools , when established , shall be and is
hereby vested in the State Board of Education .
3. There is hereby appropriated , out of the
general funds of the State , to each of these two nor-
mal schools , for maintenance and operation , the
sum of thirty thousand dollars annually . The Audi-
tor of the Commonwealth is directed to draw his
warrants for said sums , above appropriated , upon
requisitions signed by the Chairman and Secretary
of the State Board of Education . Provided , that
the above appropriation for maintenance and opera-
tion shall not become available for said Normal
Schools until the said Commission has received for
each of said schools gifts of land suitable to the pur-
poses of each school , and also gifts of buildings or
money , or both , equivalent in value to at least one
hundred thousand dollars . Provided , further , that
if gifts and donations are made , sufficient to estab-
lish one of said schools , then the sum of thirty thous-
and dollars shall be available for the maintenance
and operation of said school .
§ 4. All laws and parts of laws in conflict with
the provisions of this Act are hereby repealed .
§ 5. If any section of this Act shall be held un-
constitutional the remainder of the Act shall not be
affected thereby .
Approved March 8, 1922 .

laws.summary: This act appropriates funds to the West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons at Paducah, Kentucky. It acknowledges the institution's contribution to preparing teachers for schools across the Commonwealth, particularly in rural Western Kentucky, and emphasizes the importance of continued support to avoid negative impacts on Black teachers and the institution's progress.

CHAPTER 100 .
AN ACT for the benefit of the West Kentucky Industrial Col-
lege , established at Paducah , Kentucky , making appropriations
thereto .
Whereas , in the year 1918 , the State appropriated the small
sums of $3,000.00 annually for the years 1918 and 1919 , and
$5,000.00 for the years 1920 and 1921 , each respectively , for the
benefit of the West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Per-
sons , at Paducah , Kentucky , the former appropriations based on
the condition that said institution should deed its buildings and
grounds to the Commonwealth of Kentucky , and ,
Whereas , the said institution did in the year 1918 , by its board
of trustees , execute and deliver to the said Commonwealth its
real property, buildings and grounds , to which same the Com-
monwealth now holds the fee simple title ; and ,
Whereas , it appears and is true that this institution during its
progress has prepared more teachers who were able to pass the
required examinations for State certificates , and thereby quali-
fied to teach in the schools of the Commonwealth , than any other
school at a similar per capita expense to the Commonwealth ;
Whereas , these teachers thus qualified are now satisfactorily
filling positions in numerous schools in the rural districts of
Western Kentucky , as well as in many cities therein , including
Hopkinsville , Mayfield , Paducah , and many other of the smaller
cities , towns and villages of Western Kentucky ; and ,
Whereas , since this college is thoroughly well established , and
is doing splendid service in the instruction and qualification of
teachers , and is recognized as a valuable aid to the school work
of the Commonwealth , it would undoubtedly be no less than a
calamity to cease the support of this institution , and would be
disastrous to the efforts of the negro teachers of Western Ken-
tucky , who have begun preparation for better teaching service ,
to be compelled to abandon their already well advanced work ,
and would also be unfair to those of Western Kentucky citizens
who have heretofore given of their time and means toward the
establishment of the college , to leave the institution " suspended
in mid -air " without any reasonably fair appropriation , which ap-
pears to have been done in omitting it from the "Budget Bill ; "
and,
Whereas , the small appropriations above mentioned were in-
sufficient to put the institution on the basis to which it is justly
entitled , but enough to have the effect of retarding any assist-
ance by way of private donations or assistance , and it is certain
that the institution will be compelled to close unless the Com-
monwealth gives it needed and deserved assistance ; now, there-
fore,
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That there be and now is appropriated out
of any unappropriated moneys in the Treasury of
the Commonwealth , the sum of six thousand ( $ 6 ,-
000.00 ) dollars for the purpose of improvements to
the buildings and grounds of the West Kentucky In-
dustrial College , and to said institution an annual
appropriation of fifteen thousand ( $ 15,000.00 ) dol-
lars for the support and maintenance thereof .
The appropriations hereby made shall be paid out
in the manner now authorized by law or may here-
after be authorized by law concerning appropria-
tions to said college .
Approved March 24 , 1922 .

CHAPTER 111.
AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance
of the various departments , boards , commissions , institutions
and agencies of the State Government , except for the legisla-
tive and judicial departments and except for the common
schools , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , designating
the funds and sources from which said appropriations are to
be paid , and prescribing the manner in which same are to be
paid.
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
1. That for the purpose of providing the neces-
sary funds for the payment of salaries , cost of main-
tenance and operation of each of the departments ,
boards , commissions , institutions and agencies of
the State government named in this act , for the fis-
cal year ending June 30 , 1924 ; there are hereby ap-
propriated out of the fund or funds specified here-
in the various amounts herein shown .
§ 2. Adjutant General .-Out of the general ex-
penditure fund produced by the annual levy of fif-
teen cents , as now provided by law , there are hereby
appropriated for the benefit of the Adjutant Gen-
eral's Department of the State for use for the fiscal
year ending June 30 , 1924 , the following sums for
the following purposes :
(a ) For the payment of salaries and clerical hire ,
$12.000.00 .
(b) For the payment of traveling expenses ,
maintenance and operation , supplies and repairs ,
including printing and postage necessary for the
use of said department , $7,500.00 .
(c) As an emergency fund for the use of said.
department , same to be expended only when the
emergency exists and upon the order and with the
approval of the Governor of the Commonwealth ,
$10,000.00 .
3. Attorney General .-There are hereby ap-
propriated out of the general expenditure fund , for
the use of the Attorney General's Department of
the Commonwealth of Kentucky for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1924 , the following sums for the
following purposes :
( a ) For salaries of the Attorney General , First ,
Second and Third Assistant Attorneys General and
Law Clerk , $ 14,900.00 .
(b) For all stenographic help , the salaries to
be determined by the Attorney General , $3,900.00 .
(c) For necessary traveling expenses of the de-
partment when engaged in the State's business ,
printing , stamps and office supplies , $1,250.00 .
4. Auditor of Public Accounts .-There are
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund for the use of the Department of the Auditor
of Public Accounts of the Commonwealth of Kentuc-
ky , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , as here-
inafter set out , the following sums for the follow-
ing purposes :
( a ) For salaries and clerical hire , $35,000.00 .
(b ) For printing , stamps , office supplies and
necessary traveling expenses , $4,000.00 .
§ 5. Department of Motor Vehicles .-There is
hereby appropriated out of the sums realized from
licenses on motor vehicles , for the benefit of the De-
partment of Motor Vehicles of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky , for the fiscal year ending June 30 ,
1924 , not exceeding seventy -five cents for each motor
vehicle registered under the provisions of the law
regulating the registration of motor vehicles in the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , same to be used for
the payment of salaries , clerical hire , traveling ex-
penses , printing , stamps , office supplies and license
tags .
§ 6. Department of Banking . For the purpose
of paying the expenses of the Department of Bank-
ing of the Commonwealth of Kentucky for the fiscal
year ending June 30 , 1924 , there are hereby appro-
priated and ordered to be paid out of the fees real-
ized from an examination of sundry banks and
building and loan associations , as provided by law,
the following sums for the following purposes :
(a) For the purpose of paying salaries , clerical
help , traveling expenses , printing , stamps and of-
fice supplies , $35,000.00 .
(b) For the purpose of paying salaries , clerical
help , traveling expenses , printing , stamps and office
supplies , in the operation of the Blue Sky Depart-
ment , there is hereby appropriated and ordered to
be paid out of the fees collected under the provisions
of the Blue Sky Department the sum of $9,000.00 .
7. State Board of Charities and Corrections.-
There are hereby appropriated out of the general
expenditure fund for the use of the State Board of
Charities and Corrections , having charge of the
charitable , correctional and penal institutions of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , for the necessary ex-
penditures for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 ,
the following amounts for the following purposes :
(a ) For the purpose of paying the salaries , cleri-
cal hire , traveling expenses , printing , stamps and
necessary supplies for said State Board of Chari-
ties and Corrections , and the cost of operation , main-
tenance , improvements , repairs and all operating ex-
penses for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , for
the State Reformatory at Frankfort , State Peni-
tentiary at Eddyville , Western State Hospital for
the Insane at Hopkinsville , Central State Hospital
for the Insane at Lakeland , Eastern State Hospital
for the Insane at Lexington , Feeble -Minded Insti-
tute at Frankfort , and the Houses of Reform , $1 ,-
250,000.00 .
For the same purposes , in addition to the said
sum of $1,250,000.00 , there is appropriated to the
said State Board of Charities and Corrections all
receipts of every character and kind realized by the
said board in the operation of each and every in-
stitution under the control and supervision of said
State Board of Charities and Corrections , including
the receipts realized by the said board from the
operation of convict road camps .
$ 8. State Board of Election Commissioners.-
There is hereby appropriated out of the general
expenditure fund , for the benefit of the State Board
of Election Commissioners , for the fiscal year end-
ing June 30 , 1924 , for the purpose of paying sal-
aries , all clerical hire , for printing , stamps and all
necessary supplies , the sum of $400.00 .
9. State Board of Health .-There are hereby
appropriated out of the general expenditure fund ,
for the use of the State Board of Health for the
fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , the following
amounts to be used for the following purposes :
(a ) For the purpose of paying salaries , clerical
help , traveling expenses , printing , stamps , supplies
and all other operating expenses , $ 70,000.00 .
(b) For the prevention of venereal diseases ,
$20,000.00 .
( c ) For the prevention and treatment of tra-
choma , $11,000.00 .
(d ) For the prevention and treatment of tuber-
culosis , $10,000.00 .
( e ) For the protection of the health of mothers
and children , in accordance with Section 3 , Chap-
ter 120 of the Acts of 1920 , to be spent in co -opera-
tion with the Federal Government and in connection
with funds received from the Federal Government ,
$21,298.84 .
§ 10. Department of Agriculture , Labor and
Statistics . There are hereby appropriated out of
the general expenditure fund for the use of the De-
partment of Agriculture , Labor and Statistics , for
the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , the following .
amounts for the following purposes :
( a) For the purpose of paying all the salaries
and clerical hire for said department , $12,000.00 .
(b ) For the purpose of paying the per diem ,
traveling expenses and other expenses now allowed
by law to the State Board of Agriculture , $3,500.00 .
( c) For the purpose of paying all the expenses
of the Department of Labor , under the said State
Department of Agriculture , Labor and Statistics ,
as now allowed by law or as may hereafter be al-
lowed by law , $ 9,000.00 .
(d ) For the purpose of paying all the expenses
of the Immigration Branch (free employment ) of
said department , as now allowed by law , or as may
hereafter be allowed by law, $2,000.00 .
(e ) For the purpose of paying for the station-
ery , printing , office supplies , equipment , telephone
and telegraph bills , express , freight and hauling
charges , and postage of said department , and travel-
ing expenses of Commissioner , $5,300.00 .
(f) For the purpose of paying
allthe expenses
incurred in the field work of said department of
Agriculture , Labor and Statistics , now permitted
and allowed by law, or as may hereafter be author-
ized by law ; for defraying the expenses of said de-
partment in collecting statistics , as is now or may
hereafter be allowed by law ; ' for paying special
premiums which said department is now or may
hereafter be authorized by law to pay ; and for
creating an emergency and co -operative fund for the
use of said department , as now or may hereafter be
authorized by law , $ 15,700.00 .
§ 11. State Board of Agriculture .-There are
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund , for the use of the State Board of Agriculture ,
for the Kentucky State Fair , for the fiscal year end-
ing June 30 , 1924 , the following sums for the fol-
lowing purposes :
(a) For salaries , traveling expenses , mainten-
ance and operation , $ 10,000.00 .
(b) For premiums for the Kentucky State Fair ,
$15,000.00 .
( c ) For the purpose of meeting other necessary
expenses for the conduct of the Kentucky State Fair ,
including additional premiums , all sums realized
by the State Board of Agriculture from the sales
of concessions , admissions , advertising , entry fees ,
stall rents , donations , exhibitors ' tickets , rent of
grounds , buildings , grand stand and midway show
receipts , are hereby appropriated to the State
Board of Agriculture , for the use and benefit of the
Kentucky State Fair .
§ 12. Confederate Pension Department .-There
are hereby appropriated out of the general expendi-
ture fund , for the benefit of the Confederate Pension
Department for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 ,
the following sums for the following purposes :
( a ) For salaries , including clerical hire , $ 4, -
600.00 .
(b) For the payment of pensions heretofore al-

(c ) For printing , stamps , office supplies and
other expenses of operation , $1,900.00 .
§ 13. Kentucky Confederate Home .-There are
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund , for the benefit of the Kentucky Confederate
Home, for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , the
following sums for the following purposes :
(a) For the salaries of officers and employes ,
$14,550.00 .
(b ) For all expenses of operation and mainten-
ance, $38,450.00 .
§ 14. Custodian of Public Buildings .-There are
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund , for the benefit of the Custodian of Public
Buildings , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 ,
the following sums for the following purposes :
(a) For all salaries of Custodian and other em-
ployes , $23,000.00 .
(b) For repairs , supplies , permanent improve-
ments of public buildings , and all other maintenance
and operating expenses , including printing , stamps
and office supplies , $40,000.00 .
No repairs nor improvements shall be made by the
Custodian of Public Buildings out of any part of the
fund appropriated for said purpose , except upon
order and approval of the Board of Sinking Fund
Commissioners .
are§ 15. Kentucky Geological Survey . There
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund for the Kentucky Geological Survey for the
fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , the following sums
for the following purposes :
(a ) For the purpose of making geological ,
chemical , technical , soil and other investigations
authorized by the provisions of Chapter 34 of the
Acts of 1920 , and for the purpose of paying all sal-

Geologist , field expenses , clerical assistance , labora-

all necessary miscellaneous items of permanent im-
provement to the property and effects of the Ken-

paying for all office expenses , printing and traveling
expenses , $23,000.00 .
( b) For the purpose of making topographical
surveys in co -operation with the United States Geo-
logical Survey , as provided by Chapter 34 of the
Acts of 1920 , $ 17,500.00 .
No part of the appropriation of $ 17,500.00 herein
provided for shall be used for the purpose of paying
any of the office expenses of this department .
§ 16. Department of Mines and Mining .- There
is hereby appropriated out of the general expendi-

for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , for the pur-
pose of the payment of all salaries , clerical hire ,
traveling expenses allowed by law, printing , stamps ,
supplies and all other costs of maintenance and
operation of said department , the sum of $ 23,800.00 .
§ 17. Department of Public Roads .-For the
purpose of paying all the costs of operation and
maintenance of the Department of Public Roads
and for carrying on its activities , for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1924 , there is hereby set aside and
appropriated to the Department of Public Roads
all of the funds now realized from the three -cent ad
valorem tax on each one hundred dollars of taxable
property in the State imposed by law , or any addi-
tional or other ad valorem tax that may be imposed
by law , for exclusive benefit of public roads , and
all funds realized from the automobile license tax
now collected by law , or that may hereafter be im-
posed and collected by law for the benefit of said
department and its activities . Out of said funds
so realized and collected for said fiscal year , there is
appropriated and authorized to be paid , for the pur-
pose of paying the salaries of the State Highway
Commission and of all persons employed in the cen-
tral office , all salaries of division engineers , all costs
of inspection and supervision , and the traveling ex-
penses of all persons authorized under the law to
draw same , together with all other expenses incurred
in the maintenance and operation of said depart-
ment , exclusive of money actually spent in the con-
struction of roads , the sum of $225,000.00 .
Said sum shall be so distributed and expended for
said purposes herein enumerated as , in the judgment
of the Commissioner of Public Roads , may be best
for the efficient operation of his department and the
carying on of its activities ; but not more than $ 60 ,-
000.00 of said $ 225,000.00 shall be expended for sal-
aries and expenses of the central office , including
salary and expenses of State Highway Engineer .
All of the fund appropriated by this section , ex-
clusive of said $ 225,000.00 , shall be used exclusively
by said department for the construction of public
roads , as now provided by law or as may hereafter
be provided by law .
§ 18. Eastern Kentucky State Normal School .

benefit of the Eastern Kentucky State Normal

the purpose of paying all salaries , traveling ex-

tution for said fiscal year , all money arising from
the tax of five -eighths of one cent on each one hun-

There is also appropriated out of the general ex-

benefit of said institution the further sum of $27 , -

maintenance of said Western Kentucky State Nor-

general expenditure fund for said fiscal year for
the use and benefit of said institution the further
sum of $27,000.00 for the purpose of erecting addi-
tional buildings , purchasing equipment and for the
necessary maintenance of said Eastern Kentucky
State Normal School .
§ 19. Western Kentucky State Normal School .
-There is hereby appropriated out of the funds
and from the sources hereinafter named , for the

the purpose of paying all salaries , traveling ex-

the tax of five - eighths of one cent on each one hun-

§ 23. Kentucky State Historical Society .- There

§ 24. Insurance Department . There is hereby
