Stock Sanitary Board , for the fiscal year ending
June 30 , 1924 , for the purpose of paying all salaries ,
traveling expenses , printing , stamps , supplies and
all other expenses incident to the maintenance and
operation of said department , as now provided by
law or as may hereafter be provided by law , the
sum of $35,500.00 .
$ 37. Superintendent of Public Printing .-There
is hereby appropriated out of the general expendi-
ture fund , for the use and benefit of the Superinten-
dent of Public Printing , for the fiscal year ending
June 30 , 1924 , for the purpose of paying all salaries ,
including clerical help , traveling expenses , printing ,
stamps and office supplies , $2,000.00 .
§ 38. State Tax Commission .-There are hereby
appropriated out of the general expenditure fund ,
for the use and benefit of the State Tax Commis-
sion , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , the
following sums for the following purposes :
( a) For the purpose of paying all salaries , in-
cluding clerical help , traveling expenses , printing ,
stamps , office supplies and other expenses incident
to the operation and maintenance of said depart-
ment , as is now or may hereafter be allowed by law ,
$70,000.00 .
(b) For the purpose of making a survey of the
mineral lands of Kentucky , in order that their value
may be more accurately ascertained , $ 20,000.00 .
$ 39. State Board of Examiners of Trained
Nurses . For the use and benefit of the State Board
of Examiners of Trained Nurses , for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1924 , there is hereby appropriated
and set aside for the purpose of paying all costs
of maintenance and operation of said board, all the
fees and other collections collected for the use and
benefit of said Board , as now provided by law or as
may hereafter be provided by law .
$ 40. State Treasurer .― There is hereby appro-
priated out of the general expenditure fund , for the
use and benefit of the State Treasurer's Depart-
ment , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , for
the purpose of paying all salaries , clerical help ,
printing , stamps , supplies and all other expenses in-
cident to the maintenance and operation of said de-
partment , now authorized by law or that may here-
after be authorized by law , the sum of $ 13,250.00 .
41. Vocational Educational Board .-There are
hereby appropriated for the use and benefit of the
Vocational Educational Board of Kentucky , for the
fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , the following sums
out of the following named funds and sources and
for the following named purposes :
(a ) For the purpose of carrying on Teacher
Training Instruction in the State of Kentucky , un-
der the provisions of Chapter 7 of the Acts of 1918 ,
there is hereby appropriated out of the general ex-
penditure fund , $24,987.00 .
(b ) For the purpose of paying all the costs of
inspection and supervision of the courses in teacher
training under the provisions of Chapter 7 of the
Acts of 1918 , there is appropriated out of the gen-
eral expenditure fund , $ 2,500.00 .
§ 42. University of Kentucky .-There are here-
by appropriated and set aside out of the funds and
from the sources hereinafter designated , for the
use and benefit of the University of Kentucky , for
the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , the following
sums from the following funds and sources and for
the following purposes :
(a) For the purpose of paying salaries and all
other expenses of maintenance and operation of the
Division of Colleges of the University of Kentucky ,
in the maner now authorized by law or as may here-
after be authorized by law , there is set aside and
appropriated all the tax of one and three -fourths
cents on each one hundred dollars of taxable prop-
erty in the Commonwealth , as now allowed and au-
thorized by law.
(b) For the purpose of pay for the cost of
maintenance and operation of the Experiment Sta-
tion of University of Kentucky for said fiscal year ,
as now authorized by law , or as may hereafter be
authorized by law , there is appropriated out of the
general expenditure fund the sum of $ 50,000.00 .
(c) For the purpose of paying all the costs of the
maintenance and operation of the Extension Divi-
sion of the University of Kentucky for said fiscal
year , in the manner now authorized by law or as may
hereafter be authorized by law , there is hereby ap-
propriated out of the general expenditure fund the
sum of $142,241.30 .
(d) For agricultural instruction , same to be
paid for out of the general expenditure fund , $ 30 , -
000.00 .
(e ) For the purpose of paying the Experiment
Station of the University of Kentucky for making
all analyses for the State Board of Health under
the provisions of Chapter 65 of the Acts of 1918 ,
and for making all analyses requested by any other
department of the State government , to be paid in
equal monthly installments , $ 18,000.00 .
(f) For permanent improvements , $ 100,000.00 .
(g) For payment on University debt , $ 45,000.00 .
$ 43 . Workmen's Compensation Board .- For the
use and benefit of the Workmen's Compensation
Board , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , for
the purpose of paying all the salaries , traveling ex-
penses , printing , stamps , supplies and all other ex-
penses of the operation and maintenance of said
board , as now provided by law or as may hereafter
be provided by law , there is hereby set aside and
appropriated all the funds now collected by law , or
that may hereafter be collected by law , for the bene-
fit
ofsaid Workmen's Compensation Board
.
§44. Commissioners
ofSinking Fund
.
-There
is
hereby appropriated and set aside
tothe use of the
Sinking Fund Commissioners for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1924 , the tax now allowed by law
of one cent on each one hundred dollars of taxable
property in the Commonwealth , to be used by said
Commissioners for the purposes now authorized by
law , or that may hereafter be authorized by law .
§ 45. Visiting County Nurses .-There is hereby
appropriated and set aside out of the general ex-
penditure fund for the fiscal year ending June 30 ,
1924 , for the purpose of contributing to the com-
pensation of Visiting County Nurses , under the
provisions of Section 4 of Chapter 51 of the Acts
of 1918 , the sum of $7,500.00 .
Said sum is to be paid out only in the manner
and for the purposes set out in said Chapter 51 of
the Acts of 1918 .
§ 46. Budget Appropriation Commission .-For
the use and benefit of the Budget Appropriation
Commission for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 ,
for the purpose of paying for clerical and steno-
graphic hire and all other expenses authorized to
be incurred by said Commission under the law , there
is hereby appropriated out of the general expendi-
ture fund the sum of $500.00 .
$ 47. State Printing Commission .-There is
hereby appropriated to the State Printing Commis-
sion , for the purpose of paying for the necessary
paper for use in State printing , for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1924 , in the manner now provided
by law , the sum of $55,000.00 .
§ 48. Clerk of the Court of Appeals .-There is
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund , for the benefit of the office of the Clerk of
the Court of Appeals , for the fiscal year ending
June 30 , 1924 , for the purpose of paying all salaries ,
printing , office supplies , janitor service and other
expenses incident to the operation of said office , the
sum of $ 14,500.00 .
$ 49 . Superintendent of Public Instruction.-
There is hereby appropriated out of the public school
fund of the State for the use and benefit of the De-
partment of the Superintendent of Public Instruc-
tion for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 , for the
purpose of paying all salaries , as now fixed by law
or may be hereafter fixed by law , for all necessary
clerical, stenographic and professional assistance
in the said department , the sum of $ 45,000.00 .
$ 50. Miscellaneous .-In order to meet and pro-
vide for the payment for the fiscal year ending June
30 , 1924 , of the sums necessary to pay the costs of
suits , attorneys ' fees , conveyance of lunatics to the
various asylums for the insane , commissions on fines
and forfeitures , compensation for County Tax Com-
missioners , as now provided by law, costs of crimi-
nal prosecutions , amounts due the various clerks of
the Commonwealth for their services and authorized
to be paid out of the State Treasury , cost and dis-
tribution of public books , express charges not other-
wise provided for in this act ; the cost of the care of
graves in the Frankfort cemetery , as allowed by law ,
the yearly allowances made to idiots by the various
circuit courts of the Commonwealth , interest on
outstanding warrants or on warrants that may here-
after be issued , the per diem compensation of the
Jury Commissioners of the various counties of the
Commonwealth , the per centum of Jefferson coun-
ty fees refunded to the various officers of Jefferson
county , as now authorized by law, the sums allowed
by law for the Law Library of the Commonwealth ,
to cover all moneys that may be required to be re-
funded as now provided by law , or as may hereafter
be provided by law , the cost of public books , includ-
Acts- 11
ing record books , compensation of the various coun-
ty boards of supervisors , any and all rewards au-
thorized by law, and any and all exonerations al-
lowed to the sheriff by law, any and all amounts
authorized by law to be paid to the trustee of the
jury fund of the various counties of the Common-
wealth , and any other general expenditures now al-
lowed by law and payable out of the general expen-
diture fund of the Commonwealth , the Auditor is
authorized and directed to draw his warrant for the
amount due , and the Treasurer is authorized to pay
the same , in the manner now authorized by law for
the payment of such claims . For the purpose of
paying all costs of operation of the Legislative De-
partment of the State government , and of the judi
cial department of the State government , the com-
mon school system and salaries of Commonwealth's
Attorneys , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1924 ,
and not specifically provided for in this act , the
Auditor of Public Accounts is authorized and di-
rected to draw his warrant and the Treasurer to
pay same in the manner now provided by law for
the payment of such claims .
§ 51. Each section of this act appropriating
money is designed to be a separate and distinct ap-
propriation , and , in event any appropriation made
is held to be unauthorized by law, it shall in no wise
affect the other appropriations provided for in this
act .
NOTE . The following endorsement appears on the enrolled
bill :
"For the reasons hereto attached I hereby disapprove and veto
the following items of appropriation in this bill :
"The appropriation of $ 100,000.00 contained in Subsection (f)
of Section 42 of bill for benefit of University of Kentucky ; the
appropriation of $45,000.00 contained in Subsection (g ) of Section
42 of bill for benefit of University of Kentucky ; the appropria-
tion of $27,000.00 contained in Section 18 of bill for benefit of
the Western Kentucky State Normal School ; the appropriation
of $27,000.00 contained in Section 18 of the bill for the benefit of
the Eastern Kentucky State Normal School ; the appropriation
contained in Section 2 of the bill for the benefit of the Adjutant
General ; the appropriation of $ 1,250,000.00 contained in Section
7 of the bill for the benefit of the State Board of Charities and
Corrections ; the appropriation of $225,000.00 contained in Sec-
tion 17 of the bill for the benefit of the Department of Public
Roads .
"EDWIN P. MORROW , Governor of Kentucky ,
March 24 , 1922. ”

laws.summary: This statute appropriates funds from the general expenditure fund for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1923. It specifically allocates funds to the 'Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children' and the 'Kentucky Home Society for Colored Children', as well as the 'Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons'.
key_provisions: § 25. Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children . There are hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure fund for the use of the Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , the following sums for the following purposes : ( a ) For the purpose of paying all salaries and every other expense incident to the operation and maintenance of said department , as now or that may hereafter be provided by law , $55,000.00 . (b) For the purpose of extinguishing the deficit heretofore incurred in the operation of said institu- tion , $11,000.00 .

§ 26. Kentucky Home Society for Colored Chil- dren . There is hereby appropriated out of the gen- eral expenditure fund , for the use and benefit of the Kentucky Home Society for Colored Children , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , for the pur- pose now authorized by law , or for such other pur- poses as may be hereafter provided by law , the sum of $20,000.00 .

§ 27. Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons .-There are hereby appropri- ated out of the general expenditure fund for the use and benefit of the Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , the following sums for the following purposes : (a) For the payment of salaries and all other expenses incident to the maintenance and operation AN of said department , as now provided by law or as may hereafter be provided by law , $40,000.00 . (b) For the purpose of paying premiums on in- surance heretofore written on said property , $5,500.00 . ( c ) For the purpose of paying an outstanding note of said institution , $4,500.00 .

§ 31. Kentucky Institution for the Education of the Blind . There are hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure fund , for the use and benefit of the Kentucky School for the Blind , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , the following sums for the following purposes : (a) For the payment of salaries and all other expenses incident to the maintenance and operation of the White Department of the Kentucky School for the Blind, fifty-five thousand . (b) For the payment of salaries and all other expenses incident to the maintenance and operation of the Colored Department of the Kentucky School for the Blind , eight thousand five hundred . (c) For the educational and vocational training of the adult Blind of Kentucky , to be expended in the manner and for the purpose now provided by law , or as may heheafter be provided by law , $20,000.00 .

§ 32. Kentucky School for the Deaf .-There are hereby appropriated out out of the general expendi- ture fund , for the benefit of the Kentucky School for the Deaf , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , the following sums for the following purposes : (a) For the payment of salaries and all other expenses incident to the maintenance and operation of the Department for White Children , $ 130,360.00 . (b ) For salaries and all expenses incident to the operation and maintenance of the Department for Colored Children , $ 9,000.00 . The appropriations herein provided for under this section shall be in lieu of any per capita allow- ance per pupil heretofore allowed by the State .

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 112 .
AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance
of the various departments , boards , commissions , institutions
and agencies of the State Government , except for the legisla-
tive and judicial departments and except for the common
schools , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 ; designating
the funds and sources from which said appropriations are to
be paid , and prescribing the manner in which same are to be
paid .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That for the purpose of providing the neces-
sary funds for the payment of salaries , cost of main-
tenance and operation of each of the departments ,
boards , commissions , institutions and agencies of
the State government named in this act , for the
fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , there are hereby
appropriated out of the fund or funds specified
herein the various amounts herein shown .
§ 2. Adjutant General . Out of the general ex-
penditure fund produced by the annual levy of fif-
teen cents , as now provided by law , there are hereby
appropriated for the benefit of the Adjutant Gen-
eral's Department of the State for use for the fiscal
324, COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY
year ending June 30 , 1923 , the following sums for
the following purposes :
(a ) For the payment of salaries and clerical
hire , $12,000.00 .
(b) For the payment of traveling expenses ,
maintenance and operation , supplies and repairs ,
including printing and postage necessary for the
use of said department , $15,000.00 .
(c) As an emergency fund for the use of said
department , same to be expended only when the
emergency exists and upon the order and with the
approval of the Governor of the Commonwealth ,
$20,000.00 .
§ 3. Attorney General . There are hereby ap-
propriated out of the general expenditure fund , for
the use of the Attorney General's Department of
the Commonwealth of Kentucky for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1923 , the following sums for the
following purposes :
( a ) For salaries of the Attorney General , First ,
Second and Third Assistant Attorneys General and
Law Clerk , $ 14,900.00 .
(b ) For all stenographic help , the salaries to be
determined by the Attorney General , $ 3,900.00 .
(c ) For necessary traveling expenses of the de-
partment when engaged in the State's business ,
printing , stamps and office supplies , $ 1,250.00 .
§ 4. Auditor of Public Accounts .-There are
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund for the use of the Department of the Auditor
of Public Accounts of the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky, for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , as
hereinafter set out , the following sums for the fol-
lowing purposes :
(a) For salaries and clerical hire , $ 35,000.00 .
(b) For printing , stamps , office supplies and
necessary traveling expenses , $4,000.00 .
(c) For files and rebinding of records in the
Land Office , $ 3,000.00 .
§ 5. Department of Motor Vehicles .-There is
hereby appropriated out of the sums realized from
licenses on motor vehicles , for the benefit of the
Department of Motor Vehicles of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 ,
not exceeding seventy -five cents for each motor ve-
hicle registered under the provisions of the law
regulating the registration of motor vehicles in the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , same to be used for the
payment of salaries , clerical hire , traveling expenses ,
printing , stamps , office supplies and license tags .
§ 6. Department of Banking . For the purpose
of paying the expenses of the Department of Bank-
ing of the Commonwealth of Kentucky for the fiscal
year ending June 30 , 1923 , there are hereby appro-
priated and ordered to be paid out of the fees real-
ized from an examination of sundry banks and build-
ing and loan associations , as provided by law , the
following sums for the following purposes :
(a) For the purpose of paying salaries , clerical
help , traveling expenses , printing , stamps and of-
fice supplies , $ 35,000.00 .
(b) For the purpose of paying salaries , clerical
help , traveling expenses , printing , stamps and of-
fice supplies , in the operation of the Blue Sky De-
partment , there is hereby appropriated and ordered
to be paid out of the fees collected under the pro-
visions of the Blue Sky Department the sum of $9 ,-
000.00 .
7. State Board of Charities and Corrections .
-There are hereby appropriated out of the gen-
eral expenditure fund for the use of the State Board
of Charities and Corrections , having charge of the
charitable, correctional and penal institutions of
the Commonwealth of Kentucky , for the necessary
expenditures for the fiscal year ending June 30 ,
1923 , the following amounts for the following pur-
poses :
(a ) For the purpose of paying the salaries , cleri-
cal hire , traveling expenses , printing , stamps and
necessary supplies for said State Board of Chari-
ties and Corrections , and the cost of operation, main-
tenance , improvements , repairs and all operating
expenses for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 ,
for the State Reformatory at Frankfort , State Peni-
tentiary at Eddyville , Western State Hospital for
the Insane at Hopkinsville , Central State Hospital
for the Insane at Lakeland , Eastern State Hospi-
tal for the Insane at Lexington , Feeble -Minded In-
stitute at Frankfort , and the Houses of Reform , $1 , -
250,000.00 .
For the same purposes , in addition to the said
sum of $1,250,000.00 , there is appropriated to the
said State Board of Charities and Corrections all
receipts of every character and kind realized by
the said board in the operation of each and every
institution under the control and supervision of
said State Board of Charities and Corrections , in-
cluding the receipts realized by the said board from
the operation of convict road camps .
8. State Board of Election Commissioners.-
There is hereby appropriated out of the general ex-
penditure fund , for the benefit of the State Board
of Election Commissioners , for the fiscal year end-
ing June 30 , 1923 , for the purpose of paying salaries ,
all clerical hire , for printing , stamps and all neces-
sary supplies , the sum of $400.00 .
9. State Board of Health .-There are hereby
appropriated out of the general expenditure fund ,
for the use of the State Board of Health for the
fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , the following
amounts to be used for the following purposes :
(a ) For the purpose of paying salaries , clerical,
help , traveling expenses , printing , stamps , supplies
and all other operating expenses , $ 70,000.00 .
(b ) For the prevention of venereal diseases ,
$20,000.00 .
(c) For the prevention and treatment of tra-
choma , $ 11,000.00 .
(d ) For the prevention and treatment of tuber-
culosis , $ 10,000.00 .
(e ) For the protection of the health of mothers
and children , in accordance with Section 3 , Chapter
120 of the Acts of 1920 , to be spent in co -operation
with the Federal Government and in connection with
funds received from the Federal Government , $ 21 ,-
298.84 .
(f) For the payment of one -third of the balance
on the purchase price of the State Board of Health
Building at 6th and Main Streets , Louisville , Ky . ,
$7,500.00 .
§ 10. Department of Agriculture , Labor and Sta-
tistics . There are hereby appropriated out of the
general expenditure fund for the use of the depart-
ment of Agriculture , Labor and . Statistics , for the
fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , the following
amounts for the following purposes :
( a) For the purpose of paying all the salaries
and clerical hire for said department , $12,000.00 .
(b) For the purpose of paying the per diem ,
traveling expenses and other expenses now allowed
by law to the State Board of Agriculture , $ 3,500.00 .
(c) For the purpose of paying all the expenses
of the Department of Labor , under the said State
Department of Agriculture , Labor and Statistics ,
as now allowed by law or as may hereafter be al-
lowed by law, $9,000.00 .
(d) For the purpose of paying all the expenses
of the Immigration Branch (free employment ) of
said department , as now allowed by law , or as may
hereafter be allowed by law , $ 2,000.00 .
( e ) For the purpose of paying for the stationery,
printing , office supplies , equipment , telephone and
telegraph bills , express , freight and hauling charges ,
and postage of said department , and traveling ex-
penses of Commissioner , $5,300.00 .
(f) For the purpose of paying all the expenses
incurred in the field work of said Department of
Agriculture , Labor and Statistics , now permitted
and allowed by law, or as may hereafter be author-
ized by law ; for defraying the expenses of said de-
partment in collecting statistics, as is now or may
hereafter be allowed by law ; for paying special pre-
miums which said department is now or may here-
after be authorized by law to pay ; and for creating
an emergency and co-operative fund for the use of
said department , as now or may hereafter be au-
thorized by law , $ 15,700.00 .
§ 11. State Board of Agriculture .— There are
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund , for the use of the State Board of Agriculture ,
for the Kentucky State Fair, for the fiscal year end-
ing June 30 , 1923 , the following sums for the fol-
lowing purposes :
(a) For salaries , traveling expenses , mainte-
nance and operation , $ 10,000.00 .
(b ) For premiums for the Kentucky State Fair .
$15,000.00 .
(c) For the purpose of meeting other necessary
expenses for the conduct of the Kentucky State
Fair , including additional premiums , all sums real-
ized by the State Board of Agriculture from the
sales of concessions , admissions , advertising , entry
fees , stall rents ,. donations , exhibitors ' tickets , rent
of buildings and grounds , and from pavilion , grand
stand and midway show receipts , are hereby ap-
propriated to the State Board of Agriculture , for
the use and benefit of the Kentucky State Fair.
12. Confederate Pension Department.-There
are hereby appropriated out of the general expendi-
ture fund , for the benefit of the Confederate Pen-
sion Department for the fiscal year ending June 30 ,
1923 , the following sums for the following purposes :
( a ) For salaries , including clerical hire , $ 4 , -
600.00 .
(b) For the payment of pensions heretofore al-
lowed , or that may hereafter be allowed , $ 320,000.00 .
(c) For printing , stamps , office supplies and
other expenses of operation , $ 1,900.00 .
§ 13. Kentucky Confederate Home .-There are
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund , for the benefit of the Kentucky Confederate
Home , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , the
following sums for the following purposes :
(a ) For the salaries of officers and employes ,
$14,550.00 .
(b ) For all expenses of operation and mainte-
nance , $38,450.00 .
( c ) For the purpose of paying deficit on pre-
miums due on insurance policies on property , $3 , -
700.00 .
14. Custodian of Public Buildings .- There are
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund , for the benefit of the Custodian of Public
Buildings , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 ,
the following sums for the following purposes :
(a ) For all salaries of Custodian and other em-
ployes , $23,000.00 .
(b) For repairs , supplies , permanent improve-
ments of public buildings , and all other maintenance
and operating expenses , including printing , stamps
and office supplies , $40,000.00 .
No repairs nor improvements shall be made by
the Custodian of Public Buildings out of any part
of the fund appropriated for said purpose , except
upon order and approval of the Board of Sinking
Fund Commissioners .
§ 15. Kentucky Geological Survey. There are
hereby appropriated out of the general expendi-
ture fund for the Kentucky Geological Survey for
the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , the following
sums for the following purposes :
(a) For the purpose of making geological , chem-
ical , technical , soil and other investigations author-
ized by the provisions of Chapter 34 of the Acts
of 1920 , and for the purpose of paying all salaries ,
including the salary of the Director and State Geo-
logist , field expenses , clerical expenses , clerical as-
sistance , laboratory , field equipment , supplies ,
freight charges and all necessary miscellaneous
items of permanent improvement to the property
and effects of the Kentucky Geological Survey , and
for the purpose of paying for all office expenses ,
printing and traveling expenses , $ 23,000.00 .
(b) For the purpose of making topographical
surveys in co -operation with the United States Geo-
logical Survey , as provided by Chapter 34 of the
Acts of 1920 , $ 17,500.00 .
No part of the appropriation of $ 17,500.00 herein
provided for shall be used for the purpose of paying
any of the office expenses of this department .
§ 16. Department of Mines and Mining .-There
is hereby appropriated out of the general expendi-
ture fund for the Department of Mines and Mining ,
for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1923 , for the
purpose of the payment of all salaries , clerical hire ,
traveling expenses allowed by law, printing , stamps ,
supplies and all other costs of maintenance and oper-
ation of said department , the sum of $ 23,800.00 .
§ 17. Department of Public Roads .-For the
purpose of paying all the costs of operation and
maintenance of the Department of Public Roads and
for carrying on its activities , for the fiscal year end-
ing June 30 , 1923 , there is hereby set aside and ap-
propriated to the Department of Public Roads all
of the funds now realized from the three -cent ad
valorem tax on each one hundred dollars of taxable
property in the State imposed by law , or any addi-
tional or other ad valorem tax that may be imposed
by law , for exclusive benefit of public roads , and
all funds realized from the automobile license tax
now collected by law , or that may hereafter be im-
posed and collected by law for the benefit of said
department and its activities . Out of said funds
so realized and collected for said fiscal year, there
is appropriated and authorized to be paid , for the
purpose of paying the salaries of the Commissioner
of Public Roads and of all persons employed in the
central office , all salaries of division engineers , all
costs of inspection and supervision , and the travel-
ing expenses of all persons authorized under the
law to draw same , together with all other expenses
incurred in the maintenance and operation of said
department , exclusive of money actually spent in the
construction of roads , the sum of $ 200,000.00 .
Said sum shall be so distributed and expended
for said purposes herein enumerated as , in the judg-
ment of the State Highway Commission , may be best
for the efficient operation of his department and
the carrying on of its activities ; but not more than
$ 50,000.00 of said $250,000.00 shall be expended
for salaries and expenses of the central office , in-

It mandates the recording of personal information such as name, sex, address, age, party affiliation, occupation, color or race, apparent weight, apparent height, and other means of identification. It also includes provisions for illiterate voters and for comparing signatures.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 138 .
AN ACT providing for a system of registration of every voter
in the Commonwealth of Kentucky ; providing for the appoint-
ment of officers for the purpose of registering voters of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky in every precinct in the State ;
fixing the time and manner in which the voters of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky shall register ; providing the manner
and means of such registration , and prescribing and naming
the qualifications of voters in the State of Kentucky ; fixing
the time a voter shall reside in the State , county and precinct ,
in which he or she votes ; naming a board for the purpose of
preparing necessary forms, blanks and books for the carry-
ing out of the provisions hereof ; providing for the administra-
tion of an oath to certain persons registering ; fixing the pay
of registration officers in each and every precinct ; providing
for the notification of voters in each and every precinct of the
time and place of sitting of the officers of registration in such
precinct ; providing for and designating certain days in the
year 1922 , and annually thereafter , when the officers of regis-
tration of each and every precinct shall sit for the purpose
of registering voters and amending and correcting and purging
the list of such precinct ; providing penalties for the violation
of the law ; providing for appeal to the circuit court ; repealing
Sections 1498 , 1499 , 1501 , Sections 1 and 2 Chapter 136 , Acts
of 1918 , Kentucky Statutes , Carroll's Edition , and repealing
any and all laws in conflict herewith .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. Every citizen of the United States , not other-
wise disqualified by the law of this Commonwealth ,
twenty -one years of age , or who will become twenty-
one years of age on or before the next regular elec-
tion to be held in November , who has been a resi-
dent of the State of Kentucky one year , and of the
county six months , and of the precinct in which he
or she offers to vote sixty days next preceding the
election and who has been registered as provided by
this Act, and who is otherwise qualified , shall be en-
titled to vote for all officers elective by the people ;
provided that any person who will be or become
twenty-one years of age on or before the regular
general election held in November as provided by
law , shall be entitled to vote in any primary election
held not more than six months prior to such No-
vember election for the nomination of candidates to
be voted for at such regular November election .
§ 2. It shall be the duty of the Board of Elec-
tion Commissioners of each county in the State not
later than the 20th day of June , 1922 and annually
thereafter to appoint for each registration precinct
in the county two judges , one clerk , and one sheriff
of election to act as such in their precincts all of
whom shall hold their offices for one year and until
their successors are appointed and qualified . The
County Executive Committees of the two political
parties having representation on the State Board
and County Boards of Election Commissioners may ,
on or before the 15th day of June, 1922 and anual-
ly thereafter designate in writing for each precinct
a list of not less than eight names to the County
Board of Election Commissioners ; and from these
names , if any are so designated , the officers of regis-
tration shall be selected from said lists as follows :
One judge at each voting place shall be selected
from each of said lists , and in like manner the sheriff
shall be chosen from one of said lists and the clerk
from the other . If no lists are submitted to the
said County Board , then the officers of the registra-
tion shall be so selected and appointed as that one
of the judges at each place of voting shall be of one
political party and the other judge of a different
political party , and there shall be a like difference at
each voting place between the sheriff and clerk of
registration . No person shall be eligible as an of-
ficer of registration who has committed a homicide ,
or who has been convicted of a felony or is under
indictment therefor , or who is not sober , temperate ,
discreet and of good demeanor , or who has anything
of value wagered on the result of the next election ,
or who is a candidate to be voted for at the next
preceding election , and who is not capable of read-
ing the Constitution of the Commonwealth in Eng-
lish and of writing a plain and legible hand . It
shall be the duty of said County Board of Election
Commissioners to determine the qualification of all
registration officers before appointment . The Coun-
ty Board of Election Commissioners shall have the
power to remove all registration officers who are
disqualified under the provisions of this Act , but
no such removal shall be made within five days of
any registration day, nor shall any such removal be
made at any time without cause, and the grounds
shall be reduced to writing by said Board and made
a part of its records . If a vacancy shall occur by
removal or otherwise , it shall be filled by the Coun-
ty Board of Election Commissioners from the list
already submitted , if any, from which the officer
was selected , and in conformity with the provisions
of this Act . The County Board of Election Com-
missioners shall give due notice of said appointment
of registration officers to the Sheriff of the county ,
who shall, before the day of the next ensuing regis-
tration and within ten days next after said appoint-
ments , give each officer of registration written no-
tice of his appointment . If there shall be two or
more contending Executive Committees of the same
party in the county , then that Executive Commit-
tee which is recognized by the State Central Com-
mittee , by the written certificate of the chairman
thereof, shall be recognized by the County Board in
making the appointment of registration officers .
Should the County Board of Election Commission-
ers fail to appoint such officers of registration , or if
any of such officers fail to attend for thirty minutes
after the time for commencing the registration , or
refuse to act , the officer in attendance representing
the same political party of the absentee shall ap-
point a suitable person to act in his stead for that
registration ; or if both representatives of the same
political party are absent , the qualified voters pre-
sent affiliating with the party of said two absentees
shall elect , viva voce , suitable persons to act in their
stead . Each officer of registration shall , before en-
tering upon the duties of his office , take an oath
faithfully to discharge his duties as such officer be-
fore some person authorized to administer an oath ,
or if no such officer be present it may be adminis-
tered by the clerk of the registration , who shall in
turn be sworn by one of the judges of registration .
The
Such officers of registration shall not hold office
by election or appointment during their term , nor
shall they hold office for one year from the first
day of July following his or her appointment .
acceptance of any office , either elective or appoin-
tive, by any such officer during his or her term of
office shall, ipso facto , vacate the said office .
3. Officers of registration shall have the same
power to preserve order at the polls of registration
as is exercised by sheriffs of election at the polls .
Said officers shall register every citizen of the Unit-
ed States of his or her precinct, who shall apply to
be registered at the time and in the manner re-
quired by law, who shall be twenty -one years of age
at the next election , who has been a resident of the
state one year , of the county six months , and of the
precinct in which such person offers to register six-
ty days next preceding the election . Every person
so applying to be registered shall be required to
sign his or her full name upon the registration book
of his or her respective precinct in his or her own
handwriting which signature shall be attested by
the clerk and sheriff of said precinct and there shall
also be entered on said book in proper place pro-
vided therefor the name of such person so applying ,
sex, the address of such person , his or her age at last
birthday , his or her party affiliation , his or her oc-
cupation , if any , at the time of such registration ,
the color or race of such person , his or her apparent
weight and apparent height and other means of
identification , and the date of registration . The
clerk of the election shall indicate at the bottom of
the form when such person voted at an election or
primary .
In the event any person applying to register upon
oath shall state that he or she cannot write his or
her name as above provided the clerk shall sign the
registration book for such person , and shall note
thereon that same was done at the request of the
person so registered and upon oath that such per-
son could not write .
Any judge of a primary or general election may
require any person to write his or her name for
comparison with such person's signature .
If the officers of registration entertain any doubt
as to whether or not any person offering for regis-
tration is entitled to such registration , or if any one's
right to register is challenged , citizens may be called
in, not exceeding three in number , who shall be ex-
amined touching the qualifications of such person
or persons who offer to register .
In making the registration the clerk shall act as
the recording officer , and the judges shall decide all
questions relating to the qualifications of persons
offering to be registered , except that , in case of a
difference of opinion between the judges , the clerk
shall have the deciding vote .
It shall be the duty of the sheriff of each county
to furnish a suitable and convenient place in each
precinct for such registration .
It shall be the duty of the officers of registration
in each precinct to return the registration books
and all paraphernalia to the County Court Clerk of
the county in which the registration is held not later
than three days after the holding of said registra-
tion , and said County Court Clerk shall make an
exact copy of all said registration books , both the
original and copies to be preserved in his office and
upon each primary , special or general election the
original registration books shall be turned over by
the Clerk to the regularly appointed clerk of elec-
tion of each respective precinct for their use in
holding said election .
§ 4. The Secretary of the State of Kentucky and
the Chairman of the Executive Committee of each
of the two dominant political parties of Kentucky
shall constitute and compose a board to prepare
proper blanks , forms and books for the registration
of voters as herein provided . It shall be the duty
of said committee or board to have said blanks ,
forms and books properly prepared on or by the
25th day of June, 1922 , by which date the necessary
Acts- 14
blanks , forms and books shall be in the hands of the
County Court Clerk of each county in the State for
distribution to the officers of registration in each
precinct of the State . Said blanks , forms and books
shall be printed and prepared and furnished as
other books are now printed and prepared for the
Commonwealth . Said blanks , forms and books shall
be paid for by each county out of the county treas-
ury , as is now provided by law for the payment of
any and all other blanks , forms and books furnished
each county by the State of Kentucky . Said book
shall be so arranged as that the names of voters
may be registered alphabetically and the form of
registration for each voter shall be as near in form
as follows :

5. Each officer
ofregistration shall receive
as
compensation the sum of two dollars per day for
each day they are required to register voters , and
one dollar shall be paid to the clerk of the registra-
tion for posting notices , to be paid out of the county
treasury .
§ 6. The registration officers in each and every
precinct of this Commonwealth shall on the second
Monday in July, 1922 , proceed to register the quali-
fied voters in said precinct , as provided herein , and
such registration officers shall, in the year 1922 , be-
ginning on the second Monday in July , sit for two
consecutive days , between the hours of 6 A. M. and
9 P. M. , for the purpose of registering the qualified
voters in each and every precinct , as herein pro-
vided . Ten days prior thereto the clerk of the reg-
istration shall post written or printed notices , fur-
nished him by the County Court Clerk , in at least
six conspicuous places in said precinct , stating the
time and place of such registration , and with in-
formation contained in such notices as to the re-
quirements of this law , that all persons in order to
be eligible to vote must be duly registered .
Sixty days preceding the regular November elec-
tion 1922 the officers of registration shall sit one
day, between the hours of 6 A. M. and 9 P. M. , in
each precinct , for the purpose of permitting any
and all persons who have not previously registered
to do so . Annually thereafter such officers of regis-
tration shall sit on the second Monday in July of
each year, between the hours of 6 A. M. and 9 P.
M. for the purpose of permitting any and all per-
sons who have not previously registered to do so ,
Iand the clerk of registration shall give notice , as
herein provided , of the time and place of all regis-
trations , for at least ten days before such date of
registration .
7. Whenever a registered voter changes his or
her place of residence from one election precinct to
another in the same county , or wherever the bound-
aries of the precinct are changed by law , it shall be
lawful for such voter to apply in person for a new
registration , and it shall be the duty of the County
Court Clerk of each county , who is the custodian
of the registration books , to proceed to register
such person in such precinct as heretofore provided
for, and upon the registering of such voter in said.
new residence the County Court Clerk shall pro-
ceed to cancel on the said books the name of such
voter. No person shall be entitled to vote in any
precinct unless he or she has been properly regis-
tered therein as herein provided , and the registra-
tion thereof having taken place at least sixty days
prior to such election .
Whenever any voter shall move from one county in
this State to another county in this State , such voter
shall apply to the County Court Clerk of the county
where he is registered directing the said Clerk to
cancel his name on the registration books and said
Clerk shall then deliver to the said voter a certificate
showing that his name has been cancelled on the
registration books . The voter then shall carry such
certificate into the county to which he is moving and
shall present said certificate to the officers of regis-
tration on the next registration day and the officers
of registration shall proceed to register him as pro-
vided in this Act and shall take up his certificate
and destroy it . The County Court Clerk of each
county shall keep a book arranged alphabetically
showing the names of the voters who have changed
their voting precincts , showing the precinct re-
moved from and the precinct removed to , and the
date of such transfer .
Any registered voter may , by application to the
County Court Clerk , change his party affiliation on
the registration books not less than sixty days be-
fore any primary or general election .
§ 8. Any person who shall disturb , intimidate ,
abuse or by force or other unlawful means hinder ,
delay or disturb , or attempt to hinder , delay or dis-
turb , any member of the officers of registration ,
while performing his or her official duties , shall
be guilty of a misdemeanor , and upon conviction
shall be fined not less than ten dollars nor more
than one hundred dollars .
§ 9. Any officer of registration who shall wil-
fully fail to perform his or her duty as set forth
in this Act , shall be guilty of a misdemeanor , and
upon conviction be fined not less than ten dollars
nor more than one hundred dollars .
$ 10 . When the governing authority for any city
or county of either of the political parties casting
the highest and next highest number of votes
at the preceding election shall desire it , the
County Board of Election Commissioners shall
appoint two officers for any precinct , whose duty
it shall be to purge the polls in that particular
precinct , and these officers need not reside in the
precinct for which they act . If the governing au-
thority for the city or county of either of such politi-
cal parties shall desire to have the registration
purged in any precinct , such governing authority
shall file a request in writing with the County Board
of Election Commissioners not later than the 15th
day of September after the regular registration
for that year . In filing such request , such gov-
erning authority shall give the name and address
of each voter whose name it challenges . When such
request shall have been filed , it shall be the duty of
the County Board of Election Commissioners , not
later than the first day of October , to appoint two
officers as aforesaid , one from each of the dominant
political parties as above described . These appoint-
ments shall be made from a list of five names sub-
mitted to the County Board of Election Commis-
sioners by the said governing authority of each of
such political parties , and when so appointed the
two officers shall be sworn to faithfully discharge
their duty. The list of challenged voters shall be
turned over to these two officers , and they shall meet
in the precinct for which they are to act, at some
place designated and provided by the sheriff . Their
first meeting shall be held in said precinct on Tues-
day after the first Monday in October , and they may
summon and swear witnesses . Each voter who has
been challenged shall be notified of the time and
place of meeting by a written notice addressed to
the voter at the residence given on the registration
books , and this notice shall be prepared and mailed
by the County Clerk at least five days before the day
of hearing. The notice shall require the voter to ap-
pear before the two officers mentioned therein .
After investigation and hearing such evidence as
may be presented these officers shall determine
whether the voter was properly and legally regis-
tered . If they find that he or she was not , his or her
name shall be stricken from the registration books
by said officers . If they find that he or she was
properly and legally registered , nothing further
shall be done with said name . The registration
books for the precinct shall be turned over to these
officers when they are to hold their meetings . In the
event the two officers engaged in purging the regis-
tration books shall disagree as to whether any name
shall be stricken from the books , they or either of
them shall reduce to writing the facts as developed
and certify such statement of facts to the Clerk of
the Circuit Court , who shall assign the case of each
such voter challenged to the Circuit Judge of such
county , and wherever there are two or more Circuit
Judges the cases shall be equally divided among said
Judges , who shall immediately hear the cases de
novo . The Circuit Clerk , upon receipt of such certi-
fication by the said officers , shall immediately issue
a summons addressed to the voter to appear before
the Circuit Judge to whom the case is assigned not
later than three days after the service of such notice ,
which notice shall be served by the Sheriff of the
county , or by any officer authorized to serve sub-
poenas , or by any persons authorized under our law
to serve notices . The Circuit Clerk shall be allowed
for each case the sum of fifty cents , to be paid by the
Fiscal Court out of the county treasury . If the Cir-
cuit Judge decides that the name should be stricken
from the registration books , he shall certify to the
County Clerk to strike such name off of the books ,
and if he decides that the voter is properly and
legally registered , he shall certify to the County
Clerk that said registration is valid . The two of-
ficers in charge of purging the registration may
meet from time to time until the second Tuesday in
October , but not later , and they shall receive for
their services the same compensation as registra-
tion officers .
§ 11. It shall be the duty of the County Court
Clerk to keep the registration books safely in his of-
fice and not to suffer same to be taken therefrom ,
except the registration books may be taken as pro-
vided herein from his office on order of any Court
for the purpose of using them in any prosecution or
trial growing out of the registration involving a
voter's right to register , and in any purgation pro-
ceedings . The Clerk shall permit any citizen at any
time to copy any registration book without fee or
charge , and he shall also furnish copies at the same
rate as provided in Section 15 of this act for copying
the book kept in his office . Copies furnished to
citizens under this section shall be paid for in cash
by the person ordering them .
§ 12. In the event any registration book of any
precinct is lost or destroyed by fire or otherwise , the
County Board of Election Commissioners shall
order a new registration of voters in said precinct
as provided in this Act .
$ 13. Whenever the registration books in any
election precinct are so mutilated , blotted , defaced
or otherwise in such condition as to render them dif-
ficult, troublesome or unsafe to use them longer , the
County Board of Election Commissioners shall
order that the said books shall be copied , and in such
case it shall be the duty of the County Court Clerk
to cause fair copies to be made of the old registra-
tion books and they shall take the place of the old
books which shall be filed and preserved in the office
of the County Court Clerk as the other books are
kept , but said County Court Clerk shall not destroy
the old books .
§ 14. Any voter aggrieved by the decision of
the two officers appointed to purge, may appeal to
the Circuit Judge by filing his affidavit stating that
his name has been stricken from the registration
book and that he appeals from said order , and the
Circuit Clerk shall docket his case in the same man-
ner as in the case of a disagreement between the
purging officers .
§ 15. The County Court Clerk , for his services
under this Act, shall receive the following fees , and
no other : For copying the registration lists re-
quired to be kept in his office , or to be used in supply-
ing lost books , the sum of three cents for each voter
whose name is so copied ; the sum of five cents for
the name of each voter stricken off the lists , and
three cents for transferring the name of a voter
from one precinct to another .
The fees and expenses incurred under this Act
shall be paid as other election expenses .
§ 16. Any person who shall cause himself to be
registered in more than one election precinct , or give
a false number of the ward of his residence , or more
than once , in the same precinct , or who shall cause
himself to be registered , knowing that he is not law-
fully entitled to registration , and any person who
shall aid or abet in the commission of any of said
acts , shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor , and
shall be imprisoned in the county jail not less than
one nor more than twelve months .
17. Any officer of registration , or other person ,
who shall unlawfully alter any registration book , or
add any name thereto , or who shall willfully secrete ,
suppress or destroy any such book , or who shall
make or aid in making any false or fraudulent reg-
istration book , shall be deemed guilty of felony , and
shall be confined in the penitentiary not less than
one year nor more than five years , and shall forfeit
any office he then holds , and shall forever be disqual-
ified from holding office .
§ 18. Any person who , by himself or in aid of
others , shall forcibly break , or attempt to break up,
a registration held as provided in this article , or
shall forcibly prevent , or attempt to prevent , any
person from approaching or entering a place of reg-
istration for the purpose of registering , shall be
fined not less than one hunded nor more than five
hundred dollars , or imprisoned not less than six nor
more than twelve months in the county jail , or both .
§ 19. Sections 1498 , 1499 and 1501 , Sections 1
and 2, Chapter 136 , Acts of 1918 of the Kentucky
Statutes , Carroll's Edition , be and the same is here-
by repealed .
§ 20. All laws or parts of laws relating to the
registration of voters in this State , conflicting with
the provisions of this Act, are hereby repealed .
NOTE : The following endorsement appears on the enrolled
bill :
"Vetoed and disapproved this March 14 , 1922 , for reasons at-
tached hereto .
March 14 , 1922. "
EDWIN P. MORROW ,
Governor of the Commonwealth of Kentucky .
On a separate sheet attached to the enrolled bill appears the
following writing :
"IN HOUSE .
March 15 , 1922 .
A message was received from the Senate announcing that they
had reconsidered and passed a bill which originated in the House
entitled :
H. B. 193. (For title see bill attached .)
Together with the objections of the Governor and his veto
to said bill and his reasons therefor to the contrary notwith-
standing .
The House having previously reconsidered said bill and passed
same in accordnace with the provisions of the Constitution the
Governor's objections and his veto thereto to the contrary not-
withstanding , the Speaker declared in open session and in the
presence of the House , in open session that said bill had become
a law .
Ordered that the Chief Clerk deliver said bill as originally en-
rolled together with the action of the House of Representatives
and the Senate of Kentucky to the Governor of the Common-
wealth .
Attest : CHAS . J. HOWES ,
Chief Clerk House of Representatives ."
"IN THE SENATE .
March 15 , 1922 .
A message having been received from the House of Repre-
sentatives announcing that they had passed a bill which orig-
inated in that body , the Governor's veto to the contrary not-
withstanding , of the following title , viz.:
H. B. 193. (For title see bill attached .) Together with the
Governor's objections to said bill and his reasons therefor .
Thereupon the Senate proceeded as provided by the Constitu-
tion to reconsider said bill , and after such reconsideration the
question was taken on the passage of said bill , the objections of
the Governor and his veto to the contrary notwithstanding , and
it was decided in the affirmative by a yea and nay vote duly
entered on the Journal of the Senate by a majority of all the
members elected to the Senate .
Ordered that the Chief Clerk of the Senate deliver said bill
with the objections of the Governor thereto and his veto to the
House of Representatives with the announcement of the action
taken thereon by the Senate in order that the House may in ac-
cordance with the provision of the Constitution sent said bill to
the Governor .
Attest : GATES YOUNG ,
Chief Clerk of the Senate ."
That the Chief Clerk of the Senate and the Chief
Clerk of the House of Representatives are re-
spectively authorized and empowered to employ the
following stenographers for their respective Houses ,
to -wit : Miss Annie Louise Deeds for the Senate and
1
Mrs. Jane Adams Clay for the House , to aid them
in the prompt and efficient dispatch of the business
of their respective offices , and said stenographers
so appointed shall each receive for their services
the sum of eight dollars per day. The Chief Clerks
of their respective Houses shall issue vouchers to
the persons entitled to the same, and the Auditor of
Public Accounts is directed to draw his warrants
on the Treasurer in payment thereof out of any
funds in his hands unappropriated .
Approved January 23 , 1922 .
laws.title_raw: AN ACT providing for a system of registration of every voter in the Commonwealth of Kentucky ; providing for the appoint- ment of officers for the purpose of registering voters of the Commonwealth of Kentucky in every precinct in the State ; fixing the time and manner in which the voters of the Com- monwealth of Kentucky shall register ; providing the manner and means of such registration , and prescribing and naming the qualifications of voters in the State of Kentucky ; fixing the time a voter shall reside in the State , county and precinct , in which he or she votes ; naming a board for the purpose of preparing necessary forms, blanks and books for the carry- ing out of the provisions hereof ; providing for the administra- tion of an oath to certain persons registering ; fixing the pay of registration officers in each and every precinct ; providing for the notification of voters in each and every precinct of the time and place of sitting of the officers of registration in such precinct ; providing for and designating certain days in the year 1922 , and annually thereafter , when the officers of regis- tration of each and every precinct shall sit for the purpose of registering voters and amending and correcting and purging the list of such precinct ; providing penalties for the violation of the law ; providing for appeal to the circuit court ; repealing Sections 1498 , 1499 , 1501 , Sections 1 and 2 Chapter 136 , Acts of 1918 , Kentucky Statutes , Carroll's Edition , and repealing any and all laws in conflict herewith .

AN ACT for the benefit of the Kentucky School for the Blind
and making appropriations therefor .

monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That for the purpose of promoting and in-
suring the safety of the sightlesspupils of the Ken-
tucky School for the Blind, located in the city of
Louisville,Kentucky,now subjectedtothemenace of
the boilersof the heating plant installedin the base-
ment of said schoolbuilding, occupiedas a dormi

exceed thirty-fivethousand dollars($35,000.00), to
be used forerectingand equippinga buildingtocon-
tainthe heating plant and laundry for white and col-
ored departments .
§2 . That in view of the urgent need of reducing
thefirehazard,and safeguardingthelivesofthepu-
pilsof saidKentucky SchoolfortheBlind,an emer-
gency is declared to existand thisact shalltake ef-
fectupon itspassage and approval by the Governor .

laws.summary: This act amends Chapter 53 of the 1920 Kentucky Acts concerning boards of education in third-class cities. It details the powers and duties of these boards, including financial management, property acquisition, teacher selection, curriculum, and the establishment of high schools. Crucially, it mandates 'separate buildings and schools for the education of white and black children.' The act also revises tax levies for school purposes.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 53 .
AN ACT to amend an act entitled "An Act to repeal and re-
enact Subdivision IX of Article IV of Chapter 89 of Kentucky
Statutes , Carroll's Edition , 1915 , and the amendment thereto
as provided in Chapter 78 , at page 393 of the Acts of the
General Assembly of Kentucky , passed at its regular session
in the year 1918 , and relating to the government of cities of
the third class, and providing for a system of public schools
and the election, qualification, term of office and meetings of
the board of education of said cities of the third class and the
number that shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of
allbusiness of said boards of education ,providing for the form
of the ballot and the manner of holding the elections for the
members of said boards of education , the manner of voting ,
the manner of fillingvacancies , the powers and duties of said
boards of education , the manner in which public school prop-
erty shall be acquired , held and disposed of, including the
right of eminent domain , the manner of selecting teachers ,
officers and employes and fixing their duties, terms and com-
pensation , the selection of courses of study and text books ,
the establishment of high schools , the publication of a printed
statement at the end of each scholastic year , a report to the
city auditor or clerk with reference to the financial needs of
the boards of education , limiting the amount of tax that may
be levied for school purposes , the submission to the voters of
the question of issuing bonds for school purposes when deemed
necessary by said boards of education , and the manner in
which said elections shall be held , the manner in which the
general councils or boards of commissioners shall provide an-
nually for the school fund , the power of the boards of educa-
tion to borrow money , the manner of levying and collecting
ad valorem , poll and license taxes , separate buildings and
schools for the education of white and black children , pro-
hibiting members of the boards of education from having any
financial interest in any contract made by the boards ; pro-
viding for the election of a treasurer , the continuance unim-
paired of all contracts and liabilities, taxes , sinking funds , in-
debtedness , bonded or otherwise , the manner in which funds
shall be paid out , that citiesof the third class shall each con-
stitute one school district for taxing purposes and providing
for the taking of a census ; providing for the choice of officers
for the board of education , including a secretary and the man-
ner of fixing his salary, the establishment and maintenance of
public school libraries, the admission of pupils outside the
limits of the city, the repeal of all inconsistent laws , except
special acts pertaining to certain cities and the recognition
of the existence of an emergency ," which act is Chapter 53 of
the General Assembly of the State of Kentucky as passed at
its regular session in the year 1920 , by repealing and re -enact-
ing Sections 9 and 12 of said Chapter 53 so as to authorize
and permit the levy for school purposes by cities of the third
class of not exceeding $1.50 on each $100.00 of all taxable
property therein , in addition to the poll tax, license fees, fees
on stock for breeding purposes , on franchises , trades , occupa-
tions and professions , and the ad valorem tax for interest and
sinking fund purposes , as now mentioned and provided for in
said Section 12 of said Chapter 53 ; and declaring an emer-
gency to exist .
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That section9 of chapter 53 of the Acts of
the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Ken-
