CHAPTER 64 .
AN ACT relating to registration for elections in citiesand towns
having a population of 5,000 inhabitants or more .
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . Every citizenof the United States,not other-
wise disqualifiedby thelaws of thisCommonwealth ,
who istwenty-one years of age,or who willbecome
twenty -one years of age on or before the next regu-
lar election to be held in Novermer or on or before
the date of any specialelection,who willhave been a
residentof the State of Kentucky one year, and of
the county sixmonths,and of the precinctinwhich
he or she offersto vote sixty days next preceding
such electionand who has been registered as pro-
vided by thisact, and who is otherwisequalified,
shallbe entitledto vote for allofficerselectiveby the
people and on allmeasures or questions submitted
for determination by the voters at any regular or
specialelection.
§2 . It shallbe the duty of the Board of Election
Commissioners of each countyin which islocateda
cityor town of the first,second,third or fourth class,
not laterthan the20thday ofAugust,1924,and an-
nually thereafter, to appoint for each registration
precinct in said city or town two judges, one clerk,
and one sheriffof registrationto act as such in their
precincts,allof whom shallhold theirofficesfor one
year, or untiltheirsuccessorsare appointed and
qualified. The County Executive Committee of the
two politicalpartieshaving representationon the
State Board and County Boards of Election Com-
mishioners may ,on or before the 15th day of August ,
1924, and annually thereafter, designate in writing
for each precincta listof not less than four names
to the County Board of Election Commissioners and
from these names ,if any are so designated,the offi-
cers of registrationshall, within fivedays, be ap-
pointed from said listsas follows:One judge at each
votingplaceshallbe selectedfrom each of saidlists,
and in like manner the sheriff shall be chosen from
one of saidlists, and the clerkfrom the other,and
sheriffsand clerksshallbe appointedalternatelyso
thateach of suchpoliticalpartiesshallhave ineach
cityor county as near an equal number of sheriffs
and clerks as possible. If no listsare submitted to
saidCounty Board of ElectionCommissioners,then
the officersof registrationshallbe so selectedand
appointedas thatone of thejudges at each placeof
registrationshallbe of one such politicalparty and
theotherjudge oftheothersuchpoliticalparty,and
there shallbe a likedifferenceat each registration
place between the sheriffand clerk of registration.
No person shallbe eligibleas an officerof registra-
tionwho has committed a homicide, or who has been
convictedof a felony or isunder indictment therefor,
or who isnot sober,temperate,discreetand of good
demeanor ,or who has anything of value wagered on
the resultof the next election,or who is a candidate
to be voted for at the next election, and who isnot
capable of reading the Constitutionof the Common-
wealth of Kentucky in English and of writing a plain
hand . It shallbe the duty of the County Board of
Election Commissioners to determine the qualifica-
tion of allregistrationofficersbefore appointment .
The County Board of ElectionCommissioners shall
have the power to remove all registrationofficers
who are disqualifiedunder theprovisionsof thisact,
but no such removal shallbe made within fivedays
of any registrationday , nor shallany such removal
be made at any time without cause,and the grounds
shallbe reduced to writing by said board and made
a part of its records. If a vacancy shall occur by
removalor otherwise,itshallbe filledby the County
Board of Election Commissioners from the list al-
ready submitted, ifany,from which the officerwas
selected, and in conformitywith the provisionsof
this act. The County Board of Election Commis-
sionersshallgivedue noticeof saidappointmentof
registrationofficersto the sheriffof the county,who
shall,withinfivedays next aftersaidappointments,
give each officerof registrationwritten notice of his
appointment . If there shallbe two or more contend-
ing executivecommitteesof the same politicalparty
in the county, then that executive committee which
isrecognizedby theStateCentralCommittee ofsuch
party, by the written certificateof the chairman
thereof, shallbe recognized by the County Board of
Election Commissioners in making the appointment
of registrationofficers.
Should the County Board of Election Commission-
ers failto appoint such officersof registration, or
if any of such officersfailto attend for thirtymin-
utesafterthe timeforcommencing the registration,
or refusesto act,the officerin attendance represent-
ingthesame politicalparty of the absenteeshallap-
point a suitableperson to act in his stead for that
registration; or if both representativesof the same
politicalparty are absent,the qualifiedvoterspres-
ent affiliatingwith the party of said two absentees
shallelect,vivavoce,suitablepersonsto actin their
stead. Each officerof registrationshall,beforeen-
teringupon the dutiesof his office, take an oath
faithfullyto discharge his duties as such officerbe-
foresome person authorizedto administeran oath,
or if no such officerbe present it may be adminis-
teredby the clerkof the registration, who shallin
turn be sworn by one of the judges of registration.
The acceptanceof any office, eitherelectiveor ap-
pointive, or becoming a candidatefor any elective
office,by any such officerduring his or her term of
officeas registrationofficer, shall, ipso facto, vacate
the said office.
§3 . If, in the opinion of the county executive
committeea politicalparty entitledto submit a list
of names of the County Board of Election Commis-
sioners, for appointment as officersof registration
as hereinprovided,thereare no personsin a given
precinctwho are qualifiedto act as officersof regis-
tration, representingsuch politicalparty, such
county executive committee shallhave the right to
submit to the County Board of Election Commis-
sionersa listof names of four persons who are non-
residentsof such precinct,but residentsof the city
or county inwhich such precinctislocated,and the
two officersof registration, to which the political
party sendingin such listis entitled, in such pre-
cinct, shallbe appointed from such list. Such lists
shall be sent in at the same time but separate from
theotherlistshereinprovidedfor. Provided,thatif
any politicalparty,entitledto submit a listof regis-
trationofficers,as hereinprovided,receivedtwenty-
fiveper cent of the votes cast in any precinctat the
precedinggeneralelectionsuch politicalparty shall
submit the names of residentsof such precinct for
appointment as registrationofficersin such precinct;
and, provided, furtherthat the judgment of such
county executivecommittee as to whether there are
persons residentof any precinct,in which thepolit-
icalparty represented by such committee failedto
receivetwenty-fiveper cent of the votes cast at the
precedinggeneralelection,qualifiedto actas officers
of registrationshallbe bindingon theCounty Board
of Election Commissioners .
§4 . Officersof registration, who are qualiñed,
shallbe eligibleto appointment as officersof election,
but so much of section1487,Kentucky Statutes,edi-
tionof 1915,as providesthatthe officersof election
shallbe the officersof registration, is hereby re-
pealed .
§5 . Each politicalparty having representation
on the State Board and County Boards of Election
Commissioners shallhave the right to appoint one
challengerin each precinctby certifyingthe name
of such challenger to the officersof registrationof
theprecinctand itshallbe the duty of such officers
to permit such challenger to remain in the place
where the registrationis being conducted for the
purpose of challengingthe rightof any person to
register.
§6 . Officersof registrationshallhave the same
power to preserve order at the place of registration
ås is exercisedby sheriffsof electionat the polls.
Said officersshallregisterevery citizenof the United
States of his or her precinct,who shallapply to be
registered,at the time and in the manner required by
law,who islegallyqualifiedto voteat thenext elec-
tionaftersuchregistration. Every person so apply-
ing to be registeredshallbe required to sign his or
her fullname upon the registrationbook of his or
her respectiveprecinctin his or her own handwrit-
ing, which signatureshallbe attestedby the clerk
and sheriffof said precinct and there shall also be
entered on said book in proper place provided there-
for the name of such person applying, sex, the ad-
dressof such person,hisor her party affiliation,his
or her occupation,if any,at the time of such regis-
tration,the coloror race of such person, hisor her
apparent weight and apparent height and other
means of identification,and thedate of registration.
The clerk of the election shall indicate at the bottom
of the form when such person voted at an election
or primary .
In the eventany person applyingto registershall
stateupon oath thathe or she cannot write his or her
name as above provided the clerkshallsign the reg-
istrationbook for such person,and shallnotethere-
on thatsame was done at the request of the person so
registeredand upon oath that such person could not
write. Any officeror challengerof a primary or
general electionmay requireany person to write his
or her name for comparison with such person's sig-
nature .
If the officersof registration, or any challenger,
entertainany doubt as to whether or not any person
offeringfor registrationis entitledto such registra-
tion, or ifany one'srightto registerischallenged,
citizensmay be calledin,notexceedingthreeinnum-
ber, who shallbe examined touchingthe qualifica-
tionsof such person or persons who offerto register.
In making the registrationthe clerk shallact as the
recordingofficer, and the judges shalldecide all
questionsrelatingto the qualificationsof persons
offeringtobe registered,except that,in case of a dif-
ferenceof opinionbetween thejudgestheclerkshall
have the deciding vote.
It shallbe the duty of the sheriffof each county to
furnish a suitableand convenient place in each pre-
cinctfor such registration.
It shallbe the duty of the officersof registrationin
each precinctto return the registrationbooks and all
paraphernaliato the county court clerk of the
county in which the registrationis held not later
than three days after the holding of said registra-
tion, and said county court clerk shallmake an ex-
act copy of said registrationbooks,both the original
and copiesto be preserved in his officeand upon each
primary,specialor generalelectionthe originalreg-
istrationbooks shallbe turned over by the clerk of
the county court to the regularly appointed clerk of
electionsof each respectiveprecinctfor their use in
holding said election.
$ 7. The Secretary of the State of Kentucky and
the Chairman of the Executive Committee of each of
the two politicalpartieshaving representationon
:
the State Board and County Boards of Election
Commissioners shallconstituteand compose a board
to prepare proper blanks,forms and books for the
registrationof votersas hereinprovided. It shall
be the duty of said committee or board to have said
blanks, forms and books properly prepared on or
beforethe 25th day of August,1924,by which date
the necessary blanks,forms and books shallbe in the
hands of the county court clerkof each county in the
State for distributionto the officersof registration
in each precinctof the State. Said blanks, forms
and books shallbe printed,prepared and furnished
as other books are now printed and prepared for the
Commonwealth . Said blanks,forms and books shall
be paid for by each county out of the county treas-
ury, as isnot provided by law for the payment of
any and allother blanks,forms and books furnished
each county by the State of Kentucky. Said book
shallbe so arranged that the names of the voters
may be registeredalphabeticallyand the form of
registrationfor each voter shallbe as near in form
as follows :
FORM OF REGISTRATION OF VOTERS .
Date of Registration .
Name of Voter
Address
(Number )
Term of Residence : State .
County .
Color .
Party Affiliation .
(City , town or postoffice )(Street )
Precinct .
Occupation .
Sex .
Apparent Weight
Apparent Height
Other Means of Identification .
Signature of Voter .
Attest :
Clerk
Sheriff
(Clerk of election will indicate below when above person
votes ) .
§8 . Each officerof registrationshall receive as
compensationthe sum of two dollarsper day for
each day they are requiredto registervoters,to be
paid out of the county treasury.
§9 . The registrationofficersin each electionpre-
cinct of this Commonwealth shall on the second Mon-
day inSepteraber,1924,proceedtoregisterthequal-
ifiedvotersineach precinct,as providedherein,and
such registrationofficersshall,beginningon the sec-
ond Monday in September in the year 1924, sitfor
two consecutivedays between the hours of six a. m .
and seven p.m .for the purpose of registeringthe
qualifiedvotersineach precinct,as hereinprovided.
Annually thereafter such officersof registration
shallsitin each precinct on the second Monday in
September ,between the hours of six a.m . and seven
p .m .,for the purpose of permitting allqualifiedper-
sonswho have not previouslyregisteredto do so.
§ 10. Thirtydays precedingtheAugust primary
electionin each year, includingthe year 1924, the
County Board of Election Commissioners in each
county, where registrationis requiredunder this
act,shallappointfour qualifiedvotersof each city
er town as specialofficersof registrationfor such
city or town . The county executive committee of
the two politicalpartieshaving representationon
the State and County Boards of Election Commis-
sionersmay , on or before forty days before the Au-
gust primary in each year, designatein writinga
listof four names to the County Board of Election
Commissioners and from thesefour names , if any
are so designated,the specialofficersof registration
shall be selected from said lists as follows : One
judge shallbe selectedfrom each of said listsand in
like manner the sheriff shall be chosen from one of
said lists and the clerk from the other . If no lists
are submitted to said County Board of ElectionCom
missioners then the special officersof registration
shallbe so selectedand appointed as that one of the
judges shallbe of one politicalparty and the other
judge of a differentpoliticalparty and thereshall
be a like difference between the sheriff and clerk of
registration. Said specialofficersof registration
shallhave thesame qualificationsas regularofficers
of registration,shallreceivethesame compensation,
and shallhold theirofficefor one year or untiltheir
successorsare appointedand qualified. Said special
officersof registrationshallbe notifiedof their ap-
pointment in the same manner as officersof registra-
tion are required to be notified.
Commencing on the fourteenthday precedingthe
August primary electionin each year such special
officersof registrationshallsitfor one day,in each
county in thisState,between the hours of 6 a.m .and
7 p .m .at thecourthouse,in a room providedby the
county court clerk, for the purpose of registering
allpersons who willbe legallyqualifiedto vote at
the next August primary electionand who failedto
register at the preceding September registration.
At such special registrationthe following persons
and no others shallbe entitledto register:
1. Any person who was absent from the county
of his or her residenceduring the entiretime of the
September registrationfor that year .
2. Any person who was prevented from register-
ing by reason of his or her own sicknessor by death
in his or her immediate family.
3. Any person who moved intothe precinctof his
or her present residence after the regular registra-
tionheld during the preceding year .
4. Persons who have become of age sincethe last
electionand have the qualificationsof electors.
No persons shallbe entitledto registerat such
registrationunlessthey have the qualificationsof
votersin theprecinctsinwhich they reside. Before
registeringany personunder thissectionthe special
officersof registrationshallrequiresuch person to
make written oath as to the cause of his or her fail-
ure to attendthe lastSeptember registration. All
affidavitsprovided for under this section shall be
kept in a bound book made for that purpose . The
names of allpersonsentitledtoregister,as provided
in thissection,shallbe recorded by the clerk of reg-
istrationin the regularregistrationbook for the pre-
cinctin which such person resides. The right of any
personto registershallbe determinedby the special
officersof registrationin the followingmanner :The
judges of such registrationshallhave the right to
determine such qualificationsand in case they dis-
agree then in the firstcase the clerk of registration
shallcastthe deciding vote and in the next succeed-
ing case, in caseof disagreementof thejudges,the
sheriffof registrationshall cast the deciding vote
and so during the entireregistrationthe clerkand
sheriffshall alternatein casting the deciding vote
when thejudges are unableto agree.
§11 . Commencing on the firstTuesday in Octo-
ber of each year such specialofficersof registration
shallsitfor two successivedays in each county in
thisState,between thehours of 6 a.m .and 7 p.m.,
at the courthouse,in a room providedby the county
courtclerk, for the purpose of registeringallper-
sons who willbe legallyqualifiedto vote at the No-
vember electionand who failedto registerat the pre-
ceding September registration. At such specialreg-
istrationthe following persons and no others shall
be entitledto register:
1. Any person who was absentfrom the county
of his or her residenceduring the entiretime of the
September registrationfor that year .
2. Any person who was preventedfrom register
ing by reason of his or her own sicknessor by death
in his or her immediate family.
No person shallbe entitledto registerat such reg-
istrationunlessthey have the qualificationsof voters
intheprecinctsin which they reside. Before regis-
teringany person under this sectionthe specialoffi-
cers of registrationshallrequiresuch person to
make written oath as to the cause of his or her fail-
ure to attend the last September registration. All
affidavitsprovided for under this section shall be
kept in a bound book made for thatpurpose. The
names of allpersons entitledto register,as provided
in thissection,shallbe recorded by the clerkof reg-
istrationin the regular registrationbook for the
precinctin which such person resides. The right of
any person to registershall be determined by the
specialofficersof registrationin the following man-
ner:The judges of such registrationshallhave the
righttodetermine such qualificationand in case they
disagree then in the firstcase the clerk of registra-
tionshallcastthe deciding vote,and in the next suc-
cedingcase, in case of disagreementof the judges
the sheriffof electionshallcast the deciding voțe,
and so during such entireregistrationthe clerk and
sheriffshall alternatein casting the deciding vote
when the judges are unable to agree.
Except in countiescontaininga populationof
more than 200,000inhabitants,the County Board of
ElectionCommissioners shallappointtwelve qual-
ifiedvoters of such county, which shallcompose
threesetsofregistrationofficers,tobe selectedinthe
same manner from listssubmitted by the county
executivecommittee of the two politicalparties
aforesaid .
§ 12. In each case where a specialelectionis to
be held in any county, city, town , or subdivision
thereof, eitherfor the purpose of fillingan elective
officeor the determination of any measure or ques-
tionsubmittedto the voters, the specialofficersof
registration,provided for in section10 hereof, shall
fourteendays beforesuch electionsitfor one day,
at the courthouse in a room provided by the county
courtclerkforthatpurpose,between the hours of 6
a.m .and 7 p.m .,for the purpose of permittingall
personswho have not previouslybeen registered,as
hereinprovided,and who are entitledto register,to
do so. No person shallbe entitledto registerat such
specialregistrationexceptunder the requirements
statedin section10 hereof and the same procedure
shallbe observed as provided in section10 hereof.
Provided,thatinadditiontotheclassofpersonsen-
titledto register, as specifiedin section10 hereof,
any person not previouslyregisteredand who is
qualifiedto register, who became of age afterthe
lastprecedingNovember election, shallbe entitled
to register.
§13 . Any otherwise qualifiedvoter being an offi-
cer or employe of the United States or of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky or traveling salesman may
appear before the county court clerk of the county
of his residenceon the day immediatelypreceding
or on the day of any general or specialelectionand
upon making oath to the effectthat he was absent
from his place of residenceon allgeneral or special
registrationdays during the currentyear, and that
his absence was due to or by reason of duties per-
tainingtosuchoffice,or business,theclerkshallreg-
ister said voter and when so registered the voter
shall have the right to vote in all elections until the
next succeeding general registration.
$ 14 . Whenever a registeredvoter changes his
or her place of residencefrom one electionprecinct
to another in the same cityor town ,or wherever the
boundariesof the precinctare changed by law, it
shallbe lawfulfor suchpersonto applyinperson
for a new registrationat the regular place of regis-
trationheld in the precincton the regulardays of
registrationand at any specialor supplemental days
of registrationheld at the courthouse in the county,
as hereinbeforeprovided,and itshallbe theduty of
the officersof registrationto proceed to register
such persons in such precinctsas heretoforepro-
vided for.Such person shallat the same time and be-
fore the same officersof registrationsign a certifi-
cate of cancellationin a separate book provided
thereforby the county courtclerk,givingthe place
of residence of his previous registrationand the

and other paraphernalia. The county court clerk

celledthe names of such persons in the precinctof

Any registeredvotermay changehisparty affilia-
tion on the regular days of registrationby appear-

The county court clerkof each county shallkeep a
book arranged alphabeticallyshowing the names of
the voterswho have changed theirvotingprecincts,
showing the precinctremoved from , the precinct re-
moved to and the date of such transfer .
§ 15. Any person who shalldisturb, intimidate,

turb, any officerof registration, while performing
his or her officialduties,shallbe guiltyof a misde-
meanor , and upon convictionshallbe fined not less

§ 16. Any officerof registrationwho shallwil-
fullyfailtoperform hisor her duty,as setforthin
thisact,shallbe guiltyof a misdemeanor , and upon
conviction be fined not less than ten dollars nor more

§ 17. When the county executive committee for
any cityor county of eitherof the politicalparties
having representationon the State Board and
County Boards of Election Commissioners shallde-
sireit,the County Board ofElectionCommissioners
shallappoint two officersfor any precinct, whose
duty itshallbe topurge the registrationlistin that
precinct,and these officersneed not residein the pre-
cinctfor which they act. If the cityor county com-
mitteeof eitherof such politicalpartiesshalldesire
tohave theregistrationpurged inany precinct,such
committee shall filea request in writing with the

than the 25th day of September in any year. In fil-
ing such request, such committee shallgive the
name and address of each voter whose name it chal-
lenges. When such request shallhave been filed, it
shallbe the duty of the County Board of Election
Commissioners,not laterthan the firstday of Octo-
ber, to appoint two officersas aforesaid, one from
each of the politicalpartieshaving representation
on the State Board and County Board of Election
Commissioners . These appointments shallbe made
from a listof names submitted to the County Board
ofElectionCommissionersby thesaidgoverningau-
thorityof each of such politicalparties,and when so
appointed the two officersshallbe sworn to faithfully
discharge theirduty . The listof challenged voters
shallbe turned over to thesetwo officers, and they
shallmeet in the precinctfor which they are to act,
atsome placedesignatedand providedby the sheriff.
Their firstmeeting shallbe held in said precincton
Tuesday afterthefirstMonday inOctober,and they
may summon and swear witnesses. Each voter who
has been challenged shallbe notifiedof the time and
place of meeting by a writtennoticeaddressed to the
voter at the residencegiven on the registration
books,and thisnoticeshallbe prepared and mailed
by the county court clerkat leastfivedays before the
day of hearing. The noticeshallrequirethe voter
to appear before the two officersmentioned therein.
After investigationand hearing such evidence as
may be presented these officers. shall determine
whether the voter was properly and legallyregis-
tered. If they findthat he or she was not,his or her
name shallbe strickenfrom the registrationbooks
by saidofficers. Iftheyfindthathe or she was prop-
erlyand legallyregistered,nothingfurthershallbe
done with said name . The registrationbooks for
the precinctshallbe turned over to these officers
when they are to hold theirmeetings and upon the
conclusionof theirmeetings the registrationbook
shallbe turnedto the county courtclerk. In event
the two officersengaged in purging the registration
books in citiesof the firstclassshalldisagree as to
whether any name should be strickenfrom the books,
they or eitherof them, shallreduce to writingthe
facts as developed and certify such statement of
factsto the clerkof the circuitcourt,who shallforth-
with assign the case of each such voter challenged to
thecircuitjudge of such county,and wherever there
are two or more circuitjudges in any county the
cases shallbe equallydividedamong said judges,
who shallimmediately hear the cases de novo . The
circuitclerk,upon receiptof suchcertificationby the
said officers, shall immediately issue a notice ad
dressed to the voter to appear before the circuit
judge to whom the case is assignednot laterthan
threedays aftertheserviceof suchnotice,which no-
ticeshallbe served by the sheriffof the county,or by
any officerauthorizedto servesubpoenas,or by any
person authorizedby law to serve notices. Such no-
ticesmay be served by deliveringa copy of itto the
person to whom itisdirected,or by offeringto de-
liverittohim ;or,ifhe cannotbe found,at hisplace
of residence as shown by the registrationbook , by
leavinga copy therewith a person over the age of
sixteenyears,residinginthesame familywith him ;
or,ifno such person be there,by affixingsuch copy
to the frontdoor of suchplaceof residenceand the
person who serves such notice must make an en-
dorsement on the noticestatingwhen and how itwas
served; and,ifa copy of itbe not deliveredto the
person towhom itisdirected,the indorsementmust
statethe factauthorizingthe manner of servicepur-
sued, and if the person who serves the noticebe an
officer, his indorsementmust show his officialposi-
tion; ifhe be not an officer,he must make an affidavit
thathis endorsement istrue,thathe isover sixteen
years of age,and thathe isnot a partyto,nor inter-
ested in the proceeding. Such indorsement of an
officer and such endorsement and affidavit of one who
is not an officershall be proof of the service. Such
officeror person authorized to serve the noticeshall
make a return within three days afterthe receiptof
such notice. The circuit clerk shall be allowed for
each case the sum of fiftycents, to be paid by the
fiscalcourt out of the county treasury. If the circuit
judge decidesthat the name should be strickenfrom
the registrationbooks,he shallcertifyto the county
court clerkto strikesuch name offof the books, and
if he decides that the voter is properly and legally

that said registrationisvalid. The two officersin
charge of purging the registrationmay meet from
timetotimeuntilthesecondTuesday inOctober,but
not later, and they shall receive for their services
the same compensation as registrationofficers.
Any voter aggrieved by the decision of the two
officersappointedto purge the registrationmay ap-
pealtothecircuitjudge by filinghisaffidavitstating
thathis name has been strickenfrom the registration
book and that he appeals from said order, and the
circuit clerk shall docket his case in the same manner
as in the case of a disagreement between the purging

§ 18. In any county not having thereina cityof
the firstclass, where registrationis required, any
votermay by givingfivedays'noticein writingto

the registrationbook, the word " doubtful," and
when at an electionsuch person, whose name is
marked "doubtful," shallofferto vote, he shallbe
sworn , and his right to vote investigatedfully.
$ 19. It shall be the duty of the county court
clerkto keep the registrationbooks safely in his of-
ficeand not tosuffersame tobe takentherefrom,ex-
cept the registrationbooks may be taken as provided

zens under thissectionshallbe paid for in cash by

$ 20. In the event any registrationbook of any
precinctislostor destroyed by fireor otherwise, or

isordered,notifyinwritingby registeredletterthe

missioners,but saidregistrationshallbe held on the

$ 21. The county court clerk, for his services
under this act, shallreceivethe following fees, and
no other:For copying the registrationlistsrequired
to be kept in his office,or to be used in supplying lost
books, the sum of three cents for each voter whose
name isso copied;thesum offivecentsforthename
of each voter strickenoff the lists, and three cents

$ 22. Any person who shallcause himself to be
registeredinmore than one electionprecinct,or give
a falsenumber of his residence, or registermore
than once, in the same precinct, or who shallcause
himselftobe registered,knowing thathe isnot law
fullyentitledtoregistration,or any personwho shall
make a falseoath as to his abilityto read or write,
or any person who shallaid or abet in the commis-

felony, and shallbe imprisonedin the penitentiary

$ 23. Any officerofregistration,or purgationof-
ficer,or otherperson,who shallunlawfullyalterany
registrationbook,or add any name thereto,or who

or fraudulentregistrationbook, shallbe deemed
guiltyof a felony,and shallbe confinedin thepeni-
tentiarynot less than one year nor more than five
years,and shallforfeitany officehe then holds,and
shallforever be disqualifiedfrom holding office.
$ 24. Any person who , by himselfor in aid of
others, shallforciblybreak up,or attempt to break
up, a registrationheld as provided in thisact, or
shall forciblyprevent, or attempt to prevent, any
person from approaching or entering a place or
making any falseor fraudulentregistering,shallbe
fined not less than one hundred dollars nor more
than fivehundred dollars, or imprisoned not less
than six months nor more than twelve months in the
county jail,cr both.
$ 25. The GeneralAssembly of Kentucky,at the
session of one thousand nine hundred and twenty-
two, enacteda law providingforthe registrationof
voters in each precinct of this State. Pursuant to
theprovisionsofsuch iaw,books fortheregistration
of voters were printed on orders of the proper au-
thoritiesin each county. Said law was declared to
be unconstitutionaland voidby theCourt ofAppeals
ofKentucky and thebooks,so printed,were notused
and no registrationwas heldunder theprovisionsof
saidlaw . The form for the registrationof voters,as
contained in said books .is identical with the form re-
quiredunder the provisionshereof, exceptthatthe
form contained in said books required each person
applying to register to state his or her age, said
requirement being omitted herefrom. In order,
therefore,to save the costof printingand furnishing
to the various countiesentirelynew books of regis-
tration,they shalluse saidbooks,heretoforeprinted
and reimburse the State for same and , in such use,
the officersof registrationshallnot require any per-
son applying to registerto statehis or her age, ex-
cept thateach person applying to registershallstate
that he or she ismore than twenty-one years of age .
$ 26. If any section,paragraph,clauseor separ-
able provision of this act should be adjudged to be
unconstitutional, such decisionshallnot affect, or
render unconstitutional, any other section, para-
graph, clauseor separableprovisionof the act, it
being the intentionof the GeneralAssembly,in en-
actingthis act, to enact each section, paragraph,
clause and provision separately.
§27 . This act and each of itsvarioussections,
paragraphs,clausesand provisionsshallbe liberally
construed in favor of the purposes of thisact.
$ 28. Ali laws or parts of laws relating to the
registrationof votersin thisState, conflictingwith
theprovisionsof thisact,areherebyrepealed.
Approved March 21, 1924 .

laws.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children and the Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1925. It also appropriates funds for the White Department of the Kentucky School for the Blind. The appropriations are for the purposes authorized by law or as may be hereafter provided by law, and include funds for extinguishing deficits.

CHAPTER 112 .

schools , for the fiscalyear ending June 30 , 1925 ; designating
the funds and sources from which said appropriations are to
be paid , and prescribing the manner in which same are to be
paid .

Attached to the foregoing Act is the following veto message
signed by the Governor of Kentucky , March 24, 1924 :
House Bill No. 534 having been delivered in my office on
March 13 , 1924 , and having been examined by me , I disapprove
of Section 37 , sub -section D thereof , appropriating to the Uni-
versity of Kentucky the sum of Fifteen Thousand ($15,000.00)
Dollars for the purpose of making investigations looking to the
prevention of diseases of tobacco , and other matters pertaining
thereto, because , in my judgment , the Experimental Station of
the University of Kentucky is and has been amply provided for,
and has sufficientfunds to make any investigations it deems ad-
visable to make in the interest of Agriculture .
In view of the present financial condition of the State on the
one hand , and the fact that the need is not imperative on the
other ,I feel impelled to disapprove sub -section F of Section 37 of
House Bill 534 that seeks to appropriate Forty -five Thousand
($45,000.00) Dollars for the construction of a Chemistry building
for the University of Kentucky .
With reference to Sub -section A of section 38 of House Bill
534. I approve of the Sixty Thousand ($60,000.00) Dollars recom
mended by the Budget Commission for the benefit of the State
Board of Health , and disapprove of the additional Ten Thousand
($10,000.00) Dollars added to the amount so appropriated by the
Budget Commission by the State Legislature by an amendment .
I further disapprove of sub -section F of Section 38 of House
Bill 534 which appropriated to the State Board of Health to be
used as a payment on the building located at Sixth and Main
Streets, Louisville, Kentucky , in the sum of Four Thousand
Seven Hundred and sixty ($4,760.58) Dollars and fifty-eight cents ,
for the reason that a recent legislative investigation committee
recommended a legal investigation of the title to said prop-
erty by the Attorney General of Kentucky , and his investigation
of said title has not as yet been made .
I also disapprove of Sub - section B of Section 42 of House Bill
534 , which appropriates Seventeen Thousand Five Hundred
($17,500.00 ) Dollars to the Department of the State Geologist
for cooperative work with the United States Geological Survey ,
other provision having been made for this Department by a
separate Act of the recent Legislature .
I disapprove of all of the foregoing sub -sections of House Bill
No. 534 , in addition to the reasons hereinbefore set out , because
the financial condition of the State does not , at this time , permit
these expenditures , and I therefore veto the sub -sections of the
sections heretofore mentioned .
All of the other provisions and appropriations contained in
House Bill No. 534 are hereby approved .
W. J. FIELDS , Governor of Kentucky .
March 24 , 1924 .

Attached to the foregoing Act is the following veto message
signed by the Governor of Kentucky , March 24, 1924 :
House Bill No. 535 having been delivered in my office on
March ,13,1924 , and having been examined by me ,I disapprove of
Sub -section D of Section 37 of said House Bill No. 535 , appro-
priating to the University of Kentucky the sum of Fifteen Thou-
sand ($15,000.00) Dollars for the purpose of investigating the
prevention of diseases of tobacco , and other matters relating
thereto , because , in my judgment , the Experimental Station of
the University of Kentucky is and has been amply provided for
and has sufficient funds to make any investigations it deems ad-
visable to make in the interest of Agriculture .
In view of the present financial condition of the State on the
one hand , and the fact that the need is not imperative on the
other , I feel impelled to disapprove of sub -section F , of Section
37 , of House Bill 535 , appropriating to the University of Ken-
tucky Thirty Thousand ($30,000.00) Dollars for the completion
of a chemistry building .
I also disapprove of Sub -section A of Section 38 of House Bill
535 , relative to the additional Ten Thousand ($10,000.00) Dollars
added to the amount appropriated by the Budget Commission by
way of an amendment by the State Legislature , and approve of
the Sixty Thousand ($60,000.00) Dollars recommended and ap-
propriated by the Budget Commission .
I disapprove of all of the foregoing sub -sections of House Bill
No. 535 , in addition to the reasons hereinbefore set out , because
the financial condition of the State does not , at this time , permit
these expenditures , and I therefore veto the sub -sections of the
sections hereinbefore mentioned .
I also disapprove of Sub -section B of Section 42 of House Bill
535 , which appropriates Seventeen Thousand Five Hundred
($17,500.00 ) Dollars to the Department of the State Geologist for
co-operative work with the United States Geological Survey ,
other provision having been made for this Department by a sep-
arate Act of the recent Legislature . I, therefore , veto the above
subsection B of Section 42 of House Bill 535 .
All of the other provisions and appropriations contained in
House Bill No. 535 are hereby approved .
W. J. FIELDS , Governor of Kentucky .
March 24 , 1924 .

laws.summary: This act appropriates funds for the improvement and expansion of state normal schools. Specifically, it allocates funds for four white normal schools (Richmond, Bowling Green, Murray, and Morehead) and for the Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons at Frankfort, as well as for a new normal school for colored people in the western part of the state. It also allocates funds for the Kentucky Geological Survey and the Kentucky School for the Blind.

CHAPTER 137 .
AN ACT for the benefit of the Kentucky School for the Blind
and making appropriations therefor.
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssembly oftheCom-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That for the purpose of promotion and in-
suring the safety of the sightlesspupils of the Ken-
tucky School for the Blind, located in the city of
Louisville, Kentucky, now subjectedto the menace
of the boilersof the heating plant installedin the
basement of said schoolbuilding, occupied as a dor-
mitory, thereishereby appropriateda sum not to
exceed thirty-fivethousand dollars($35,000.00) to
be used for erectingand equipping a buildingto con-
tainheating plant and laundry for white and colored
departments .
§2 . That in view of the urgent need of reducing
the firehazard, and safeguardingthe livesof the
pupilsof said Kentucky School for the Blind, an
emergency isdeclaredto existand thisact shalltake
effectupon itspassage and approval by the Gover-
nor .
Approved March 20 , 1924 .

There are hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure fund for the use of the Kentucky Home Society for White Children , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1929 , the following sums for the following purposes : (a) For the purpose of paying all salaries and every other expense incident to the operation and maintenance of said department as now, or that may hereafter be , provided by law, $ 80,000.00 .

There is hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure fund for the use and benefit of the Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1929 , for the purpose now authorized by law , or for such other purposes as may be hereafter pro- vided by law , the sum of $ 25,000.00 .

§ 36. Kentucky Institution for the Education of the Blind . There are hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure fund for the use and benefit of the Kentucky School for the Blind , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1929 , the following sums for the following purposes : (a) For the payment of salaries and all other ex- penses incident to the maintenance and operation. of the White Department of the Kentucky School for the Blind, $ 60,000.00 . (b) For the payment of salaries and all other ex- penses incident to the maintenance and operation of the Colored Department of the Kentucky School for the Blind, the sum of $ 9,500.00 . (c) For the education and vocational training of the adult blind of Kentucky , to be expended in the manner and for the purpose now provided by law , or as may hereafter be provided by law , $ 20,000.00 . (d ) For premium on insurance , $ 5,000.00 . (e) For a Workshop and Manual Training De- partment , the sum of $ 25,000.00 . (f) For a Junior Department Building for Girls , the sum of $33,000.00 .

CHAPTER 11 .

$600,000.00 .
Said sums shall be so distributed and expended
for said purposes herein enumerated as , in the judg-
ment of the State Highway Commission may be 'best
for the efficient operation of the department and
the carrying on of its activities , but no more than
$200,000.00 of said $ 600,000.00 shall be expended for
the cost of making preliminary and final location

000.00 herein specifically set apart , the Highway

dation of the Governor , set aside and expend out
of its revenues not to exceed $75,000.00 for co - oper-

supervision of the Director and State Geologist of
the Geological Survey .

of the Acts of 1920 , same to be paid from the

52. Insurance Department . There is hereby set

1929 , for the payment of salaries and all other ex-
penses of maintenance and operation of said depart-

lections to which said department is now entitled

$ 53. State Board of Examiners of Trained
Nurses . For the use and benefit of the State Board

appropriated for the purpose of paying all cost of

$ 54. Workmen's Compensation Board . For the
use and benefit of the Workmen's Compensation

the purpose of paying all salaries , traveling ex-
penses , printing , stamps , supplies , and other ex-
penses of the operation and maintenance of said
board , as now provided by law , or as may hereafter
be provided by law , there is hereby set aside and
appropriated all the funds now collected by law, or
that may hereafter be collected by law , for the bene-
fit of said Workmen's Compensation Board .
$ 55 . Department of Motor Transportation .
There is hereby appropriated out of the funds col-
lected under the provisions of Chapter 112 of the
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky of 1926 , for the use and benefit of the
Department of Motor Transportation , for the fiscal
year ending June 30, 1929 , for all salaries and ex-
penses incident to the enforcement of said act , as
provided by law, not to exceed the sum of $25,000.00 .
§ 56. Commissioners of the Sinking Fund . There
is hereby appropriated and set aside to the use of
the Sinking Fund Commissioners , for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1929 , the ad valorem taxes and other
revenues as now, or may hereafter be, provided by
law , to be used by said commissioners for the pur-
poses now authorized by law , or that may hereafter
be authorized by law .
$ 57 . Miscellaneous . In order to meet and pro-
vide for the payment for the fiscal year ending June
30 , 1929 , of the sums necessary to pay the costs of
suits , attorneys ' fees , conveyance of lunatics to the
various asylums for the insane , commissions on fines
and forfeitures , compensation for county tax com-
missioners , as now provided by law , costs of crim-
inal prosecutions , amounts due the various clerks of
the Commonwealth for their services and authorized
to be paid out of the State Treasury , cost and dis-
tribution of public books , express charges not other-
wise provided for in this act ; the cost of the care of
graves in the Frankfort cemetery , as allowed by
law, the yearly allowances made to idiots by the
various courts of the Commonwealth , interest on
outstanding warrants or on warrants that may here-
after be issued , the per diem compensation for the
jury commissioners of the various counties of the
Commonwealth , the per centum of Jefferson County
fees refunded to the various officers of Jefferson
46 COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY ·
County, as now authorized by law , the sums allowed

all moneys that may be required to be refunded as
now provided by law , or as may hereafter be pro-

boards of supervisors , any and all rewards auth-
orized by law , and any and all exonerations allowed
to the sheriff by law , any and all amounts author-
ized by law to be paid to the trustee of the jury fund
of the various counties of the Commonwealth , and
any other general expenditures now allowed by law
and payable out of the general expenditure fund of
the Commonwealth , the Auditor is authorized and

and the Treasurer is authorized to pay the same, in
the manner now authorized by law for the payment
of such claims . For the purpose of paying all costs
of operation of the Legislative Department of the
State government , and of the Judicial Department
of the State government , the common school sys-
tem and salaries of Commonwealth's Attorneys , for
the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1929 , and not speci-
fically provided for in this act , the Auditor of Pub-
lic Accounts is authorized and directed to draw his
warrant and the Treasurer to pay the same in the
manner now provided by law for the payment of
such claims .
§ 58. Each section of this act appropriating
money is designated to be a separate and distinct
appropriation , and , in event any appropriation
made is held to be unauthorized by law , it shall in
no wise affect the other appropriations provided for
in this act .
ACTS OF THE General ASSEMBLY 47
VETO MESSAGE
HOUSE BILL NO . 746
It is necessary for the State of Kentucky to live within its
income ; the Constitution requires it . The Budget Commission
undertook to distribute the limited funds of the State to its
several schools , institutions and agencies according to their
needs . When so distributed there would be no deficit , but the
General Assembly amended the budget bill by increasing the
amount of items in some instances and by putting in new items
in other cases , so as to augment the total several hundred thou-
sand dollars without making any provision for the raising of
this money . If the bill , as passed , should be approved the State
would be thrown in debt in a large sum . Everyone realizes that
most of the items thus added by the General Assembly were for
a good purpose and in almost every instance deserving . But
the State cannot spend money that it does not have . It must
cut according to its cloth just as a private citizen must do in
the operation of his business . Had the General Assembly levied
a tax sufficient to raise the revenue necessary for the payment
of these several different items to the budget , as submitted by
the Budget Commission , I would have felt warranted in approv-
ing most all of these items , but in the absence of such levy and
provision to meet the expense , some of these items must be and
are vetoed .
The items disapproved are given herein below :
Subsection (f ) of Section 30 , relating to the State Board of
Health and reading , "For Department of Bacteriology and
Epidermiology, the sum of five thousand and four hundred dol-
lars ( $5,400.00 ) for the increase of salaries of employees of such
department ." This item as originally proposed by the Budget
Commission was for three thousand dollars ( $3,000.00 ) , but was
increased by amendment to five thousand and four hundred dol-
lars ( $5,400.00 ) . I disapprove the increase of two thousand , four
hundred dollars ( $2,400.00 ) . But if the executive has power only
to veto an entire item and not merely that added by an amend-
ment to the budget bill , then the whole of this item is disap-
proved .
Item ( i ) of subsection (i ) of Section 30 , reading , " Repairs to
old building , roof, toilets and baths , etc. , ten thousand dollars
($10,000.00 ) ." This item is disapproved and stricken from the
appropriation .
Item ( 2 ) of subsection (i ) of Section 30 , reading , " Repairs
to central heating plant , fifty thousand dollars ( $50,000.00 ) ," is
disapproved and stricken from the appropriation .
Item ( 3 ) of subsection (i ) . of Section 30 , reading " Repairs to
laundry , twenty -five thousand dollars ( $25,000.00 ) ," is disapproved
and stricken from the appropriation .
Item (4 ) of subsection ( i ) of Section 30 , reading " Replacement
and repairs of hospital equipment , five thousand dollars ( $5,-
000.00 ) ." I disapprove this item , and it is stricken from the ap-
propriation .
Subsection ( e ) of Section 36 , reading , "For a workshop and
manual training department the sum of twenty -five thousand dol-
lars ( $25,000.00 ) ," is disapproved and stricken from the appro-
priation .
Subsection (f ) of Section 36 , reading , "For a Junior Depart-
ment Building for Girls , the sum of thirty -three thousand dollars
( $33,000.00 ) ," is disapproved and stricken from the appropria-
tion.
Item (e ) of Section 39 , reading , "For the maintenance and
improvement of the Blue and Gray State Park in Todd County ,
twenty-two thousand dollars ( $22,000.00 ) ." This item as orig-
inally proposed by the Budget Commission in the budget bill was
four thousand five hundred dollars ( $4,500.00 ) , and was increased
by amendment to twenty-two thousand dollars ( $22,000.00 ) . I
disapprove the increase of seventeen thousand five hundred dol-
lars ( $17,500.00 ) . But if the executive has power only to veto
an entire item and not merely that added by amendment to the
budget bill , then the whole of this item is disapproved .
Item ( d ) of Section 42 , reading , "For the Eastern State Hospi-
tal at Lexington for the purpose of paying for additional farm
lands , the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ( $25,000.00 ) , pro-
Ivided that in event the Board of Charities and Corrections and
the State Purchasing Commission are unable to purchase suita-
ble farm lands at a reasonable price before March first , 1929 ,
then this amount of twenty -five thousand dollars ( $25,000.00 )
shall become available for any other purpose named in para-
graph ( a ) of Section 42 ," is disapproved and stricken from the
appropriation .
There are other items that have been increased and other new
items added which for good reasons are not disturbed , among
them are items increasing the appropriation to the Industrial
College for colored people at Frankfort , and the Industrial
Schools for colored people at Paducah . These two institutions
have had but little help from the State during their existence ,
and have been doing great work . The dollars thus spent have
been stretched to cover as many of the needs of the institutions
as possible . When the increased appropriations are allowed to
stand these institutions will not have received their fair share
of aid from the State in comparison with other educational insti-
tutions of the State .
All other items of the budget bill , being House Bill No. 746 ,
not specifically mentioned in this veto message , are approved .
This March 24 , 1928 .
FLEM D. SAMPSON , Governor ,
Commonwealth of Kentucky .

CHAPTER 12 .
AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance
of the various departments , boards , commissions , institutions
and agencies of the State government , except for the legisla-
tive and judicial departments , and except for the common
schools , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1930 ; designating
the funds and sources from which said appropriations are to
be paid , and prescribing the manner in which same are to be
paid .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. Executive Department. There are hereby
appropriated out of the general expenditure fund
for the Executive Department of the State govern-
ment , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1930 , the
following sums for the following purposes :
(a ) For salary of the Governor , private secre-
tary and stenographic help and other employes ,
$13,900.00 .
( b ) For contingent and maintenance fund , $ 6 , -
000.00 .
(c) For printing , stamps , office supplies , extra
help , and operation of the department , $3,100.00 .
§ 2. Commissioner of Pardons . There are hereby
appropriated out of the general expenditure fund
for the use and benefit of the Commissioner of Par-
dons , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1930 , the
following sums for the following purposes :
( a ) For salary of the commissioner , $4,000.00 .
(b) For stenographic help , traveling expenses ,
stamps and stationery , $ 2,000.00 .
§ 3. Lieutenant Governor . There is hereby ap-
propriated out of the general expenditure fund for
the use and benefit of the Lieutenant Governor , for
the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1930 , for the purpose
of paying clerical hire and other expenses , the sum
of $2,500.00 .
§ 4. Secretary of State . There is hereby appro-
priated out of the general expenditure fund for the
use and benefit of the Department of Scretary of
State , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1930 , for
the purpose of paying all salaries , clerical help ,

penses incident to the operation of said department ,
the sum of $21,800.00 .
§ 5. Attorney General . There are hereby ap-
propriated out of the general expenditure fund for

(b) For stenographic help , the salaries to be de-
termined by the Attorney General , $ 11,100.00 .
( c) For necessary traveling expenses of the de-
partment , when engaged in the State's business ,
printing , stamps and office supplies , $4,000.00 .

priated out of the general expenditure fund for the
use and benefit of the State Treasurer's Depart-
ment , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1930 , for
the purpose of paying salaries , clerical help , print-

general expenditure fund for the use of the Depart-

(d) For the purpose of paying for the station-

$40,000.00 .

§ 12. Clerk Court of Appeals . There is hereby

§ 13. Railroad Commission . There is hereby ap-

§ 14. State Librarian . There is hereby appro-

§ 16. Department of Banking . There is hereby

of the Department of Banking , for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1930 , for the purpose of paying all
salaries , printing , stamps , supplies and other ex-

17. Kentucky Securities Department . There

§ 18. State Board of Election Commissioners .
There is hereby appropriated out of the general ex-

$ 19. Confederate Pension Department . There

(a) For salaries , clerical hire , printing , stamps ,

(b) For the payment of pensions heretofore al-

the Commonwealth , the auditor is authorized and di-
rected to draw his warrant for the amount due , and
the Treasurer is authorized to pay the same , in the
manner now authorized by law for the payment of
such claims . For the purpose of paying all costs of
operation of the Legislative Department of the
State government , and of the Judicial Department
of the State government , the common school system
and salaries of Commonwealth's Attorneys , for the
fiscal year ending June 30 , 1930 , and not specifically
provided for in this act , the Auditor of Public Ac-
counts is authorized and directed to draw his war-
rant and the Treasurer to pay the same in the man-
ner now provided by law for the payment of such
claims . '
58. Each section of this act appropriating
money is designed to be a separate and distinct ap-
propriation , and , in event any appropriation made
is held to be unauthorized by law, it shall in no wise
affect the other appropriations provided for in this
act .
1
VETO MESSAGE
HOUSE BILL NO . 747
It is necessary for the State of Kentucky to live within its
income ; the Constitution requires it . The Budget Commission
undertook to distribute the limited funds of the State to its
several schools , institutions and agencies according to their
needs . When so distributed there would be no deficit , but the
General Assembly amended the budget bill by increasing the
amount of items in some instances and by putting in new items
in other cases so as to augment the total several hundred thou-
sand dollars without making any provision for the raising of
this money . If the bill as passed should be approved , the State
would be thrown in debt in a large sum . Everyone realizes that
most of the items thus added by the General Assembly were for
a good purpose and in almost every instance deserving . But
the State cannot spend money that it does not have . It must
cut according to its cloth just as a private citizen must do in
the operation of his business . Had the General Assembly levied
a tax sufficient to raise the revenue necessary for the payment
of these several different items to the budget as submitted by
the budget commission , I would have felt warranted in approv-
ing most all of these items , but in the absence of such levy and
provision to meet the expenses , some of these items must be
and are vetoed .
The items disapproved are given herein below :
Subsection ( e ) of Section 30 , relating to the State Board of
Health and reading , "For Department of Bacteriology and
Epidermiology , the sum of five thousand and four hundred dol-
lars ( $5,400.00 ) for the increase of salaries of employes of such
department ." This item as originally proposed by the Budget
Commission was for three thousand dollars ( $3,000.00 ) , but was
increased by amendment to five thousand and four hundred dol-
lars ( $5,400.00 ) . I disapprove the increase of two thousand four
hundred dollars ( $ 2,400.00 ) . But if the executive has power only
to veto an entire item and not merely that added by an amend-
ment to the budget bill , then the whole of this item is disap-
proved .
In subsection ( e ) of Section 30 there is also this provision ,
"for infancy , maternity and child health , forty -seven thousand
dollars ($ 47,000.00 ) for the year 1929 to 1930. " This item is dis-
approved in toto and stricken from the appropriation .
In subsection (h ) , item 1 of Section 30 , there is a provision
reading : "To provide hospital building , fifty thousand dollars
($ 50,000.00 ) ." This I disapprove in toto and strike from the ap-
propriation .
Item ( 2 ) of subsection (h ) of Section 30 of the bill , reads :
"To provide equipment of beds , five thousand dollars ( $5,000-
.00 ) ." This I disapprove and same is stricken from the ap-
propriation .
Item 3 of subsection (h ) of Section 30 of the bill , reading :
"To provide kitchen equipment , fifteen thousand dollars ( $ 15,-
000.00 ) ." This is disapproved and stricken from the appropria-
tion .
Item 4 of subsection ( h ) of Section 30 of the bill reads : "To
provide equipment of treatment room , fifteen thousand dollars
( $ 15,000.00 ) ." This item is also disapproved and stricken from
the appropriation .
Subsection ( e ) of Section 36 , relating to Kentucky Institution
for Education of the Blind , reads : "For a junior department
building for boys , the sum of thirty -three thousand dollars
($33,000.00 ) ," and this item is disapproved and stricken from
the appropriation .
Subsection (f) of Section 36 , reading : "For the erection and
equipment of a building to contain swimming pool , gymnasium
and auditorium , the sum of seventy -nine thousand dollars ( $79 ,-
000.00 ) ." This is disapproved and stricken from the appropria-
tion .
Subsection ( e ) of Section 42 , reading : " For one -half the
amount necessary to purchase farm lands for the Eastern State
Hospital , twenty -five thousand dollars ( $25,000.00 ) , provided
however that in the event the Board of Charities and Correc-
tions and the State Purchasing Commission are unable to pur-
chase suitable farm lands at a reasonable price before July 10 ,
1929 , then this amount of twenty-five thousand dollars ( $25 ,-
000.00 ) shall become available for any of the purposes named in
paragraph ( a) of Section 42 ; or , if only a portion of this sum
be expended for farm land then any remaining part of the
twenty-five thousand dollars ( $ 25,000.00 ) may be used for pur-
poses named in paragraph ( a ) of Section 42 ," is disapproved
and stricken from the appropriation .
There are other items that have been increased and other new
items added which for good reasons are not disturbed , among
them are , items increasing the appropriation to the Industrial
College for colored people at Frankfort , and the Industrial
Schools for colored people at Paducah . These two institutions
have had but little help from the State during their existence ,
and have been doing great work . The dollars thus spent have
been stretched to cover as many of the needs of the institutions
as possible . When the increased appropriations are allowed to
stand these institutions will not have received their fair share of
aid from the State in comparison with other educational institu-
tions of the State .
All other items of the budget bill , being House Bill No. 747 , not
specifically mentioned in this veto message , are approved .
This Mach 24 , 1928 .
FLEM D. SAMPSON , Governor ,
Commonwealth of Kentucky .

laws.summary: This statute outlines the requirements for superintendents of state institutions to provide detailed information about patients, including their race, upon admission and during their stay. It establishes a framework for the management of patients categorized by mental health conditions, which historically has been used to enforce racial segregation in healthcare and institutional settings.
key_provisions: § 41. Patients ; What Immediate Information to Board to be Furnished Upon Admittance , Death , Discharge , Parole , Escape , Change of Committee . The superintendent of each institution , upon receiv- ing a patient , shall immediately furnish the board with the following information , viz .: Name , age , sex, color or race , former address , date of commitment , county from which committed , former commitments if any, together with the name of his committee and parents, or, if a married woman , the name of her husband . The superintendents shall also furnish the follow- ing information immediately upon the happening of the fact concerning which information is required , viz : Date of death or discharge with the reason therefor ; escapes , returns , removals and paroles of patients ; changes in the person designated as com- mittee for the patient.

$ 46. Distribution of Patients According to Ca- pacity of Institution ; Separation of White and Col- ored Patients . Whenever the number of patients sent to any asylum is greater than can be properly accommodated and cared for by that institution , and there is at the time capacity for the reception and care of the patients at any of the other asylums , it shall be the duty of the board of charities and cor- rections and superintendent of such other asylum to receive as many of those rejected at the former for want of room as can be properly accommodated . When , upon application to the proper asylum , the patient is rejected for want of room , immediate ap- plication shall be made to another . The board of charities and corrections is empowered and directed to take care that each of the asylums is kept full to its utmost capacity and such patients as are receiv- able by it, as long as any such patients in the state are unprovided for , and that each receive its due proportion of the patients in excess of the ordinary capacity of the asylum ; the white and colored pa- tients shall not be kept in the same building .

State Hospital at Lakeland , Ky., State Hospital for the Crim-

kinsville , Ky ., Feeble -Minded Institute at Frankfort , Ky., and
House of Reform for girls in Shelby County , Ky .; providing
