shall execute bond in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars
( $25,000.00 ) for the faithful discharge of his duties , and pre-
scribing his duties ; that no commissioner or other officer shall
sell anything to the institutions , and providing a penalty for
violation ; that the board may appoint superintendents , as-
sistants and other employees for each institution , fix their
salaries and prescribing their duties ; that the superintendents
of each institution for the Insane and Feeble -Minded shall
keep a register of all patients which shall contain a history
of each patient received into the asylum ; that the superin-
tendent of each institution shall keep a restraint record which
shall show the number of persons in each institution subject
to restraints which record shall be open to inspection of the
board at all times ; that the board may appoint a receiver and
prescribe his duties ; that the receiver shall execute bond
in a sum to be fixed by the board ; that the board shall pro-
vide for such officers and employees for each institution and
for such clerical and other assistants as it may deem neces-
sary ; that the board may not dispense with the office of
commissioner of public institution , superintendent or receiver ;
that no commissioner , officer or employee of the Board of
Charities and Corrections or any of the institutions under
its control shall accept a free gift from any person or cor-
poration who has or had a contract with said board or any of
its institutions under its control , and fixing a penalty for
violation ; providing that all officers and servants of each in-
stitution shall be exempt from military duty, from working
on the public highways , from service on juries ; that no officer
or servant shall be required to give personal attendance as a
witness in any civil suit out of the county , but their depositions
may be required in lieu thereof ; that the fiscal years of the
institution shall begin July 1st and close June 30th ; the
superintendents of each institution and Board of Charities and
Corrections shall make a report to the Governor of the con-
dition of the institutions under their charge which report the
Governor shall communicate to the Legislature at its next
regular session ; that each superintendent in charge of an in-
stitution shall prepare and submit to the board annually , or
as often as required , a budget or estimate of the expenditures
required for the maintenance of such institution ; that the
board shall prepare annually a budget for all the institutions
and agencies under its control and submit same to the Gov-
ernor or the Budget Commission ; the board may apportion
its appropriation made for the benefit of the institutions as
between the various institutions in such manner as the in-
terest of such institutions require ; that the appropriation
made for the Board of Charities and Corrections shall be pay-
able by warrant drawn by the Auditor monthly for such sums
of money as are necessary to operate the institutions under
its control, including salaries to all officers and employees .
The order shall be signed by the Commissioner of Public In-
stitutions and approved by the chairman of the board ; pre-
scribing the duty of the Auditor ; providing that the super-
intendent of each institution shall have power to purchase
necessary incidental and emergency supplies for his institu-
tion subject to the approval of the Board of Charities and
Corrections . The superintendent of each institution shall ex-
amine all claims and accounts against their respective in-
stitutions and report any irregularity to the board . They
shall not direct any claim to be paid unless it is just , legal
and right . Providing that the Commissioner of Public Insti-
tutions shall keep a record of the payment of money , receipts ,
deposits and disbursements ; that the Governor may direct the
State Inspector and Examiner to inspect the books and ac-
counts of the Board of Charities and Corrections or any in-
stitution , and make the report of the financial condition and
management of any institution under the control of said
board ; that said board shall have full control of all institutions
named in this act , and that it is their duty to inquire and ex-
amine into the government and management of the inmates ,
official conduct of officers and employees , conditions of build-
ings and grounds , and for any neglect or refusal on the part
of members of said board they shall be subject to a penalty
of two hundred and fifty dollars ( $250.00 ) ; that said board is
authorized to keep the buildings , furniture and other property
under their control insured ; that they are authorized to cancel
at any time , or cause to be cancelled , any insurance in their
judgment ; that the board may issue license to charitable
organizations supported in whole or in part by appropriations
from the State Treasury ; that no such organizations or repre-
sentative thereof shall solicit outside the county in which it is
located ; that any person violating this provision may be fined
in any sum not less than fifty dollars ( $ 50.00 ) nor more than
two hundred dollars ( $200.00 ) ; that the board is vested with
the power of eminent domain and the procedure to condemn
real estate is the same as condemnation proceedings for rail-
road purposes ; that the University of Kentucky shall , at the
request of the Board of Charities and Corrections , examine
and report on any lands or soils which the board may wish
to investigate , and to advise said board of the quality and
character of soil , water supply , sanitation , agricultural and
engineering problems . The services rendered by said Uni-
versity shall be free , but it shall be entitled to receive its
necessary expenses in making said investigations , and said
Board of Charities and Corrections shall make such rules and
regulations as are necessary for the management and control
of the institutions named in this act .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
1. Powers and Duties of Board . The State
Board of Charities and Corrections is hereby vested
with authority to and shall , except as otherwise
hereinafter provided , exercise all the powers and
privileges and discharge all the duties connected
with or necessary to carry out the purposes for
which said board was created .
2. Corporate Powers . The board shall be a
body politic and corporate and have the powers to
sue and be sued , contract and be contracted with ,
and is invested with all the powers necessary to
carry into full effect the purposes of its establish-
ment .
§ 3. Institutions Under Board of Charities and
Corrections . The institutions hereby placed under
the control and management of the State Board of
Charities and Corrections are nine in number and
are as follows :
State Reformatory at Frankfort , Ky .
State Penitentiary at Eddyville , Ky .
Houses of Reform , Greendale , Ky .
Eastern State Hospital at Lexington , Ky .
Central State Hospital at Lakeland , Ky .
State Hospital for the Criminally Insane , Lake-
land , Ky .
Western State Hospital at Hopkinsville , Ky.
Feeble -Minded Institute at Frankfort , Ky .
House of Reform for Girls in Shelby County , Ky.
§ 4. Regulations Governing Institutions ; Politi-
cal Activity Prohibited ; Penalty . The board shall
make rules and regulations for the strictly non-
partisan management of the institutions under its
control . Any member or employee of the board, or
any officer or employee of any institution under its
control , who shall engage in political activity or who
shall in any manner contribute , or cause to be con-
tributed , money or any other thing of value to any.
person for election purposes , or who shall influence
or attempt to influence legislation through the in-
strumentality of his official position , shall be re-
moved from his office or position by the board in
case of an officer or employee , and by the governor
in case of a member of the board . Any person or
persons wilfully violating the provisions of this sec-
tion shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and
shall be fined in any sum not less than fifty ( $ 50.00 )
nor more than one thousand dollars ( $ 1,000.00 ) .
§ 5. Commissioner of Public Institutions ; Pow-
ers and Duties ; Removal ; Purchase of Supplies . The
board shall appoint as its principal agent a person
to be known as the Commissioner of Public Institu-
tions and shall fix his compensation . Said commis-
sioner of public institutions shall have general
charge , subject to the supervision and control of the
board , of the institutions of the state which are un-
der the jurisdiction of said board and shall perform
such duties and exercise such powers as the board
may , from time to time , direct . Said commissioner
shall be subject to removal by the board at any time .
The commissioner of public institutions shall, except
as provided for in the duties of the State Purchasing
Commission , under the direction and authority of
the board and with its approval , establish and en-
force a system of open and competitive bidding on ,
and purchasing of , all institution supplies where and
whenever such supplies can be so purchased to the
advantage of the state and its wards , and in making
such purchases , supplies common to two or more in-
stitutions may be included in one contract .
§ 6. Oath of Office ; Bond . Before entering upon
his duties the commissioner of public institutions
shall take the oath of office required of other state
officers , a record of which shall be entered upon the
executive journal in the governor's office , and he
shall execute a bond to the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky in the sum of twenty -five thousand ($ 25,000 )
for the faithful discharge of his duties and shall
give as surety on said bond a solvent and recognized
surety or guarantee company , the premium on same
to be paid by the state . Said bond to be sufficient
must be approved by the chairman of the board and
filed in the office of the secretary of state .
§ 7. Members of Board and Officers Forbidden
to Make Contracts With Institutions ; Penalty . No
commissioner or other officer shall sell anything to
the institutions herein mentioned , or make any con-
tract with them in which he is directly or indirectly
interested . Any violation of this act shall subject
the person so offending to a fine of not less than two
hundred and fifty dollars nor more than one thous-
and dollars upon conviction had upon indictment by
the grand jury of the county in which is situated
the institution to which the articles were sold or
with which, or any of the officers of which , the con-
tract was made .
$ 8. Superintendent and Receiver for Each In-
stitution ; Compensation . The board shall appoint ,
upon the recommendation of the commissioner of
public institutions , a superintendent and receiver
for each of the institutions under its management
and control , and shall fix the compensation of each
of said superintendents and receivers .
9. Qualifications , Employment and Discharge
of Officers and Employees ; Salaries . The qualifica- .
tions of the superintendent and of all assistants and
employees in each institution shall be such as the
board may prescribe , provided , however , that the
superintendent of the house of reform for girls shall
be a woman . The superintendents shall employ such
number of officers and employees and at such salar-
ies as the board may from time to time prescribe ,
but the superintendent of each institution shall have
full authority to employ and discharge all officers
and employees of his or her respective institutions
except the receiver or other officer or employee
charged with the duty of buying or receiving of sup-
plies , which officer or employee shall be appointed
by the board.
§ 10. Superintendents ; Oath of Office ; Bond .
Before entering upon his duties each superintendent
shall take an oath to faithfully discharge the duties
of such superintendent and shall execute bond in the
sum of ten thousand dollars ( $10,000 ) and shall pro-
vide as surety on said bond a solvent and recognized
•
surety or guaranty company , and the premium on
same shall be paid by the state . Said bond , in order
to be sufficient , shall be approved by the chairman of
the board and filed in the office of the secretary of
state .
§ 11. Superintendent to Have Charge of Institu-
tion and Inmates . The superintendent shall have
the general management , supervision and control of
the institution , and the inmates thereof, subject to
the rules and regulations of the board of charities
and corrections , and he shall devote his entire time
thereto .
§ 12. Patients , Record of ; Case Histories ; Acci-
dent Book . The superintendent of each institution
for the insane or feeble -minded shall cause to be
kept a register of all patients , showing their names ,
ages , residences , dates of reception and discharge or
death , and by whose authority received or dis-
charged . He shall cause to be kept a case book or
record in which shall be entered a history of the case
of each patient received into the asylum , as far as it
is possible to make out such history from creditable
information ; also the condition at time of admission ,
together with a detailed statement of medical treat-
ment ; an " accident book " in which shall be recorded
a statement of all accidents , whether serious or
slight , to any of the patients of said asylum , whether
self-inflicted or occurring otherwise , together with
a statement of the causes of such accidents or in-
juries ; and also the names , if any , of the persons
who have been witnesses thereof . Said record shall
be open to inspection of the board of charities and
corrections at all times and shall be filed and kept
among the records of the institutions .
13. Restraint Record for Each Institution ;
What it Shall Show ; Duty of Superintendent . The
superintendent of each institution for the insane or
feeble -minded shall cause to be kept a " restraint
record " which shall show the name of each person
within said asylum subjected to restraints to allay
excitement by any means whatsoever ; also the char-
acter of said restraint , when and how long employed
in each case, by whose authority and also the reason
for using same . Mechanical restraint should not be
applied in any case without the express direction
and under the supervision of one of the physicians
in charge of said hospital , nor shall restraining ap-
paratus be kept upon the wards when not in use .
Said restraint record shall also show the number of
attendants on duty in each month and whether the
same was sufficient or more than sufficient for the
protection and well -being of all patients in the asy-
lum . Said record shall be open to inspection of the
board of charities and corrections at all times and
shall be filed and kept among the records of the in-
stitution .
§ 14. Receiver ; Duties . It shall be the duty of
the receiver to receive all goods and supplies of any
and all kinds purchased for the institution , take
charge of them , see that they correspond with the
bills accompanying them, in character , quality and
quantity ; weigh or measure the same and distribute
them to each and every department of the institution
as the superintendent may direct by written order ;
and , in a book for the purpose , open an account with
each and every department , charging therein cost
price for all goods so received and distributed . The
books shall be open at any and all times for the in-
spection of the superintendent , board of charities
and corrections, the governor , a committee of the
legislature , or any person appointed by either for
examination .
15. Receiver ; Oath of Office ; Bond . Before
entering upon his duties each receiver shall take an
oath to faithfully discharge the duties of such re-
ceiver and shall execute bond in a sum to be fixed
by the board and shall provide as surety on said
bond a solvent and recognized surety or guaranty
company , and the premium on same shall be paid by
the state . Said bond , in order to be sufficient , shall
be approved by the chairman of the board and filed
in the office of the secretary of state .
§ 16. Board May Create Necessary Offices . The
board shall provide for such officers and employees
for each institution and for such clerical and other
assistants for itself as it may deem necessary , ex-
cept that the board may not dispense with the com-
missioner of public institutions or a superintendent
and a receiver for each institution .
§ 17. Receiving Other Compensation or Further
Perquisite Prohibited ; Penalty . Officers and em-
ployees shall not be entitled to receive , directly or
indirectly any other or further perquisite or com-
pensation .
18. Use of Institution Fund or Property for
Private Purposes Prohibited ; Penalty . Any officer ,
employe or other person connected with any of said
institutions , who shall use or authorize the use of
any money or other thing of value for private pur-
poses not authorized by law, shall be amenable to
the punishment now provided for such offenses , and ,
in addition thereto , shall be reported by any person
cognizant of the fact to the board of charities and
corrections , who shall cause to be removed from the
employment of the state any person wilfully guilty
of said offense .
$ 19. Qualification of officers and employees . All
officers and employees under the board of charities
and corrections shall be selected for merit and fit-
ness only and with the exception of persons em-
ployed for special or temporary service shall give
all of their time to the service of the board .
§ 20. Employees ; Recommendation of by Board
Members Prohibited ; Responsibility of Superinten-
dent . No member of the board shall recommend or
urge that any person shall be employed by such sup-
erintendent in any capacity in any of the institutions
placed under their control , and the superintendent
of each institution shall be held fully responsible by
the board for the satisfactory management of said
institution and shall be subject to removal at any
time by the board .
§ 21. Members and Employees Not to Accept
Fees ; Offices Vacated . No commissioner , officer or
employee of the board of charities and corrections ,
or of any of the institutions under its control shall
accept any fee or gift for any purpose from any cor-
poration or person who has at the time or has had a
contract with said board of charities and corrections
or any of its institutions under its control , to do any-
thing connected therewith . Any commissioner , offi-
cer or employee who violates the provisions of this
act shall ipso facto forfeit his office or position and
the same shall be declared vacant .
§ 22. Exemption of Board Officers and Em-
ployees from Military , Road Service , and Atten-
dance as Witnesses . The commissioners and all offi-
cers and servants of each institution shall be ex-
empt from militia duty , from working on the public
highway , and from serving on any jury . Nor shall
the officers and servants be required to give personal
attendance as witnesses in any civil suit out of the
county in which the institute is situated , but their
deposition shall be taken in lieu thereof .
$ 23. Fiscal Year ; Reports to Governor and
Legislature . The fiscal year of the institutions shall
begin July 1st and close June 30th , and the superin-
tendent of each institution and the board of charities
and corrections shall bi-annually make a report to
the governor of the condition of the institutions un-
der their charge , exhibiting the amount of income
and expenditure and from what source the income.
was received and for what use the expenditure was
made , and the number of inmates received and dis-
charged , or left during the year, with such other
facts and suggestions as they may deem important ,
which reports the governor shall communicate to
the legislature at its next regular session .
§ 24. Annual Budget for Each Institution ; Ap-
portionment of Appropriations . Each superinten-
dent of an institution under the control and manage-
ment of the board shall prepare and submit to the
board annually , or oftener , if required by the board ,
a budget or estimate of the expenditures required
for the maintenance and conduct of such institution
and the board shall prepare an annual budget for all
of the institutions and agencies under it and submit
same to the governor or the budget appropriation
commission . The board may apportion the appro-
priation made for the benefit of the institutions un-
der the control and management of the board as be- .
tween the various institutions in such manner as in
its judgment the interests of such institutions re
quire .
§ 25. Appropriation ; Expenditure ; Salaries ;
Orders for Payment ; How Approved ; Auditor . Ap-
propriations made for the board of charities and
corrections shall be payable by warrant drawn by
the Auditor . The board may draw upon the auditor
of public accounts monthly for such sums of money
as are necessary to run the institutions under its
control , including the salaries due all officers and
employees . The order upon the auditor shall spec-
ify the purpose for which the expenditure was made
and the amount and the persons to whom paid . The
order shall be signed by the commissioner of public
institutions and approved by the chairman of the
board , and shall not be issued except by order of the
board entered of record , specifying the amount and
the purpose for which the expenditure was made
and to whom . When such order is received by the
auditor he shall draw his warrant on the state trea-
surer in favor of the person specified in said order ,
and the amount directed to be paid and said war-
rant must specify for what purpose the money is to
be used and the fund from which said money is paid ,
and the state treasurer shall , out of the money in
the state treasury appropriated to the board of
charities and corrections pay said warrants . Said
orders and warrants shall be carefully preserved
and shall become vouchers for the amount paid out
specified by them .
§ 26. Supplies ; When Superintendent May Pur-
chase . The superintendent of each institution shall
have the power to purchase necessary incidental and
emergency supplies for his institution , subject to the
approval of the board of charities and corrections ,
to whom he shall render a monthly itemized state-
ment , giving the facts and circumstances of each ex-
penditure .
§ 27. Claim ; Duty of Superintendent and Re-
ceiver ; Procedure of Board . The superintendent
shall examine all claims and accounts against their
respective institutions and report any fact or cir-
cumstance indicating any irregularity , fraud or
wrong to the board of charities and corrections ; and
if they have any doubt of the justice or legality of
any claim, they may require both the superintendent
and the receiver to endorse their opinion in writing
on the back thereof ; and it shall be the duty of said
officers to endorse any claim when required by the
board to do so ; and the board of charities and cor-
rections shall not direct any claim, or part thereof,
to be paid until they are satisfied , from such inves-
tigation as may be necessary , that the same is just ,
legal and right ; and no claim of any kind shall be
paid , in whole or in part , whether presented by an
officer of the institution or other person until it shall
have been examined and approved by the receiver
and submitted to the board of charities and correc-
tions and determined by them to be just and right ,
and directed to be entered upon the record of its
proceedings ; and the commissioner of public insti-
tutions shall not issue any order for the payment of
money upon the auditor of public accounts except
for the amount of claims which have been so sub-
mitted to the board , allowed by it and ordered to be
paid .
§ 28. Claims ; Procedure for Payment ; Reports
of Money Collected ; Books to be Kept . Whenever
the commissioner of public institutions shall issue
an order for the payment of money he shall cause
the number , amount and date thereof, and the name
of the person in whose favor it is made , to be en-
tered by the secretary in a separate book kept for
that purpose ; and whenever he shall receive any
money for the use of the institutions he shall cause
the same to be entered by the secretary in said sep-
arate book , but in a different part of it , stating the
amount of money and when and from whom re-
ceived , and thereupon he shall deposit said money
and other means ( of whatever character they may
be ) with the treasurer and take his receipt therefor ,
and preserve it as a voucher .
§ 29. Governor May Direct Examination By
State Inspector . It shall be the duty ofthe gover-
nor whenever , in his opinion , the interest of the com-
monwealth demands it, to direct the state inspector
and examiner to inspect the books and accounts of
the board of charities and corrections or of any in-
stitution and report its true financial condition and
management as respects receipts and disbursements
and the property thereof .
§ 30. Orders of Board ; Investigation of Condi-
tions ; Inspection of Books , Premises , Buildings ,
Etc .; Duties of Officers and Penalty for Refusal to
Obey Orders . The said board of charities and cor-
rections shall have full power at all times to look
into and examine the conditions of the several in-
stitutions of the state heretofore mentioned , finan-
cially or otherwise , to inquire and examine into the
government and management of their inmates , the
official conduct of the officers and employees of same ,
the condition of the buildings , grounds and other
property connected therewith , and in all other mat-
ters pertaining to their usefulness and good man-
agement , and for these purposes they shall have free
access to the grounds , buildings and all books and
papers relating to said institutions , and all persons
now or hereafter in any manner connected with the
same are hereby directed and required to give such
information and afford such facilities for inspection
as said board may require , and any neglect or re-
.fusal on the part of any officer or person connected
with such institution to comply with the provisions
of this section shall subject the offender to a penalty
of two hundred and fifty dollars , to be sued for and
collected by said board of charities and corrections ,
and to accrue to and become a part of the general
funds of said board .
§ 31. Buildings to be Insured . The board of
charities and corrections shall keep the buildings
and furniture of the institutions constantly insured ,
and the amount of premium on each insurance shall
be certified to the auditor by the commissioner of
Acts-4
public institutions and secretary of the board of
charities and corrections and thereupon the auditor
shall draw his warrant on the treasurer for the pay-
ment of money for the amount of such premiums
payable to the persons shown to be entitled to same
by such certification . But , nothing herein contained
shall deprive the commissioners of the sinking fund
of Kentucky of any powers they now have or that
may hereafter be given them by law to insure or
cause to be insured or to cancel or cause to be can-
celled any insurance on the buildings and personal
property belonging to Kentucky or any of its de-
partments or institutions including the property
herein mentioned , and all powers herein given are
subject to the powers now existing or that may here-
inafter be given to said commissioners .
32. License to Charitable Societies ; Penalty
for Violation . The board may issue license to char-
itable organizations supported in whole or in part
by appropriations from the state treasury or repre-
sentatives thereof to solicit funds in the state of
Kentucky , and no such organization or any repre-
sentative thereof shall solicit funds outside of the
county in which it is located unless license permit-
ting same is issued to it by the said board . Any per-
son violating the provisions of this section shall be.
guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction shall be
fined in the sum of not less than fifty ($ 50.00 ) nor
more than two hundred dollars ( $ 200.00 ) .
33. Eminent Domain. When it is necessary
for the state board of charities and corrections to
own other real estate for its use and is unable to
purchase the same from its owner or owners thereof, '
then said board is invested with the power and auth-
ority to condemn real estate for its use and pur-
poses in the same manner as real estate is con-
demned for railroad purposes .
§ 34. Examination and Report on Sites . The
University of Kentucky shall at the request of the
state board of charities and corrections examine
and report on any and all lands which the board may
wish to investigate , with a view to purchase or lease ,
so that the board may be fully advised as to the
quality and character of the soil , water supply , san-
itation and other agricultural and engineering prob-
lems . The said university shall be entitled to re-
ceive its necessary expenses in connection with said.
investigation .
§ 35. Power of Board ; Management and Control
of Institutions ; Rules ; Sale of Products ; Transfer
of Patients ; Expenditure of Surplus Proceeds .
Said board of charities and corrections shall have
full and complete management and control over all
asylums for the insane and feeble -minded institutes
of the Commonwealth of Kentucky , that are now or
may be hereafter established . Said board shall pre-
scribe rules and regulations for the government of
said institutions , for the proper maintenance and
treatment of patients , for the preservation of build-
ings and grounds , for the use and cultivation of
farms and gardens , and the sale of surplus produce ,
the purchase of clothing, food , medicine and all sup-
plies needful to same , and such rules and regula-
tions as prescribed shall be faithfully observed by
all the officers and employees of said institutions ,
and have the power to remove inmates from one
asylum to another . And the said board shall have
power to expend in their discretion any surplus
standing to the credit of said institutions from time
to time , in carrying out the purpose of this act ; and
in so doing they may use such surplus at any of the
institutions under their control without reference
to the fact that such surplus may have arisen at an-
other institution .
1
$ 36 . Board of Patients Other than Paupers to
be Paid in Advance ; Orders of Commitment to be
Conditioned ; Exceptions ; Provisions for Refund .
No patients , except those who are paupers accord-
ing to the definition of " pauper " in this statute , ex-
cept drug addicts admitted voluntarily under agree-
ment , or persons who give bond , shall be received
or retained in any of the institutions for the insane
or feeble -minded of this state , unless six months '
board be always paid in advance , and the board for
the residue of the time they may remain in the insti-
tution be secured by the obligation of one or more
sufficient residents of this state ; and the court or
officers shall make their orders for the committal of
all patients (with the above exceptions ) , to the insti-
tution conditioned upon such prepayment being
made and security given . But if the patient be dis-
charged or die before the expiration of the six
months paid for , a proper proportion of the amount
paid shall be refunded .
§ 37. Persons Liable for Support of Patients ;
Suit to Recover ; Rights of Other Dependents .
Where the patients have been, or may be, supported
in any of the institutions embraced in the provisions
of this act have , or shall acquire estates which can
be subject to debt , they shall be liable for their board
and maintenance , and the board of charities and cor-
rections is authorized and directed in every such
case to sue for in name of such institution and re-
cover the amount of such patient's board at the rate
fixed by the board or so much thereof as such estate
will suffice to pay for the time they shall have been
respectively kept and maintained therein and not
otherwise paid for , and by proper proceedings to
subject their estates , respectively , to payment
thereof ; and when the husband , wife or parent of
any such patient, who has been or may be supported
.
in any of said institutions , shall have an estate suffi-
cient for the support of such patient in addition to
the support of any other who may be dependent on
such husband , wife or parent , in like manner to sue
for and recover from such husband the amount of
his wife's board, or from such wife the amount of
her husband's board, and from such parent the
amount of his or her child's board at the rate afore-
said , for the time they shall have been supported
by such institution .
§ 38. Support of Patients ; Rate to be Charged .
The board may fix the rate to be paid for the sup-
port of a person by his committee or by relatives
liable for such support , or by those not liable for
such support , but willing to assume the cost thereof ;
but such rates shall be sufficient when possible to
cover a proper proportion of the cost of mainten-
ance and of necessary repairs and improvements ,
and the same rate shall be charged to all persons .
§ 39. Recovery of Support of Patients . The
board shall have power to take all necessary steps
by suit or otherwise to secure from relatives and
friends who are liable therefor or who may be will-
ing to assume the cost of support of any person sup-
ported by the state , reimbursement , in whole or in
part , of the money expended for the support of any
patient confined or maintained in any of the hos-
pitals for the insane or the feeble -minded institu-
tions .
§ 40. Employment of Attorney ; Attorney Gen-
eral ; Cost of Litigation ; Disposition of Money Col-
lected ; Limitation of Action . The board shall have
power to employ counsel , upon the advice and ap-
proval of the Attorney General , to institute or de-
fend such actions or proceedings as in their judg-
ment may be necessary or proper to enforce the pay-
ment or reimbursement for board and maintenance
of patients . In case of failure of suits , the expense
thereof shall be certified by the commissioner of
public institutions to the state auditor who shall
provide for its payment out of the funds appropri-
ated for the use of said board .
The net sums realized in such suits shall be paid
over to the state auditor and turned over into the
state treasury and become a part of the funds for
the use of the board. The statute of limitation pro-
viding the time in which actions for such recovery
may be instituted shall not run against recovery
herein provided for until from and after the time at
which said estate is acquired .
§ 41. Patients ; What Immediate Information to
Board to be Furnished Upon Admittance , Death ,
Discharge , Parole , Escape , Change of Committee .
The superintendent of each institution , upon receiv-
ing a patient , shall immediately furnish the board
with the following information , viz .: Name , age , sex,
color or race , former address , date of commitment ,
county from which committed , former commitments
if any, together with the name of his committee and
parents, or, if a married woman , the name of her
husband .
The superintendents shall also furnish the follow-
ing information immediately upon the happening of
the fact concerning which information is required ,
viz : Date of death or discharge with the reason
therefor ; escapes , returns , removals and paroles of
patients ; changes in the person designated as com-
mittee for the patient.
$ 42 . Admissions for Compensation ; Quarters
May Occupy ; Rules . The state board of charities
and corrections may authorize the superintendent of
any state institution for the feeble -minded , epileptic
or insane to admit thereto under a special agree-
ment mentally defective persons who are residents
1
of the state , other than poor and indigent persons ,
when there is room for such persons therein . But
no person so admitted shall be permitted to occupy
more than one room in any institution , and shall be
subject to the general rules and regulations of the
institution .
§ 43. Rates , Bonds , Removal to Private Institu-
tions . The board of charities and corrections shall
fix the rates to be charged for the maintenance of
feeble -minded , epileptic and insane persons or idiots
admitted to state institutions under agreement , the
payment of which shall be secured by a surety com-
pany bond approved by the board or by other ade-
quate security or by a deposit , and bills therefor
shall be collected monthly . The superintendent may
recommend to the board the removal of such per-
sons to duly licensed private institutions , and the
board shall have power in its discretion to compel
such removal .
$ 44. Pay Patients From Other States . Under
no circumstances shall it be permitted that by the
reception of pay patients from other states , the asy-
lum be so crowded that any delay shall be incurred
in the immediate reception of patients resident in
this commonwealth either paying or pauper .
§ 45. Non -Residents to be Returned ; From
What Fund Expenses Paid . If an order be issued by
any judge committing to a state institution for the
feeble -minded , epileptic, insane or idiots , poor or
indigent person who has not acquired a legal resi-
dence in this state , the board of charities and cor-
rections shall return such mentally defective person ,
either before or after his admission to the institu-
tion, to the country or state to which he belongs , and
for such purpose may expend so much of money ap-
propriated for the care of the feeble -minded and
insane persons as may be necessary .

$ 46. Distribution of Patients According to Ca-
pacity of Institution ; Separation of White and Col-
ored Patients . Whenever the number of patients
sent to any asylum is greater than can be properly
accommodated and cared for by that institution ,
and there is at the time capacity for the reception
and care of the patients at any of the other asylums ,
it shall be the duty of the board of charities and cor-
rections and superintendent of such other asylum
to receive as many of those rejected at the former
for want of room as can be properly accommodated .
When , upon application to the proper asylum , the
patient is rejected for want of room , immediate ap-
plication shall be made to another . The board of
charities and corrections is empowered and directed
to take care that each of the asylums is kept full to
its utmost capacity and such patients as are receiv-
able by it, as long as any such patients in the state
are unprovided for , and that each receive its due
proportion of the patients in excess of the ordinary
capacity of the asylum ; the white and colored pa-
tients shall not be kept in the same building .
§ 47. Board May Transfer Patients to Institu-
tion Where They Will be Best Cared For. Any
feeble -minded or epileptic person committed to a
state institution and becoming insane , may be trans-
ferred to a state hospital for the insane by the board
of charities and corrections , and any feeble - minded
or epileptic person confined to a state hospital for
the insane , and who is not insane may be transferred
by the state board of charities and corrections to
the institution for feeble -minded and epileptic per-
sons .
§ 48. Feeble -minded Females Not to be Kept in
Poor House ; Transfer to State Institution . It shall
be unlawful for any county poor farm , or poor
house , or any home or institution providing prima-
rily for poor or infirm persons , to receive or permit
to remain in its shelter a feeble -minded female un-
der forty-five years of age , providing there is room
in the institution for the feeble -minded for such per-
sons , in which case such person must be transferred
to such institution .
§ 49. Duty of Health Officer ; Segregation and
custody to Prevent Procreation . It shall be one of
the special duties of every health officer and every
public health nurse to institute proceedings to se-
cure the proper segration and custody of feeble-
minded persons likely to become fathers or mothers
of other feeble -minded persons .
§ 50. Aiding Marriage of Feeble -Minded Per-
sons , Idiots or Lunatics . It shall be unlawful to aid
or abet the marriage of any feeble -minded person
or to attempt , or to aid or abet an attempt to , the
marriage of an idiot or lunatic and any person
found guilty of a violation of this provision shall be
fined not less than fifty dollars ( $ 50.00 ) nor more
than five hundred dollars ($ 500.00 ) .
§ 51. Home ; Farm Colony for Feeble -Minded
Persons . There shall be continued and maintained a
training school for feeble -minded persons , also
maintained a farm colony for them to be located on
land suitable for farming , stock raising and fruit
growing . Such buildings shall be maintained suffi-
cient to accommodate the inmates .
$ 52. Epileptic Persons May be Transferred .
The board is hereby authorized to establish and
maintain a suitable place for epileptic persons and
segregate them from feeble -minded and insane per-
sons , if convenient to do so . It is authorized to trans-
fer said persons to such hospital as is best suited
for the treatment of such cases .
§ 53. Objects and Purposes . The object and
purpose of said state institutions for feeble -minded
"
or for epileptic persons shall be the mental and phy-
sical training , the treatment and custody of feeble-
minded or of epileptic persons , the promotion of
their happiness and well -being and the study of
mental deficiency ; and such institutions shall have
all rights and powers which may be necessary and
proper for carrying out the purpose for which they
are established .
§ 54. Care, Custody and Training . It shall be
the duty of the superintendent of said institution to
provide such care and training for each inmate as
may be necessary to render him more useful and
happy and to make him as nearly self - supporting as
his mental capacity may permit .
$ 55. Manufacture of Articles . The inmates of
said institution may manufacture and produce for
their use , or for the use of other state institutions ,
such articles , furniture , clothing , tools , products and
other supplies and engage in such labor or work of
construction as may be approved by the state board
of charities and corrections .
56. No Person Admitted Under Six Years of
Age . There shall be received into said institution ,
subject to such rules and regulations as the board of
charities and corrections may adopt and pursuant to
the provisions of this act , feeble -minded and epilep-
tic persons of not less than six years of age .
§ 57. Allowance For Pauper Idiot . A person
having the care , custody or charge of an idiot may
by filing with the Auditor a certified copy of the in-
quisition and the order of the court adjudging an
idiot to be a pauper, have an allowance to a pauper
idiot of not more than $75.00 per annum to be paid
as follows : One -half of said allowance and not more
than $ 37.50 out of the state treasury to be properly
certified by the court holding said inquest to the
auditor for payment , and one -half of said allowance
·
but not more than $37.50 to be allowed and properly
certified by the court holding said inquest to the fis-
cal court of said county in which said inquest is held
for payment .
Should the idiot for which an allowance is made
die or cease to be a pauper , a proportionate part of
the allowance from the anniversary date of the al-
lowance to the day of his death or his ceasing to be
a pauper, may be paid .
$ 58. Court May Make Allowance For Pauper
Idiot . No money shall be drawn from the state trea-
sury for the support of an idiot unless the circuit
court wherein the inquest is held shall make the al-
lowance at the time of the inquest .
$ 59. Allowance ; What Persons Not Entitled to .
No allowance shall be made for the maintenance of
any person under the age of eight years , nor for one
who at times , by epileptic fits or other malady , is en-
feebled in mind, or who had not been found to be a
pauper idiot.
$ 60. Inquest to be Held Every Fifth Year.
Every fifth year after the first inquest , before any
order shall be granted by the court for the mainten-
ance of an idiot or a feeble -minded person out of his
own estate , or out of the state treasury , the idiot or
feeble -minded person , in like manner , shall be
brought into the court, or his presence dispensed
with , for the reasons herein allowed ; and the court
shall cause the jury to be empaneled , who shall be
sworn as provided in this article ; and also to in-
quire, and true report to make from the evidence ,
whether the person whom they have in charge has
before been found , by verdict of a jury and judg-
ment of a court , an idiot or a feeble -minded person ,
and whether and what change , if any, has taken
place in his mind , physical condition , and estate
since the previous inquest .
§ 61. Allowance ; Copy of Inquest to be Furn-
ished Auditor . A copy certified by the clerk of each
original and subsequent inquisition , shall be trans- .
mitted to the auditor of public accounts ; without
such transcript the auditor shall issue no warrant
for the amount allowed by the court .
§ 62. Circuit Clerk to Furnish Annually List of
Pauper Idiots ; Penalty . The circuit court clerk of
each county shall transmit to the auditor , on or be-
fore the tenth of September in each year, a list of
the pauper idiots in his county ; if he fails to do so
without good cause he shall be fined fifty dollars .
63. Definitions . The term " feeble -minded
person " means a person with a defect in mental de-
velopment , which is due to causes operating at birth ,
or at an early age, and which is of such a degree that
he is incapable therefrom of caring for himself or
managing his affairs and requires supervision , care ,
training , control or custody for his own welfare or
for the welfare of others or the community .
The term " epileptic person " means a person who
has epileptic attacks and is known to be losing his
mental capacity as a result of these attacks , and is
so distinctly enfeebled that he needs care and cus-
tody for his own welfare , or for the welfare of
others , or for the community .
The word " idiot " means a person who has been
from birth or infancy deficient in mental capacity ,
and destitute of the ordinary intellectual powers .
The word "lunatic ," or term " insane person "
means one who , having had a mind , has lost it .
§ 64. Drug Addicts . The word "lunatic , " " in-
sane person" or " persons of unsound mind " wher-
ever and whenever used in any law with relation
thereto , or in this act shall be construed to include
any and all persons who by the use of any drug or
narcotic has lost the power of reasoning correctly ,
or whose power to reason has been and is impaired
by the use of any drug or narcotic to such an extent
as to render such person dangerous to himself or
herself , or to any other person , or whose condition
by reason of the use of such drug or narcotic is such
as to be detrimental to his or her own welfare or the
welfare of the public .
$ 65 . Drug Addicts ; Admission to Institution ;
Conditions . Any person who has been a resident of
this state for more than one year , who may be ad-
dicted to the use of narcotic drugs , may , upon his
agreement in writing to remain in any one of the
institutions in this state , provided for persons of
unsound mind , for a period of six months or longer
if necessary for a cure , stating his or her addiction
to the use of said narcotic drug , supported by the
certificate of at least two reputable and duly licensed
physicians who shall have engaged in the practice
of medicine for two or more years , which certificate
shall be based upon personal examination of such
person , be admitted as a voluntary patient to any
institution of this state provided for the care of per-
sons of unsound mind .
§ 66. Drug Addicts ; Maintenance ; Rules ; When
to be Released . Any person addicted to the use of
any drug or narcotic if admitted to any of the insti-
tutions under the control of the board of charities
and corrections , if not indigent or a pauper , shall
be required to pay such sum for his or her mainte-
nance and treatment , and at such time , as the board
may by rule prescribe . All voluntary patients of
this class shall have the same standing and be sub-
ject to the same laws , rules and regulations as are
provided for this class of persons of unsound mind,
except that such voluntary patients shall have the
right to leave such institution at any time after the
expiration of six months or after the expiration of

§ 70. Petition for Inquest ; What It Shall State .
The petition , verified as required in the preceding
section , shall set forth the name and residence of the
person concerning whom the petition is filed , the
name , residence of the parent or parents , if known ,
and of the husband or wife , if any , and the name and
residence of the person having custody , control and
supervision of such person ; or if no such person is
known to the petitioner , then of some near relative
or that such is unknown to the petitioner .
§ 71. Court to Appoint Attorney ; Common-
wealth's Attorney . In any case of inquest the court
shall appoint some member of the bar to represent
and protect the interests and rights of the person al-
leged to be of unsound mind , and it shall also be the
duty of the attorney for the commonwealth to pre-
vent the finding of any person to be of unsound mind
who , in his opinion is not such .
$ 72. Notice of Inquest ; Person to be Notified ;
Service of Summons . All persons named in the pe-
tition , including the alleged feeble -minded person ,
epileptic , insane person or idiot , if of legal age , shall
be notified of such proceeding by a summons issued
requiring the parent or parents , guardian or other
person having the custody , control or supervision
of such person or with whom such person may be , to
appear with such person at a time and place to be
stated in the summons , which time shall not be less
than three ( 3 ) days after service . The parents of
such person , if living , if their residence be known to
the petitioner , or the legal guardian , if one there be ,
and his residence is known to the petitioner , or if
there be neither parent or guardian whose residence
is known to the petitioner , then some near relative ,
if his or her residence be known to the petitioner ,
shall be notified also of the proceedings .
§ 73. Failure of Person Summoned to Appear ;
When Court May Hold Inquest . If a person sum-
moned as herein provided shall fail without reason-
able cause to appear and abide by the order of the
court, he may be proceeded against as in the case.
of contempt of court . On the return of the summons
or other process , or on the appearance of such al-
leged feeble -minded , epileptic , insane person or
idiot with or without summons or other process in
person before the court , together with the return of
the service of notice , if there be any person notified ,
or upon the personal appearance or written consent
to the proceedings of the person or persons , if any
be notified , or as soon thereafter as may be , the
court shall proceed to hear and dispose of the case .
§ 74. Trial by Jury , if Desired . In proceeding
under this act the person alleged to be feeble-
minded , epileptic or insane , and appearing before
the court , or any person interested in such person ,
shall have the right to demand for such alleged
feeble -minded , epileptic or insane person a trial by
jury , which shall be granted as in other cases , unless
waived ; or the court on its own motion may call a
jury to try such case . The court in its discretion
may conduct the trial or inquest in chambers .
§ 75. Evidence ; Witnesses May be Summoned .
The court may in its discretion require other evi-
dence in addition to the petition and the certificates
of the examining physicians , and he may require the
attendance at the hearing of said physicians and of
any other witnesses . The alleged feeble -minded , ep-
ileptic , insane person or idiot or any one represent-
ing him shall have the right to summon witnesses
and to present evidence as in other cases made and
provided .
§ 76. Examining Physician ; Qualifications ; Fee
Paid by County ; Certificate . When a petition for
the trial and commitment of an alleged feeble-
minded , epileptic, idiot or insane person has been
properly filed with the clerk of the court, the court
shall appoint two physicians to examine such per-
sons and to certify to the court as to their findings in
the case. These physicians shall be selected where
possible because they have made special study of
feeble -mindedness and mental diseases and shall be
entitled to a fee of $3.00 each for such examination
and certificate , to be paid by the county in which the
commitment is made , upon a certified copy of an or-
der of allowance made by the circuit court holding
the inquest .
§ 77. Examination ; Certificate, What It Shall
State ; To Be Verified . The certificate shall state
that the person has been examined by each of the
medical examiners making the certificate within
three days prior to the date of the certificate , and
that in their judgment he is an idiot or is feeble-
minded , epileptic or insane in the sense of this act
as the case may be , if such be the fact , and requires
supervision, control and care for his own welfare
or for the welfare of others or of the community ;
and it shall further state whether such supervision ,
control and care can best be provided by commit-
ment to an institution for the feeble -minded , the ep-
ileptic or for the insane , or by commitment to guar-
dianship . The certificate shall be in the form pre-
scribed by the State Board of Charities and Correc-
tions , and shall state the facts and circumstances
upon which the judgment of the medical examiners
is based , and shall be sworn to before a notary or the
clerk or judge of the court.
§ 78. Presence of Persons Charged ; When Dis-
pensed With . No inquest shall be held unless the
person charged to be an idiot , insane , feeble -minded
or epileptic is in court ; provided , however , that the
personal presence of such person may be dispensed
with when it shall appear by the oath or affidavit of
two regular practicing physicians that they have
personally examined such person and that they ver-
ily believe that his condition is such that it would be
unsafe to bring him into court .
$ 79. Inquest ; Oath to be Administered to Jury ;
Form of ; Instructions of Court . The following oath
shall be administered to the jury : " You do swear
that you will well and truly inquire , and from the
evidence say , in your verdict , whether A B , the per-
son whom you have in charge , is of unsound mind ,
and if of unsound mind , whether he is an idiot or
lunatic that is , whether he was destitute of mind
from infancy or has lost it since birth ; and if he has
lost it since his birth , that you will state when , and
as far as you can from the evidence the cause of it.
You will also inquire and state his birth and resi-
dence , and whether he has been brought into this
state by any person , and by whom , for the purpose
of becoming a charge upon the Commonwealth .
That you will find what estate , the value thereof, he
owns in possession , reversion, or remainder ;
whether his parents are alive ; where they reside ;
and whether they have estate sufficient to support
the person under trial ; whether he is capable of
laboring in whole or in part , and what part , for
his support ." The judge shall instruct the jury
upon the whole case , so as to enable them to' de-
cide the question whether the defendant is an idiot
or lunatic .
But this oath shall not be confused with or in any
wise conflict with the oath to be given upon the in-
quest of an imbecile as prescribed in section 2155 .
§ 80. Pauper ; Who Is ; Verdict ; Orders of
Court . A person is a pauper , idiot , or lunatic ,
within the meaning of this act , who has been found
by the verdict of a jury to be :
(a) An idiot or lunatic .
(b) That he or she is unable to work for a sup-
port .
(c) That he or she has no estate sufficient for
support .
(d ) That his or her parents if alive have not suf-
ficient estate to maintain him or her, and the jury
must find whether the person's parents are alive or
dead .
(e ) If a wife , that her husband has not sufficient
estate to support her and that he is unable to work
for a support .
(f) If a husband , that his wife has not sufficient
estate to support him .
The order of the court shall be made on proof and
so state , and shall state the facts as found by the
jury , and shall also state the age of the person and
that the idiot or lunatic is then alive and a pauper .
§ 81. Court to Make Necessary Orders ; Estate
of Persons ; Appointment of Committee . The judge
who presides at such inquest may make all orders
for the care of the person found to be an idiot ,
feeble -minded , epileptic or insane , or incompetent
to manage his estate ; and if it is found upon the in-
quest that such person has an estate , or it is for any
other reason necessary , it shall be the duty of the
court to make all necessary orders for the appoint-
ment of a committee and the security of the estate
of such person.
$ 82 . Disposition of Person ; Court To Make
Necessary Orders . The court may order such per-
son to an asylum for the insane , or to the institution
for the feeble -minded , as the facts may warrant ;
or the court may commit such person to a properly
licensed private institution , or to a committee whom
the court may find to be proper , able and competent
to minister to the welfare of such person , except as
otherwise provided .
$ 83 . Resident Lunatics and Idiots ; To Which
Asylum To Be Sent . Unless otherwise designated
by the board of charities and corrections , lunatics
and idiots , resident in Kentucky , and found in the
counties of Pendleton , Harris , Scott , Franklin , An-
derson , Mercer , Boyle , Garrard , Rockcastle , Laurel ,
Knox and Bell, or any county east of these , when
sent to an asylum , shall go to , and be received under
legal requirements by , the eastern Kentucky asylum
for the insane , at Lexington , if there be room
therein . Those found in any county west of these
and east of the counties of Hancock, Ohio , Butler ,
Warren and Allen , shall be sent to , and in like man-
ner received by the central asylum for the insane ;
and those found in the counties last named and the
residue of the state shall be sent to and in like man-
ner be received by, the western Kentucky asylum
for the insane .
$ 84. Immediate Notice to Superintendent of In-
quest ; Duty of Court . It shall be the duty of the
judge of the court in which any person shall be or-
dered to an institution to at once , by wire or letter ,
notify the superintendent of the institution to which
said person is ordered , that such order has been
made and advise him of the sex and condition of the
person .
§ 85. Conveyance and Return of Patients ; Fe-
males ; Cost ; How Paid . When the superintendent
of any institution receives notice by wire or letter
from the judge of the court in which the inquest was
held that an order has been entered ordering an
idiot , feeble -minded person , epileptic or lunatic to
the institution of which he has charge , he shall im-
mediately send a competent attendant to convey
said person to said institution , and only the actual
traveling expenses of conveying any person to any
of the said institutions shall be paid . The superin-
tendent shall itemize the expenses of conveying all
such persons to his institution and shall send a
statement thereof to the commissioner of public in-
stitutions , who shall present said statement to the
auditor of public accounts , and said expenses shall
be paid as provided for in the manner for the pay-
ment of claims . In returning any patient to the
country whence he or she was sent , when necessary ,
the cost of returning them shall be paid in the same
manner . Only one person shall be paid out of the
state treasury for conveying any patient . Each fe-
male committed to any institution shall be accom-
panied by a female attendant , unless accompanied
by her father , brother , husband or son .
86. Information to be Furnished With Com-
mitment . With the commitment of a feeble - minded ,
epileptic , insane person or idiot to an institution for
the feeble -minded , epileptic , insane or idiots , a copy
of the petition , the certificate of the physicians and
the order of commitment , together with a written
statement of the judge and the history of the pa-
tient's case as hereinafter provided shall be sent to
the superintendent of such institution .
§ 87. History of Patient's Case ; Contents of ;
Written Statement ; Duty of Judge at Inquest .
When a person shall be found to be an idiot , feeble-
minded or insane under the provisions of this act
the judge who presides at the inquest shall ascer-
tain and draw up a brief history of such person's
case, embracing the following points :
1. Age ; occupation ; married or single ; habits ;
education . 2. What relations , if any , have been in-
sane, feeble -minded or epileptic . 3. Date of first
•
attack or symptoms ; how exhibited ; whether trou-
ble has since changed in character . 4. Supposed
cause ; what illusions or hallucinations if any ;
whether subject to fits , and if so , of what character
or duration , natural temper and kind of affections
toward relations . 5. Any attempt 'at suicide ; what
propensity to mischief , or violence , if any exhib-
ited . 6. Periodical frenzy and lucid intervals and
duration of each . 7. What restraint has been im-
posed and what treatment used . 8. What injury , if
any , about the head received ; what bodily injury,
defect or disease . 9. The financial condition and
what estate , if any, the person has in possession , re-
version or remainder, and the financial conditions
and what estate the persons liable for his or her
support have , if any, as far as such conditions can
be ascertained ; together with whatever else may be
deemed material to enable the superintendent of an
institution to understand the case. Said statement
or a copy shall be sent with the record to the institu-
tion to which the person may be assigned .
$88. Commonwealth or County Attorney : Infor-
mation to Furnish ; Penalty for Failure. The com-
monwealth or county attorney in attendance at the
inquest shall ascertain and furnish to the superin-
tendent information as to the address of the pa-
tient , and also the name of the patient's parents,
their address , and if the party be married , the name
of the husband or wife and his or her address . This
information the said attorney may have the clerk
endorse on the inquest and history of the case to be
forwarded the superintendent .
§ 89. Disposition of Patient If No Vacancy In
Institution ; Duty of Judge and Superintendent ;
Necessary Orders ; Commitment to Guardianship .
If a vacancy in any institution does not exist or if
there is not room in the institution for the person
sought to be committed , the superintendent shall re-
turn the papers to the judge , and thereupon , with
out further proceedings , the judge shall , unless
otherwise specially provided by law , issue a supple-
mentary order committing the feeble -minded , epil-
eptic , insane person or idiot to guardianship until
a vacancy exists in the institution . In such case
the judge shall send to the superintendent a copy of
the supplementary order of commitment to guard-
ianship and a copy of the original order of commit-
ment , the petition , the certificate of mental defi-
ciency or epilepsy and his written statement .
$ 90. Occurrence of Vacancy ; Disposition of
Patient ; Termination of Guardianship ; Duty of
Superintendent to Give Notice and Send for Pa-
tient ; Allowance Prorated . When a vacancy occurrs
in an institution to which a court has sought to com-
mit a patient but because , through lack of accommo-
dation at said institution for such patients , the pa-
tient was committed to guardianship , the superin-
tendent shall immediately notify the judge and clerk
of the court having charge of the patient and shall
send an attendant to convey such patient to the in-
stitution . Such person shall be delivered to the at-
tendant immediately upon arrival and the commit-
ment to guardianship shall thereupon cease and the
original order of commitment to the institution
shall take effect .
$ 91. Pauper Idiot Not to Be Sent to Asylum
Unless Dangerous : Verdict at Inquest to Show . No
order shall be made by any court or officer for send-
ing a pauper idiot to an asylum , nor shall such idiot
be received therein unless the jury by their verdict
on the inquest , shall find that he is so dangerous or
uncontrollable that he can not be safely and prop-
erly kept by a committee within the county .
§ 92. Refusal to Receive . The superintendent
or person in charge of any institution for the feeble-
minded or insane may refuse to receive any person
upon an order of commitment , if the papers pre-
sented do not comply with the provisions of this
act, or if in his judgment the person is not feeble-
minded or insane within the meaning of this act .
The attendant sent for a patient shall examine the
papers before he conveys the patient to the institu-
tion and shall not convey the patient if his papers
are incomplete , but his approval of them shall not
be conclusive .
§ 93. Conveyance to Asylum ; When County to
Pay ; Mileage Allowed and When Not Paid ; Orders
of Court . If the court wherein an inquest is held
shall order as necessary an additional guard his ex-
penses shall be paid by the county and the costs
shall not exceed six cents per mile for the guard or
guards and patient , each , going , and six cents per
mile for the guard returning , the distance to be es-
timated by the nearest usual route of travel . If the
patient can not be received by the asylum , six cents
per mile for his returning shall also be allowed ; but
no allowance for expenses of either guard or pa-
tient to or from the asylum shall be made unless
either an application has been made first by letter
to the superintendent or an order of court made to
carry the patient to the asylum immediately on ac-
count of violent and dangerous character .
§ 94. Idiots , Epileptics and Harmless Lunatics ;
Disposition of . All pauper idiots , epileptics and
harmless , incurable lunatics shall be returned by the
asylum in which they may be confined to the several
counties from which they are sent and delivered
into the custody of their friends , if any ; if not , then
to the county judge , or , if they be residents of and
sent from the city of Louisville , then to the mayor
of that city, who shall make suitable provision for
their keeping out of the annual appropriation al-
lowed for such persons . The superintendent and
his staff shall investigate each case carefully , and ,
if they all concur in the opinion that an inmate can
be safely sent back , they shall order such patient re-
turned to the county from whence he was sent and
shall deliver with him a certificate of their finding .
95. Restoration ; Inquest ; Discharge as Cured .
No person who has been adjudged of unsound mind
at an inquest shall be discharged from any institu-
tion whatever as cured or restored until he has been
found, by an inquest for restoration held in the
court which adjudged him of unsound mind , to be
cured or restored .
§ 96. Inquiry as to Restoration ; Verdict ; Judg-
ment . Whenever it shall appear , from an affidavit
filed , to the county or circuit court in which any per-
son has been adjudged of unsound mind, that a per-
son of unsound mind has been restored to his pro-
per senses, or that the inquest was false or fraudu-
lent the court shall forthwith direct the facts to be
inquired into by a jury in open court and make all
necessary orders and decrees in the premises .
If the jury shall find the person charged who had
heretofore been found of unsound mind , to be of
sound mind then the court shall enter an order and
judgment that said person is restored and give him
all the rights and privileges of a person of sound
mind.
§ 97. Duty of Clerk of Court ; Penalty . When
an inquest of restoration is held and the person
upon whom the inquest is held is adjudged to be of
sound mind and is restored , the clerk of the court
shall locate among his records the order adjudging
such person a person of unsound mind and the in-
dex thereof and shall note said restoration thereon

§ 101. Appeal to Circuit Court . Circuit Courts
shall have the jurisdiction in all cases for the restor-
ation of persons to sound mind , and any party in
interest shall have the right to appeal from the
judgment of the County Court to the Circuit Court ,
and upon the appeal the Circuit Court shall hear the
proceedings de novo .
§ 102. Unlawful Inquest ; Penalty . Whoever
shall knowingly conspire or contrive to have one
unlawfully or fraudulently adjudged an idiot or
feeble -minded or insane , or confined in any institu-
tion whatever within the boundaries of this state
for the feeble -minded , epileptic or insane , shall be
fined not less than $ 100 nor more than $ 500 , or im-
prisoned not less than three months nor more than
one year , or both .
103. Penalty for Bringing Persons Into This
State to be a Charge Upon the State or Fraudu-
lently Procuring an Adjudication as an Idiot . Who-
ever shall bring or cause to be brought into any
county or city of this commonwealth from any state
or country any feeble -minded , epileptic, insane per-
son or idiot with the intent to make him a charge
upon this commonwealth , or who shall fraudulently
secure any adjudication that a person is a pauper
idiot with the purpose of securing the allowance
provided by this act , shall be fined $ 100 or impris-
oned three months or both , and shall further be li-
able , at the suit of the commonwealth , for all dam-
ages incurred thereby , including the cost of trans-
portation .
§ 104. Release of Patients Upon Certificate of
Superintendent . Whenever in the judgment of the
superintendent of a state institution for the feeble-
minded , epileptic or insane the condition of an in-
mate has sufficiently improved so that his release
will not be injurious to him or detrimental to the
public welfare , or because he is not a proper case for
treatment at any state institution , the superinten-
dent may , on filing his written certificate with the
board of charities and corrections , release such per-
son , unless the person is held upon an order arising
out of a criminal offense . Before making such cer-
tificate , the superintendent shall satisfy himself by
sufficient proof that friends or relatives of the per-
son are willing and financially able to receive and
properly care for such person after his discharge ,
if he is unable to care for himself . If the person to
be discharged be poor or indigent , he shall be re-
turned to the county judge in the county from which
he was committed , or to the mayor of the City of
Louisville , as elsewhere provided for in the case of
pauper idiots , epileptics and harmless incurable
lunatics .
§ 105. Request to Discharge Patients ; Proced-
ure If Discharge Refused . If the superintendent is
unwilling to discharge a person upon request being
made to do so and so certifies in writing , giving his
reasons therefor , the judge of the county court in
the county in which the institution is situated may ,
upon such certificate and an opportunity for a hear-
ing thereon being accorded the superintendent , and
upon such other proof as may be produced before
him, direct , by order, the discharge of such person ,
upon such security to the people of the state as he
may require , for the good behavior and maintenance
of the person so discharged .
§ 106. Family or Friends : Removal of Patients
By . The superintendents of the several asylums
shall have the right and authority to permit the
family or friends of patients whose condition of
mind and health is such as , in the opinion of such
superintendents , may be taken care of and treated
properly outside of the asylum, to be taken from the
asylum, either permanently or for such length of
time as the superintendent may deem prudent .
§ 107. It is the intention of the General Assem-
bly to enact this act in sections and if any provision
or section of this act shall be held for any reason to
be void or ineffective it shall not effect the remain-
der of the act .

and enacting the following in lieu thereof relating to the State Board of Char- ities and Corrections , a body politic and corporate , prescribing their duties , powers and administration of the following de- partments , namely , State Reformatory at Frankfort , Ky ., State Penitentiary at Eddyville , Ky., House of Reform , Green- dale , Ky., Eastern State Hospital at Lexington , Ky. , Central State Hospital at Lakeland , Ky., State Hospital for the Crim- inally Insane , Lakeland , Ky., Western State Hospital at Hop- kinsville , Ky ., Feeble -Minded Institute at Frankfort , Ky., and House of Reform for girls in Shelby County , Ky .; providing for the election of a Commissioner of Public Institutions who shall execute bond in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ( $25,000.00 ) for the faithful discharge of his duties , and pre- scribing his duties ; that no commissioner or other officer shall sell anything to the institutions , and providing a penalty for violation ; that the board may appoint superintendents , as- sistants and other employees for each institution , fix their salaries and prescribing their duties ; that the superintendents of each institution for the Insane and Feeble -Minded shall keep a register of all patients which shall contain a history of each patient received into the asylum ; that the superin- tendent of each institution shall keep a restraint record which shall show the number of persons in each institution subject to restraints which record shall be open to inspection of the board at all times ; that the board may appoint a receiver and prescribe his duties ; that the receiver shall execute bond in a sum to be fixed by the board ; that the board shall pro- vide for such officers and employees for each institution and for such clerical and other assistants as it may deem neces- sary ; that the board may not dispense with the office of commissioner of public institution , superintendent or receiver ; that no commissioner , officer or employee of the Board of Charities and Corrections or any of the institutions under its control shall accept a free gift from any person or cor- poration who has or had a contract with said board or any of its institutions under its control , and fixing a penalty for violation ; providing that all officers and servants of each in- stitution shall be exempt from military duty, from working on the public highways , from service on juries ; that no officer or servant shall be required to give personal attendance as a witness in any civil suit out of the county , but their depositions may be required in lieu thereof ; that the fiscal years of the institution shall begin July 1st and close June 30th ; the superintendents of each institution and Board of Charities and Corrections shall make a report to the Governor of the con- dition of the institutions under their charge which report the Governor shall communicate to the Legislature at its next regular session ; that each superintendent in charge of an in- stitution shall prepare and submit to the board annually , or as often as required , a budget or estimate of the expenditures required for the maintenance of such institution ; that the board shall prepare annually a budget for all the institutions and agencies under its control and submit same to the Gov- ernor or the Budget Commission ; the board may apportion its appropriation made for the benefit of the institutions as between the various institutions in such manner as the in- terest of such institutions require ; that the appropriation made for the Board of Charities and Corrections shall be pay- able by warrant drawn by the Auditor monthly for such sums of money as are necessary to operate the institutions under its control, including salaries to all officers and employees . The order shall be signed by the Commissioner of Public In- stitutions and approved by the chairman of the board ; pre- scribing the duty of the Auditor ; providing that the super- intendent of each institution shall have power to purchase necessary incidental and emergency supplies for his institu- tion subject to the approval of the Board of Charities and Corrections . The superintendent of each institution shall ex- amine all claims and accounts against their respective in- stitutions and report any irregularity to the board . They shall not direct any claim to be paid unless it is just , legal and right . Providing that the Commissioner of Public Insti- tutions shall keep a record of the payment of money , receipts , deposits and disbursements ; that the Governor may direct the State Inspector and Examiner to inspect the books and ac- counts of the Board of Charities and Corrections or any in- stitution , and make the report of the financial condition and management of any institution under the control of said board ; that said board shall have full control of all institutions named in this act , and that it is their duty to inquire and ex- amine into the government and management of the inmates , official conduct of officers and employees , conditions of build- ings and grounds , and for any neglect or refusal on the part of members of said board they shall be subject to a penalty of two hundred and fifty dollars ( $250.00 ) ; that said board is authorized to keep the buildings , furniture and other property under their control insured ; that they are authorized to cancel at any time , or cause to be cancelled , any insurance in their judgment ; that the board may issue license to charitable organizations supported in whole or in part by appropriations from the State Treasury ; that no such organizations or repre- sentative thereof shall solicit outside the county in which it is located ; that any person violating this provision may be fined in any sum not less than fifty dollars ( $ 50.00 ) nor more than two hundred dollars ( $200.00 ) ; that the board is vested with the power of eminent domain and the procedure to condemn real estate is the same as condemnation proceedings for rail- road purposes ; that the University of Kentucky shall , at the request of the Board of Charities and Corrections , examine and report on any lands or soils which the board may wish to investigate , and to advise said board of the quality and character of soil , water supply , sanitation , agricultural and engineering problems . The services rendered by said Uni- versity shall be free , but it shall be entitled to receive its necessary expenses in making said investigations , and said Board of Charities and Corrections shall make such rules and regulations as are necessary for the management and control of the institutions named in this act .
