laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 48 .
AN ACT providing free textbooks for all the children of the
State who attend free public schools , grades one to eight , in-
clusive ; providing for the purchase of books by the State ;
providing for the distribution of the books to the pupils ; and
providing for a reasonable expense for those engaged in the
distribution .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the State Board of Education is hereby
authorized and empowered and it is made its duty
to purchase books from the contractors of textbooks
used in the free public schools of the State and to
distribute the same without cost to the pupils at-
tending such schools , grades one to eight , inclusive ,
within this State in the manner and upon the condi-
tions hereinafter set out :
§ 2. That in order to carry out the provisions of
this Act : ( one ) There is hereby appropriated out of
the State Treasury , annually, a sum sufficient to
cover the cost and distribution of Free Textbooks
herein provided for , and the Treasurer , of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky , is hereby directed to pay
for same, upon presentation of triplicate voucher
for same, signed by the Superintendent of Public
Instruction and approved by the State Board of
Education . (two) There is hereby appropriated ,
annually , for a period of two years , the sum of Fif-
teen Thousand Dollars , or so much thereof , as may
be necessary , to be used by the State Board of Edu-
cation in the Administration of this Act , as herein
provided and provided that any unused portion of
the same , shall biennially be covered into the gen-
eral funds of the Treasury .
§ 3. The purchase and distribution of free text-
books by the State shall be under the management
of the State Superintendent of Public Instruction ,
subject to the approval of the State Board of Edu-
cation .
$ 4. That it shall be the duty of the Superinten-
dent of Public Instruction , subject to the approval
of the State Board of Education , to purchase the
textbooks from the publishers with whom the Text-
book Commission has entered into contract . Such
purchases to be upon requisitions of county super-
intendents , independent graded school principals ,
and city superintendents as hereinafter provided .
§ 5. That the Superintendent of Public Instruc-
tion shall prepare or cause to be prepared requisi-
tion forms on which all county superintendents , in-
dependent graded school principals , and city super-
intendents shall requisition the books needed for
the next ensuing school term in the districts of
their respective jurisdictions . Such requisition
shall be filed with the superintendent of Public In-
struction at least one hundred and twenty ( 120 )
days before the beginning of school in the various
districts . The Superintendent of Public Instruc-
tion , under direction of the State Board of Educa-
tion, shall order the textbooks , which have been
requisitioned , from the various publishers accord-
ing to the terms of the contracts entered into by and
between the State Textbook Commission and the
publishers . Such textbooks shall be shipped by the
Publisher , by prepaid freight , express or parcel
post , as directed by the Superintendent of Public
Instruction , direct to the County Superintendents ,
City Superintendents , and principals of schools , as
may be directed by the Superintendent of Public
Instruction . The Publishers shall issue invoices in
triplicate . Invoice number one shall be sent direct
to the Superintendent of Public Instruction and In-
voices number two and three shall be sent to the
superintendent or principal receiving the textbooks .
Upon receipt of the textbooks the superintendent
or principal shall check the shipment against the
invoice and O. K. invoice number two to the Super-
intendent of Public Instruction as a receipt of the
shipment . The State Board of Education may then
order payment .
§ 6. That all textbooks purchased under the
provisions of this Act are and shall remain the
property of the State . The superintendents and
principals making requisition for the textbooks are
custodians of the books in their respective jurisdic-
tion . They shall issue the books to the various
schools and districts in their jurisdiction accord-
ing to the rules and regulations which shall be form-
ulated by the Superintendent of Public Instruction ,
subject to the approval of the State Board of Edu-
cation .
§ 7. That specific rules as to the requisition ,
distribution , care and use of textbooks shall be
made by the State Superintendent of Public In-
struction , subject to the approval of the State
Board of Education ; provided , that such rules shall
not conflict with the provisions of this Act ; nor with
the uniform textbook law under the terms of which
contracts for books have been made or may here-

CHAPTER 65 .
AN ACT to appropriate the sum of one hundred eighty -four thou-
sand , one hundred forty -five ( $ 184,145.66 ) dollars and sixty-
six cents for the use and benefit of the Kentucky State In-
dustrial College for Colored Persons for the training of teach-
ers and industrial leaders , to restore a dormitory that was
burned upon the campus of said Kentucky State Industrial
College for the Training of Teachers and Industrial Leaders
on the 13th day of December , 1926 , and for equipment and
other improvements upon the campus of said college , and
authorizing and directing the Auditor of Public Accounts to
draw his warrant in favor of the trustees of said college at
such times and in such amounts as said trustees shall order ,
as said work progresses until the whole sum of one hundred
eighty -four thousand , one hundred forty -five ($ 184,145.66 ) dol-
lars and sixty-six cents is expended in such improvements and
appropriating said one hundred eighty -four thousand one hun-
dred forty -five ( $ 184,145.66 ) dollars and sixty-six cents out of
the general expenditure fund of the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky and making said appropriation of said one hundred
eighty -four thousand , one hundred forty -five ( $ 184,145.66 ) dol-
lars and sixty-six cents for improvements upon the campus of
said college and for no other purpose .
All of which appropriation and expenditure to be credited with
the full amount of all insurance collected on account of the
burning of said girls ' dormitory to be replaced .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That the sum of One Hundred Eighty-four
Thousand , One Hundred Forty -five ($ 184,145.66 )
Dollars and Sixty -six cents be and is hereby appro-
priated out of the general expenditure fund of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky for the benefit of the
Kentucky State Industrial College for the Training
of Teachers and Industrial Leaders , for the pur-
pose of erecting and equipping a girls ' dormitory
upon the Campus of said College to take the place
of the dormitory and equipment destroyed by fire
on said campus on December 13 , 1926 , said sum to
be used exclusively for the erection of said dormi-
tory and for the purpose of equipment and for mak-
ing other improvements upon the campus of said
College , and said sum so appropriated is appro-
priated for the immediate use of the Trustees of
said College for the erection and construction of
said building and said improvements aforesaid .
All said building equipment and improvement
shall be let publicly at open and competitive bidding
to the lowest and best bidders , after advertising
same for not less than ten days in one or more
newspapers of general circulation and published in
this state and otherwise if desired , stating the time ,
place , and conditions of such lettings , with right to
reject any or all bids and readvertise .
$ 2. The Auditor of Public Accounts is hereby
authorized and directed to draw his warrant in
favor of the trustees of the aforesaid College at
such times and for such amounts as said Trustees
shall direct against appropriation until the entire
sum of One Hundred Eighty-four Thousand , One
Hundred Forty -five ( $ 184,145.66 ) Dollars and
Sixty-six cents is used for said purpose aforesaid .
Said sum so appropriated shall be credited by
the amount of insurance received on account of the
burning of the building this appropriation is made
to replace .
§ 3. Whereas owing to the burning of the girls '
dormitory upon the campus of the College herein
mentioned and the crowded , unsanitary and un-
healthful conditions in which the pupils of said Col-
lege are placed and by reason of lack of room and
by reason of said College being hampered and re-
tarded in its beneficial work and by reason of the
lack of room , an emergency is now and hereby de-
clared to exist and this bill shall take effect and be
in force from and after it is passed and approved
by the Governor as the needs of said College are im-
mediate and imperative .
Approved February 21 , 1928 .

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 84.
AN ACT to enable cities of the third class to adopt and operate
under the city manager form of goverment , and amending
section three thousand four hundred and eighty b-three of Car-
roll's Kentucky Statutes , one thousand nine hundred and
twenty-two edition .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That any city of the third class may become
organized and be governed under the city manager
form of government according to section one thou-
sand four hundred and eighty b-three as herein
amended and section three thousand four thousand
(hundred ) and eighty b-four , three thousand four
hundred and eighty b-five , three thousand four hun-
dred and eighty b-six, three thousand four hundred
and eighty b - seven , three thousand four hundred
and eighty b-eight , three thousand four hundred
and eighty b-nine , three thousand four hundred
and eighty b-ten , three thousand four hundred and
eighty b-eleven , three thousand four hundred and
eighty b-twelve , three thousand four hundred and
eighty b-thirteen , three thousand four hundred and
eighty b-fourteen , three thousand four hundred and
eighty b-fifteen , three thousand four hundred and
eighty b-sixteen , three thousand four hundred and
eighty b- seventeen , three thousand four hundred
and eighty b-eighteen , three thousand four hundred
and eighty b-nineteen , three thousand four hundred
and eighty b-twenty , three thousand four hundred
and eighty b-twenty -one , three thousand four hun-
dred and eighty b-twenty -two , three thousand four
hundred and eighty b-twenty -three , three thousand
four hundred and eighty b-twenty-four , three thou-
sand four hundred and eighty b-twenty -five , three
thousand four hundred and eighty b -twenty -six,
three thousand four hundred and eighty b - twenty-
seven , three thousand four hundred and eighty b-
twenty - eight , three thousand four hundred and
eighty b-twenty - nine , all of said sections being of
Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , one thousand nine
hundred and twenty-two edition , and according to
the provisions of this act by proceeding as herein
provided . Organizing under this act shall not
change the corporate entity of any such city , nor
alter the body politic and corporate .
§ 2. All laws , statutes , by-laws , ordinances and
resolutions in force , applicable to and governing
any city of the third class before the adoption of
city manager form of government , and not inconsis-
tent with this act , shall continue to be in force after
said adoption until altered or repealed in the regu-
lar manner .
§ 3. That section three thousand four hundred
and eighty b-three of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes ,
one thousand nine hundred and twenty-two edition ,
be amended by repealing all of said section and re-
enacting in lieu thereof the following : It shall be
the duty of the county judge in the county , in which
is located a city of the third class proposing to take
the sense of its voters , as herein provided , upon
the change in organization and government , upon
the application by written petition signed by a num-
ber of legal voters , of said city equal to twenty per
centum ( 20 % ) of the votes cast in said city , at the
last proceeding (preceding ) general election , to re-
ceive said petition , and at the next regular term
thereafter to make an order on his order book di-
recting an election to be held in said city at the next
regular election and not earlier than sixty days
after said application is lodged with the said judge ,
which order shall direct the sheriff , or other officer
of said county who may be appointed to hold said
election , to open the polls at each and all of the vot-
ing places in said city upon the question as to
whether or not the citizens in said city are in favor
of the organization and government of said city , un-
der the provisions of this act or such other acts as
may utilize the election procedure herein specified .
The question to be submitted to the voters shall be :
"Are you in favor of the organization and govern-
ment of the city of ( naming the city in which vote is
to be taken ) , under the City Manager Form of Gov-
ernment ( or Commission Form of Government , as
the case may be ) , according to the provisions of an
act (naming this act and giving the year or date of
passage or approval or both ) . " It shall be the duty
of the County Clerk to give to the sheriff of the
county , or to such officers as may be appointed to
hold said election , a certified copy of the order of
the County Court as it appears on the order book ,
within five days after such order is made ; and it
shall be the duty of said sheriff , or other officer , to
have said order published in some weekly or daily
newspaper published or circulated in said county ,
for at least two weeks before the election , and also
to advertise , the same by printed or written hand-
bills , posted in conspicuous places in said city , for
the same length of time . If there is no weekly or
daily newspaper published in said city , or the pro-
prietor of said paper refuses to publish such notice ,
the printed or written handbills provided for shall
be sufficient notice . The sheriff or other such officer
shall have the advertisement and notices herein
·
provided for posted as here required , within seven
days after he receives the order of the county court .
All elections provided for in this act , except the pri-
mary elections , shall be held on the regular election
day by the regular election officers . If it shall be
found that a majority of the legal votes cast at the
election hereinabove provided for were given for or
against said proposition submitted , it shall be the
duty of the canvassing board to certify that fact ,
which certificate shall be delivered to the clerk of
the county court and a copy thereof delivered to the
clerk or recorder of the city , and at the next regu-
lar term of said court , the county judge shall cause
the same to be spread on the order book of said
court, and the entry of said certificate in the order
book , or copy thereof , shall be prima facie evidence
of the facts therein contained . When a majority of
the votes cast shall be in favor of organizing and
governing the city under the provisions of this act ,
and said fact shall be certified as hereinbefore pro-
vided , by the said canvassing board to the county
clerk, a copy of which shall be certified to the city
clerk, and said copy of said certificates shall be
spread upon the records of said county , as herein.
provided , and upon the records of said city at the
next regular meeting of the city council ; thereupon
said city shall be organized and governed by the
provisions of this act .
§ 4. The mayor shall be elected for a term of
four years, beginning on the first Monday in Janu-
ary following his election ; and shall receive an an-
nual salary , to be determined by the legislative
body of the city prior to his election , of not more
than Seven Hundred and Fifty Dollars ( $ 750.00 ) .
§ 5. The Commissioners shall be elected each
for a term of two years , beginning the first Monday
Acts- 11
in January, following their election ; and each shall
receive an annual salary , to be determined by the
legislative body of the city prior to his election , of
not more than Five Hundred Dollars ( $ 500.00 ) .
§ 6. Under the City Manager Form of Govern-
ment the board of commissioners shall select and
employ a city manager who shall not be an officer
or official of the city but the executive agent of the
mayor and board of commissioners in the manage-
ment of city affairs . Neither the mayor nor board
of commissioners nor any commissioner shall dic-
tate the appointment of any person to office or em-
ployment by the city manager , or in any manner in-
terfere with the city manager or prevent him from
exercising his own judgment in the appointment of
officers and employees in the administrative service .
Except for the purpose of inquiry the board of com-
missioners and its members shall deal with the ad-
ministrative service solely through the city man-
ager , and neither the board of commissioners nor
any members shall deal with the administrative
service solely through the city manager , and neither
the board of commissioners nor any member thereof
shall give orders to any of the subordinates of the
city manager , either publicly or privately . Any dic-
tation , prevention , orders , or other interference on
the part of the mayor or of a member of the board
of commissioners with the administration of the
city shall be deemed to be a misdemeanor , and upon
conviction any member so convicted shall be sub-
ject to a fine not exceeding Five Hundred Dollars or
imprisonment for a term not exceeding two months
or both , and such conviction shall operate to re-
move him, and the judgment of the court shall de-
clare the office vacant .
§ 7. The Mayor shall preside at meetings of the
board of commissioners and perform such other
·
•
duties consistent with this office as may be imposed
by the board of commissioners . He shall be rocog-
nized as the official head of the city for all ceremo-
nial purposes , by the courts for the purpose of serv-
ing civil processes , and by the governor for mili-
tary purposes . In time of public danger or emer-
gency he may, with the consent of the board of com-
missioners , take command of the police and main-
tain order and enforce the laws . During his ab-
sence or disability his duties shall be performed by
another member appointed by the board of commis-
sioners .
·
§ 8. The city manager shall be chosen by the
board of commissioners solely on the basis of his
executive and administrative qualifications . The
choice shall not be limited to inhabitants of the city
or state . He shall be employed for an indefinite
period . He shall be removable at will by the board
of commissioners , but such removal shall not be ef-
fected by a reduction in the compensation of the
city managers , and if removed at any time after
having served for six months he may in writing de-
mand written charges and a public hearing on the
same before the board of commissioners prior to the
date on which his final removal shall take effect , but
during such hearing the board of commissioners
may suspend him from office . Such public hearing
shall be fixed by the board of commissioners not to
exceed thirty days after such demand therefor .
During the absence or disability of the city man-
ager the board of commissioners shall designate
some properly qualified person to perform the
duties of the office . The city manager shall receive
such compensation as may be determined by the
board of commissioners .
$§ 9. The city manager shall be responsible to
the board of commissioners for the proper admin-
istration of all affairs of the city , and to that end
shall make all appointments , except as otherwise
provided in this law . Except when the board of
commissioners is considering his removal , the city
manager shall be entitled to be present at all meet-
ings of the board of commissioners and of the com-
mittees and to take part in their discussion .
$ 10 . The board of commissioners shall create
by ordinance such administrative departments as in
the judgment of the board are reasonably required
for the efficient , orderly and economical administra-
tion of the business affairs of the city ; and may at
any time create new departments , combine or abol-
ish existing departments , or establish temporary
departments and may also prescribe by ordinance
the functions of each department and provide for
the appointment or employment of a Director of
each , or of one or more of such departments . Di-
rectors of departments shall be appointed by the
city manager , and may be removed by him at any
time . Any person employed in any department
may be removed at any time by the directors of such
department , or by the city manager , subject to such
civil service rules and regulations as may be
deemed necessary for the efficient and non -political
handling of city affairs .
§ 11. Powers of Subpoena .- The board of com-
missioners , the city manager , and any officer or
board authorized by them , or either of them, shall
have the power to make investigations as to city af-
fairs , to subpoena witnesses , administer oaths , and
compel the production of books and papers .
§ 12. Annual Budget . Once each year the city
manager shall prepare and submit to the board of
commissioners an annual budget for the ensuing fis-
cal year , based upon detailed estimates furnished
by the several departments and other divisions of
the city government , according to a classification as
nearly uniform as possible . The budget shall pre-
sent the following information : ( a ) An itemized
statement of the appropriations recommended by
city manager for current expenses and for perma-
nent improvements for each department and each
division thereof for the ensuing fiscal year with
comparative statements in parallel columns of the
appropriations and expenditures for the current
and next preceding fiscal year , and the increases or
decreases in the appropriations recommended ; ( b )
An itemized statement of the taxes required and of
the estimated revenues of the city from all other
sources for the ensuing fiscal year , with compara-
tive statements in parallel columns of the taxes and
other revenues for the current and next preceding
fiscal year, and of the increases and decreases esti-
mated or proposed ; ( c ) A statement of the financial
condition of the city ; and (d ) Such other informa-
tion as may be required by the board of commis-
sioners . Copies of the budget shall be printed and
available for distribution not later than two weeks
after submission to the board of commissioners and
a public hearing shall be given thereon by the board
of commissioners or a committee thereof before ac-
tion by the board of commissioners .
Temporary§ 13. Appropriation Ordinance ;
Appropriation ; Transfers .-The board of commis-
sioners shall pass an annual appropriation ordi-
nance , which shall be based on the budget submit-
ted by the city manager . The total amount of ap-
propriations shall not exceed the estimated reven-
ues of the city . Before the annual appropriation
ordinance has been passed , the board of commis-
sioners , with the recommendation in writing of the
city manager , may make appropriations for the cur-
rent department expenses , chargeable to the appro-
priations for the year when passed , to an amount
sufficient to cover the necessary expenses of the var-
ious departments until the annual appropriation is
in force . No other liabilities shall be incurred by
any officer or employee of the city, except in accord-
ance with the provisions of the annual appropria-
tion ordinance or under continuing contracts and
loans authorized under the provisions of this char-
ter . At any meeting after the passage of the ap-
propriation ordinance , and after at least one week's
notice , the board of commissioners may amend such
ordinance , so as to authorize the transfer of un-
used appropriated for one purpose to another pur-
pose , to appropriate available revenues not in-
cluded in the annual budget .
§ 14. Each fiscal year an annual audit shall be
made of all the accounts of all city officers ; and
upon the death , resignation , removal or expiration
of the terms of the director of finance , an audit shall
be made of his accounts . Such audits shall be made
under the provisions of any law for the inspection
and audit of municipal accounts by state officers ;
and if there is no such state inspection such audits.
shall be made by qualified public accountants , se-
lected by the board of commissioners , who have no
personal interest , direct or indirect , in the financial
affairs of the city or of any of its officers ; or em-
ployees . The board of commissioners may at any
time provided for an examination or audit of the
accounts of any officer or department of the city
government . The board of commissioners shall re-
quire bonds with adequate surety of such amounts
as it may deem advisable , from the city manager ,
the director of the department of finance and from
any other city employee whose duties , in the opinion
of said board , require a bond for faithful perform-
ance . Any premiums on any or all of said bonds
may at the discretion of the board of commissioners
be paid by the city .
§ 15. The adoption by any city of the third class
of the city manager form of government as herein
provided shall not as to any such city , unless such
city shall have heretofore adopted and be operat-
ing under the Commission Plan of Government , be-
come effective or go into operation until the expira-
tion of the year for which the duly elected city offi-
cials may have been elected .
16. The provisions of this act shall be sever-
able , and if any of the provisions shall be held to
be unconstitutional , the decision of the court shall
not affect the validity of the remaining provisions .
Approved March 21 , 1928 .

CHAPTER 94 .
AN ACT to amend sections ten (10 ) and eleven ( 11 ) of chapter
sixty -four , Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky one thousand nine hundred and twenty-four , "An
Act relating to registration for elections in cities and towns
having a population of five thousand inhabitants or more .” Ap-
proved March twenty-first , one thousand nine hundred and
twenty -four .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That section ten , chapter sixty -four , of the
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky , one thousand nine hundred and twenty-
four , be amended by inserting after the word " reg-
istration " in line fifty and before the word “ at ” in ,
line fifty -one in said section ten of said printed act ,
and insert the following words : "But in counties
where registration is required in only one town or
city-then the registration shall be held in that town
or city and not at the county seat when registration
is not required in the county seat town or city . Also
amend section eleven ( 11 ) of said act by inserting
after the word " registration " and before the word
1
"at" in line eight of said section eleven (11 ) the
following words : " But in counties where registra-
tion is required in only one town or city , then the
registration shall be held in that town or city and
not at the county seat or city when registration is
not required in said county seat town or city ." So
that said sections ten ( 10 ) and eleven ( 11 ) will when
amended read as follows : Section ten . Thirty days
preceding the August primary election in each year,
including the year one thousand nine hundred and
twenty -four, the County Board of Election Commis-
sioners in each county , where registration is re-
quired under this act , shall appoint four qualified
voters of each city or town as special officers of reg-
istration for such city or town . The county execu-
tive committee of the two political parties having
representation on the State and County Board of
Election Commissioners may , on or before forty
days before the August primary in each year , desig-
nate in writing a list of four names to the County
Board of Election Commissioners and from these
four names if any are so designated , the special offi-
cers of registration shall be selected from said lists
as follows : One judge shall be selected from each
of said list and in like manner the sheriff shall be
chosen from one of said lists and the clerk from the
other . If no lists are submitted to said County
Board of Election Commissioners then the special
officers of registration shall be so selected and ap-
pointed as that one of the judges shall be of one po-
litical party and the other judge of a different po-
litical party and there shall be a like difference be-
tween the sheriff and clerk of registration . Said
special officers of registration shall have the same
qualifications as regular officers of registration
shall receive the same compensation , and shall hold
their office for one year or until their successors are
appointed and qualified . Said special officers of
registration shall be notified of their appointment
in the same manner as officers of registraton aire
required to be notified . Commencing on the four-
teenth day preceding the August primary election
in each year such special officers of registration
shall sit for one day , in each county in this State ,
between the hours of six a . m. and seven p . m . at
the courthouse , in a room provided by the county
court clerk , for the purpose of registering all per-
sons who will be legally qualified to vote at the next
primary August election and who failed to register
at the preceding September registration . " But in
counties where registration is required in only one
town or city- then the registration shall be held in
that town or city and not in the county seat town or
city.'" At such special registration the following
persons and no others shall be entitled to register .
1. Any person who was absent from the county
of his or her residence during the entire time of the
September registration for that year .
2. Any person who was prevented from register-
ing by reason of his or her own sickness or by death
in his or her immediate family .
3. Any person who moved into the precinct of
his or her present residence after the regular regis-
tration held during the preceding year .
4. Persons who have become of age since the last
election and have the qualifications of electors .
No person shall be entitled to register at such reg-
istration unless they have the qualifications of voters
in the precincts in which they reside . Before reg-
istering any person under this section the special
officers of registration shall require such person to
make written oath as to the cause of his or her fail-
ure to attend the last September registration . All
affidavits provided for under this section shall be
kept in a bound book made for that purpose . The
names of all persons entitled to register , as pro-
vided in this section , shall be recorded by the clerk
of registration in the regular registration book for
the precinct in which such person resides . The right
of any person to register shall be determined by the
special officers of registration in the following
manner . The judges of such registration shall have
the right to determine such qualification and in case
they disagree then in the first case the clerk of reg-
istration shall cast the deciding vote and in the next
succeeding case, in case of disagreement of the
judges, the sheriff of the registration shall cast the
deciding vote and so during the entire registration
the clerk and sheriff shall alternate in casting the
deciding vote when the judges are unable to agree .
Section 11. Commencing on the first Tuesday in
October of each year such special officers of regis-
tration shall set for two successive days in each
county in this State , between the hours of six a . m .
and seven p . m ., at the courthouse , in a room pro-
vided by the county court clerk, for the purpose of
registering all persons who will be legally qualified
to vote at the November election and who failed to
register at the preceding September registration .
"But in counties where registration is required in
only one town or city- then the registration shall be
held in that town or city , and not at the county seat
or city when registration is not required in said
county seat town or city . " At such special registra-
tion the following persons and no other shall be en-
titled to register .
1. Any person who was absent from the county
of his or her residence during the entire time of the
September registration for that year .
2. Any person who was prevented from register-
ing by reason of his or her own sickness or by death
in his or her immediate family . No person shall be
entitled to register at such registration unless they
have the qualifications of voters in the precincts in
which they reside . Before registering any person
under this section the special officers of the regis-
tration shall require such person to make written
oath as to the cause of his or her failure to attend
the last September registration . All affidavits pro-
vided for under this section shall be kept in a bound
book made for that purpose . The names of all per-
sons entitled to register , as provided in this section ,
shall be recorded by the clerk of registration in the
regular registration book for the precinct in which
such person resides . The right of any person to
register shall be determined by the special officers
of registration in the following manner ; the judges
of such registration shall have the right to deter-
mine such qualification and in case they disagree
then in the first case the clerk of the registration
shall cast the deciding vote , and in the next succeed-
ing case, in case of disagreement of the judges the
sheriff of election shall cast the deciding vote , and
so during such entire registration the clerk and
sheriff shall alternate in casting the deciding vote
when the judges are unable to agree . Except in
counties containing a population of more than two
hundred thousand inhabitants , the County Board of
Election Commissioners shall appoint twelve quali-
fied voters of such county , which shall compose the

§ 2. All acts or parts of acts in conflict with this
Act are to the extent of such conflict hereby repealed .

laws.summary: This statute establishes a registration process for qualified voters in cities of the fourth class, which includes those with populations under five thousand, aligning their registration process with that of larger cities. This could imply a system that may have been used to disenfranchise certain groups, particularly Black voters, in the context of Jim Crow laws.

CHAPTER 97.
AN ACT repealing sections one thousand four hundred and
eighty -six to one thousand five hundred and six , inclusive , of
Kentucky Statutes , Carroll's one thousand nine hundred and
twenty -two edition , relating to registration in certain cities
and towns, including cities of the fourth class , and enacting
in lieu thereof an act providing for registration for elections
in cities of the fourth class , including those having population
of less than five thousand .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
That sections one thousand four hundred and
eighty-six to one thousand five hundred and six , in-
clusive , of Kentucky Statutes , Carroll's one thou-
sand nine hundred and twenty-two edition , be and
the same are hereby repealed , and there is hereby
enacted in lieu thereof the following : In all cities
of the fourth class in this Commonwealth , including
those cities of the fourth class which have a popula-
tion of less than five thousand , there shall be a reg-
istration of all the qualified voters of said cities ,
which shall be held and conducted at the times and
in the manner now provided by law for registration
in cities of the first , second , third and fourth classes
in which the population is more than five thousand ,
as provided by chapter sixty -four of the Acts of the
General Assembly of one thousand nine hundred
and twenty -four . All laws or parts of laws in con-
flict herewith are hereby repealed .
Approved March 17 , 1928 .

CHAPTER 125 .
AN ACT to amend chapter one hundred and thirty -eight of the
Session Acts of one thousand nine hundred and twenty, en-
titled "An Act for the benefit of the Red Cross Association
(colored ) of Louisville ," by increasing the appropriation
therein from five to ten thousand dollars per annum and in-
creasing the bond required thereunder from ten to twenty
thousand dollars .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
That chapter one hundred and thirty -eight of the
Session Acts of one thousand nine hundred and
twenty entitled " An Act for the benefit of the Red
Cross Association ( colored ) of Louisville , be , and
the same is , hereby amended by inserting the words
" Ten Thousand Dollars " in lieu of the words Five
Thousand Dollars therein in reference to the appro-
priation made for the benefit of the Red Cross As-
sociation (colored ) of Louisville , and that the man-
agement of the Red Cross Hospital agrees to main-
tain not less than five ( 5 ) beds especially for the
colored cripple children of Kentucky and to provide
board , clothing, nursing , medical treatment and
such other special treatment such as X-ray pictures
and machanotherapy for said children , and wherein
it directs the Auditor of Public Accounts to issue
his warrant , and further amending said act by sub-
stituting the words "Twenty Thousand Dollars in
lieu of Ten Thousand Dollars wherein it refers to
the bond to be executed by the Red Cross Associa-
tion (colored ) of Louisville , so that said chapter
when it is amended shall read as follows :
Section 1. That there is hereby appropriated
out of any money in the treasury , not otherwise ap-
propriated , the sum of Ten Thousand Dollars per
annum payable annually for the benefit of the Red
Cross Association ( colored ) and the Auditor of
Public Accounts be , and he is , hereby authorized
and directed to draw his warrant upon the treasury
annually in favor of said Red Cross Association
(colored ) for the sum of Ten Thousand Dollars :
Provided , no part of said appropriation shall be
paid until there has been executed on the part of
said association a bond the sum of Twenty Thou-
sand Dollars , to the Commonwealth of Kentucky
with good and sufficient surety, stipulating and pro-
viding that all of said sums of money so appropri-
ated shall be used for the equipment of a hospital to
care for the indigent sick of the Colored race , to be
treated under the supervision and care of their own
people , to equip , maintain and conduct , in connec-
tion with said hospital , a nurses training school ,
where girls of the Colored race may be trained in
practical and professional nursing ; to keep and
maintain in said hospital not less than five ( 5 ) beds
for the care and treatment of invalid and sick Col-
ored children , whose parents are not able to pay for
such treatment , and such children as may be
brought from the Colored Orphan's Home , Colored
Reform School , Colored Blind Asylum and Colored
Children's Home Society, and also that the manage-
ment of the Red Cross Hospital agrees to maintain
not less than five (5 ) beds especially for the Colored
Cripple Children of Kentucky and to provide board,
clothing, nursing , medical treatment and such other
special treatment such as X-ray pictures and mech-
anotherapy for such children, and in no instance
shall any of said sum be paid for officer's salaries ,
but as indicated to be used for purely charitable
purposes to pay for equipment , maintenance ,
nurses , matron, food , medicines , and physicians '
services , and as provided in charter of the institu-
tion , and a failure to so do to be a forfeiture
thereof . Said bond shall be approved by the Audi-
tor of Public Accounts and kept as a record in his
office . If any part of said appropriation be not so
applied then all of such part thereof as may be un-
expended shall be returned to and covered into the
State treasury . Said association , by its proper of-
ficers , ( shall ) make an annual verified statement
and settlement with the Auditor of Public Accounts
showing when , where and how said appropriations ,
have been applied and disbursed , and said associa-
tion shall keep such books of accounts , as to its re-
ceipts and expenditures as may be prescribed by
the State Inspector and Examiner , and which said
books of accounts shall be subject to examination
and audit by said State Inspector and Examiner :
Provided , further , that said association shall not at
any time , or in any manner , anticipate any pay-
ments to it by reason of any appropriations hereby
made .
Section 2. The said Auditor of Public Accounts ,
is authorized and directed to draw his warrants
upon the treasury in favor of said Red Cross Asso-
ciation (colored ) on the first day of July , one thou-
sand nine hundred and twenty -eight , and annually
on the same day and date thereafter , for the sum
of Ten Thousand Dollars .
Section 3. All laws or parts of laws in conflict
herewith are hereby repealed .
Approved March 21 , 1928 .

laws.summary: This statute outlines the qualifications and appointment process for registration officers in Kentucky for the 1930 general initial precinct registration. It specifies that officers must not have been convicted of a felony, must be sober, temperate, discreet, and of good demeanor, not be a candidate in the upcoming election, and be capable of reading the Kentucky Constitution in English and writing legibly. The statute also details the partisan appointment of deputy registrars and inspectors, requiring them to be of opposite political affiliations within each precinct. Compensation for these officers is set at five dollars per day. The Board has the power to remove disqualified officers.

guilty of a misdemeanor , and upon conviction there-
of be fined not less than ten dollars nor more than
one hundred dollars for each offense .
§ 31. Any person who shall , by himself or in
aid of others , forcibly break up or attempt to break
up the initial registration in any precinct , or dis-
turb , intimidate , abuse , or, by force or other unlaw-
ful means , delay or disturb any officer of registra-
tion while performing his official duties , or intimi-
date , abuse or , by force or threats , attempt to pre-
vent any lawful registrant from registering , or ap-
proaching or entering a place of registration , shall
be guilty of a misdemeanor , and upon conviction
thereof shall be fined not less than one hundred dol-
lars nor more than five hundred dollars , or impris-
oned in the county jail for not less than six months
nor more than twelve months , or both so fined and
imprisoned .
$ 32. This Act and each of its various sections ,
paragraphs , clauses , and sections , shall be liberally
construed in favor of the purposes of this Act .
§ 33. If any section , paragraph , clause or separ-
able provision of this Act should be adjudged to be
unconstitutional , such decision shall not affect , or
render unconstitutional any other section , para-
graph , clause or separable provision of the Act , it
being the intention of the General Assembly in en-
acting this Act to enact each section , paragraph ,
clause and provision separately .
34. All laws or parts of laws , relating to the
registration of voters in cities of the first class in
this State , in conflict with the provisions of this Act
are hereby repealed .

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 144.
AN ACT concerning the title records and leases of land owned
or leased by the State , making the Secretary of State the
custodian of all records , judgments , deeds , maps and abstracts
T
of title or other papers or records , and all leases of the com-
monwealth , prescribing his duties relating thereto for the
recording and keeping of such records , and authorizing copies
to be used in evidence in lieu of the original ; providing that
the Commonwealth of Kentucky shall be named as grantee or
lessee instead of naming any of its officers , departments ,
boards , or any other departmental agencies , requiring complete
information of the title to be furnished to the Attorney
General and his written approval of the title before land may
be paid for by the State , and making provision concerning
property acquired by condemnation or through payment of
damage for injury to land , requiring all instruments conveying
or vesting land , or interest in land , in the State to be recorded
in the county wherein the greater portion thereof lies , and
providing the duties of the county clerks in regard thereto ,
providing for similar information , and the approval of the
Attorney General respecting leases to the State and for the
safekeeping of said leases . Requiring each department , offi-
cer, board , association , commission , branch , or other persons
or person occupying or using land or building on behalf of
the State to deliver a sworn list of such land with all records
available to the Attorney General within sixty ( 60 ) days after
the passage and approval of this act, and providing for the
cooperation of all State departments or officials in carrying
out the purposes of this act , and imposing penalty as liquidated
damages for failure and making provisions for the recovery
of such damages . Requiring the Attorney General within
sixty ( 60 ) days after this Act becomes a law to proceed to
supply the Commonwealth with complete information concern-
ing the title to all lands now owned by the State , requiring
the Secretary of State within six ( 6 ) months after this Act
becomes a law to record and keep said records obtained by
the Attorney General , and declaring an emergency to exist , and
that this Act shall take effect immediately upon its passage .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
WHEREAS , the Commonwealth of Kentucky has
been for over a hundred years gradually acquiring
land for state purposes , and
WHEREAS , it now owns the grounds of the
Capitol building , and power house , the grounds of
the old Capitol , the grounds of the penitentiary ,
Feeble Minded Institute , Arsenal , and Industrial
College for Colored Persons in Franklin county , the
grounds of the State Fair , of the Kentucky Chil-
dren's Home , the School for the Blind , and of the
Central State Hospital in Jefferson county , the
grounds of the University of Kentucky , the School
of Reform , Agricultural Experiment Station , and
Eastern State Hospital in Fayette county , the
grounds of the School for the Deaf at Danville , the
grounds of the Western State Hospital in Christian
county , the grounds of the Normal schools at Mur-
ray , Bowling Green , Morehead , Richmond , the
grounds of the West Kentucky Industrial School at
Paducah, the grounds of armories at Barbourville ,
London , Hopkinsville and Bowling Green , the
grounds of the penitentiary at Eddyville in Lyon
county , the grounds of the Confederate Home in
Oldham county , several tracts of forest land totaling
3,624 acres in Harlan county , Pioneer Memorial
State Park in Mercer county , Jefferson Davis Park
and Blue and Gray State Park in Todd county , and
Natural Bridge Park in Powell and Wolfe counties ,
and many other tracts of land in various counties
not herein specifically mentioned , and
WHEREAS , a vast sum of money has been
expended in years past for the acquisition of all of
said land , and ,
WHEREAS , many of said tracts of land are
composed of several smaller tracts which were pur-
chased and assembled to provide the larger tract ,
and ,
WHEREAS , there are no complete records of the
title or boundaries of many of said tracts of land ,
and ,
WHEREAS , there is no centralized collection of
record of any of said lands but all of the records of
1
said lands are at present scattered throughout the
various departments of the State government , and ,
WHEREAS , the present method of keeping the
records of such a valuable and scattered property is
unwise , and ,
WHEREAS , the Commonwealth is acquiring land
in many counties for many purposes such as for
parks , schools , institutions , penal farms , monu-
ments , experiment stations , and other State pur-
poses ,
§ 1. The Secretary of State shall be the custo-
dian of all the records , judgments , deeds , maps , and
abstracts of title of all land or buildings owned or
used for governmental purposes by the Common-
wealth , and of leases of all land or buildings leased
by the Commonwealth for a longer total or con-
tinuous time than one year , except deeds to rights of
way for State or federal roads but not including
State owned bridges or the approaches to bridges .
§ 2. It shall be the duty of the Secretary of State
to record in a book kept in his office for that purpose
all such records , judgments , deeds , maps and
abstracts of title , and in another book similarly
kept , all leases , and to file , safely keep , and have
accessible , the original papers so recorded as well
as the book wherein they are recorded . It shall be
the duty of the Secretary of State to index and cross
index such original papers and record books , and
to index the matters therein concerned or recorded
according to the county wherein the property is
located and also according to the use or department
of the State government using such property . Such
records and indexes shall be public records , but shall
not be moved from the office of the Secretary of
State and whenever any of such records shall be
necessary as evidence , a true copy thereof, certified
to by the Secretary of State , shall be used in lieu
of the original record or paper .
§ 3. The Commonwealth of Kentucky shall here-
after be named as the grantee of any and all land
or any interest in land conveyed to it or for its use
or for the use of any of its departments , boards ,
agencies , commissions or any of its officers , or to
any and all land which is wholly or in part paid for
out of State funds , or which it acquires by gift or
devise .
§ 4. Whenever any land or any right , easement
or interest in any land is to be paid for out of funds
belonging to the State , the grantor shall submit with
the deed conveying such land, a true abstract of the
title to such land , the correctness of which shall be
attested by the county attorney, which abstract shall
show complete information concerning any action
or proceeding concerning said property or said title ,
together with all references to deed , mortgage ,
power of attorney, will , execution , lis pendens ,
option , mechanic liens or other books , tax bills ,
giving page numbers , dates , case numbers and all
other references and the description of the property ,
and the grantor shall submit with such abstract an
accurate map or plat of the boundaries of the land
therein conveyed as made by a competent surveyor
within three months prior to the date of the deed
conveying such tract or tracts of land to the State ,
said map showing the corners , angles and calls of
such boundaries , and the whole shall be submitted
to and approved by the Attorney General before the
Auditor of Public Accounts or officer upon whom
claim for payment is made therefor , shall issue his
warrant or pay for such land . When the Attorney
General shall have given his written approval to the
title and purchase of such land , all records herein
mentioned pertaining thereto including the opinion
of the Attorney General shall be deposited with ,
recorded and safely kept by the Secretary of State
as provided in Section 2 .
§ 5. Whenever the Commonwealth shall acquire
title to any land or any right , easement or interest
in any land as contemplated in Section 1 hereof, by
condemnation proceedings , or through payment of
damages for an injury to any land , the Secretary
of State shall be furnished a certified copy of the
judgment of the court vesting title to the Common-
wealth in said real estate certified by the clerk
thereof and the other information thereof as re-
quired in Section 4 and shall keep and record such
information as provided in Section 2 .
§ 6. All deeds and judgments conveying or vest-
ing in or to the State any land or right , easement or
interest in any land shall be recorded in the office
of the clerk of the county court of the county wherein
such land or the greater part thereof lies , and when
so recorded such deed together with the county
clerk's certificate of record shall be transmitted
forthwith by the county court clerk to the Secretary
of State , and the county clerk before transmitting
said deed to the Secretary of State , shall endorse
on said deed , the Deed Book and page number and
county where he has recorded it as follows :
" Recorded in Deed Book Page
County Court Clerk's Office . "
§ 7. Before any lease of any land or building
(excluding the lease of not more than six offices in
any office building ) shall be occupied by any officer ,
department , board or branch of the State Govern-
ment for any governmental purpose , or be paid for
out of funds belonging to the State , the lessor shall
submit the lease and with it the plat or map men-
tioned in the preceding section and have said lease
and map approved by the Attorney General and
recorded and kept by the Secretary of State as set
out in Section 2. The Commonwealth of Kentucky
shall be named as the lessee in all leases for govern-
mental purposes or for the use of the State instead
of naming therein an officer , board , department or
branch of the State government .
$ 8. (a ) Within sixty days after the passage and
approval of this act , each officer , board , department ,
association , commission , branch or other persons or
person who now have title to or have leased , or who
is or are occupying or using as owner or lessee any
land or building for the use of the State , or which
heretofore so occupied or used any land or buildings
which have been abandoned but which have not been
sold or conveyed by law by the State , or which was
or is paid for in whole or in part out of funds belong-
ing to the State , or was conveyed or bequeathed to
the State , shall prepare a list of said property , and
deliver same to the Attorney General . Said list
shall be in the form of an affidavit and shall be sworn
to by the person submitting it and shall show when
said property was acquired or leased , the amount
for which it was purchased or leased and by what
law said purchase or lease was authorized . With
said list and attached thereto , shall be delivered
every deed , abstract of title , judgment or court
record , map , plat , lease , or any other record or
memorandum in his or its possession pertaining to
such property , and each officer , board , department ,
association , commission , branch or other persons or
person so using or formerly using property as
herein mentioned shall co -operate with the Attorney
General or any person designated by him in carry-
ing out the purposes of this act , and in disclosing
any property so owned or used of which no record
or memorandum is available.
(b ) Penalty . The officer , individual members
of a commission or board, head of department or
person in charge of any such property shall pay to
the Commonwealth the sum of one ( $ 1 ) dollar per
day as liquidated damages for failure to comply with
· paragraph ( a ) above , such sum to be deducted from
the monthly salary of such person or persons each
month such person or persons so fail to comply
herewith if such person or persons are paid out of
funds belonging to the State , and if not paid out of
funds belonging to the State , such sum may be re-
covered as damages by an action at law against such
person or persons , in any court of Franklin County
having jurisdiction of the amount involved .
9. Within sixty ( 60 ) days after this act be-
comes a law, the Attorney General shall proceed to
examine the title to and make a complete abstract
of any such land or lands which in his opinion
should be examined or abstracted , and he shall or
may employ a competent surveyor or engineer for
the purpose of running the boundaries of all lands
herein mentioned and drawing a map or plat thereof ,
of which there is not already a map or plat made
and in the possession of the officials of the Common-
wealth .
§ 10. The Secretary of State may , within six ( 6 )
months after this act becomes a law, employ one
clerk for the purpose of copying or recording and
filing records herein mentioned , but such clerk shall
not be employed longer than the time necessary to
complete such duties of the Secretary of State con-
cerning property now owned by the State , it being
the intention of this General Assembly to impose
upon the Secretary of State and the Attorney
General in addition to their usual duties now
imposed by law, the additional duties in the future
set (out ) in Sections 1 to 7 hereof.
§ 11. Whereas the State is continually acquiring
property under the existing laws , and whereas more
than a year may be necessary to assemble the
records herein mentioned , and whereas these records
should be collected as herein provided as speedily
as possible , an emergency is declared to exist and
this act shall take effect immediately upon its
passage .
Approved March 22 , 1930 .

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 164 .
AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and mainte-
nance of the various departments , boards , commissions , insti-
tutions , and agencies of the State Government of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky , except for the legislative and judicial
departments , and except for the common schools , for the fiscal
years ending June 30 , 1931 , and June 30 , 1932 , designating the
funds and sources from which said appropriations are to be
paid , and prescribing the manner in which same are to be paid .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. Executive Department . There are hereby
appropriated out of the general expenditure fund
for the Executive Department of the State Govern-
ment , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1931 , the
following sums for the following purposes :
(a- 1 ) For salary of the Governor , private secre-
tary , stenographic help and other employes , and for
printing , stamps , office supplies , extra help and
other operations of the department , the sum of
$16,900.00 .
(b-1 ) For contingent and maintenance fund , the
sum of $6,000.00 .
There are hereby appropriated out of the general
expenditure fund for the Executive Department of
the State Government , for the fiscal year ending
June 30 , 1932 , the following sums for the following
purposes :
(a - 2 ) For salary of the Governor , private secre-
tary , stenographic help and other employees , and
for printing , stamps , office supplies , extra help and
other operations of the department , the sum of
$16,900.00 .
(b-2 ) For contingent and maintenance fund , the
sum of $6,000.00 .
$ 2. Lieutenant Governor . There is hereby ap-
propriated out of the general expenditure fund for
the use and benefit of the Lieutenant Governor , for
the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1931 , for the purpose
of paying clerical hire and other expenses , the sum
of $1,500.00 .
There is hereby appropriated out of the general
expenditure fund for the use and benefit of the
Lieutenant Governor , for the fiscal year ending June
30 , 1932 , for the purpose of paying clerical hire and
other expenses , the sum of $1,500.00 .
§ 3. Secretary of State . There is hereby appro-
priated out of the general expenditure fund for the
use and benefit of the Department of Secretary of
State , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1931 , for
the purpose of paying all salaries , clerical help,
printing , stamps , office supplies , and all other ex-
penses incident to the operation of said department ,
the sum of $21,600.00 .
There is hereby appropriated out of the general
expenditure fund for the use and benefit of the
Department of Secretary of State , for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1932 , for the purpose of paying all
salaries , clerical help , printing , stamps , office sup-
plies, and all other expenses incident to the opera-
tion of said department , the sum of $21,600.00 .
§ 4. Attorney General . There is hereby appro-
priated out of the general expenditure fund for the
use of the Attorney General's Department of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , for the fiscal year
ending June 30, 1931 , the following sums for the
following purposes :
(a- 1 ) For salaries of the Attorney General ,
Assistant Attorneys General , law clerks , and for
stenographic help , the sum of $39,300.00 .
(b- 1 ) For necessary traveling expenses of the
department , when engaged in the State's business ,
printing , stamps , office supplies , furniture and
books , the sum of $5,700.00 .
There are hereby appropriated out of the general
expenditure fund for the use of the Attorney Gen-
eral's Department of the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1932 , the
following sums for the following purposes :
(a- 2 ) For salaries of the Attorney General , As-
sistant Attorneys General , law clerks and for steno-
graphic help , the sum of $39,300.00 .
(b- 2 ) For necessary traveling expenses of the
department , when engaged in the State's business ,
printing , stamps , office supplies , furniture and books ,
the sum of $4,700.00 .
§ 5. Auditor of Public Accounts . There is
hereby appropriated out of the general expenditure
fund for the use of the Department of the Auditor of
Public Accounts of the Commonwealth of Kentucky ,
for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1931 , for salaries ,
clerical hire , printing , stamps , office supplies , and
necessary traveling expenses , the sum of $ 45,700.00 .
There is hereby appropriated out of the general
expenditure fund for the use of the Department of
Auditor of Public Accounts of the Commonwealth of
Kentucky , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1932 ,
for salaries , clerical hire , printing , stamps , office
supplies , and necessary traveling expenses , the sum
of $45,700.00 .
§ 6. State Treasurer . There is hereby appro-
priated out of the general expenditure fund for the
use and benefit of the State Treasurer's Depart-
ment , for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1931 , for the
purpose of paying salaries , clerical help , printing ,
stamps , supplies , and all other expenses incident to
the maintenance and operation of said department ,
the sum of $ 17,000.00 .
There is hereby appropriated out of the general
expenditure fund for the use and benefit of the State
Treasurer's Department , for the fiscal year ending
June 30 , 1932 , for the purpose of paying salaries ,
clerical help , printing , stamps , supplies , and all other
Acts- 18
expenses incident to the maintenance and operation
of said department , the sum of $17,000.00 .
§ 7. Department of Agriculture , Labor and Sta-
tistics . There are hereby appropriated out of the
general expenditure fund for the use of the Depart-
ment of Agriculture , Labor and Statistics , for the
fiscal year ending June . 30 , 1931 , the following
sums for the following purposes :
(a- 1 ) For the purpose of paying all salaries and
clerical hire for said department , $12,500.00 .
(b-1 ) For the purpose of paying per diem , travel-
ing expenses , and other expenses now allowed by
law to the State Board of Agriculture , $4,500.00 .
(c-1 ) For the purpose of paying all the expenses
of the immigration branch (free employment ) of

key_provisions: AN ACT appropriating eighteen thousand ( $18,000.00 ) dollars to the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons , at Frankfort , Kentucky , for the purpose of paying outstanding accounts for services rendered and material bought and furnished to the officers and employees of said Institution for the school year ended June 30 , 1928 , the budget allowed not being sufficient to satisfy said eighteen thousand ( $ 18,000.00 ) dollars . Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky :

§ 1. That there is hereby appropriated to the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored per- sons , at Frankfort , Kentucky , the sum of eighteen thousand ( $ 18,000.00 ) dollars to be paid out of the General Expenditure Fund to satisfy obligations and accounts incurred by the officers and employees of said Institution to maintain it during said school year , this amount being necessary to maintain and operate said Institution in excess of the budget allowed for that school year. 2. Before the Auditor shall allow any account claimed , he shall require of the claimant an itemized statement of the account which shall show the date each item of expense was incurred and the claimant shall be further required to make affidavit in proof of his claim , the form of such affidavit to be prepared and approved by the Attorney General . The Auditor may also require proof of claimant as to the validity of his claim other than his own affidavit if Auditor so desires . No interest on claims shall be allowed . 3. The persons who hold any indebtedness against said Institution are in need of their money and have been compelled to wait for the payment of same with the loss of interest on the claims and , for this reason , an emergency is declared to exist and this act shall become a law upon its passage and approval by the Governor . Neither approved nor disapproved .

laws.full_text:
AN ACT appropriating eighteen thousand ( $18,000.00 ) dollars
to the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons ,
at Frankfort , Kentucky , for the purpose of paying outstanding
accounts for services rendered and material bought and
furnished to the officers and employees of said Institution for
the school year ended June 30 , 1928 , the budget allowed not
being sufficient to satisfy said eighteen thousand ( $ 18,000.00 )
dollars .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That there is hereby appropriated to the
Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored per-
sons , at Frankfort , Kentucky , the sum of eighteen
thousand ( $ 18,000.00 ) dollars to be paid out of the
General Expenditure Fund to satisfy obligations
and accounts incurred by the officers and employees
of said Institution to maintain it during said school
year , this amount being necessary to maintain and
operate said Institution in excess of the budget
allowed for that school year.
2. Before the Auditor shall allow any account
claimed , he shall require of the claimant an itemized
statement of the account which shall show the date
each item of expense was incurred and the claimant
shall be further required to make affidavit in proof
of his claim , the form of such affidavit to be prepared
and approved by the Attorney General . The Auditor
may also require proof of claimant as to the validity
of his claim other than his own affidavit if Auditor
so desires . No interest on claims shall be allowed .
3. The persons who hold any indebtedness
against said Institution are in need of their money
and have been compelled to wait for the payment of
same with the loss of interest on the claims and , for
this reason , an emergency is declared to exist and
this act shall become a law upon its passage and
approval by the Governor .
Neither approved nor disapproved .

GOVERNOR'S MESSAGE
It is my purpose to have the State live within its income .
Section 171 of our Constitution , among other things , provides :
"The General Assembly shall provide by law an annual
tax, which with other resources , shall be sufficient to defray
the estimated expenses of the Commonwealth for each
fiscal year ."
I requested that the General Assembly do this by some
method , but it failed to grant my request or make provision by
an annual tax sufficient to permit the Commonwealth to stay
within its income for the next two fiscal years .
In view of this situation, there is only one course left open
to me for the accomplishment of my desire and the fulfillment
of the law . That course is , the reduction of the expense of the
State by veto of certain appropriations and parts of appropria
tions made to various departments of the Commonwealth in
House Bill 378. Thus , as near as possible , require the Common-
wealth to live within its income , prevent the creation of debt ,
and save the taxpayers of the Commonwealth from further
burdens ..
