( $13,000 ) , and further provides that the said institution shall
receive other benefits in the way of fees , etc.
I hereby veto the appropriation of forty thousand dollars
( $40,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and
June 30 , 1934 , to the extent of ten thousand dollars ( $10,000 ) ,
and approve Section 34 in the sum of thirty thousand dollars
($30,000 ) for each of the two fiscal years aforesaid , and approve
said Section 34 in all of its provisions except as herein indicated .
Section 35 of said House Bill 378 appropriates from the
general fund for the use and benefit of the Kentucky Institution
for the Education of the Blind for the fiscal year ending June
30 , 1933 , and the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1934 , by item a-1
the sum of sixty-five thousand dollars ( $ 65,000.00 ) for each of
said fiscal years , to be used for the payment of salaries and
other expenses incident to the maintenance and operation of
the white department of said institution ; and by item b -1 it
appropriates eight thousand , five hundred dollars ( $ 8,500.00 )
for each of said fiscal years to the colored department of said
institution ; and by item c -1 for educational and vocational
training for the adult blind for each of said fiscal years eighteen
thousand dollars ( $ 18,000.00 ) . For like purposes and to like
departments the appropriations in said bill for the fiscal year
ending June 30, 1934 , are designated as a-2, b-2 and c -2.
I hereby veto items a-1 and a-2 to the extent of ten thousand
dollars ( $ 10,000.00 ) in each item , and approve said items in the
sum of fifty -five thousand ( $55,000.00 ) for the fiscal years end-
ing June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto items b-1 and b-2 of section 35 to the extent
of five hundred dollars ( $500.00 ) of each item , and approve item
b-1 and b -2 in the sum of eight thousand dollars ( $8,000.00 ) for
each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto items c-1 and c -2 of section 35 of said bill
to the extent of one thousand dollars ( $ 1,000.00 ) each , and ap-
prove item c-1 and c- 2 of said bill to the extent of seventeen
thousand dollars ( $17,000.00 ) for each of the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Section 36 of said House Bill 378 makes an appropriation
to the Kentucky School for the Deaf for the two ensuing fiscal
years 1933 and 1934. By items a-1 and a-2 of said section there
is appropriated for the payment of salaries and other expenses
incident to the operation of the white department of said school
the sum of one hundred and nineteen thousand , four hundred
dollars ( $119,400.00 ) .
By items b-1 and b -2 of said section there is appropriated
the sum of six hundred ( $ 600.00 ) dollars for each ensuing fiscal
year for the purpose of educating and developing children born
blind and deaf .
By items c-1 and c-2 there is appropriated for the colored
department of said institution eight thousand dollars ( $8,000.00 )
for each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 ,
1934 .
I hereby veto items a-1 and a -2 of said section to the extent
of fourteen thousand , four hundred dollars ( $ 14,400.00 ) for each
of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and
approve items a-1 and a-2 of section 36 for the sum of one
hundred and five thousand dollars ( $105,000.00 ) for each of
the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby approve items b-1 and b-2 of section 36 for the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , in toto .
I hereby veto items c-1 and c-2 of section 36 of said bill
to the extent of five hundred dollars ( $500 ) for each of the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and ap-
prove said items of said bill in the sum of seven thousand , five
hundred dollars ( $7,500 ) for each of said fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Section 37 of said House Bill 378 makes appropriation to
the Kentucky Crippled Children Commission for the two fiscal
years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , for the purposes
as shown by said bill in the sum of one hundred and forty
thousand dollars ( $140,000 ) for each of the two fiscal years
ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto said appropriation for each of said fiscal
years to the extent of thirty thousand dollars ( $30,000 ) and
approve said section . in the sum of one hundred and ten thousand
dollars ( $ 110,000 ) for each of said fiscal years ending June 30 ,
1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Section 38 of House Bill 378 makes certain appropriations
to the Kentucky Park Commission for the purpose of maintain-
ing and improving the State parks set out in said section 38
the sum of twenty thousand dollars ( $20,000 ) for the fiscal
years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and in addition
thereto sets apart for each of the two fiscal years the fees and
income received from the various State parks named therein .
I hereby veto Section 38 to the extent of ten thousand dol-
lars ( $ 10,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 ,
and June 30 , 1934 , and approve said section in the sum of ten
thousand dollars ( $10,000 ) ' for each of said fiscal years , and
further approve Section 38 to the extent of appropriations of
fees and income received from the various State parks therein
mentioned .
Section 38 % of House Bill 378 makes an appropriation of
the income and fees from the Jefferson Davis Memorial to the
board of trustees thereof and provides for the manner of pay-
ment .
I hereby approve said section 38½ in toto .
Section 39 of House Bill 378 appropriates for the use and
benefit of the State Purchasing Commission , including salaries
and traveling expenses of its members , etc., the sum of nine
thousand dollars ( $9,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto said appropriation for said two fiscal years
1933 and 1934 to the extent of one thousand dollars ( $ 1,000 )
and approve said appropriation in the sum of eight thousand
dollars ( $ 8,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending June 30 ,
1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Section 40 of House Bill 378 appropriates to the Vocational
Education Board from the general expenditure fund for the use
and benefit thereof for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 ,
and June 30 , 1934 , by items a-1 and a-2 for each of said fiscal
years the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ( $25,000.00 ) .
I hereby approve said appropriation in said sum for the fiscal
years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Said section also by items b-1 and b-2 appropriates to said
department the sum of twenty -one thousand dollars ( $21,000.00 )
for each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 ,
1934 .
I hereby veto items b- 1 and b-2 of said section 40 to the
extent of one thousand dollars ( $1,000.00 ) for each of said fiscal
years and approve same in the sum of twenty thousand dollars
( $20,000.00 ) for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June
30 , 1934 .
Section 41 of said House Bill 378 is an appropriation to the
Department of Public Welfare . Items a -1 and a-2 of section 41
appropriates the sum of one million , three hundred thousand
dollars ( $1,300,000.00 ) for each of the fiscal years ending June
"
30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , to be used for the purpose of paying
salaries , clerical hire , traveling expenses , printing , stamps ,
necessary supplies , cost of operation , maintenance and improve-
ments , repairs , and operating expenses for the State Reforma-
tory, State Penitentiary , Western State Hospital , Central State
Hospital , Eastern State Hospital , Feeble Minded Institute , and
the Houses of Reform .
I hereby veto said appropriation to the extent of one hun-
dred thousand dollars ( $100,000.00 ) for the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and approve said appropriation
in the sum of one million , two hundred thousand dollars ( $1,-
200,000.00 ) for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June
1934 .30,
I hereby approve items b-1 and b-2 of said section of said
bill in toto .
Section 42 of House Bill 378 makes an appropriation to the
Morehead State Teachers College in the sum of two hundred
and sixty -five thousand dollars ( $265,000.00 ) , and in addition
the fees and other operating receipts of the institution , for the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , for the
various purposes set out in said section 42 of said bill .
I hereby veto said section to the extent of the appropriation
of two hundred and sixty-five thousand dollars ( $265,000.00 ) for
the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
At the time the aforesaid appropriation was made it was
supposed that House Bill 654 would remain a law . However, I
was forced to veto House Bill 654. Having done so , provision
is made for the Morehead State Teachers College by the provi-
sions of Chapter 152 , Acts of 1930 , and thereunder it obtains its
funds on a percentage basis .
I hereby approve so much of Section 42 as appropriates to
said college the fees and other operating receipts , and the
requirements of said bill as to the handling of said receipts
and fees .
Section 43 of House Bill 378 appropriates to the Murray
State Teachers College from the general fund for the fiscal
year ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , for the purposes
as set out in said section 43 of said bill the sum of two hundred
and sixty-five thousand dollars ( $265,000.00 ) , and in addition to
said amount the fees and other operating receipts of the
institution .
I hereby veto so much of said bill as appropriates to said
college the sum of two hundred and sixty-five thousand dollars
( $265,000.00 ) for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and
June 30 , 1934 .
At the time the aforesaid appropriation was made it was
supposed that House Bill 654 would remain a law . However ,
I was forced to veto House Bill 654. Having done so , provision
is made for the Murray State Teachers College by the provisions
of Chapter 152 , Acts of 1930 , and thereunder it obtains its funds
on a percentage basis .
I hereby approve so much of section 43 as appropriates to
said college the fees and other operating receipts , and the
requirements of said bill as to the handling of said receipts and
fees .
Item b-1 of section 43 of said bill makes an appropriation to
said Murray State Teachers College for the fiscal year ending
June 30 , 1933 , for the purpose of paying a deficit in the sum of
one hundred and thirty thousand dollars ( $130,000.00 ) .
I hereby approve said appropriation for said fiscal year, 1933 .
Section 44 of House Bill 378 appropriates to the Western
State Teachers College the sum of four hundred and forty -five
thousand dollars ( $445,000.00 ) for the fiscal years ending June
30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and in addition thereto the fees and
operating receipts of the institution .
I hereby veto said appropriation to the Western Kentucky
State Teachers College for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 ,
and June 30 , 1934 , to the extent of four hundred and forty-five
thousand dollars ( $445,000.00 ) .
At the time the aforesaid appropriation was made it was
supposed that House Bill 654 would remain a law . However,
I was forced to veto House Bill 654. Having done so , provision
is made for the Western Kentucky State Teachers College by
the provisions of Chapter 152 , Acts of 1930 , and thereunder it
cbtains funds on a percentage basis .
I hereby approve so much of section 44 as appropriates to
said college the fees and other operating receipts , and the re-
quirements of said bill as to the handling of said receipts and
fees .
Section 45 of House Bill 378 appropriates to the Eastern
Kentucky State Teachers College the sum of three hundred and
twenty -five thousand dollars ( $325,000.00 ) for the fiscal years
ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and in addition the
fees and other operating receipts of the institution for said two
fiscal years .
I hereby veto said appropriation in the sum of three hundred
and twenty-five thousand dollars ( $325,000.00 ) for the fiscal years
ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
At the time the aforesaid appropriation was made it was
supposed that House Bill 654 would remain a law . However , I
was forced to veto House Bill 654. Having done so , provision
is made for the Eastern Kentucky State Teachers College by
the provisions of Chapter 152 of Acts of 1930 , and thereunder it
obtains its funds on a percentage basis .
I hereby approve so much of section 45 as appropriates to
said college the fees and other operating receipts , and the re-
quirements of said bill as to the handling of said receipts and
fees .
Section 46 of House Bill 378 appropriates to the University
of Kentucky by items a-1 and a-2 for the purposes therein set
out, the sum of nine hundred and seventy thousand dollars
( $970,000.00 ) for each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 ,
and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto said appropriation to the extent of nine hun-
dred and seventy thousand dollars ( $970,000.00 ) for the fiscal
years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
At the time the aforesaid appropriation was made it was
supposed that House Bill 654 would remain a law . However, I
was forced to veto House Bill 654. Having done so , provision is
made for the University of Kentucky by the provisions of Chap-
ter 152 , Acts of 1930 , and thereunder it obtains its funds on a
percentage basis .
By items b-1 and b-2 there is appropriated to said college
for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , for
agricultural instruction the sum of twenty-five thousand , five
hundred dollars ( $25,500.00 ) .
I hereby approve said items b-1 and b-2 for the fiscal years
ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Items c-1 and c -2 of section 46 appropriate for the two fiscal
years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , the sum of ten
thousand dollars ( $ 10,000.00 ) for the purposes of paying salaries
and expenses and maintaining a summer school .
I hereby veto items c-1 and c-2 of section 46 of said bill in
toto .
Item d-1 of section 46 appropriates seventeen thousand dol-
lars ( $17,000.00 ) for equipment of library stacks for the fiscal
year ending June 30 , 1933 .
I hereby veto said item d -1 to the extent of two thousand
dollars ( $2,000.00 ) and approve same in the sum of fifteen thou-
sand dollars ( $15,000.00 ) for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1933 .
Items e-1 and d -2 of section 46 of said bill appropriate to
the experimental station of the University of Kentucky for the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , the sum of
fifty thousand dollars ( $50,000.00 ) for each fiscal year .
Items e-2 and f-1 of said section 46 of said House Bill 378
appropriate for the maintenance of public service laboratories ,
etc. , the sum of twenty-two thousand dollars ( $22,000.00 ) for
each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby approve items e- 1, d-2, e-2 , and f-1 for each of the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Items g-1 and f-2 of section 46 of House Bill 378 appropriate
to the Princeton Experimental Station for the fiscal years end-
ing June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , the sum of twenty-five
thousand dollars ( $25,000.00 ) ; and items h-1 and g-2 of section
46 of said bill appropriate to the Quicksand Experiment Station
for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , the
sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ( $ 25,000.00 ) .
I hereby veto each of said appropriations to the extent of
ten thousand dollars ( $10,000.00 ) each for the fiscal years end-
ing June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and approve said appropria-
tions for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 ,
in the sum of fifteen thousand dollars ( $15,000.00 ) each .
Item i-1 of section 46 of said House Bill 378 appropriates the
sum of fourteen thousand dollars ( $ 14,000.00 ) for the purpose
of constructing an abattoir at the University of Kentucky .
I hereby veto said appropriation as contained in item 1-1
of section 46 of said bill in toto .
Items j -1 and h-2 of section 46 of said House Bill 378 ap-
propriate for the purpose of agricultural extension work the sum
of one hundred and seventy -nine thousand , five hundred and
thirty -one dollars ( $179,531.00 ) for the two fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto said appropriation for said two fiscal years
to the extent of fifty -nine thousand , five hundred and thirty -one
dollars ( $59,531.00 ) for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 ,
and June 30 , 1934 ; and approve said appropriation in the sum
of one hundred and twenty thousand dollars ( $120,000.00 ) for
said purposes for each of said fiscal years .
Items k-1 and 1-2 of section 46 of said House Bill 378 ap-
propriate to the University of Kentucky fees , rentals , etc. , and
place about such collections certain restrictions and require-
ments .
I hereby approve said items k-1 and i -2 of said bill for the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Items e-1½ and d-2 % of section 46 of said House Bill 378
appropriate two thousand , five hundred dollars ( $2,500.00 ) for
each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 ,
to be used for the purpose of quarantining diseased plants and
inspecting nurseries .
I hereby veto said appropriation .
I hereby approve sections 47 , 48 , 49 , 50 , 51 , 52 and 53 of
House Bill 378 .
I hereby approve sections 54 , 55 , 56 , 57 , 58 , 59 , and 60 of
House Bill 378 , for the two fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 ,
and June 30 , 1934 .
Section 61 of House Bill 378 appropriates for the fiscal years
ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , for the use and benefit
of the county tax commission , the sum of three hundred fifty
thousand dollars for each of said years .
I hereby veto said section to the extent of twenty -five thou-
sand dollars for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June
30 , 1934 , and approve same in the sum of three hundred , twen-
ty-five thousand dollars ( $325,000 ) for each of said fiscal years .
I hereby approve sections 62, 63 , 64 , 65 , 66 , 67 , 68 , 69, 70 , 71
and 72 of House Bill 378 .
Section 73 of House Bill 378 appropriates for the purposes
of paying Jefferson county fees , the sum of two hundred fifty
thousand dollars ( $ 250,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto said appropriation to the extent of fifty thou-
sand dollars ( $50,000 ) for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 ,
and June 30 , 1934 , and approve said appropriation in the sum
of two hundred thousand dollars ( $200,000 ) for the fiscal years
ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby approve sections 74 and 75 of House Bill 378 .
Section 76 of House Bill 378 appropriates from the General
Expenditure Fund for the benefit of legislative sessions for the
fiscal year ending June 30 , 1933 , the sum of five thousand dollars ,
and for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1934 , the sum of one
hundred seventy thousand dollars ( $ 170,000 ) .
I hereby veto section 76 of said bill whereby it undertakes
to appropriate five thousand dollars ( $5,000 ) for the purpose of
legislative sessions for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1933 , and
approve said section as to the appropriation of one hundred
seventy thousand dollars ( $ 170,000 ) for the benefit of the legis-
lative session for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby approve section 77 of House Bill 378 .
Section 78 of House Bill 378 appropriates the sum of two
thousand dollars ( $2,000 ) for each of the two fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , to be used as rewards .
I hereby veto said section of said bill in toto .
Section 79 of House Bill 378 appropriates for the two fiscal
years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , for the use and
benefit of the Board of Supervisors , the sum of twenty-nine
thousand dollars ( $29,000 ) for each of said two fiscal years .
I hereby veto Section 79 of said bill to the extent of four
thousand dollars ( $4,000 ) , for each of said two fiscal years end
ing June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and approve said Section
79 in the sum of Twenty -five thousand dollars ( $25,000 ) for the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby approve Sections 80 and 81 of House Bill 378 .
Section 82 of House Bill 378 appropriates the sum of ten
thousand dollars ( $ 10,000 ) for the fiscal years ending June 30 ,
1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , for the purposes of refunds to sheriffs
for exonerations allowed .
I hereby veto Section 82 of House Bill 378 making an ap-
propriation for refunds to sheriffs for exonerations allowed .
Section 83 of House Bill 378 makes an appropriation for
refunds to sheriffs , money advanced by them to trustees of the
jury fund for the purposes of paying circuit court jurors , the
sum of twenty -seven thousand dollars ( $27,000 ) for the fiscal
year's ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto said section to the extent of seven thousand
dollars ( $ 7,000 ) for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and
June 30 , 1934 , and approve said section in the sum of twenty
thousand dollars ( $20,000 ) for the fiscal years ending June 30,
1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Section 84 of House Bill 378 appropriates out of the sinking
fund for the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 ,
ten thousand , two hundred dollars ( $ 10,200 ) for each of said
fiscal years .
I hereby veto said Section 84 of House Bill 378 in toto .
Section 85 of House Bill 378 appropriates out of the General
Expenditure fund for the use and benefit of Supervisors of
Chiropracters for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1933 , and for
the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1934 , the sum of four thousand
dollars ( $4,000 ) for each of said fiscal years .
I hereby approve Section 85 of said bill .
Section 86 of House Bill 378 appropriates for the use and
benefit of the trustees of the jury fund the sum of five hundred
thousand dollars ( $500,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto said appropriation to the extent of fifty
thousand dollars ( $50,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and approve said Section 86 of
said bill in the sum of four hundred fifty thousand dollars
($450,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and
June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby approve Sections 87 and 88 of House Bill 378 .
Section 89 of House Bill 378 appropriates for each of the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , the sum of
two thousand eight hundred dollars ( $2,800 ) for the use and
benefit of the Board of Bar Examiners .
I hereby veto said section 89 of said bill for each of the two
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , to the
extent of eight hundred dollars ( $ 800 ) and approve said section
89 in the sum of two thousand dollars ( $2,000 ) for each of the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby approve Sections 90 and 91 of House Bill 378 .
Section 92 of House Bill 378 appropriates the sum of five
million , five hundred fifty thousand dollars ( $5,550,000 ) for each
of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , to the
school fund .
I was forced to veto House Bill 654 , and having done so,
the school fund will obtain its percentage under Chapter 152 ,
Acts 1930 .
I, therefore , veto Section 92 of House Bill 378 in toto .
I hereby approve sections 93 , 94 , 95 , and 96 of House Bill 378 .
Section 97 of House Bill 378 appropriates from the general
expenditure fund of the State for each of the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , the sum of ten thousand dollars
( $10,000 ) for paying for diseased live stock condemned and
destroyed by order of the Live Stock Sanitary Board .
I hereby veto said section 97 of House Bill 378 to the extent
.of five thousand dollars ( $5,000 ) for each of the fiscal years end-
ing June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and approve said Section
97 of said House Bill 378 in the sum of five thousand dollars
($5,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and
June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby approve Section 98 of House Bill 378 .
Section 99 of House Bill 378 appropriates from the General
Expenditure fund to My Old Kentucky Home Commission the
sum of two thousand dollars ( $2,000 ) for each of the fiscal years
ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and also appropriates
thereto receipts and fees received by said commission during
the two mentioned fiscal years ,
I hereby veto Section 99 of House Bill 378 to the extent of
the appropriation of $2,000 for each of the fiscal years , and
approve the remainder of said section .
Section 100 of House Bill 378 appropriates from the General
Expenditure fund for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1933 , the
sum of five hundred thousand dollars ( $500,000 ) and for the
fiscal year ending June 30 , 1934 , the sum of one million , two
hundred fifty thousand dollars ( $ 1,250,000 ) for the use and bene-
fit of the Equalization School Fund of the Commonwealth of
Kentucky .
I hereby veto the appropriation so made for the fiscal year
ending June 30 , 1933 , to the extent of three hundred fifty
thousand dollars ( $ 350,000 ) and approve same for the said fiscal
year in the sum of one hundred fifty thousand dollars ($150,000 ) .
I hereby veto the appropriation of one million , two hundred
fifty thousand dollars ( $1,250,000 ) for the fiscal year ending June
30 , 1934 , to the extent of one million , fifty thousand dollars
( $1,050,000 ) and approve of said appropriation for the fiscal
year ending June 30 , 1934 , in the sum of two hundred thousand
dollars ( $200,000 ) .
Section 101 of House Bill 378 appropriates for each of the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , the sum of
two hundred fifty thousand dollars ( $250,000 ) known as an
emergency fund .
I hereby veto said appropriation for each of the two fiscal
years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , to the extent of
two hundred thousand dollars ( $200,000 ) for each of said fiscal
years , and approve of said appropriation in the sum of fifty
thousand dollars ( $50,000 ) for each of the two fiscal years end-
ing June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby approve Sections 102 , 103 and 104 of House Bill 378 .
Section 105 of House Bill 378 appropriates to the Armory
Commission , for certain purposes , the sum of fifty thousand
dollars ( $50,000 ) for each of the two fiscal years ending June
30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
I hereby veto said appropriation to the extent of five
thousand dollars ( $5,000 ) for each of the two said fiscal years ,
and approve of said appropriation to the extent of forty -five
thousand dollars ( $45,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Section 105 % of House Bill 378 appropriates from the Gen-
eral Expenditure Fund for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1933 ,
the sum of ten thousand dollars ( $ 10,000 ) for the purpose of
carrying out the provisions of Senate Resolution No. 24 , of the
General Assembly of 1932 , providing for a commission to suggest
amendments to the Constitution .
I hereby veto said Section 105½ of House Bill 378 in toto .
Section 106 of House Bill 378 appropriates for the use and
benefit of the Kentucky Progress Commission , the purposes
therein set out , for each of the fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 ,
and June 30 , 1934 , the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars
($25,000 ) .
I hereby veto said appropriation to the extent of fifteen
thousand dollars ( $15,000 ) for each of the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and approve said appropriation
in the sum of ten thousand dollars ( $10,000 ) for each of the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Section 107 of House Bill 378 appropriates from the general
expenditure fund for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1933 , the
sum of four hundred , eighty -one thousand dollars ( $481,000 ) to
be used by the State Board of Charities and Corrections for
the purposes of paying off a deficit created by said department
during the fiscal years 1931 and 1932 .
I hereby veto said section 107 of House Bill 378 , to the
extent of eighty -one thousand dollars ( $81,000 ) and approve
said appropriation for the said fiscal year in the sum of four
hundred thousand dollars ( $400,000 ) .
I hereby approve Sections 108 and 109 of House Bill 378 .
Section 111 of House Bill 378 appropriates from the General
Expenditure Fund for each of the Fiscal years ending June 30 ,
1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , the sum of thirteen thousand , five hun-
dred dollars ( $ 13,500 ) to the Kentucky Children's Bureau , for
the purposes set out in said section .
I hereby veto said section to the extent of three thousand ,
five hundred dollars ( $3,500 ) for each of the fiscal years ending
June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 , and approve said appropriation
in the sum of ten thousand dollars ( $10,000 ) for each of the
fiscal years ending June 30 , 1933 , and June 30 , 1934 .
Given under my hand , this 28th day of March , 1932 .
(Signed ) RUBY LAFFOON ,
Governor of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky .
laws.title_raw: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and mainte- nance of the various departments , boards , commissions , insti- tutions , and agencies of the State Government of the Com- monwealth of Kentucky for the fiscal years ending June thirty , nineteen hundred thirty -three , and June thirty , nine- teen hundred thirty -four, designating the funds and sources from which said appropriations are to be paid , and prescrib- ing the manner in which same are to be paid , and repealing all annual blanket and or continuing appropriations not pro- vided for in this Act , and all laws or parts of laws in con- flict with any provision thereof.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, p. 456
laws.summary: This statute outlines the requirements for voter registration in Kentucky, including the collection of personal information such as name, address, color or race, sex, physical characteristics, party affiliation, occupation, birthplace, age, length of residency, naturalization status, and other means of identification. It also details procedures for voters who are unable to write their names, requiring them to make a mark attested by the clerk after an investigation and oath.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, ch. 94, pp. 496–500
laws.summary: This act amends existing legislation concerning free public libraries in cities and towns of certain classes. It introduces provisions for establishing free public libraries, their support, and crucially, mandates separate funds and separate libraries for the white race and the Negro race. It also outlines the taxation of separate property of the two races and the division of funds derived from such taxation.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 94 . AN ACT to amend chapter 146 of an Act of the General Assem- bly passed at its 1920 session entitled " An Act relating to free public libraries in cities and towns of the third , fourth , fifth and sixth classes of this Commonwealth ", the same being sections 2741d -1 to and including 2741d -5 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes , Official edition 1930 ; by adding thereto sections pro- viding that certain libraries in said cities and towns shall be free public libraries , how they may become such , for their support , for separate funds , separate libraries for the white race and for the Negro race , for taxing separate property of the two races and the division of funds , for issuing warrants on claims , for appointment of the first board of trustees and defining the construction to be applied to this amendment . Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky :

§ 1. In cities and towns of the classes named herein in which there is no free public library , but in which a library building which cost at least ten thousand dollars ( $ 10,000,00 ) in cities of the third , fourth and fifth classes , or at least five thousand dol- lars ( $ 5,000.00 ) in towns of the sixth class , and is reasonably of that value , has been or hereafter may be erected , and fully paid for by voluntary dona- tions made by citizens and business organizations of said city or town and the vicinity thereof, not including in any one donation any amount over two per cent of the whole sum contributed , on a lot in said city or town , the fee - simple title to which is in a library association or corporation or trustees for library purposes , and which lot is fully paid for and free from incumbrance , and which library building and lot with the emoluments thereof are devoted wholly to library purposes , and into which library building and library , all citizens of said city or town , or all white citzens thereof , or all colored citizens thereof, as the case may be , have , and shall continue to have , free and equal rights of admitttance into said library building and free and equal rights and privileges to the use of the library as named and provided for in this Act, shall be entitled to and shall have all of the aid , benefits , and applications of the terms and provisions herein , and in said chapter 146 ; provided , however , the two -tenths of one mill on each

§ 2. If a library building herein provided for has been or hereafter shall be erected from volun- tary donations as herein named , for the separate and exclusive use of each of said races in such city or town and a library is or shall be maintained therein according to the provisions of this amend- ment for each separate race , the revenue derived from the one-half of all fines , forfeitures , and costs from the police court, appropriated in section 5 of said chapter 146 shall , when paid to the treasurer of the city or town, be credited to the library fund of said separate library organizations , respectively , in the proportion per capita as the total number of citizens of such city or town belonging to each of the respective races bears to the total population of the city or town as shown by the last preceding census made by the official authorities of the said city or town . The revenues derived from the ad valorum tax against property belonging to the respective races shall be credited to the library fund for which the levy was made , giving to each the amount col- lected on property of each race , respectively , viz .: credit to the library fund for the white race the revenue received from property of the white race and credit to the library fund for the Negro race the revenue received from property of the Negro race . Amounts received from ad valorum taxes on all property and any and all other taxes received for library purposes , shall be apportioned to the said libra

§ 3. If in any of said cities or towns only one of the library buildings named and provided for in section 1 hereof has been or heerafter may be erected and a library installed therein for the sep- arate and exclusive use of only one of the said races of said city or town , such free public library shall receive the full amount of the fines , forfeitures and costs appropriated in section 5 of said chapter 146 , and the full amount of taxes levied for library pur- poses on all the other property of said city or town subject to taxation for school purposes , except there shall be no tax levied on any property of the race who do not have free access to the said building and library.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 94 .
AN ACT to amend chapter 146 of an Act of the General Assem-
bly passed at its 1920 session entitled " An Act relating to
free public libraries in cities and towns of the third , fourth ,
fifth and sixth classes of this Commonwealth ", the same being
sections 2741d -1 to and including 2741d -5 of Carroll's Kentucky
Statutes , Official edition 1930 ; by adding thereto sections pro-
viding that certain libraries in said cities and towns shall be
free public libraries , how they may become such , for their
support , for separate funds , separate libraries for the white
race and for the Negro race , for taxing separate property of
the two races and the division of funds , for issuing warrants
on claims , for appointment of the first board of trustees and
defining the construction to be applied to this amendment .
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. In cities and towns of the classes named
herein in which there is no free public library , but
in which a library building which cost at least ten
thousand dollars ( $ 10,000,00 ) in cities of the third ,
fourth and fifth classes , or at least five thousand dol-
lars ( $ 5,000.00 ) in towns of the sixth class , and is
reasonably of that value , has been or hereafter may
be erected , and fully paid for by voluntary dona-
tions made by citizens and business organizations
of said city or town and the vicinity thereof, not
including in any one donation any amount over two
per cent of the whole sum contributed , on a lot in
said city or town , the fee - simple title to which is in
a library association or corporation or trustees for
library purposes , and which lot is fully paid for and
free from incumbrance , and which library building
and lot with the emoluments thereof are devoted
wholly to library purposes , and into which library
building and library , all citizens of said city or town ,
or all white citzens thereof , or all colored citizens
thereof, as the case may be , have , and shall continue
to have , free and equal rights of admitttance into
said library building and free and equal rights and
privileges to the use of the library as named and
provided for in this Act, shall be entitled to and
shall have all of the aid , benefits , and applications
of the terms and provisions herein , and in said
chapter 146 ; provided , however , the two -tenths of
one mill on each one dollar ( $ 1.00 ) named in sec-
tion 1 of said chapter 146 as the least popular sub-
scription required , and the one mill on each one
dollar ( $ 1.00 ) named in said section and in section 3
thereof as the maximum limit of the tax levy author-
ized therein shall, for all separate class libraries
provided for in this section , be based or levied upon
each one -dollar ( $ 1.00 ) of all property which is sub-
ject to taxation for other municipal purposes in such
city or town owned by all persons of the race or
races , respectively , to whom is given free access to
said library building and library ; provided , the min-
.
imum valuation of the library building erected or
that may be hereafter erected by voluntary dona-
tions , as herein provided , for the exclusive use of
the class or race known as the Negro or colored race ,
shall be four thousand dollars in cities of the third ,
fourth and fifth classes and two thousand ($2,000.00 )
in towns of the sixth class .
§ 2. If a library building herein provided for
has been or hereafter shall be erected from volun-
tary donations as herein named , for the separate
and exclusive use of each of said races in such city
or town and a library is or shall be maintained
therein according to the provisions of this amend-
ment for each separate race , the revenue derived
from the one-half of all fines , forfeitures , and costs
from the police court, appropriated in section 5 of
said chapter 146 shall , when paid to the treasurer of
the city or town, be credited to the library fund of
said separate library organizations , respectively , in
the proportion per capita as the total number of
citizens of such city or town belonging to each of the
respective races bears to the total population of the
city or town as shown by the last preceding census
made by the official authorities of the said city or
town . The revenues derived from the ad valorum
tax against property belonging to the respective
races shall be credited to the library fund for which
the levy was made , giving to each the amount col-
lected on property of each race , respectively , viz .:
credit to the library fund for the white race the
revenue received from property of the white race
and credit to the library fund for the Negro race the
revenue received from property of the Negro race .
Amounts received from ad valorum taxes on all
property and any and all other taxes received for
library purposes , shall be apportioned to the said
library funds in the way and manner that is now or
hereafter may be , provided by law for common or
graded school purposes .
§ 3. If in any of said cities or towns only one of
the library buildings named and provided for in
section 1 hereof has been or heerafter may be
erected and a library installed therein for the sep-
arate and exclusive use of only one of the said races
of said city or town , such free public library shall
receive the full amount of the fines , forfeitures and
costs appropriated in section 5 of said chapter 146 ,
and the full amount of taxes levied for library pur-
poses on all the other property of said city or town
subject to taxation for school purposes , except there
shall be no tax levied on any property of the race
who do not have free access to the said building and
library.
§ 4. Members of the first board of any public
library herein provided for shall be appointed imme-
diately after the tax is levied or subscriptions have
been made and approved by the mayor or chief exec-
utive-one for one year , one for two years , one
for three years and two for four years ; thereafter
the term of office shall be for four years and until
their successors are appointed and qualified .
$ 5. Each warrant issued on claims allowed for
such public libary shall specify the proper library
fund out of which it is payable if there are more
than one library fund .
§ 6. The trustees and managing authorities of
any library which they desire shall become a free
public library herein authorized or a majority of
the members of each thereof may file their petition
with the common council or governing authority of
such city or town or county requesting that such
library property be declared a free public library
as provided for in said chapter 146 ; but no such
library property shall be in any way affected by
this law until such petition is so filed .
The petition shall state the facts and conditions
existing as required herein to become a free public
library and shall be sworn to by one of the petition-
ers . The council or governing authority may require
additional proof of the statements in the petition .
An appeal may be taken from the decision of the
council or governing authorities by any of the peti-
tioners or any taxpayer of said city or town to the
Circuit Court of the county .
§ 7. The provisions of this act shall not in any
way apply to any free public library heretofore or
hereafter organized under said chapter 146 , except
those libraries named in section 1 of this amend-
ment which shall hereafter be organized ; but all
provisions of said chapter 146, not inconsistent with
this amendment , shall apply to all libraries named
in section 1 of this amendment .
§ 8. If any portion of any provision of this act
shall be adjudged to be unconstitutional such judg-
ment shall not affect any other portion and the re-
mainder of the act shall continue in force and effect .
If the provision in section 3 hereof for the use of
fines , forfeitures and costs in the police court shall
be adjudged to be unconstitutional , the library
therein named shall receive its proportional part of
said fines , forefeitures and costs as provided for in
section 2 hereof .
Neither approved nor disapproved .

laws.summary: This act designates a specific road as part of the primary system of State highways. The route is described as beginning on Federal Highway Number sixty-two, near the Mollie Pettit farm in Caldwell County, extending by the Silver Star School House to the Emerson Place, identified as 'colored', and then intersecting the Cadiz road near Jim Tandy's place.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 343 . ----3 AN ACT to establish as part of the State primary road systemi a road to be known as project Number beginning on Federal Highway Number sixty-two , at or near the farm known as the Mollie Petit farm in Caldwell County , Kentucky , extending thence by Silver Star School House to what is known as the Emerson Place , colored , thence intersecting the Cadiz road near Jim Tandy's place . Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky :

§ 1. That the road beginning on Federal High- way Number sixty -two , at or near the farm known as the Mollie Pettit farm in Caldwell County extend- ing thence by Silver Star School House to what is known as the Emerson Place , colored , then inter- secting the Cadiz road near Jim Tandy's place be and the same is hereby designated and established as part of the primary system of State Highways of the Commonwealth of Kentucky ; to be known as the State Primary Road Project Number 2. The construction , maintenance , supervision and control of the said road shall be subject to all the terms and conditions as set out and provided for in Chapter seventeen , Acts of the General Assembly of one thousand nine hundred and twenty , establishing and creating a primary system of State Highways , Neither approved nor disapproved .

ARTICLE I.
General Provisions
1. Uniform system of common schools .-There
shall be maintained throughout the Commonwealth
of Kentucky a uniform system of common schools
in accordance with the Constitution of the Common-
wealth and the school laws .
2. Common school defined ; who may attend .-A
common school " shall be interpreted as meaning
an elementary and/or secondary school of the Com-
monwealth supported in whole or in part by public
taxation . No school shall be deemed a "common
school " as defined in this act or receive support
from public taxation unless such school be taught
by a qualified teacher or teachers for a term of
seven or more months during the school year and
at which every child residing in the district , be-
tween the ages of six and eighteen years, has had
the privilege of attending , whether contributing
towards defraying the expense or not ; providing
that nothing herein shall prevent any person over
eighteen years of age from attending the common
schools of the district in which he resides , and that
said person shall not be required to contribute
towards defraying the expenses or pay tuition fees ;
provided further that a board of education may, in
its discretion , make a reasonable tuition charge of
those persons who have completed a course of study
or curriculum of the highest level in the school or
schools maintained by the board .
3. School year .-The school year shall begin on
the first day of July and end on the thirtieth day
of June.
4. Six-year old child may enter school .-Any
child who is six years of age or who will become

fers from the school of one district to the school
of another district until after the pupil has demon-

grade or course to which he has been promoted .
6. School month and school day defined .— Twen-
ty school days , or days in which teachers are actu-
ally employed in the schoolroom , shall constitute a
school month in the common schools of the Com--
monwealth , including such legal holidays as the
State Board of Education may declare to be ob-
served ; but no teacher shall teach on Saturdays
except in cases of emergencies and then only upon
authorization of the State Board of Education . Six
bours af actual school work shall constitute a school
day ; and under no circumstances shall the daily ses-
sion , including recesses and intermissions , exceed
nine hours in length .
7. Bible to be read .--The teacher in charge shall
read or cause to be read a portion of the Bible daily
in every classroom or session room of the common
schools of the Commonwealth in the presence of
pupils therein assembled , and no child shall be re-
quired to read the Bible against the wish of his
parents or guardian . The failure to ( of ) any teach-
er to conform to this act shall be cause for revoca-
tion of his certificate in the manner provided by
law .
8. White and colored not to be taught in same
school ; penalty.—It shall be unlawful for any per-
son , corporation , or association of persons to main-
tain or operate any college , school , or institution
where persons of white and negro races are both
received as pupils for instruction ; and any person
or corporation who shall operate or maintain any
such college , school , or institution shall be fined one
thousand dollars ( $1,000 ) and any person or cor-
poration who may be convicted of violating the pro-
visions of this act shall be fined one hundred dol-
lars ( $100 ) for each day they may operate such
school, college , or institution after such conviction .
Any instructor who shall teach in any school , col-
lege , or institution where members of said two
races are received as pupils for instruction shall
be guilty of operating and maintaining same and
fined as herein provided .
It shall be unlawful for any white person to at-
tend any school or institution where negroes are
received as pupils or receive instruction , and it shall
be unlawful for any negro or colored person to at-
tend any school or institution where white persons
are received as pupils or receive instruction . Any
person so offending shall be fined fifty dollars ( $ 50 )
foreach day he attends such an institution

10. Gift , donation , or devise to school fund.—
The State Board of Education is authorized to ac-
cept any gift , donation , or devise to the schools
under its supervision or control and to provide for
the adminsitration of such gift , donation , or devise .
11. Sectarian , infidel, or immoral books prohib-
ited . No books or other publications of a sectarian,
infidel , or immoral character shall be used or dis-
tributed in any common school of the Common-
wealth , nor shall any textbook or other publication
be used which reflects on any religious denomina-
tion, nor shall any sectarian , infidel , or immoral
doctrine be taught in any school .
12. Free textbooks and necessary school sup-
plies may be provided by boards of education in any
school district . The board of education of any
school district shall have the power and the right
to furnish textbooks and other necessary school sup-
plies free of charge to indigent children in its school
district or to such other children as it deems advis-
able and under such rules and regulations as it may
adopt.

When the boards of two or more contiguous school

shall be appointed at least one attendance officer or

attendance officers in such united districts shall be

Attendance officers and assistant attendance of-

its attendance officer and assistant attendance of-
ficers incurred in its district .
Controversies arising in attendance districts re-
lating to attendance matters should be submitted
to the State Board of Education for settlement , and
in case an agreement suitable to all parties cannot
be reached the State Board may dissolve the united
attendance district . In case of such dissolution ,
each school district involved may unite with other
contiguous school districts in forming a united at-
tendance district or set up its own attendance sys-
tem in accordance with the provisions of this act .
The provisions of this act relating to attendance
officers shall become effective July 1 , 1934 .
7. Office to be provided .-The office of the sup-
erintendent of schools shall be deemed the office of
the attendance offcer and suitable space shall be
provided therein or adjacent thereto for him.
8. Records and reports .- The attendance officer
shall beep such records and make such reports as
are required by law , by regulation of the State
Board of Education , by the state attendance officer ,
and by his superintendent and board of education ."
9. Duties of attendance officer . The general
duties of the attendance officer shall be (a ) to en-
force the compulsory attendance and census laws in
the attendance district which he serves ; (b) to ac-
quaint the school with the home conditions of the
child , and the home with the work and advantages
of the school ; ( c ) to ascertain the causes of irregu-
lar attendance and truancy , and seek the elimination
of these causes ; (d) to secure the enrollment in
school of all children who should be enrolled and
to keep all enrolled children in reasonably regular
attendance ; (e) to perform such other duties as may
be assigned him by the State Board of Education
or the district board .

11. Purchase of books and supplies for indigent
children . It shall be the duty of the superintendent

'be less than two hundred dollars ( $ 200 ) annually in
any county school district and fifty dollars ( $ 50 )
in any independent school district .
12. Cases of non -attendance to be investigated .
-The attendance officer shall have the power to in-
vestigate in his district any case of non -attendance
at school of any child under sixteen years of age ,
or any child suspected of being under sixteen years
of age , and he may take such action in accordance
with laws as the superintendent of schools may
direct or as he himself may deem proper in the ab-
sence of specific directions .
13. Police power.--The attendance officer and
assistant attendance officers shall be vested with po-
lice powers and the authority to serve warrants ,
and shall have the power and authority , under the
direction of the superintendent of schools and the
district board of education , the state attendance of-
ficer , or the State Board of Education , to institute
proceedings against any officer , parent, guardian ,
person , partnership or corporation violating and
(any ) provisions of the laws relating to compul-
sory attendance and the employment of children .
He shall have authority to enter workshops , fac-
tories , stores , and all other places where children are
employed and do whatever may be necessary in the
way of investigation or otherwise to enforce the
laws relating to compulsory attendance and the em-
ployment of children of compulsory school age . And
any officer , manager , director , or other person who
refuses to permit or in any way interferes with the
entrance therein of such attendance officer or in any
way interferes with any investigation therein shall
be guilty of a violation of this act and punishable
as hereinafter provided .
14. Definition of truancy .--Any child shall be
deemed a truant in the meaning of this act who
shall have been absent from school without valid
excuse for more than three days or tardy on more
than three days , any absence for less than half of a
school day being regarded as tardy . Any child shall
be deemed an habitual truant who shall have been
reported as a truant more than three times .
15. Reports to superintendent of schools .- The
principal or teacher in charge of any school , public ,
private , or parochial , shall report to the superin-
tendent of schools of the district in which the school
is situated the names , ages , and places of residence
of all pupils in attendance at their schools together
with such other facts as said superintendent may
require to facilitate the carrying out of the provi-
sions of the laws relating to compulsory attendance
and employment of children . Such reports shall be
made within the first two weeks of the beginning of
school in each school year .

16. Teachers to report withdrawals ; notices of
transfer . Whenever any child of compulsory age
withdraws from school , the teacher of the child shall
ascertain the reason. The fact of the withdrawal
and the reason therefor shall be immediately trans-
mitted by the teacher to the superintendent of
schools of the district in which the school is situated .
If the child who has withdrawn from school has done
so because of change of residence , the next residence
shall be ascertained and shall be included in the
notice thus transmitted . The superintendent shall
thereupon forward a card showing the essential
facts regarding the child and stating the place of
his new residence to the superintendent of schools
of the district to which the child has moved . The
State Board of Education shall prescribe the forms
to be used in the operation of this section .
Violation and Penalties
17. Notice of violation .- Every parent , guard-
ian , or custodian of any child residing in any school
district in the Commonwealth of Kentucky shall be
held legally responsible for any violation of this
act by such child . Before any proceedings are in-
stituted aganist such parent , guardian , or custodian
for violation of this act a written notice of such
violation shall be served on such person by the at-
tendance officer , and one day shall be given for the
termination of such violation . After such one day's
notice , if the violation is continued or if the pro-
visions of this act are again violated during the
school term by such child or ward , no further notice
shall be necessary , and such parent or guardian
shall be punishable as hereinafter provided . A no-
tice , under the provisions of this section , by reg-
istered mail or by personal service by the attendance
officer shall be a legal notice .
18. Law applicable to all children residing in the
Commonwealth .-Every child actually resident in
the Commonwealth shall be amenable to the laws re-
lating to compulsory attendance and neither he nor
the person in charge of him shall be excused from
the operation of said laws or the penalties under
them on the ground that the child's residence is
seasonable or that the parent of the child is a resi-
dent of another state . The board of education of
any school district shall admit without tuition
charge any child actually resident in the district who
would otherwise be deprived of school privileges in
this Commonwealth .
19. Work permits .-It shall be unlawful for any
person , firm or corporation to hire or employ or per-
mit any child between the ages of seven years and
sixteen years as heretofore defined , to work in any
gainful occupation until such person, firm , or cor-
poration shall have secured and placed on file in the
office of such person, firm , or corporation the work
permit for such child as hereinbefore described .
20. Penalty for violation by parent .-Any par-
ent, guardian , or custodian who has charge or con-
trol of a child between the ages aforesaid and who
willfully fails to comply with the foregoing require-
ments shall be guilty of a misdemeanor , and on con-
viction thereof shall be punished by a fine not to ex-
ceed ten dollars ($ 10 ) and costs for the first offense ,
and not to exceed twenty dollars ( $ 20 ) and costs for
each subsequent offense ; but the court trying the
case may , in its discretion , suspend enforcement of
the punishment , if the child be immediately placed
in attendance at a school as aforesaid , and may
finally remit the same if such attendance has contin-
ued regularly for the full school term . School at-
tendance may be proved by an attested certificate
of the principal or teacher in charge of the school .
21. Penalty for violation by employer.-Any
person , corporation , or firm , or agent or officer of a
corporation or firm that fails to comply with any or
all of the provisions of this act relating to compul-
sory attendance or that employs or suffers or per-
Acts-10
mits an ( any ) child to be employed in violation
thereof is guilty of a misdemeanor and shall , upon
conviction thereof, be punished by a fine of not less
than fifty dollars ( $ 50 ) nor more than two hundred
dollars ( $200 ) , or by imprisonment in the county
jail for not more than sixty ( 60 ) days or both such
fine and imprisonment for each and every offense .
22. Penalty for violation by school officer or
teacher . Any principal or teacher , or other school
officer who shall willfully fail to comply with the
provisions of this act shall be deemed guilty of a mis-
demeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be fined
not less than twenty-five dollars ( $ 25 ) nor more
than fifty dollars ( $50 ) and may have his certificate
revoked .
23. Penalty for violation by attendance officer.-
Any attendance officer or assistant attendance of-
ficer who willfully fails to comply with the provi-
sions of this act shall be guilty of a misdemeanor
and upon conviction thereof shall be fined not less.
than twenty-five dollars ( $25 ) nor more than fifty
dollars ( $50 ) , and in addition thereto shall be re-
moved from office and have his certificate revoked .
24. Disposal of fines .—All fines imposed here-
under and all sums required to be paid as penalties
under this act shall, after payments of the costs and
prosecution and of recovery thereof, be paid into
the treasury of the district board of education and
become a part of the school fund of the district .
School Census
25. Continuing census required.-Each board of
education shall maintain a permanent and con-
tinuing school census , of such nature that the num-
ber of children therein , the names and ages of such
children , the nationality , occupation and post office
address of each parent , guardian , or custodian may
be determined at any time in each school district .

28. Penalty for false report of census .- Should
any attendance officer or other person willfully or
fraudulently report a larger number of children of
school age in any district than the actual number , or
otherwise make a false report of the census to the
Superintendent of Public Instruction , he shall be
liable to a fine of not less than fifty dollars ( $50 )

false swearing, and in addition , he shall be removed
from office , and, in the case of an attendance officer ,
shall have his certificate revoked .
29. Distribution of state per capita .- The Super .
intendent of Public Instruction shall have the power
to distribute the state per capita to each school dis-

Special Schools
32. Parental or truant schools .-The board of
education of any independent school district em-
bracing a city of the first or the second class , is
hereby authorized and empowered to equip , main-
tain, and conduct one or more parental or truant
schools for the purpose of affording a place where
children of compulsory school age , and coming with .
in the provisions of this act , and of the statutes of
this Commonwealth concerning neglected , de-
pendent , and delinquent children , may be enrolled
for the purpose of discipline and instruction here-
inafter provided .
Such school or schools may be located either with-
in or without the corporate limits of the city ; pro-
vided, however , that such school or schools shall
not be located outside the county in which such city
is located , and , provided further , that no such
school shall be located at or near any penal institu-
tion .
No religious instruction shall be given in such
school or schools except as is allowed by law to be
given to public schools , but the board of education
shall make suitable regulations so that inmates shall
receive religious training in accordance with the
belief of such children's parents or guardians , either
by allowing such religious services to be held in such
institution or by arranging for the attendance of
public service elsewhere .
Any child committed to such school or schools ,
upon an order duly entered by the county court , may
be allowed to return home upon probation and to
remain while upon probation , subject to the friendly
visitation and supervision of a probation officer of
said county court, and subject at any time to be re-
turned to such school if said child , in the opinion
of the county court , shall violate the terms and con-
ditions of its probation . No child shall be released
upon probation in less than four weeks from the
time of his or her commitment , nor thereafter , un-
less the court shall be satisfied that said child who
is probationed , will attend regularly some public
or private school as herein provided . If any child
so released upon probation shall be regular in his or
her attendance in school , and his or her conduct as a
pupil shall be satisfactory for a period of one year
from the date upon which he or she was released
upon probation , he or she shall be finally discharged
from such parental or truant school , and shall not
be recommitted thereto , except in a subsequent pro-
ceeding undertaken according to the provisions of
this act , and to the statutes of this Commonwealth
concerning neglected , dependent , and delinquent
children .
Any child released from said school or schools
upon probation as herein provided , who shall violate
the conditions of his or her probation at any time
within one year thereafter shall, upon the order of
the county court , be returned to such parental or
truant school and shall not again be released upon
probation within a period of three months from the
date of such re-entering ; and if such child shall
violate the conditions of a second release upon pro-
bation , he or she shall be recommitted to such school
and shall not be released therefrom on probation
until he or she shall have remained in such school
one year.
The board of education of independent school dis-
tricts embracing cities of the first or the second
class may establish any rules of regulations con-
cerning such schools not inconsistent with this act
or the Constitution or laws of this Commonwealth .

Within the meaning of this act , a semester shall
consist of eighteen weeks (one-half year ) of stand-
ard college or university work , and a semester hour
shall consist of one academic or college hour per
week for one semester .

certificate in administration and supervision . At-
tendance officer certificates and emergency certifi-

school in this Commonwealth .

4. Attendance officer's certificate . The State

cation of attendance officers .
4a . Emergency certificates . When a district

The State Board of Education , may at its discre-

State Department of Education under the direction
of the Superintendent of Public Instruction , in ac-
cordance with rules and regulations approved by
the State Board of Education for such examina-
tions .
5. Certificates of former issue . The validity of
any certificate or license in force at the time this
act goes into effect shall not be impaired by this
act, and such certificate or license shall be reissued
or renewed in accordance with the terms of the law
applying at the date of issue .
—6. Renewal of certificates . Certificates lower
than the standard provided for in this act may be
raised to a higher grade only by completing in a
standard college or university the amount of aca-
demic and professional work prescribed for such
renewal or for such higher grade certificate .
7. Fees .-A fee of two dollars ( $ 2 ) shall be paid
for each issuance of a certificate and a fee of one
dollar ($ 1 ) for each renewal or conversion from
lower to higher grade . Fees thus collected shall be
used toward defraying operating expenses of the
Division of Teacher Training and Certification of
the State Department of Education .

dation of the Superintendent of Public Instruction ,
revoke , for immorality , misconduct in office , incom-
petency , or willful neglect of duty , any certificate
issued under this act , or any certificate or license
issued under any previous act , to superintendents ,
