ARTICLE XV-DEPARTMENT OF INSURANCE
§ 1. Department of Insurance . There is hereby
created a Department of Insurance , consisting of a
Commissioner of Insurance and a deputy Commis-
sioner , who shall be appointed by the Governor of
the Commonwealth on the effective date of this Act ,
to serve during the will and pleasure of the Gover-
nor , and their successors in office shall be appointed
to hold office in like manner. The Commissioner of
Insurance and Deputy Commissioner shall be citi-
zens of Kentucky , at least 30 years of age ; and the
qualifications for such appointments shall include
four years of responsible experience in the manage-
ment of substantial public or private enterprises .
The Commissioner of Insurance shall receive an an-
nual salary of Five Thousand ( $ 5,000.00 ) Dollars
per year ; and the deputy Commissioner shall re-
ceive a salary of Four Thousand, Two Hundred
($4,200.00 ) Dollars per year, payable monthly as
other state salaries are paid .
The Commissioner of Insurance and the Deputy
Commissioner shall qualify by taking the consti-
tutional oath of office and by executing bonds to the
Commonwealth of Kentucky for the faithful per-
formance of the duties imposed upon them by law ,
which bonds shall be renewable annually or oftener
if required by the Governor . In the case of the
Commissioner of Insurance the bond shall be in the
penal sum of $ 100,000.00 ; and the Deputy Commis-
sioner shall execute bond in the sum of $ 50,000.00 .
The premiums on said bonds shall be paid as other
expenses of the Department .
§ 2. Department of Insurance . All functions ,
duties and authority heretofore vested in the Audi-
tor of Public Accounts , Insurance Department , the
Insurance Commissioner of the State of Kentucky ,
the Auditor of Public Accounts as Fire Marshall
and Superintendent of Fire Insurance Rates , as to
the supervision of fire insurance , rate making , and
for the examination and prohibiting rebating and
discrimination in fixing and collecting fire insurance
rates , requiring companies to maintain and cooper-
ate in maintaining and operating rate -making bu-
reaus , inspecting and surveying by such bureaus ,
and all other acts and duties as provided by Chap-
ter 16 of the Acts of 1920 General Assembly being
Section 762b -1 to 762 - b -36 inclusive and Sections
744 to 762 inclusive , Kentucky Statutes , Carroll's
1930 Edition, and all other laws relating thereto , are
transferred to and vested in the Department of In-
surance .
ARTICLE XVI-DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND MINERALS
§ 1. There is hereby created a Department of
Mines and Minerals which shall consist of a Chief
Inspector of Mines and such Deputy Inspectors as
provided by law .
§ 2. Division of Geology . There is hereby cre-
ated in this Department a Division of Geology
which shall be in charge of a geologist who shall
have pursued the study of geology in some standard
college or university for a period of four years , and
in addition thereto have had not less than four
years of practical experience in field and laboratory
work as such . Said geologist shall be designated as
State Geologist . Said geologist , the chief mine in-
spector and the deputy inspector shall be appointed
by the Governor for a term of not exceeding four
years and may be removed by the Governor at his
pleasure . The salary of said State Geologist shall
not exceed the sum of Two Hundred and Fifty Dol-
lars ( $ 250.00 ) per month . He shall be responsible
to the Department of Mines and Minerals .
§ 3. Bureau of Mineral and Topographical Sur-
vey. The Bureau of Mineral and Topographical
Survey as provided by Chapter 26 , page 250 , of the
Acts of the General Assembly of 1932 is hereby
abolished , and all the duties and functions hereto-
fore vested by law in the said Bureau of Mineral
and Topographical Survey are now transferred to
and vested in the Department of Mines and Min-
erals .
ARTICLE XVII-DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND
BUDGETARY CONTROL
§ 1. There is hereby created a Department of
Finance and Budgetary Control which shall consist
of the Governor , Chairman of the State Tax Com-
mission , Auditor of Public Accounts , State Inspec-
tor and Examiner , and the Secretary of the Execu-
tive Cabinet . The Governor shall be ex- officio chair-
man , and the Secretary of the Governor's Execu
tive Cabinet shall be Secretary .
$ 2. Functions and Duties . All functions here-
tofore vested in the Budget Commission are hereby
transferred to and vested in the Department of
Finance and Budgetary Control , which department
shall have and exercise all the administrative func-
tions of the State , except as otherwise provided
herein , in relation to :
(a) Developing financial policies and plans for
consideration by the Governor and the General As-
sembly as the basis for his budget report and the
recommendations to the General Assembly . Pre-
paring the detailed budget for submission to and
consideration by the General Assembly .
(b) Coordinating and supervising the fiscal af-
fairs and fiscal procedures of the State to insure the
carrying into effect of the definite financial policies
and plans approved or prescribed by the General
Assembly .
(c) Fiscal reporting .
$ 3. The State Budget Officer shall in person
and with such assistance as the Department of Fi-
nance and Budgetary Control may provide and
under the direction of the Department :
(a) Keep in continuous touch with the opera-
tions , plans and needs of the several agencies of the
State , and with the sources and amounts of revenue
and other receipts of the State .
(b ) Appraise the quantity and quality of serv-
ices rendered by each agency , and the needs for
such services and for any new services .
(c ) Prepare the biennial budget report for the
Governor's approval and submission to the General
Assembly .
(d ) Prepare a State Budget for each fiscal year.
( e) Recommend transfers between appropria-
tions under the provisions of law, to become effec-
tive upon approval by the Board of Finance and
Budgetary Control .
(f) Examine and recommend work programs
and periodical allotments to the several agencies ,
and changes therein , subject to the approval of the
Board of Finance and Budgetary Control .
(g) Develop plans for improvements and econo-
mies in organization and operation of the several
agencies, and install such plans as approved by the
respective heads of agencies or as directed by the
Governor , the General Assembly or the Board of
Finance and Budgetary Control .
(h) Devise and prescribe the forms of opera-
tion reports to be required periodically from the
several agencies and require the several agencies to
make such reports .
(i) Edit , verify , and reduce to concise and read-
able form, every annual , biennial , or other report or
publication of any kind proposed by any agency
to be printed out of public funds .
(j ) Examine and approve all statements and re-
ports on the financial condition , and estimated fu-
ture financial condition and operations of the state
goverment and the several agencies , before any such
reports are released to the Governor , to the Gen-
eral Assembly , or for publication ; receive and deal
with all requests for information as to financial
conditions and operations of the State ; prepare
such unit costs and cost statistics as may be re-
quired from time to time.
(k) Advise and assist the Board of Finance and
Budgetary Control , the Governor , and the General
Assembly and the Appropriations Committees there-
of , on request , in any matters relating to the func-
tions of the department .
(1) Recommend a unified and integrated system
of accounts covering the form of all accounts to be
kept and all financial reports to be rendered for the
State as a whole and any of its agencies .
(m ) Keep a summary of the financial transac-
tions of all the agencies of the State .

§ 1. The Department of Library and Archives

ARTICLE XXI-INDEPENDENT AGENCIES
§ 1. The Railroad Commission , the Workmen's
Compensation Board , the Board of Election Com-
missioners , the State Racing Commission , the Board
of Bar Examiners , and Judicial Council shall con-
tinue and remain independent agencies and perform

ARTICLE XXII- STATE INSPECTOR AND EXAMINER
§ 1. The State Inspector and Examiner shall re-
main an independent auditing agency exercising all

Any powers conferred upon said State Inspector
and Examiner by this Act shall be in addition to
those now conferred by law .
§ 2. State Board of Accountancy . The State
Board of Accountancy as now constituted shall be

Examiner .
ARTICLE XXIII —THE EXECUTIVE CABINET
The Governor , Secretary of State , Auditor , At-
torney General , Chairman of the State Highway
Commission , Superintendent of Public Instruction ,
Commissioner of Agriculture , Labor and Statistics ,
Treasurer , Chairman of the State Tax Commission ,
Adjutant General , Chairman of the Department of
Public Welfare , Commissioner of Insurance and the
Commissioner of Banking and Securities shall con-
stitute the Governor's Executive Cabinet . They
shall meet at least once monthly at such times and
places as may be provided by rule , and at other
times and places upon the call of the Governor .
The Executive Cabinet shall consider such mat-
ters involving general administrative policies and
procedure , relations between departments and other
agencies and desirable measures for cooperation be-
tween departments and other agencies as the Gov-
ernor , the Secretary of the Executive Cabinet , or
any member may place before it , and shall advise
and consult with the Governor at his request upon
all matters affecting the welfare of the State and
relating to the several departments and agencies .
The Governor shall be Chairman of the Executive
Cabinet. The Executive Cabinet and the Secretary
thereof, shall be deemed to be attached to the office
of the Governor and not constitute a separate de-
partment or agency of the State .
There shall be a Secretary of the Cabinet who
shall be appointed by the Governor upon the basis
of his qualifications therefor . The qualifications for
such appointment shall include four (4 ) years of
responsible experience in the management of sub-
stantial public or private business enterprises . The
Secretary of the Executive Cabinet shall prepare all
matters for consideration by the Executive Cabinet .
The Secretary of the said Cabinet shall also be the
Secretary of the Department of Finance and
Budgetary Control and of the Department of Public
Property. His salary shall be fixed by the Governor
within the constitutional limits , and he shall hold
office at the pleasure of the Governor . He shall keep
the minutes and records of the Executive Cabinet .
He shall make continuous studies and accumulate
and compile information for the use of the Execu-
tive Cabinet and the members thereof and the Gov-
ernor relative to the business management and the
operation of the State government , and shall cur
rently supply the members with copies of available
reports and documents and other material relating
to the conditions and problems of the State , the dif-
ficulties that individual departments and agencies
have to overcome , the manner in which the problems
of each department and other agencies relate to
those of other departments and of other agencies ,
and to the State government , and the methods by
which similar problems have been met and solved in
other jurisdictions . He shall assist the Governor in
handling and in securing a coordination of the ef-
forts of the several departments and other agencies
with respect to matters of administration which do
not pertain specifically to individual departments or
other agencies .
The Secretary of the Executive Cabinet shall not
hold office in the organization of any political party .
He shall deal solely with the administrative and
operating processes and procedures and such facts
relative thereto as may be of use in the carrying out
of any administrative policies that may be adopted .
It is hereby declared to be the policy of the State
to regard the office of the Secretary of the Executive
Cabinet as a continuing one , the primary purpose
of which shall be to place at the disposal of each
succeeding administration of the State government ,
the accumulated knowledge and experience of the
encumbent relative to the course of business man-
agement , and the program of the State, the past
action in such matters and the reasons therefor , and
the studies of the projects and undertakings that
the State has in progress at any time.
It shall be the duty of the Secretary of the Execu-
tive Cabinet to investigate the merit of service of
the employees in the several departments in the
State Government and , whenever , in his judgment
any one or more employees in any department are
not rendering meritorious service or not needed to
properly carry on the functions of such department ,
it shall be his duty to file a complaint with the Execu-
tive Cabinet, setting out his findings with reference
to such employee or employees , and the Executive
Cabinet shall hear and determine whether or not
such employee or employees are rendering meritori-
ous service and are needed in such department to
properly carry on its functions , and shall recom-
mend to the Governor what disposition should be
made with reference to such employee or employees
and thereupon, the Governor may, upon recom-
mendation of a majority of the members of the Cab-
inet either discharge or continue such employee or
employees as in his judgment the best interests of
the State may require .
ARTICLE XXIV- GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 1. Transfer of Functions . Whenever functions
heretofore vested in , or exercised by, any agency
are by this Act transferred in whole or in part to
and vested in a department or other agency created
or continued by this Act, the department or other
agency in which such functions are vested shall be
the successor to the agency in which such functions
have heretofore been vested and every act done in
the exercise of such functions by or under the
authority of the department or other agency to
which such functions are hereby transferred , shall
have the same force and effect as if done by the
former agency . Whenever such former agency is
referred to , or designated in any law , contract or
document , such reference or designation shall be
deemed to refer to the department or other agency ,
hereunder to which the functions of such former
agency so referred to or designated have been trans-
ferred and vested by the terms of this Act .
§ 2. Transfer of Records and Equipment . Upon
the taking effect of any transfer of functions pro-
vided by this Act , all books , papers , records , prop-
erty and pending business theretofore made , used ,
acquired or conducted by any previously existing
agency in the exercise of functions are hereby trans-
ferred to and vested in the agency succeeding to
such functions .
§ 3. Transfer of Officers and Employees . All
officers and employees whose functions are trans-
ferred hereby from an existing agency and vested
in a different agency , created or continued by the
terms of this Act, shall be transferred with their
functions to the department in which their functions
or the major part thereof are hereby vested , and
shall so far as practicable continue to perform their
usual duties until the expiration of their respective
terms for which they were appointed or elected , but
the head of each department shall have power to
abolish unnecessary positions and employments to
transfer employees between positions , and to change
the duties , titles and compensations of existing po-
sitions and services , and to discharge any such em-
ployees not satisfactory to the head of such depart-
ment .
§ 4. Transfer of Appropriations . Whenever
functions heretofore vested in any agency are trans-
ferred by the terms of this Act and vested in a dif-
ferent agency , the balances of appropriations to the
credit of the agency from which such functions are
transferred available for expenditure in the exer-
cise of such functions shall be transferred to the
credit of the agency to which such functions are
hereby transferred , and shall be made available
under the provisions of this Act, for expenditure
by such agency in the exercise of such functions in
accordance with the law. :
Where two or more functions provided for by
existing appropriations are not segregated to the
purposes for such function , but are divided between
two or more agencies , the divisions of such ap-
propriations shall be determined by the Governor ,
with the approval of the Department of Finance
and Budgetary Control .
5. Heads of Departments . The heads of de-
partments provided herein shall have direction and
control of their respective departments , and , sub-
ject to the provisions of this Act, shall through such
departments exercise such powers and perform such
duties as vested by law in the several departments
under their direction and control and in any agency
thereof . Except as otherwise expressly provided by
this Act, the heads of the departments shall be ap-
pointed by the Governor on the basis of their merit
and fitness to perform the duties and exercise the
responsibilities of their respective offices .
§ 6. Governor May Remove Officers . The Gov-
ernor shall have the power to remove , for cause
deemed sufficient by him, the head or deputies of
any departments , who are subject to appointment
by him.
§ 7. Termination of Conflicts Between Depart-
ments . In all cases where question arises between
departments or other agencies or officers or boards
thereof as to their respective functions , or where
departments or other agencies issue conflicting
orders or make conflicting rules , the Governor , with
the advice of the Executive Cabinet , shall determine
the questions and action shall be had in accordance
with the decision .
§ 8. Administrative Rules . The Governor , with
the approval of the Executive Cabinet, may pre-
scribe such rules for the conduct of the administra-
tive departments , not inconsistent with law , as he
may deem necessary or expedient . The heads of
each department may likewise provide such rules
as they may deem necessary and expedient for the
work of their departments and for making effective
the provisions of law not inconsistent herewith or
with the general rules prescribed by the Governor
§ 9. When the Act Is Effective . The provisions
of this Act shall be and become effective at 12 o'clock
midnight , June 30 , 1934 .
$ 10 . Inconsistent Laws Repealed . It is the pur-
pose of this Act to provide a uniform , integrated
and comprehensive plan of organization for the
executive departments of the Government of the
Commonwealth for the exercise of all executive and
administrative functions of the State . All laws and
parts of laws in conflict herewith are hereby repealed
to the extent of such conflict .
§ 11. Constitutionality . If any part or portion
of this Act shall be held unconstitutional or invalid
for any reason , the remainder of the Act shall never-
theless remain in full force and effect .
Approved February 28 , 1934 .

laws.title: AN ACT to regulate the Fees of Justices of the Peace.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1865, ch. 695, pp. 42–43
laws.summary: This act outlines the fees for various services provided by Justices of the Peace in Kentucky. Notably, it includes specific fees for actions related to slaves, such as arresting and carrying a slave before a justice, and whipping a slave by order of an officer. These provisions, while framed as fee regulations, directly address the legal and penal treatment of enslaved individuals, reflecting the racial hierarchy and control mechanisms prevalent during the post-Civil War era, which continued into the Jim Crow period.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1865, p. 197
laws.summary: This resolution requests the Governor to urge the President to immediately remove all "negro troops" from Kentucky. The justification provided is that their presence is detrimental to citizens, they commit outrages, and their presence causes irritation to former owners and citizens. The resolution also requests that white soldiers be assigned for duty in their place.
key_provisions: 1865 . Resolved by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky : That the Governor of this Commonwealth be authorized to pay ,or cause to be paid,out of the militaryfund,to each sol- dierand officerof saidregiments,whatever may be found due them forsaid service,upon a correctadjustment of theirac- counts,the pay of said allowances of soldiersand officersof the army of the United Statesto be the basisof said settle- ment . Approved June 3,1865. No. 95 . RESOLUTION requestingthe PresidenttowithdrawNegro Troopsfromthe State of Kentucky . WHEREAS , Negro soldiersthat have been recruitedin the State of Kentucky have been quartered in differentpartsof the State,much to the detriment of the citizensthereof, said troopscommitting many outragesupon the livesand property of citizens; and whereas, Kentucky isone of the loyalStates of the Union ,and thereforeentitledto allthe privilegesand immunities of other loyal States; and there existsno neces- sityforthe presenceof said troopswithin the State; in fact, theirpresenceis a sourceof great irritationto theirformer owners and the citizensgenerally; therefore, Resolved, That the Governor be requested to respectfully request and earnestlyurge the immediate removal of all negro troopsfrom the State by the Presidentof the United States; and that,forthenecessaryprotectionof thepeople,a sufficientnumber of white soldiersmay be assignedforduty to this Commonwealth . Approved June 3, 1865.

laws.summary: This act directs the Auditor of Public Accounts to issue a warrant to Thomas M. Hicks for $671.70, payable from the runaway slave fund. This is compensation for a negro woman and her child who were purchased by Hicks but later taken by U.S. military authorities. Hicks must provide bond to indemnify the state and pay the former owner if they prove ownership and claim proceeds from runaway slaves.

It explicitly states that voters must be 'white male citizens' over the age of twenty-one, with specific residency requirements. It also includes an additional category of voters: 'white male citizens' who live outside the town but within Montgomery county, provided they own real estate within Mount Sterling subject to taxation.

laws.summary: This act directs the Auditor of Public Accounts to issue warrants for the care of 'lunatics of color' sent to the Lunatic Asylum, provided certain conditions are met, similar to the process for white persons. It implies a separate or distinct process for the care of Black individuals with mental illness.
key_provisions: § 1. laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1913, pp. 125–127
laws.summary: This act levies an additional tax of two dollars on every male negro and mulatto over eighteen years of age. The collected funds are to be used exclusively for the support of negro and mulatto paupers and the education of negro and mulatto children within the county where the tax was collected. It mandates separate tax columns for negroes and mulattoes and outlines the process for allocating funds to negro schools, including per-scholar allowances and reporting requirements.

laws.title: AN ACT for the benefit of School District No. 1, in Harrison county, and other School Districts similarly situated.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 2002, p. 131
laws.summary: This act validates the report of a colored school taught in School District No. 1, Harrison County, in 1866, as a common school, and allows for similar colored schools to be recognized. It addresses a failure by trustees to report the colored school, which the commissioner states was taught under the provisions of a previous act.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 2002 . AN ACT forthe benefitof School DistrictNo. 1,in Harrison county, and otherSchool Districtssimilarlysituated. Approved March 9, 1867.

laws.title: AN ACT to incorporate the African Cemetery Company, of Bourbon County.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1031, pp. 225–226
laws.summary: This act incorporates the Bourbon County Cemetery Company and mandates that at least half of the land owned by the company must be set aside for the burial of persons of color who are not stockholders or lot owners. The remaining land can be divided and sold.

laws.title: AN ACT to amend the 10th article of the Charter of the City of Louisville.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 575
laws.summary: This act amends the charter of the City of Louisville's public school system. It allows non-resident taxpayers to send their children to city schools free of tuition, but explicitly prohibits children of the African race from attending schools with white children. It also mandates that school taxes paid by persons of the African race be kept as a separate fund and used for the education of African race children within the city, potentially establishing separate schools for them.

Those livingin thecounty,and not paying taxeson citypropertyinLouisville,shallnot be permittedto send theirchildren to said schools: Provided,That nothing in this act shallpermit or authorize the general council of the cityof Louisville,or board of trusteesof saidpublic schools , to suffer children of the African race to become pupilsof said schoolswith white children; and that the said general council and board of trusteesshallkeep as a separatefundthe schooltax leviedby saidcity,and paid by persons of the African race within said city; and shall apply and use said schoolfund ortax so paid by persons of the Africanracein the educationof childrenof parents of the Africanraceresidingwithinsaidcity,orwho pay a schooltaxtosaidcity;and forthatpurposemay esestablish such schoolsin saidcity,and adopt rulesfortheirregula- tion and government .

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1433, pp. 616–639
laws.summary: This section of the act grants the mayor the power to investigate and arrest individuals involved in unlawful assemblages, specifically mentioning gatherings for gaming, drinking, or any purpose not allowed by law. Crucially, it explicitly includes provisions for mixed-race gatherings ('where the said assemblage shall, or may be constituted partly of white and partly of black population') and allows the mayor to proceed with the power of the county and his officers to arrest all persons unlawfully assembled.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1868, ch. 805, pp. 275–276
laws.summary: This act authorizes the Hancock County Court to levy additional taxes. Specifically, it allows for an additional ad valorem tax of eight cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property, an additional poll tax of one dollar on each white male over twenty-one years old, and a tax of two dollars on each negro or mulatto male over eighteen years old. The revenue from the white male poll tax and the negro/mulatto male poll tax is to be applied in the same manner as other taxes raised by law. The revenue from the first two sections (ad valorem and white male poll tax) is to be applied to the discharge of present indebtedness and current expenses of the county.

CHAPTER 805 .
AN ACT to authorizethe Hancock County Court to levy additionalTaxes .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1. That the county court of Hancock county ,a ma-
jorityof thejusticesof the peace of saidcounty concur-
ring,be ,and ishereby ,authorizedto levy an ad valorem tax
of eight cents on each one hundred dollars' worth of tax-
able propertyin saidcounty,in additionto the tax now
authorizedby law .
§ 2. That saidcountycourt,a majorityof thejusticesof
the peace concurring,be,and ishereby,authorizedtolevy
a poll tax of one dollaron each white male over the age
of twenty-one years,in additionto the tax of two dollars
now leviedby law .
§3 . That saidcountycourt,a majorityof thejusticesof
the peace concurring,be,and is,authorizedto levy a tax
of two dollars on each negro or mulatto inale in said
county ,over the age of eighteen years,in addition to the
tax now authorizedby law , to be appliedin the same
manner and forthe same purposesas othertaxesso raised
are now by law .
§4 . That the sheriffcollectand account for the taxes
hereinauthorizedto be levied,in the same manner ,and
underthesame responsibilities,as othercountylevyisnow
collectedand accounted for by said sheriff. That the taxes
allowed to be levied by the firstand second sections of
thisactbe appliedto thedischargeof thepresentindebt-
ednessand currentexpensesof the county.
§5 . That the provisionsof thisact shallapply to the
presentyear,eighteenhundred and sixty-eight,only,and
said act shalltake effectfrom itspassage .
Approved March 6, 1868.

laws.summary: This section outlines the qualifications for voting in an election in Versailles, Kentucky. It specifies that only free white male citizens, aged twenty-one, who have resided in the state for two years and the town for one year, and who have paid their poll tax for the preceding year, are eligible to vote. It also details the process for examining poll books, determining election results, and handling contested elections and vacancies.
key_provisions: §77 . Every free white male citizen of the age of twenty -one years,who has residedin the State two years, or in saidtown one year nextprecedingthe election,and who has paid hishead or poll-tax fortheprecedingyear, shall be entitled to vote at said election; but such voter shall, at the time of the election, be a resident of said town ,and have residedthereinforsixtydays next pre- ceding the same .

laws.summary: This act imposes an additional tax of fifteen cents per one hundred dollars of property value for the year 1870 and each succeeding year to increase the Common School Fund. Crucially, the tax is to be levied and collected from the property of white persons only. Furthermore, the revenue generated from this and previous acts for common school purposes shall be expended and appropriated for the education of white children exclusively. Any diversion of these funds for purposes other than the exclusive education of white children will cease the levying of this tax.

laws.summary: This statute outlines the process for the Superintendent of Public Instruction to estimate and apportion state revenue for common schools. It specifies that the apportionment is based on the number of 'white children' between the ages of six and twenty. The statute also details how funds are allocated to districts and teachers, and how uncalled-for funds are reinvested. The explicit mention of 'white children' for apportionment is a key indicator of racial segregation in education.

laws.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to establish a Work -house in Christian County," approved January 28, 1870.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, ch. 288, pp. 457–458
laws.summary: This act establishes a work-house in Christian County, Kentucky. It mandates that individuals convicted of vagrancy in Christian County shall be confined in this work-house instead of the county jail. The court can adjudge confinement for a period not exceeding six months. The county court is authorized to make confined persons labor on streets and public highways, and to appoint a person to keep the work-house and employ guards. This provision takes effect upon the erection of the work-house.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1233, p. 47
laws.summary: This act repeals a previous act that provided benefits to Negroes and Mulattoes. It then states that Negroes and Mulattoes will be taxed the same per capita and on real and personal estate as the white population, with no additional taxes. This effectively removes any special provisions or benefits previously afforded to Black individuals and places them under the same tax structure as white citizens, while explicitly mentioning racial groups.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 1233 . AN ACT to repeal an act, entitled " An act for the benefit of the Negroes and Mulattoes of this Commonwealth ," approved March 9, 1867 . Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyoftheCommonwealth of Kentucky:

§2 . That hereafterthe same tax per capita, and the same rateof taxationon real and personalestate(ex- cepttaxesforcommon schoolpurposes),shallbe collected of all the negroes and mulattoes in this Commonwealth as of the white population, and no other.

laws.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to establish a State House of Reform for Juvenile Delinquents," approved February 15th, 1869.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1926, p. 121
laws.summary: This act amends a previous law establishing a State House of Reform for juvenile delinquents. It mandates that all white male and female persons between the ages of eight and seventeen, convicted of vagrancy, petit larceny, or any crime less than murder, shall be committed to this House of Reform. It also specifies that females will not be committed until the Governor announces that provisions have been made for their care in the institution.

laws.summary: This act designates School District No. 14 in Simpson County to encompass the entire town of Franklin. It specifies that only schools taught by regularly qualified white persons will be considered common schools. The trustees are required to report the number of white pupils of common school age attending these schools and to pro rata the school fund among these schools based on the number of white pupils attending each.
key_provisions: §2 . It also empowers them to levy taxes to pay for the interest and redemption of these bonds. Crucially, it explicitly states that only the property of white persons shall be taxed for these purposes, and that an increase in per capita tax shall apply to white persons only.

The assessment thereof shallbe made in the manner that is now provided by law for the assess- ment of propertyin saidtown ; and the collectionof the tax shallbe had in the manner that is alsoprovidedby law . 2d. The money thus raisedshallbe appliedexclusively to the payment of the interestupon the bonds herein authorizedtobe issued,and to theirredemption at ma- turity,or at theoptionof the board of trustees: Provided, however, That onlythe propertyof whitepersonsshallbe taxed for the purposes of this act . 3d. Said board of trusteesare hereby authorized to in- creasethe percapitatax of the personsliableunder the presentlaws to pay the same ,to any amount not exceed- ing two dollarsin addition to the amount now assessed and collected: Provided,however, That the provisions of this subdivisionof this section shall apply to white per- sons only .

§1 . That the board of trusteesof the town of Clover-
portare hereby authorizedtoissuethe bonds ofsaidtown

ceedingone dollarupon each one hundred dollars' worth

ment of propertyin saidtown ; and the collectionof the

law .

3d. Said board of trusteesare hereby authorized to in-
creasethe percapitatax of the personsliableunder the

ing two dollarsin addition to the amount now assessed
and collected: Provided,however, That the provisions of

§7. But no tax shallbe levied,and thisactshallnot be
1871 .
1871 . deemed tobe in force,untilthe same shallbe ratifiedby a

laws.summary: This act amends the charter of the town of West Point by authorizing the election of a police judge and empowering the trustees to build a lockup. Crucially, Section 2 states that Section 5 of a previous amendment shall apply to the colored as well as the white population, implying that previous provisions may have been race-specific. The lockup is for confining individuals convicted of violating town ordinances and failing to pay fines, with a daily confinement rate.

laws.summary: This statute outlines the eligibility requirements for serving on the Common Council of the city of Paducah. Specifically, it states that a councilman must be a 'white male citizen of the United States,' among other qualifications related to age, residency, property ownership, and holding other offices. It also details conditions under which a council member's office would be vacated.

DISTRIBUTION OF POWERS OF GOVERNMENT .

wards as the interestof the citymay ,in theiropinion,re-
quire,layingthem offas nearlyequal in qualifiedvoters

Section 7 explicitly states that all officers of the town, including the police judge, town marshal, and five trustees, "shall be white males over twenty-one years old, and residents of said town." This racial qualification for holding public office is a hallmark of Jim Crow legislation.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1340 .
AN ACT to create the Officeof Superintendent of the Negro Paupers of
Mercer County .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That the countycourt of Mercer county may ap-
point some fitand discreetperson to act as superintend-
ent of the negro poor of said county .
§ 2. That itshall be the duty of said superintendent to
take care of,manage ,and controlthe negro paupers in
1871 .
1871 . said county ; to provide for each person committed to
his charge a comfortable maintenance and support, and
proper medical attention; and in the eventof the death
of any such person,to have the same buried.
§3 . Said superintendent, in the behalf of the county
court,shall have power to make such contracts, in the
management of said business,as he may deem expedient,
to providehomes forsuch personsas may be committed
to his charge ; but in no case shall said superintendent
pay more than sixty-five dollarsfor the support of any
one person, or more than ten dollarsfor burial expenses .
§ 4. It shallbe the duty of said officertocollect,receive,
and disburseany and allmoney thathas heretoforebeen
or thatmay be hereafterappropriatedby the Legislature
or county court of Mercer ,for the benefitof said paupers ;
and may directthe county attorney to collect,by suit or
otherwise,from the present sheriffor any former sheriff,
or any otherperson of Mercer county, any money that
may be due now or that hereaftermay become due from
saidofficersorpersons,or which constitutesa partof said
fund .
§ 5. That all contracts made by said superintendent
shallbe in writing,and signedby the parties,and shall
be paid by said superintendent out of the fund allowed
for that purpose, as above mentioned .
§ 6. Before said officeris permitted or allowed to use
and expend the fund, or any part of the same , appro-
priatedby the countycourtforthe benefitof negro pau-
pers,he shall firstexhaust in the payment of said con-
tracts the fund known as the " Negro Pauper Fund ,"
collectedin each year , and heretofore set apart by law
forthebenefitof such persons. Said officershallreceive
onlysuch persons as he is directedby the orderof the
county court,or of the judge in vacation.
§ 7. That allcoloredpersonswho areresidentsof Mer-
cer county, and have not been brought into said county by
any person forthe purpose of becoming a charge upon the
same , and are the owners of no property in possession,
reversion,or remainder ,and are incapable of laboring,in
whole or in part,for theirsupport,and whose parents are
unable to support them ,shall be deemed paupers within
the meaning of thisact,and may , by proper order, be
placed upon the county for support.
§ 8. That it shall be the duty of said officerto make a
reportin writing, and under oath, of all his acts and
doings under and by virtue of this act, to the county
court of Mercer , at itsOctober term in each year ; said
reportshallshow the amount of money collected, re-
ceived, and disbursedby said officerduring the year;
from whom receivedand towhom paid,and the number
of persons committed to his charge, and the name of
each ; and shall exhibit all his contracts made for the
support of said paupers ,and vouchers for other expend-
itures .
§ 9. That said officershall be required,before entering
upon the dutiesof saidoffice,toexecutebond with good
security,payable to the county court of Mercer county ,
and to be approved by the court,stipulatingfor a faithful
discharge of all the duties of his officeby virtue of this
act; and shall be allowed , at each court of claims , a
reasonable compensation for his services,to be paid out
of the fund in his own hands ,or otherwise,if the court
direct .
§ 10. This act shalltake effectfrom itspassage .
Approved February 22, 1871.

laws.summary: This act amends the charter of the City of Newport, establishing requirements for its police force. Specifically, it states that police officers must be 'white citizens of the United States' and residents of the city for one year preceding their election. The act also outlines the election process for the police force by a board of police commissioners.
key_provisions: §1 . That the cityof Newport may have and maintain a police force, with distinctionof grade , and of uniform and badges to be worn by the chief, lieutenants, and policeman , as may be prescribedby ordinance of the city council. They shall be white citizensof the United States, and residentsof said cityfor one year preceding theirelection,not lessthan twenty -four years of age , and known to be moral ,sober, and sagacious; none of them shalltake any part or interferein electionsfurtherthan to vote. They shall be elected in the following manner : The mayor of said city,the presidentof the citycouncil, and the chairman of the committee on policeof the city council,shall constitutea board of police commissioners for one year ,without pay ; and on the firstMonday in January in each year, afterthe presentyear,or within ten days thereafter, they shallelectthe whole police force of said city for that year . The police for the year 1871 shall,in the same manner ,be elected by said board, within thirtydays afterthe passage of thisact.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1343 .
AN ACT to amend the Charter of the City of Newport .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That the cityof Newport may have and maintain
a police force, with distinctionof grade , and of uniform
and badges to be worn by the chief, lieutenants, and
policeman , as may be prescribedby ordinance of the city
council. They shall be white citizensof the United
States, and residentsof said cityfor one year preceding
theirelection,not lessthan twenty -four years of age , and
known to be moral ,sober, and sagacious; none of them
shalltake any part or interferein electionsfurtherthan to
vote. They shall be elected in the following manner :
The mayor of said city,the presidentof the citycouncil,
and the chairman of the committee on policeof the city
council,shall constitutea board of police commissioners
for one year ,without pay ; and on the firstMonday in
January in each year, afterthe presentyear,or within
ten days thereafter, they shallelectthe whole police
force of said city for that year . The police for the
year 1871 shall,in the same manner ,be elected by said
board, within thirtydays afterthe passage of thisact.
§2 . The policemen so elected shall each be commis-
sioned by the mayor forone year ,and until his successor
isqualified,which said commission shall be a warrant of
authority. They shalleach take an oath,and givebond,
with good surety,to be approved by the citycouncil,for
the faithfulperformance of theirduty .
§3 . At the annual sessionof the policecommissioners,
they shallnominate a chiefof police,and a lieutenantto
1871 . thechief, and reportthesame to thecitycouncilfortheir
approval or rejection,each to serve forone year ,and until
his successorisqualified.
§ 4. The chiefofpoliceand lieutenantshallnot,directly-
or indirectly,purchase,or inany way obtaincontrolof,the
claimsof any policemanforhispay,or any partthereof;
and ifeitherofthem do so,theyshallat once be dismissed
from office. The salaryor pay of the chief,lieutenant,
and of the policemen , shall be exempt from execution,
attachment , and distress.
§5 . The mayor may ,at any time ,convene the police
commissioners for the purpose of fillingvacancies,or to
attend to any other business within the scope of their
authority. Vacancies shallbe filledby said board of
commissioners for the unexpired term vacated .
§ 6. Said board of commissioners shall nominate the
lieutenantsof police, and reportthe same to the city
council for their approval or rejection. The number of
lieutenantsand policemenand theirpay,and the pay of
the chief and firstlieutenant,shall,from time to time ,be
fixedand regulatedby ordinance of the citycouncil.
§7 . Said board of commissioners shalldismiss any and
every member of the police for intermeddling with, or
directlyor indirectlytakingany part in,electionsfurther
than to vote ; for intentionallyomitting or failingto per-
form any dutiesincumbent upon him as a policeman;
forwanton breaches of the law or ordinances of the city,
or the rulesof government of the police; for immoral
conduct,or for other sufficientcause ; but every police-
man so dismissedmay appeal to the citycouncil,and if
the action of said policecommissioners be not sustained
by the council,he shall be restored to his place ; but
duringthependency of such appealhe shallbe suspended
from office.
§ 8. Persons arrestedby the police or marshal of said
city,or by any of hisdeputies,forany offenseagainstthe
cityordinances,shallbe placed in the cityjail,if neces-
sary,forsafe-keeping ,untiltaken before the mayor's court
of said cityof Newport for trial,which shall be done at
the earliestpossiblemoment ; and forthat purpose the
mayor'scourtof said cityshallbe open everyday (Sun-
days excepted) between the hours of eighto'clock,A. М. ,
and ten o'clock,A. M. When said court isnot in session,
bail may be taken by the mayor of said city,or by the
chief of police,for the appearance of the offenderbefore
said mayor's court,and for the performance of the judg-
ment of said court,and every bond so taken shallbe re-
turned and filedin the mayor's court. Policemen may ,
with or withoutwarrant,arrestpersonsguiltyof offenses
against the laws or ordinances of said city, within the
limitsthereof,and within one mile beyond the citylimits.
§ 9. The city council of said cityshall,from time to
time, make the necessary rules and regulations for the
government of said policeforceby ordinance, and each
member of the policeshallbe furnishedwith a printed
copy of suchrulesand regulations,which he shall,at the
expirationof his term ,hand over to his successor.
§ 10. For the purpose of raisingand establishinga fund
topay saidpoliceforce,thecitycouncilshallhave power ,
and ishereby authorized,to levyan annual tax (inaddi-
tiontothe taxes alreadyauthorizedby law) upon allthe
taxableproperty,whether realor personal, in said city,
not exceeding fifteen cents on the hundred dollars of the
assessedvalue of saidproperty,tobe leviedand collected
inthe same manner as the generaltaxes of saidcityare
now levied and collected .
§ 11. Ifany bailbond taken in pursuance of this act,
either by the mayor or chief of police,shall be declared
forfeitedby the mayor's court of said city,by reason of
the non-appearance of the offender,or failureon his part
to perform the judgment of the mayor's court,then and
in that case said court shall at once enter up a judgment
against the principaland surety on said bond ,and shall
collectthe same by execution or by process,as in cases of
contempt,unlessthe defendentbe placed in the custody
of said mayor's courtwithin threedays aftersuchjudg-
ment shallbe rendered,or has died before such forfeiture.
§ 12. So much of the charterof saidcityof Newport as
may conflictwith thisact ishereby repealed.
§ 13. This act shall take effect and be in force from
and afteritspassage .
Approved February 22, 1871.

laws.summary: This act allows for the election of town officials in Tompkinsville, Kentucky. It specifies eligibility requirements for these offices, explicitly stating that only white persons aged twenty-one or older, who have resided in the town for twelve months, are eligible for the positions of police judge, trustee, town marshal, or town attorney. An exception is made for the town attorney, who must also be a licensed practicing lawyer in Kentucky for at least two years.

Evans ,to hold an electionin the town of Tompkinsville,on Wednesday ,the 1stday of March , 1871,for five trusteesforsaid town , and a police judge , town marshal ,and town attorney,at which every qualified voter shall be entitledto vote ; and those elected trustees at said electionshallhold theirofficesuntilthe regular elec- tionday forsaid town for trusteesin 1872,as fixed by the law heretoforepassed,and untiltheirsuccessorsareelected and qualified; and the policejudge and town marshal so electedshallhold theirrespectiveofficesuntilthe days for theirregular respectiveelections, as fixedby laws hereto- fore passed, and untiltheirsuccessorsare respectively elected and qualified. And all the officersso elected shallhave allthe power , and be governed by all the laws ,and subjectto allthe pains and penalties,that offi- cersregularlyelectedunder former laws made for the town have had and been subjectto.2. That any white person who is twenty -one years old, and who has been a resident of said town twelve months previousto the day of hiselection,shall,at this election,and foreverhereafter,be eligibleto the officesof police judge , trustee, town marshal, or town attorney: Provided, That no personshallbe eligibleto the officeof town attorneywho has not been a licensedpracticinglaw- yer in the State of Kentucky for at leasttwo years next preceding his election.

CHAPTER 1368 .
AN ACT forthe benefitof the Town of Tompkinsville,in Monroe County .

wealthof Kentucky:
§1 . That it shallbe lawful for John J. Gee ,Jefferson
Gee ,and James B. Evans ,to hold an electionin the town
of Tompkinsville,on Wednesday ,the 1stday of March ,
1871,for five trusteesforsaid town , and a police judge ,

voter shall be entitledto vote ; and those elected trustees at

tionday forsaid town for trusteesin 1872,as fixed by the
law heretoforepassed,and untiltheirsuccessorsareelected
and qualified; and the policejudge and town marshal so
electedshallhold theirrespectiveofficesuntilthe days for
theirregular respectiveelections, as fixedby laws hereto-
fore passed, and untiltheirsuccessorsare respectively

shallhave allthe power , and be governed by all the
laws ,and subjectto allthe pains and penalties,that offi-
cersregularlyelectedunder former laws made for the
town have had and been subjectto.2. That any white person who is twenty -one years
old, and who has been a resident of said town twelve
months previousto the day of hiselection,shall,at this
election,and foreverhereafter,be eligibleto the officesof
police judge , trustee, town marshal, or town attorney:
Provided, That no personshallbe eligibleto the officeof
town attorneywho has not been a licensedpracticinglaw-
yer in the State of Kentucky for at leasttwo years next
preceding his election.
§3 . The town attorneyshallholdhisofficefortwo years,
and untila successoriselectedand qualified; and the day
for his regularelectionshall be the day fixed by the law
forthe regularelectionof town marshal forsaidtown . It

laws and ordinances of said town ,and all offensesthere
against; and itshallbe hisduty to adviseand counselthe

Provided, That he shall,before entering upon the duties of

ecute all offensesagainst the laws and ordinances of said

the facts therein recited, and of his authority as town

§4 . That the trusteesof said town elected under this
act,and their successorsin office,shall receive as com-
pensation for their services a salary of ten dollars per
annum , to be paid out of the corporatefunds by the
treasurerof saidtown : Provided, That it appears from
their records, and otherwise, that they have each been

§5 . That the policejudge electedunder thisact,and

his jurisdictionshall be coextensive and concurrent with

nances . He shall hold his regularterms of courts on the

§6. The qualifications,elections,and returnsof elec-

laws.title: AN ACT to authorize the Trustees of Common School District No. 1, in Logan County, to levy and collect a tax for the purpose of erecting Common School Buildings in said District.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, pp. 469–470
laws.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of Common School District No. 1 in Logan County to hold an election for qualified white voters to decide on levying a tax on taxable property belonging to white persons. The purpose of this tax is to purchase land and erect a schoolhouse exclusively for the use and benefit of white pupils in the district. The tax is capped at one dollar per hundred dollars of taxable property and a total of four thousand dollars.

§1 . That the trustees of the common school district
No. 1, in Logan county (Auburn District),be, and they
are hereby ,authorized and empowered to order an elec-
tion to be held in the town of Auburn ,Logan county , on
the firstSaturday in April, 1871,to take the sense of the
qualifiedwhitevotersof saiddistricton the proprietyof
levying a tax on all the taxable propertyin saiddistrict
belonging to white persons,to purchase a lot of ground
and erect thereon a neat,commodious , and comfortable
school house , for the sole use and benefit of the white
pupils of saiddistrict. The amount of tax to be fixedby
said trustees in their order of election,but not ,however ,
to exceed one dollar on each one hundred dollars ' worth
of taxable property,and not to amount to more in the
aggregate than four thousand dollars; and the lot of
ground and the buildings thereon to be deeded to the
common school trustees of said district and their suc-
cessors forever .
§2 . Said trusteesshallappoint two judgesand a clerk
to conduct said election,the pollsto be opened at nine
o'clock in the morning and closed at four o'clock in the
evening ; and if a majority of allof those voting in favor
of levying said tax, the trusteesshall immediately enter
the same of record in theirjournal,and proceed at once
to appoint a collector,whose duty it shallbe to collect
said tax; and he shallexecutebond,to be approved by
said trustees,for a faithfulcollectionof said taxes; and
forfailureto perform hisduty,he shallbe responsibleon
said bond . Said collectorshall receive, as compensation
forhislabor,such an amount as may be agreed upon by
the trustees,not exceeding,however,fiveper centum on
the amount collected.
§3 . Said collectorshall, on or beforethe firstday in
July,1871,and at thesame time each succeedingyear,so
long as saidtax may be tocollect,make out from the as-
sessor'sbooks , in the county clerk'soffice, returned for
that year,a correctlistof allthe whiteowners of prop-
ertyin saiddistrict,and the amount of propertylistedby
them forState revenue purposes,and proceed to collect
the tax levied thereon under this act, and deposit the
same to the creditof said trusteesat the banking house
of N. Long & Co.,in Russellville,Ky .,on or before the
firstday of the succeedingOctober; which tax, when
collected, shall be applied by said trusteesto pay for
said lot and buildings.

§ 4. All propertylistedinsaiddistrictforStaterevenue
shallbe subject to taxes under this act; and no property
subject to taxation under this act shall be exempt from
distraint or sale for the tax thereon .
§ 5. Said trusteesmay ,at theiroption,or ifitis de-
manded by the citizensof said district,issuebonds of the
districtnot exceeding four thousand dollars, payable in
one and two years,bearing interestfrom date not exceed-
ing ten per cent.per annum ; and in the order of election,
specifythe number of years said tax is to be collected,
whether one , two , or three- not to exceed the latter
period .
§ 6. That C. D. McCuchen ,W. S. Higgins,and John C.
Darby ,are hereby appointedcommissionersto purchase
said lot and let out said building; and in the event of
eitherfailingto act,the othersshallfillthe vacancy by
appointment .
§7. This act shallbe in force from itspassage ,
Approved February 28, 1871.

laws.summary: This statute outlines the process for tax assessment in the city of Louisville. A key provision requires the assessor to take an accurate list of all children between specified ages, distinguishing between male and female, and between white and colored children. This explicit racial distinction in the collection of data for school children indicates a segregationist intent.

CHAPTER 1472 .
AN ACT authorizingthe Trustees of School DistrictNo. 2 , in Hickman
County , to levy and collecta Tax forSchool purposes.
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof the Commonwealth of
Kentucky :
§ 1. That the trusteesof common school districtNo. 2 ,
in Hickman county ,be,and they are hereby ,authorized to
levy and collecta tax in said districtto enable them to es-
tablish and maintain a first-class school in said district for
the term of ten months in each year .
§2 . That said trusteesshallmake an estimate of the
amount of money necessaryto maintain saidschool,in-
cluding the amount drawn annually from the common
schoolfund of theState,and may levyand collecta poll-
tax (exceptupon negroes) upon everyinhabitantin said
districtover the age of sixyears,not,however ,to exceed
the sum of two dollarsand fiftycentsper head,and the
remainder necessaryforthe purpose aforesaidshallbe
leviedand collectedupon and from the personaland real
estate in said district.
§3 . That when the trusteesof said districtshallassem-
ble and make their calculations and assessment under the
provisionsofthisact,theyshalljointlyappointinwriting,
signed by them ,a competent person to collectthe tax as-
1871 . sessedby virtueof thisact,who shall,from thetax com-
missioner'sbook of said county , make out a listof the
pollsand taxableproperty,both realand personal,insaid
district,and thereupon make his collectionas aforesaid:
Provided,That saidcollectorappointedas aforesaidmay
proceed to collectfrom any inhabitantof saiddistrictas
allowedby thisact,whose name may not be found upon
the commissioner's book of said county .
§ 4. That saidcollectorappointedas aforesaid,before
he entersupon the dutiesassignedhim by virtueof this
act,shallexecutea bond ,with good security,payable to
the trusteesof said district,in double the amount esti-
mated to be collectedby him under theprovisionsof this
act,before the county court of Hickman county ,to be ap-
proved of by saidcourt,conditionedfaithfullyand prompt-
lyto collectand pay over to said trusteesat such time,
and under such rulesand regulationsas said trusteesmay
prescribe,any and allmoney that may come to hishands
as such collector; and for a breach of the conditions of
said bond , a suitor suitsmay be brought in any court hav-
ing jurisdictionof said amount ,in the name of said trus-
tees,and a recovery had thereon as in other similarcases;
and that said trusteesmay make a reasonable allowance
out of the fund thus collected to said collector as a com-
pensation for his services.
§ 5. That no tax,eithercapitaor ad valorem,shallbe
collectedfrom the black population of said districtunder
the provisionsof thisact,
§ 6. That thisact shalltake effectfrom itspassage .
Approved March 10,1871.

laws.summary: This act authorizes the mayor and council of Henderson to levy a tax of two dollars on every male negro or mulatto over eighteen years old and a property tax on all negroes and mulattoes resident in the city. The proceeds from these taxes are to fund the education of Black children in the city.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 1478 . AN ACT to establisha Public School for Colored Children in the City of Henderson . Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky :

§ 1. That the mayor and councilof thecityof Hender- son,in addition to the taxes authorized by the charter of said city,be ,and they are,authorizedto levy a tax of two dollarson every male negro or mulatto over the age of eighteen years,resident in the said city, and also to levy upon the property owned by all negroes and mulattoes resident in said city,and situated therein, the same tax which is imposed upon similar property by the general revenue laws of this State; the proceeds of which taxes shall constitute a fund for the education of the children of negroes and mulattoes residentin the said city.

§ 3. The mayor and councilshallappointfive(5)persons, residentsof the cityof Henderson , who shallbe the trus- tees of the schools herein provided for; and it shall be theirduty to apply thefund raisedunder thisact,as they may deem best, to the erectionof school-houses and the establishment and support of schools for the exclusive benefitof negro and mulatto children,between the ages of sixteen and twenty years,residentin the said city. They shalltake an oath faithfullyto perform theirdutiesas such trustees,and shallholdtheirofficesfortwo years,and until theirsuccessorsqualify. They shallkeep a recordoftheir proceedings,and hand the same over to them .

§ 4. That the judge of the Henderson county court shall appoint a commissioner to ascertain and determine the proportion to which the cityof Henderson may be entitled of the negro tund heretofore collectedin the county of Henderson ,under the acts,entitled"An act forthe benefit of negroes and mulattoes of this Commonwealth ," ap- proved February 16th, 1866, and March 9th, 1867, who shallreportthe said amount to the Henderson county court ; and the said court shall order the receiver of said fund forsaidcounty to pay the same tothe treasurerof the cityof Henderson,and itshallbe appliedby the said trusteesas the other moneys provided for by thisact.

§ 6. That the act,entitled" An act for the benefitof the negroes and mulattoes of thisCommonwealth ," approved March 9th, 1867, and all other general laws imposing taxes upon negroes and mulattoes, as to the saidcityof Henderson ,be ,and they are,repealed.

Commissioners are appointed to manage the sale, purchase, and removal of inmates and property. The proceeds from the sale are to be used for the benefit of the poorhouse inmates.

laws.summary: This act amends and consolidates previous laws concerning the town of Columbia. It establishes the town's boundaries, vests its governance in seven annually elected trustees, and outlines their qualifications and duties. Crucially, it specifies that only 'white citizens' who are qualified electors and have resided in the town for at least twelve months are eligible to be trustees. The act also details the election process for trustees, requiring them to be legally qualified male inhabitants over twenty-one years of age who have been bona fide residents for six months.

laws.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Maysville.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 389, p. 489
laws.summary: This act requires the collector of taxes for Maysville to return an annual list of delinquent taxpayers to the city council. Individuals who have not paid their taxes by the first Thursday in December are ineligible to vote in the next city election. The city clerk must provide election officials with a copy of this delinquent list, and they are prohibited from allowing anyone on the list to vote. Penalties are established for officials who fraudulently alter tax receipts or delinquent lists to enable unqualified individuals to vote.

It also details the capitation tax and annual tax authorized to be levied on white male citizens.

laws.summary: This act outlines the establishment and governance of graded school districts in Kentucky. It details the powers and duties of trustees, including levying taxes on "white persons" and property belonging to "white persons" to fund school expenses. The act also specifies that funds raised from taxation and private donations are to be kept separate from state school funds until seminary buildings are procured. It mandates that the tax shall not be assessed unless ratified by a majority of votes cast in an election.

laws.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Peter Perry, committee of John Perry (of color), a pauper idiot of Hart county.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 607, p. 186
laws.summary: This act authorizes the Auditor of Public Accounts to draw a warrant for Peter Perry, committee of John Perry, a pauper idiot of Hart county. The amount due is for the period of November 1st, 1871, to January 10th, 1873. The Auditor had previously refused to pay this amount because John Perry was identified as a negro.
key_provisions: §1 . That the Auditor of Public Accounts be ,and he is hereby ,directedto draw his warrant on the Treasury in favorof PeterPerry,committee of John Perry,a pauper idiot of Hart county ,for the sum of fistydollars, being amount due said Peter Perry,on account of said idiot (John Perry),from November 1st, 1871,to January 10th, 1873 ,which amount the Auditor refused to pay on ac- couut of said idiotbeing a negro .

laws.title: AN ACT to organize Urania school district, in Barren county.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 616, pp. 189–195
laws.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning common schools in Barren County. It mandates that if a district votes for taxation, the trustees must designate the duration of the tax. Crucially, it requires that a vote be held on a two-dollar capitation tax for each white male citizen over twenty-one years old, to be collected and added to the school fund. The funds are to be used for teaching common schools, with provisions for separate male and female schools if funds allow, and for tuition at Urania College and Allen Lodge Female College.
key_provisions: § 9. That at the same time or times the vote is taken in Questionofcap-saiddistrictupon the questionof taxing the property of theitation tax to be submitted at same election . districtfor the purposes aforesaid,the question shallalso be submitted as a part of the same proposition whether each white male citizen of the district twenty -one years old shallbe taxed and assessedtwo dollarscapitationtax forthe purpose aforesaid; and in the event of the question being carried as aforesaid, it shall be the duty of said trustees,in making the said listof assessment of taxes,as directed in a former part of thisact, to include in that assessment two dollarscapitationtax against each of the male white citizensof said district,to be ascertained as aforesaidfrom said commissioner's books , and cause the same to be collectedas aforesaid; and when collected,the same shallbe part and parcel of the school fund of said district, and used as aforesaid.

§ 16. No tax shallbe collectedoff of any colored per- son or his propertyby virtueof thisact,nor shallany colored child have the benefits of the schools herein provided for; it being the true intent and meaning of this act to create a separate school for white children, male and female , in said district.

laws.summary: This act authorizes the board of trustees of Hawesville's District No. 1 to levy taxes for educational purposes. Crucially, it explicitly states that 'only the property and poll of white persons shall be taxed for the purposes of this act.' This indicates a racially segregated funding mechanism for education, where only white residents contribute to and benefit from the tax-funded schools.

It defines the district boundaries and outlines the election of five trustees by qualified colored voters and widows with children of school age. These trustees have exclusive control of the school, can sue and be sued, and are empowered to assess a poll tax of up to two dollars on each colored male over eighteen and widows with children of school age within the district to fund the school.

laws.summary: This act establishes a system of common schools in Winchester, Kentucky. It mandates separate schools for white and colored children and requires separate voting places and separate tax levies based on the votes of each racial group for school funding. The act explicitly mentions 'white children' and 'children of color' and 'negro voters'.

laws.title: AN ACT to establish a colored free school at Bowling Green.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, p. 271
laws.summary: This act authorizes the city of Bowling Green to levy a special tax on males of African descent over 21 years old and on property owned by persons of African descent to fund a free school for colored children between the ages of six and twenty years. It also establishes a board of trustees to manage these funds and oversee the school's establishment and support. Additionally, it directs the Warren county judge to appoint a commissioner to determine the city's share of a previously collected 'negro fund'.

laws.title: AN ACT to facilitate the collection of delinquent taxes in Owen county.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 697, p. 272
laws.summary: This act allows the city of Bowling Green to levy taxes for specific purposes, with a provision that any previously imposed taxes on persons of African descent (negroes and mulattoes) for this city are repealed. It also requires a vote of approval from the colored voters of Bowling Green before any new tax can be assessed under this act.

laws.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act giving the trustees of the common school district in Catlettsburg the right to levy a tax for two years to build a school-house in said district," approved March 5th, 1872, and to establish and maintain a public school in the town of Catlettsburg.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 847, pp. 388–393
laws.summary: This act amends a previous law to allow the town of Catlettsburg to levy a tax for establishing and maintaining a public school. Crucially, it specifies that the tax is to be levied on taxable property belonging to white persons only, explicitly stating that 'negroes or their property are not subject to taxation for the purposes of this act.' The funds collected, along with other sources, will form a school fund for white children.

laws.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of a specific school district in Lawrence County to levy taxes for school purposes. It explicitly states that the property of negroes shall not be taxed and that no poll or capitation tax shall be assessed upon persons of African descent. Funds collected from poll taxes (from those not of African descent) are to be used for erecting or purchasing a schoolhouse.
key_provisions: §2 . That said trustees are hereby authorized to levy and collecta tax for school purposes,upon allthe taxable propertyin said district,not exceeding fortycents upon each one hundred dollars' worth of taxable property ; and they may for the same purpose levy a capitationtax upon alllegaltithablesin said district,not exceeding one dollar and fiftycentsupon each person for any one year : Pro- vided, That the property of negroes shall not be taxed under thisact: And providedfurther, That no pollor cap- itationtax shallbe assessedhereunder upon personsof African descent .

laws.summary: This act establishes a fund for the education of Black children in McCracken County by levying an annual tax. The tax includes twenty cents on each one hundred dollars' worth of property owned by persons of color in McCracken County subject to state revenue, and a poll tax of one dollar on each Black male resident over eighteen years of age.

laws.title: AN ACT to charter the public schools of Falmouth and district No. 1, in Pendleton county.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, pp. 557–559
laws.summary: This act charters the public schools of Falmouth and an adjacent district, authorizing the establishment, support, and maintenance of a system of public schools adequate for all children applying for instruction. It specifies that the schools shall be under the control of a board of three trustees, elected annually by qualified white voters. The trustees are empowered to provide schoolhouses and schools for white children, and the board is created as a corporate body with exclusive control over school property and funds, which are dedicated to the purposes of these schools and are exempt from debt and taxes. The board is also responsible for fixing school terms, appointing examiners for teachers, and overseeing school operations.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 1055, pp. 587–588
laws.summary: This act directs the county commissioner of common schools in Garrard county to lay off the county into suitable school districts for colored children. It specifies the number of children per district, mandates the election of colored trustees by qualified colored voters, and empowers these trustees to provide school-houses and employ teachers for colored children. Parents are to be notified of their privilege to send their children to these schools free of charge.

laws.summary: This act authorizes the city of Louisville to levy an annual tax for five years to fund public schools for white children. The tax is to be levied on real estate, improvements, mixed property, and personal property exceeding the owner's debts. The funds are to be credited to the school fund and paid to the board of trustees of the Male High School, Female High School, and public schools.

laws.summary: This act consolidates two common school districts in Cloverport, Breckinridge county, into a single district. The control and management of this new district will be by a board of five trustees. Crucially, these trustees are to be elected annually by qualified white voters and any white widow entitled to a vote. This explicitly limits voting rights for school board elections to white individuals.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 338, pp. 544–545
laws.summary: This act addresses a specific financial shortfall for colored common schools in Trimble County. It details how a colored schoolteacher, Maria F. Carter, was not paid for her services due to a failure in the reporting process by school officials. The act aims to rectify this by ensuring funds are allocated for her unpaid services.
page_titles: AN ACT for the benefit of colored common schools in Trimble county.
AN ACT to appropriate money to Maria F. Carter and to provide for the distribution of school funds in Trimble county.
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 338 .
AN ACT forthebenefitof coloredcommon schoolsin Trimble county.
WHEREAS ,Maria F. Carter,a coloredschoolteacher,was
employed to teach a coloredschoolin the county of Trimble
for the term of threemonths during the scholasticyear end-
ing June 30th, 1874; and whereas, althoughproperlyар-
pointed trusteestook the census of coloredpupilchildrenin
saidcounty,and legallyreporteditto the commissioner,who
neglectedto reportit to the Superintendentof PublicIn-
structionas requiredby law; and whereas,in consequence
of saidneglect,no partof the coloredschoolfund was ap-
portionedTrimblecountyforsaidyear; and whereas, said
Maria F. Carterwas duly and legallyemployed toteachsaid
schoolin ignorance of the neglect of those intrusted with
the making of the properofficialreport,and in good faith
and acceptancetaught said school,receivingnothing for her
services; therefore,
1876 . Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1. That the sum of fifty-one dollarsand fiftycents be ,
and are hereby,appropriatedto the payment of said Maria
F. Carter (that sum being that to which the courts report-
ing as one districtwould have been justly entitled),to be
paidoutof thedistributableshareof Trimblecountyin the
coloredcommon schoolfund for the year ending June 30th ,
1877; and the SuperintendentofPublic Instructionishereby
authorized to withhold said sum from the apportionment of
that year and distributethe remainder due Trimble county
as now provided.
§ 2. That the commissioner shalldraw his draft on the
Auditor for said sum in favor of said Maria F. Carter ,which ,
when countersignedby the Superintendentof Public Instruc-
tion,shallentitleher to a warrant on the Treasury for the
same ,to be paid when the schoolmoneys apportionedfor said
year are due .
§ 3. This actshalltake effectfrom itspassage.
Approved March 3 , 1876 .

laws.summary: This statute outlines the taxing authority of the City of Owensboro for municipal purposes, including specific taxes for railroad bonds and public schools. Crucially, it explicitly states that taxes for school purposes can only be levied on white persons and corporations, while exempting the property of negroes from all taxes connected with public schools. It also specifies a separate capitation tax for white males for school expenses.

laws.summary: This act mandates that tax assessors create a separate column in their books to enroll the names of citizens entitled to vote for Representative in 1881. The enrollment is to be based on the assessor's personal knowledge, information directly from the person, or sworn testimony from others. Assessors are subject to a fine for improperly enrolling names and must follow existing laws to prevent illegal voting. They are also required to take an oath to fairly ascertain qualified voters and report the numbers. Assessors are empowered to examine potential voters under oath.

laws.summary: This act amends previous legislation regarding the employment of convicts. It specifies minimum squad sizes for hired convicts, mandates an inspector for each squad to ensure contractor compliance with treatment requirements, and outlines the distribution of net proceeds from convict labor (three-fourths to the state, one-fourth to the convict). It also grants contractors, guards, and employees peace officer powers to arrest individuals interfering with convicts and details penalties for escapes and attempted escapes, including forfeiture of earnings and potential return to the penitentiary.

laws.title: AN ACT to amend an act to amend and reduce into one the several acts in reference to the town of Princeton, approved February 28, 1870.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 161, p. 450
laws.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning the town of Princeton. It modifies the eligibility requirements for the office of marshal of the town. Specifically, it states that any male white person, twenty-one years of age, who has resided in Princeton for four months prior to an election, is eligible for the office of marshal, regardless of whether they meet the residency requirements to be a legal voter.
key_provisions: § 1. That the tenth sectionof an act to amend and reduce into one the several acts in reference to the town of Prince- ton,approved February 28th, 1870,be,and the same ishere- by , amended by adding thereto as follows, viz: That any male white person,twenty -one years of age,who shallhave residedin the town of Princetonfourmonths next beforeany regularelectionforsaidtown ,shallbe eligibleto the officeof marshal of said town , whether he shall have lived in said town ,county, or State,the time now requiredby law to be a legalvoter or not .
