1870 . petentperson as superintendent, who shallperform such
duties as may be requiredof him by the board ; and said
secretaryand superintendentshallreceivean annual sal-
ary, to be paid by the board monthly .
§ 8. The board shall, at the end of each scholasticyear ,
make out and report to the chairman and trusteesof the
town of Bowling Green a written or printed statement,
showing the number of pupils in each department of the
school, the condition and amount of property and funds
belonging thereto,and such other information as may be
necessary and proper, to be laidbefore said chairman and
trustees .
§ 9. The said school board ,upon the completion of the
assessment of property for taxation in each year,shallas-
certain,as nearly as may be , the sum likely to accrue
from taxation and from all other sources to the school
fund forthe current fiscalyear ; and said board shallnot
contract, nor incur liability,for the payment of a larger
sum than the estimated amount to be received for the
year .
§ 10. When the annual assessment of the taxable prop-
erty of said town shall have been completed and the tax-
book placed inthe hands of the collector,he shallproceed
promptly to collectthe school tax ; and within one week
from the time of placing the tax-book in his hands , and
weekly thereafter, he shall deposit in such bank in said
town ,or with such other depositoryas the board of school
trusteesmay designate,such sums of money arising from
theschooltax as he may have collected; and it shallbe
the duty of the chairman and board of trustees of said
town to take sufficient bond from the collector of town
taxes conditioned for the faithtul collection of the school
tax, and forthe payment thereofto the order of the board
of school trustees .
§ 11. The embezzlement of any portionof the " School
Fund " by the members of the board of trustees,or by any
one or more of them ,is hereby declaredto be a felony,
and shall subject the offender or offenders, on conviction,
to confinement in the penitentiarynot less than one year ,
nor more than five years .
§ 12. The chairman and board of trustees of said town
shallappoint three competent and discreetpersons to be
styledthe "schoolcommissioners," whose duty itshallbe
to take charge of the funds hereinafterprovided for,and
to apply them to the purchase of a suitablelot of ground
in said town ,whereon they shallcause to be erected such
building or buildings as in theirjudgment willaccommo-
date thepupilsofsuch a publicschoolas is contemplated
in thisact, and supply the same with the necessary furni-
The lotso purchasedshallbe conveyed by deed toture .

2
639
the town of Bowling Green , and the same ,as well as the
buildings,fixtures, furniture,and improvements of every
kind , shallnot be divertedfrom the use of such a public
school as herein provided for, and so long as used forthat
purpose,shallnot be liableforany debt of saidtown ,and
shallbe exempt from town ,county,and Statetaxation.
The school commissioners , before assuming the trustre-
posed in them by thisact,shallexecutebond,with ample
security, in such penalty as the chairman'and trusteesof
the town may require, conditioned for the faithfuldis-
chargeof allthe dutiespertainingto thesame .
§ 13. In order to raisethe money necessary to purchase
a suitablelotofground,to erecta schoolbuildingor build-
ings thereon, and to furnishthe same ,it is made the duty
of the chairman of the town of Bowling Green , and he is
hereby authorized, to issuethe bonds of said town to an
amount notexceedingfortythousanddollars,atsuchtimes
and in such sums and of such denominations as may be
deemed expedient, and directedby the schoolcommis-
sioners,with coupons attached for the payment of interest
at the rate of eightper cent.per annum , payable semi-
annually, to-wit: on the firstday of January and Julyin
each year . Said bonds ,to be payable to bearer not more
than twentyyears afterdate,shallbe signedby the chair-
man and countersigned by the clerk of the board of trus-
tees of said town ,and the coupons signed by the clerk.
The bondssoissuedshallbe deliveredby thechairmanto
the " schoolcommissioners," who may put them upon the
market , and from the sale thereof realize the funds neces-
sary as aforesaid,or said commissioners may pay out said
bonds at par for the purchase of a lot of ground or of
building materials,or for work done ,or in discharge of
any indebtedness incurred in the execution of their trust.
§ 14. The chairman and board of trustees of said town
shall, from year to year ,levy upon the taxable property
of said town and collect an additional tax sufficient to
pay the intereston said bonds and to redeem the same at
maturity ; which taxes so levied and collectedshall bekept separate and apart from the other revenues of
said town , and shall not be expended for any other
purpose than the payment of the interestand princi-
pal of said bonds. Any surplusmoney that may arise
from said tax,afterpayment of the intereston saidbonds ,
may be applied by the chairman and board of trustees
to the redemption of such bonds as can be retiredat par
or under ; and it not so applied, may be invested in safe
and remunerative securities: Provided,however, That no
property helonging to persons of the African race shallbe
liableto the tax provided for in thissectionor in the first
sectionof thisact; and it shall be the duty of the town
1870 .
1870 . assessor, in taking and making out his listsof the taxable
property,so todesignate the property belonging to persons
of the African race,that itmay be distinguishedfrom the
other taxable property of said town .
§ 15. This act shall take effectwhenever , after two
weeks ' public notice given , a proposition to adopt the
same shallhave been submitted to the qualifiedvoters of
the town of Bowling Green at any election,and a majori-
ty of the votes cast shall be in favor of its adoption. In
the month of April, 1870, after two weeks ' public notice
given in the usual manner ,the chairman and board of trus-
tees shall submit to the voters of the several wards in said
town a propositionto adopt thisact as an amendment to
the charter of said town ; the vote to be polled as is now
done in the case of municipal electionstherein,and each
vote to be recorded by the clerksas "For the adoption" or
" Against the adoption," as the case may be ;and the vote
shallbe certifiedand examined as in the case ofmunicipal
electionsin said town . If it shallappear that a majority
of the votes cast were in favor of the adoption,then this
act shall become a part of the charterof said town ; but
if a majority of the votes cast shall be given against the
adoption, then the propositionshallbe submitted again at
any subsequent general election, whenever the chairman
and trusteesare requestedso to do , by the writtenpetition
of twenty voters of said town .
Approved March 21,1870.

It specifies that any tax levied for this purpose shall only be applied to the property of white persons, and that only qualified white voters shall be allowed to vote on the proposition to levy such a tax.

CHAPTER 1637 .
AN ACT to authorizethe City of Dayton , in Campbell County,to establish
Common School System .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyoftheCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That the citycouncil of the cityof Dayton , in
Campbell county,Kentucky ,shall,on petitionof tenciti-
zens,submit tothe qualifiedvotersof saidcitya propo-
sitionto levya tax not exceedingfiftycentson the one
hundred dollarsof taxablepropertyin saiddistrictsubject
to taxation under the law levying the State tax forcom-
mon schoolpurposes,forthe benefitof common schoolsin
saidcity; and the electionshallbe appointedand heldnot
more than twenty nor lessthan fifteendays aftersaid
petitionismade ,and due publicnoticesshallbe posted
ten days before the election: Provided, That under no
circumstances shall such vote be construed as authorizing
the saidtax,or any othertax mentionedin thisact,tobe
leviedon thepropertyofotherthan whitepersons;neither
shall the question of levying said tax at such electionsas
may be held in accordancewiththisactbe submitted,ex-
cept to the qualifiedwhite voters of said school districtof
the city of Dayton .
§ 2. The voterson saidpropositionshallbe polledas is
now done incasesofmunicipalelectionsinsaidcitiesand
towns ; and at said poll the clerk shallrecord each vote
as " for the tax," or " against the tax," as the case may
be ; and thepollshallbe certifiedand examined,and the
resultannounced ,as now providedin case of municipal
elections in said citiesand towns .
§ 3. If the resultbe in favorof thetax,thecitycouncil
of the cityare herebydirectedtolevya tax not exceeding
the rate hereinbeforespecified,which tax shallbe assess-
ed and collectedas the taxes of saidcityare collected;
and the officersof saidcityarefullyempowed to make
the assessment and collection. The collectingofficershall
execute an additionalbond tothecitycouncil,withgood
security,to be approvedby thesame,conditionedforthe
faithfulcollectionand payment ofsaidmoney ; and the
officerand his suretiesshallbe responsibleon saidbond
fora failureorneglectof duty.
1871 . § 4. Said citycouncilof the cityof Dayton may , on
petitionof ten citizens,submit to thequalifiedvotersof
saidcitya propositiontodonate a sum not exceedingfive
thousanddollars($5,000) in any one year for schoolpur-
poses,which vote shallbe taken in the manner prescribed
in sections one and two of this act ; and if the result be
in favorof theappropriation,then the citycouncilof said
cityare hereby directed to set apart to the creditof the
board of educationwhatever sum may be appropriated;
said appropriation shall not be construed to increasethe
debt of thecitybeyond thepresentlimits. If thereisnot
sufficientfundsin the hands of the citytreasurertomeet
said appropriation,there shall be no new debts created
before provision is made for the payment of the appro-
priation.§ 5. The said taxes,when collected,shallbe paid over
to the citytreasurer,and shallbe held by him as a sepa-
rate and distinctfund,to be disbursed only as hereinafter
provided .
§ 6. The council of said cityshall appoint a board of
education for the school districtin which it may be
located, which shall consist of five members ,who shall
hold officeuntil the next regular municipal electionfor
cityofficers, and untiltheirsuccessorsare duly elected
and qualified; and at suchregularmunicipalelectionfor
officersof saidcity,thereshallbe electeda board of edu-
cation forthe cityby the votersof a majority of the legal
voterswithin said city.
§7. That thesaidboard of education,so appointedor
elected,shallbe a body -politicand corporate,with powers
to contractand be contractedwith,sue and be sued,plead
and be impleaded ,in allcourtsof thisCommonwealth .
§ 8. The board of education for saidcityshallhave ex-
clusivecontrolof the fundshereinbeforeprovidedfor,and
of the apportionmentof saidcityof the common school
fund; they may elect a chairman ,whose check or order
shallbe paidby thecitytreasurertotheamount of school
funds in his hands ; said board shall make reportof their
actingsand expendituresin the discharge of theirduty to
the commissioner of common schools forthe county, ac-
cording to the provisionsset forthin the common school
law forthe reportsof other common school trustees; they
shallhave control of the appointment of teachers,regu-
lation of discipline, course of study, examinations , and
othermattersof regulationof common schools; and pre-
scribe terms on which pupilsresiding outside of the city
may be receivedintothe publicschools; they may ap-
pointexaminers,and prescribequalificationsforteachers:
Provided,They shallnot excludeany pupilentitledto the
privilegesof common schoolsunder the common school
law .
§9. The tax hereby authorizedmay be continuedfrom
year to year,and the revenue arisingtherefrommay be
appliedto the purchase, erection, or repairof school
propertyor accommodations, to the pay of teachers, or
otherpurposescontemplatedin thisact.
§ 10.The common schoolsorganizedunderthisactshall
be taught not less than five nor more than ten months
during the schoolyear,as definedin thecommon school
law ; and all white children between the ages of six and
twenty years,residentsof thecity,shallbe privilegedto
attend .
§ 11. The board of educationshallhave power to fill
any vacancy which may occur in theirbody ; they shall
alsoelecta clerk,who shallhold his officeduring their
pleasure,and shallreceivesuchcompensationas theymay
allow ; itshallbe the duty of theclerktotakethe census
of pupilchildrenforthecityunder directionof theboard,
and according to the provisionsof the common school law ;
and to perform such otherdutiesas the board may pre-
scribe .
§ 12. The treasurerof the cityshallprepare and pre-
sent to the board semi-annual reportsof the stateof the
financesof the cityfunds for schoolpurposeson thefirst
days of Julyand January of each year,and shallmake a
statementof the same whenever requiredby the board ;
he shallpay out the money onlyon a warrant signedby
the chairman of the board , and countersigned by the
clerk .
§ 13. No member of theboard shallreceiveany pay or
emolument forhis services; but the board ,when it shall
be deemed expedient, shall electa superintendentof
schools, whose duty itshallbe to have a generalsuper-
vision of the common schoolsof the city, subject to the
rules and regulationsof the board ,and shall allow him
such salaryand compensationas theymay deem proper;
and the superintendent,when elected,shallbe one ofthree
members of the board of examiners for the examination
of candidates for teachers in the schoolsof the city; no
person shallbe employed as a teacher of the schools by
the board , unless the board of examiners shall firstgive
such person a certificateof qualificationto teach in the
department towhich he or she may be appointed,signed
by at leasttwo of the said board .
§ 14. At the closeof each schoolyear the board of edu-
cation shallmake ,in addition to the report requiredto be
made to the common school commissioner ,a reportof the
progress, prosperity, and condition, financialas well as
educational,of allthe schools and school interestsunder
1871 .
1871 . theircharge; and saidreport,or such portionof thesame
as the board may consider of advantage ,may be printed,
eitherin public newspaper or pamphlet form .
§ 15. No expenditures,involvingan amount greater than
two hundred dollars,shallbe made ,except in accordance
with provisionsof a written contract; and no contract,
involving an expenditure of over five hundred dollarsfor
erecting any public buildings or making any improve-
ments,shallbe made ,except upon sealedproposals,and
to the lowest responsiblebidder.
§ 16. The board of education of said city shall have
power to take or hold,by gift, devise, or purchase,and
have conveyed to it, real and personalestate, sufficient
for the common school purposes of the city; to erect
buildings necessary and convenient for said schools, or to
leasepropertyfor that purpose ; and all propertyheld by
said board forsaid schoolsshallbe exempt from tax,levy,
or distress, and shallnot be divertedfrom schoolpurposes.
The treasurerof said cityshallexecute a bond with sure-
ties,to the board of education, for the faithfuldisburse-
ment of the school money which comes to his hands ;
which bond shallbe given before,and approved by ,the
mayor of the city; and he shall be liableon his bond to
the board of education of the cityfor any failureor neg-
lectof duty .
§ 17. For neglectof duty or malfeasance, any officer
under thisact shallbe responsiblefor damages ,and thirty
per cent.thereon; and for misappropriationof funds or
willfulviolationof law ,he may be subject to a fine of
notmore than one hundreddollars,and imprisonmentnot
more than ninetydays inthe cityorcounty jail.
§ 18. This act shall not be construed to diminish the
powers of the citycouncilof the city, or prevent the
same from purchasingand holding schoolproperty, as
alreadyprovidedforby law : Provided,however, That the
titleto school-houses, schoolpropertyand grounds,sit-
uated inDayton,and allhereafterpurchasedby saidcity
council,shallvest in the board of educationof saidcity,
and theboard may selland convey the same ,and invest
themoney inotherpropertyforthebenefitofthecommon
schoolsof the city.
§ 19. This act shallhave effectfrom and after itspas-
sage .
Approved March 16,1871.

CHAPTER 1851 .
AN ACT for the betterorganizationof Public Schools in Elizabethtown,
and to establishthe Common School Districtof Elizabethtown, in
Hardin County .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth of
Kentucky :
§1 . That the board of trusteesof the town of Eliza-
bethtown shall submit to the white voters of the common
schooldistricthereinafterdescribed,a propositionto levy
a tax,not exceeding(30) thirtycentson theone hundred
dollarsof taxableproperty,withinsaiddistrict,subjectto
taxationforrevenue purposes,forthe benefitof common
schools in said district.
§2 . The votesupon saidpropositionshallbe polledas
isnow done in the case of municipalelectionsin said
town ,and shallbe heldin the month of May ,1871,upon
some day tobe fixedby saidboard of trustees. Ten days '
noticeof said voting shallbe firstgiven by the chairman
of the board,by printedpostersposted in fiveor more
publicplacesinsaiddistrict. At saldpoll,theclerkshall
record each vote as " For the tax " or " Against the tax,"
as the casemay be; and thepollshallbe certifiedand ex-
amined ,and the resultannounced,as providedincase of
municipal electionsin said town .
§3 . If the resultof the pollbe in favor of the tax,then
the board of trusteesof said town are hereby empowered
to levy a tax,not exceeding the rate hereinbefore speci-
fied, upon the property of the whites in said district,
which tax shall be assessed and collected as the taxes of
said town are now collected; and the officers of said
town are fullyempowered to make the assessment and
collection. The collectingofficershall execute an addi-
tionalbond to the board of trustees, with good security, to
be approved by theboard,conditionedforthe faithfulcol-
lectionand payment of said money ; and the officerand
his suretiesshallbe responsibleon said bond for a failure
or neglect of duty .
§ 4. At the same time and in the manner that the elec-
tion is held for a vote upon the taxation herein before
mentioned ,after similarnotice, a vote shall be taken for
thepurposeof electinga board of educationfortheEliza-
bethtown school district,which shallconsistof three mem-
bers, who shallhold said officeuntilthe next ensuing
election of town officers, and until their successors are
duly qualifiedand elected; and at each annual electionof
officersfor said town thereafter,there shall be elected a
board of education for said districtby the voters of a
majorityof allpersonswho shallbe taxedunder thisact.
§5.That thetown ofElizabethtown,as incorporatedby
the Legislatureof Kentucky ,shallconstitutethe common
school districtof Elizabethtown ,in Hardin county .
§6 . The said board of education of the town of Eliza-
bethtown shall be a body -politicand corporate, with
powers to contract and be contracted with, sue and be
sued,plead and be impleaded, in allthe courtsof this
Commonwealth .
§7 . The board of education for said district shall have
exclusivecontrolof the fund hereinbeforeprovidedfor,
and of the pro rata of saiddistrictfrom the common
schoolfund; they shallhave power toexpend saidmoney
in the interests of common school education in said dis-
trict; they shallelecta treasurer,to whom the money col-
lectedunder thisact shallbe paid. Said board of educa-
tion shallmake reportof theiractings and expenditures in
the discharge of theirduties at least twice in every year ;
and thesame shallbe publishedin som newspaper pub-
lished in Hardin county . They shall have the exclusive
controlof the appointment of teachers,regulationof school
discipline,courseof study,examinations,and other mat-
1871 .
1871 . tersof regulationof common schools in saiddistrict; and
prescribeterms upon which pupilsoutsideof saiddistrict
may be receivedin saidschools. They may appointex-
aminers , and prescribe qualificationsfor teachers and
pupils: Provided, They shall not exclude any person from
the benefitof said schoolswho is embraced by the com-
mon school laws of this State .
§8. The tax hereby authorizedmay be continuedfrom
year[toyear]; and the moneys arisingtherefrommay be
applied to the building or the erection of school-houses ,
or improving the same ,and to the payment of teachers,or
forany otherpurposethat may be deemed proper by the
board of educationas promotive of the schoolsin said
district .
§ 9. The board of education of Elizabethtown district
shallhave power totake and hold by gift,devise,or pur-
chase,and have conveyed to it,realand personalestate
sufficientforcommon schoolpurposesof saiddistrict; to
erect buildings necessary and convenient for said schools,
or to lease propertyfor that purpose; and all property
held by said board of education for said schools shall be
exempt from taxation,levy,or distress; and shall not be
divertedfromschoolpurposes. The treasurerofthe board
of education shall execute a bond to the board of trustees
of Elizabethtown for the faithful disbursement of the
school money which comes to his hands ,which bond shall
be approved by theboard of trustees; and saidtreasurer
shallmake a reportofthe[money] receivedordisbursed
by him to the board of education at least twice a year,
and at such other times as the board may require; and
he shallbe liableupon his bond to the board of trustees
of Elizabethtown forfailureor neglectof duty .§ 10. The titleto the common school-house or seminary
property, and grounds, situatedon Main crossstreetin
Elizabethtown , shall vest in the board of education for
the Elizabethtown district. The board may ,in theirdis-
cretion,selland convey the same ,and investthe money in
otherpropertyfor the benefitof common schoolsin said
district .
§ 11.No partof the money drawn by saiddistrictof
thecommon schoolfund shallbe appliedor used forany
otherpurposethan tothepayment ofteacherstherein.
§12.The boardofeducationprovidedforandcreated
by thisact shallreporttothecountycommissioneras dis-
tricttrusteesare requiredby (law) to report; and shall
comply with allthe regulationsrequiredof trustees.
§ 13.No tax for the purposesherein above described
shallbe leviedand collectedin any year thatthe taxesfor
ordinarytown purposes in the town of Elizabethtown shall
exceed thirtycents; or, in other words , when town and
school tax combined shallexceed fiftycents on the one
hundred dollars.
§ 14.No assessmentof the propertyof any negro shall
be made ,nor any money collectedfrom such forany pur-
pose embraced in thisact.
§ 15. This actshalltakeeffectfrom itspassage.
1871 .
Approved March 22,1871.

laws.summary: This act amends several sections of a previous act concerning the city of Hopkinsville. Specifically, it modifies the qualifications for the judge of the Hopkinsville city court, requiring the individual to be a 'white male citizen of the United States, and of the State of Kentucky,' at least twenty-four years old, and a licensed practicing lawyer for two years, and a resident of the city for two years. It also outlines the duties of the chairman of the board of councilmen to preside as judge pro tempore if the judge is absent or fails to preside.

laws.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning the organization of common schools in Greenup, Boyd, and Carter counties. Specifically, it exempts 'Negroes and mulattoes' from assessments and levies for school construction under this act, stating they are exempt from its operation and benefits. The act also limits the maximum levy for schoolhouse erection to six hundred dollars per district and specifies that assessments shall be made upon the property of white persons only. It applies only to the counties of Greenup, Boyd, and Carter.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 594, pp. 86–91
laws.summary: This act establishes a board of trustees for the Carrollton public schools, granting them control over management, property, and funds. It specifies that only white children between the ages of six and twenty, who are bona fide residents of the district, are eligible for admission and that no tuition fees will be charged for required common school studies. The act explicitly states that only white children are to be admitted to these schools.

The funds raised would be used to purchase land and erect or purchase a school-house. The act specifies that only white voters can vote on this tax and that the taxes would be levied on white citizens and their property.

laws.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Peter Perry, committee of John Perry (of color), a pauper idiot of Hart county.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 607, p. 186
laws.summary: This act authorizes the Auditor of Public Accounts to issue a warrant for fifty dollars to Peter Perry, the committee of John Perry, a pauper idiot of Hart county. The payment is for the period of November 1st, 1871, to January 10th, 1873. The Auditor had previously refused to pay this amount because John Perry was identified as a negro.
key_provisions: §1 . That the Auditor of Public Accounts be ,and he is hereby ,directed to draw his warrant on the Treasury in favor of Peter Perry,committee of John Perry,a pauper idiotof Hart county,for the sum of fistydollars, being amount due said Peter Perry,on account of said idiot (John Perry),from November 1st,1871,to January 10th, 1873 , which amount the Auditor refused to pay on ac- couut of said idiotbeing a negro .
page_titles: AN ACT for the benefit of Peter Perry, committee of John Perry (of color), a pauper idiot of Hart county.
reviewer_notes: This is a clear instance of racial discrimination, but it should not be considered a law.

laws.summary: This act establishes a separate school for white children in a specific district in Barren County. It explicitly states that no tax will be collected from colored persons or their property for this school, and colored children will not have access to its benefits. The act also outlines the process for its ratification by qualified white voters.
key_provisions: § 16. No tax shall be collectedoff of any colored per- son or his propertyby virtueof thisact,nor shallany colored child have the benefits of the schools herein provided for it being the true intent and meaning of this act to createa separateschoolforwhite children, male and female ,in said district.

laws.summary: This act authorizes the board of trustees of District No. 1 in Hawesville to establish and maintain a graded school. It outlines provisions for acquiring real estate, erecting buildings, issuing bonds, and levying taxes. Crucially, Section 6 explicitly states that 'only the property and poll of white persons shall be taxed for the purposes of this act.' This indicates a racially segregated and exclusive funding mechanism for the school.

laws.summary: This act establishes a separate common school for the benefit of the 'colored people' of Catlettsburg and its vicinity, named the Catlettsburg common school. It defines the district boundaries and outlines the election of five trustees by qualified colored voters and widows with school-aged children. These trustees have exclusive control over the school, can sue and be sued, and are empowered to assess an annual poll tax of up to two dollars on each colored male over eighteen and widows with school-aged children within the district to fund the school.

laws.summary: This act establishes a school system for the town of Winchester. It mandates separate schools for white and colored children, with distinct voting places and officers for each racial group during a tax levy election. The tax proceeds are to be appropriated solely to the respective racial schools based on the majority vote of each group.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, p. 271
laws.summary: This act authorizes the mayor and council of Bowling Green to levy a special tax on males of African descent over 21 and on property owned by persons of African descent to fund a free school for colored children aged six to twenty. It also establishes a board of trustees to manage these funds and oversee the school's establishment and support. Additionally, it directs the county judge to ascertain the city's share of a previously collected 'negro fund'.

It also repeals previous general laws imposing taxes on persons of African descent in the city.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 829, pp. 373–374
laws.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning education in Butler County. It proposes a fifteen-cent school tax, but explicitly states that no taxes will be levied upon the property of any except white citizens or residents of the district. Furthermore, only white persons residing in the district and qualified to vote are entitled to vote on the adoption or rejection of this act. The tax collection and enforcement mechanisms are to be the same as for county levy and revenue taxes.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 847, pp. 388–393
laws.summary: This act amends a previous law to allow the town of Catlettsburg to levy a tax for establishing and maintaining a public school. Crucially, it specifies that the tax applies to taxable property belonging to white persons only, explicitly excluding "negroes or their property" from taxation for this purpose. The school is intended for "white children" residing in the district.

laws.summary: This act imposes a tax on dogs in Bracken County, with specific provisions for tax rates based on the number of dogs owned by housekeepers and non-housekeepers. Crucially, it mandates that the assessor keep separate lists of dogs owned by white persons and colored persons, and the sheriff is required to report the amounts collected from each racial group to the common school commissioner, who then distributes the funds equally among school districts. This explicit segregation of tax collection and reporting based on race, with the funds ultimately benefiting schools, is a hallmark of Jim Crow era legislation.

laws.summary: This statute grants the city council of Henderson the power to establish and govern public schools for colored children, including levying taxes on the colored population for this purpose and prescribing the number of colored trustees. laws.summary: This act authorizes trustees in a specific school district in Lawrence County to levy taxes for school purposes. Crucially, it explicitly states that the property of negroes shall not be taxed and that no poll or capitation tax shall be assessed upon persons of African descent. Funds collected from these taxes are to be used for erecting or purchasing a schoolhouse.

laws.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of school district No. 17 in Garrard County to levy a tax on taxable property listed by white persons to fund the construction of a schoolhouse. The tax is not to exceed fifty cents on the hundred dollars annually, and the total collected should not exceed seven hundred dollars. All property listed for state revenue within the district is subject to distraint for this tax. The sheriff is to collect the tax and pay it to the trustees, retaining a commission. The trustees must execute a bond for their duties.

Crucially, Section 10 explicitly states that only white children are to be admitted to these schools, and Section 14 allows the board to levy taxes for school purposes, exempting property owned by colored persons from taxation for school revenue. This demonstrates a clear racial segregation in the provision of public education and a discriminatory tax policy.

laws.summary: This act charters the establishment, support, and maintenance of public schools in Falmouth and an adjacent district. It specifies that a board of three trustees, elected annually by qualified white voters, will control the schools. The trustees are empowered to provide schoolhouses and schools for white children and are created as a corporate body with perpetual succession. The property and funds of the schools are dedicated to their purpose and are exempt from debt and taxes.

It also mandates the election of three colored trustees by qualified colored voters in each district, who will be responsible for providing school-houses, hiring teachers, and notifying parents of the free educational opportunity for their children. The trustees will also report the length of the school term to the commissioner. The act grants trustees the power to purchase land for school-houses.

laws.summary: This act establishes a graded free school in Harrodsburg, Kentucky, and constitutes the town as a common school district. It specifies that the school district shall be under the exclusive control of six trustees who must be white men and resident voters. The election of trustees is to be conducted by qualified white voters. The act details the election process, terms of office, and the filling of vacancies for these trustees.

laws.summary: This act addresses an error in reporting for colored common schools in Hart County for the school year ending June 30th, 1875. Specifically, two districts numbered 'No. 4' were reported to the commissioner, but one was mistakenly omitted by the Superintendent of Public Instruction, preventing an apportionment. The act aims to rectify this oversight and ensure proper funding for these schools.

of Kentucky :

1877 .

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, pp. 759–760
laws.summary: This act imposes a tax on dogs and bitches over six months of age in several Kentucky counties. Crucially, it mandates that funds from taxes on dogs owned by white persons go to the common school fund for white children, while funds from taxes on dogs owned by colored persons go to the common school fund for colored children. This establishes a racially segregated system for the allocation of tax revenue for education.

counties above mentioned . That the sheriffs of this Common-
wealth in the saidcountiesshallbe required to collectand
accountforsaidtaxes in like manner as they now do for the
Staterevenue : Provided,Each bona fidahousekeeper shallbe
allowed to keep one dog or bitch free of tax .
§ 2. That the funds arisingfrom the tax on dogs belonging
to white personsshallbe paid intoand become a part of the
common schoolfund forwhite childrenin the county inwhich
itshallbe levied; and the funds arisingfrom the tax on dogs
belonging to coloredpersons in each of saidcountiesshallbe
paid intoand become a partof the common school fund for
coloredchildrenin the county in which it is levied,and the
saidfunds shallbe appliedin likemanner as the other school
funds are applied.
§ 3. That any person concealing, or attempting or aiding
to conceal,or failingto list,any dog or bitch so as to avoid
paying the tax or taxes requiredin the firstsectionof this
bill,shallbe consideredguiltyof a misdemeanor ,and liable,
on conviction thereof, to a fineof not lessthan fivenor more
than fifteendollars,to be recovered beforeany justiceof the
peace of the county in which the offenseoccurs.
§ 4.That every person owning ,having,or keeping any dog
or bitchshallbe liableto the partyinjuredforalldamages
done by suchdog or bitch; and itshallbe lawfulforany per-
son to kill,or cause to be killed,any dog or bitchwhich he
may findroamingat largeon hispremiseswithoutthe pres-
ence of the owner or keeper of said dog or bitch; and itshall
be furtherlawfulfor any person at any time to kill,or cause
to be killed, any dog or bitchwhich may be or may have been
found killing,worrying,or injuringany sheep or lambs ; and
when any person issued forthe killingof a dog or bitch,and
his defense is under this act,he shall be a competent witness
to prove the same .
§ 5.All actsor partsof actsin conflictherewith are hereby
repealed .
§ 6. This actshalltake effectfrom and afteritspassage.
Approved March 20, 1876.

CHAPTER 662 .
AN ACT toorganizeand establisha system of public schoolsin the Eliza-
bethtown common school district, in Hardin county, forwhite children
in said district .
Be itenactedbytheGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That allthe territorynow embraced within the
boundary of saidElizabethtowndistrict,in thecounty of
Hardin,or which may hereafterbe added thereto,be,and
VOL . IH- LOC . L.- 13
1
ishereby,incorporatedas a schooldistrict,which shallbe
under the control and management of a board of trus-
tees,consistingof fivein number ,electedby the white
citizensof said district,as hereinafterdirected.
§ 2. The persons so electedfrom said districtshallcon-
stituteand be styled" The Board of Trustees of the Eliz-
abethtown DistrictPublic Schools;" and by that name
shallbe known as a body -politicand corporate; and may
sue and be sued,contractand be contractedwith; may
buy and selland convey real and personal estate; and
thetitleto allschoolpropertyin saiddistrictshallvestin
said board of trustees,and theirsuccessors in office, for-
ever .
§ 3. Said board of trusteesshallbe electedfora period
of two years,at an electionto be held at the court-house
in Elizabethtown on the firstMonday in April, 1878,and
shall hold their officeuntil their successors are elected and
qualified,and shallnot be entitledto receiveany com-
pensation fortheirservices.
§ 4. The saidtrusteesso electedshall,beforeorganiz-
ing,take an oath,to be administered by the clerk of any
court of record in Hardin county , to faithfullydischarge
theirduties,and shallmeet and organize within one week
aftertheirelection; and they shallorganize by electinga
president,a treasurer,and a clerk,allof whom shallbe
elected from the members of the said board ,who shall
each hold his officeforone year. In case of a vacancy
occurringin the officesof president,treasurer,or clerkof
said board ,from any cause ,the said board may fillsuch
vacancy by electingone of theirnumber ,who shallhold
untilthe next regular electionfor said office. In case of
the absenceorinabilityof thepresidentto act,a majority
of the members attending a meeting may elect one of
theirnumber as chairman, who shallpreside and dis-
charge the dutiesof presidentpro tempore. The said
board shallannually,at their firstmeeting afteran elec-
tionof trustees,and theirqualificationin each year,elect
president,treasurer,and clerkfor said board,who shall
each holdhisofficeuntilhissuccessoriselectedand qual
ified. The treasurerand clerkshallperform,respectively,
such duties as pertain generally to the positionsof treas-
urer and clerk, and all other such duties as may be pre-
scribedby the said board of trustees.
§5 . The said board of trustees shall,at their firstregu-
lar meeting ,determine by lot, and designate and name
the two members of said board whose term of office shall
expire in one year from their election, which decision
shallbe recorded in theirjournal,and the term of office
of the two members so designated shall expire in one
year from their election; but they shall each hold his
officeuntilhissuccessoriselected and qualified. And on
the firstMonday in April, 1879,there shallbe an election
held at the court-house in Elizabethtown , in the same
manner as hereinprovided,to fillthe placesof the said
two members so expiring,whose terms of officeshallbe
for two years, and shall hold until their successors are
elected and qualified.
§ 6. The controland management of the public schools
of said district, and the property and funds belonging
thereto,and which may in any way accrue to them ,or for
their establishment,management ,or maintenance under
this act or otherwise,shall be vested in the said board
of trustees and their successors in office.
§7 . The said board of trustees shall have power to
make allneedful by -laws and rulesfor the government of
themselvesand theirappointees,and forthe dispatchof
business,and for the management , control,and govern-
ment of the schools in said district .
§8 . A majority of the members of said board of trus-
tees shallconstitutea quorum for the transaction of busi-
ness . They shallmeet at least once a month ,and shall
fixthe time and place of theirmeeting ,and may meet as
often as to them may seem necessary,for the transaction
of business. A majority of those present at any meeting
may transactany business,exceptin the making of con-
tractsforthe purchase or sale of real estate,or forthe
erectionof any building,or forthepaying out of money ,
or the employment of teachers,in which casesa majority
.
of the entireboard must concur; and the yeas and nays
shallbe polledand recordedin thejournal.
§ 9. The said board of trusteesshallhave the power to
employ a superintendent for the schools for said district,
when ,in theirjudgment ,they shalldeem itbest to do so;
they shallhave power to employ allneedful teachers,
principals,and assistants,and with fullpower to suspend
or dischargesuperintendentsand teachersemployed by
them for incompetency , inefficiency, or other cause, of
which they shallhave the sole right to determine ; they
shallagree with superintendents and teachers as to their
compensation,which contractsshallbe reduced to writ-
ing,which shallbe signedby the presidentof the board,
forthe saidboard of trustees,and by the superintendent
or teacher .
§ 10. Said board of trusteesshallnot have the rightto
suspend or dischargeany superintendentor teacher in
theiremploy, except upon charges firstmade and pre-
sentedin writingto the board,and filedwith clerkthere-
of,statingin conciselanguage thegrounds and specifica-
tions of the charge or charges,which may be done at any
regular or called meeting of the said board of trustees:
Provided, Said charges are preferredby or through some
member of saidboard: And provided, That the superin-
tendent or teacher against whom charges are to be made
shall have at least one day's notice thereof in writing,
which noticeneed not specifythe grounds of the charge
to be made .
§ 11.The saidboard of trusteesshall,at any meeting
at which any charge is preferredagainst a superin-
tendentor teacher,of which the partycharged has had
the noticerequired,proceed at once to an investigation
of the charge,unlessthe party charged shallbe present
and requesta postponement forthe purpose of preparing
a defense,when the board may ,sufficientor reasonable
cause being shown ,postponethe investigation,from time
to time, not exceeding two days at a time. The pro-
ceedingshad in the investigationin such cases shallbe
reduced to writing, includingthe testimonyheard, and
!
ifthe same result in the suspension or discharge of the
partycharged from the positionheld by him ,saidparty,
if aggrieved,shallhave the rightto an appeal to the
" State Board of Education ," who shall have the power
to' affirm or reverse the decision, whose action shall be
final: Provided, That forthe purpose of the said appeal,
the party appealing shallbe entitledto a trueand com-
pletetranscriptof the record of the board of trustees
made in the investigationof the charge : And provided,
The appealhereingrantedshallbe taken,and therecord
filed with the clerk of the " State Board of Education "
withinsixtydays from the terminationof the investiga-
tionby the said board of trustees.
§ 12. The saidboard of trusteesshallcause to be kept
a regular and correctrecord of alltheirproceedings in a
well-bound book ,which shallbe open at alltimes tothe
inspectionof the citizensof saidElizabethtowndistrict.
§ 13. The said board of trusteesshallhave power to
prescribethe branches of educationto be taughtin the
schools,grade the pupils and classes,and prescribethe
necessary qualificationsfor, and the mode of examina-
tionof,pupilsor personsapplying foradmissionto the
schools .
§ 14. The said board of trusteesshall, at the end of
each scholasticyear , make out a general report,showing
the number of pupils taught in each department during
the year , the average daily attendance , etc.; also, the
receiptsand expenditures,and conditionofthe funds and
propertybelonging to the schooldistrict,and such other
informationas the cause of public education requires,
and cause the said reportto be publishedin the county
newspaper .
§ 15. The treasurerof saidboard,beforeenteringupon
his duties,shallexecute a bond to the board of trustees,
with good and ample sureties,to be approved by the said
board of trustees, conditioned for the faithfulperform-
ance of his dutiesunder thisact, or prescribedby the
said board , and for the faithfulhandling of allmoney or
funds coming to his hands as such treasurer; and forany
infractions or violation of said bond , the treasurer and
his suretiesmay be sued in the Hardin circuitcourt, and
held liable therefor on said bond .
§ 16. All white children over six years of age , and
under twenty years of age ,residingwithin said district,
shallhave equal rightto admission to the schools of said
district, and no fees or charges for their tuition shallbe
charged them; and it is expresslyprovided that white
children only are to be admitted into said schools.
§ 17. No catechism or other form of religiousbelief
shall be taught, or inculcated in, nor shall any class-
book be used or adopted for said schools, which reflects
upon any religiousdenomination; nor shallany schoolor
class be so conducted as to interferewith the religious
belief of parents or pupils.
§ 18. The trusteesshall annually ,during the month of
April,take an exact census of allthe white childrenthen
residingwithin the said district,who will be ,on the first
day of July following,between the ages of sixand twenty
years,and,on or beforethe firstday of May , reporta
list of the same to the commissioner of common schools
for Hardin county, specifyingthe name , age, sex,and
names of the parents or guardian of each child.
§19 . The commissioner of common schools for Hardin
county shall annually make an estimate of the share or
proportion of the State or Common School Fund which
would be coming to the said Elizabethtown district; and
shallannually pay over to the treasurerof the saidboard
of trustees herein created the full amount of such pro-
portion or share : Provided, The said commissioner may
pay the same installmentsas itcomes to his hands ; which
shall be held and used by the said board of trusteesas
the other funds herein provided for.
§20 . For the purposes of holding an election forthe
board of trusteesprovided for herein,on the 1stday of
April,1878,thepresentboard of educationof Elizabeth-
town now acting shallgive notice of said election,by
postingup noticesatthree or more prominent placesin
Elizabethtown for ten days next preceding the day of
election: Provided, That thereafterthe said board of trus-
tees shall, at each succeeding election for members of
said board of trustees,give similar notice as herein re-
quired. At all electionsfor members of the said board
of trusteesheld hereunder , the qualifiedwhite voters of
the said Elizabethtown districtshall be the electors ; and
any white widow ,having a childbetween six and twenty
years of age ,may alsovote in person or by written proxy .
The commissioner of common schools for Hardin county
shallappointsome personsto act as judge and clerkat
such election,and thereafterthe said board of trustees
shallappointsome person to act as judge,and the clerk
of said board of trustees shall act as clerk at all suc-
ceeding elections for members of said board of trustees .
The judge of said electionsshallgive the casting vote in
cases of a tie, and give a certificateof election to the
person elected, signedby himselfand the clerk of the
election .
§ 21. Any male white person,who is over the age of
twenty-one years,and has been forthreeyears nextpre-
ceding his election a citizen of said Elizabethtown dis-
trict,shallbe eligibleto an electionas a member of said
board of trustees for said district.
§22. In case of vacanciesoccurringby thedeath,res-
ignation,or removal from said district,or continued ab-
sence therefrom, for two months consecutively, of any
member or members of said board of trustees, a ma-
jorityof the remaining members of said board of trus-
tees shall fillsuch vacancies by electing some qualified
citizen of the district thereto .
§23. Itshallbe the duty of saidboard of trusteesto be
diligentin their effortsto promote the best interestsof
said schools in said district; they shalldo equal rightto
thepoor and the rich, and shallinviteand encourage all
the white children in said districtto attend the schools ,
and inform them and theirparents that such is theirright,
though they themselvesmay contributenothingtowards
paying the expenses of the school; and no arrangement
shall be made for the benefit of some individuals to the
exclusion of any others: Provided, They shall not, by
reason of theiractionsas said board of trustees,be held
individuallyorpersonallyresponsiblein any event,except
forgross violationof their duties,or through malice they
commit a wrong .
24. The said board of trusteesmay ,by an order,fix
upon some regulartime in each year forthe electionof
superintendentand teachersto the severalgrades of the
school,and may electa janitorforthe school-rooms,and
agree with him as to compensation .
§25 . The commissioner of common schools for Hardin
county is to have no control whatever over the schools
within said Elizabethtown district .
§ 26. Said board of trusteesshall not assessany negro
property in said districtfor the benefit of said schools
therein .
§27 . The said board of trusteesmay admit into any of
the schoolsinsaiddistrictany whitechildrenwithinthe
school ages prescribedherein,who are non -residentsof
the saiddistrict,or any personswithinthe district,or any
who are non -residents,over the age of twenty years,upon
such terms and conditions,and upon the payment of such
charges,as to the said board may seem right.
§ 28. The said board of trustees of said Elizabethtown
school districtshall,upon some day to be fixedby them ,
submit to the qualifiedwhite voters of said district, a
proposition to levy a tax,not exceeding thirtycents in
any one year upon the one hundred dollars' worth of
taxable propertysituatedwithin said district: Provided,
That when the boundary line of said districtpasses
through the lands of any person whose homestead is
situated within said district, the whole of said land shall
be subjectto the tax herein authorized; and all property
subject to taxation for State revenue and county levy
purposesshallbe taxed forthe purposesherein. This tax
is to be called and known as a school tax, and is to be
used exclusivelyforthe purpose of defrayingthe yearly
expensesof the schoolsin saiddistrict,and shallalways
be collectableand payable only in money .
§ 29. The said board of trustees shall cause said elec-
tion for the vote upon said tax to be held on theday
fixedupon by them ,and they shallappointsome person
to act as judge of said election,who ,togetherwith the
clerk of the board of trustees,shallhold the said election,
fifteendays ' notice thereof being firstgiven,by a notice
to be insertedin any weekly newspaper publishedin
Elizabethtown ,which notice shallstate the amount and
object of the tax proposed to be raised, and the time and
place of taking the vote : Provided, That when a vote
upon said proposition to tax shallbe taken ,votes shall
be received from 9 o'clock,A. M , till5 o'clock,P. M.
All white male citizensof saiddistrictentitledby law to
vote, and allwhite widows over the age of twenty -one
years, who have a child between the ages of six and
twenty years,or who own propertysubjectto be taxed
under thisact, may also vote in person or by written
proxy .

§ 30. At said poll the judge of the electionshalldecide
upon the qualificationsofelectorsproposingto vote; and
the clerk of said election shall record cach vote as
the tax" or " againstthe tax," as the case may be; and
the pollshallbe certifiedto by saidjudge and clerk,and
returnedbeforethe saidboard oftrustees;and ifa major-
ityof the votes cast shallbe in favor of said tax,the said
board of trusteesshallappoint an assessor, who shall,
after firstbeing sworn to faithfullydischarge his duties,
assessallthe propertywithinthedistrictsubjectto taxa-
tion herein,and return a true and fairlistof the same to
said board of trustees,who shall cause to be made out
tax receipts,such as are requiredforthe purposesofcol-
lectingthe State revenue tax, and listthe same with the
sheriffof Hardin county ,taking his receipttherefor,who
shallcollectand pay over the same to the said treasurer
of said board of trustees within ninety days from the
time he receives them ; and said sheriff shall be held re-
sponsible on his officialbond for the faithfulcollectionof
the same ,and subjectto the same penaltiesthathe now
isby law , for failureto collectthe State revenue ; and he
may collectby levy, distress,or sale,in the same manner
as he is authorizedby law to collectthe State revenue,
and for his compensation he shallreceive five per cent.
on alltaxes he collectsand pays over as required,to be
deducted at the time he pays the same .
§31 . The said board of trustees shall, after said tax
has been once voted on and carried, be authorized to
annually have the same assessed and collected as pro-
vided herein : Provided , If the said tax should fail to
carry at said election, the said board may submit the
vote upon the same as often as they may think proper to
do so .
§32 . The said board of trusteesshall also levy annu-
ally a capitation or poll-tax, of not exceeding two dol-
lars, on each white male citizen within the districtover
twenty-one years of age, to be assessedby them , and
collectedby the sheriffof Hardin county , at the same
time and in the same manner as the other said tax herein
isdirected to be collected,and the sheriff is to be liable to
the same extent,and in the same way , and receive the
same compensation for collecting.
§ 33. The fund arisingfrom the said taxes herein pro-
vided for shallbe paid into the hands of the treasurerof
the board of trusteesby the sheriff, and his receipttaken
thereforby the 15th day of October in each year ,or said
sheriffshall be deemed a delinquent,and liable to the
same penalties as sheriffsor collectorsof State revenue
are by law , and proceeded against in the same way , ex-
cept that the proceeding shall be in the name of " The
Board of Trustees of the Elizabethtown District Public
Schools," and in the Hardin circuitcourt; the execution
upon any such judgment in any such cases shallbe di-
rected to the jaileror coroner of Hardin county , or to
any officerthe courtmay direct; and saidjailer,coroner,
or other officer,shallcollectand account forthe same ,and
be responsibleupon his officialbond as in casesof other
executions placed in his hands .
§ 34. The treasurer of said board of trustees shall an-
nually,on thefirstMonday ofJulyineachyear,make a
statementto the saidboard of trustees,showing the con-
ditionand amount of fundsremaining in hishands,after
defrayingallthe expensesof the schoolsin saidEliza-
1
1
bethtown school districtfor the closing school year ; and
whatever surplus may be thus shown in his hands shall,
at the end of each scholasticyear,be set apart by an
order of the said board of trustees and constituted a sink-
ing fund ,to be thereafterheld exclusivelyfor the purpose
of purchasing a siteand grounds on which to erect school
buildingsfor said schooldistrict, to be so expended by
said board of trustees whenever there shall accumulate a
fund sufficient, in theirjudgment ,to purchase grounds,
and erect such buildings thereon as will be suitable and
sufficient to accommodate all the white children within
said districtthat are entitledto the privileges of said
school : Provided , The said board of trustees shall loan
out said funds,from time to time, until needed for the
purposesherein,takingbond and good securitytherefor,
bearing a legal rate of interest.
§35 . All money and funds coming into the treasuryof
said board of trustees shall be under the exclusive control
and management of the said board of trustees,and shall
be used by them forthe solepurpose of, and benefitof
said schoolsin said district, and for the purchase of
grounds , and the erection of school buildings thereon:
And be itprovided, That ifany member of said board of
trustees,or thetreasurerthereof,shallwillfullysquander,
or appropriateto hisown use any of the funds or money
soheldby them,belongingto the saidschooldistrict,he

§36 . The said board of trusteesshallhave the right to
condemn any privatepropertyforschoolpurposes,when-
everin theiropinionitshallbe necessary,by firstpaying
therefor,in money ,itsfaircash value,if such value can

then, upon applicationof the board of trustees, the
countycourt of Hardin county shallissue a writ of ad
quoddamnum ,directedto the sheriffof Hardin county, to

laws.summary: This act mandates the establishment and maintenance of a public school specifically for children of the African race in Paducah, to be known as the Colored Public School of Paducah. It outlines the supervisory roles of the general public school trustees, including appointing teachers, setting rules, and adopting textbooks. It also establishes an advisory board of five qualified colored voters to assist in the school's governance.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 775 . AN ACT to establisha public school for childrenof the African race in the city of Paducah . Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky :

§ 1. That the trusteesof the public school of the cityof Paducah shallestablish,organize, and maintain a public school for children of the African race residing in the said city, which shall be known as the Colored Public School of Paducah .

§2 . The trusteesof the public school shallexercise a general supervision over the said colored public school, appointteachers,make rulesand regulations,adopt text books and a course of studyfor the same ,and appoint, within twenty days from the passage of thisact, fivedis- creet qualifiedcolored voters in the city,who shallbe the advisory board of trusteesof the colored public school.

§3 . The trusteesof the publicschoolshallprescribe the duties of the colored trustees, make rules and regula- tions for theirgovernment ,appoint teachers and remove them forcause,and supplyallvacanciesin thesaidadvi- sory board caused by death , resignation, removal from office, or removal from the city.

§4 . The funds for the support of the coloredpublic school shallconsistof the pro rata from the State forthe education of colored childrenresidingin the cityof Padu- cah , all taxes collectedfrom the colored persons of said cityunder the provisionsofthe citycharterforfiveyears from the firstday of January,1878.and such otherfunds as are or may be set apart by law ,donation ,or otherwise, for the use and benefitof the said colored public school.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 775 .
AN ACT to establisha public school for childrenof the African race in
the city of Paducah .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1. That the trusteesof the public school of the cityof
Paducah shallestablish,organize, and maintain a public
school for children of the African race residing in the
said city, which shall be known as the Colored Public
School of Paducah .
§2 . The trusteesof the public school shallexercise a
general supervision over the said colored public school,
appointteachers,make rulesand regulations,adopt text
books and a course of studyfor the same ,and appoint,
within twenty days from the passage of thisact, fivedis-
creet qualifiedcolored voters in the city,who shallbe the
advisory board of trusteesof the colored public school.
§3 . The trusteesof the publicschoolshallprescribe
the duties of the colored trustees, make rules and regula-
tions for theirgovernment ,appoint teachers and remove
them forcause,and supplyallvacanciesin thesaidadvi-
sory board caused by death , resignation, removal from
office, or removal from the city.
§4 . The funds for the support of the coloredpublic
school shallconsistof the pro rata from the State forthe
education of colored childrenresidingin the cityof Padu-
cah , all taxes collectedfrom the colored persons of said
cityunder the provisionsofthe citycharterforfiveyears
from the firstday of January,1878.and such otherfunds
as are or may be set apart by law ,donation ,or otherwise,
for the use and benefitof the said colored public school.
§5 . The fund provided for in thisact shallbe kept sep-
arate,collectedand disbursed as the funds for the support
of public schools of thisState now are or may hereafter
be .
§6 . To enable the trustees of the public school to
provide,by purchase or otherwise,suitable grounds and
buildingsfor the colored school of Paducah ,the trustees
of said public school shallhave the right,if in their dis-
cretion they may deem it proper ,to issue the bonds of
said colored public school in an amount not exceeding
five thousand dollars, to bear any rate of interest not
exceeding eightper cent.per annum ,in such amounts as
they may see proper ,the bonds to be signed by the pres-
ident and secretaryof the trusteesof the common schools
of Paducah . Said bonds , if issued, may be sold by the
trusteesof the common schools for money ,or may be ex-
changed for real estate on which to locate said colored
public school, and for labor in the erection of school
buildingson thesame . Said bonds may be made payable
at such times as the trusteesof the common schools may
thinkproper. To saidbonds may be attachedcoupons to
represent the intereston said bonds ,payable half yearly
at some bank in the cityof Paducah ; the coupons to be
signed by the clerk of the trustees of the common schools
alone .
§7. This actshalltake effectthirtydays afteritspas-
sage .
Approved April 5, 1878.

CHAPTER 799 .
AN ACT to incorporate" The Board of Trusteesforthe Graded City School
of Cynthiana, Kentucky ."
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That A. J. Beale ,T. A. Frazer ,A. W. Lydick ,R.
M. Martin , H. McDowell , W. V. Prather, Luther Van-
hook , and R. C. Wherritt, citizensof Cynthiana , Ken-
tucky,and at thispresentthe duly constitutedboard of
trusteesfor the graded cityschool of said city,and their
successorsin office,be,and they are hereby declared to
be ,a body-corporateand politic,with perpetualsucces-
sion,by the name and styleof " The Board of Trustees
fortheGraded CitySchoolof Cynthiana,Kentucky ;" and
as such,by that name shall be capable in law of con-
tractingand being contracted with,suing and being sued,
in all courts and places,and in all matters whatsoever .
The absolute and unconditional control of the graded
city school for said city is hereby vested in said board
of trustees; and the said board are hereby empowered to
do all those things necessary and proper to be done to
secure the successfulmanagement thereof,with fullpower
and authorityto buy ,sell,hold, or convey ,in theircorpo-
rate capacity,any estate,eitherreal,personal,or mixed.
§2 . No person shallbe eligibleto the officeof trustee,
except he be a white male,residentof the cityof Cyn-
thiana, and over twenty -one years of age .
§3 . The term of officeof each member of the school
board shall be four years from the date of their elec-
tion; and whenever vacanciesoccur,by expirationof the
term of officeor otherwise,the board shallorder an elec.
tionto supplythe same ; said electionsto be held at the
same time ,under the supervisionof the same officersof
election,and in the same manner as the cityelectionsfor
saidcityof Cynthianaare now held: Provided,That such
vacancies as occur by resignation,death ,or otherwise than
by expirationof term of office,may be temporarilyfilled
by the board of trustees,upon itsown motion or election.
§4. The officersof saidboard shallconsistof a presi-
dent, vice president, clerk, treasurer, attorney, and col-
lector. The president,vice president,clerk,and collector
of said board shall be electedby said board at the first
regularmeetingthereofin May ,1878. The presidentand
vice president thereof shall,each of them ,be members of
the board of trustees . The treasurer of the board of trus-
tees shall be the same as the treasurer of the city of Cyn-
thiana,electedat the same time,in the same manner ,and
shallhold his officeforthe same period as now prescribed
by the charterof said city. He shall,before enteringupon
the discharge of his duties,execute bond , with good and
sufficientsureties, to be approved by the board,for the
faithfulperformance of his duties. He shall keep all
funds which may come into his hands ,for the use or the
benefit of the board of trustees aforesaid,separate and
distinctfrom all other funds, and shall make a monthly
statement of his accounts to the board of trustees . The
clerk of the board shall be elected as aforesaid for the
period of one year, and shallhold his officeuntilhis suc-
cessor is elected and qualified, and shall receive for his
servicessuch compensation as the board may fixor deter-
mine upon . The board shall have power to fixand de-
termine the duties of each and every one of its officers,
and to remove any of their officersor members for any
gross misconduct or neglect of duty ,by a two -thirdsvote
of the whole board . The board may make and alter, at
their pleasure, a set of by -laws for theirgovernment :
Provided, That the same be not in conflictwith any of
the provisionsof thisact.
§ 5. The " board of trusteesfor the graded cityschool
of Cynthiana,Kentucky," shallhave the power and au-
thorityin each year to levyand collectan ad valorem
tax on allthe propertyin the cityof Cynthiana.belong.
ing to white persons,subjectto taxation,not exceeding
fifty(50) centson each one hundred dollars'($ 100) worth
of such assessedproperty. The tax listshallbe made
out by the clerk of the board of trustees from the city
assessor'slistor report, as made to the common council
of said cityin each year . He shallarrange the said list
alphabetically, and set down therein the name of each
tax-payer , and the aggregate value of the taxable prop-
erty listedby the same ,and opposite thereto the amount
of tax due thereon,at the rateor per centage as fixed by
the board for that year . The listas so made out shallbe
placed in the hands of the treasurerof the board for col-
lection,and the taxes for the use and benefit of said board
of trustees shall be collected in the same manner as other
taxes,by law ,are collectedin said city,exceptthatsuch
tax-payers as shallnot pay to the treasurer of the board
the respectiveamounts of taxes owing by them to the
said board in each year ,on or before a day certain to be
fixed and advertised by said board at least fifteendays
prior thereto, shall be declared delinquent tax-payers.
The said board may then order a listof said delinquent
tax-payers to be made out by the clerk,and placed in the
hands of the collectorof the board ,who shallhave power
and authorityto collectthe same ,together with a penalty
ofnot exceedingten (10) per cent.added. If such delin-
quents do not pay the amount of tax owing by them to
the collectoron or before the firstday of November in
each year ,together with allcosts and penaltiesthereon,
then,at any time aftersaid date,the collectormay pro-
ceed to collectthe same by levy, distraint, attachment ,or
garnishment ,in the same manner as by law sheriffsare
directed to collecttaxes; and chapter 92 of the General
Statutes, articles8 and 9 thereof, are hereby adopted and
made a part of thisact of incorporation,so far as itspro-
visionsin the directionto sheriffswillapply to thecollec-
tor of the board in the collection of taxes within the city
of Cynthiana .
§6 . The collector of the board shall be elected at the
firstregular meeting of said board in May , 1878, and
yearly thereafter; and before he shall enter upon the
dischargeof his duties as such,he shallexecute bond ,
with good and sufficientsureties,to be approved by the
board,forthe faithfulperformance of hisduties; and he
shallmake monthly reportsin writingto the board of
such collectionsas he may have made for them , and at
the close of each year shallmake a finalsettlement of his
accounts with the board .
§7 . Only such white males, over the age of twenty-
one years of age,residentsof the cityof Cynthiana,and
who are in all respects qualifiedto vote for members of
the common council,and other officersof said city,shall
be entitled to vote for members of the " board of trustees
of the graded cityschool of Cynthiana ,Kentucky ."
§ 8. The cityattorneyof the cityof Cynthiana shall
be ex officiothe legal adviser and attorney for the board
of trustees aforesaid, and it shallbe his duty to render
the said board such professional services as they may
require of him in theircorporate capacity.
§9 . The board of trustees aforesaid shall be the sole
judges of the qualificationsand the electionof theirofficers
and members ,except the treasurerand attorney,and shall
have power to decide all contested electioncases which
may arisein connection with said board ; and shall,in
any proceedings had under thissection,proceed in man-
ner and form as directedby the General Statutes of Ken-
tucky, chapter 33, article7, so far as itsprovisioncan
apply .
§ 10. The board of trusteesshall,from time to time ,as
they may deem expedient,prescribe forms,rules and reg-
ulations, and a uniform system of text-books and course
of studyfor the graded cityschoolsof Cynthiana,Ken
tucky. They shallemploy for each school under their
careand jurisdictiona principaland such assistantteach-
ers as they may consider necessary, with fullpower to
discharge any of said teachersor principalswhen such
dischargeshall,in theiropinion,be demanded by the best
interest of the school . The board shall visit each school
at least once a month . A majority of them may expel
any pupilwhose conductin theiropinionmeritssuch
punishment . The board shallkeep the school buildings
in repair,furnish fuel,books , stationery, and such other
apparatus or articlesas they may deem fitand proper
forthe successfulmanagement of said schools. All pay-
ments made by the board to theirteachers, or on account
of any other expense incurredin carrying on said schools,
shallbe by drafton the citytreasurer,made payable out
of funds belonging to the board of trusteesin his hands
to the order of the payee ,specifyingwhen and for what
the appropriationwas made , signed by the presidentor
vice president of the board , and attestedby the clerk.
§ 11. The common school districtin which Cynthiana
is situatedshall,from and afterthe passage of thisact,
be limitedtothe boundary of the cityof Cynthiana,and
shallonly be extended as the limitsof the said citymay
be enlarged .
§ 12. The children of the age prescribed by the com-
mon school law of the State, of every white citizen of
Cynthiana,Kentucky,may attendthe graded cityschools
of said cityfree of charge .
§ 13. No books ,tracts,papers ,catechisms,or other pub-
lications of an infidel or denominational character , shall
be used or distributedin the said graded cityschools,nor
shall any sectarian or infideldoctrines be taught therein.
§ 14. The childrenof white persons,not citizensof Cyn-
thiana,may attendthe saidgraded cityschoolsupon pay-
ing to the treasurer of the board such tuition fees as the
board of trusteesmay ,from time to time,prescribe,and
producing the said treasurer'sreceipt therefor to the
principal of the school; and such payment shallbe by the
treasurer placed to the credit of the board of trustees:
Provided, That persons who were entitledto attend the
lateHarrisonAcademy ,may attendthe graded cityschool
upon the same terms upon which they would have been
entitledto attend said academy .
§ 15. This act of incorporation is subject to the pro-
visions of an act, entitled"An act in relation to the
transferof propertyof the Harrison Academy to the city
of Cynthiana ," approved February 13th, 1873 .
§ 16. All acts and parts of acts inconsistentwith the
provisions of thisact are hereby repealed.
§ 17. This act shall take effectfrom and afteritspas-
sage .
Approved April 5, 1878 .

laws.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act for the benefit of school district No. 39, in Bath county," approved February 9th, 1876.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 587, p. 452
laws.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning school district No. 39 in Bath County. It specifies that only qualified white male voters and white widows with children between the ages of six and twenty years residing in the district have the privilege of voting for the trustees of the Sharpsburg Male and Female College. Widows can vote in person or by proxy. It also sets residency requirements for voters and limits each voter to one vote for each of the five trustees.
key_provisions: §1 . That chapter 134 of the Acts of the General As- sembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky , entitled"An act for the benefit of school district No. 39 , in Bath county," approved February 9, 1876, be, and the same is hereby ,so amended that all the qualifiedwhite male voters of said district, and white widows residing in said district,who have children between the ages of six and twenty years,shall have the privilege of voting for the trustees of said Sharpsburg Male and Female College; the said widows having the right to vote either in per- son or by written proxy .

CHAPTER 587 .
AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act for the benefit of school district
No. 39,in Bath county," approved February 9th, 1876 .
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That chapter 134 of the Acts of the General As-
sembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky , entitled"An
act for the benefit of school district No. 39 , in Bath
county," approved February 9, 1876, be, and the same
is hereby ,so amended that all the qualifiedwhite male
voters of said district, and white widows residing in said
district,who have children between the ages of six and
twenty years,shall have the privilege of voting for the
trustees of said Sharpsburg Male and Female College;
the said widows having the right to vote either in per-
son or by written proxy .
§2 . That no person shall be a qualifiedvoter at said
election for trustees who shall not have been a bona fide
resident of said school districtNo 39 for at least sixty
days before said election; and that no one , whatever
may be the amount of stock he may hold in said build-
ing,shall have the privilege of casting more than one
vote for each of five trustees .
§3 . That the election for said trustees shall be held on
the firstSaturday in June , 1878,and annually thereafter
upon theday upon which the trusteesof common schools
are requiredto be electedby the common schoollaw of
the State .
§4 . That thisact shalltake effectfrom itspassage .
Approved April 8,1878.

laws.summary: This act authorizes the trustee of colored school district No. 1 in Ohio County to erect a schoolhouse, not exceeding $1000 in value, for the use of colored school children. The building is to be used solely as a schoolhouse.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 924 . AN ACT to authorize the erection of a school building in colored school dis- trictNo. 1, in Ohio county, and to levy a tax therefor. Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky :

§1 . That it shall be lawful for the trustee of colored school districtNo. 1, Ohio county , and his successors,to cause to be erected in said district a school -house , not exceeding in value,including the necessary furniture to be placed therein, the sum of one thousand dollars,for the use and benefit of the colored school children in said district .

§ 3. For the purpose of erecting said house the school trustee of said district, and his successors , shall have power and authorityto levy and collectan annual tax on allreal and personal estateowned by the colored citi- zens in said district,of not exceeding one dollaron each one hundred dollars' worth , and shall have power and authorityto levy and collectan annual capitationtax on allcoloredpersons,over twenty-one years of age in said district, of not exceeding fivedollars.

§ 4. The said trustee, and his successors, shall have power and authorityto call out for labor on said build- ing all the male colored citizens in said district between eighteen and fiftyyears of age ,not exceeding two days in any one week ; and a failureto work , when called out, may be prosecutedby saidtrusteeand successorsas road hands are now prosecuted for failing to labor on roads and the same fine collected, which shall be for the use and benefit of said district .
§ 6. This act shall not be in force until ratifiedby a majority of all colored voters in said districtwho vote on the ratificationhereof, at an election to be held by the trustee of said district.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 925, pp. 503–504
laws.summary: This act, passed in 1878, grants the Mt. Sterling Library Association the power to levy taxes on real and personal property owned by colored citizens in a specific district, not exceeding one dollar per one hundred dollars worth. It also allows for a capitation tax on colored persons over twenty-one, not exceeding five dollars. Furthermore, it authorizes the trustee to call out male colored citizens between eighteen and fifty years of age for labor on a building, not exceeding two days per week, with penalties for failure to work similar to those for road hands. The act specifies that the taxes are to be collected like school taxes and that the act will only be in force if ratified by a majority of colored voters in the district.

The tax would be levied on property owned by white persons in the town, not exceeding thirty cents per one hundred dollars, to be used for common school education, excluding building erection. The act specifies that printed notices of the vote must be posted and published in a local paper.

laws.summary: This act mandates the establishment and maintenance of a separate public school for African race children in Frankfort, Kentucky. It outlines the roles of the general public school trustees and an advisory board of colored voters, and specifies the funding sources for this segregated school.

§2 . The trusteesof the public school shallexercise a generalsupervisionover the coloredpublicschool,make rulesand regulations,adopt text-books and a course of studyforthe same ,and appoint,withintwenty days from the passage of this act, five discreet, qualified colored voters in the city, who shall be the advisory board of trustees of the colored school ,

§3 . The trusteesof the publicschoolshallprescribe the duties of the colored trustees,make rulesand regula- tions for their government , remove them for cause ,and supply allvacanciesin the saidadvisoryboard caused by death ,resignation, removal from office,or removal from ' the city.

§ 4. The fund for the support of the colored public school shall consist of the pro rata from the State for the educationof coloredchildrenresidingin the city, and such othersums of money as are now ,or may here- afterbe,set apart by law or ordinanceor otherwise,for the supportof thesaidcoloredpublicschool. §5 The fund providedforin thisact shallbe kept separate, collectedand disbursedas the funds for the supportof the publicschoolare.
