CHAPTER 872 .
AN ACT to incorporatethe Mutual Life Aid Associationof Mayfield, Ken-
tucky .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
Incorporators .
Style .
§ 1. That D. G. Smith , P. L. Henson , L. L. Henson ,
A. P. Boone , J. D. Landrum , J. E. Wallace , and B. A.
Neale , and othersthat they may associatewith them ,
are hereby constituted a body -corporate and politic,in
the name and style of the Mutual Life Aid Association
of Mayfield ,Kentucky ; and in said name and styleshall
have the rightto contract,purchase,hold,and sellprop-
erty, to sue and be sued in all the courts of this State,
for the purpose of operating the business hereinafter de-
scribed .
Purposes
§2 . The object of this association is to unite all ac-
ceptable white persons between the ages of fifteenand
sixty-six years into a benevolent associationfor mutual
protection, to promote morality, temperance , industry,
economy , benevolence , and charity, and to ameliorate
theconditionof sufferinghumanity by providinga bene-
ficiaryfund on the plan of mutual assessment and en-
dowment in which the living and the representatives of
deceased members of the association shallparticipate as
the executing board of the association shall determine .
§3 . That said association shall have the power to
make and adopt a constitution,by-laws and regulations,
not contrary to the Constitution and laws of this State
or of the United States,for the government and regula-
tionsof the said societyin itswork .
§ 4. That the private property of the members of this
associationshallbe exempt from the debts of the associa
tion,and any process of law to subject such property to
such debts shall be void .
§ 5. This act shalltake effectfrom itspassage .
Approved April 7, 1882.

It establishes conditions under which actions to recover land can be initiated, which may disproportionately affect marginalized groups.

CHAPTER 922 .
AN ACT to amend the charterof the cityof Louisville.
Be itenactedby the General Assemblyof the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That forthe purpose of the assessments,re-assess-
ments , and corrected assessments hereinafter directed and
authorized to be made ,real estatein said cityshall be so
classified that the surface of the soil and all beneath such
surface shall be denominated " land," and all and every
thing attached to,builton , or growing from such surface,
and in legalcontemplation a part of it,shall be denomi-
inated " improvements ," and personal property, as used
in thisact, shallbe construed and held to embrace every
class and species of property other than lands and im-
provements .
§2 That the assessorof said cityshallassessat itsfair
cash value, on the firstday of September ,in the year
1882 ,and on the firstday of September in each and every
year thereafter,all the land, improvements ,and personal
property in said city and liableto taxationunder the
revenue laws of the State of Kentucky ; also allthe per
sonal property outside the territoriallimits of said city,
but which on the date of itsassessment belongs to persons
residingin said city,and which is not assessedfor,and on
which taxes are not actually paid to the city, State,
county,town ,or placewhen situated; also,allthe lands,
improvements , and personal property in said citybelong-
ing to any denomination ,institution, association,society,
or corporation whatever , and from which such denom-
ination, institution, association, society, or corporation
receives an income , rent, or profit over or above the
necessarysupport of such institutionas are exclusively
charitable, viz: infirmaries,orphan asylums ,and widows
and orphans 'homes : Provided,First,that merchandise on
which a licensetax ischarged and paid shallnot be liable
to be assessed under the provisions of thisact; and sec-
ond , from the assessed valuation of personal property
there shall be deducted the actual amount of the bona fide
enforceable indebtedness which the owner thereof owes
as the principalobligorat the date of itsassessments.
Said assessorshallalso listin each year all the persons
who on the firstday of September in the year in which
listed were male inhabitants of said city, and over the
age of twenty-one years. Every person who has his
residenceor principalplace of businessin saidcityshall
be regarded as a person residing in said citywithin the
meaning of thissection: Provided, No tax shallbe assessed
on tools,implements ,or material of manufactures in said
city,nor any licensebe required of them for sellingtheir
own manufactures .
§3 . That in making the assessments and listsprovided
for and required in the second section hereof,the said
assessor shall annually ,and prior to the 1st day of No-
vember in each year ,or as soon thereafteras practicable,
make out and return not lessthan four assessment books ,
and shallcause to be entered therein,and as near as may
be in alphabeticalorder,the names of allpersons listed
under the second section hereof , and the names of all
persons,so far as the same are known to said assessor,
who are the owners or possessors of lands,improvements ,
or personal property,liableto be assessed under the pro-
visions of thisact, and opposite the name of such person ,
owner , or possessor the number and block of each of his
lots,according to the maps now in the officeof said as-
sessor, and originallyprepared by the LouisvilleAbstract
and Loan Association,the value per front foot of each
lot,when such lot fronts on a public way ; the value in
gross of each lot; the value of the improvements ,if any ,
upon it; the assessedvalue of allhis personalproperty,
and whether such person ,owner ,or possessor was ,on the
Istday of September in the year in which listed,a male
inhabitant of said city,over the age of twenty -one years.
Any lot of land which is not now designated by a num-
ber on the maps referredto in this section, and any lot
of land which is now so designated ,but is hereafter sub--
divided, shallbe designatedby said assessorby an ap-
propriate serial number , and shall by such numbers be
designated in the assessment books . No mistake or error
in or omission of the right name of the owner or pos-
sessor of eitherlands or improvements liable to be as-
sessed under the provisions of thisact,shall in the least
impair any assessment thereof,ifsuch land be designated
inthe assessmentbooks by itscorrespondingnumber and
block on the maps referredto in this section; or if such
improvement be designated on said assessment books by
the number and blockcorrespondingtothatby which the
land on which such improvements are situatedis desig-
nated on the maps referredto in this section, or if such
land or improvements be otherwisesufficientlyidentified
in the assessment books .
§ 4. Every person owning or possessing lands,improve-
ments , or personal property liableto be assessed under
the provisions of this act,shall, prior to the 1st day of
October in the year 1882, and in every year thereafter,
return to said assessor, under oath ,on a form to be pre-
pared and furnishedby said assessorat his office,allof
his lands and improvements ,and the value of allhis per-
sonalpropertyliableto be assessedunder the provisions
of this act. Any person failing to make returns when
and as requiredby thissection,shallbe deemed guiltyof
a misdemeanor , and on conviction thereof shall be fined
not less than ten nor more than twenty dollars for each
offense, and each day's failureto make returns after the
firstfine,shallbe deemed a separateoffense. All prose
cutions for violations of this section shall be had in the
citycourt of said city, and all fines for such violations
shall, when collected, be paid into the treasury of said
city. In the event of the failureor refusalof any person
owning or possessing lands, improvements ,or personal
property liableto be assessedunder the provisionsof
thisact to make returns as herein required,said assessor
may ,nevertheless,from the bestinformationhe can pro-
cure, assessallthe lands, improvements, and personal
propertyso liable,and belongingto or possessedby the
person so failingor refusing to make returns, and shall
add twenty-fiveper cent.to the faircash value thereof,
and such cash value and percentage so added shallbe
treated and held as the assessed value of the lands,im-
provements ,and personal property of the person so fail-
ing or refusing to make returns .
§5 . The assessment books provided for in the third
section hereof shall remain open in the officeof said
assessor from the fifteenthto thirtiethday of Novem-
ber,inclusive,in each year , and every person who con-
sidersthat his lands or improvements have been assessed
for more than itsfair cash value must within said days
filewith the assessorhis complaint ,specifyingthe partic-
ulars wherein the excessive assessment occurs , and such
complaint shall be during said period from the fifteenth
to the thirtiethday , inclusive, of November ,investigated
by the board of equalization,which board shallapprove
or reduce the assessment , as may appear to such board
just and right. Said board may ,afternoticeto the person
to be charged therewith, increase any assessment,ifupon
investigationsuch board is satifiedthat the assessment
as made was less than the fair cash value of the lands ,
improvements,or personalpropertyassessed. The board
of equalization shall be composed of three discreetciti-
zens of said city,of recognized integrityand ability, tax-
payers of saidcity,and not in arrearagesto saidcityfor
taxes,and not applicantsfor such appointment, to be
appointed by the mayor , with and by the consent and
approval of the board of aldermen . The mayor of said
cityshall,in the month of September,1882, appoint the
members of said board of equalization: one forthe term
of one year ,another for the term of two years, and an-
other for the term of three years; and said mayor shall,in
the month of September in each year thereafter, appoint
a member of said board of equalization for the term of
three years . For the purpose of appointing the members
of the said board of equalization, said cityisdivided into
three districts. The firstdistrictisthat part of said city
east of First street. The second districtis that part of
said citywest of First street, and east of Seventh street;
and the third districtis that part of said city west of
Seventh street; and one member of said board of equali-

zation shallbe appointed from each of said districts. In
the event of a removal of any member of said board
from the districtfor which appointed ,or in the event of
the death or resignationof any member of said board ,or
in the event of a request by the general council for the
removal of any member of said board ,the mayor ,by and
with the advice and consent of the board of aldermen ,
shallappoint a successor to fillthe unexpired term of the

a writing under his hand ,appoint one or more ,and not

February 17th, 1866, and entitled" An act establishing a
Board of Commissioners of Taxes and Assessments for

§ 6. Said assessor may , at any time before the taxes
levied in pursuance thereof are paid ,correct any assess-

§ 7. Said assessorshallcommence during the month of

§ 8. Said assessor shall annually appoint ,by and with

9. An attested copy of an entry in the assessment

the date of the purchase ,and all taxes and assessments
on and against such land or improvements paid by such
purchaser , his representative or assignee, with interest
on such payments at the rate of twenty per cent. per
annum from the date made ; and whenever any land or
improvements sold under the provisions of this section
are redeemed , such redemption shall be noted by the
clerk of the board of aldermen on the record of the re-
port of such sale, and for which noting said clerk shall
be entitledto demand ,and shall receive from the person
so redeeming ,a fee of one dollar.
§ 11. If land or improvements sold under authority of
the tenth section of this act be not redeemed within the
time therein allowed ,the purchaser thereof at such sale,
or his assignee or heirs, may demand , and shallreceive,
from the clerk of the board of councilmen , a deed there-
for, in substance as follows : " It appearing from the
report of sales made by the receiver of city taxes that
on the - day of — , 18 , said receiver of city taxes
sold to - (a certainlot of land or improvement
on a certain lot of land, as the case may be) in the city
of Louisville, in the State of Kentucky , and which in
said report isdesignated as lotNo. — ,block No. — , and
that the same has not been redeemed ; now , therefore , I
- , clerk of the board of councilmen of said city,
by virtue of the authority vested in me , do hereby sell
and convey the aforesaid(lotof land or improvement ) in
fee-simple to - In testimony of allwhich ,test
my officialsignature on this,the day of , 18 .
一 .
- , clerk of board of councilmen ." And which
deed shall operate to vest in the person therein desig-
nated as the grantee a full,complete , and perfect titleto,
and to divestallothersof any ownership of or interest
in or claim against the lands or improvements therein
conveyed ; and such clerk shall be entitledto demand ,
and shall receive from the person , other than the city of
Louisville,to whom he executes such deed , a fee of one
dollar , and such deed shall be a recordable instrument
without acknowledgment before or certificateof the
clerk of a county court or other officer: Provided, That
such owner of real estate or improvements sold under
the process of section eleven, in all instances where the
purchaser , his representative, or agent is unknown or
cannot be found , may , within the time named ,pay suchsu
sum , with the interest aforesaid, to the receiver of city
taxes, who shallbe responsiblefor the same on his bond .
§ 12. Any person to whom a deed is executed and de-
livered by the clerk of the board of councilmen , under
the authority of the eleventh section hereof, may , upon
notice given five days prior to his application therefor,
enter his motion in the Louisville chancery court for a
writ of possession,commanding the marshal of said court
to put him in the possession of the land or improvement
described in said deed ,and on his filingsaid deed ,or an
attested copy of the record thereof, the chancellor shall
award , the clerk of said court shall issue,and the marshal
of said court shall execute such writ. The person enter-
ing such motion shallpay to the clerk of said court a tax
of fiftycentsforthe benefitof the State, and shallpay to
the officersof the court allcostsincurred by him in such
proceeding . The notice provided for in thissection shall
be given by at least one insertion in one of the news-
papers printedand publisheddailyin the cityof Louis-
ville, and shall be in form and substance as follows :
" Notice is hereby given that I will,on the - day of -— ,
18- , enter a motion in the Louisville chancery court for
a writ requiring the marshal of said court to put me
intothepossessionof (here describetheland or improve-
ment ). A. B." One of the issuesof the newspapers
containing the notice shall be filed when the motion is
entered , and shall be evidence that the notice was given .
No action shall be instituted or maintained to recover
the possession of lands or improvements from the person
or those claiming under him to whom such land or im-
provements were conveyed by the clerk of the board of
councilmen under the authority of the eleventh section
hereof , unless such action be instituted within six months
from the date of such deed , nor shall such action be in-
stitutedunless the person institutingthe same pays and
tenders into court for the defendants to such action the
purchase price of such land or improvements at the sale
thereof made by the receiver of citytaxes, with interest
thereon at the rate of twenty -five per cent.per annum
from the date of such sale; also the sum of all taxes
on and assessmentsagainstsuch land or improvements
paid by the defendants to such action, or those under
whom they claim , with interest thereon at the rate of
twenty -five per cent. per annum from the date of such
payments ,and the fullvalue of any and allimprovements
or additionsput on or added to such land or improve-
ments by the defendants to such action , or those under
whom they claim. The city of Louisville shall, in all
cases where it is a purchaser at sales made by the re-
ceiver of city taxes,be entitledto the same rights and
remedies as any other purchaser .
§ 13. In addition to the remedies herein given ,the city
of Louisville shall have the right to institute an action in
the Louisvillechancery court for the recovery of the
amount of any unpaid tax billor tax billsand interest,
and the enforcement of itslien,and may in such action,
without bond or affidavit,sue out a general attachment
similar to that provided for in chapter three of title
eight of the Code of Practice in civil cases .
§ 14. The general council shallannually ,by ordinance ,
fix and determine the amount or rate of tax to be levied
on each one hundred dollars of the assessed value of
the lands,improvements,and personalpropertyassessed
under the provisionsof thisact in the year in which such
taxes are levied, and the rate of taxation thus fixed shall
be uniform on all the classes of property assessed,pro-
vided that there shallbe levied annually , for the benefit
of the treasury of said city, a tax of two dollarson every
person listedunder the third section hereof: Provided,
That the rate of taxation annually levied under this act
shallnot exceed the sum now authorizedby law .
§15 Said receiverof city taxes shall, on or before the
31st day of December , in the year 1882, and in every
year thereafter, state and settlehis accounts with and
receive a quietus from the finance committee of the gen-
eral council, and in such settlements said receiver of city
taxes shallbe allowed no creditfor any uncollected tax
bill, unless such committee believe, from the evidence
offered,that such uncollected tax bill could not have been
collected by such receiver of city taxes, and for the
amount of every uncollected tax bill for which such
committee refuses in such settlement to allow a credit,
said receiverof citytaxes,and the suretieson his official
bond ,shall be liableto account for and pay to said city,
the same as if such tax billshad been collected; but such
receiverof citytaxesshallbe subrogatedtothe rightsof
said cityas against the persons owing such uncollected
tax bills. In the event that such receiver fails to obtain a
quietus at such settlement, such failureshallbe reported
to the board of aldermen at their next meeting thereafter,
whereupon such board of aldermen shallat once declare
the officeof receiverof citytaxes to be vacant , and order
the treasurerof said cityto immediately take possession
of allthe moneys ,books ,bills, registers,accounts,& c , of
the officeof such receiver of citytaxes,and at the next
meeting of the general council thereafter there shall be
elected in joint session, on viva voce vote,a receiver of
city taxes for the unexpired term of such defaulting
receiverof citytaxes.
§ 16. The general councilmay , by ordinance not in
conflictherewith , regulate the officeof the receiver of
city taxes, the officeof assessor, and the collectionof
taxes, and may by ordinance fix the compensation of
any of itsofficersor employes ,and define theirstudies.
§ 17. In all cases when land or improvements pur-
chased by the cityof Louisville,at the salesthereof made
by the receiver of citytaxes, are redeemed , the redemp-
tion money shall be paid to the treasurer of said city,
and in allsuch cases allunpaid taxes assessed and levied
by said city on such land or improvement shall be re-
garded as having been paid by said cityon the day of
and prior to such redemption .
§ 18. All courts in the county of Jefferson shall take
judicial notice of the passage , approval , contents, and
publication of each ordinance of the city of Louisville,
§19 . The generalcouncilof the cityof Louisvilleshall
have power by joint resolution to adjourn for not longer
than thirtydays at any time ,but shall be subject to be
convened at any time by notice from the mayor .
§20 . That no principalof any school,and no principal
or teacher of any private sectarian or other school, shall
admit to any such school any child or minor who shall
not have been vaccinated within five years next preced-
ing the admission or application for admission to any
such school of such child or minor ; or shall any such
principalor teacher retainin, or permit to attend any
such school,any child or minor who shallnot have been
vaccinated within five years next preceding the taking
effect of this statute . The evidence of such vaccination
to be presented to any such principal or teacher,as is
mentioned above , shall be a certificatesigned by the
health officeror any practicing physician.
§21 . The healthofficeris hereby empowered to visit
any and allpublicand privateschoolsin the city,and to
make ,or cause to be made ,any examination of the chil-
dren and minors in attendance therein as often as he
may deem necessary to secure compliance with the pro-
visions hereof .
§ 22. Any principal of a public school, or principal or
teacher in any private or other school, who shallviolate
any of the provisionsof this statute, or shall in any way
prevent or attempt to prevent the health officerfrom
exercising the power conferred by thisact, shall be fined
for each offense not less than five dollars nor more than
one hundred dollars,recoverable upon ordinance warrant
in the city court, and be paid into the citytreasury.
§23 . The first eighteen sections of this act will take
effectfrom on and after the 1st day of September , 1882 ,
and sections 19 , 20 , and 21 hereof will take effect and be
in force from and afterthe passage of this act; and all
laws and partsof laws in conflictherewith are hereby
repealed .
Approved April 8, 1882.

CHAPTER 955 .
AN ACT authorizingthe children within the schoolage in certaindistricts
adjoiningNewport ,Dayton , and Belleview, in Campbell county,to attend
common schoolsin saidci'yand towns .
Be itenactedbytheGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That the children within the common school ages
residingwithin the districtshereinafternamed ,in Camp-
bellcounty ,shallhave the right, and may attend the pub-
lic schools in the respective city and towns to which
said districtsare attached,and the boards of education in
Newport ,Belleview,and Dayton shallbe authorizedto
receive the per capita of common school fund due said
children in said districtsrespectively.
§ 2. Those children residingin all that territorylying
between the corporate limitsof the city of Newport and
the line of the Belleview magisterialdistrict,the line of
the Highland district, and the north line of the John
Hills school districtand Licking river, may attend the
Newport schools.
§3 . The children in the magisterial districtof Belle-
view ,lying outside the corporate limitsof that town ,shall
have the privilegeof attendingthe public schoolsin
Belleview .
§ 4. The childrenoutside of Dayton and in the present
Dayton magisterialdistrictshallhave the rightto attend
the publicschoolsin Dayton .
§5 . The white children in said districtsshall attend the
schools for white childrenin said city and towns ,and the
colored children in said districtsshall have the right to
attend the colored schoolsin said cityand towns .
§ 6. This act shall be in force from and afterits pas-
sage .
Approved April 11, 1882.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 959 .
AN ACT to incorporatethe Kenton Savings Bank .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That Frank P. Helm , Max Herbst , Alex .Davezac ,
John L. Sandford , and John O. Richards , and theirasso-
ciates,successors,and assigns,be ,and are hereby ,created
a body-politicand corporate,by the name and styleof
the Kenton Savings Bank , the capital of which shall
not exceed one hundred thousand dollars, divided into
shares of fiftydollarseach, to be subscribedand paid
for by individuals, companies , and corporations, in the
manner hereinafter specified; which subscribers and
shareholders, their successors and assigns, are hereby
created a body -politicand corporate,by the name and
style aforesaid, and by that name ,under the restrictions
hereinafter prescribed, shall be competent to contract
and be contracted with,to sue and be sued ,plead and
be impleaded , answer and be answered , defend and
be defended,in allcourtsand places,and in allmatters
whatever , as natural persons; with fullpower to acquire,
hold,possess,use,occupy,and enjoy,and the same to sell,
convey , and dispose of, allsuch real estate,goods ,effects,
and chattels as shall be convenient for the transaction of
itsbusiness (provided the value thereof shallnot exceed
twenty -fivethousand dollars), or which may be conveyed
to said institutionas surety for any debt ,or which may
be received in discharge of any debt,or purchase in sat-
isfactionof any judgment or decree in its favor, or in
the purchase of any property on which it may have a
lien; and said institutionmay have and use a common
seal,change , alter, and renew the same at pleasure ; and
may ordain and put in execution such by -laws ,rules and
regulations,for the government of the same as may be
deemed necessary: Provided, They be not contrary to the
Constitution and laws of this State or of the United
States .
§ 2. The institutionshall not at any time owe , either
by bond ,bill, note,or other contract,an amount exceed-
ing the amount of capitalstock actuallypaid in,exclu-
sive of sums due on deposit; and in cases of excess,the
president and directors, under whose administration it
shallhave taken place,shallbe liablefor any or all the
debts of said institution, in theirindividualcapacities,
by joint and several actions of debt against them , or any
of them , their heirs, executors,or administrators, in any
court having jurisdictionthereof,by any creditoror cred
itorsof the same ,and shall be prosecuted to judgment
and execution, any condition or agreement to the con-
trarynotwithstanding: Provided,That ifthe presidentor
any of the directorsmay be absent when the excess may
be contracted or created, or being present,shall dissent
from the act by which the excess is about to be contracted
or created,he or they shall not be liable under this sec-
tion, ifhe or they shall,within ten days from the creation
of such excess or dissentthereof, make affidavitof their
absence or dissent, and filethe same for record with the
recording officerof the county ; and moreover ,within ten
days give noticethereofin some newspaper printedin
the county , and shallin said notice calla meeting of the
shareholders, which they are hereby authorized to do .
§3 . That the business of the institutionshall be to
receive money on deposit, upon which it may pay an
interestto the depositor of not more than six per cent.
nor lessthan two per cent.per annum , as it may choose ,
dependent upon the length of time for which said deposit
may be made ; to loan money ,discount billsof exchange ,
the promissorynotesmade payable to any person or per-
sons or order, or payable to this institutionor order, and
negotiableand payable at theirbank ,or at any bank or
officeof discount and deposit, and indorsed to and dis-
counted by said institutionshall be , and are hereby ,
placedupon the same footingas foreignbillsofexchange ;
tobuy and sellforitsown purposes,forcompensation,on
commission or margin ,bonds , stocks, and all commercial
commodities and securities, and to do a general banking
business ,
§ 4. Said institutionshallnot at any time failor refuse
to pay itsdeposits in gold or silver, or currency of the
like kind and value of that deposited; and in case the
officers, in the usual business hours at their banking
house, shallrefuseor unreasonably delay payment as
aforesaid, then demandable by any person entitledto
receive the same ,said institutionshallbe liable to pay
damages at the rate of twelve per cent. per annum on
the amount thereof, from the time of such failure, re-
fusal,or delay,untilpayment thereof.
§5 . That the real and personal estate,business,prop-
erty, funds, and prudentialconcerns of said institution
shall be under the direction and control of five directors,
who shall be stockholders ; and after the firstelection
shall have been stockholders at least three months pre-
vious to their election; they shall be residents of this
State, and citizensof the United States, and after the
firstelectionthey shallbe elected annually on the second
Monday inJanuary. Each directorshallbe a stockholder
in hisown right. They shallholdtheirofficesforone
year , and until their successors shall be chosen . All
elections after the firstshall be conducted by two at
least of the stockholders appointed by the directors.
The stockholdersso appointed shallgive at leastthirty
days ' notice of the time and place of said election. The
electionshallbe by pluralityof votes,to be counted and
read in public afterthey are taken . No directoror officer
of any bank shallbe eligibleas a directorin thisinstitu-
tion,and any directorbecoming a directoror officerof a
bank , or while under protest in this institutionfor the
non -payment of debt, shall be held to have vacated his
office; nor shall two partners in trade, nor shall one
partner,while anotheris a directorin a bank , be eligi-
ble as directors in this institution at one and the same
time ; and if the president or any director or officerof
the institution shall fail or become insolvent after his
election or appointment , he shall become incapable to
serve, and shall be held to have vacated his place, nor
shall he be appointed to serve in this institutionuntil
his debts are paid, or until he obtains a fulldischarge
from the same ; nor shall any one who has ever failed
in business be eligibleto the officeof president,director,
or other officeruntilallhis debts are paid, or he be fully
discharged from same . If, from any cause , an election
should not be held on the day fixed by this charter, it
shallbe the duty of the board to give noticeimmediately ,
as before required, that an electionwill be held on the
firstMonday of the succeeding month ,and said election
shallbe conducted as required in the regular elections.
§6 . That at all meetings of the stockholders, and at
all elections under this charter , each shareholder shall be
entitledto one vote for every share held in his own right.
After the first election, no share shall entitle the holder
to a vote,unless the same has been held by the person
claiming to vote at least three months prior to the time ,
and so appear on the books of the institution. Any
stockholderentitledto vote may do so in person or by
proxy,such proxy being granted to a stockholderwho is
not eitherpresident,director,or other officerin the same ;
and no person who is not a citizen of the United States
shallbe permitted to vote on his stock.
§7 . That the directors shall select one of their own
number as president, who shall preside at all meetings ;
and in case of a vacancy in said office,the residue of the
directorsshall elect a president pro tem. They shallfill
all vacancies which may occur in their own body ,and
appoint such officers, clerks, and servants, as deemed
expedient, fixtheircompensation, define theirpowers
and prescribetheirduties,and shallrequireof them such
bonds,penalties, and securitiesas deemed requisitefor
the securityof the institution,which bonds shall be ex-
amined at leastonce a year , and be renewed ,from time
to time ,so as to secure the institutionfrom loss; and all
such officersshallhold theirplacesduring thepleasureof
the board .
§8 . The presidentand directors, any three of whom
may constitutea quorum for the transactionof business,
may , from time to time , make such by -laws ,rules and
regulations, for the government of the institution, as
deemed expedient,not contraryto the provisionsof this
charteror the by-laws and ruleswhich the stockholders,
at theirannual or other meetings, may , from time to
time,prescribe: Provided, For thatpurpose a concurrence
of a majority of allthe directorsshallbe necessary.
§ 9. The president and directorsshallhold stated meet-
ings at leastonce a year ,and calledmeetings may be had
whenever deemed necessary. All questionsbefore the
board shallbe taken viva vice; and the yeas and nays on
any proposition submitted shall be entered on record at
the request of any member ,and no vote shallbe recon-
sidered when a lessnumber ispresent than when the vote
was given .
§ 10. It shall be the duty of the president,on the first
day of January in each year,to pay to the Treasury of
thisState fiftycents on each one hundred dollars' of stock
held and paid for in said institution,which shallbe in full
of all tax or bonus .
§ 11. That it shallbe the duty of the presidentand
directors, and they are hereby required, as often as once
every three months ,to cause a strictexamination to be
made of the cash and cash accounts of the institution,
and a fulland complete statement shallbe made out and
entered on the journal of the proceedings of the board .
§12 . That itshallnot be lawful for the cashier,clerks,
teller, or other subordinate officers,eitherdirectlyor indi-
rectly,to engage in,or carryon,any otherbusinessthan
that of said institution, without the specialleave of the
president and directors; nor shall any of them , either
directlyor indirectly,become indebted to the same ,either
as borrower ,indorser, surety, or otherwise.
§13 . That if the cashier,clerks,teller,agent ,or other
officer, shall,without the authorityof the president and
directors,appropriate any of the funds of said corpora-
tion to his own use or that of any other person ,or shall
willfullyfailto make correctentries,or shallknowingly
make false entries,on the books of the institution, with
intent to cheat or defraud the corporation or any other
person,to hide or conceal any improper appropriationof
the funds,the officerso offending shallbe deemed guilty
of felony,and shall,upon conviction thereof,be sentenced
to confinement in the jailor penitentiaryof thisState for
a period of not lessthan two nor more than fiveyears.
§14 . The president and directorsshall keep a record
of theirproceedings, which they shallproduce to the
stockholders when by them demanded at any regular
meetings .
§ 15. The president,cashier, and other officers,before
entering upon the discharge of their respective duties,
shalltake an oath before some judicial officerfaithfully,
honestly, impartially, and to the best of their skilland
judgment ,to dischargeallthe dutiesof theirrespective
officesunder thischarter,or which may be requiredof
them by the by-laws , rules and regulations, of the cor-
poration.
§ 16. This institutionshall not contract for or receive
a greaterrate of interestthan at the legal rate per annum
forthe loan or use of money ; and intereston promissory
notes,negotiable and payable at the same ,and there dis-
counted , shall be calculated on the true time such notes
have to run .
§ 17. The president and directors shall issue certifi-
cates of stock to the holders thereof for so much as shall
be paid for; and the shares of the capital stock shall be
considered and held in law as personal property, and
assignable and transferable only in such manner and at
such place as the presidentand directorsshall,by their
by laws,prescribe. Certificatesof deposit shallbe oblig-
atory on said institution, and shall be transferable or
assignable when made payable to order.
§ 18. The general meeting of the stockholdersshall be
held annually on the second Monday in January in each
year ,at the time of the annual election,to which meet-
ing the president and directorsshallpresent an accurate
statement of the condition and affairsof the institution;
and general meetings of the stockholders may be called,
as providedin thischarter,or by the presidentand di-
rectors when they deem it desirable, or by any number
of stockholdersthe by -laws shallrequire,
§19 . That the persons above named are hereby con-
stituted commissioners to open books and receive sub .
scriptionsfor the capital stock of said institution, and to
superintend the election of the firstboard of directors,
any three of whom shall be competent to exercise the
powers and perform the dutiesrequiredby thissection.
§20 . The said commissioners shall have power , and
they are hereby authorized and required, on the second
Monday in March next,or at such other time within one
year thereafteras they shalldeem expedient, having
given not less than thirty days ' notice thereof in some
newspaper for the subscriptionof the capitalstock of
said institution, and cause books to be kept open from
10 o'clock A. M. until 2 o'clock P. M. , for at least ten
days , or untilat leastone hundred shares shallhave been
subscribed, when the same may be closed; and if more
than two thousand shares shall have been subscribed by
individuals, companies , and corporations, the commis-
sionersshalldeduct the excess from the largest subscrip-
tion in such manner that no subscriptionshallbe reduced ,
and leave the subscriptionof another larger.
§ 21. That if the whole two thousand shares of capital
stock shall not be taken when the books shall first be
opened ,the president and directorsmay cause the books
to be opened at any time and place they may direct,
givingthirtydays' noticethereofin some newspaper ,and
cause them to be kept open not less than ten days , or
until the whole of the balance of the stock shall have
been taken ; and the president and directorsmay require
such premium on the stock sold at the re-opening of the
books as they shall deem right, and such premium shall
be thepropertyof the institution.
§22 . That when not less than one hundred shares of
the capitalstockshallhave been taken,itshallbe their
duty to give notice in some public newspaper , and ap-
`point a day for the electionof the firstboard of directors,
who shall hold their officesuntil the succeeding annual
election,and not lessthan thirtynor more than sixtydays '
notice shall be given of the time and place of electing
said board ; and at least three of said incorporators shall
act as inspectorsof said election.
§ 23. That the payment of the shares of the capital
stock held by individuals, companies , and corporations
shall be made at the time and in the manner following ,
viz : Five dollars on each share to the commissioners at
the time of subscribing , and five dollars on each share
within ten days after the election of the firstboard of
directors, and five dollars every sixty days thereafter,
untilthe whole amount of said stockispaid: Provided,
That the board shallhave power to prolong the time for
the payment of each installment after one half of the
amount of each share shallhave been paid .
§ 24. Should any of the subscribersto the stock of said
institutionfailor refuse to pay for their stock, as herein
provided ,the president and directors,firstgiving public
notice in two or more newspapers for the space of thirty
days, by resolutionentered on the records, may forfeit
such stock, and proceed ,at such time as they may deem
expedient,tore-sellthe same ; and allpartialpayments
made on any stock which shall be forfeitedshall be so
sold for the benefit of such stockholder .
§ 25. That so soon as ten thousand dollarsof the capi-
tal stock shallhave been subscribed by individuals,com-
panies ,or corporations, as heretofore required,the presi-
dent and directors shall cause some suitable person to
count the money paid in,and to certifythe same to the
president and directors; and when he shall so certify,
and upon such appearing to be the fact, the said institu-
tion isthen hereby authorized to commence business.
§26 . This act shallbe in force from itspassage : Pro-
vided, An organization is effectedwithin twelve months
from its approval by the Governor ; but if no organiza-
tion is effectedwithin the above specifiedtime,thisact
shallbe void. The Legislature reservesthe rightto alter
and amend thisact at pleasure.
Approved April 15, 1882 .

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1882, ch. 978, p. 460
laws.summary: This statute amends an act related to the Shelbyville and Louisville Turnpike Road Company, stipulating that no tolls shall be charged to individuals traveling to or from school or church on Sundays, while imposing fines for those who falsely claim to be traveling for religious purposes.
page_titles: Amendment to the Shelbyville and Louisville Turnpike Road Company Act
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 978 .
AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act to amend and reduce into one
the severalacts in relationto the Shelbyvilleand LouisvilleTurnpike
Road Company ," approved February 28, 1882 .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1.That sectionsevenof an act,entitled" An actto
amend an act to amend and reduce into one the several
acts in relationto the Shelbyvilleand LouisvilleTurnpike
Road Company ," be amended by adding thereto follow-
ing words : " Said company shall charge no tollagainst
scholars going to or from school, or to persons going to
or from theiraccustomed placesof worship on Sunday ."
§2 . Whoever shall defraud , or attempt to defraud , the
company ,by traveling on said road on Sunday ,under the
pretext of going to or from church , when in factthey are
not going to or from church ,shall, for every such offense,
upon conviction,be fined ten dollars.
§3 . All finesimposed and paid under this act shallgo
to the common school fund of Jeffersoncounty .
§4 . This act shall take effect and be in force from
and afteritspassage .
Approved April 15 , 1882

laws.summary: This statute allows trustees of a school district to impose a tax on white male citizens for the purpose of funding education, thereby establishing a system that implicitly excludes Black citizens from participating in the educational funding process.
key_provisions: § 3. Said trustees shall have power to contract for a suitablebuilding and grounds ,in which the school in said districtshallbe held, without being required to erect any school building, and they in each year may impose a per capitatax of not exceeding one dollar and fiftycents on each white male citizenover the age of twenty -one years in said district,to be collectedby the sheriffof said county as other taxes are collected, and the proceeds applied by the trustees to the furnishing,repairing, and improvement of such grounds and buildings as the trus- tees may obtain,by lease or other contract,to be used for school purposes .

§5 . Said trusteesmay ,by an order entered upon their records, submit to the qualifiedwhite voters of said school districtat the August election, 1882, and not oftener than once in each year thereafter, at a regular election,the propositionto vote a tax in such sum as the trusteesmay direct, not exceeding twenty -five cents on each one hun- dred dollars' worth of taxable property in said school districtbelonging to white persons,to be applied to the payment of teachers in the districtschool. Such election shallbe heldby the regularofficersof electionunder the same rulesprovided by law for other elections; and if, at any electionheld forthat purpose,as herein provided,a majority of the legallyqualifiedwhite voters in said dis- trictshallbe cast in favor of such tax,itshallbe the duty of the county judge of said county, upon presentation to him of a certificate to that effect from the officers of election,to enterupon the order-book of the county court an orderimposing such tax as may be voted. Said tax shallbe collectedby the sheriffof said county as other taxesare directedby law to be collected,and paid to the treasurer of the board of trustees .

§7 . No provision of thisact shallbe construed so as to affectin anywise the general law in relation to schools for colored childrenin said district,nor shall any colored person be subjectto any tax or receiveany benefitcon- templated by thisact.

CHAPTER 980 .
AN ACT for the benefit of common school district No. 25 , in Oldham
county .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1. The boundary of common schooldistrictNo. 25,in
Oldham county,known as the Lagrange district,shallbe
as follows : Beginning at the residence of William Dun-
can ; thence to the residence of M. Hoagland ; thence to
the residence of Ben . Callahan ; thence to the residence
of John Buckner ; thence to the residence of John Taylor ;
thence to the residence of Samuel Blakemore ; thence to
the residence of Wm . Ratcliffe; thence to the residence
of Alex .Mackey ,including Morris Phelan and Quinn ;
thence with a straightline to the beginning . Said dis-
trictshall embrace all persons living in said boundary ,
including the persons named in the foregoing boundary ;
and the cominon school commissioner of said county shall
have no power to alter or change said districtin any
respect, and no election for trustees shall hereafter be
held in said district .
§2 . The present board of trustees of the Funk Semi-
nary in Lagrange ,and thosewho may hereafterbe cho-
sen to fillvacancies in said board of trustees,shall be
ex officiotrusteesof said common school district, with
perpetual succession; and the officerschosen by said Funk
Seminary trustees shall likewise be the officersof the
common school trustees. In all matters pertaining to
the management of the common schools in said district,
said trusteesshallbe subject to the provisions of the gen-
eral law ,except as herein otherwise provided .
§ 3. Said trustees shall have power to contract for a
suitablebuilding and grounds ,in which the school in said
districtshallbe held, without being required to erect any
school building, and they in each year may impose a
per capitatax of not exceeding one dollar and fiftycents
on each white male citizenover the age of twenty -one
years in said district,to be collectedby the sheriffof said
county as other taxes are collected, and the proceeds
applied by the trustees to the furnishing,repairing, and
improvement of such grounds and buildings as the trus-
tees may obtain,by lease or other contract,to be used for
school purposes .
§4 . Said trustees are hereby empowered to receive
and invest any money heretofore collected by taxation
for the purpose of erecting a common school-house in
saiddistrict,and they shallapply the income of any such
fund towards the payment of teachers in said district.
They may also receive any bequest or donation hereto-
foremade ,or which may hereafterbe made forthebene-
fitof saiddistrict,and apply the same as directedby the
donor or devisor,and in the absence of such direction, in
such manner as in theirdiscretionwill best promote the
interest of the districtschool. They may employ any
number of teachers that may be necessary to properly
conduct the school in said district, and the amount that
may be due said districtin each school year ,from the
common school fund of the State, shall be paid upon the
order of the board of trustees to their treasurer , and be
by him applied to the payment of teachers, as the board
may direct. But no teacher shallbe employed by said
trusteeswho is not qualifiedas provided by the general
law .
§5 . Said trusteesmay ,by an order entered upon their
records, submit to the qualifiedwhite voters of said school
districtat the August election, 1882, and not oftener than
once in each year thereafter, at a regular election,the
propositionto vote a tax in such sum as the trusteesmay
direct, not exceeding twenty -five cents on each one hun-
dred dollars' worth of taxable property in said school
districtbelonging to white persons,to be applied to the
payment of teachers in the districtschool. Such election
shallbe heldby the regularofficersof electionunder the
same rulesprovided by law for other elections; and if, at
any electionheld forthat purpose,as herein provided,a
majority of the legallyqualifiedwhite voters in said dis-
trictshallbe cast in favor of such tax,itshallbe the duty
of the county judge of said county, upon presentation
to him of a certificate to that effect from the officers of
election,to enterupon the order-book of the county court
an orderimposing such tax as may be voted. Said tax
shallbe collectedby the sheriffof said county as other
taxesare directedby law to be collected,and paid to the
treasurer of the board of trustees .
§ 6. For all the purposes of this act said trustees are
created a body -politicand corporate,and they may sue
and be sued ,defend and be defended , in any court of this
Commonwealth , by the name of The Trustees of Com-
mon School DistrictNo. 25,in Oldham county .
§7 . No provision of thisact shallbe construed so as to
affectin anywise the general law in relation to schools
for colored childrenin said district,nor shall any colored
person be subjectto any tax or receiveany benefitcon-
templated by thisact.
§ 8. This act shall take effect from and after the 15th
day of June , 1882.
Approved April 15 , 1882 .

laws.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the Swiss colony in Bernstadt, Laurel county.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1882, ch. 985, pp. 468–469
laws.summary: This statute allows for the creation of a special school district for children who are not proficient in English, permitting instruction in French and German while mandating daily English instruction. It reflects a segregated approach to education based on language proficiency, which historically aligns with Jim Crow practices.
page_titles: Establishment of a Special School District
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 985 .
AN ACT for the benefitof the Swiss colony in Bernstadt, Laurel county .
WHEREAS , A censusof the pupilchildren,now fifty-five
(55) in number ,of theSwiss colony at Bernstadt,Laurel
county , could not be taken in time to enable the com-
missioner of common schools to lay off a special district
for theirbenefit; and whereas ,the said children are not
sufficientlyacquainted with the English language to be
profited by attending the neighboring districtschools;
therefore ,
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That the commissioners of common schoolsishere-
by authorized to lay off,under the directionof the Super-
intendent of Public Insrtuction, a special school district
in said county ,embracing all the pupil children of said
colony , and to appoint a board of trusteesforsaid district.
§2 . The course of instruction for the common school
of said districtshall be the same as that prescribed for
the common schools of the State,but may be conducted
through the media of the French and German languages :
Provided, That the English language be daily and duly
taughtto everypupil of the school; but nothing in this
act shall be construed to authorize the conduct of any
other common school in the Commonwealth except
through the exclusive medium of the English language .
§3 . The text-books for said school shall be prescribed
by the State Board of Education , and the teacher of said
school must duly obtain a county certificateor a State
certificatebefore entering upon the discharge of his
duties .
§4 . That when said school shall have been taught ac-
cording to law and the provisions of this act,the com-
missionersshallduly report the same tothe Superintendent
of Public Instruction, as every common school is now re-
ported, for approval and for payment .
§ 5. This actshalltake effectfrom itspassage,and be
in force until the regular meeting of the next General
Assembly .
Approved April 15 , 1882 .

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1882, ch. 1019, pp. 501–502
laws.summary: This statute appropriates property formerly owned by a deceased colored individual for the benefit of colored schools in Petersburg, Kentucky, establishing trustees to manage the property and its income for educational purposes.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 1019 . AN ACT forthe benefitof the coloredschoolsin Petersburg,Kentucky . WHEREAS , It is represented to the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky that Samuel Youell , colored,died intestatein the year 1872, in the town of Petersburg ,county of Boone ,State of Kentucky ,owning at the time of his death lots No. 172 and No. 173 in said town , without heirs entitled to the same ; and whereas , a petitionfrom sundry citizensof the town of Petersburg has been presented to thisGeneral Assembly ,praying for the appropriation of said property to the use and for the benefitof the colored schools in said town ; therefore, Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth of Kentucky :

§1 . That lots No. 172 and No. 173 in the town of Pe- tersburg, county of Boone , State of Kentucky ,formerly the property of said Samuel Youell , deceased , now the propertyof the Commonwealth of Kentucky ,by escheat, be ,and the same are hereby , appropriated to the use and for the benefit of the colored schools of said town .

§2 . That S. G. Botts,R. Randall , and W. H Terrill, be ,and they are hereby , made and appointed trustees, in whom the titleto said lots is hereby vested for the pur- poses aforesaid; and they shallhave power and authority to leasethe same from year to year,and apply the rents and profitsaccruing therefrom in aid of said schools; or they may ,in theirdiscretion,use one or both of said lots for said school purposes ; or they may selland convey one or both of them , and reinvest the proceeds of the sale in other real estate for school purposes , as aforesaid; or in some other safe investment , and apply the income therefrom to the education of the colored children in said town .

CHAPTER 1019 .
AN ACT forthe benefitof the coloredschoolsin Petersburg,Kentucky .
WHEREAS , It is represented to the General Assembly
of the Commonwealth of Kentucky that Samuel Youell ,
colored,died intestatein the year 1872, in the town of
Petersburg ,county of Boone ,State of Kentucky ,owning
at the time of his death lots No. 172 and No. 173 in said
town , without heirs entitled to the same ; and whereas , a
petitionfrom sundry citizensof the town of Petersburg
has been presented to thisGeneral Assembly ,praying for
the appropriation of said property to the use and for the
benefitof the colored schools in said town ; therefore,
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That lots No. 172 and No. 173 in the town of Pe-
tersburg, county of Boone , State of Kentucky ,formerly
the property of said Samuel Youell , deceased , now the
propertyof the Commonwealth of Kentucky ,by escheat,
be ,and the same are hereby , appropriated to the use and
for the benefit of the colored schools of said town .
§2 . That S. G. Botts,R. Randall , and W. H Terrill,
be ,and they are hereby , made and appointed trustees, in
whom the titleto said lots is hereby vested for the pur-
poses aforesaid; and they shallhave power and authority
to leasethe same from year to year,and apply the rents
and profitsaccruing therefrom in aid of said schools; or
they may ,in theirdiscretion,use one or both of said lots
for said school purposes ; or they may selland convey
one or both of them , and reinvest the proceeds of the

or in some other safe investment , and apply the income

laws.title: AN ACT to establish an additional voting place in the Marion precinct, in Crittenden county.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1882, ch. 1051, p. 540
laws.summary: This statute establishes an additional voting place in the Marion precinct of Crittenden County, requiring voters on different sides of a road to vote at different polling places, which can be interpreted as a mechanism to segregate voters based on their residence.
page_titles: Establishment of Additional Voting Place in Crittenden County
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1051 .
AN ACT to establishan additionalvoting place in the Marion precinct,in
Crittenden county .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That an additionalvoting place be ,and the same is
hereby ,created and establishedin precinct number one ,
in Crittenden county ,said place of voting to be at such
house in the town of Marion ,or such part of the court-
house as may be designated by the Crittenden county
court , by an order entered of record in said court at some
regular term to be held at least ten days before a regular
or specialelection; and said place of voting,when des-
ignated by the county court,shall be known as polling
place number two in said electiondistrict,and the voting
place now provided by law shall be known as polling
place number one .
§2 . It shall be the duty of the county court of said
county to appoint officersof electionto take the vote at
said pollingplaces numbers one and two at the same time
thatofficersof electionare appointed in the other pre-
cincts of said county .
§ 3. All voters in said election district number one liv-
ing on the west side of the Princeton and Ford's Ferry
road are required to vote at polling place number one in
said precinct, and those living on the east side of said
road shallvote at polling place number two in said pre-
cinct .
§4 . The sheriff of Crittenden county is required to
cause fiftynoticesto be printedin large type,tobe paid
for as other election expenses , and cause said notices to
be posted through said electionprecinct, at leastten days
before the next regular election,informing the citizensof
the provisions of this act .
§ 5. This act shall take effectfrom and after itspas-
sage .
Approved April 15, 1882.

vent horse -racing , or fast or reckless riding in the streets ;

§ 38. Said council shallhave exclusive jurisdictionof

country .
§40 . This act to be in full force and effect when rati-
fiedby a majority of the legal votes in said limits.

Be it enactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth

§ 1. That the titleto the act to organize and establish
a system of public schools in the city of Bowling Green

be ,and the same is hereby , amended by strikingout the

not exceed ," and before the words " the said bonds ," and
insertingin lieuthereof the words " thirty-fivethousand ,"
and also by striking out the words " Provided, That no
propertybelongingto coloredpersons shallbe subjectto
any taxationprovidedforin thisact;" and alsoby strik-
ing out the words " ten cents," occurring after the words
" shall not exceed ," and before the words " on each one
hundred dollars," and insertingin lieu thereof the words
" twelve cents ."
§5 . Section thirteen of the act to which this act is an
amendment ishereby amended by strikingout the words ,
" a certifiedcopy of said order or minute shall be pub-
lishedin the Bowling Green newspapers for at least
twenty days preceding said election,such publication to
continue until the time of said election," and in lieu
thereof these words shallbe inserted: " said electionmay
be held ten days afternoticeof the time and places of
voting shallhave been given by publicationin any one
of the newspapers publishedin Bowling Green," and also
by strikingout the words," immediatelyqualifiedand ."
§ 6. Section fourteen of the act to which this act is
an amendment is hereby amended by strikingout the
words " twenty cents," occurring afterthe words " not ex .
ceeding ," and before the words , " upon each one hundred
dollars," and insertingin lieuthereof the words " twenty-
eight cents," and also amended by strikingout the proviso
in the lastclause of said section,which provisoisin the
followingwords , to-wit: " That the property of colored
persons shallnot be taxed under thisact."
§7 . The board of trustees of said schools shallestab-
lishand maintain separate school buildingsfor white and
colored children,and no white childshallbe permitted to
attendthe schoolsprovided for coloredchildren,and no
colored child shall be allowed to attend the schools pro-
vided for white children; and untilsuitablebuildings can
be erectedor purchased,saidboard of trusteesmay lease
for one or more years any building or part of a building
forthe purpose of carryingon any ofthe schoolsprovided
for herein .
§8 . The board of councilmen may make the firstlevy
of taxes for the payment of the interestor principalof
the bonds to be issued, and for defraying the current ex-
penses of said schools,upon the same propertyand the
same pollsassessedby the cityfor the general revenue of

herein may be made at any time within ten days after

majorityof the tax-payers voting have voted in favor of
the issualof the bonds provided for herein.
§ 9. All laws or parts of laws in conflictwith thisact
be , and the same are hereby ,repealed.
§ 10. This act shall take effect and be in force from and
afterits passage .

CHAPTER 1136 .
AN ACT in relationto the town of Providence, in Webster county .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That an act , entitled " An act to regulate and
make uniform the jurisdictionof police officersin the
counties of Webster and Monroe ," approved February
23 , 1874 , be , and the same is hereby , so amended as not
to apply to the town of Providence , in said Webster
county .
§2 . That the incorporation boundary of the said town
of Providence be , and the same is, so changed as to
include allthe adjacent railroadbeds and depot grounds .
§3 . That the board of trustees for the said town of
Providence shall consist of five white male members and
legal voters of the town .
§4 . That the board of trustees for the said town of
Providence shall have power to make all by -laws regu-
lating the public works and expenditures of the town .
§5 . That all former acts and resolutions of the board
of trustees for the said town of Providence are hereby
approved ,so far as relatesto repairing streetsand assess-
ing taxes .
§6 . All acts parts of acts in conflictwith thisact are
hereby repealed.
§7 . That this act shall take effect from and after its
passage .
Approved April 19,1882 .

CHAPTER 1144 .
AN ACT to amend , digest, and reduce into one all acts incorporatingthe
city of Lexington .
Be itenactedby the General Assembly ofthe Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
60
§1 . That so much of the county of Fayette as is con-
tained within the following bounds ,to-wit: One mile from
the court-house in every direction,shallbe ,and hereby is
declared to be , a city, and the inhabitants thereof are
continued a body -corporate and politic, with perpetual
succession, by the name and styleof the City of Lex-
ington," with power to govern themselves by such
ordinances and resolutionsfor municipal purposes as
they may deem proper ,not to conflictwith the charter
nor the Constitution of thisState,nor the Constitution of
the United States; to acquire property for municipal pur-
poses,by purchase or otherwise; to hold the same and all
property and effectsnow belonging to said city, held
either in its own name or in the name of others , for the
use of said city,for the purposes and interestsfor which
the same were granted or dedicated; to use, manage ,im-
prove , sell,and convey , rent or lease the same , and to
have likepowers over property hereinafteracquired ; and
as such , by that name ,shall be capable in law of con-
tracting and being contracted with, of suing and being
sued , of pleading and being impleaded , answering and
being answered , into all courts and places, and in all
matters whatsoever ; and may have and use a corporate
seal, and change ,alter, and renew the same at pleasure.
§2 . The fiscal,prudential,and municipal concerns of
said city, with the government and control thereof,shall
be vested in one principalofficerto be calledthe mayor ,
and one city council,consistingof twelve persons,to be
denominated the board of councilmen ,who shall be elected
the firstSaturday in March next in the way hereinafter
prescribed, all of whom shall hold their officesfor two
years,and untiltheirsuccessors shallbe duly elected and
qualified; all of said officersshall have resided in said
citytwo years next precedingtheirelection,shallbe male
citizensof the United States and of this State,bona fide
residents of the ward for which they may be chosen ,
housekeepersor owners of real estatein said city,hold
no other civiloffice,nor be directly or indirectlyinter-
estedin any contractwith saidcityor in any application
therefor,or a candidateforor hold any officeor employ-
ment for pay in any company or corporation which holds
or is an applicant for any contract with said city, the
terms,rates,or prices of which are subject to modifica-
tion or enforcement by the board of councilmen , nor be
in arrears to the cityfor money collected or held without
a settlement or quietus therefor. Stockholders in other
corporations may be eligible, but shall not vote on or
interferedirectlyor indirectlywith any matter or ques-
tion affectingany contractbetween such company and
the city,or affecting any right or duty under any such
contract- and allsaid officersshallhave attained the age
of twenty -four years . The absence of any of the fore-
going qualificationsshallrender a person ineligibleeither
as mayor or councilman , and if occurring after election
or during his term of office, shallwork a forfeitureof his
office, and the board of councilmen shallso declare, pro-
ceed to fillthe vacancy as hereinafter prescribed.
Wards .
§3 . That itshallbe the duty of said mayor and coun-
cilmen that shallbe firstelected under this act to lay off
the said city into four wards , for the purposes herein
named , as nearly equal as possible as to number of
inhabitants, improvements , and permanent boundaries ,
each of which wards is to be entitled to elect three coun-
cilmen , to be members of the board of councilmen ; but
the mayor and councilmen may , in their discretion,
increase the number of said wards to not exceeding
twelve , with at alltimes an equal number of councilmen
from each ward ; and it shallbe the duty of said mayor
and councilmen , from time to time , to alter the bounda-
ries of the wards so as to equalize the number of the
inhabitantsin each as nigh as may be; but such altera-
LOC L , VOL . 11-39
tion shallnot be made except on a general census of all
the inhabitantsbeing previouslytaken.
City Elections.
§4 . That on the firstSaturday in March ,in 1882, and
on the same date bienniallythereafter,the male inhabi-
tants over twenty -one years of age of said city, who at
the time being are citizens of the State of Kentucky ,
and inhabitantsof said city, and bona fide residents
thereof for the space of six calendar months previous to
said election,and of the ward in which he offersto vote
at least sixtydays prior to the election, and who shall
have paid the capitationtax assessedby the cityon or
before the fifteenthday of January preceding the day of
election,shallmeet in wards in which they respectively
reside, and vote for the councilmen such ward shall be
entitledto elect, and for a mayor , a city attorney, a
treasurer, a collector, an assessorand auditor, a city
physician,a surveyor, a keeper of the poor and work-
house ,a recorder and clerk of the recorder'scourt,allof
whom shall hold officefor the term of two years, and
until their successors shall qualify; and it shall be the
duty of the mayor and councilmen in officeto cause an
alphabeticallistof the qualified voters in each ward to
be made out ten days before the firstSaturday in March ,
and to appoint three suitable persons in each ward as
inspectorsof the election,and to furnishthem with a list
of voters,and a warrant directingthem , or a majority of
them , to hold the election in the same manner as other
elections are held in this State . Notice of the time and
place of holding the electionsin the respective wards
shallbe publishedin one or more of the public newspa-
pers printed in said city, with the names of the ward
inspectors. The election shall be held during the same
hours, to be directedby the mayor and councilmen ,in all
the wards ; the saidinspectorsshallexhibitto allpersons
claimingthe same the listof the qualifiedvotersrespect-
ively; and on closing the pollsat the hour mentioned in
theirwarrant ,they shall declare the same , and the three
persons having the highest number of qualifiedvotes
shall be declared as duly elected councilmen in each
ward . The vote given for mayor shall be added up by
the inspectors, and the poll-books shall be certifiedby a
majority of said inspectors and sworn to as just and
true returns of the election , which oath shall be admin-
isteredby the clerk of the county court or any justice of
the peace . The inspectors shall return said poll-books
to the board of examiners for Fayette county within
three days next aftersaid election.
§5 . That in the event of the death , resignation,ineli-
gibility, or refusalto act of the mayor ,the councilmen
shallproceed to electone of their own number to supply
his place ,and the person so elected shallbe the mayor of
said cityuntila new electionishad and the mayor elected
is sworn into office; and the mayor and the councilmen
shall immediately proceed to order another election to
supply such vacancy for the residue of the time as in the
originalelectionof said mayor ; and in the like event of
one or more councilmen , the board shall direct a new
election in the ward or wards in which the vacancy shall
happen ; and in case of a vacancy in eitherof the other

CHAPTER 1344 .
AN ACT to establish a system of common schools for the town of Beech
Grove , McLean county .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That William H. Hardin , M. G. Ashby , W. H.
Jobe,S. S. Tinsley,and James Tinsley, the presenttrus-
tees of said town of Beech Grove , and theirsuccessors,
be ,and they are hereby ,constituteda board of education
for said town , and so much of school districtNo. 5 as is
included.in corporate limitsof said town ,whose duty it
shallbe to control and manage the public school within
saidboundary; and by that name shallbe known as a
body -politic and corporate ; may contract and be con-
tracted with , sue and be sued; may buy and sellreal
estate and personal property; and the titleto all school
property in said districtshallvest in said board and their
successors forever .
§2 . That the chairman of the board of trustees of
Beech Grove shall be the chairman of the board of educa-
tion for said district .
§3 . The board of educationshallelecta secretaryand
treasurer,and itshallbe the duty of saidboard to require
of said treasurer elect a good and sufficientbond for the
faithfulperformance of hisdutiesas such. It shallbe the
duty of the treasurer to receive all moneys ,from what-
ever source,receiptfor the same ,and pay it out on the
order of the chairman ,taking a receiptfor the same ,and
at all times keep a record of his acts always open for
inspectionby said board,and perform such otherduties
as may be prescribedby said board of education. The
1
secretary shall attend all meetings of the board , keep
theirrecordsand papers,and perform such otherduties
as the board may prescribe from time to time .
§4. Should a vacancy occurinsaidboard of education,
it shall be the duty of the board to electand supply any
such vacancy that may occur from time to time,said elec-
tion to be forthe unexpired term of the person or persons
vacating .
§5 . The controland management of thepublicschool
of the town of Beech Grove ,and the propertyand funds
belonging thereto, and which may accrue in any way to
them , or for theirestablishment,management ,or mainte-
nance under this act or otherwise , shall be vested in said
board of education and their successors in office.
§6 . The said board of education shallhave power to
make allby -laws and rules for the government of them-
selves and theirappointees,and for the dispatch of busi-
ness, and for the management ,control, and government
of the schools,and to enforcesuch by-laws and rulesby
suitablefinesand penalties,to be recovered in any court
haying jurisdictionof the amount ; and allsuch finesand
forfeituresshall be paid to the treasurer of said board of
educationby the collectingofficer,and shallbe a part of
the school fund for said district .
§7 . A majority of the members of said board shallcon-
stitutea quorum for the transactionof business. They
shall meet at least once in each month , and shall fix the
time of their meeting , and shall meet as often as to them
may seem necessary for the transaction of business.
§8. The board of education shall appoint allteachers
and other persons necessary to successfullycarry on said
school,and prescribeallrulesfor itsgovernment ,and fix
their compensation or salaries, and may dismiss or sus-
pend any teacher or other person appointedby them .
The board shall prescribe the branches of education to
be taught in the school,and grade the same in future as
may seem necessary by the board .
§ 9. That allwhite children over six and under twenty
years of age within said districtshallhave equal rightof
admission to the school of said district,and no fees or
charges for their tuitionshall ever be charged in said
school; but the board of education therein has the right
to admit any whitenon -residentpupilintothe saidschool
upon such terms and conditions, and upon payment of
such charges as to the said board may seem reasonable .
§ 10. That the trustees of the town of Beech Grove
are hereby directedand empowered to levy a tax not to
exceed twenty -five cents on the one hundred dollars'
worth of taxable propertyin said town ,to be collected
and paid to the treasurer of the board of education for
school purposes ,to be paid out by him on the order of
the chairman of the board of education .
§11 The propertyof whitepersonsonlyshallbe taxed
for the purposes herein indicated.
§ 12. That the provisions herein shallbe construed as
to require that said school shall be taught in said town
at leastfivemonths in each year ,or any other time that
may be establishedby the common schools in the State
of Kentucky .
§ 13. This act shall be in force from and afteritspas-
sage .
Approved April 22, 1882 .
