CHAPTER 1356 .
AN ACT to incorporate the Perpetual Mutual Benefit Association .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That W. F. Bell,Fayette Hewitt ,James Montgom- Incorporators.
ery,Ivy Twyman ,Wm . Ditto, W. J. Macey ,F. P. Straus ,
A. B. Montgomery ,C. M. Fraize,J. W. Matthis, W. H.
Marriott,J. E. Sheets,John Highbaugh ,George W. Strick-
ler, Samuel Gray , T. R. McBeath , Nick Mercer , Enos
Keith ,D. M. Rodman , and theirassociatesand successors,
be,and they are hereby,createda body-politic,under the
name of " The Perpetual Mutual Benefit Association," Style.
with power to sue and be sued ,contract and be contracted
with ; and shallhave perpetual succession, with the right
to hold all real estate or other funds necessary in the
judgment of the board of directorsfor itsuses and pur-
poses, and may dispose of the same ; and may make and
use a common seal,renewable and changeable at pleas-
ure ; and may make such by -laws and regulationsas may
be deemed necessary for fullycarrying out the purposes
of this act of incorporation, not inconsistent with the
laws of United States or of this State .
§2 . The principalplace of business of said corporation Placeofbusiness
shallbe in Elizabethtown ,Kentucky , and any fiveof the
incorporators named in preceding section may ,in person
or by proxy , proceed to organize and elect a board of
directorsand other officersprovided for herein.
Directors .
Purposes .
§3 . The affairsof said association shall be managed
by a board of directorsof not lessthan five(5) nor more
than twenty-one (21),five(5) of whom shallbe residents
of Hardin county and counties contiguous thereto, and
constitutea local board ,who shall manage the affairsof
the association,and a majority of whom shallconstitute
a quorum . The remaining sixteen (16) shall constitute
an advisory board ,and may reside in any portion of the
United States; they shall be chosen by the members of
the association upon the second Monday in January of
each and every year , and shall hold their officesuntil
their successors are qualified. Vacancies in the board of
directorsmay be filledby the board itself,and any director
so elected shall hold his officeuntil the subsequent an-
nual meeting ; and in case no electionisheld on the day
named ,the president,by order of the board of directors,
may calla meeting for such purpose,upon ten days'no-
ticepublished in some paper in Elizabethtown or Louis-
ville. This board shallelectfrom theirnumber a president
and secretary,or such other officersas they may deem
requisitefor the management of the business of the asso-
ciation, and may ,by by -laws ,regulate the duties of each .
§4 . The object of this association is to create and
provide a beneficiary fund for the families or relations
of deceased members , or for the benefit of members in
sickness , and the board of directors shall determine who
shallbe members ,upon what terms they willbe received;
may reject all applications for membership ; fix and de-
termine the sums to be paid by members , either upon
admission or as monthly dues , and control and invest the
funds as they may deem best; may require bonds for the
faithfulperformance of theirduty from the officerschosen.
to manage the business,and do allother acts necessary to
fullycarryout the benevolentpurpose of the association.
§5 . The members of the associationshallbe arranged
as they are recorded into divisions. No divisions shall
exceed two thousand members . Members shall be sober ,
discreet,peaceable ,moral men . New members may be
admitted to any divisionat any time tillthe same isfull..
i
Each division,except those named in section six(6),shall
be filledbefore another is begun , and kept filledas fast
as vacancies occur .
§6 . There may be one or more divisions,to be com-
posed only of citizens of Hardin county and counties
contiguousthereto,which shallpay on each whole policy,
on the death of the insured, $ 2,000, and on each half
policy $ 1,000,and the members thereof shallbe assessed
at each death in the proportions provided in section nine
(9) sufficientto pay the policy,providedthe assessments
shallbe as provided in section nine (9),and the amount
paid on each policy as provided in section thirteen(13),
until there shall be enrolled in the division at least 200
members .
§7 . Upon the decease of any member of thisassocia-
tion,the fund to which his family is entitledshallbe paid
as may be designated in the application for membership ,
or by will of the member ; thisbeing changed by death,or
otherwiseimpossible,itshallgo- first,to the widow and
children; second ,to his mother ; third,to his legal heirs.
The fund due deceased members shall not be subject to
the claims of creditors,and shallnot be reached by attach-
ment , garnishment , or other process of law , so as to
divert from the family of such members .
§ 8. There shall be an admission fee of six dollars and Admissionfee.
such annual dues as may be requiredby the board of
directors, and upon the death of a member an assessment
such as may be determinedto be just,as hereinafterpro-
vided ,the board of directorshaving power to change the
admission fee and annual dues as , and in the same man-
ner,they are empowered to change assessments.
§ 9. The members shallbe divided intoclassesaccording Classes.
totheirseveralages ;those from twenty -one (21) to twenty-
five(25) shallconstituteone class,those from twenty -five
(25) to twenty-nine (29) another,thosefrom twenty-nine
(29) to thirty-three(33) another,those from thirty-three
(33) to thirty-six(36) another,those from thirty-six (36)
to thirty-nine (39) another,thosefrom thirty-nine (39) to
forty-two (42) another ,those from forty-two (42) to forty-
five(45) another,those from forty-five(45) to forty-seven
(47) another,thosefrom forty-seven (47) to forty-nine (49)
another,those from forty-nine (49) to fifty-one (51) an-
other,thosefrom fifty-one (51) to fifty-three(53) another,
those from fifty- three (53) to fifty-five (55) another, and
every year thereafter shall constitute a class. The as-
sessments at each death of a full member , and of each
half member ,where his policyhas to be paid by assess-
ment ,and not out of the surplus as hereinafterprovided ,
shall be as follows: On the death of a whole member ,
seventy cents on each full member of the age of the
firstclass, seventy-fivecents on each full mumber of the
age of the second class,and thus increasing itfivecents
on each full member of each class up to and including
fifty-seven (57) years,and one half of the above amounts
on each half member ; and upon the death of a half mem-
ber , the assessment on each full member shall be the
same as on a half member upon the death of a fullmem-
ber as above,and upon a half member one half of that
upon a fullmember . The board of directorsshallfixthe
amount of assessments on all over fifty-seven (57) years
old, and may , by a two -thirds vote, change the classes
and assessments on the classes in each division , to be
submitted to a vote of the members of such division
before the change takes effect.
§ 10. No member shall be taken in this association
whose business requires him to travel on railroads one
fifth or more of his time , or whose residence is south of
the thirty-sixth(36th) degree of north latitude; and any
one remaining or going south of that degree of latitude
between the first of June and the fifteenth of October ,
without the permission of the presidentor board of direct-
ors,and shallthereby,beforehe obtainssuch permission,
contractany diseasefrom which death ensues,the policy
shall be void .
§ 11. The members of each county shall constitute a
body , a majority of whom may hold meetings to elect
delegates to represent them in voting and otherwise as
they may direct,and may , at these meetings ,require the
board of directorsto lay before them a fullstatement of
the transactions of the association in the month of Feb-
ruaryin each year.
§ 12. Upon receiving notice of the death of a member ,
the secretary or other officershall send notice of same to
each surviving member of his division ,and demand ,with-
in thirtydays,the assessment made upon each. If any
member shallfailto pay within thirtydays from the send-
ing of this notice,he shall forfeitall rightsin the asso-
ciation and all claims to its benefits, and can only be
reinstatedby a two-thirds vote of the board of directors,
and the payment of allarrearages; a notice addressed to
the member at post-officenamed in the applicationfor
membership ,or other address subsequently furnished the
association,shall be considered a legal notice for allthe
purposes herein.
§ 13. The fund due deceased members shallbe paid
within sixty(60) days after legal notice of the death of
such member is given to the association,and such legal
notice of death shall be the written claim of the bene-
ficiaryof deceased member ,giving name ,age ,place,and
circumstance and cause of death , accompanied by the
sworn statement of his physician,and the minister or un-
dertaker officiatingat the funeral of such member ,that
he died as set out in the claim . Unless such claim is
asserted within one year from the death of a member ,
any right of recovery shall be forfeited. The amount
paid by the associationas a beneficiaryfund to deceased
members shallnot exceed two thousand ($2,000) dollars,
and shallnot be lessthan ninety (90) per cent. of the
assessment realized from every member of the division
in which deceased member was registered. The living
members shallbe bound in law to pay allassessments
made and dues; but they may withdraw from the asso-
ciationby giving written notice to the secretary or chief
officerof the associationof such intention. After giving
this notice, all liabilityfor assessments and dues shall
cease and determine , as shall also any liabilityof the
association to him .
§14 . Whenever the surplus of funds in the hands of
the associationfor any divisionshallexceed fivethousand
($ 5,000) dollars,enough to pay a policy,the excessshall
be appliedtopayment of policies,and theboard of direct-
ors may pay policiesout of the surplus when less than
that amount is on hand . Such payments on each policy
shallequal the amount realizedfrom the lastassessment
in that division .
§ 15. The members shall in no way be liablefor the
debts of the association .
§ 16. This associationshallnot be subjectto the in-
surance laws of this Commonwealth , nor shall they be
required to make any deposit or pay any tax or charge
requiredof lifeinsurancecompanies,but may reportto
the Insurance Bureau annually,or oftener if they desire.
§ 17. This act shall take effectfrom and afteritspas-
sage .
Approved April 24, 1882 .

CHAPTER 1391 .
AN ACT to amend the charter of the town of Columbus , in Hickman
county .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1. That an act,entitled" An act to amend the char-
ter of the city of Columbus , in Hickman county ," ap-
proved March 18th, 1872,be so amended as to read : that
no person shallbe allowed to vote at any municipal elec-
tion in said cityuntilthe person offeringto vote shall
have paid all poll-taxes due said city of Columbus by
the person offeringhis vote .
§ 2. This act shalltake effectfrom and after itspas-
sage .
Approved April 24, 1882.

CHAPTER 1419 .
AN ACT to incorporatethe Emmett Mutual Aid Association.
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That Wm . McCready , W. B. Hoke ,John McAteer , Incorporators.
M. Boland , James A. Hagan ,Frank P. Carroll, Herbert
Kelly ,M. J. McAuliffe ,Frank E. Corrigan , Wm . O'Con-
ner,John Gillen,Matt O'Doherty,and John R Seers,and
their associates and successors, be, and they are hereby ,
createda body-corporate,with perpetualsuccession,un-
der the name of " The Emmett Mutual Aid Association ," Style.
the object being to provide financialaid to the widows
orphans , heirs, devisees, and assigns of deceased mem-
bers of the association ; and under said name it shall
have power to contract and be contracted with ,sue and
be sued , in all the courts of this Commonwealth .
§ 2. The principal place of business of said corpora- Placeofbusiness
tion shall be in Louisville, Kentucky , where allelections
for directorsand officersshallbe held ; and every member
of this association being entitled to one vote in electing
said board of directors, and said vote may be cast by
the member in person or by hiswrittenproxy.
§3 . The said corporation shallbe controlledby a board Directors.
of directors, of not less than seven or more than twelve
members ,one thirdof whom shallbe electedeach year
at the annual election , and hold the office of director for
three years,or untiltheirsuccessorsare elected and qual-
ified.
§ 4. The annual election of directors shall be on the Election.
firstMonday in May of each year,and the directorsmay ,
as soon as practicable aftersaid election,electfrom their
number a president, vice president,secretary, treasurer,
and medical examiner , who shall hold their office for
President .

- Secretary .
one year from their election, and until their successors

§ 5. The corporators herein named shallconstitutethe

shall hold for the long and short term .
§ 6. The officerselected by the directors,before enter-
ing upon theirduty ,shalltake an oath before some one
authorized by law to administer oaths, that they will
faithfullyand to the best of their abilityperform the
duties of said office,and honestly account for and pay
over allmoneys that they may receiveto theirsuccessors,
as directedby the directorsand providedfor by the by-
laws of this association
§7 . The presidentshallpreside at allmeetings ,but shall
not vote except in case of a tie. He shallsign allcertifi-
cates of membership and orders drawn on the treasurer,
and perform such other duties as may be required by the
directors,and appoint such other officersas the associa-
tion may need .
§ 8. The vice president shall possess the powers and
perform the duties of the president in his absence ; and in
the absence of the presidentand vice president,the board
shallelecta presidentpro tem. from one of their number ,
who shallexercise allthe powers of the president.
§9 . The secretary shallkeep a record of all the meet-

association, conduct its correspondence , receive all the
money due the association,receiptforthe same ,and pay

his receipttherefor. He shall prepare allcertificatesof
membership , noticesof death,and registerallmember-
ship and deaths in a well-bound book,also the amount
paid to the representativeof any deceasedmember . He
shall,withinfortydays afternoticehas been servedupon
the members ,make a record of allthose who have paid
and have not paid. He shallsemi-annually,or as often
as required by the board ,present a written statement of
the condition of the association .

§ 14. The qualificationsfor membership in thisassocia-

CHAPTER 1454 .
AN ACT to organize and establisha public schoolin the town of Madison-
ville, Kentucky .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assemblyof the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1. That allthe territorynow embraced within the
limits of the town of Madisonville, or which may here-
after be embraced within the limits of said town , shall
be ,and is hereby ,incorporated as a school district,which
shall be under the controland management of a board of
trustees appointed by the board of councilmen of said
town as hereinafter directed .
§ 2. The board of councilmen of said town shall, at
theirfirstregular meeting afterthe adoption of this act
by the voters of said town authorized to vote as herein-
afterprovided ,and at theirfirstregular meeting in June
of each year thereafter, appoint fivesuitablemale white
persons,residentvoters of said town ,as school trustees;
and the persons so appointed shall constitute and be
styled" The Board of Trustees of the Madisonville Pub-
licSchool ;" and by that name shallbe known as a body-
corporateand politic; and may sue and be sued,contract
and be contracted with ; may buy ,sell, and convey real
and personal estate; and the titleto allschool property in
said districtshall vest in said school board and their suc-
cessors forever .
LOC . L., VOL , H- 68
§3 . The saidtrusteesso appointed shalltake an oath
faithfullyto discharge theirduties, and shall,at any time
within one month after their appointment ,meet and or-
ganize . The chairman of the board of councilmen of
said town shall be president of said board . In case of
his absence or inabilityto act,a majority of said board
shall elect one of their number as chairman to preside
and discharge the duties of chairman pro tempore.
§ 4. In the appointment of the board of trusteesof the
Madisonvillepublic schoolit shallbe unlawful for the
board of councilmen to select more than one member of
same from any one religiousdenomination or pursua-
sion .
§ 5. The said board of the public school shall appoint
some suitable person as secretary and treasurer, who
shallhold his officefor two years,and untilhis successor
is appointed and qualified; and shallperform such duties
as generallypertain to the positionof secretaryand
treasurer,and allsuch duties as may be prescribedby
the said school board
§ 6. All vacancies in said school board shall be imme-
diatelyfilledby the board of councilmen of said town by
the appointment of some person with the qualifications
as hereinbefore prescribed; but no person shall, at the
same time , be a member of the board of councilmen and
a member of said school board , except the chairman ..
The removal of a member from said town shall vacate
his position.
§7 . The controland management of the publicschool
of the town of Madisonville,and the propertyand funds
belonging thereto, or which may accrue in any way to it,
or for its establishment, management , or maintenance
under this act or otherwise , shall be vested in the said
school board and their successors in office.
§8 . The said board of trustees shall have power to
make all by -laws and rules for the government of them-
selvesor theirappointees,and for the dispatchof busi-
ness,and for the management ,control,and government
of the school,and to enforce such by -laws and rules by
suitablefinesand penalties,to be recoveredin any court
having jurisdictionof the amount . They shallappoint
allteachersand otherpersonsnecessaryto carryon said
school,and prescribeallrulesfortheirgovernment ,and
fix their compensation or salaries, and may dismiss or
suspend any teacheror otherperson appointed by them ;
prescribe the branches of education to be taught in the
school, grade the classes, and prescribe the necessary
qualificationsfor,and the mode of examination of,pupils
or persons applying for admission to any class.
§9 . A majority of the members of said board shallcon-
stitutea quorum for the transaction of business. They
shallmeet at leastonce in every month , and shallfixby
by -law a regular meeting once in each month ,and may
meet as often as to them may seem necessary for the
transaction of business. A majority of those present
may transact any business except in the making of a
contract, for the purchase or sale of real estate,for the
erection of any building, or for the paying out of money ,
in which casesa majorityof the board must concur,and
the yeas and nays must be polled and recorded in the
journal .
§ 10. Said board shallcause to be kept a regular and
correctjournal of theirproceedings in a well-bound book ,
which at alltimes shallbe open to the inspection of any
member of said board , or any member of the board of
councilmen of said town ,or any committee appointed by
the board of councilmen of said town .
§ 11. The board of trusteesof said public school shall,
at the end of each scholasticyear ,make out and return to
the board of councilmen of said town a written or printed
statement ,in such form as may be required by the said
board of councilmen,showing the number of pupils in
said school,and the grade or class to which they belong ,
and whether the said pupils are within the legal age or
localityto entitlethem to free admission to said school,
and such other information as the board of councilmen of
said town may ,from time to time ,require. It shall be
the duty of said schoolboard of trusteesto do and per
form any and all other acts imposed by the common
school law of this Commonwealth on the trustees of the
common schools of this State as modified herein .
§ 12. All white children between the age of six and
twenty years residingwithin the corporate limitsof said
town shallhave equal rightsof admission to the school of
said district; but the board of trustees of said public
schoolmay prescribethe termsand ratesupon which any
other white persons not embraced in the above -mentioned
class may be admitted to said public school.
§13 . No catechism or other form of religious belief
shallbe taughtor inculcatedin,nor shallany class-book
be used or adopted for said school which reflectsupon
any religiousdenomination or politicalpersuasion ; nor
shall any class be so conducted as to interferewith the
religiousor politicalbeliefof parentsor pupils.
§ 14. The secretaryand treasurer,before entering upon
his duties , shall execute a bond to the board of trustees
of the Madisonvillepublicschool,with good and ample
suretiesto be approved of by the said board of trustees,
conditioned for the faithfulperformance of allhis duties,
and to account for and pay over to the proper persons all
money which may come to his hands by virtue of his said
office. The secretary shall attend all meetings of the
board, keep theirrecordsand papers,and perform such
other duties as may be required or prescribedby the said
board of trustees . The treasurer shall receive and dis-
pense the money belonging to the school fund, see that it
isproperlycollected,keep accurateand true accounts in
well-bound books of allhisacts,and perform such other
dutiesas may be prescribedor requiredby said board of
trustees. The said secretary and treasurer shall receive
for his servicesa salary to be fixedby the said board , and
paid at such timesas they may direct.
§ 15. The commissioner for common schools of Hopkins
county shallannually make an estimateof the share or
proportionof theStatecommon schoolfundwhich would
be due to the school district of the town of Madisonville
as hereinbeforedesignated, and shallpay over to the
board of trustees of the Madisonville public school the
amount due said district on said account , which fund
shallbe used only in payment of teachers in said school.
§ 16. The board of trusteesof said public school may
admit into said school white children who are non -resi-
dents of the town of Madisonville,or otherwhite pupils
who are not within the school age ,or entitledto equal
rightsof admissionas hereinbeforeprescribed,upon such
terms and conditions, and upon the payment of such
charges as to them may seem right.
§ 17. The board of councilmen for said town shall
cause to be levied and collected an annual tax at the
rate of not exceeding twenty cents upon each one hun-
dred dollars' worth of the same property owned by white
persons that istaxed by the town for town purposes ; the
assessment and collection to be made at the same time
and in the same manner as required by law for the city
revenue . This tax shall be called and known as the
school tax, and only be payable in money ,and is to be
used for the purpose of defraying the yearly expenses of
the said public school, including repairs on school build-
ings and premises: Provided,That only the propertyof
white persons shallbe taxed under thisact : And provided
further,That said tax in thissection mentioned shall not
be levied untilafterthe school building mentioned in this
charter shallbe completed and paid for.
§ 18. The board of councilmen of said town shallpro-
vide the funds forbuying the necessary grounds ,building
the school buildings; and for that purpose the board of
trusteescreated by this act, and their successors, are in-
vested with allthe property,money ,rights, and creditsof
thetrusteesof oldMadisonvilleSeminary; and the board
of trusteescreated by this act are authorized to selland
convey the said seminary house and lot situated in the
town ofMadisonville,and describedina deed from Joseph.
Fuqua to the trustees of said Madisonville Seminary ,
and apply theproceedsthereof,and any money otherwise
providedby thisact,not otherwisespecificallyappropri-
ated, to the erection of a school building or buildings in
the town of Madisonville. The said trustees may sell
said seminary house and lot publicly or privately upon
such terms as they may deem advisable, and convey to
the purchaser or purchasers the titlein fee-simple to the
same . When said board of trustees shall have effected a
sale of said seminary lot,it shallbe their duty to report
the same , together with the amount of the proceeds of
same ,to the board of councilmen of said town .
§ 19. It shall be the duty of the board of councilmen
of saidtown,and they are hereby authorized,empow-
ered,and required,to raisean amount by taxation on the
property of said town sufficientto erect a school build-
ing or buildings, and to furnish and equip same in such
manner as is authorized by thisact, and as the board of
trusteesof the public school may deem proper and right;
but said amount so authorized to be raised , when added
to the proceeds of the sale of said seminary lot,shallnot
exceed the sum of fifteen thousand dollars . Said amount
to be raised for the purposes aforesaid shall be divided
into four equal installments,and to be levied for in the
following manner , to-wit : The board of councilmen of
said town shallcause to be leviedand collectedupon
the same property in the said town as is taxed by the
State for common school purposes , and by the town for
municipal purposes , the assessment to be made at the
same time as requiredby law formunicipal purposesfor
the year 1882,a tax to pay the firstinstallmentof said
amount , and the cost of collectingthe same : Provided,
however, That no property owned by negroes shall be so
taxed ; and they shall cause to be levied in the same
manner , and upon the same terms, an amount each year
sufficientto pay each installmentas itfallsdue. Said
installmentsshallbe due on the firstday of January,
afterthe levy is made for its payment , or after it should
have been made as hereinprovided. If itshouldbecome
necessary, in order to make said three last installments
available forthe purposes mentioned in thisact,then the
board of councilmen of said town , in their discretion,
are authorizedand empowered to borrow any amount
not exceeding the amount of said three lastinstallments,
and forthat purpose may issuebonds or scrip,not less
than ten dollars nor not exceeding in denomination one
hundred dollars,running not longer than the time fixed
for the payment and collectionof said installments,and
bearing interestat any rate not exceeding six per cent.
per annum , payable at the maturity of said bonds or
scrip. The bonds or scrip in this section provided for
shall be made payable to bearer, shall be signed by the
chairman of the board of councilmen ,and attestedby the
clerk of said board of councilmen of said town ,shallpass
by delivery, and shallbe sold or discounted by the board
of councilmen of said town ,or such person as they may
authorize, forthe best price they can get, or paid out for
any building, or any other indebtedness created on ac-
count of said public school building or buildings. The
said board of councilmen shall, at the time the levy is
made to pay said installments,levy an additionalamount
to pay the intereston the installment levied for and all
cost of collecting the same .
§20 . The town assessor shall make the assessments
necessary for the fixing and collectionof all amounts
provided by thisact,under such provisions and rules as
may , from time to time, be prescribed by the board of
councilmen of said town . All said amounts as are here-
in required to be raised shallbe collectedby the marshal ,
or a collectorappointed by the board of councilmen ,by
levy,distress,or sale, in the same manner as the town
revenue is collected; and the officerfor said sums shall,
with his sureties,be responsible upon his officialrevenue
bond forthe faithfulperformance of his duties, with such
penalties as are now prescribedby law for delinquencies.
§ 21. The funds arisingfrom the levies directed to be
made by section twenty of this act, and the bonds or
scripby said section authorized to be issued,shallbe paid
and delivered into the school treasury, or the said bonds
or scripmay be delivered to the board of trusteesof said
public school,and by them used for the said building or
buildings,and the purchase of ground,eitherby cashing
them or paying them to contractorsand othersto whom
the said board may be indebted on account of same .
§ 22. All money in the school treasuryshallbe under
the control and management of the board of trustees of
saidpublicschool,and used by them forthe solepurpose
of saidpublicschool,and purchase of propertyand erect-
ing of buildingstherefor. If any of said trusteesor the
treasurer shall, without authority of the board , use or
appropriateany of saidfundsto hisown use,he shallbe
deemed guiltyof embezzlement,and be punished as pro-
vided by the general laws of this State for the crime of
enbezzlement .
§ 23. This act shall not take effect and be in force until
ratifiedby a majorityof the legal white votersvoting
at an electionto be held in said town And for the pur-
pose of taking the sense of the qualified voters of said
town upon the ratificationof thisact, the board of coun-
cilmen shall order an election to be held at the court-
house in Madisonville, on a day to be designated , not.
sooner than fifteendays afterthe order is made . Due
notice shallbe given of said election by publication in a
newspaper in said town (if one be published) for one
insertion,and by writtenor printednoticespostedup at
not less than five public places within the town limits.
The board of councilmen shallappoint two judges and a
sheriff, residents of the town ,to hold said election,and
the clerk of the board of councilmen shall act as clerk
thereof. A poll-book shallbe prepared , in one column of
which shall be entered the names of those voting in favor
of the ratification of this act , and in the other column
shall be entered the names of those voting against the
ratification of this act . The officers of said election
shallcertifythe resultto the board of councilmen ,and if
itappears that a majority of the legal white votersvoting.
at said election are in favor of the ratificationof this act ,
itshallbe the duty of said board of councilmen ,by order
of record upon their order-book ,to declare the resultof
said electionin accordance with the return made by the
officersof said election,whereupon this act shall be in
fullforce: Provided,however,That no vote shallbe ordered
for the ratificationof this act until the present bonded
debt of said town is reduced below ten thousand dollars .
§24 . That ifthe qualifiedvoters of said town shall be
against the provisions of this act under an election held
pursuant to section twenty -three,then the question may
be re-submitted in the same manner at the expiration of
one year from the firstelection; but not more than two
elections shall be held for the purpose of taking the
sense of the voters upon the ratificationof thisact.
§25 . The expenses of the elections authorized by this-
act shall be paid by the board of councilmen of said
town .
§ 26. This act shalltake effectfrom itspassage .
Approved April 24 , 1882 .

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 822 .
AN ACT to organizeand establisha system of common and graded schools
in the town of Dover , and in common school districtnumber two , in
Mason county .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1. That the boundary of common school districtnum-
ber two , in Mason county ,be enlarged and extended so
as to include allthe inhabitants within boundary : begin-
ning on the Ohio river,the corner of Mason and Bracken
counties; thence with the boundary line between those
counties a distance of two and one -half miles ; thence
four and one -half miles east ; thence two and one -half
miles north to the Ohio river; thence down the river to
the beginning ; which boundary shall be and remain the
boundary of said common school districtuntilthe same
ischanged by an act of the Legislature of Kentucky .
§2 . Said schooldistrictshallbe a body politicand cor-
porate ,under the name of " The Trustees of the Dover
Graded and Common School ," and as such , and by that
name ,may sue and be sued ,contract and be contracted
with,and exerciseallpowers necessaryto carryout and
effectuatethe purposes for which it is organized . The
titleto all common school property within said district
shallvestinsaidcorporation,and itisherebyauthorized
to use, occupy ,and control allsuch property , and to take
titleto any propertythat may hereafterbe conveyed to it
for the use and benefit of the common schools of said dis-
trict, and to draw and expend in the support of such
schools so much of the common school fund of the State
as may be due said district,from year to year ,under the
common school laws regulating the distributionand ex-
penditure of said fund.
§3 . Said corporation shallbe under the exclusive con-
trol and management of a board of five trustees, to be
elected by the persons resident within said districtquali-
fied by law to vote for common school trustees. The
first election for trustees under this act shall be held at
the school-house in Dover ,on the firstSaturday in June ,
one thousand eight hundred and eighty-four, as, and in
the manner school trusteesare now required to be elected
by the general laws of the State. So soon as these trus-
teesare chosen,they shallqualifyby taking the oath as
prescribed for common school trustees, and draw lotsto
ascertain which of them shall hold officefor one year ,
which for two years,which for three years ,which for four
years,and which for fiveyears; itbeing the intentand
purpose of this act to require one trustee to be elected
annually ,on the firstsaturday in June ,for the term of
fiveyears afterthe firstelection. Should a vacancy oc-
cur at any time ,by death or resignation,such vacancy ,
for the unexpired term ,shall be filledby the remaining
members of the board .
§4 . The trusteesshallorganize,within two weeks after
theirelection,by electingone of theirnumber chairman,
and such other subordinateofficersas they may deem
proper; and they may requireany of saidofficersto give
bond ,with personal security,to insure a proper discharge
of such duties as may be assigned them . The board is
authorizedto pass such by-laws as it may deem proper
or necessary to carry out the purposes of thisact,not in-
consistent with the Constitution or laws of the State .
§ 5. Itshallbe the dutyof thisboard toorganizeand
maintain a system of common and graded schools within
said district,and to have the same taught for ten months
in every year , to which every white childin said district,
within the common school age , shall have free access,
and the rightto attend free of charge at all times, as he
might have the same rightswere thisschool taught under
and pursuant to the provisions of the laws of the State
which regulate the common schools of the State. This
board of trusteesis also authorized to organize and main-
tain a separate common school forthe benefit of the col-
ored children within said district .
§ 6. Itshallbe the duty of the board to have a census
taken and the number of scholars within the common
school ages resident within said districtascertained, in
the month of April,every year , and to report the number
to the Superintendent of Public Instruction,and to make
such reports of their school as are required from school
trusteesunder the general laws of the State.
§ 7. The said board of trustees is authorized to levy
and collectan annual poll-tax, not exceeding two dollars
on each poll,alsoan annual tax not exceedingfiftycents
on each one hundred dollars in value of all the taxable
property within said district, as the same is assessed for
Statepurposes,also,the net proceedsof allfinesimposed
for infractionsof the criminal and penal laws of the
State, within said district,afterpaying costs and commis-
sions, shall be paid to said trustees, for the use of the
schools within said district. That collected from the
white people shallbe used in the maintenance and sup-
port of the schools established for the benefit of white
children, and that collectedfrom colored people shallbe
used for the maintenance and support of such schools as
may be established for the benefit of colored children.
The tax thus levied shall be listed with the sheriff of the
county of Mason , whose duty itshallbe to collectthe
same and pay the money to the board of trusteeswhen
collected, and he and his suretiesshall be responsible
therefor,as in case of other taxes : Provided,however,That
the provisions of section seven ,so far as itapplies to tax-
ation,shall not take effectuntil ithas been ratifiedand
approved by a majority of the legallyqualifiedvoters
residingwithin said district,and voting at any electionfor
the consideration of that section, and the county judge of
Mason county and the justicesof the peace of Dover pre-
cinct,are authorized to arrange for and order an election
for the consideration of said section,giving public notice
by printed handbills, at least ten days before said elec-
tion ; and if a majority of the legally qualifiedvoters,
voting at said election,vote in favor of the tax , as pro-
vided in section seven , it shall thereafter be in full force
and effect .
§ 8. The board of trusteesis hereby authorized to es-
tablish schools on such plan as they deem best; to alter
and change their plans as often as they wish ; to employ
teachers and discharge the same ; fixand change salaries,
and generally to manage and control the common schools
within said districtas they may deem it to be to the in-
terest of the public,but in conformity to law and to the
rights of allpartiesinterested. Said trusteesshall make
an annual settlement with the county court of Mason
county , and in such settlement show what moneys they
have received and paid out under the provisions of this
act, and produce vouchers for allpayments made .
§ 9. The trusteesshall have the power to admit schol-
ars from other districtsto the school,and to assesstheir
tuitionfor the privilegeof attending the same .
§ 10. This act shalltake effectfrom the date of itspas-
sage .
Approved April 17, 1884 .

laws.summary: This statute outlines the use of convicted individuals and delinquent taxpayers for labor on county roads and streets. It allows county judges to assign work to those convicted of penal offenses, including working off fines, and to use restraints like ball and chains to prevent escape. It also mandates that delinquent capitation taxpayers in Webster County work off their taxes on roads, with surveyors authorized to collect taxes or oversee the work. Penalties are imposed for non-compliance.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 825 .
AN ACT forthebenefitof Webster and Hopkins counties, relatingto the
public roads in said counties .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . The county judge of Webster county shalldivide
all of the roads of said county into precincts, and as
often as may be necessary appoint a surveyor in each
precinct,whose duty itshallbe to superintendthe roads
therein,and seethatthe same isworked and kept in such
repair as the agreement of the contractors thereon with
the county court requires. No surveyor shallbe allowed ,
unlessby consentofthe court,to resignsuch place under
two years,excepthe remove from the precinct. Any sur-
veyor may be removed at any time by said court.
§2 . The clerk of the county court shall, within ten
days after the appointment of a surveyor of said road ,
delivera copy of the order to the sheriffof the county
(or to a constableiftherebe no sheriff),containinga full
and complete description of the precinct, and take his
receipttheretor. Such officershall, within fifteendays
thereafter,delivera copy of the order and a description
of the precinct to the surveyor,and return the originalto
the clerk'sofficeof the Webster county court with the
time of the service indorsed, which shall be evidence of
the factsstatedtherein. The clerkshallpost up in his
office,once in every year , a listof allthe suveyors in the
county,designatingthe precinctof each surveyor. The
clerk,sheriff,or otherofficerfailingto perform the duties
prescribedin thissection,shallbe finedtwo dollarsand a
half for each neglect .
§ 3. Each surveyorof a publieroad shallbe furnished
with a copy of the contract for the working of the road
in his precinct. He shallreport to the county judge any
failureupon the part of the contractor thereon . He shall
certifyto the county judge when the contract has been
properlycomplied with. He shallbe exempt from jury
service, and from poll-tax for road purposes during his
continuancein saidoffice. For a failureto perform any
of his dutiesprescribedby thisact,said surveyor shall
be fined therefor not less than five nor more than fifteen
dollars for each offense , to be recovered by warrant in
the name of the Commonwealth of Kentucky ; and the
quarterlycourt shallhave exclusivejurisdictionof all
proceedingsagainstsurveyorsof roads.
§ 4. The county judge shall,at the court-house door in
Dixon ,on the firstMonday in Aprilin each year (and at
such other times as he shall find necessary),let out the
working and keeping in repair the public roads in Web-
stercounty ,to the lowest and best bidder,for such length
of time as he may choose (not exceeding his own term of
office),after due advertisement of two insertionsin the
county paper, ifthere be one, and by printed notices
posted up for at leastfifteendays before such lettingat
the voting places of each voting precinct in the county :
Provided , That the fund raised by the levy court under
this act shallbe sufficientto work all of the public roads
in said county , and if not sufficient, then it shall be used
at such places and for such roads as the county court may
think best,having due regard to the public good and the
wants of the differentparts of the county .
§ 5. Each contractor shall execute to the Common-
wealth a bond ,with good security,to be approved by the
county judge ,in double the amount he is to receivefor his
contract, for the faithfulperformance of said contract,
and said bonds shallbe filedat the next regular term of
the Webster county court afterthe letting,which shallbe
noted of record and the bonds kept on fileby the clerk of
the court in his office in bundles marked “ contractors '
bonds ;" and certifiedcopiesofsaidbonds shallbe compe-
tent as evidence , and the county judge shall deliver to
each surveyor a copy of the contract for working the
road in such surveyor's precinct. Any contractor who
shall fail,in whole or in part, to complete his contract
within the time and in the manner prescribed therein, or
who , having contracted to keep any part of the public
roads in good order for traveling or hauling ,or any bridge
or culvertin good repair,and who shallfailto do so,shall,
for every failure, be deemed guiltyof a misdemeanor , and
upon conviction shallbe fined not lessthan ten nor more
than one hundred dollars .
§ 6. All fines assessed under this act shall be collected
as otherfines,and shall[inure] to the benefitof the road
fund of Webster county, and shallbe paid out by the
sheriffunder the ordersof the countyjudge.
§ 7. The countyjudge shallprovidework on the roads
of the county or on the streetsof towns forsuch persons
convictedof penal offensesas may ,by orderofthe proper
authority,be required to work on roads or streets, or to
work out fines assessed against them on the roads or
streetsunder the provisions of general or special laws ,
and may ,when necessary,put a balland chain upon any
such persons to prevent their escape , and if necessary ,
may employ some suitable person to oversee and guard
them while at work .
§ 8. The county judge shallletout the construction or
repairing of the bridges in Webster county not included
in the agreement of any contractor, or the levy court may ,
in theirdiscretion,appoint a specialcommissioner to let
out any bridge or bridges,and provide for his compensa-
tion therefor, and such county judge or special commis-
sioner shall be held liable for any failurein regard to
any bridge so let by them respectively, and the court
may require bond with surety from the special commis-
sioner .
§ 9. That alldelinquent capitationtax-payers of Web-
ster county shall be required to work out their taxes at
such times on the roads in their several precincts as the
surveyor thereof may require,for which work such delin-
quents shallhave creditat the rate of one dollar for each
fullday's work performed by him . For failingor refus-
ing to comply with the order of said surveyor when
notified, all such delinquents are made liable to the
penalties now imposed by law for persons failing or re-
fusing to work on roads. The several surveyors are
authorized and empowered to collectthe taxes due from
such delinquents in their several precincts,if they shall
elect to pay the same rather than work on the roads,
and the same shall be held and applied as part of the
road fund ,and reported and paid over by said surveyor
to the county judge , taking and filingwith the county
clerk his receipttherefor;and said clerkshallgive to said
surveyora certifiedcopy of saidreceipt,which shallhave
the same effectin his hands as the original.
10. The county court of Webster county may open
roads not exceeding sixtyfeet in width , or may increase
the width of established roads to sixty feet, anything in
the general laws to the contrary notwithstanding .
§ 11. That the courts of the justicesof the peace in and
for Webster county shallhave jurisdictionconcurrent with
the quarterly court of all proceedings against road con-
tractors under this act, and it shall be the duty of any
justiceor the county judge upon his own knowledge or
upon complaint of any surveyor,or upon the information,
under oath,of any citizen, that any part of the public
road is out of repair, to issue his warrant against the de-
linquent contractor,returnable to his own or some other
justices' court,or to the Webster quarterlycourt,and upon
the execution and return thereof such proceedings shall
be had as are had in other Commonwealth cases. In pro-
ceedings under this act the defendant shall have no
right to claim his district, and both the Commmonwealth
and defendant shallhave the rightof appeal from justices'
courts to the quarterly court,and from the quarterlycourt
to the circuit court .
§ 12. Itshallbe the duty of the county attorney to pros-
ecute allwarrants under thisact,and forsuch prosecutions
he shall receive twenty -five per cent. of the finesrecov-
ered , and upon his failurethe court may appoint some
attorneyin his stead,who shallreceivesaidcommission
for his services . All fines assessed under this act shall be
collected as other fines,and shall inure to the benefit of
the road fund of Webster county , and shall be paid out
by the sheriff,or other collectingofficer,under orders from
the county judge .
§ 13. It shallbe unlawfulforthe county judge,county
attorney,sheriff,collectorof the revenue ,or any surveyor ,
to become ,directly or indirectly,interested in any con-
tractfor working roads, or building or repairing bridges ;
and itshallbe unlawful for either of said officersto buy
or become interested in any claim growing out of said
work or contract. For a violationof thissection,either
of said officersshall be guilty of a misdemeanor , and ,
upon indictment and conviction thereof,shall be fined
not less than fiftynor more than five hundred dollars.
This section shall be given in charge to the grand jury
by the judge of the Webster county court.
§ 14. Any person who shallwillfullyor negligentlyin-
jure,destroy,or obstruct any of the said public roads or
bridges, or any of the culverts or ditches on said roads ,
shall be fined not less than five nor more than twenty-
five dollars, to be recovered in like manner as the fines
prescribedherein for surveyors, and shallalso be liablein
double damages to the county , or any person aggrieved
or injured,to be recovered in any court having jurisdic-
tion of the amount . It shallbe the duty of surveyors to
reportpromptlyto the countyjudge any violationof this
section .
§ 15. The county court,a majority ofthejusticesagree-
ing,shall, on some regular county court day ,assessa tax
of not more than fifteen cents on each one hundred dol-
lars' worth of property assessedfor revenue purposes ,and
a capitation tax not exceeding two dollars on each per-
son in said county required by the general law to work
on roads .
§ 16. The ad valorem and capitation tax provided for
in section of this act shall be collected as other revenue
due the county is collected,and under the same obligations
by the collectingofficer,and shallbe paid out by said col-
lecting officerto road contractors on the order of the
judge of the Webster county court.
§ 17. Chapter ninety-four of the General Statutes is
hereby adopted and made part of this act,except when
itcomes in conflict with the provisions of this act ; and all
other road laws passed for Webster county are hereby
repealed .
§ 18. That an electionshallbe held in Webster county
on the firstMonday in August ,one thousand eight hun-
dred and eighty-four,at which two pollsshallbe opened ,
one " for the road law " and the other " against the road
law ;" and if it shall be found that a majority of those
who voted upon the question have voted for the law ,
then this act shall be in full force ; should there not be a
majority for said law at said election,then the county
court may ,at any regularsubsequent election,have polls
opened as provided for in thissection; and ifat any such
election there is a majority of persons voting in favor of
thislaw ,itshallthen be in fullforce; and whenever said
law is adopted ,the county court may , as provided in sec-
tion six,proceed at once to levy the tax and order itscol-
lection .
§19 . That it is hereby made the duty of the county
court, for at least one month before any vote istaken , as
provided in section eighteen,to have this act published
in the county newspaper ,if there be one , and also have
the same printed and posted up at one or more places
in each precinct before said election, and also at or near
the pollson the day said electionis held. Said election
shall be held as other general electionsare held,by the
same officers,and the pollsshallbe compared and re-
sultannounced by the same board who compare the polls
in general elections, two of whom may act : Provided,
That a failureto comply with any part of thissectionby
said court shallnot make void the adoption of this act if
a majority vote for it.
§20 . This act shalltake effectfrom itspassage .
Approved April 17 , 1884.

CHAPTER 961 .
AN ACT to amend the charter of the Owenton High School, in Owen
county .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That the board of trustees of the Owenton High
School shallhave the same power to submit the question
of local taxation in aid of the common school in said dis-
trict, as is now vested by law in the trustees of common
schools by virtue of chapter eighteen, General Statutes,
and the acts amendatory thereof, and in addition to the
powers conferred by the charter,shall have the same
powers and responsibilitiesas common school trustees
under the general laws of this Commonwealth .
§2 That the money thus raised by taxation may ,in
addition to the objects specified in section five, article
two , chapter eighteen, General Statutes, or to the ex-
clusionthereof, in whole or in part,be applied to the
payment of intereston any bonds hereafterissued by
saidboard, forthe purpose of raisingmoney to purchase
a new site,and build and furnish a new school-house ,or
to repair or refurnish the present school house ,and to
the providingof a sinkingfund,not exceedingsuch pro-
portion annually of the amount of such bonds as one
year shallbear to the whole number of years such bonds
have to run from their date ; and the said board shall
have discretionarypower as to whether or not such sink-
ing fund shallbe created.
§3 . That said bonds shallbe so issued as that not more
than one thousand dollarsshallfalldue within any one
period of four years from theirdate ,and shall not ex-
ceed in the aggregate six thousand dollars; but it shall
be lawful for said board,at any time,to pay off said
bonds, or any part thereof, before maturity: Provided,
Such partialpayment amount to one hundred dollars.
§ 4. During the periodwhile any such tax isin force,
the said Owenton High School shall be regarded as a
common school,and subjectto allthe laws relatingto
common schools for at least five months in each school-
year , and such additional time in each year as the tax is
applied, in whole or in part,to the payment of the salary
of any teacher or teachers therein .
§5 . That the said bonds shall constitutea lien on the
propertyinwhich theirproceeds are invested,eitherby
purchase or by buildingor repairing.
§ 6. That the election for trustees shalltake place on
the firstSaturday in June,insteadof the firstSaturday
in July.
§7 . That section seven of an act, entitled"An act to
charter the Owenton High School ," approved February
fourteen, one thousand eight hundred and seventy-three,
be amended by striking out the words " at the option of
said board of trustees," and by striking out the words
" now have ," at the end of said section .
§ 8. That the said school shallbe for whites only, and
the question of said tax shall be submitted to and de
cided by the qualifiedwhite electors,and collected from
the property of white persons in said district.
§ 9. This act shalltake effectfrom itspassage .
Approved April 22 , 1884.

That the present board of trustees of the South Carrollton Male and Female Academy shall hold their officetillthe firstSaturday in July, one thousand eight hundred and eighty-four,on which day , and on the same day of each succeeding year , the white male voters of the common school districtin which said academy is located shall hold an election for a new board of trus- tees, to consist of three members ; and the board of trus- tees now in office,or which may hereafter be elected, shall hold their office tilltheir successors are elected and qualified .

CHAPTER 994 .
AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act to charter the South Car-
rolltonMale and Female Academy ."
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That the present board of trustees of the South
Carrollton Male and Female Academy shall hold their
officetillthe firstSaturday in July, one thousand eight
hundred and eighty-four,on which day , and on the same
day of each succeeding year , the white male voters of
the common school districtin which said academy is
located shall hold an election for a new board of trus-
tees, to consist of three members ; and the board of trus-
tees now in office,or which may hereafter be elected,
shall hold their office tilltheir successors are elected and
qualified .
§2 . Itshallbe the duty of the trusteesto advertise all
electionsheld under thisact,by written or printed notices,
posted at the front door of said academy building,and in
at least two other public places in said common school
districtnumber twelve ,for ten days preceding the day of
election, which notice shall be signed by the president
and secretaryof the board for the time being.
§3 . All acts and partsof actsin conflictwith thisact
are hereby repealed.
§4. This act shalltake effectfrom itspassage.
Approved April 24 , 1884 .

laws.summary: This act authorizes the board of councilmen of Frankfort to issue bonds up to $10,000 for the purpose of procuring a suitable building, furniture, fixtures, and apparatus for the "colored public school" of the city. The bonds are to be sold at face value and the funds used for this specific school.
key_provisions: §1 . Whereas , the board of councilmen of the cityof Frankfortis authorizedby the citycharterto build,pur- chase ,or procure any additional grounds or buildings which may be necessary for common school purposes; therefore ,to enable the board of councilmen to realize a fund sufficientto procure a suitablebuilding,and neces- sary furniture, fixtures, and apparatus for the colored public school of the city,the said board of councilmen may issuebonds of the cityto the amount of ten thou sand dollars,of the denomination of fivehundred dollars each,with coupons attached,forthepayment of interest, which interestmay be at any rateper annum notexceed- ing sixper cent.,and shallbe payable semi-annually,to- wit: on the firstday of January and July,at theFarmers ' Bank ofKentucky ,Frankfort,Kentucky ; saidbonds to be payable twenty years afterdate at said Farmers' Bank of Kentucky . The bonds to be signedby the mayor and countersignedby the clerk, with the corporateseal of the cityattached, and the coupons to be signed by the clerk; which said bonds,so issuedas aforesaid,shallbe put upon the market by the mayor and sold,and from the sale thereof shall be realized the said fund as aforesaid : Provided , That the said bonds shallnot be sold for a less sum than their face value .

§3 . The fund realized from the sale of said bonds shall be kept separate and apart from the other funds of the city, and shall be styled the Colored School Building Fund , which fund shall not be used for any other than the purpose herein named .

§ 4. When a suitablebuilding and necessary furniture, fixtures,and apparatus shallhave been procured for the coloredpublicschoolof saidcity,the balance of the said building fund ,if any shall be then remaining ,shall be placed to the credit, and be made part,of the fund for the support of the colored public school.

§5 . The board of trustees of the public schools and the committee on education of the board of councilmen shall constituteand be styled the School Building Com- mittee. The chairman and secretary of the board of trusteesof the publicschoolsshallbe respectivelychair- man and secretary of the said school building committee , which building committee shall have power to expend the said colored school building fund for the purpose atoresaid. The said fund shall be disbursed upon order of the said committee ,and upon warrants signed by the chairman and secretary thereof.

CHAPTER 1015 .

forschoolpurposes.

Frankfortis authorizedby the citycharterto build,pur-

therefore ,to enable the board of councilmen to realize a

may issuebonds of the cityto the amount of ten thou
sand dollars,of the denomination of fivehundred dollars
each,with coupons attached,forthepayment of interest,
which interestmay be at any rateper annum notexceed-
ing sixper cent.,and shallbe payable semi-annually,to-
wit: on the firstday of January and July,at theFarmers '
Bank ofKentucky ,Frankfort,Kentucky ; saidbonds to be
payable twenty years afterdate at said Farmers' Bank
of Kentucky . The bonds to be signedby the mayor and
countersignedby the clerk, with the corporateseal of
the cityattached, and the coupons to be signed by the
clerk; which said bonds,so issuedas aforesaid,shallbe
put upon the market by the mayor and sold,and from the
sale thereof shall be realized the said fund as aforesaid :
Provided , That the said bonds shallnot be sold for a less
sum than their face value .
§ 2. The board of councilmen shall,from year toyear,
levy upon the taxable propertyin said city,and collect
an additional tax sufficientto pay the interest on said
bonds , and redeem and pay off the same when they shall
become due ,which said taxes, as levied and collected,
shallbe kept separate and apart from the other revenues
of the city, and shallnot be used for any other purposes
than the payment of the interestand principal of said
bonds .
§3 . The fund realized from the sale of said bonds shall
be kept separate and apart from the other funds of the
city, and shall be styled the Colored School Building
Fund , which fund shall not be used for any other than
the purpose herein named .
§ 4. When a suitablebuilding and necessary furniture,
fixtures,and apparatus shallhave been procured for the
coloredpublicschoolof saidcity,the balance of the said
building fund ,if any shall be then remaining ,shall be
placed to the credit, and be made part,of the fund for
the support of the colored public school.
§5 . The board of trustees of the public schools and
the committee on education of the board of councilmen
shall constituteand be styled the School Building Com-
mittee. The chairman and secretary of the board of
trusteesof the publicschoolsshallbe respectivelychair-
man and secretary of the said school building committee ,
which building committee shall have power to expend
the said colored school building fund for the purpose
atoresaid. The said fund shall be disbursed upon order
of the said committee ,and upon warrants signed by the
chairman and secretary thereof.
§ 6. The bonds provided for in thisact shallnot be sub-
ject to taxation for citypurposes .
§7 . All acts or parts of acts in conflictherewith are
hereby repealed.
Approved April 25, 1884 .
