Registration of Voters
An Act to Amend and Re-enact Chapter 30 of the General Statutes, Relating to Elections
An Act to amend an act entitled "An act to regulate elections in this Commonwealth," approved March 11, 1890, and to provide for the registration of voters in the city of Louisville.
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1033 .
AN ACT to provide for a registration of voters in the city of Louisville .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
Officers.
§1 . That the county judge of Jefferson county ,the
sheriffof said county , and the clerk of the Jefferson
county court, shall constitute a board which shall, be-
tween the firstand fifteenthdays of June ,in each year .
appoint four sober and discreet citizensin each election
precinctof the cityof Louisville,two to act as judges of
registration,one as clerkof registration,and one as sheriff
of registration,in the precinctsfor which they are ap-
pointed. No person shallbe eligibleas judge, clerk, or
sheriffwho is not a voter in the precinct for which he is
appointed,and a house-keeper. And when thereare two
distinctpoliticalparties,said officersof registrationshall
be so selectedas that one of the judges at each precinct
shallbe of one politicalparty,and the other of the op-
posing politicalparty. They shall serve for one year
from the time of their appointment ; and each officerof
registration, before entering upon the discharge of his
duties,shall take the oath prescribed by section one ,ar-
ticleeight,of the Constitution,and shall,during the period
of his term of service,be excused from jury duty .
2. The sheriffof Jefferson county shall, at least five
days before the general registrationin each year ,as pro-
vided for in this act,give each officerof registration
written notice of his appointment . Should the court,
sheriff, and clerk failto appoint ,or should allthe officers
appointed failto attend at the place of registrationfor
one hour afterthe time for commencing the registration,
or refuseto act,then the sheriff,judge , or clerk, or either
of them that can be found,of the county,shallappoint
officersto act in their stead for that registration; but
should one or two officersbe in attendance ,he or they
may fillvacancies for the purpose of conducting that
registration, and may administer the necessary oaths of
office .
§3 . Officersof registrationshallhave the same power
to preserve order at the places of registrationas is ex-
ercisedby officersof electionsat the polls. Ifthe officers
of registrationentertain any doubt as to whether or not
any person offering for registration is entitled to such reg-
istration, or it any one's right to registeris challenged ,
citizensmay be called in,not exceeding three in number ,
who shall be examined touching the qualificationsof
such person or persons who offerto register.
Forms .
§ 4. It shallbe the duty of the county clerkof Jeffer-
son county to prepare the proper forms and cause to be
printed two registrationbooks for each precinct in the
cityof Louisville,one of which shallbe kept in hisoffice
to be used as provided in section seven of this act, and
the other furnished to the clerks of registration and elec-
tion before each registrationor election day ,as herein-
Name.
Residence.
Color.
afterprovided . Said books shall be so arranged as that
the names of voters may be registered alphabetically,
and shall be ruled and headed as follows :
AugustElection.
NovemberElection.
General Registration.
§5 . The officersof registration shall attend at the
voting places of their respective precincts on the first
Monday in July in each year , and on the two next suc-
ceeding days , from the hours of six in the morning until
nine in the evening , and shall record in the registration
book , which shallbe furnished by the clerk of the county
court to each registrationclerk, a listof such qualified
voters of the precinct as may apply for registration. If
either of said days shall fallupon the fourth day of the
month , then said fourth day shallbe omitted as a day of
registration, and the registrationshall proceed on the
next succeeding day as it said fourth day had not inter-
vened . Said listof voters shallbe in alphabetical order,
and shall show the name of the person registered, the
name of the street or alley, and number of the house ,
lodging ,or tenement in which he lives,and whether he
be white or colored; and if said house ,lodging, or tene-
ment be not numbered , the location thereof shall be
described in the registration book as accurately as is
practicable,giving the street,and between what streets.
No person shallbe registeredwho does not personally
appear before the officersof registration; and if he be
not personallyknown to one of the officers, or if any
by -stander shalldemand it,he shall be sworn by one of
the officers,and interrogatedby him or by such by-stander
touching hisqualificationsas provided in thisact. Op-
DecemberElection.
SpecialElections.
Remarks.
positethe name of each person so sworn the clerkshall
write the word " sworn ," which entry shallbe prima facie
evidence of such swearing in any prosecution under this
act. Said registrationin July shall be known as the
general registration; and any person then registeredmay
vote at all elections until the next general registration,
unless he becomes disqualifiedafterregistering.
Qualifications.
§ 6. Every person shallbe entitledto be registeredwho
would be entitledto vote at the next succeeding August
election; that is to say , every male citizenwho , on that
day ,shallhave attained the age of twenty -one years ,and
shall have resided in the State two years, or in the city
one year ,and in the precinct in which he offersto register
sixtydays . No person shall be registeredwho does not
personallyappear before the officersof registration, and
ifhe be not personallyknown to one of the officers,or if
any by -stander shalldemand it,he shallbe sworn by one
of the officers, and interrogated by him or by such by-
stander touching his qualificationsas provided in this
section. Oppositeto the name of each person so sworn ,
the clerk shallwrite the word " sworn ," which entry shall
be prima facieevidence of such swearing in any prose--
cution under this act .
Aliens .
§7 . Any alien possessing all the qualificationsof a
voternamed in sectionsixof thisact,except citizenship,
shall be entitled to be registered , but the clerk shall write
oppositeto hisname ,inthe column headed " Remarks ,"
the works " not naturalized ;" and such alien shall not be
entitledto vote at any electionheld under that registra-
tion unless he shallproduce to the officersof electionhis
naturalizationpapers in due form of law .
Mode of Registering.
§8 . In making the registration,the clerk shall act as
the recording officer,and the judges shalldecide allques-
tions relatingto the qualificationsof persons offeringto
be registered,except that,in case of a differenceof opin-
ion between the judges ,the clerk shallhave the casting
vote . It shall be the duty of the clerk to number ,con-
secutively , the names recorded under each letter of the
alphabet as they are taken down ,and at the close of the
registrationhe shallsign his name as clerk afterthe last
name recorded under each letter as aforesaid , in such
manner as that no more names can be recorded above
his, and shallfoot up and certifyin the back of the reg-
istration book the whole number of names recorded at
that registration; and this certificateshallbe signed by
allthe officersof registrationbefore leaving the place of
registration,and in the presence of by -standers,any two
of whom may ,[if] they desire,sign theirnames as wit-
nesses thereto. In addition to the requirements above ,
the clerk shallsign his name as such clerk at the foot of
each page .
Return and Custody of Books.
It
§ 9. On the day following the close of the registra-
tion the clerk shall deliver the registrationbook into
the hands of the clerk of the county court, or one of
his deputies, and shall take his receipt therefor.
shall be the duty of said county clerk to keep said
books safelyin his office,and not to sufferthe same to
be taken therefrom , except as provided in thisact. He
shallalso cause to be made one copy of each registra-
tion book in the blank book retained by him as provided
in section four of this act, which shall be kept in his
office, and not be taken therefrom for any purpose . In
case of loss of any registrationbook , a copy shall be
made by the county clerk from the copy retained in his
office, which copy shallbe used in registrationsand elec-
tions with the same effect as the original . The clerk
shall permit any citizen at any time to copy any regis..
trationbook without fee or charge ,and he shallalso fur-
nish copies at the same rate as provided in sectiontwenty
of thisact for copying the book kept in his office. Copies
turnished to citizensunder this section shallbe paid for
in cash by the person ordering them .
SpecialRegistrations.
§ 10. On Tuesday next afterthe firstMonday in Octo-
her ,one thousand eight hundred and eighty-four, and on
the same day in every second year thereafter,there shall
be a registrationof those persons whose names were not
registeredat the previous July registration, and who but
for this act would be entitled to vote for electors for Pres-
ident and Vice President or for members of Congress at
the ensuing election. On the firstWednesday in Novem-
ber in each year there shall be a registrationof those
persons whose names are not already on the registration
books for that year ,and who but for this act would be
entitledto vote at the ensuing municipal election. When
by virtue of any future act of the Legislature, or of any
proclamation or writ of election issued under existing
laws , an electionisordered for any day other than one of
the days mentioned in sections six and ten of thisact,at
which a vote is to be taken in the city of Louisville,it
shallbe the duty of the sheriffof Jeffersoncounty to fix a
day for the registrationof those entitledto vote at such
election,whose names are not already on the registration
books for that year ,and to publish notice of such day as
a part of his notice of the election,and where ,by virtue
of the citycharteror any speciallaw ,an electionor vote
is ordered to be held or taken in the cityof Louisvilleat
any other time than one of the days aforesaid,then the
council or other body or person so ordering said election
or vote shall,at the same time ,fixa day for the registra-
tion of those persons entitledto vote thereat whose names
have not been recorded on the registrationbooks of that
year,and shallrequirethe same to be publishedin like
manner as the time and place of said electionor vote are
requiredby law to be published. Registrationsunder this
section shall be known as special registrations, and any
person so registered shall be entitledto vote at allelec-
tionsheld priorto the next general registration. Regis-
trations prior to special elections shall be held not less
than ten days prior to the election.
§ 11. On the day priorto each registrationprovidedfor
in the previous section,the county clerk shall deliver to
the registrationclerksthe registrationbooks fortheirsev-
eral precincts; and on the day of such registrationthe
registrationofficersshallattend at theirseveral places of
registration,and shallregisterthe names of allpersons
appearing before them who may be entitledto vote at
the election for which the registrationisheld,and whose
names are not alreadyon the registryforthatyear. The
names shallbe recordedimmediatelyfollowingthe names
recorded at the previous registration,and the registration.
shallbe conducted and the books returned as provided in
sectionsfive,six,seven ,eight, and nine of this act. Im-
mediately afterthe books are so returned,the county clerk
shallcause the names recorded at that electionto be cop--
iedintothe book retainedin hisoffice,as providedin sec-
tion nine of this act .
Removals .
§ 12.Any person removing from one precinct to another
afterhaving been registered for that year ,may apply to
the clerk of registrationof the precinct from which he
removes , on a registrationday , and have his name can-
celed offby writing oppositeto it the word " removed ,"
and thereupon said clerk shall give him a certificatein
the following form : " This isto certifythat has
-removed from the precinct, ward , to the
precinct,-- ward , and that his registrationhas been
canceled. (Signed), clerk." Upon pre-
senting said certificateto the officersof registrationof
the precinct to which he has removed ,he shallbe entitled
to be there registered,if he possesses the other qualifica-
tionsnamed in sectionsix of thisact; and no person so
removing , after being registered, shall be registered in
another precinct without the production of such a cer-
tificate .
Striking offNames .
§ 13. Any voter may , by giving five days ' notice, in
writing,to any person whose name has been registered,
move the county court to strikehis name from the regis-
ter; and both parties may introduce witnesses, not ex-
ceeding two in number on each side . Said notice must
be served personally. If,at the hearing ,the court shallbe
of the opinion that the person registeredis not lawfully
entitled to register,it shall direct the clerk to strike his
name from the registerby inserting opposite to it the
words ," stricken offby order of the county court.
-
clerk." If the person upon whom notice is at-
tempted to be served cannot be found, the clerkshall
write opposite such name on the registrationbook the
word " doubtful;" and when , at an election, such person
whose name is marked doubtful shall offer to vote , he
shallbe sworn , and his rightto vote investigatedfully.
§ 14. On the Saturday previous to the firstMonday in
August ,one thousand eight hundred and eighty-four,and
on the juridicalday previous to every electionto be held,
or vote of the people to be taken thereafter,in the city of
Louisville,the clerk of the county court shalldeliver to
the clerks of election the registrationbooks for their
several precincts, together with the poll-books , which
said registrationand poll-books shall be produced by
said clerks at their several precinctswhen the polls are
opened on the day of the election. At said electionno
vote shallbe received unless the name of the person offer-
ing to vote is on the registry provided in this act, or
unless he produce before the officersof electionhis writ-
ten affidavit,stating that he was necessarilyabsent from
the city, or that he was illand unable to attend, or that
some named member of his family was so illas to require
his constant attention, such absence or illnesscovering
the period allowed for registration, and stating facts
showing him to be a qualifiedvoter of the precinct,and
also the factsin reference to his residence required to be
entered on the register, and shallalso prove ,by the writ-
ten affidavitof a registeredvoter of the precinct, who is
a householder,that he knows such person to be a quali-
fiedvoter,and statingthe factsin referenceto such per-
son's place of residence required to be entered on the
register. Said affidavitsshallbe returned by the officers
of electionto the county clerk, indorsed as follows :
" Filed before us this
18- .
day of
-,Judges,"
And shallbe kept on fileby the county clerk. Any vote
received by the officersof electionin contravention of this
act shall be void, and shall be rejected from the count .
The officersof election shall,when a vote is cast, mark
opposite to the name of the person voting,in the column
of the registrationbook provided for that election, the
word " voted ," and at the close of the election ,and before
closing or leaving the voting place,shallmark opposite
the name of each person who has not voted at that elec-
tion the words " not voted ." The registration book shall
be returnedto the county clerkby the clerk of the elec-
tion the day next succeeding the election.
False Registration.
§15 . Any person who shallcause himself to be regis-
teredin more than one electionprecinct,otherwisethan
is provided in sectiontwelve of thisact, or more than
once in the same precinct,or who shall cause himself to
be registered,knowing that he is not lawfully entitled to
registration; and any person who shall aid or abet in the
commission of any of said acts,shallbe deemed guilty of
a misdemeanor , and shall be imprisoned in the county
jailnot lessthan one nor more than twelve months .
False RegistrationBooks.
§ 16. Any officerof registrationor other person who
shallunlawfullyalterany registrationbook ,or add any
name thereto, or who shall willfullysecrete, suppress,
or destroyany such book ,or who shallmake or aid in
making any falseor fraudulentregistrationbook ,shall
be deemed guilty of felony, and shall be confined in the
penitentiary not less than one nor more than five years ,
and shall forfeitany officehe then holds, and shall for-
ever be disqualifiedfrom holding office.
,
Perjury .
§ 17. Any person who shallwillfullymake any false
statement , under an oath , lawfully administered under
this act,shall be deemed guilty of perjury, and confined
in the penitentiary not less than one nor more than five
years .
ObstructingRegistration.
§ 18. Any person who , by himself or in aid of others,
shallforciblybreak up ,or attemptto break up ,a regis-
tration held under thisact, or shall forciblyprevent , or
attempt to prevent ,any person from approaching or en-
tering a place of registrationfor the purpose of regis-
tering , shall be fined not less than one hundred nor more
than five hundred dollars,or imprisoned not less than
six nor more than twelve months in the county jail, or
both .
§19 . No witness shall be excused from testifyingbe-
fore any grand jury, or in any prosecution or indictment
under thisact, on the ground that his testimony may
criminate himself; but no such testimony shall be used
against him in any prosecution, except for perjury in
giving the same .
Fees .
§20 . For his services under this act the county clerk
shall receivethe following fees, and no other : For copy-
ing the registrylistsrequired to be kept in his office, or
to be used in supplying lostbooks ,the sum of two cents
for each voter whose name is so copied ; for his services
under section thirteenof thisact,the sum of twenty five
cents for the name of each voter stricken off the lists;
for receiptingto clerks of registrationand election for
registrationbooks,the sum of fivecents for each book
receipted for. The sheriffshall receive for serving the
noticesprovided for in section two ,the sum of sixtycents
for each actual service. Officers of registration shall
receivethree dollarsper day for each day employed in
attending at the place of registration,but clerks of reg-
istrationand election shall not be entitledto any pay ,
except upon the production of the county clerk'sreceipt
for theirrespectiveregistrationbooks ,which receipt shall
be the voucher of the officerpaying them . The cityof
Louisvilleshallpay allfeesand expenses incurredunder-
this act for registrations .
§ 21. A copy of this act shallbe printed in each regis--
trationbook made under itsprovision.
§ 22. This act shall take effect and be in force from its-
passage .
Approved April 28, 1884..

laws.summary: This act outlines the process for road contractors in Todd County, Kentucky. It details the execution of bonds, approval by the county judge, and payment procedures. Crucially, Section 8 mandates that the Todd County judge shall provide work on county roads or town streets for persons convicted of penal offenses who are required to work on roads or streets, or to work out fines. This provision allows for the use of convicted individuals, potentially including those from the Black community who were disproportionately convicted of offenses, for forced labor on public works, a common characteristic of Jim Crow era labor practices.

CHAPTER 1162 .
AN ACT to provide for good roads in Todd county, and to regulate tax-
ation in the same .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1. Itshallbe the duty of the judge of the Todd coun-
tycourtto dividesaidcounty intoroad precincts,and ,as
oftenas may be necessary,to appoint a surveyorin each
of said precincts,whose duty it shall be to superintend
the roads therein,and to see that the same are worked
and kept in such repair as the agreement of the contract-
or thereon with the Todd county court requires. No sur-
veyor shallbe allowed , unless by consent of the court,to
resign such place under two years,except he removes
fromtheprecinct. Any surveyormay be removed atany
time by said court.
§2 . The clerk of the county court of said county shall,
withinten days afterthe appointment of a surveyorof a
road precinct,delivera copy of the orderof saidappoint-
ment to the sheriffof said county ,containing a fulland
complete description of the said precinct and the roads
therein, and take his receipt therefor. And said sheriff
shall, within fifteendays thereafter,deliver a copy of the
said order to the said surveyor , and return another copy
thereof to the clerk's office of said court , with his indorse-
ment of the fact and time of said service made thereon ;
which return shall be evidence of the facts therein stated .
Said clerk shallpost up in his office,once in every year ,a
listof the names of all the surveyors of road precincts
in saidcounty,to be made as aforesaid,designatingthe
precinctof each surveyor. The clerkor sherifffailingto
performhisdutiesas prescribedin thisact shallbe guilty
of a misdemeanor , and , on conviction thereof, shall be
fined five dollars for each neglect,to be recovered on a
warrant against him in the name of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky before the judge of the quarterlycourt or
any justiceof the peace of Todd county.
§ 3. Each surveyor of a road precinct in said county
shallbe furnishedwith a copy of the contractfor the
working of the roads in his precinct; and it shall be his
duty to reportto the county judge of Todd county any
failureon the part of the contractor to perform his duties
under said contract, and also to certifyto said judge
when the said contract has been properly complied with .
Said surveyor shall be exempt from jury services, and
from alltaxation for county purposes ,during his term of
service as surveyor as aforesaid. For a failureto dis-
charge any of his dutiesprescribedby thisact,saidsur-
veyor shallbe guiltyof a misdemeanor , and shall, on
conviction thereof, be fined not less than five nor more
than fifteendollars for each offense, to be recovered by
warrant against him in the name of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky , in the Todd quarterly court, which court
shallhave exclusivejurisdictionof allproceedings against
surveyors of road precincts.
§ 4. The judge of the Todd county court shall, at the.
court-house door in Elkton ,Todd county ,Kentucky ,on the
second Monday in March of each year , and at such other
time as he shall deem necessary,letout the working and
keeping in repair and improving of the public roads in
Todd county to the lowest and best bidder,for such length
of time ,not exceeding two years ,as he may elect, after
having firstadvertised the time ,terms , and place of said
lettingby at least two insertionsin a newspaper pub-
lishedin Todd county ,if one should be published in the
county at the time , and by a printed notice posted up for
at least fifteendays before such lettingat the voting
place or places in each voting precinct in said county :
Provided , That the fund raised by the levy court under
this act shall be sufficientto work all of the public roads
in said county : And provided further,That if said funds
should not be sufficientto keep in order and good condi-
tion all the public roads of said county ,then, and in that
event,said fund shallbe used at only such places and for
such roads as the said judge may deem best,having due
regard to the public good and the wants of the different
parts of the said county .
L
i
§5 . Each road contractorshallexecute a bond ,with
good surety.payable to Todd county,covenantingto per-
formhiscontract,which shallbe setforthand specifiedin
saidbond ,and which bond shallbe approved by the said
judge,and by him deliveredto the clerkof said court,
who shallkeep the same as a part of the recordsof his
office,and on which bond said county may recover of said
contractor,by action in the Todd circuitcourt,alldam-
ages which itmay sustainby the failureof saidcontract-
or to comply with the terms of said contract.
§6 . Itshallbe the duty of saidjudge,afterhe issatis-
fied, by the report of the surveyor of the precinct for
which any contract is made ,that the contractor for the
work in said precincthas well and trulyperformed his
contract, to make an order on the order-book of said
court directingthe sheriffof said county to pay said con-
tractorthe contractpriceforsaidwork . Said judge may
make an order or orders directing the contract price for
said work to be paid from time to time during the pro-
gress of saidwork ,but shallnever order payment to be
made for any work not actuallyperformed,and shallat
all times,before the completion of said work according
to contract,retain or keep back a sufficientamount of
the said contractprice to insurethe completion of said
work according to contract.
§7 . All fines assessed under this act shallbe collected
as other fines,and shallinure to the benefit of the road
fund of Todd county ,and shallbe paid out by the sheriff
of Todd county , under the orders of the county judge
thereof .
§ 8. The judge of the Todd county court shallprovide
work on the roads of said county,or on the streetsof
towns therein, for such persons convictedof penal of-
fenses as may , by order of the proper authorities, be
required to work on roads or streets,or to work out fines
assessed against them on the roads or streetsunder the
provisions of general or speciallaws, and may , when
necessary,put a ball and chain upon such persons to
LOC . L.,VOL 11-43
prevent their escape; and, if necessary, may employ
some suitableperson to oversee and guard them while at
work .
§ 9. That all delinquent capitation tax-payers , and
otherswhose taxes cannot be collected,of Todd county,
shallbe required to work out their delinquent taxes, at
such times on the roads in theirseveral road precincts as
the surveyor thereof may require,or as the judge of the
Todd county court may contract for; for which work
such delinquents shallhave creditat the rate of one dol-
larforeach fullday'swork performed by him. For fail-
ing or refusing to comply with the orders of said sur-
veyors, when notified, all such delinquents are made
liableto the penaltiesnow imposed by law againstper-
sons for failingor refusingto work on roads.
§ 10. The county court of Todd county may open
roads,not exceeding sixtyfeet in width ,or may increase
the width of establishedroads to sixtyfeet, anything in
the generallaws to the contrarynotwithstanding.
§ 11.It shallbe the duty of the county attorney to
prosecute all offenders under this act, for which service
he shallreceive twenty -fiveper cent. of the fines recov-
ered; and upon his failure to prosecute, the court may
appoint some other attorney to prosecute in his stead,
who shallreceive the same compensation forhis services.
All fines assessed under this act shall be collected as
other fines, and shall inure to the benefit of the road
fund of Todd county ,and shallbe paid out by the sheriff
under orders of the Todd county court.
§ 12. It shall be unlawful for the judge of the Todd
county court,the county attorney,sheriff,collectorof the
revenue , or any surveyor of a road precinct of Todd
county,tobecome ,directlyor indirectly,interestedin any
contract for working roads, or building or repairing
bridges in Todd county; and it shall be unlawful for
eitherof said officersto buy , or to become interestedin,
any claim growing out of said work or contract. For a
violation of this section, any of said officersshall be
guiltyof a misdemeanor , and , upon convictionthereof,
shallbe fined not less than fiftynor more than fivehun
dred dollars,to be recovered on indictment of the grand
jury in the Todd circuitcourt; and thissectionshallbe
given in charge to the grand jury of the Todd circuit
court .
§ 13. Any person who shallwillfullyor negligently
destroy, injure, or obstructany of the public roads or
public bridges of Todd county ,or any of the culverts or
ditcheson said roads,shallbe guiltyof a misdemeanor ,
and, upon conviction, finednot lessthan ten or more
than fiftydollars,to be recovered on warrant in the Todd
quarterlycourt, and shallalso be liablein double dam-
ages to Todd county , or to any persons aggrieved or
injured,to be recoveredby suitin any courtof thisCom-
monwealth having jurisdictionof the amount . It shall
be the duty ofthe surveyorof any road precinctin which
any such damage or injuryis done to reportthe same
promptly to thejudge of the Todd county court.
§14 . The court of claims of Todd county shall, at their
regular sessionin each year ,or at such other time as they
may deem best, levy for each year a tax of not more
than fifteen cents on each one hundred dollars ' worth of
propertyin Todd county,which may be assessedforrev-
enue purposes,and a capitationtaxof notexceedingone
dollar and fiftycents on each person in said county who ,
under existinglaws ,isrequired to work on roads .
§ 15. All the taxes provided for in this act shallbe col-
lectedby the sheriffof Todd county,forwhich he shall
be paid the same compensation as he is now allowed by
law for collectingthe county levy; and said sheriffand
the suretieson his bond for the collectionof the county
revenue shallbe responsibleforallthe moneys that come
to his hands under the provisions of thisact.
§ 16. All the taxes collected under this act by an ad
valorem tax, and all fines that may be collected under
thisact,and such part of the taxes collected under this
act by a capitationtax as the courtof claims of Todd
county may , from time to time ,designate, shall consti-
tute a fund ,to be known as the road fund ,and shall,
when collected,be held by the sheriffof Todd county,
and by him paid,when and as orderedby the judge of
the Todd countycourt,accordingto theprovisionsof this
act .
§ 17. The county judge of Todd county ,in advertising
and in making contracts for work to be done on the
public roads of Todd county,shallhave fullpower and
authority to advertise and contract for all such work ,
repairs, and improvements to be done on any of the
publicroadsof Todd county as may ,in hisjudgment , be
for the best interestof said county ; and this power may
likewisebe exercisedby saidjudge in the opening or
widening of any road .
§ 18. It shall be unlawful for the judge of the Todd
county court, or for the court of claims or county court
of Todd county ,to use or apply any of the finesor any of
the money collectedon ad valorem tax under the provis-
ions of this act,for any purpose other than the working ,
repairing, and improving of the public roads of Todd
county as providedby thisact.
§ 19. In making contracts for the working ,repairing,
or improvement ofthepublicroadsasaforesaid,thejudge
of the Todd county court may make such terms with the
contractor or contractors of any such work , as to the
work or labor to be performed by delinquent tax-payers ,
or by personsconvictedof penal offenses,as may be best
forsaid county ; and in case the saidjudge makes any such
agreement astodelinquenttax-payers,itshallbe the duty
of the surveyor of the road precinct in which said delin-
quents live,to assistas far as he isablein carryingout
said contract ,
§20 . The court of claims of Todd county shallnot
have the power to make forroad purposes,or forthe or-
dinary expenses of the county ,any other or greater levy
of taxes, either by ad valorem or capitation tax, than
they are authorizedto do by the fourteenthsectionof this
act .
§ 21.No provisionsof the general law is repealedby
thisact which does notcome inconflictwithitsprovisions.
§ 22. This act shall not take effectunless and until it
isratifiedby a majorityof allof the qualifiedvotersof
Todd county voting thereon ,at the regular August elec-
tionfor one thousand eight hundred and eighty-four; and
forthe purpose of taking the sense of said voters thereon
at said election, it shall be the duty of the sheriff of
Todd county to give notice by printed advertisement ,
posted at each voting place, and at two other public
placesin each voting precinctin Todd county,and in a
newspaper printed in Todd county ,ifthere should then be
such a paper published,that a pollwillbe opened at the
regular electionto be held on the firstMonday in August ,
one thousand eighthundred and eighty-four,at each vot-
ing place in Todd county , to take the sense of the voters
of Todd county on the adoption of this act. It shallbe
theduty of the clerkof the Tode county courtto furnish
the officersofelectionat each votingplace in saidcounty
a book suitableforthatpurpose ,one column of which shall
be headed " For the road law ," and the other " Against
the road law;" and it shallbe the duty of the sheriffof
the electionat each of said voting places to ask each voter
who may vote at saidelectionthisquestion,to-wit: " Are
you for or against the road law ? " and itshallbe the duty
of theclerkof saidelectiontoproperlyrecordeach voter's
vote on said question,and of the officersof the election
at each of said voting places in said county to count and
certifythe result of said vote,as they are required to do
thatofothervotesatsaidelection; and thesaidpoll-books
shall be returned to the office of the clerk of the Todd
county court as other poll-books are required to be re-
turned. Said poll-books shallbe compared and the result
of said electioncertifiedby the same officers, at the same
time ,and in the same manner that other poll-books are
requiredto be compared and certified. Ifa majorityof
all of the qualifiedvoters of Todd county voting at said
electionon saidquestionshallvote forsaidlaw,thejudge
of the Todd county court shallstatethatfacton the record-
book of said court,after which this act shall be in full
force and effect .
Approved April 23, 1884.

It also defines voter qualifications for school board elections, explicitly including "all the white qualified voters" and certain tax-paying or child-rearing widows or maids, while generally qualifying voters based on age, citizenship, and taxpaying status, with an exception for sex.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1201 .
AN ACT for the benefitof Kuttawa common schooldistrict, inLyon
county .
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That hereafter the Kuttawa common school district
shall be bounded as common school district number twen-
ty-nine,embracing the town of Kuttawa , Lyon county ,
Kentucky ,is now bounded ,subject only to such changes
as shall be hereafter made by the concurrent action of
the board of trustees of said district and the common
school commissioner of Lyon county .
§2 . A common school shallhereafterbe taught in said
district for not less than five nor more than ten months
of each year ,at which allwhite childrenbetween the age
of six and twenty years residingtherein shall receive in-
structionwithout any charge therefor.
§3 . The exclusivemanagement , regulation,and con-
trolof said school, and of the school fund received from
the State or nation,and of the fund raisedby taxation
under this act , shall be vested in a board of education , to
be composed of six persons.
§ 4. The present board of common school trusteesshall
be members of said board of education during the term
of officefor which they were elected.
§5 . The members of said board of education of Kut-
tawa shall possess the qualificationsof voters of said
district,and shall be a body -politicand corporate ,under
the name of the Board of Education of Kuttawa .
§ 6. On the lastSaturday in June ,one thousand eight
hundred and eighty-four,an electionshallbe held at some
convenient place in the town of Kuttawa ,between the
hours of nine, ante meridian ,and six,post meridian , for
the purpose of electingfour members of the board of
education .
§7 . At the electionsprovided forherein,allthe white
qualifiedvoters, and any widow or maid who is a tax-
payer , or who has childrenbetween six and twenty years
of age, and , exceptingsex,qualifiedto vote,and being
citizensof said district, shallbe voters therein.
§ 8. At the firstelectionfor members of the board of
education ,the three persons receiving the highest num-
ber of votes shall hold officefor four years; and the one
receiving the next highest number , and the two common
school trustees stillremaining in office,shall hold office
fortwo years,and each shallcontinue in officeuntil his
successor is elected and qualified. Each second year
thereafter,at the time,place ,and manner herein desig-
nated, an electionshall be held for three members of the
board ,to serve four years .
§ 9. Said electionsshallbe held in the manner prescribed
for the election of common school trustees .
§ 10. Within ten days afterthe election,the board of
education shalldeliverto each person elected a certificate
of election .
§ 11. Within ten days afterreceiving such certificateof
election,the person shall make oath before any one quali-
fiedto administer an oath to faithfullydischarge the duties
of his office as member of the board of education .
§ 12. The board of education of Kuttawa shall have
power to contract, sue,and plead as a person ; to levy
and collecta tax of not exceeding fortycents on the one
hundred dollars' worth of taxable property,and a poll-
tax of not more than two dollarsper head ; and to receive
and use any property now in possession of the common
school trustees; to receive conveyances of land , and
buy or erectsuch buildingsas may be necessaryforthe
Kuttawa common school; to appoint members to fill
allvacancies in office; to appoint a secretary,collector,
treasurer, assessor, janitor, examiner of teachers, super-
intendent of the school, and fix the salaries of each ; to
expend the funds receivedby them for schoolpurposes;
to establishand control a necessary common school; to
regulate and prescribe rules for the government of the
same ; to prescribe the course of study therein; to ex-
amine , or cause to be examined , teachers; to reprove ,
dismiss,or expel or suspend any teacher or officersap
pointedby them,forinefficiency,neglect,or violationof
duty , or immoral conduct ; to prescribe text books ; to fix
the number of departments in said school; to grade the
school, and regulate the progress of scholars from grade
to grade , and from department to department ; to admit
to the benefits of said school non -resident pupils and
pupilsnot embraced in the schoollaw ,and charge them
tuition therefor; to make by -laws and rulesfor the gov-
ernment of the board and school ; to enlarge the district
when necessary,by consent of the county common school
commissioner; and such otherpowers as may be neces-
saryand proper to effectthe objectscommitted to their
charge : Provided, That before the tax as herein provided
for islevied and collected,the same shallbe submitted to
the white voters of said common school district, at the
election to be held under the supervision of the present
trustees of the Kuttawa common school,previous notice
thereof having been firstgiven ,by written or printed no-
ticesof the said electionbeing posted at fiveof the most
public places in the said district,forat leastten days next
before the day of the said election,statingthe time ,place,
and object of the said election ; and if at said election a
majority of the votes cast shall be in favor of said tax ,
the same shallbe levied and collectedas provided for in
thisact; but if the majority be against the said tax,then
it shall not be levied or collected . And at said election
the question shallbe distinctlyasked each voter,"Are you
for or against the proposed school tax in this district? "
and his vote shall be recorded according to his answer
and certifiedaccordingly; and the said tax shallbe col-
lectedby the collectorappointed by the said board of
education, as provided in sectionfourteen of thisact.
§ 13. Itshallbe the duty of the board of education ,as
soon as properly organized ,to at once buy the building
known as Kuttawa High School , and the lot on which
the same stands,for a sum not exceeding two thousand
dollars, it being understood that said house and lot can
be purchased for said sum ; but in case the board are
unable to buy said house and lot for the sum above
specified,by the stockholders refusing to sell,it shallbe
the duty of the board to select and purchase suitable
grounds,and have erectedthereonsuitablebuildingsfor
the school herein provided for; to employ teachers,and
cause a school to be taught therein; to superintend,
regulate , and control the same ; to assess, so far as au-
thorized by this act, a tax each year for the purpose
of paying for said house and lot,or grounds and build-
ings,and to pay a sufficientnumber of teachers therein;
and the miscellaneous expenses of the school; to take
care of the school property ; receive and disburse the
funds pertaining to the school; select suitable teachers;
fix salaries; grade the school; provide fuel; and such
other duties as they are empowered to do by this act;
make suitable reports to the common school commis-
sioner of the county ; to take titleto them and theirsuc-
cessors in their corporate name for all school property ;
to surrender all school property and funds to their suc-
cessors; and do and perform all other necessary duties
incident to the execution of the trust confided to it.
§ 14. The taxes herein imposed shallbe a lienupon the
property of the person or company owing the same ,situ-
ated in said district. The assessor's book shall be deliv-
ered to the collectoron or before the firstday of July of
each year,and he shallat once make -up therefromhis
tax -book and proceed to collectthe taxes. Said taxes
shallbe due on and after the tenth day of July of each
year,and shallbe paid over by the collectorto the treas-
urer of the board of education , as follows : one -third
thereofon thefirstday of September each year; one-third
on the the firstday of November of each year ; one third
on thefirstday ofJanuary following; and shallgive bond
to the board of education for the faithfulperformance of
his duties; and shall have power to collect said taxes,
when necessary,by processof law ,as the sheriffcollects
ordinary taxes.
§ 15. Allpropertyshallbe liableforthe taxesthatare
hereinprovidedfor,thatisliableforStatetax and county
levy .
§ 16.All theprovisionsof thisactshallbe construedas
applyingtothepersonsand propertyof the whitecitizens
only, of said district.
§ 17. This act shall take effectand be in force from its
passage .
Approved May 1, 1884.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1371, pp. 1087–1088
laws.summary: This act amends existing statutes regarding vagrancy in Fleming County. It mandates that convicted vagrants be sentenced to hard labor for 50 to 100 days. Jailers are required to ensure convicted individuals work eight hours a day, with refusal leading to a bread and water diet. A provision is made for the dependents of convicted laborers, with a daily payment of twenty-five cents to be covered by the county or the beneficiary of the labor.
page_titles: An Act to amend section one hundred and eleven of the General Statutes, in relation to vagrancy in Fleming county.
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1371 .
AN ACT to prevent idlenessand vagrancy in Fleming county .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1. If any person be found in Fleming county idling,
rambling,or loiteringabout,as provided in chapterone
hundred and eleven of the General Statutes,the county
judge, or any justiceof the peace of Fleming county,
shall issue a warrant for the arrest of such person ,who
shall be given a reasonable opportunity to prepare for
trial; and if found guilty of the offensecharged in said.
chapter,shallbe sentenced to hard laborfora periodof
not lessthan fiftynor more than one hundred days .
§ 2. Itshallbe the duty of the jailerof Fleming coun-
ty to see that any person convictedof the offenseof va-
grancy,as provided above,shallbe furnishedwith work
and compelled to labor eighthours a day ; and any per-
son convicted as aforesaid refusing to labor, shall be
compelled to live on bread and water until said person
is willing to work ; but said time not to be deducted from
said person'sterm of labor.
§3 . Any person convicted as aforesaidwho shallhave
a wife or childrendependent on him for support,and who
iscompelledto laborunder sentenceofconvictionas pro-
vided herein, his wife or children shallreceive and be al-
lowed the sum of twenty- five cents per day ; the amount
provided forto be paid by the county should the county
receive the benefitof the labor; but if any town or city
corporation,or individual,procure or receive the benefit
of said labor,then such corporation or person must pay
the wife or childrenthe sum of twenty-fivecentsper day
during the time said person so labors.
§ 4. This act to take effectfrom and afteritspassage .
Approved May 10, 1884.

CHAPTER 1393 .
AN ACT to revisethe charter of the cityof Paducah , and reduce intoone
the severalactsrelatingthereto.
Be itenactedby theGeneralAssemblyof theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That the boundaries of the cityof Paducah shall
be as follows,to-wit: Beginning at a pointknown as the
northwest corner of lotnumber fifteen, of the division of
the estate of William Clarke , on the south side of the
Ohio river,one hundred and seventy -four poles below the
north side of Clay street; thence south forty-three degrees
west threehundred and forty-two poles,to the corner of
Paducah Cemetery ; then south fifteendegrees sixteenmin-
utes east, with the line between said cemetery and the
addition of Flournoy , Harris, Trimble ,and Norton ,sev-
enty-threeand one-halfpoles,to an ironmonument inthe
center of Clay street; thence south thirty-four degrees
east with the line between King and Bradshaw , ninety
polesto a stake; thence north fifty-six degrees east fif-
teen poles to an iron monument ; thence south thirty-nine
degrees east with the line dividing lot number thirteen
from lotsnumbered five,four,three, and two ,of the divis-
ion of the estateof Wm .Clarke,three hundred and twenty-
ninepolesto a mulberryin the base linemarked one and
two ;thence south sixty-seven degrees east with said base
lineto the center of Island creek,at the mouth of Cross
creek; thence in the center of Island creek,and with the
meanders thereof, to its mouth on the Tennessee river;
thence with a course north fifty-sixdegrees eastto the low
water linethereof on Tennessee Island; thence down the
Tennessee river, with the low -water line thereof,binding
on Tennessee Island,tothe lower end of said island;thence
north fifty-six degrees east across the Ohio river to the
low -water line of the same on the Illinoisshore ; thence
down the Ohio river with the low -water line thereof ,bind-
ing on the Illinoisshore,to a pointwhere a linefrom the
beginning point of thisboundary above described,with a
course north forty-three degrees east, will intersectsaid
low -water line; thence south forty-three degrees west
across the Ohio river to the beginning ; and the territory
embraced within thisboundary ishereby declared to be a
city, and the inhabitants thereof are created a body -pol-
iticforever, with perpetual succession,by the name of
the cityof Paducah , and by that name retainingand
possessingthe power to sue and be sued, plead and
be impleaded , contract and be contracted with ; to have
and to use a common seal,and the same to alter,change ,
and renew at pleasure; and to hold,enjoy,lease,or sell,
or dispose of any property now vested in the city of
Paducah , or any person or corporation for said city,or
which may be hereafter acquired ,to the intent and pur-
poses forwhich the same is,was , or may be granted , not-
withstanding itslocality; and in allsuitsagainst the city
serviceor processshallbe (served) upon the mayor ,and
in his absence upon the clerk and marshal of said city.
The cityshallhave policejurisdictionin Kentucky ,out-
side the corporate limits,for one and a half miles all
around from said boundary .
§2 . The cityshallbe divided into sixwards ,as follows: Wards.
FirstWard . All that portion of the city north of the
center line of Monroe street, extended from the river out
to the corporation line.
SecondWard . All that portionof the citybetween the
firstward , as above described, and Broadway street.
Third Ward . Allthatportionofthecitybetween Broad-
way and the centerlineof Washington street,extended
from the riverout to the corporation line.
Corporate pow-
ers .
City council.
Qualifications.
FourthWard . All thatportionof the citybetween the
third ward , as above described,and the center line of
Adams street, extended out from the river to the corpora-
tion line .
FifthWard . All that portion of the citybetween the
center line of Adams street and the center line of Ten-
nesseestreet,extendingfrom the riverto the corporation
line .
Sixth Ward . All that portion of the city between the
center line of Tennessee street and the southern bound-
ary line of the city, extending from the river to the
boundary line aforesaid. The boundaries of said wards
may be changed ,or the number of the wards increased,
by the council of said city. Representation shall be as
nearly equal and uniform as may be , and regulated by
the number of the qualifiedvoters.
Powers of Government .
§3 . The corporate powers of the city of Paducah shall
be divided into three distinct parts,viz : legislative, ex-
ecutive,and judicial; and no officerof one of the depart-
ments shallexerciseany power properlybelonging to
either of the others,except in the instances herein ex-
pressly permitted .
LegislativeDepartment .
§4 . The legislativepower shall be vested in the coun-
cil of the city of Paducah , which shall consist of two
members from each ward in the city,electedby the qual-
ified voters of each ward , as herein directed , and hold
theirofficesfor two years,and until theirsuccessors are
duly elected and qualified. The election for councilmen
shall be held on the firstMonday in March in each year .
§5 . No person shallbe eligibleas a councilman of the
city of Paducah who ,at the time of his election, is not
a male citizenof the United States,who has not attained
the age of twenty -four years , and who has not resided
within the corporate limitsof said cityfor two years next
preceding his election,and who is not a bona fideresident
of the ward for which he may be chosen ; and if he or
|
hiswife is not the owner ,bonafide,of realestatein the
city of Paducah ,or who holds or discharges any officeor
agency under the city of Paducah , the county of Mc-
Cracken ,the State of Kentucky ,or the United States of
America ,or any department thereof, or any foreign gov-
ernment whatever ,or who , at the time of his election,is
interested,directlyor indirectly,in any contract with the
city of Paducah ,or who isbound on any bond to the city,
eitheras principalor security,or holdsany officeof trust
or salary in any corporation which holds any contract
with said city, the terms, rates, or priceswhereof are
subject to modification or enforcement by the said coun-
cil; and no collectoror keeper of the cityfunds or money
shallbe eligibleuntil he has settledwith said city,and
obtained a quietus : Provided, No person shall be ineli-
gibleto officeinthecityby reason of being on any license
bond to said city,either as principal or surety.
§6. If,afterelection,any member of the councilshould
remove from the ward from which he was chosen , or
accept any officeor agency,the holding or discharging
of which would have rendered him ineligible, or do any
other act which would render him ineligibleto his seat
as a member of said council,his officeshallbe thereby
vacated,and the vacancy filledas herein directedwith
regard to fillingvacancies .
§7 . Stockholdersin corporationsmay be eligible,but
shall not vote on any question directlyor indirectlyaf-
fectingsuch corporation,or any rightor duty under the
same .
§8 . No person shall be ineligibleby reason of his
being an officerin the militiaof Kentucky .
§ 9. The council shall keep , or cause to be kept , a cor-
rect journal of its proceedings , and immediately after
adjournment of each session, at which one or more or-
dinances are passed , and before enforcing same , shall
cause such ordinance or ordinances to be published at
leastonce,in some newspaper publishedand printedin
Paducah , to be selected annually by the council, or as
may be prescribedby ordinance; and itshallbe the duty
Compensation
of the council every ten years or oftener,if two -thirds of
allthe councilmen in officedeem it proper ,to revise and
publishin pamphlet form the charterand amendments
thereto, and the ordinances of the council,for such distri-
bution as may be prescribed by ordinance .
§ 10. The members of the council shall meet within one
week aftertheir election; and shall meet regularly every
two weeks , and oftener ifthe interestsof the citymay re-
quire it; and shallmeet upon theirown adjournment ,and
determine the rules of their own proceedings ; and shall
designate by ordinance the time and place of theirmeet-
ings.
§ 11. The council shall,by ordinance ,have the power
to allow and fixthe compensation of itsmembers fortheir
attendance at itsmeetings ,whether regular or called; but
such compensation shallnot exceed threedollarsfor each
member for each meeting ; and they shallbe exempt from
servingon juriesof allkinds,and from militaryduty dur-
ing the term of service.
§ 12. A majority of the members of the council shall
constitutea quorum to do business; but a smaller number
may adjourn from day to day,and may compel the at-
tendance of absent members in such manner and under
such penalties as may be prescribed by ordinance .
§ 13.The council may ,by ordinance ,prescribethe rules
of itsproceedings, and by proper penaltiesenforce the
same ,and punish members for disorderlybehavior ,and ,
by the concurrence of two -thirds of all the members
elected,may expel a member for improper conduct.
§14 . The council may electfrom the police of the city
a sergeant-at arms and door -keeper ,and shall prescribe
the duties to be performed by these officers; and the po-
liceofficersthus servingas door-keeper or sergeant-at-
arms shall not receive additional compensation for such
services .
§ 15. The council shalljudge of the qualification,elec-
tion,and returnof itsown members ,and shallprescribe,
by ordinance,the manner in which any or allcontested
elections shall be determined .
streets,& c .§ 16. No ordinance of the council requiring the im- Improvementof
provement of streetsand alleys of the cityat the expense
of lot -owners shall have force as a law unless the same
be voted for by two -thirds of all the councilmen then
elected, nor unless the yeas and nays thereon be recorded
in the journalof proceedings:Provided,That iftheown-
ers of a majority of feetfront on any street or alley, or
part of the same ,not lessthan one block in length,shall
petitionthe council to have same improved , in such case
the councilshallhave the power ,by a vote of a majority

improvement of such street or alley, or part thereof, as
aforesaid; thevoteofsaidmajority,however,shall[be]by

That when the council shall require the improvement of
that part of the several streetsof the cityrunning to the
river, which lies between ordinary high-water mark , or
top of the bank of the river, and low -water mark , one-
half of the cost of said improvement shall be borne by
the cityand the other half by the owners of the grounds
fronting on the same .

§ 17. All assessments of rates of taxation upon the Assessments.
property of the cityof Paducah shall be ascertained
and fixed by a no lessnumber than two thirds of allthe
members of the council then elected, and the order or
resolutionlaying the per centum of taxes upon the tax-
able property of said cityshallbe passed and evidenced
by a vote of the council, upon the calls of the yeas and
nays, to be recorded upon the journal of proceedings.
All other laws and resolutionsof said council,except as
hereinprovided,shallbe valid,if voted forby a majority
of the members present.
§ 18.Upon allquestionsvoted upon by the councilany
member shallhave the rightto callfortheyeas and nays,
and have the same recorded upon the journal of pro-
ceedings .
§19. The councilshallhave powers,withinthe cityLevyandcollect
limits,to levy and collect taxes,at the rate not exceed-
ing two and one half dollars on each hundred dollars'

doing business in the city.

§ 22. To make regulations to prevent the introduction
or spreading of contagious or infectiousdiseases in the
city; to pass quarantine laws , and enforce the same ,
within five miles of the boundary of the city; to estab-
lishhospitalsor pest-houses in or outside of the city,and
to make regulationsfor theirgovernment ; and to make
allregulations to secure the general health of the inhab-
itantsof the city.
§ 23. To prevent,abate,and remove physicalnuisances
at the cost and expense of the owners or occupants ,or of
partiesupon whose ground they exist, and define and .
declare,by ordinance , what shall be a nuisance ,and to
punish by fine any person keeping ,causing ,erecting, or
committing a nuisance ,eitherphysical or moral .
§ 24. To provide the citywith water ; to erecthydrants ,
fire-plugs, and pumps in the streetwithin or beyond the
limitsof the city; and forthispurpose may subscribefor
stock in a water -works company , not exceeding one hun-
dred thousand dollars,and pay forsame in the bonds of
the city, or may issue her bonds for not exceeding one
hundred thousand dollars, and construct operate , and
maintain water -works : Provided, Any ordinance sub-
scribingstock as aforesaid,or for issue of bonds forbuild-
ing water -works as aforesaid,shall be firstsubmitted to
a vote of the qualifiedvoters of the city; and if a major-
ityat such election shallvote in favor of the ordinance ,
then the ordinance shall be a law .
§25 . To open, receive, alter, widen, extend, grade,
pave ,gravel, or otherwise improve,clean, and keep in
repairstreets,alleys, avenues,lawns ,wharves,landings,
public grounds and squares, in the manner hereinafter
provided ,and to drain the streetsand public places, and
to condemn land for draining purposes in the manner
and under the proceedings required herein.
§ 26. To establish, erect, and keep in repairbridges,
culverts, and sewers , and regulate the use of same ; to
erect dams , and cover them over when the interests of
the public require it.
§ 27. The councilshallhave power to pass ordinances
to require the construction of sewers in the streets or
alleys at the cost of the owner or owners of the ground
fronting such sewers ; and the cost of such sewers to be
apportioned according to the number of feetfront each
may own in front of said sewer ; and a lien is hereby
created on the said ground for the cost thereof. Said
sewers,when requiredto be constructed,the councilshall
order done by the passage of an ordinance , which shall
fullydeclare and prescribe the kind and extent of the
sewer .
§ 28. The advertisements,contracts,and other proceed-
ings shall conform in all respects to similar proceedings
for the construction of streets .
§ 29. To provide for the lightingof the streets,market-
houses,and otherpublicbuildings,rooms,and offices.
§30 . To establish, support, and regulate policemen,
night-watches ,and patrols,and prescribetheirduties and
compensation .
§ 31. To erect market -houses ,establishmarket places,
and provide for the government and regulation thereof;
and elect market -masters and inspectors of articlessold
therein,prescribe their duties, and fix their compensa-
tion; and to provide for the condemnation and destruc-
tion of stale and unwholesome meats and vegetables;
and may licensethe use of market -house stalls,under such
regulations, and for such sums , as itmay deen proper .
§ 32. To provide for the erection and repair of needful
public buildings for the city; and for inclosing and im-
proving allpublic grounds belonging to the city.
§33. To improve and preservethe navigationof the
Ohio and Tennessee riverswithin the citylimits.
§ 34. To erect, make , and repair wharves and docks ;
to regulate and fixthe wharfage thereat; and to license,
tax, and regulate wharf -boats,coal-boats, and flat-boats ;
and may tax each wharf-boat kept in frontof said city
not less than three hundred dollars per year ; and tax
other boats or water -craftslying in front of the city at a
rate of not lessthan fiftydollarsnor more than one hun-
dred and fiftydollarsper annum for each boat .
§ 35. To regulate the stationing and anchoring of ves-
sels or boats or raftswithin the citylimits,and the de-
positing of freightor lumber on the public wharves .
§36 . The council shall prescribeby ordinance the
amount of tax for any licenseauthorizedby thischar-
ter,and not herein fixed,at any sum ,in theirdiscretion;
and the council shall have power to prescribe by ordi-
nance penalties against those who may failto obtain a
licensein any case wherein a licenseis requiredby this
charter,not exceeding a fineof fifteenhundred dollars.
§37 . The council shall have power to provide for the
prevention and extinguishment of fires,and to regulate
and establishfirecompanies ,to electfireengineers, and
all officersand men , prescribe theirduties and fix their
compensation ; and the volunteer members of such com-
panies ,who receive no pay ,shallbe exempt from serving
on juriesand of paying poll-tax so long as they remain
active members of such company ; to regulate and restrain
the erection of wooden buildings,and to provide for the
removal of same when builtcontrary to the ordinances of
the city; to appoint firewardens and property guardians ,
with fullpower to arrestand keep away from the vicinity
of any fire idle or suspicious persons lurking near the
same , and to compel any person or persons present to
assist in extinguishing firesor prevent the spreading of
same ,and to have the power to compel allpersons pres-
ent at a fire to assistin the preservation of property
exposed to the dangers of the fire, and to prevent the
purloiningor stealingof goods or propertyat such fire,
and such other powers as may be prescribedby ordi
nance .
§ 38. To regulate the sweeping and cleaning of chim-
neys ,and to fixthe fees therefor, and prescribe the man-
ner of collection ,
§ 39. To regulatethe storageof gunpowder ,rosin,tar,
pitch,cotton,and allothercombustiblematerial; and to
appoint some suitable person or persons, at reasonable
terms , to enter and examine such houses as they may
designate, in order to ascertain whether any of such
houses are in a dangerous condition with reference to
fires,and to cause such as are dangerous to be immedi-
ately put in a safe order and condition.
§ 40. To erect and keep in repairaccurate public scales,
and to electa public weigher or weighers to attend to the
same , and fixfees and compensation for his service; and
to regulate the weights and measures to be used in the
city,in allcaseswhere the same are not providedforby
law .
§41 . To provide for the measurement of lumber , and
all other building material .
§ 42. To provide forthe inspection,weighing ,and meas-
urement of hay , stone, coal, charcoal, fire-wood , beef,
pork,bacon ,meal,flour,whisky in barrels,hogsheads,or
other vessels, and coal oil: Provided,however, Nothing in
this act shallbe so constructed as to authorize the inspec-
tion or weighing of any of the articlesenumerated which
are to be shippedbeyond the limitsof the city,except at
the requestof the owners thereof, or the agent having
charge .
§ 43. To pass ordinancesrequiringallcoal and wood ,
when sold and delivered in the city, to be weighed or
measured by the publicweigher; and tofixadequate pen-
altiesfor the violationof same ; also requiring allaurora
or other illuminating oils,before being sold in the city, to
be inspectedby the publicinspector,and if found by him
to be of a dangerous quality,to report the same to the
mayor at once; and the council shallfixby ordinance
penalties for violationof thissection.
§ 44. To provide for and regulate the inspection of
butter, lard, and other provisions; to regulate the vend-

ing of meat , and all other articlesof consumption , as
may be enumerated by ordinance ; and to restrainand
prevent the forestallingof provisions brought to the city
forsale; and to prevent hucksters from forestallingsuch
provisionsas may be brought to the cityfor sale; and
to fix by ordinance the penalties for the violationof this
section .
§ 45. To erect a work -house ,poor -house , and house of
correction, and to provide for the regulation and gov-
ernment thereof .
§ 46. To provide for the appointment or electionof all
officersof the city,servantsand agents of said city,not
otherwise provided for,and fixcompensation and fees
for theirservices; and to regulate the pay and fees of all
juries,witnesses,and others for services rendered under
thisact,or under any ordinance .
§ 47. To license,tax, and regulate ferrieson the Ohio
and Tennessee riverswithin the limitsof the city,and
to fix the rates and charges thereon , or they shall have
the power to lease,under such terms as shallbe deemed
to the interestof the city,any such ferryfor a term of
not exceeding five years,and require of the lessee such
bonds as may be proper to insure the observance of law
and fullcompliance with the terms of the lease : Pro-
vided,however, That no existingcontract with the city for
the lease of the ferry shall,in anywise , be affected or
impaired by thisact.
§ 48. To levy and collectannually ,upon every male of
the citytwenty -one years of age or over, and who is a
residentof said city,a head or personal tax not exceed-
ing three dollars; and provide for the collectionof the
same by levyand saleof the personaland realproperty
of the person against whom said tax is assessed.
§49 . To prevent and restrainany riot, rout, noise,
disturbance,or disorderlyor unlawful assembly in any
street,house,or other place in the city,and for the ar-
rest and confinement of the parties engaged or taking
part in the same .
§ 50. To prevent and remove any and allencroach-
ments intoorupon any street,alley,orsidewalk,any lane,
avenue ,wharf , or public grounds establishedby thischar-
teror by ordinance,which now exists,or which hereafter
may be established; and to exercisecomplete and perfect
controlover allpublic squares or commons belongingto
the city,and over allproperty,realand personal,belong-
ing to the citylying within or beyond the limitsof said
city; and the possession or holding of any street, alley,
or other public grounds ,commons ,public easement , in or
out of the city,by any person,shallnot be deemed ad-
verse but amicable ; and no time shallrun against the city
in reference to such property or rights untilnotice of ad-
verse claim shallhave been served upon the council.
§ 51. To appoint and remove at pleasure, and pre-
scribe the duties, compensation , and fees of the follow-
ing officers: wharf -master , warden or keeper of the
work -house or house of correction, keeper of the poor-
house, keeper of the pest-house, superintendentand
keeper of the hospital, cityphysician, market-masters,
sextons, inspectors, gaugers , weighers , measurers , street
inspectors,keeper of the cityprison,gas-lighter, and any
other servants or agents of the city.
§ 52. The council may release any surety upon any
bond that may have been executed to the city, by and
with the written consent of the principal and co-sureties,
and with theirwritten consent receive other securityup-
on such bond ; and the council shallhave the power to
release a security upon any bond hereafter executed to
the city, and receive another in his room and stead ; and
the former securitiesand the new suretiesor surety thus
substituted,together with the principalin the bond , shall
be bound by such sum or additional bond ; but it shall
not be requiredof any person electedin said cityto be
releasedupon any bond executed to saidcityas surety
beforehiselection; but beforeany such person electedto
officequalifies,he shallobtainreleaseas such security
as herein provided .
§53 . To prevent training of horses or breaking the
same , or exhibiting of stallionsin the streetsand other
public places of the city,and to provide for theirremoval
from the city,or the killingof mischievous or vicious ani-
mals,and forthe punishment,by suitablefinesor penal-
ties, of the owner or keeper of such animals for allowing
them to run at large; and they shall have the power ,by
suitableordinances, to prevent hogs ,dogs , and other ani-
mals from running at large in the city.
§ 54. The council may grant the right of way over the
streetsand otherpublicgrounds of the cityto any rail-
road company or streetrailroadcompanies ,for such time ,
and in such manner ,and on such conditions as may seem
proper ; and shallhave a supervising control over the use
of same , and shall regulate speed of cars,signals, and
fare on street cars; and under like condition and super-
vision,may grant the rightof way that may be necessary
to gas ,electriclight,telegraph and telephone companies .
§ 55. To make rules, regulations, by -laws , and ordi-
nances for maintaining the peace ,good government , and
orderof the city,and the preservationof the property of
the city,and the trade and commerce and manufactures
thereof,as the council may deem expedient , not repug-
nant to the Constitution of this State or of the United
States,and to enforce the observance thereof by inflicting
penaltiesand finesnot exceding one hundred dollars for
any offense; and to make allordinanceswhich may be
necessaryforthe carryingintoeffectthe power vestedby
this act in the citygovernment ,or any department or of-
ficethereof; but no ordinance that may be passed by the
council shall relate to more than one subject, and that
shallbe expressed in the title,except as herein provided .
§56 . The council shall have the power to purchase
lands for and locatecemeteriesand forother purposes,
either within the citylimits or elsewhere in McCracken
county,and exercisefulland complete controlover the
same ; and enforce the regulation and management there-
of by adequate finesand penalties; and may appoint one
or more sextons, and regulate their duties and fix their
compensation .
§ 57. The council shall have power ,at eitherof the
regularmeetings in the month of April,one thousand
eighthundred and eighty-four,to electthree persons to
be styled trustees of Oak Grove Cemetery , and said trus-
tees shall have the control and superintendence of said
cemetery ,under the ordinances and resolutions of the
council,and who shall perform the duties prescribed by
the council, and shall hold their officefrom the time of
their appointment until the firstMonday in June , one
thousand eight hundred and eighty-five, or until their
successors are duly elected. The council,at eitherof its
regular meetings in the month of June , one thousand
eight hundred and eighty-five,shall elect three persons
as trustees ; and the council shall divide said trustees into
three classes; the firstshall hold his officefor one year ,
the second shall hold his officefor two years, and the
thirdshallhold officefor threeyears,respectively,from
the time of their election in June , one thousand eight
hundred and eighty-five, or until their successors are
duly elected or appointed; and in the month of June
thereafterof each year , at eitherof itsregular meetings ,
the council shall elect one trustee for the term of three
years; and the council shallfillallvacancies in said trus-
tees by election,at the firstmeeting of the council after
receiving notice of the vacancy . The officeof trustee
of Oak Grove Cemetery shall not be incompatible with
the officeof councilman ,and said trusteesshallnot receive
any salaryor feesfortheirservices,and shallbe residents
of the city, and bona fide owners of lotsin said cemetery .
§58. The councilshallhave the power to defend by
ordinance what shallconstitutevagrancy ,and the punish-
ment thereof .
§ 59. The council,in the name of the city,shallhave
power to subscribeforand hold and sellstockin any pub-
lic corporation for the building of roads and bridges in
the Commonwealth of Kentucky , and in one or more
railroad companies for the building of railroads in the
northwest side of the Ohio river, terminating in Paducah ,
to be paid by the bonds of the city,bearing interestnot
exceeding fiveper cent.per annum ,the subscriptionnot
to exceed one hundred thousand dollarsto any one road ;
and to purchase and hold any personal or real estate
within or without the limits of the city; and to borrow
money ,subject to the following qualifications: The coun-
cilshallnot have the power , on behalfof the city, to
createany new debt or liabilityexceeding twenty thou-
sand dollarsfor one objector purpose,nor subscribefor
stock in any incorporated company ,or give the bonds of
the cityin payment therefor, in amount exceeding the
sum of twenty thousand dollars; nor shall the council
have power to appropriate money ,directlyor indirectly,

§ 80. There is hereby establisheda sinking fund for the
