and whenever a verdictshallbe had ,the court shallgive
judgment condemning such land or other materialfor
the use of said city, and for the amount of damages
assessed,and also to the owner for his costs; ifthe ver-
dictshallbe for more than was assessed by the commis-
sioners, and such valuation, when tendered or paid to
the owner or owners , or deposited in bank to the credit
of the owner or owners ,and a certificateof depositfiled
in said court, shall entitlethe said cityto the land or
material valued ,and the titleto the same ,and the inter-
est and duration of interestvalued by said commission-
ersor assessedby the jury; and itshallnot be necessary,
afterthe report of the commissioners upon the land or
material as hereinbefore provided for,in order to the use
and occupation of the same ,to await the issue of the
proceedings,in case exceptions are filedto the report;
and the report of the commissioners , afterthe payment
or tender to the owner ,or deposit in bank ,of the amount
assessed, shallbe a bar to allactions fortaking and using
such property .
§ 194. All costs,contracts, and proceedings of the coun-
cilof the cityof Paducah ,from the eleventh day of Feb-
ruary,one thousand eighthundred and seventy-one, up
to February fifth, one thousand eight hundred and seven-
ty-three,be ,and the same are hereby ,legalizedand made
valid .
§ 195. In any case of litigationnow pending , or that
may hereafter be instituted, wherein the records, or a
certifiedcopy of any proceedings of the council, which
proceedingwas had priorto the eleventhday of Febru-
ary,one thousand eighthundred and seventy-three,may
lawfully be introduced as evidence ,itshall be lawful for
any party interestedin such suit or litigation, either as
plaintiffor defendant, to introduce,eitherorallyor by
deposition, the mayor , clerk of the council, or any one or
more of the councilmen who were in office at the time
of the making up of the record so offered as evidence ,
to explain and testifyas to the realaction of saidcoun-
cil touching the matters in litigation, and to show that
the charter has in fact been complied with, whether the
records thereof show the fact or not : it being the intent
of thisact that the records of said cityin regard to public
improvements within the citylimitsshallnot be conclu-
siveproof of the actionof said council,but shallbe sub-
ject to contradictionor modification,just as any other
evidence by the mayor ,clerk,or councilmen .
§196 . All actionsagainstthe cityof Paducah ,or any
officerthereof,to recover taxes or assessments which have
been or may be illegallyassessedor collected,shallbe
prosecuted within one year after the cause of action
arose ,and not afterwards .
Public Schools .
§ 197. The public schools of the cityshallbe managed
and controlled by two trustees elected from each ward ,
styled " trusteesof the public schools," who shallpossess
the same qualificationsas to age , sex , residence, and
property as councilmen ; and one trustee shallbe elected
from each ward at the general electionin March in each
year ,whose term of officeshall be two years,and until
theirsuccessors are elected and qualified.
1. The trusteesof the public schools shallhave power
to elector appoint such officersas may be necessary for
their own government , and to require covenant , with
surety,from any or allofficersforthe faithfuldischarge
of their duties; to make by -laws , not in conflictwith
this charter, for carrying out the duties of their office,
and for the government of itsown officers,schools,teach-
ers,pupils,and employes;to determinetheirown rulesof
proceeding ,and to appoint superintendents,teachers,and
other officersand employes , and regulate and fix their
terms, duties, and compensation, and remove them at
pleasure .
2. The trusteesshall, before entering upon the duties
of theiroffice, make oath or affirmationas prescribed in
this charter,and shall meet at least once a month . A
majority of all the trustees elected shall be a quorum
for the transaction of business; and they shall keep a
correct record of all their proceedings, open to inspec-
tion of the citizens .
3. The councilof the cityof Paducah shallhave power
to levy and collecta tax in each year upon allthe taxa-
ble property of the city,for the support and maintenance
of the public schools, not to exceed twenty -five cents on
each one hundred dollars' worth of taxable property ,and
a head or poll-tax not to exceed one dollar; and the col-
lectorof taxes shall,without unnecessarydelay,pay to
the treasurer of the public schools the amount of taxes
collectedby him under the levy for school purposes,
and take his receipt therefor, which shall be a sufficient
voucher in any settlement of the collectorwith the coun-
cilor trusteesof the public schools.
4. The trustees shall have power to receive from the
school commissioners of McCracken county , or from any
other source,any and allsums of money provided by law
for school purposes .
5. The trusteesof the public schools shallprovide and
maintain ,out of the funds levied or otherwise provided
for the purpose , suitable buildings, teachers, and other
employes , sufficientfor the education of all children of
the city between six and twenty years of age ,and shall
provide separate buildings and schools for education of
white and black pupils.
6. The trustees of the public schools shallbe trustees
of the Male University and the Female Seminary of the
city.
7. The trusteesof the public schools shallmake annual
reports to the council,showing all items of income and
expenditure , and the condition and attendance of the
schools,classifyingthe same so as to make itconvenient
for reference,which report shallbe published.
Miscellaneous .
§ 198. Each officer of the city elected at a general
election by the people , or elected by the council (except
councilmen and trusteesof the publicschools),shallex-
ecute a covenant to the city of Paducah , with three or
more good and sufficientsureties,to be approved by the
council,conditioned that he will well,truly,and faithfully
execute and discharge all the duties of his officeaccord-
ing to law ; that he will faithfullyand promptly make
and file all settlements,and account for and pay over,
according to law and the orders and ordinances of the
council ,all money and moneys which shall come to his
hands as such officer; and that he will turn over to his
successor,or to such person as may be designatedby the
council, allbooks, papers, and propertyof any descrip-
tion, belonging to his office, or the city of Paducah ,or
shall have come to his hands by virtue of his office.
Upon the failureof any officerto execute such covenant
for thirtydays ,his officeshallbe declared vacant .
§ 199. The city of Paducah shall have a lien upon
all property, real and personal, subject to execution,
owned or belonging to the treasurer,collectorof taxes,
or assistantchief of police respectively, at the date of
the execution of their respective covenants , or which
may thereafterbe acquiredby him,which lienshallnot
be discharged until such officershall have obtained
quietus for any public dues for which he may be bound .
No covenant of any officershallbe satisfiedor void upon
the first,or any other recovery,untilthe city of Paducah ,
and every person aggrieved by the acts or omissionsof
the officer,shallhave been recompensed .
a
§ 200. The councilmay ,at any time,requireadditional
suretiesupon the covenant of any officer,or may require
an officerto execute a new covenant ; and upon failure
of such officerto furnish additional sureties,or execute
a new covenant when required to do so, and within the
time prescribedby the council,hisofficeshallbe declared
vacant .
§201 . Each officerof the city,before entering on the
discharge of the duties of his office, shalltake and sub-
scribe the following oath or affirmation , to-wit : " I do
solemnlyswear (or affirm, as the case may be)that I will
support the Constitutionof the United States and the
Constitutionof the State,and be faithfuland trueto the
Commonwealth of Kentucky , so long as I continue a
citizenthereof; and that I will faithfullyexecute ,to the
best of my ability, the officeof of the city of
Paducah ,accordingto law ; and I do solemnly swear (or
affirm) that, since the adoption of the present Consti-
tution,I,being a citizen of this State,have not fought a
duel with deadly weapons withinthe State,nor out of it,
with a citizen of this State; nor have I sent or accepted
a challengeto fighta duel with deadly weapons with a
citizen of this State ; nor have I acted as second in car-
rying a challenge,or aided or assistedany person thus
offending: so help me God ;" which oath or affirmation
shall be filedwith the clerk of the council.
| §202 . All ordinances or parts of ordinances of the
cityof Paducah now in force, not in conflictwith this
charter, shall continue in force until repealed by the
council; and alllaws vestingrightsin,or imposing du-
tiesupon ,the cityof Paducah ,not herein supersededor
repealed,shallremain in forceuntilrepealedby the Gen-
-eralAssembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky .
§203 . The recognized records of the trustees of the
town of Paducah , and of the city of Paducah , and all
bonds and contracts executed to the said town or city,
shallremain in fullforce; and remaining in the proper
offices of said city, are hereby declared to be public
records; and copies thereof, certifiedby the proper offi-
cer or keeper thereof,shallbe evidence in all courts to
the same extentthat the originalwould be on due proof.
§ 204. If, from any cause ,the council shallfailto ap-
point or electany officerat the time fixedhereinforthe
appointment or election,it shallbe lawful for the coun-
cil to make such appointment or election at any time
thereafter in all cases where the council has the power
of appointment or election.
§ 205. This act shall be designated and cited as the
general charter of Paducah .
§ 206. The officersof the city of Paducah now in office
shall hold and discharge the duties thereof untilthe elec-
tion and qualificationof their successors as provided
herein, and the firstelection for the following officers
shallbe: formayor ,firstMonday in March ,one thousand
eight hundred and eighty-five; one councilman and one
trusteeof public schools, firstMonday in March , one
thousand eight hundred and eighty-five; for judge of
Paducah citycourt, firstMonday in August, one thou-
sand eight hundred and eighty-six; for cityattorney, first
Monday in August, one thousand eight hundred and
eighty-six; for clerk of the council and treasurer, first
Monday in June,one thousand eighthundred and eighty-
five .
§ 207. All laws or parts of laws in conflictwith this
act are hereby repealed.
§ 208. This act shallgo into effectand be in fullforce
from and afterthe date of itspassage .
Approved May 12, 1884..

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1431 .
AN ACT forthe benefitof common schooldistrictnumber forty-three,in
Graves county.
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That all territoryembraced within the limits of
common school districtnumber forty-three, in Graves
county,and the white personslivingin said district,be,
and they are hereby , created and incorporated as school
districtnumber forty-three, Graves county , which shall
be under the control of the trustees of said district elect-
ed as now provided by law .
§2 . The trustees of said districtshall have power to
make allby -laws and rulesfor the government of them .
selves and their appointees, and for the management ,
control, and government of the school, and to enforce
such by-laws and rulesby suitablefinesand penalties,
to be recoveredin any courthaving jurisdictionof the
amount ,to be paid, when collected,to the trustees, and
be a part of the schoolfund forsaiddistrict.
§3 . The trusteesof said district,in addition to taking
the oath prescribed by the common school law , shallexe-
cute a bond to thecommon schoolcommissionerofGraves
county ,conditioned for the faithfulperformance of their
duties as trustees, and to pay over to the proper person
in due time allmoney which shallcome into their hands
as trustees .
§4 . The said trustees shallcause to be kept a regular
and correctjournal of alltheirproceedings in a well
bound book ,which shallat alltimes be open to the in-
spection of any one of said trustees, or any citizen of
said school district .
§ 5. Said trusteesshallappoint allteachersand other
persons necessary to the successful carrying on of said
school, fix their salariesor compensations ,and for good
cause dismiss or suspend any teacher or other person
appointed by them ,and prescriberulesfor the govern-
ment of the school; and in no case whatever shall any
other than a graduate of some college or university of
good reputation be appointed as superintendent or prin-
cipal of said school; and in no case shalla teacher be
appointedto act in saidschoolwho has not had previous
experience in teaching,and who does not hold a first-
class firstgrade certificatefrom commissioner of common
schoolsof Graves county. The trusteesshallalso pre-
scribe the branches of education to be taught in said
school, which may , in addition to the common school
courseprescribedby theState,includethe usualcurricu-
Jum of studiestaught in the high schools and colleges of
this or other States, or such parts thereofas shallbe
deemed fitby the trusteesof said school.
§6. That allwhite childrenover sixand under twenty
yeas of age ,within said district,shallhave equal rights of
admission to the school of said district, and shall not be
charged anything for tuition; but said trusteeshave the
power to admit any white non -resident pupil into said
school upon such terms and conditions,and upon the
payment of such charges,as the trusteesmay deem suita-
ble ; and all sums received for such tuition shall consti-
tutea partof the schoolfund of saiddistrict.
§7 . The said trusteesshallhave the powers and rights,
in addition to the powers herein expresslygranted , which
pertain ,by the general common school law ,to trusteesof
common schools. They shall make all such enumera-
tions and census returns to the common school commis-
sioner of Graves county as are or may be required by
the general common school law ; and shallhave the right
to receiveand appropriateto the said schoolthe funds or
taxes due or to become due from the State and all other
sources to the common schools; and itshallbe the duty
of the common school commissioner of Graves county to
pay the same to them at such times as payments are
prescribed in the revised school laws of the Common-
wealth .
§ 8. The trustees shallhave power to regulate and de-
termine the lengths of terms and sessionsof said school
for each year ; and for what length of time such schools
shall be taught in each department of said school, and
the number of hours in the day : Provided,however, They
shall have taught a five months ' term free every year .
§ 9. No books , tracts, papers , or catechisms,or other
publications of a sectarian, denominational , or infidel
character , shall be used or distributed in said school , nor
shall any sectarian or infideldoctrine be taught therein.
§ 10. The said trustees, at the end of each scholastic
year,shallcause to be made out a report,in writing,
showing the amount of receiptsand expenditures for the
year ,and the amount of funds on hand , if any , and the
condition of the property belonging to the district, and
the value thereof; the number of pupilsin each depart-
ment of the school,the number of pay and free pupils
being separate in said report, and such other facts and
information as the cause of public education requires.
§ 11. In addition to the fiftycents now allowed by law
to be assessedagainsteach patronof the schoolby the
trusteesthereof, an additional fiftycents may be assessed
againstsaid patrons by saidtrustees,for the purpose of
furnishing fuel for said school and repairing the school-
house and other school property.
LOC . L.,VOL . II- 77
§12. In additiontothepowersand dutieshereingrant-
ed the trustees,the trusteesof said school shall have all
rights and powers that are now given by the common
school laws of this State .
§ 13. That this act shall take effectfrom and after its
passage .
Approved May 12, 1884 .

laws.title: AN ACT to authorize the levy and collection of additional tax in aid of public schools in common school district number sixteen, Breckinridge county.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1489, pp. 1350–1351
laws.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of common school district number sixteen in Breckinridge County (Hardinsburg district) to levy an ad valorem tax of up to twenty cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property and a capitation tax of up to one dollar and fifty cents per person over twenty-one years old. Crucially, it specifies that 'only white persons and property belonging to white persons shall be taxed.' The trustees are required to declare the tax amount annually by May 1st.
key_provisions: §1 . That the trustees of common school district num- ber sixteen, Breckinridgecounty (the Hardinsburg dis- trict), shall annually cause to be levied and collectedan ad valorem tax of not exceeding twenty cents on each one hundred dollars worth of taxable property, and a capitation tax of not exceeding one dollar and fiftycents on each person over the age of twenty -one years within said district: Provided, That only white persons and property belonging to white persons shallbe taxed .
page_titles: AN ACT to authorize the levy and collection of additional tax in aid of public schools in common school district number sixteen, Breckinridge county.
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1489 .
AN ACT to authorize the levy and collection of additional tax in aid of
public schoolsin common school districtnumber sixteen, Breckinridge
county .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of theCommonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That the trustees of common school district num-
ber sixteen, Breckinridgecounty (the Hardinsburg dis-
trict), shall annually cause to be levied and collectedan
ad valorem tax of not exceeding twenty cents on each
one hundred dollars worth of taxable property, and a
capitation tax of not exceeding one dollar and fiftycents
on each person over the age of twenty -one years within
said district: Provided, That only white persons and
property belonging to white persons shallbe taxed .
§ 2. Said trustees shall,annually , on or before the first
day of May in each year,by an entryon a recordbook
to be kept by them,declarewhat amount of tax,both ad
valorem and capitation,shallbe collectedin saidyear.
§3 . Said trustees, in the collectionof said tax ,shall
be governed by the law as now embraced in the General
Statutes, and amendments thereto, except that the col-
lectorof said tax (who may be appointed by said trus-
tees) shallpay same to the chairman of said board of
trustees, and shall make settlement with said board .
§4 . The taxes collected hereunder , after paying ex-
penses of collection,shall be used and expended for the
improvement of and keeping in repairthe common school
propertyin saiddistrict,forthe payment of teachers,for
the extension of the school term beyond the term of five
months ,if the same shall be sufficient, and for the aid
and maintenance of public schools in said district; and
shallbe in addition to, and supplemental of,the pro rata
share of the general school fund due said district.
§5 . The chairman of said board of trustees,before he
shall receive any money under this act, and before the
collectorshallpay him any,shallgo beforethe Breckin-
ridge county court, and execute an approved covenant ,
with good security, a bond for the faithfulperformance
of his duties hereunder ,which bond shall be filed with
and preserved by the clerk of said court among the rec-
ords of his office .
§ 6. This act shall take effectfrom its passage ; but
shall not be enforced until it has been submitted to the
qualifiedwhite voters of said district, and a majority of
those voting on the question shall have voted in favor
of said tax. Said questionshallbe submitted,and the
vote thereon shall be taken , in the same manner as now
prescribed by law for voting upon question of taxation
forschoolpurposes; and may be submitted, and the vote
thereon taken,at any time designatedby the board of
trustees,the noticenow prescribedby law having first
been given .
Approved May 10 , 1884 .

laws.title: AN ACT creating an additional voting place in the fourth magisterial district, of Fayette county.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1518, pp. 1392–1393
laws.summary: This act establishes an additional voting place in Fayette County's fourth magisterial district, designating the Bell school-house as polling place number two. It mandates that voters residing east of the Louisville, Cincinnati, and Lexington Railroad must vote at polling place number one, and those west of the railroad must vote at polling place number two. The sheriff is required to post notices informing voters of this division.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1518 .
AN ACT creatingan additionalvoting place in the fourthmagisterialdis-
trict, of Fayette county .
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§1 . That an additionalvoting place be , and the same
ishereby , created and establishedin magisterial district
number four, of Fayette county , the place of voting to be
the Bell school-house, on the old Frankfort Turnpike
Road . The said place of voting shallbe known as poll-
ing place number two ,and the presentplaceof voting as
pollingplace number one: Provided,It meets with the
approval of the county court,a majorityof the justices
concurring therein .
§2 . It shall be the duty of the county court of said
county to appoint officersof electionto take the vote at
said polling places numbers one and two at the same
time that officersof election are appointed in the other
electionsof said county .
§3 . All voters in said magisterialdistrictnumber four,
livingon the east side of the Louisville,Cincinnati,and
Lexington Railroad ,are required to vote at polling place
number one in said district, and those living on the west
side of said railroad shall vote at pollingplace number
two in said precinct.
4 The sheriffof Fayette county is required to cause
fiftynotices to be printed, in large type ,and cause said
notices to be posted throughout said magisterialdistrict
for at least ten days before the next regular election,
informing the voters of the provisions of this act, and
also to cause the same to be published for the same length.
of time in at leasttwo papers publishedin the cityof
Lexington .
§5 . This act shallbe in forcefrom and afteritspas-
sage .
Approved May 10, 1884.

laws.title: AN ACT to prohibit the sale of spirituous, vino us, and malt liquors, in common school district number thirty, in Graves county.

laws.summary: This act prohibits the sale or gifting of spirituous, vinous, or malt liquors within common school district number thirty in Graves county. Violators face fines. Notably, Section 4 specifies that if persons of color violate the act, the fines shall be appropriated to the benefit of the colored school in said district.
key_provisions: § 4. If persons of color should violatethe provisions of this act, the fines for same shall be appropriated to the benefit of the colored school in said district .
page_titles: AN ACT to prohibit the sale of spirituous, vinous, and malt liquors, in common school district number thirty, in Graves county.
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1536 .
AN ACT to prohibitthe sale of spirituous, vinous, and malt liquors, in
common school districtnumber thirty, in Graves county.
Be itenactedby theGeneral Assembly of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky :
§ 1. That it shall be unlawful for any person ,in any
quantity whatever , to sellor give to another any spirit-
uous ,vinous, or malt liquors,or a mixture of either,with-
in the limitsof common school districtnumber thirty,in
Graves county , Kentucky .
§ 2. Any person found guilty of a violation of thisact,
shall,upon conviction,be finedin the sum of not more
than sixtydollarsand not lessthan twenty dollars,recov-
erable either upon a warrant before any justice of the
peace in saidcounty,or upon indictmentin theGraves
circuit court .
§ 3. All finesand forfeituresarisingunder thisact,after
payment of officers'fees,shallbe appropriatedto thepub-
lic school in said district .
§ 4. If persons of color should violatethe provisions of
this act, the fines for same shall be appropriated to the
benefit of the colored school in said district .
§5 . This act shalltake effectand be in force from and
after the firstday of May ,one thousand eight hundred
and eighty-four .
Approved May 8 , 1884 .

The taxes so raised shallbe used by the board of trusteesin payment of the debts created in the purchase of the lot and the erection of the common school -house thereon in said district, and for the repair and improve- ment of said school building and grounds , owned and occupied by the white citizens.

mon schoolproperty in said district.
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Commonwealth

§1 . That the trustees of common school district num-
ber one,in Grayson county,duringthe years one thou-
sand eight hundred and eighty-four and one thousand
eighthundred and eighty-five,are hereby authorizedto
levy and collectan ad valorem tax,foreach of said years ,

laws.summary: This act establishes a common school in a specific district in Louisa, Kentucky. It outlines the boundaries of the district, the duration of the school year (5-10 months), and specifies that 'all white children between the ages of six and twenty residing therein shall receive instruction without any charge therefor.' The management and control of the school and its funds are vested in a board of education whose members must possess the qualifications of 'white voters of said district.' Elections for the board are to be held annually, and only 'white qualified voters, and any maid or widow who is a tax payer' are eligible to vote.

laws.summary: This act addresses the difficulty in finding qualified teachers for colored common schools in Floyd County. It authorizes the superintendent and board of examiners to issue special licenses to individuals to teach these schools, acknowledging that there were no local colored teachers who could obtain certificates under the existing rigid examination requirements. The preamble states the importance of these schools for the cultural development and civic duties of colored citizens.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 885 . AN ACT forthe benefitof coloredcommon schoolsof Floyd county ,and to authorize the superintendent and board of examiners of common schoolsof saidcounty " to issuespeciallicenseto persons to teach col- ored common schoolsof said county." WHEREAS , The colored people of Floyd county have been unable to obtain teachers to teach their public schoolsin said county sincethe revised com- mon schoollaw went intoeffect,caused by therebeing no coloredteacherswho was livingin said county, or near thereto, who could obtain certificatesunder the rigid examination which the present common school law requires; and whereas, it is right that they should have common schools, as now provided for other citizensunder existinglaws,that they may be , come cultured and enabled to more fullydischarge their duties as such citizens; therefore, Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com- monwealth of Kentucky :

§1 . That the county superintendent of common schoolsof Floyd county and hisboard of examiners be, and they are hereby, authorized and empowered to issuespeciallicenseto a person who cannot have theexamination required by the common school law, for the purpose of teachingany coloredcommon schoolin any common school districtin said county , when it shall appear to the satisfactionof said super- intendent and his said board of examiners that said person so licensedis qualifiedto teach the colored pupilsresidingin said common school districts, and therecannot be a qualifiedteacher had to teach the same .

CHAPTER 885 .
AN ACT forthe benefitof coloredcommon schoolsof Floyd county ,and
to authorize the superintendent and board of examiners of common
schoolsof saidcounty " to issuespeciallicenseto persons to teach col-
ored common schoolsof said county."
WHEREAS , The colored people of Floyd county
have been unable to obtain teachers to teach their
public schoolsin said county sincethe revised com-
mon schoollaw went intoeffect,caused by therebeing
no coloredteacherswho was livingin said county, or
near thereto, who could obtain certificatesunder the
rigid examination which the present common school
law requires; and whereas, it is right that they
should have common schools, as now provided for
other citizensunder existinglaws,that they may be ,
come cultured and enabled to more fullydischarge
their duties as such citizens; therefore,
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the county superintendent of common
schoolsof Floyd county and hisboard of examiners
be, and they are hereby, authorized and empowered
to issuespeciallicenseto a person who cannot have
theexamination required by the common school law,
for the purpose of teachingany coloredcommon
schoolin any common school districtin said county ,
when it shall appear to the satisfactionof said super-
intendent and his said board of examiners that said
person so licensedis qualifiedto teach the colored
pupilsresidingin said common school districts, and
therecannot be a qualifiedteacher had to teach the
same .
§2 . That the provisionsof thisact shallonly apply
and extend to and including the school year ending
June the thirtieth, one thousand eight hundred and
eighty-eight(1888).
§3 . This act shall take effect from and after its
passage .
Approved May 1, 1886.

CHAPTER 931 .
AN ACT to incorporatethe LittleMount Cemetery Company , in
Spencer county .
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
$ 1.That JesseMaratta, Frank Davis, W. S. Allen,
andtwo otherpersonstobe designatedby them,and
theirsuccessors, be, and the same are hereby , incor-
porated under the name of the LittleMount Cemetery
Company , and under that name they may sue and be
sued, contractand be contracted with, and perform
such other duties and exercise such other privileges
as are usuallyconferredon similarcorporations.
§ 2. Said company shallbe authorizedand ready to
transactbusiness when and so soon as said corpora-
tors shall meet and elect out of their number three
directors, who shall have the full management and
controlof the affairsof the company , subject to the
control of the stockholders as hereinafter stated . The
firstboard of directors shall hold their offices for one
year, and untiltheirsuccessorsare electedand quali-
fied,and annually afterthe date of the firstelection
three directorsshall be elected by the stockholders .
§ 3. The board of directors shall, out of their num-
ber, annually electa president, secretaryand treas-
urer, who shallhold their officesfor one year, and
untiltheirsuccessorsare electedand qualified. The
treasurershallexecute a bond to the company ,with
approved security,forthe faithfulperformance of his
duties, and that he will account for and pay over to
the proper parties all moneys and funds when re-
quired with which he has been intrusted, and said
bond shallbe deliveredto the Spencer county clerk
forsafe-keeping ; and any person injured may sue on
saidbond , and recoversuch damages as he may have
sustainedby any failureof the treasurerto perform
his duties . The treasurer shall collect and distribute
the funds of the company ,and keep a faithfulaccount
of same .
§4. The purpose of thisincorporationisto establish,
preserve and beautifya cemetery near LittleMount,
Spencer county, Kentucky ; and this company shall
have power to apply to the courtsof Spencer county
and have such lands condemned for the use of the com-
pany as itmay deem proper, not exceeding ten acres.
The landshall,ifitcannotbe acquiredby contract,be
condemned in the same manner and before the same
courts and with same proceedingsasisnow provided by
law for the condemnation of lands for the use of rail-
road and turnpike companies . When the company
shallhave selectedthe locationof the cemetery, and
so soon as the price to be paid the owner or owners
has been fixed by agreement between the partiesor
by the judgment of the court,as providedhereinwhen
no agreement can be made ,the company may proceed,
before paying forthe lands,to have the land surveyed
and laidoffinto lotsand roads and drives, and may
proceed to advertisesaid lots for sale, in such por-
tions thereofas they may deem proper, and on such
terms as may be fixed by the directors; and may sell
the same on condition that enough such sales are
made to purchase the land and establishthe cemetery ;
and when a sufficientnumber of salesare so made ,
they may be made absolute, and the proceeds col-
lected and applied to the payment of the lands and
ornamenting and beautifying the grounds, and for
such other purposes as the directorsmay prescribe
incident to the organization. But no soil shall be
broken or any possession of any owner interfered
with until a sufficient number of sales shall have been
made to securethe purchase of the lands designated,
and provided the incorporatorsnamed herein shallbe
personallybound forsuch damages as any owner may
sustainby any necessaryintrusionupon hispremises,
in the event the cemetery isnot locatedthereon.
§ 5. The purchasers of the lots, and those who in-
vest theirfunds in the enterpriseby giftor donation,
and theirpriviesin estateor otherwise, shallbe the
stockholders , and shall be entitled to one vote for
every fivedollarsthus invested; and certificatesof
stock may be issuedby the directorsto any such per-
son, and the company is authorizedto receivedona-
tionsand giftsforthe purposes of thisact.
§ 6. Obligationsof the company must be, if in
writing, signedby the presidentand secretary; and
certificatesof purchase so signed may be given to
purchasers of lots, designating number and other
description, which may be recorded in the county
clerk'sofficeas evidenceof title,and preservedby the
secretary. The board of directors shall have full
power of regulatingthe placesand manner of inter-
ment ,in order to preserveharmony and uniformity.
and have fullpower of rejectingany bidder for lots,
so as to confinecolored people to one portion and
white people to another, and may vitiateand annul
any saleor transferof lotsin violationof such regu-
lations, and may exercise a general control of the en-
tire inclosure .
§ 7. This act shall take effect and be in force from
itspassage .
Approved May 7, 1886.

laws.summary: This act mandates that funds received by the Hawesville board of education from licenses set aside for school purposes be divided equally between white and colored schools. The treasurer is required to distribute these funds proportionally based on the school census, paying the colored school trustees their share. Failure to comply within one month allows the colored school trustees to take legal action.
key_provisions: §1 . That from and afterthe passage of thisact all money receivedby treasurerof the board of educa- tion of said city derived from licensesset apart for schoolpurposesinthelaws governingsaidcity,shall be for the benefit of the white and colored schools alike,and itshallbe theduty of saidtreasurertodi- vide the same in proportionto the number of children of school ages reported at the last preceding school census,and to pay over to the trusteesof the colored schooltheirproportionof the same ;and on hisfailure to do so within one month after receivingthe same, may be proceeded againston his bond by the trustees of saidcoloredschool in the mayor's court or circuit court,by motion or petitionas they may elect.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 992, pp. 517–526
laws.summary: This statute outlines procedures for challenging voter registration. It details how to serve notice to a registered voter, form a committee to hear evidence, and strike names from the register if deemed unlawfully registered. It also describes a process for marking voters as 'doubtful' if they cannot be served notice, requiring them to be sworn in and their right to vote investigated at the election.

CHAPTER 992 .
AN ACT toprovidefora registrationof votersin the cityof Paducah.
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
Officers.
§ 1. That the councilof the cityof Paducah shall,
at theirfirstregularmeeting in January of each year,
elect four sober and discreet citizens in each ward of
the cityof Paducah , two to act as judges of registra-
tion, one as clerkof registration,and one as marshal
of registrationin the ward for which they are elected.
No person shallbe eligibleas judge,clerk or marshal
who is not a voter of the ward in which he is elected,
and a housekeeper in the ward forwhich he iselected.
When thereare two distinctpoliticalpartiessaid offi-
cersof registrationshallbe so selectedas that one of
the judges in each ward shallbe of one politicalparty
and the other of the opposite politicalparty. They
shall serve for one year from the time of theirelection;
and each officerof registration,before entering upon
the discharge of his duties, shalltake the oath pre-
scribedby section1,article8,of the StateConstitution,
and during the period of his term of serviceshallbe
excused from jury duty .
§ 2. The councilclerkshall, at leastfivedays before
the registrationin each year, give each registration
officerwritten notice of his election. Should the coun-
cilfailto elect, or should all or any of the officers
electedfailto attendat the placeof registrationfor
one hour afterthe time for commencing the registra-
tion,or should allor any of said officersrefuseor de-
clineto act, then the mayor of the city of Paducah
shallappointofficersto actin theirstead for that reg-
istration, and may administer to them the necessary
oath of office.
§3. Officersof registrationshallhave the same power
to preserve order at the places of registration as is
exercisedby officersof electionsat the polls in State
elections. If the officersof registrationentertainany
doubt as to whether or not any person offeringfor
registrationis entitledto such registration, or if any
one'sright to registeris challenged, citizensmay be
calledin,not exceeding threein number , who shallbe
examined under oath touching the qualificationsof
suchperson who offersto register,which oath may be
administeredto any the persons so examined by any
oneofthejudges of registration.
Forms .
§4. It shallbe the duty of the clerkof the council
toprepare the proper forms and cause to be printed
two registrationbooks for each ward in the city of
Paducah, one to be kept in his officeto be used as
provided in section 9 of this act, and the other
furnishedto the clerks of registrationand election
beforeeach registrationor electionday , as herein-
afterprovided. Said books shallbe so arranged as
thatthe names of votersmay be registeredalphabet-
ically,and shallbe ruled and headed as follows:
AugustElection
MarchElection
Color
Residence
Name
REMARKS .
Registration .
§5 . The officersof registrationshall attend at the
voting places of their respectivewards on the first
Monday in January of each year,except in 1887 ,when
they shallattend on the firstMonday after their elec-
tion and on the next succeedingday from the hours
of six in the morning untileightin the evening ,and
shall record in the registrationbook , which shallbe
furnishedby the clerkof the councilto each registra-
tion clerk, a listof such qualifiedvotersof the ward
as may apply for registration. Said list of voters
shall be in alphabeticalorder, and shall show the
name of the person registered,the name of the street
or alley, describing brieflythe house in which he
lives,givingthe streetand between what two streets
itislocated. No person shallbe registeredwho does
not personallyappear before the registrationofficers;
and ifhe be not personallyknown to one of the offi-
cers, or if any bystander shalldemand it, he shallbe
sworn by one of the officersand interrogatedby him,
or by such bystander, touching his qualificationsas
provided in this act. Opposite the name of each per-
son so sworn the clerk shall write the word " sworn ,"
which entry shall be prima facie evidence of such
swearing in any prosecutionunder thisact. Any per-
son registeredmay vote at allelectionsuntilthe next
registration,unlesshe becomes disqualifiedafterregis-
tering.
Qualifications.
§6. Every personshallbe entitledto be registered
who would be entitled to vote at the next succeeding
March election; that is to say, every male citizen
who , on that day, shallhave attainedthe age of
twenty-one years,and shallhave residedin theState
two years, or in the county one year and sixty days
in the ward in which he offersto register.
Aliens .
§ 7. Any alienpossessingallthe qualificationsofa
voter, named in section6 of thisact,except citizen-
ship, shallbe entitledto be registered, but the clerk
shallwrite opositehis name , in the column headed
" Remarks ," the words " not naturalized; " and such
alienshallnot be entitledto vote at any electionheld
under that registration, unlesshe shallproduce to
theofficersof electionhis naturalizationpapers in due
form of law .
Mode of Registering.
§8 . In making the registration, the clerk shallact
as the recording officer, and the judges shalldecide
allquestionsrelatingto the qualificationsof persons
offeringto be registered,exceptthat,incaseof a dif-
ferenceof opinion between the judges,the clerk shall
have the casting vote. It shall be the duty of the
clerkto number , consecutively, the names recorded
under each letterof the alphabet as they are taken
down , and at the close of the registrationhe shall
sign his name as clerk after the last name recorded
under each letteras aforesaid, in such manner as that
no more names can be recorded above his, and shall
footup and certifyin the back of the registration
book the whole number of names recorded at that
registration; and this certificateshall be signed by
allthe officersof registrationbeforeleavingthe place
of registration, and in the presenceof bystanders
any two of whom may ,ifthey desire,sign theirnames
aswitnessesthereto. In additionto the requirements
above, the clerk shallsign his name as such clerk at
thefootof each page .
Return and Custody of the Books .
§9 . On the day followingthe close of the registra-
tion,theregistrationclerksshalldeliverthe registra-
tionbooks into the hands of the clerk of the council,
and take his receipttherefor. It shallbe the duty of
theclerkof the councilto keep said books safelyin
hisoffice, and not suffer the same to be taken there-
from, except as provided in this act. He shallalso
cause to be made one copy of each registrationbook in
the blank book retainedby him as provided in section
4 of thisact, which shallbe kept in his office, and not
be taken therefrom for any purpose . In case of loss
of any registrationbook , a copy shallbe made by the
clerk of the council from the copy retained in his
office,which copy shallbe used in registrationsand
electionswith the same effectas the original. The
clerk of the council shallpermit any citizenat any
time to copy any registrationbook without fee or
charge,and he shall also furnishcopies at the same
rateas provided in section17 of this act for copying
the book kept in his office. Copies furnished to citi-
zens under thissectionshallbe paid for in cash by the
person orderingthem .
Removals .
§ 10. Any person removing from one ward toanother
afterhaving been registeredfor that year,may apply
to the clerk of registration of the ward from which
he removes, on a registrationday ,and have his name
canceledoffby writingoppositeto itthe word " re-
moved ," and thereupon said clerk shall give him a
certificatein the followingform : " This is to certify
that ward to thehas removed from the
ward ,and that hisregistrationhas been canceled.
(Signed) — , clerk." Upon presentingsaidcer-
tificateto the officersof registrationof the ward to
which he has removed , he shall be entitled to be
thereregistered, if he possessthe other qualifications
named in section 6 of this act ; and no person remov-
ing, after being registered, shall be registeredin
another ward , without the production of such a cer-
tificate .
Striking Off Names .
§ 11. Any votermay ,by giving fivedays' notice, in
writing, addressed to, and served on, any person
whose name has been registered, move the councilof
the cityof Paducah , at itsnext regular meeting, not
!
less than five days after service of said notice, to
strike the name of such person from the register.
The council shallthereupon,at once, appoint a com-
mittee, consistingof three members of the council,
who shallhear proof on the question of strikingthe
name of such person from the register; and if the
committee shallbe of opinion that the person regis-
tered is not lawfully entitledto be registered, after
hearing the proof, the committee shall direct the
clerk of the council to strike his name from the
registerby insertingopposite his name the words ,
" Stricken by order of the council committee, — ,
clerk of the council." The person having the notice
served and the person upon whom it is served,may
each introduce not exceeding two witnesses on a side.
Within two days afteritsappointment by the council,
the committee shall hear proof of the parties on the
question of registration, and shall make report in
writing of the resultof itsaction,which reportshall
be filed with the clerk of the council within one week
after the appointment of the committee. If the per-
son upon whom noticeis attempted to be served can

Notably, it specifies that lists of property owners and tithes for taxation purposes shall be made for 'all the white owners of property' and 'all the white tithes residing in said district.' Additionally, it allows for a per capita tax on 'each white male person of twenty-one years of age residing in said district.'

It shallbe the duty of the trusteescreatedun . der thisact to give ten (10) days' noticebefore the electionin June , 1886,to the voters of said district, that an electionwillbe held for the purpose of voting a tax for erecting a new school-house, and for the election of trustees ; said notice shall be posted in no less than three (3) prominent places within saiddis- trict. The board of trusteesfor said districtshall, within ten days afteran electionvoting a tax,make out a true and correct list of all the white owners of propertyinsaiddistrict,and oftheamount and value of property owned by each subject to taxation for revenue purposes, and of allthe white tithesresiding in said district. Said board of trustees shall have full power to choose the locationof saidschool-house .

§ 7. In addition to the foregoingprovisionforlevy- ing a tax, the board of trusteesfor saiddistrictmay , at itsdiscretion,levya tax each year of two (2) dollars per head on each white male person of twenty -one years of age residingin saiddistrict.

CHAPTER 1001 .
AN ACT fixingthe boundary and for the benefitof the school district
No. 67,in Fleming county .
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the boundary of common school district
No. 67, of Fleming county, shall be as follows, to
wit : Beginning with the farm of James Biddell;
thence down Buchanan creek, including James Rodg-
ers' farm ; thence down said creek to the lower corner
of C. W. Hammond's farm , including said farm ;
thence south,includingJ. R. Crawford's,John Boon's
and A. E. Collins' farms ; thence down Hoover run,
excluding W. S. Price'sfarm, to J. C. Bishop's farm,
includingsame ; thence east, including Mrs. Lavina
Alexandria's, Sanford Gray's,Robert Harper's, Wm .
H. Price's, J. N. Price'sand W. S. Williams' farms,
to the James Biddell farm, including same , or the
place of beginning,includingallthe lands and premi-
ses within said boundary .
§ 2. The superintendent of common schools for
Fleming county shall not change the boundary of
said districtwithin a period of five years after the
passage of this act, unless by the unanimous consent
of the board of trustees for said district.
§3 . A tax not exceeding twenty -five cents on the
one hundred dollars'worth of taxableproperty in said
districtmay be levied in any one year, and for a
period not exceeding three (3) successiveyears, at
any one electionby a majorityof thequalifiedvoters
presentand voting therefor; and those only shall be
deemed qualified to vote who reside in said district,
and are entitled to vote for common school trustees .
§ 4. The following citizens, resident within said dis-
trict, are hereby created a board of trustees : J. R.
Crawford , Wm . S. Williams, and C. W. Hammond ,
who shall hold their officeuntil the firstSaturday in
June ,when the qualifiedvotersof saiddistrictshall
proceed toelectthree(3)trustees,one fora periodof
one year,one fortwo years,and one forthreeyears,or
untiltheirsuccessorsare duly electedand qualified.
§5 . Said trusteesappointed in this act shall have
untilthe fifteenthday of May ,1886,to listallchildren
within school age resident within said district, and to
report to the county superintendent; and all listsof
school children, and assessmentsnow made by other
districtsof said children, is hereby declarednull and
void ; and said county superintendentshallcorrectall
said lists to conform with the new lists and assess-
ments made under this act .
§ 6. It shallbe the duty of the trusteescreatedun .
der thisact to give ten (10) days' noticebefore the
electionin June , 1886,to the voters of said district,
that an electionwillbe held for the purpose of voting
a tax for erecting a new school-house, and for the
election of trustees ; said notice shall be posted in no
less than three (3) prominent places within saiddis-
trict. The board of trusteesfor said districtshall,
within ten days afteran electionvoting a tax,make
out a true and correct list of all the white owners of
propertyinsaiddistrict,and oftheamount and value
of property owned by each subject to taxation for
revenue purposes, and of allthe white tithesresiding
in said district. Said board of trustees shall have full
power to choose the locationof saidschool-house .
§ 7. In addition to the foregoingprovisionforlevy-
ing a tax, the board of trusteesfor saiddistrictmay ,
at itsdiscretion,levya tax each year of two (2) dollars
per head on each white male person of twenty -one
years of age residingin saiddistrict.
§ 8. All the money raisedby taxes voted, levied, as-
sessed and collectedaccordingto the provisionsof this
act shall be expended for nothing else than for the
purchasing of a sitefor a districtschool-house, the
building , repairingor furnishingthe same , and for
fuel and other necessary articlesfor the proper con-
ducting of saidschool; and forfencingand necessary
out-buildings,and forthe betterpayment of the teach-
er or teachersof said school, or for the extension of
the term of the common school in said district for a
period longerthan fivemonths ; or forthe payment of
debts contractedby the trusteesin the interestof the
common school in said district.
§ 9. Said board of trustees shall be controlled and
governed by the common school law , when the same
is not inconsistent with this act .
§ 10. This act shall take effect from and after its
passage .
Approved May 7, 1886 .

laws.summary: This act incorporates the Kentucky Mutual Aid Association, outlining its purpose to provide weekly benefits for members during sickness or disability. It details the powers of the board, membership conditions, and benefit limits. Crucially, Section 8 explicitly states that only 'free-born white men between the ages of eighteen and forty-five' are eligible for membership.
key_provisions: §8.No personshallbe eligibleto membershipin said corporationexcept free-born white men between the ages of eighteenand forty-five.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 1094 .
AN ACT toincorporatetheNationalSickand AccidentFund inAdair-
ville, Logan county, Kentucky .
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That Dr. R. P. Townsend ,E. Fasy , M. L. Fu-
gate, W. E. Jenkins, J. W. Porter, F. L. McKernan ,
J. G. Orndorff and S. C. Gooch , and their associates
and successors,be,and are hereby, createdthe body-
politic, under the name of the National Sick and
Accident Fund , with power to sue and be sued, con-
tractand be contractedwith, and shallhave perpet-
ual succession,with rights to hold real estate and
other property and funds necessary, in the judgment
of the board of directory,for itsuse and purposes,
and may disposeof the same at will; and may adopt
and use a common seal,renewable and changeable at
pleasure;and may make such by -laws and regulations
as may be deemed necessary to fully carry out the
purposes of this act of incorporation .
§2. The principalplace of businessof saidcorpora-
tionshallbe Adairville, Kentucky ; and any four of
the incorporatorsabove named may , in person or by
proxy, afterbeing duly notified, proceed to organize
and electboard of directoryand other officerspro-
vided herein .
§3 .The affairsof saidcorporationshallbe managed
by a board of directoryof not lessthan fivenor more
than fifteenpersons; seven of saidboard shallbe resi-
dentsofLogan county,Kentucky,and shallconstitute
a localboard , a majority of which shall constitutea
quorum to do business; the remaining eight shall
constitutean advisory board, and may residein any
partof the Stateof Kentucky . The board of directory
shallbe chosen by the members of the corporationon
the fourth Tuesday in June of each year, and shall
enterupon the discharge of theirduties on the first
day of July thereafter. They may be qualified
at any time after their election; and previous to
entering upon the discharge of their duties the
presidentof said corporation, or any person com-
petent to administer an oath, may qualify said
members elect. Board of directory and all other
officersshall hold their offices until their successors
are elected and installed . Vacancies in the board
may be filledby the board itselfand any directorso
elected shall hold his office until the next annual elec-
tion. Should the firstof July fallon Sunday, the
directorselectshallmeet on the day precedingand
organize. Should no electionbe held on the day men-
tionedabove, the president, by orderof the board,
may calla meeting for such purpose upon ten days '
notice,published in some newspaper in Kentucky or
otherwise .
§4. The board shallelectfrom itsnumber a presi-
dent, a vice-president, a secretaryand a treasurer,
and such other officersas it may be necessary to man-
age the businessof the corporation,and may regulate
the dutiesof each by by -laws.
§5 . The objectof the corporationshallbe to pro-
vide weekly benefitsfor itsmembers during sickness
orwhen disabledby accident; and theboard shallhave
power to assessitsmembers to pay such benefit, also
to charge a membership fee and quarterly dues , the
amount of all of which it may fix by by -laws . It
shallhave power to prescribeby itsby -laws the con-
ditionsupon which members shall be admitted, and
classifythe risks, and fixthe assessments and mem
bership fee in accordance therewith; to divide the
risksinto separate classesif they think best, and
keep the business of each class separate from the
other .
§ 6. The weekly benefitsshallnot be lessthan five
nor more than fiftydollars,to be paid to the applicant
upon conditions prescribed by the by -laws of said
board : Provided ,however,That no more than twenty-
six weeks shallbe paid to any member within any one
year .
§7. No person shallbe admitted a member of said
corporationuntilhe shallhave complied with the con-
ditionsprescribedby the by -laws of said corporation.
The board shall have power to appoint a medical
examiner, who shall be a graduate of some medical
college, to whom allapplicationfor membership shall
be submitted, and he shallwrite his opinion on said
application; and upon the approval of said medical
examiner and the payment of such fees, assessments
and so forth, as the by -laws may prescribe, shallbe-
come a member of said corporation, unlessthe board
directotherwise, and a certificateof membership shall
be issued to him ,signedby thepresidentand secretary
of the board .
§8.No personshallbe eligibleto membershipin
said corporationexcept free-born white men between
the ages of eighteenand forty-five.
§ 9. The board shallcreatetwo separatefunds, one
to be known as the " benefit fund " and the other as
the " permanent fund ." Ninety per cent. of allmon-
eys received from assessments shall be placed to the
creditof the " benefitfund ," and shallbe used only to
pay weekly benefits. All moneys receivedfrom fees,
dues and other sources, and the remaining ten per
cent.of assessments,shallbe placedto the creditof the
permanent fund,and may be used to defray the ex-
penses of the corporation,or as the board may direct.
§ 10. The weekly benefitdue members shallnot be
subject to the claims of creditors, and shallnot be
reached by attachment, garnishment, or other pro-
cessesof law, so as to divertit from itsmembers or
their families .
§ 11. The members of the corporationshallbe bound
inlaw to pay allassessments,dues and so forth; they
may , however , withdraw from the corporationby giv-
ing written notice to the secretaryor chief officerof
the corporationof such intention, afterwhich alllia-
bilitiesshall cease for assessments , dues and so forth,
that may thereafteraccrue; and in case of failureto
pay assessments, quarterly dues and so forth, shall
be debarred from receiving any benefitswhatever
to which they might otherwise have become entitled
during such delinquency. The board may suspend
any member forfailureto pay dues, assessments and
so forth, and when so suspended can only be restored
to membership by actionof the board.
§ 12. All claims againstthe corporationforbenefits
must be assertedwithin one year from the time when
they might have been claimed, or the rightto recover
same shall be forfeited .
§ 13. The individualshallin no way be liableforthe
debts of the corporation .
§ 14. This associationshallbe subjectto the act of
April 19, 1884,regulatingco-operativeinsurance com-
panies of other States,so far as the same may be appli-
cable to a company of thisState.
§ 15. All benefitclaimsshallbe paid as soon as prac-
ticableafterthe necessaryproof has been made ; but in
no case shallpayment be withheld more than sixty
days aftertheproofhas been approvedby theboard.
§ 16. This act shall take effectfrom and after its pas-
sage .
Approved May 14, 1886.

laws.title: AN ACT to authorize the city of Lexington to issue bonds to the amount of thirty thousand dollars for school purposes.
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1142, p. 717
laws.summary: This act authorizes the city of Lexington to issue bonds up to $30,000 for school purposes. The funds are to be used for purchasing land and erecting schoolhouses for both white and colored children, with the determination of the number of schoolhouses for colored children left to the discretion of the general council.
key_provisions: §1 . That the mayor and general councilof the city of Lexington are hereby authorized and empowered to issuebonds of saidcityin any amount not exceed- ing thirtythousand dollars,payable thirtyyears after date,but redeemable any time after ten years there- from, at the option of the city, and bearing interestat a ratenot exceeding fiveper centum per annum , pay- ablesemi-annually; the proceeds arisingfrom the sale of said bonds to be applied to the purchase of a suit- able lot or lots, and the erection thereon of a school- house for white children, and such school house or houses for colored children as to the general council may be deemed necessary.

CHAPTER 1142 .
AN ACT to authorize the city of Lexington to issue bonds to the

Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the mayor and general councilof the city

laws.summary: This act places common school district No. 79 in Logan County, which includes Lewisburg, under the management of the Lewisburg High School trustees. These trustees will act as common school trustees and are responsible for all legal duties. The statute explicitly states that the commissioner will draw and pay money due to the district for 'white children' to the treasurer, who will use it for paying teachers. It also outlines tuition rates for non-residents or those outside common school age and grants benefits to stockholders living outside the district.

laws.summary: This act establishes a graded school within a specific district and explicitly states that the school shall be exclusively for white children. It outlines the powers and duties of the board of trustees, including admission of pupils, enforcement of rules, taking a census, and receiving and appropriating state funds for white pupils. The act also allows for the admission of scholars over common school age from other districts or within the district, with tuition fees.

laws.summary: This act regulates primary elections in Franklin County, Kentucky. It stipulates that only members of a political party can vote in that party's primary election. It also outlines penalties for illegal voting, including fines and imprisonment. Additionally, it requires a two-year residency in the state to vote.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 727, pp. 572–573
laws.summary: This act provides relief to W. H. Hays, surety for the late sheriff of Hardin county, by allowing him to retain funds that were paid on his behalf for poll taxes assessed against negroes. These taxes were deemed unconstitutional by a U.S. court and therefore uncollectible from the taxpayers.
page_titles: AN ACT for the relief of W. H. Hays, surety for H. C. Hays, late sheriff of Hardin county.
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 727 .
AN ACT forthe benefitof W. H. Hays , of Bullittcounty.
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the Auditor of Public Accounts be, and
he ishereby, authorizedand directedto refund to
W. H. Hays , surety for H. C. Hays , late sheriffof
Hardin county, the sum of two hundred and thirty-
eight dollars, the same being for poll-tax assessed
againstnegroes, which was paid in on settlementof
said sheriff'saccount by the said W. H. Hays , surety
as aforesaid, but never collectedfrom the tax-payer
on account of a decision of the United States court
declaring such tax to be unconstitutional.
§ 2. This act shall take effect from and after its
passage .
Approved March 26,1888.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 748, pp. 622–626
laws.summary: This statute outlines the process for a school district to vote on and levy a school tax. It specifies the election procedures, including the use of a poll-book with columns for 'For school tax' and 'Against school tax'. The collected tax, combined with the common school fund, is to be used for paying teachers to teach a common school of five months each year, which shall be free to all white children in the district within the common school age. The statute also details the duties of election officers and the board of trustees in recording the election results and levying the tax.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 772, pp. 664–668
laws.summary: This act establishes a board of three trustees to manage and maintain a system of common and graded schools within a specific district. It mandates that every white child in the district, within the common school age, shall have free access and the right to attend these schools free of charge. laws.summary: This act amends a previous law regarding voter registration in Covington, Kentucky. It outlines procedures for appointing registration officers, preserving order at registration sites, and challenging a person's right to register. Notably, it specifies that registration books should include a column for 'color'.

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 861 .
AN ACT to providefor a registrationof votersof the cityof Cov-
ington.
Officers.
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the county judge of Kenton county, the
sheriffof said county, and the clerk of the Kenton
county court, shall constitutea board, which shall,
between the firstand fifteenthdays of June in each
year, appoint four sober and discreetcitizens, in each
electionprecinctof the city of Covington, two to act
as judges of registration,one as clerkof registration,
and one as sheriffof registration, in the precincts for
which they are appointed. No person shall be eligi-
ble as judge,clerkor sheriffwho isnot a voterin the
precinctfor which he isappointed and a housekeeper,
and when there are two or more distinctpoliticalpar-
ties, said officersof registrationshall be so selected as
that one of the judges of each precinctshallbe of one
politicalparty, and the other of the opposing politi-
cal party, the clerk to be selectedfrom the third
politicalparty (provided that there should be more
than two distinctpoliticalpartiesat the time of regis-
tration) ; they shallserve for one year from the time
of theirappointment ,and each officerof registration,
before enteringupon the dischargeof hisduties, shall
take the oath prescribedby section1, article8, of the
Constitution, and shall, during the period of his term
of service,be excused from jury duty .
§ 2. The sheriffof the county shall, at leastseven
days before the general registrationin each year, as
provided for in this act,give each officerof registra-
tion written notice of his appointment . Should the
court, sheriffor clerk failto appoint, or should all
the officersappointed failto attend at the place of
registration for two hours after the time for com .
mencing the registration, or refuse to act, then the
sheriff, judge or clerk, or either of them that can
be found in the county , shall appoint officersto act
in their stead for that registration; but should two
officersbe in attendance, they may fillvacancies for
the purpose of conducting that registration, and may
administer the necessary oaths of office.
If
§ 3. Officers of registration shall have the same
power to preserve order at the placesof registration
as is exercised by officersof election at the polls.
the officersof registrationentertainany doubt as to
whether or not any person offeringforregistrationis
entitledto such registration, or if any one's right to
registeris challenged, citizensmay be calledin, not
exceeding three in number , who shall be examined
touching the qualificationsof such person or persons
who offerto register.
Forms .
§ 4. It shallbe the duty of the county clerkof Ken-
ton county to prepare the proper forms , and cause to
be printed two registrationbooks foreach precinctin
the cityof Covington, and one of which shallbe kept
in his office,to be used as provided in section9 of this
act, and the other furnishedto the clerksof registra-
tionand election, before each registrationor election
day , as hereinafter provided . Said books shall be so
arranged as that the names of voters may be regis-
tered alphabetically, and shallbe ruled and headed
as follows: Name , residence, color,August election,
October election, November election,specialelection,
remarks .
General Registration .
$ 5. The officersof registrationshall attend at the
voting placesof theirrespectiveprecinctson the first
Monday in July in each year, and on the next suc.
ceeding day , from the hours of nine in the morning
!
until nine in the evening , and shall record in the reg-
istrationbook , which shall be furnished by the clerk
of the county court to each registrationclerk, a list
of such qualifiedvoters of the precinctas apply for
registration. If either of said days fall upon the
fourth day of the month , then said fourth day shall
be omitted as a day of registration, and the registra-
tion shall proceed on the next succeeding day as if
said fourth day had not intervened. Said list of
voters shallbe in alphabeticalorder, and shallshow
the name of the person registered, the name of the
streetor alley, and the number of the house,lodging
or tenement, in which he lives, and whether he be
white or colored; and if said house ,lodging or tene-
ment be not numbered , the locationthereof shallbe
described in the registrationbook as accurately as
is practicable, giving the street and between what
streets. No person shall be registeredwho does not
personally appear before the officersof registration,
and if he be not personallyknown to one of the offi-
cers,or ifany by-standershalldemand it,he shallbe
sworn by one of the officersand interrogatedby him ,
by such by -stander,touching his qualificationsas
provided in thisact. Opposite the name of each per-
son so sworn the clerk shall write the word " sworn ,"
which entry shallbe (prima facie) evidence of such
swearing in any prosecution under this act. Said
registrationin July shall be known as the general
registration, and any person then registeredmay vote
at all electionsuntil the next general registration,
unlesshe becomes disqualifiedafterregistration.
Qualifications.
§ 6. Every person shall be entitled to be registered
who would be entitled to vote at the next succeeding
August election; that is to say, every male citizen
who , on that day , would have attained the age of
twenty -one years, and shallhave residedin the State
two years, or in the county of Kenton one year, and
in the precinctsixty days . No person shall be reg-
isteredwho does not personally appear before the
officersof registration; and if he be not personally
known to one of the officers, or ifany by -standershall
demand it, he shall be sworn by one of the officers
and interrogatedby him ,or by such by -stander,touch-
ing his qualificationsas provided in this section.
Aliens .
§ 7. Any alien possessing all qualificationsof a
voter named in section6 of this act, except citizen-
ship, shall be entitled to be registered, but the clerk
shallwriteoppositeto his name ,in the column headed
" remarks ,” the words " not naturalized," and such
alien shall not be entitledto vote at any electionheld
under that registration, unlesshe shallproduce to the
officers of election his naturalization in due form of
law .
Mode of Registration .
§ 8. In making the registrationthe clerk shall act
as the recordingofficer, and the judge shalldecide all
questionsrelatingtothe qualificationsof personsoffer-
ing to be registered, except that in case of a difference
of opinion between the judges the clerkshallhave the
casting vote. It shall be the duty of the clerk to
number consecutivelythe names recorded under each
letterof the alphabet as they are taken down , and at
the closeof the registrationhe shallsign his name as
clerk after the last name recorded under each letter as
aforesaid , in such manner as that no more names can
be recorded above his, and shall foot up and certifyin
the back of the registrationbook the whole number
of names recorded at that registration, and this cer-
tificateshallbe signed by allthe officersof registration
before leaving the place of registration, and in the
presence of by -standers, and any two of whom may ,if
they desire,signtheirnames as witnessesthereto. In
addition to the requirements above, the clerk shall
sign his name as such clerkat the foot of each page .
E
E
Return and Custody of Books .
§ 9. On the day following the closeof the registra-
tionthe clerkshalldeliverthe registrationbook into
the hands of the clerk of the county court or any one
of his deputies, and shall take his receipttherefor.
It shall be the duty of said county clerk to keep said
books safely in his office, and not to sufferthe same to
be taken therefrom , except as provided in this act ;
he shall also cause to be made one copy of each
registrationbook in the blank book retained by him
as provided in section4 of this act, which shall be
kept in his office, and not to be taken therefrom for
any purpose. In case of loss of any registration
book , a copy shallbe made by the county clerk from
the copy retained in his office, which copy shall be
used in registrationand electionswith the same effect
as the original. The clerk shallpermit any citizen,
at any time, to copy any registrationbook without
fee or charge ; and he shallalsofurnish copiesat the
same rate as provided in section20 of this act for
copying the book kept in hisoffice. Copies furnished
citizensunder this section shall be paid for in cash by
the person ordering them .
SpecialRegistration.
§ 10. On Tuesday after the firstMonday in Septem-
ber, 1888, and on the same day in every year thereaf-
ter, there shall be a registrationof those persons
whose names were not registeredat the previous July
registration, and who ,but for thisact, would be enti-
tledto vote forsuch person or persons as were candi-
dates at the ensuing election. On the second Monday
in October, 1888, and every second year thereafter,
thereshall be a registrationof those persons whose
names were not registeredat the previous September
registration, and who ,but for thisact,would be enti-
tled to vote at the ensuing municipal election. When
by virtue of any future act of the Legislature, or of
any proclamation or writ of electionissued under ex
istinglaws, an electionisordered for any other than
one of thedays alreadyhereinprovidedfor,atwhich
a vote is to be taken in the city of Covington, it
shall be the duty of the sheriffof Kenton county
to fix a day for the registrationof those entitledto
vote at such electionwhose names are not already on
the registrationbooks for that year, and to publish
noticeof such day as a part of his noticeof the elec-
tion; and where, by virtueof the citycharter or any
special law , an election or vote is ordered to be held
or taken in the cityof Covington at any other time
than one of the days aforesaid. Then the councilor
otherbody or person so orderingsaid electionor vote
shall, at the same time, fix a day for the registration
of those persons entitledto vote thereat, whose names
have not been recorded on the registrationbooks for
thatyear, and shallrequire the same to be published,
in like manner as the time and place of said election
or vote are requiredby law to be published. Regis-
trations under this section shall be known as special
registrations, and any persons so registered shall be
entitled to vote at all elections held prior to the
next generalregistration. Registrationspriorto spe-
cialelectionsshallbe held not lessthan tendays prior
to the election .
§ 11. On the day priorto each registration,provided
in the previoussection,the county clerk shalldeliver
totheregistrationclerksthe registrationbooks fortheir
severalprecincts; and on the day of such registration
the registrationofficersshall attend at their several
placesof registration, and shallregisterthe names of
all persons appearing before them who may be en-
titled to vote at the election for which the registra-
tion is held,and whose names are not already on the
registryfor that year. The names shallbe recorded
immediately following the names recorded at the
previous registration; and the registrationshall be
conducted and the books returned as hereinbeforepro-
vided . Immediately afterthe books are so returned ,
the county clerk shallcause the names recorded at
that electionto be copied intothe book retainedin his
officeas provided in section9 of thisact.
Removals .
§ 12. Any person removing from one precinct to an-
other, afterhaving been registeredfor that year,may
apply to the clerkof registrationof the precinctfrom
which he removes, on a registrationday , and have his
name canceledoffby writingopposite to it the word
" removed ," and thereupon saidclerk shall give him
a certificatein the following form : “ This is to certify
that has removed from the precinct,of ward
to precinct of ward , and that his reg-
istrationhas been canceled. (Signed), - , clerk."
Upon presenting said certificateto the officersof reg-
istrationof the precinctto which he has removed , he
shallbe entitledto be there registered,if he possesses
the other qualificationsnamed in section 6 of this act ;
and no person so removing , afterbeing registered,
shall be registeredin another precinct without the
production of such a certificate.
Striking off Names .
§ 13. Any voter may , by giving fivedays' notice in
writing to any person whose name has been registered,
move the county court to strike his name from the
register,and both partiesmay introducewitnesses, not
exceeding threein number on each side; said notice
must be served personally. If, at the hearing, the
court shallbe of the opinion that the person regis-
tered isnot lawfullyentitledto register,itshalldirect
the clerk to strikehis name from the registerby in-
serting opposite to it the words , " Stricken off by
order of the county court . — , clerk." If the per-
son upon whom noticeis attempted to be served can
not be found, the clerkshallwriteoppositesuch name
on the registrationbook the word " doubtful;" and
when at an electionsuch person whose name ismarked
doubtful shall offerto vote, he shall be sworn and his
rightto vote be investigatedfully.
§ 14. On the Saturday previous to the firstMonday
in August ,1888,and on the judicialday previous to
every electionto be held or vote of the people to be
taken thereafterin the cityof Covington, the clerk of
the county court shall deliver to the clerks of election
the registrationbooks for their severalprecincts, to-
getherwith the poll-books,which saidregistrationand
poll-books shallbe produced by said clerks at their
severalprecinctswhen the polls are opened on the
day of election. At said election no vote shall be re-
ceived unless the name of the person offeringto vote
is on the registryprovided in this act,or unless he
produce, before the officersof election, his written
affidavitstatingthat he was necessarilyabsent from
the city,or that he was illand unable to attend, or
that some named member of his family was so ill
as to require his constant attention, such absence
or illnesscovering the period allowed for registra-
tion, and statingfacts showing him to be a qualified
voter of the precinct, and alsothe facts in reference
tohis residencerequiredto be entered on the register,
and also prove by written affidavitof a registered
voter of the precinct, who is a householder, that he
knows such person to be a qualifiedvoter, and stating
the factsin referenceto such person's placeof resi-
dence required to be entered on the register. Said
affidavitsshallbe returnedby the officersof the elec-
tionto the county clerk, indorsed as follows: “Filed
before us this - day of , 18— . ——judges ;"
and shallbe kept on fileby the county clerk. Any
vote receivedby the officersof electionin contraven-
tion of this act shall be void, and shall be rejected
from the count . The officersof election shall, when
a vote is cast, mark opposite to the name of the per-
son voting, in the column of the registrationbook
provided for that election, the word " voted ;" and
at the close of the election, and before closing or
