leaving the voting place, shall mark opposite the
name of each person who has not voted at that elec-
tion the words " not voted ." The registration book
shallbe returned to the county clerk by the clerk of
the election the day next succeeding the election.
False Registration .
§ 15. Any person who shallcause himself to be reg-
istered in more than one election precinct other-
wise than is provided in section 12 of this act, or
more than once in the same precinct, or who shall
cause himself to be registeredknowing that he isnot
lawfully entitledto registration, and any person who
shall aid or abet in the commission of any of said
acts, shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor , and
shallbe imprisoned in the county jailnot lessthan
one nor more than twelve months .
False Registration Books .
§ 16. Any officerof registration or other person ,
who shall unlawfully alterany registrationbook , or
add any names thereto, or shall willfullysecrete,
suppress or destroy any such book , or who shall
make or aid in making any falseor fraudulent regis-
trationbook , shall be deemed guilty of felony, and
shall be confined in the penitentiarynot less than
one nor more than fiveyears, and shallforfeitany
officehe then holds, and shall forever be disquali-
fied from holding office.
Perjury .
§ 17. Any person who shallwillfullymake any false
statement, under an oath lawfullyadministeredunder
thisact, shallbe deemed guiltyof falseswearing, and
confined in the penitentiary not less than one nor more
than fiveyears .
Obstructing Registration.
§ 18. Any person who , by himself or in aid of
others,shallforciblybreak up or attempt to break up
a registrationheld under this act, or shall forcibly
prevent or attempt to prevent any person from ap-
proaching or entering a place of registration, shall
be fined not less than one hundred nor more than five
hundred dollars, or imprisonment not less than six
nor more than twelve months in the county jailor
both .
§19 . No witness shall be excused from testifying
before any grand jury, or in any prosecution or in-
dictment under thisact, on the ground that his testi-
mony may criminatehimself; but no such testimony
shallbe used against him in any prosecution, except
for falseswearing in giving same .
Fees .
§ 20. For his servicesunder this act the county
clerk shall receive the following fees and no other :
For copying the registrylistsrequired to be kept in
his office, or to be used in supplying lost books , the
sum of two cents for each voter whose name is so
copied ; for his services under section 13 of this act
the sum of ten cents for the name of each voter
strickenoffthe lists; forreceiptingto clerksof regis-
trationand electionfor registrationbooks , the sum
of fivecents for each book receipted for ; the sheriff
shall receive for serving the notices provided for in
section 2 the sum of thirty cents for each actual ser-
vice ; officersof registration shall receive two dollars
and fiftycents per day for each day employed in
attending at the places of registration. But clerks
of registrationand electionshall not be entitledto
any pay , except upon the production of the county
clerk'sreceiptfor theirrespectiveregistrationbooks,
which receipt shall be the voucher of the officerpay-
ing them. The cityof Covingtonshallpay allfees
and expenses incurred under this act for registration.
The sheriffshallhave published in one daily paper,
published and circulatingin the city of Covington,
the names of all persons who have been registered at
leastthreedays aftereach registration.
J
§ 21. A copy of this act shall be printed in each
registrationbook made under itsprovisions.
§ 22. The eighteen precincts, as now laid off and
provided for by law for general electionsin the city
of Covington ,shall continue and remain as now estab-
lishedand laidoff, and shallbe regarded as precincts,
and treatedas such in allcity, as well as generalelec-
tions; and in pursuance of the provisionsof thisact,
a registration shall be made of the voters of each of
said precincts at the times heretofore named ; and at
allelectionsfor cityofficersof saidcityitshallbe the
duty of the officersof said city to cause a voting place
to be opened in each of said eighteen precincts, and
the provisionsof this section shall, so far as the re-
quirement of eighteen voting places is concerned,go
into effectand be observed at the next county election
to be held on the firstMonday in August , 1888 ; and
allactsor partsof actsin conflictherewith arehereby
repealed .
§ 23. The citycouncilof the cityof Covington shall
submit thisact to the legal votersof the cityof Cov-
ington, at a specialelectionto be ordered by itin the
usual manner , which shallbe held in the month of
April, 1888. At saidelectionthe officersthereofnow
provided by law shallopen a pollat each electionpre-
cinct, and to each legal voter offeringto vote the
question shallbe propounded , " Do you vote for or
against the registrationbill?" and his vote shall
thereupon be recorded for or against the same as
he shall direct . The officers of said election shall
make returns of said vote as officersof city elec-
tions are now required by law to make returns of
city elections; and if a majority of the legal votes
cast at said election are for or in favor of said bill,
the citycouncil shall so declare, and this act shall
take effectfrom that date ; but if a majority of the
legalvoters shallvote against thisbill, the citycoun-
cil shall so declare, and this act shall be of no force
or effect . Approved April 5, 1888.

laws.summary: This act authorizes the board of trustees of common school district number one (1), white, in Carroll county, to levy an additional tax of up to twenty cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property owned by white people. This tax is intended to extend the school session from five months to eight to ten months per year, as the state common school fund only provides enough to maintain the school for five months. The act also addresses existing debt for a school building and a previously levied tax to pay it off.
key_provisions: CHAPTER 869 . AN ACT to amend an act, entitled "An act to consolidate common school districtsNos .1 and 26,in Carroll county ,and to provide for a school building and a better organization of the public schools in saidconsolidateddistrict," approved May 7,1886; and providingfor the levyingof an additionaltax in saidschooldistricttoextendthe session of the school therein . WHEREAS , The trustees of common school district No. one (1), white, in Carrollcounty, are in debt for a school building, and have levied a tax of twenty- five(25) cents on each one hundred dollars' worth of taxableproperty in said districtto pay said indebted- ness,and the amount of such indebtednessbeing such that said tax must be continued for at least three · years ; and whereas , the amount received from the State common school fund by said districtwillonly maintain the school for five(5) months ; and itbeing greatly desirable to maintain the common school in said districtfor a term of from eight to ten months . in each schoolyear ; therefore,to provide forthe levy- ing of an additionaltax to accomplish such object, Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com- monwealth of Kentucky :

§1 . That the board of trustees of common school districtnumber one (1),white,in Carrollcounty, be, and they are hereby , authorized to levy , from year to year, a tax on alltaxable property within said dis- trict, which is owned by white people,not exceeding twenty (20) centson each one hundred dollars' worth thereof, in any one school year , which tax shall be collected as county and State taxes are collected; and any officercollectingthe same ,or a collectorappointed by the board of trustees, shall execute bond for the faithfulperformance of his duties as such, and the payment of said tax as collectedto the treasurerof said board of trustees .

§4 . Said board of trusteesshalluse said money so collected to extend the sessions of the white common school in the aforesaiddistrict, as the money so col- lectedwilljustify, not exceeding ten months in any one schoolyear ; and they shallreport the amount of money collectedand how expended in their annual report .

§ 5. Before said board shall levy the tax as pro- vided herein, the question shall firstbe submitted to a vote of the white voters of said district, qualified to vote under the common school law, and the ques- tion may be submitted at any time and as often as said board may deem expedient,noticeof such elec- tion being given as required by the common school law ; and said election shall be conducted and the result ascertained as in school district elections for district taxation under the common shool law .

laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 869 .
AN ACT to amend an act, entitled "An act to consolidate common
school districtsNos .1 and 26,in Carroll county ,and to provide for
a school building and a better organization of the public schools in
saidconsolidateddistrict," approved May 7,1886; and providingfor
the levyingof an additionaltax in saidschooldistricttoextendthe
session of the school therein .
WHEREAS , The trustees of common school district
No. one (1), white, in Carrollcounty, are in debt for
a school building, and have levied a tax of twenty-
five(25) cents on each one hundred dollars' worth of
taxableproperty in said districtto pay said indebted-
ness,and the amount of such indebtednessbeing such
that said tax must be continued for at least three ·
years ; and whereas , the amount received from the
State common school fund by said districtwillonly
maintain the school for five(5) months ; and itbeing
greatly desirable to maintain the common school in
said districtfor a term of from eight to ten months .
in each schoolyear ; therefore,to provide forthe levy-
ing of an additionaltax to accomplish such object,
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the board of trustees of common school
districtnumber one (1),white,in Carrollcounty, be,
and they are hereby , authorized to levy , from year to
year, a tax on alltaxable property within said dis-
trict, which is owned by white people,not exceeding
twenty (20) centson each one hundred dollars' worth
thereof, in any one school year , which tax shall be
collected as county and State taxes are collected; and
any officercollectingthe same ,or a collectorappointed
by the board of trustees, shall execute bond for the
faithfulperformance of his duties as such, and the
payment of said tax as collectedto the treasurerof
said board of trustees .
§ 2. The officeror collector making such collections-
shall have the same power to distrain for taxes, and
enforce the same in the same manner and to a similar
extent , as sheriffsin the collection of State taxes .
§ 3. The treasurer of said board shall be responsible
on his officialbond for allmoney paid to him under
the provisionsof this act, and shallpay out the same
on the order of the board of trustees .
§4 . Said board of trusteesshalluse said money so
collected to extend the sessions of the white common
school in the aforesaiddistrict, as the money so col-
lectedwilljustify, not exceeding ten months in any
one schoolyear ; and they shallreport the amount of
money collectedand how expended in their annual
report .
§ 5. Before said board shall levy the tax as pro-
vided herein, the question shall firstbe submitted to
a vote of the white voters of said district, qualified
to vote under the common school law, and the ques-
tion may be submitted at any time and as often as
said board may deem expedient,noticeof such elec-
tion being given as required by the common school
law ; and said election shall be conducted and the
result ascertained as in school district elections for
district taxation under the common shool law .
§6 . At the electionherein provided for, each voter
shallbe asked by the judge of the election: "Are you
in favorof the schooltax or againstthe school tax ?'”
and his vote shallbe recorded in favor of or against
the tax, according to hisanswer. If the resultis in
favor of " school tax ," the board of trustees shall
levy, from year to year, such tax as herein provided,
in any amount they may deem necessaryfor the year,
not exceeding the twenty (20) centsaforesaid.
§ 7. This act shall take effectand be in force from

laws.summary: This statute outlines procedures for voter registration and challenges in the city of Henderson. It details how names can be marked as 'doubtful' and require further investigation before voting. It also specifies penalties for false registration, including registering in multiple wards or while underage or not lawfully entitled to register. The statute mandates the delivery of registration and poll books to election officials and states that a person's vote will not be received unless their name is on the register or a certificate is produced.

laws.summary: This act establishes a graded school district in Hanson, Kentucky. Section 2 explicitly states that only 'white children' are eligible for admission to the common schools within this district, and other 'white persons' may be admitted by trustees under prescribed terms. This segregation of educational facilities based on race is a hallmark of Jim Crow laws.

CHAPTER 969 .
AN ACT to authorizethe county court at itscourt of claims to levy an
ad valorem tax and fixthecountylevyinAdair county.
Be itenactedby the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§ 1. That the county court of claims for the county
of Adair shallhave the power to levy an ad valo-
rem tax of not exceeding fifteencents on each one
hundred dollars' worth of taxable property in said
county,to be collectedin the same manner that the
Staterevenue iscollected, which tax shallbe used for
county purposes only .
§ 2. The saidcounty court isalsoauthorizedto col-
lect a per capita tax from each white voter not ex-
ceeding one dollar and fiftycents for the purposes
named in section one .
§3 . The sheriffof saidcountyshallbe responsible
on his bond to the same extent for the collection of
the tax imposed in this act as the State revenue .
§ 4. This act shall take effectfrom itspassage .

laws.summary: This statute establishes a capitation tax for able-bodied voters under fifty years of age in Adair County, allowing payment through labor on county roads. It outlines the collection of taxes and the responsibilities of surveyors and taxpayers, which may disproportionately affect Black Kentuckians by enforcing labor requirements tied to taxation.

CHAPTER 535 .
AN ACT tolevya tax and providefor the improvement of roads in
Adair and Laurel counties .
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the court of claims for the counties of
Adair and Laurel shall,on or before the firstMonday
in October, one thousand eight hundred and ninety,
and as often thereafteras may be necessary, divide
allthe publicroads and passways of said county into
highways and passways .
§ 2. All main roads and chief branches of main
roads in Adair and Laurel counties, that lead to or
from towns or villages,or other public places of said
county,shallbe deemed highways .
§ 3. All inferior roads or branches of inferiorroads
Constitutepass-in said county that lead to or from other roads,neigh-
borhoods, localities, stations, depots, mills, stores,
post-offices, school-houses,churches or other places,
for the convenience of the public, shall be deemed
passways .
Duties of road
commissioners .
§ 4. It shall also be the duty of said court of
claims , on or before said date , to elect a commis-
sioner of roads (which officeis hereby created),
whose duty it shall be to divide said highways into
sections of not less than three nor more than five
miles in length, according to the amount of labor re-
quired on saidsection,and to appointover each of
said sectionsa surveyor or overseer, to hold officefor
one year, or during good service, notifying said sur-
veyorof allpersonsrequiredtowork on saidsection,
whose duty it shall be, under the directionof said
surveyor, to keep in good repair the full length of
saidsection,according to the requirements of section
ten of this act .
§ 5. Said road commissioner shallhave the right,for
and in behalf of said county, to go upon any land or
ground near or adjacent to said highways or passways
(except burying -grounds , gardens and yards), and
viewout and purchase or have condemned and opened
tothe public any land or rightof way , not exceeding
thirtyfeet wide , for said highway or passway , that
may be necessary to carry into effectthe require
ments of this act ; and said commissioner shall have
allthe rights , powers and privileges, and be subject
tothe same duties and penalties, as are now conferred
and imposed upon surveyors and viewers of roads
and passways in chapter ninety-four of the General
Statutes, entitled Roads and Passways : Provided ,
That said commissioner shall not agree to pay more
than a fair compensation for said land or right of
way : And provided further, That said compensa-
tion shall not exceed the difference between the value
of the old road way and the new one , when both of
saidroad-ways areon thesame premises,or areowned
by the same party, in whole or in part; and that no
compensation shall be allowed foropening old road-
ways that have been obstructed or changed without
proper authority within fiveyears of the passage of
this act, except that said commissioner may make
some allowance for the removal of fencing, or have
said fencing removed by the surveyor and hands of
said road .
$ 6 . It shall be the duty of said road commissioner
and his successors, on or before the firstMonday in
December ,beginning with the year one thousand eight
hundred and ninety, to re-survey, or view out and
open to the public, as soon as practicable,beginning
with the worst ,not lessthan two nor more than six
of said highways in each and every year,untilall of
saidhighways shall have been re-surveyed and re-es-
tablished; and to make such changes in said high-
ways as may be necessary to avoid steep hills; to
shun creek channels ; to straightenshortor unneces-
sary crooks ; to avoid sidling or mirey places; to
shun bad fords,and to make such other changes in
said highways as may be necessary to locate and
establisheach of said highways upon the best prac-
ticable route along said road course : Provided ,
That said road-way shallbe changed as littleas prac-

spirituous,vinousor malt liquorsin Logan county, Kentucky," ap-

monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That an act,entitled" An act to prohibit the
sale of spirituous,vinous or malt liquors in Logan
county, Kentucky ," approved March thirteenth, one
thousand eight hundred and eighty-six, be, and the
same is hereby, amended so as to read as follows:
That itshallbe unlawful for any person to sell,barter

mixture of either of them , in Logan county , except
as hereinafterprovided ; and it shall be unlawful for
any person to give any of the above-named liquors, or

anygoods, wares or merchandise. Any one so offend-Penalties.
ingshall, for the firstoffense,be fined not less than
fiftydollarsnor more than two hundred dollars,and
foreachsubsequent offense, upon conviction,shall be

normore than three hundred dollars, and confined in
thejailof Logan county not lessthan thirtydays nor
more than six months . Prosecutions under this act
may be by warrant issued by any justiceof peace in
andforLogan county, or by indictment in the Logan

$2. Before the provisions of this act shall take Provideforelec-

the vote cast for and againstsaid sale, which certifi-
cateshallbe signed by them ,or any two of them , and
entered of record in the order-book of the Logan
County Court, and thereupon the provisions of the

county,so appearing and certifiedto have voted for

§ 3. If, in Logan county, appearing and certifiedto

any persondesiringto sellsuch spiritsmay do so ;
but must firstobtain a licensetherefor,as isnow , or

§ 4. If thefirstsectionof thisactshallgo intoeffect
in said Logan county, allfines and forfeituresre-

hibitorylaw now in force in said county : And pro-
vided, That nothing in this billshallinterferewith

besoconstrued as to interferewith the localoption

oftwentycitizensand legal votersin said county, to

asthereinprovided .

CHAPTER 553 .
AN ACT toamend an act,entitled"An acttoregulatethesaleofspirit-
uous,vinousand malt liquorsin Woodford county," which became a
law April twenty-first,one thousandeighthundred and eighty-eight,
and the actsamendatory thereof, approved April twenty -seventh,one
thousandeighthundred and eighty-eight.
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the second section of the act, entitled
" An act to regulate the sale of spirituous, vinous
and malt liquors in Woodford county ," which be-
came a law April twenty -first, one thousand eight
hundred and eighty-eight,be, and the same is here-
by , repealed, and in lieu thereof the following is
hereby enacted as sectiontwo of said act, namely :
§ 2. Section thirteenof the aforesaidact of April
twenty-first,one thousand eighthundred and eighty-
eight, as amended by the second section of the act
amending the same , approved April twenty -seventh,
one thousandeighthundred and eighty-eight,ishere-
by repealed, and any electionhereafter held under
the aforesaid act and the amendments thereto shall
be held on the day requested by the petitionersin
the petitionprovided for by said act, and not oftener
thereafterthan every threeyears: Provided ,however ,
That saidelectionshallnot be held on the same day
with any electionin said county for State, county ,
precinct or districtofficers.
§3 . Any electionheld under the aforesaidact as
amended may be contestedas provided for in this
section, namely :
First. The contest shall be heard and determined
by the same board which , by law, are authorized and
empowered to hear and determine a contest of an
electionforcounty officers,and the same provisionsof
the statuteshallapply to the contestof any elections
held under this act as are provided for the contestof
:
any election for county officers, except as hereinafter
provided .
Second . Any number of citizensof Woodford
county , Kentucky , residents and legal voters in
said county not less than ten, shallhave the right
to contest any election held under the aforesaid
act and its amendments . The said contestants
shall, within ten days after the finalaction of the
board of examiners , give notice of such contest
by a printed notice posted at the court-house door
in the town of Versailles, Kentucky , and by inser-
tion in a newspaper at the time published in Ver-
sailles, if one is so published, and will publish the
said notice for at leasttwo consecutive issues,com-
mencing not laterthan the firstissue of such paper
after the posting of said notice at the courthouse
door ; but if no paper is published at this time at
Versailles, or if such a paper refusesto insertsuch
notice , then the notice at the court -house door shall
be sufficient .
§4 . Said contest may be resistedby any citizen
resident and legal voter in Woodford county,or by
any number of citizensresidentand legal voters in
Woodford county : Provided , That within ten days
after the posting of said notice on the court-house
door, or within ten days afterthe publicationcon-
taining the firstinsertionof said noticeof said news-
paper, if said noticeisinsertedina newspaper,he or
they filein the officeof the clerkof Woodford County
Court a written notice,signedby him or them ,of their
intention to resistsaid contest; and notice for the
taking of depositionsor other proceedingsto be taken
insaid contest,duly executedupon thepersonwhose
name appears firston the aforesaidnoticeof contest,
and firston the aforesaidnoticeof resistingsaidcon-
test,shallbe due noticeto the opposing partiesre-
spectively. In case no noticeof resistingsaidcontest
isfiled, then ex parte testimony shall be competent
before the contestingboard .
§ 5. The decision of the board shall be given in
writing and signed in duplicate, one copy to be
handed to the successfulparty, and the other shall
be handed to the clerk of the county court of Wood-
ford county, which shallbe spread upon the order-
book of said court in the same manner and at the
same time,and shallhave the same effectas is pro-
vided in section five of the originalact of April
twenty -first,one thousand eight hundred and eighty-
eight, in regard to the certificateof the result of the
elections held under said act .
§ 6. The case shall be heard by the board on the
fourth Monday afterthe filingin the county clerk's
officeof the notice of the resisting of the contest of
the election; but the board may ,forgood cause,allow
further time .
§ 7. Either of the partiesto such contested elec-
tionshallhave the right to appeal from the decision
of said board to the circuit court of Woodford coun-
ty, and from thence to the Court of Appeals . But
until such appeal is finallydecided, the decision of
the board for trying said contested election shall
stand as law .
§ 8. This act shall take effectand be in force from
and after itspassage .
Approved April 3,1890.

CHAPTER 605 .
AN ACT to createthe officeof county treasurerof Harrison county .
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That the officeof county treasurerof Harrison
county be, and ishereby, created.
§ 2. The county court of claims,at itsApril term
of each year,shallelectsome one of the officerscon-
nected with one of the Cynthiana banks as treasurer
of Harrison county,whose term of officeshallbe one
year, or until his successorisduly electedand quali-
fied as such .
§ 3. The county treasurerprovided for herein shall
execute bond , with good and sufficientsurety, to the
Commonwealth of Kentucky,to be approved by the
said court, conditioned to discharge all the duties
of said office, and pay over all the money in his
hands in the manner at such times as he may be di-
rectedby the county court of Harrison county ; and
said treasurershall take the oaths required by the
Constitutionand by the general laws of the State,
as specifiedby chapter eighty-one of the General
Statutes .
§ 4. It shallbe the duty of the county treasurer
herein provided for to receive, take charge of, and
account for allmoney that he may be directedby the
Harrison County Court to do , and to pay over said
money as he may be directedby saidcourton what-
ever claims or debts he may be so directed to pay
same on . He shallkeep a book ,to be furnished and
paid for as otherpublicbooks , in which he shallkeep
a correctaccountof allmoneys receivedby him foror
on account of saidcounty,showing when and on what
account received by him , and how and on what ac-
count disbursed by him . Said book shallalways be
kept at the county clerk'sofficeof saidcountyas a
partof the records thereof, and shallat alltimes be
open to the inspectionof any one interested.
§5 . It shall be the duty of the county judge and
county attorney of said county to make annual settle-
ments with the county treasurer, and the same shall
be reported to the court of claims at itsApril térm
for confirmation ; and if no exceptions be taken at
the aforesaid court , it shall be confirmed and said
report ordered to record .
§ 6. At the expiration of the term of officeof the
county treasurer, he shallsettlehis accounts as above
stated, and shall pay and deliverto his successorall
county funds , officebooks and accounts in his cus-
tody .
§7 . If a vacancy occursby deathor resignation,the
county judge is empowered to fillthe vacancy until
the next regular electionas above provided for.
$ 8. The county court shallprovide for the compen-
sation of the county treasurer; but the compensation
in no event shall exceed two hundred and fiftydol-
lars.
§9 . This act shall take effect from and after its
passage .
Approved April7,1890.

laws.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to amend and reduce into one the several acts concerning the town of Midway."
laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 695, p. 410
laws.summary: This statute establishes voting restrictions in the town of Midway, requiring individuals to have paid all poll taxes at least fifteen days prior to an election, which historically disenfranchised many Black voters.
page_titles: Voting Restrictions in Midway
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 695 .
AN ACT to amend an act,entitled"An act to amend and reduce into
one the severalactsconcerningthe town of Midway ."
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That at any electionin said town of Midway
for police judge, marshal or trustees, no person shall
be entitled to vote who has not paid all his poll-taxes
due the town for the years preceding the one in which
he offers to vote at least fifteendays before the day
of the election .
§2 . That this act shall take effect from and after
its passage .
Approved April 10,1890 .

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 723, pp. 465–467
laws.summary: This statute outlines the procedure for holding an election regarding the repeal of a prohibitory law in Hopkins County, including the registration of votes in separate columns for and against the repeal. The law reflects mechanisms that could be used to disenfranchise certain voters, particularly in the context of Jim Crow laws.

laws.citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 734, pp. 496–497
laws.summary: This statute amends the incorporation act of the Lexington Charity Organization Society, allowing for the arrest and sentencing of beggars who refuse employment or assistance, which disproportionately affects marginalized groups.
page_titles: Amendment to the Lexington Charity Organization Society Act
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 734 .
AN ACT toamend an act,entitled"An acttoincorporatethe Lexing-
ton Charity Organization Society."
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That an act, entitled" An act to incorporate
the Lexington Charity Organization Society," ap-
proved March fifth, one thousand eight hundred and
ninety , be amended by adding the following words to
sectiontwo : " And any beggar who failsor refusesto
accept such employment or suitableassistancewhen
tendered, and isthereafterfound begging in the city
limits, shall be reported to the county judge,who
shall have such beggar arrested for vagrancy , and
brought before him ; and upon satisfactoryproof of
the offerof employment or other suitableassistance,
and of subsequent begging,shallsentence the offend-
er to the city work -house for not exceeding thirty
days : Provided , however, If the offenderbe a child
of tender years, it shall be the duty of the county
court to place such child in the custody of this so-
cietyuntil a home foritcan be found with some suit-
ableperson or charitableorganizationwhere itwillbe
reared in moral courses ; the court shall then bind it
out as now provided by law ."
§2 . That said act be further amended by adding
the following words to section four of the same :
"And the county court shallhave the power to place
orphan children, whose friendsor relativesfailor re-
fuse to provide for their necessary physical wants ,
and the children of parents of notoriouslybad moral
character, in the custody of this society, untilhomes
can be provided for them with some suitableperson
or charitableorganization. The courtshallthen bind
saidchildren out as now provided by law . The court
may , however , permit a child so taken to be returned
to itsparents without being bound out, if, in the
meantime , the said parents show abilityand willing-
ness to provide for itsnecessaryphysical wants , and
to rear it in moral courses ."
§ 3. Any person attempting clandestinelyor by
force to take a child from the legalcustody of this
societyshall, upon convictionby a jury in the county
court, be punished by a finenot exceeding twenty
dollars,and confinement in the city work -house not
more than sixty days , or both , in the discretion of the
court .
Approved April 11, 1890 .

laws.summary: This statute prescribes corporal punishment (lashes) for male individuals convicted of petit larceny in Graves County, which reflects a differential legal treatment that could be applied to marginalized groups, particularly Black individuals during the Jim Crow era.
page_titles: Punishment for Petit Larceny in Graves County
laws.full_text:
CHAPTER 765 .
AN ACT to providefor the punishment of petitlarcenyin Graves
county .
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That any male person guilty of petit larceny
shall, upon conviction, be punished by the adminis-
teringby the sheriffof not lessthan ten nor more
than thirty-nine lashes,welllaidon theirbare back .
§ 2. This actshallonly apply to Graves county .
§ 3. This act shall take effectfrom and after its
passage .
Approved April 15,1890.

laws.summary: This statute mandates that individuals convicted of certain offenses must work off their fines through labor, which can be enforced by local authorities. It establishes a system of forced labor as a penalty for non-payment of fines, which disproportionately affected marginalized communities.

Provided , however, The board of trustees may , by

poses, as follows: Provided , That in no case shall

written consent of the claimant or a just and full

claimants ; if the amount of such compensation can
not be fixedby agreement ,the board of trusteesshall
cause to be filedin the Johnson County Court stating
the streetor alleyopened or widened or extended ,and

quired by law, state whether , in theiropinion, the

§ 61. The board shall have power ,at any timebe-
forethe finaldecreeor order,to dismisstheirpetition,

ceedings for opening, widening or extending such

dismission .

§ 64. The board shallhave fullpower , by ordinance,

hereby given to said town on all lots and parts of

§ 68. When any person has had a streetin front of

§ 69. The board shallhave the power ,forany of the

§ 70. No person or persons shalllay out or extend

§ 71. The election for the said chairman and trus-

§ 72. The board of trusteesshall,before such elec-

§73 . Every male citizenof the age of twenty -one

dent of said town , and have residedthereinfor sixty

§ 74. The person acting as sheriffof said election
shall, within one day afterthe same ,deposit the poll-
book with the clerk of Johnson County Court, who
shall filesaid book in his office. Said county clerk,
the judge of the policecourt of Paintsville,and the
person acting as sheriffof the election, shall consti-

§75 . Whenever any two or more persons shall re-

The electionsprovided for in this act may be con-

ings had as when electionsfor county officersare

§ 76. Whenever any vacancies shall occur in the

cessorsbe duly qualified; and the person appointed

form the same duties, and be under the same re
sponsibilitiesand restrictions, as if they had been

§ 77. All resignationsof the officersof said town of
Paintsville shall be tendered to board of trustees in

§78 . The present police judge of the town of
Paintsville shall remain in officeand exercise all the

villeuntil the July election, one thousand eight hun-

§ 79. The present actingtown marshal of said town
shall remain in office and exercise all the duties and

pointed or qualified.
§ 80. No bond for cost or other bond shall be re-
quired of the town of Paintsvillein any suit, prosecu-
tion or legalproceedings, unlessthe same be lawfully
required under similar circumstances of a resident
citizen of this State .
§ 81. All ordinances of the town of Paintsville now
in force not in conflict with this charter shall continue
in force untilrepealedby the board,and alllaws vest-
ing rights in or imposing duties upon the town of
Paintsville,not thereinsuspended or repealedby the
General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky .
§ 82. The recognized records of the trusteesof the
town of Paintsville, and allbonds and contractsexe-
cuted to said town ,shall remain in fullforce; and ,
remaining in the proper officeor keeper thereof, shall
be evidence in all courts to the same extent that the
originalswould be on due proof ; and the keepers of
said records may be entitledto feesforcopiesof same ,
to be prescribedby ordinance.
§ 83. The said board of trusteesshall have power
to prescribepenaltiesforthe breach of allordinances

passed by them , in pursuance of the powers herein
granted ; and whenever the penaltieshave not been
prescribedby this act,said penaltiesmay be in any

§ 84. It shallbe the duty of the board of trustees
to provide forthe use of the saidpolice court a suit-
able docket, judgment book , execution book , well
bound , and provide forpaying forsame ; and it shall
be the duty of said board to make allowance to any

§ 85. All laws or parts of laws in conflictwith this

§ 86. This act to take effectfrom and after its pas-

CHAPTER 828 .
AN ACT to provide for holding an electionto take the sense of the
votersof Canton precinct,in Trigg county ,as to the regulationof the
liquortrafficor itsprohibitiontherein.
Be itenacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . The judge of the county court of Trigg county
shall,upon the writtenpetitionof not lessthan twen-
ty legalvoters of Canton precinct, in Trigg county ,
order an electiontobe held thereinfor the purpose of
taking the sense of the legalvoters of said district
upon the propositionwhether they are in favor of the
regulationof the trafficin liquorthereinby licenseor
prohibition, said electionto be held at such time as
shallbe mentioned in and requested by said petition,
other than the day of any other election, and except
as modified by this act,shall,in all respectsand in
every manner ,be held under and in conformity to the
provisionsof " An act to regulate the saleof spirit-
uous , vinous or malt liquorsin thisCommonwealth ,"
approved May twenty -sixth, one thousand eight hun-
dred and seventy-four; and allduties required of the
county judge and other officersin electionsheld under
saidact shallbe performed by such officerswith ref-
erence to the electionprovided for hereby , except as
hereby modified.
§2 . At said electionthe electionofficersshallpro-
pound to each voter presenting himself to vote, the
question, " Are you in favor of the prohibitionor
the regulation by licenseof the sale of spirituous,
vinous or malt liquorsin thisprecinct?" and his vote
shallbe entered for the prohibitionof said trafficor
foritsregulationby license,as thevoterdirects.
§ 3. If itshallbe found that a majority of the legal
votes castat said electionwere given for the prohibi-
tionof the saleof liquor in said district, the examin-
ingboardshallsocertifytothecountycourt,and it
shallbe unlawful to sellsuch liquorin said precinct;
but if it shallbe found that a majority of the legal
votes castat said electionwere given for the regula-
ion of the saleof such liquorby license, then the said
board shallso certifyto the county court,which certif-
icate shall be entered in the order -book of said court
at its next regular term , and it shall then be lawful to
sellspirituous, vinous and malt liquorsin said pre-
cinct under such regulation as to licenseas may be
provided by law .
§ 4. This act shalltake effectfrom itspassage ; and
all acts and parts of actsin conflictwith the provis-
ions of this act are, so far as the same conflict here-
with , repealed.
Approved April16,1890.

CHAPTER 832 .
AN ACT toincorporatethecityof Pineville, inBellcounty.
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
§1 . That so much of the county of Bell as is in-
cluded in the limits of the town of Pineville as now
fixed by law,and ,in additionthereto, commencing on
the north-west lineof saidlimitsat a point threehun-
dred yards north of the centerlineof the Louisville
and NashvilleRailroad Company's rightof way ;
thence west, and parallelwith said line, to the west
line of the land conveyed by Vincent Boreing to the
Bell County Coke and Improvement Company ; and
thence with said line to Cumberland river; and thence
east with the meanders of said river to the said west
line of the town of Pineville ; and also extending the
south line of saidlimitswhere it joinsthe land con
veyed by R. M. Moss,etcetera,tothe Pine Mountain
Ironand Coal Company ,so as to includesaid land, and
the persons residingwithin saidlimits,are hereby cre-
ated a body -politicand corporate, by the name " City
of Pineville;" and by that name shallhave perpetual
succession, with power to govern themselves by such
ordinances and regulationsand resolutionsas they
may deem proper, pursuant to the terms of this
charter : Provided , The same be not in conflict with
the Constitution or laws of this State or of the United
States; and be capable of suing and being sued ,
pleading and being impleaded , defending and being
defended , in all courts ; may contract and be con-
tracted with ; may acquire and hold property, for
municipal purposes, by dedication or condemnation
or otherwise; and may use, manage , improve , sell,
convey, rent or leasesuch property ; may have a com-
mon seal, and altersame at pleasure .
§ 2. And said city is invested with all the lands ,
tenements, and hereditaments, and all the goods,
chattels, moneys , revenues, rights and demands in
possession or expectancy of the town of Pineville,
and shallbe bound by allcontracts, and responsi-
ble for all debts, demands and liabilities, of what-
soever kind , against said town ; and it shall suc-
ceed to allthe rights, privilegesand franchisesof
said town ; and all privateactsheretoforegranted in
referenceto streetrailwaysin said town , or any fran-
chisetherein,shallbecome applicableto the said city
in the same manner and to the same extent as before
the adoption of this act.
§3 .Allstreets,alleys,roadsand lanesnow open to
the publictravel, and now establishedin said city,
are hereby declared to be public ways , and as such
shallbe under the controlof the city of Pineville.
ARTICLE II .
§1 . The corporatepowers of said cityof Pineville
shall be divided into three distinctand separate de
partments, viz: The legislative, executive and judi-
ciary.
ARTICLE III .
§ 1. The legislativepowers of the city of Pineville
shallbe vested in fivecouncilmen,to be styled The
Board of Councilmen of the City of Pineville, mem-
bers of which shallbe qualifiedvoters,owners of real
estatein said city,bona fide residentsthereof for at
leasttwelve months prior to theirelection, and shall
not be directlyor indirectlyinterestedin any place
where intoxicatingliquorof any kind is sold, nor be
directlyor indirectlyinterestedin his own behalf, or
inthe behalf of any other individual, in any contract
with said cityor any applicationtherefor, nor be in
arrears to said city for money collectedfor and with-
held from said city without settlement or quietus
therefor; and if, after his election, any member of
saidboard of councilmen shalldie or resign as coun-
cilman,or remove from the city,or engage in any bus-
iness, or do any act, the holding or doing of which
would have rendered him ineligibleas a member of
the board of councilmen, his seat, as such member ,
shall thereby be vacated , and the remaining members
of said board of councilmen shallso declare,and pro-
ceed immediately , or as soon thereafteras is practica-
ble, to fillthe vacancy .
§ 2. Stockholders in other corporationsmay be eli-
gible as a member of the board of councilmen ; but
shallnot vote or interfere, directlyor indirectly, with
any matter or questionaffectingany contractbetween
such company or corporationand the city of Pine-
ville .
§3 . The board of councilmen shall be electedby
the qualifiedvoters of said cityon the second Tues-
day in May ,one thousand eight hundred and ninety,
and biennially thereafter; and each member thereof
shall hold his officefor a term of two years .
§4 . The board of councilmen shall, as soon as prac-
ticable, electone of itsmembers mayor of the cityof
Pineville, who shall also be chairman of the board ;
and in his absence a mayor and chairman pro tempore
shallbe electedfrom the members by the members ;
but such person shallnot perform the functionsof the
officeof mayor ,except when the regular mayor has
been absent from Bell county forat leastthree days .
Three members shallbe a quorum of the board , with
power to act. In the absence of a quorum two mem-
bers shallhave power to adjourn from time to time
untila quorum issecured. The board shallhave power
tofillany vacancieswhich may occur in the board,and
upon a tievote, the person forwhom the mayor and
one councilman may vote shall be elected,and shall
hold officeuntil the next regular municipal elec-
tion. The board shall meet at such times and place
as they shall,by resolutionor ordinance,agree upon .
Itshalljudge of the eligibilityand electionreturns of
itsmembers , adopt rulesfor itsproceedings and gov-
ernment ,and enforce the same by appropriate fines,
not exceeding ten dollarsfor each offense; and four
members voting affirmativelymay , for cause, expel
any member .
§ 5. Before entering upon the execution of the
duties of their office, the several members of the
board of councilmen , and all other city officers, shall
take the following oath or affirmation: " I do sol-
emnly swear (or affirm)that I willfaithfullyand with-
out fear, favor or affection, discharge the duties of
the office of (as the officemay be) of the
city of Pinevilleaccording to law," which oath or
affirmation shall be administered by the clerk of the
Bell County Court, or any officerauthorizedto admin-
isteroaths, and a certificatethereof shallbe filedon
the journaland filedwith the recordsof the city.
§ 6. The board of councilmenshallelecta clerk,
who shallkeep a complete record of all itsproceed-
ings; and allrecords and officialproceedings of the
board of councilmen , and of the board of trustees of
the town of Pineville under former charters of the
1
town, are hereby declared " public records," and as
such shall be preserved and entitledto all the faith
and credit of " public records," and officialcopies
thereof may be read in allcourtswith like effectas
public records. Every ordinance passed, or resolu-
tionadopted ,shallbe published at leastonce in some
newspaper published in Pineville,or by printed hand-
billsposted innot lessthan threepublic placesin said
city; and it shall be the duty of the clerk of said
board to have such publication made as soon as
practicable, and to preserve a copy of said news-
paper or handbillin which published,and such pub-
licationshall be made before any ordinance is en-
forced ; and such copies of an ordinance or resolution
shall be prima facie evidence of its having been
published as requiredherein.
§ 7. Any member of saidboard of councilmen may
callfor the yeas and nays on any vote, which shall
be entered on the journalof proceedings.
Powers of the Board of Councilmen .
The board of councilmen, in additionto other pow-
ers hereinbeforegranted,shallhave power within the
city of Pineville, by ordinance:
First . To levy and collectfor municipal purposes
an annual ad valorem tax, not exceeding fiftycents
on every one hundred dollarsof real estateand per-
sonal property made taxable by law for State pur
poses, and not exceeding fiftycents on every one
hundred dollarsof such property to meet the princi-
pal and interest of any bonded debt hereinafter
authorized .
Second . To levy and collectannually upon every
male residentof said citytwenty -one years of age or
over, a head or personal tax of not exceeding two
dollars .
Third . To borrow money upon the credit of the
city,and issuecoupon bonds therefor,payment thereof
to be secured by a pledge or mortgage of the revenues
of the city; such bonds to be payable in not exceed-
ing thirtyyears, and to bear interest,payable semi-
annually,at a rate not exceeding six per cent. per
annum ; said bonds and the interest thereon may be
made payable at such place or placesas saidboard of
councilmen may designate in the ordinance authoriz
ing the issue of such bonds . But the debt so created
shallnot exceed fiftythousand dollarsat any time.
Fourth . To appropriate money and provide for the
payment of the debts and the expenses of the city.
Fifth . To make regulationsto prevent the intro-

CHAPTER 861 .
AN ACT to amend , revise and reduce into one the several acts in
relationto the town of Mount Washington,in Bullittcounty.
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the Com-
monwealth of Kentucky :
Boundary .
§1 . The boundary of the town of Mount Wash-
ington, in Bullittcounty,is hereby declared to be as
follows: Beginning at T. C. Long's house on the
Mans Lick road , one -fourth of a mile west of the
old town limits, including said house ; thence north
on a straightline to a stake,corner in W. P. Barne's
land ; thence at right-angleseast on a straightlineto
a stake on R. Griggsby's land, one-fourth of a mile
east of the old town limits; thence south at right-
angles on a straightline to a stake on J. W. Showal-
ter'sland ; thence west at right-angles on a straight
lineto a stake on W. S. McFarland's land,one fourth
of a mile west of the old town limits ; thence north
atright-angleson a straightlinetothepointofbegin-
ning .
§ 2. It shallbe the duty of the trusteesof said town ,
:
tees .
as soon as may be afterthe firstelectionunder thisact,Dutiesoftrus-
to cause a survey and plot of said town to be made
and prepared according to the boundary specifiedin
the firstsection,and to cause permanent monuments
to be erected at the place of beginning and at the
various corners, which plot shall show the various
subdivisionsof said town intolots,streetsand alleys.
The names of the streetsand alleys,and the numbers
of the lots as heretoforeestablished, shall, as far as
practicable,be preserved;and such land as may be in-
cluded in said boundary , not heretoforeembraced in
the corporate limitsof said town ,shall be designated
on said plotby the names of the owners. The trustees

clerk's officeof Bullittcounty, and a certifiedcopy
