Attorneys prosecuting such cases receive 20% of the damages, and informers receive $10.

statutes.statute_citation: A Digest of the General Laws of Kentucky, 1866, pp. 74–76
statutes.title: AN ACT authorizing the board of managers of the Western Lunatic Asylum to appoint a superintendent of said institution. SEC. I. That the board of managers of the Western Lunatic Asylum, be and they are hereby authorized, when the same in their opinion is necessary, to appoint a superintendent for…
citations: A Digest of the General Laws of Kentucky, 1866, pp. 74–76
statutes.summary: This act amends existing statutes regarding the appointment of managers for lunatic asylums and the appointment and duties of superintendents for the Western Lunatic Asylum. It specifies how vacancies in the board of managers are filled and outlines the qualifications, salary, and removal powers for the superintendent. The text also includes sections on divorce proceedings and militia organization, but the most relevant part for Jim Crow analysis is the section concerning free negroes and mulattoes being deemed guilty of felony if they come into the state with the intention of remaining, or come for any purpose other than obedience to court process, with penalties including penitentiary confinement and potential life imprisonment for re-entry after release on bond.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 556, p. 78
statutes.title: AN ACT in relation to the marriage of negroes and mulattoes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 556, p. 78
statutes.summary: This act regulates the marriage of Black individuals in Kentucky. It allows Black individuals to marry each other under the same regulations as white persons, with separate record-keeping. It also validates existing cohabiting relationships and their issue. Crucially, it prohibits interracial marriage between Black and white individuals, making it a felony punishable by at least five years in the state penitentiary. The act defines 'negroes and mulattoes' based on ancestry.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 559, pp. 78–79
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for rebuilding Western Lunatic Asylum.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 559, pp. 78–79
statutes.summary: This act regulates the marriage of Black individuals in Kentucky. It allows Black individuals to marry each other under the same regulations as white persons, with separate record-keeping. It also validates existing cohabiting relationships and their issue. Crucially, it prohibits interracial marriage between Black and white individuals, making it a felony punishable by at least five years in the state penitentiary. The act defines 'negroes and mulattoes' based on ancestry.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 595, p. 83
statutes.title: AN ACT prescribing punishment for felonies and misdemeanors by free negroes and mulattoes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 595, p. 83
statutes.summary: This act states that all persons, regardless of color, will be subject to the same pains and penalties for felonies and misdemeanors as white persons. However, it explicitly continues in force existing laws for the punishment of negroes and mulattoes for rape on white women.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 603, pp. 84–85
statutes.title: AN ACT repealing and amending certain sections, articles, and chapters of the Revised Statutes and Session Acts approved since the adoption of the Re vised Statutes, concerning slaves and free negroes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 603, pp. 84–85
statutes.summary: This act repeals or amends various sections of the Revised Statutes and Session Acts related to slaves and free negroes. Specifically, it repeals articles on patrols, the listing of slaves, and provisions for whipping slaves. It also amends a section to remove the penalty of whipping for a free person and a slave, and repeals sections related to runaway slaves and makes all negroes and mulattoes liable to certain provisions.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 621, pp. 90–91
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend article1, chapter64, Revised Statutes, title"Master and Apprentice."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 621, pp. 90–91
statutes.summary: This act amends the Master and Apprentice law. It repeals Section 5 of Article 1, Chapter 64 of the Revised Statutes. The new Section 2 outlines the requirements for apprenticeship contracts, including the age of the minor, the trade to be taught, medical attention, food, clothing, and humane treatment. Crucially, it specifies that if the apprentice is not a negro, the master must teach them to read, write, and common arithmetic. If the apprentice *is* a negro, the master is bound to pay them at the end of the apprenticeship, implying a different standard of education or compensation based on race.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 636, p. 92
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the negroes and mulattoes in this Commonwealth.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 636, p. 92
statutes.summary: This act establishes a separate fund from taxes collected from negroes and mulattoes for their benefit. Half of this fund is designated for the support of their paupers, and the remainder for the education of their children. It mandates a $2 poll tax on male negroes and mulattoes over 18, requires separate record-keeping for their taxable property, and allows for separate schools for negro and mulatto children. Paupers are to be supported from this fund based on county court certifications.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 672, p. 93
statutes.title: AN ACT in relation to contracts with negroes and mulattoes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 672, p. 93
statutes.summary: This act allows parties in labor contracts between white persons and negroes or mulattoes to stipulate that the contract is entire. If either party abandons the contract without good cause, the other party is considered to have completed their part. All such contracts must be in writing and attested by a white person.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 770, p. 825
statutes.title: AN ACT to revive and re-enact the act to incorporate the town of Stamping Ground, in Scott county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 770, p. 825
statutes.summary: This act revives and re-enacts a previous act incorporating the town of Stamping Ground. It modifies the election of trustees and specifies that the capitation tax authorized in a previous section shall be assessed, levied, and collected from all white citizens and resident negroes or mulattoes twenty-one years of age.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 818, pp. 107–108
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the vagrant laws.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 818, pp. 107–108
statutes.summary: This act defines vagrancy as being an able-bodied person loitering without means of support, not laboring, or abandoning a family without provision. Convicted vagrants are to be apprehended, tried, and if found guilty, sentenced to labor for a period not exceeding twelve months. Those over twenty-one are to be sent to houses of correction, or if none exist, a superintendent will be appointed by the county court to oversee their labor.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 881, pp. 109–110
statutes.title: AN ACT to regulate coffee-houses in this Commonwealth.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, ch. 881, pp. 109–110
statutes.summary: This act requires coffee-house keepers to execute a bond and take an oath before selling spirituous or vinous liquors. The bond is conditioned on keeping an orderly house, not selling to disorderly or intoxicated persons, and specifically not selling to any minor or freenegro in violation of the laws of the Commonwealth. The county court must approve the bond and be satisfied of the keeper's good character.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, p. 129
statutes.title: RESOLUTIONS concerning the Freedmen's Bureau and charges against General Fisk
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1866, p. 129
statutes.summary: These resolutions from the Kentucky General Assembly in 1866 request the withdrawal of military forces and the Freedmen's Bureau from the state. They state the legislature's intent to enact laws for the 'colored population' that are just and humane, suited to their 'present condition,' and provide necessary protection. The resolutions also authorize a committee to investigate charges against General C. B. Fisk and report their findings to the Governor and President. A separate resolution rescinds the tenth joint rule of the two Houses.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1031, pp. 225–226
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the African Cemetery Company, of Bourbon County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1031, pp. 225–226
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the Bourbon County Cemetery Company and mandates that at least half of the land owned by the company must be set aside for the burial of persons of color who are not stockholders or lot owners. The remaining land can be divided and sold.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1433, pp. 616–639
statutes.title: AN ACT to reduce into one, amend, and digest the acts and amend a tory acts incorporating the City of Lexington. City Incorporated.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1433, pp. 616–639
statutes.summary: This section of the act grants the mayor the power to investigate and arrest individuals involved in unlawful assemblages, specifically mentioning gatherings for gaming, drinking, or any purpose not allowed by law. Crucially, it explicitly includes provisions for mixed-race gatherings ('where the said assemblage shall, or may be constituted partly of white and partly of black population') and allows the mayor to proceed with the power of the county and his officers to arrest all persons unlawfully assembled.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1562, pp. 83–84
statutes.title: AN ACT to appropriate money and provide for the erection of additional buildings at the Eastern Lunatic Asylum.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1562, pp. 83–84
statutes.summary: This act appropriates $150,000 for the construction of additional buildings at the Eastern Lunatic Asylum. It specifically directs the erection of a building for 250 additional white patients and the enlargement of a detached building for 70 negro patients.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1661, pp. 91–92
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend Chapter 34 of the Revised Statutes, title" Es cheats and Escheators." Be.it enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky:
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1661, pp. 91–92
statutes.summary: This act amends Chapter 34 of the Revised Statutes concerning Escheats and Escheators. It specifies that if a free person of color dies intestate, and their heirs would have inherited but were previously held in slavery, or if a free person of color dies leaving a will that bequeaths property to individuals who were previously held in slavery, these heirs, legatees, and devisees (or their heirs) are now competent to inherit or receive the property.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1882, p. 122
statutes.title: AN ACT in relation to Idiots and Lunatics.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1882, p. 122
statutes.summary: This act directs the Auditor of Public Accounts to issue warrants for the care of 'lunatics of color' sent to the Lunatic Asylum, provided certain conditions are met, similar to the process for white persons. It implies a separate or distinct process for the care of Black individuals with mental illness.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1913, pp. 125–127
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the Negroes and Mulattoes of this Commonwealth.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 1913, pp. 125–127
statutes.summary: This act levies an additional tax of two dollars on every male negro and mulatto over eighteen years of age. The collected funds are to be used exclusively for the support of negro and mulatto paupers and the education of negro and mulatto children within the county where the tax was collected. It mandates separate tax columns for negroes and mulattoes and outlines the process for allocating funds to negro schools, including per-scholar allowances and reporting requirements.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 2002, p. 131
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of School District No. 1, in Harrison county, and other School Districts similarly situated.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, ch. 2002, p. 131
statutes.summary: This act validates the report of a colored school taught in School District No. 1, Harrison County, in 1866, as a common school, and allows for similar colored schools to be recognized. It addresses a failure by trustees to report the colored school, which the commissioner states was taught under the provisions of a previous act.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 575
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the 10th article of the Charter of the City of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 575
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of the City of Louisville's public school system. It allows non-resident taxpayers to send their children to city schools free of tuition, but explicitly prohibits children of the African race from attending schools with white children. It also mandates that school taxes paid by persons of the African race be kept as a separate fund and used for the education of African race children within the city, potentially establishing separate schools for them.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 1690, p. 293
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate " The Southern Institution for the Amelioration of the Condition of the Deaf, Dumb, and Blind Negroes."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 1690, p. 293
statutes.summary: This act incorporates "The Southern Institution for the Amelioration of the Condition of the Deaf, Dumb, and Blind Negroes." It grants the institution the power to purchase land and other property, open subscription books for donations, and manage its affairs through appointed officers and directors. The institution is established to serve a specific racial group, indicating a segregationist purpose.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 1762, p. 346
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Common School District No. 23, in McCracken County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 1762, p. 346
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of Common School District No. 23 in McCracken County to levy a tax for common school purposes. Crucially, it explicitly states that the colored population of the district shall not be included in the tax and that colored children shall not be admitted to the common school of the district. The act requires a vote of qualified voters for its adoption.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 1887, pp. 450–456
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish the Boundaries and Taxable Limits, and to amend the Charter, of the City of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 1887, pp. 450–456
statutes.summary: This section of the act grants the general council of Louisville the power to establish and maintain a 'house of reform for white females'. It also allows judges to commit white females to this institution instead of the city work-house or jail for offenses not amounting to a felony. The commitment is limited to one year. The statute explicitly mentions 'white females', indicating a racial distinction in the application of this reformatory institution.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 2091, pp. 617–618
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of William O. Murrell, of Adair County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 2091, pp. 617–618
statutes.summary: This act allows William O. Murrell to file a petition in circuit court to address a failed consideration in his bond with the county court. The bond involved providing care for a negro pauper who was formerly a slave. The negro has since refused to provide service as stipulated, leading Murrell to claim the consideration for his bond has failed.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 2095, pp. 626–627
statutes.title: AN ACT authorizing a change of venue in the case of Sidney and others, of color, against May's administrator.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1867, ch. 2095, pp. 626–627
statutes.summary: This act allows plaintiffs identified as 'Sidney and others, of color' to request a change of venue in a pending Madison circuit court case if they file an affidavit stating they cannot receive a fair trial due to undue influence and prejudice against them.

statutes.statute_citation: The Code of Practice in Civil and Criminal Cases for the State of Kentucky, 1867, p. 732
statutes.title: The Code of Practice in Civil and Criminal Cases-1867
citations: The Code of Practice in Civil and Criminal Cases for the State of Kentucky, 1867, p. 732
statutes.summary: This excerpt from the 1867 Code of Practice in Civil and Criminal Cases outlines judicial procedures and judgments. Notably, it includes a template for an action concerning personal property where the plaintiff seeks the recovery of a 'negro man, Joe,' and damages for his detention. This specific example demonstrates the legal framework for property disputes involving enslaved or formerly enslaved individuals, reflecting the post-slavery but still racially stratified legal landscape of the era.

statutes.statute_citation: The Code of Practice in Civil and Criminal Cases for the State of Kentucky, 1867, § 656, pp. 211–215
statutes.title: SEC. 656. *Order in which proof to be given on trial.* The party who begins the case must ordinarily exhaust his evidence before the other begins.
citations: The Code of Practice in Civil and Criminal Cases for the State of Kentucky, 1867, § 656, pp. 211–215
statutes.summary: This statute outlines who is competent to testify in civil actions. It lists several categories of individuals who are incompetent, including those convicted of certain crimes, infants under ten, those of unsound mind, spouses, attorneys, persons with an interest in the issue, and 'Negroes, etc.'. All other objections to a witness's testimony are to be considered as affecting their credibility.

statutes.statute_citation: The Code of Practice in Civil and Criminal Cases for the State of Kentucky, 1867, § 9, pp. 589–591
statutes.title: SEC.9. Modes of preventing offenses.
citations: The Code of Practice in Civil and Criminal Cases for the State of Kentucky, 1867, § 9, pp. 589–591
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the criminal jurisdiction of justices' courts and city/police courts in Kentucky. It specifies the types of misdemeanors and offenses these courts can hear, differentiating penalties based on whether the accused is a 'free person' or a 'slave'. It also details concurrent and exclusive jurisdiction with circuit courts and allows for the removal of cases from circuit court to lower courts. An amendment from 1856 is also included, which repeals exclusive jurisdiction of justices of the peace over surveyors of public roads and grants circuit courts jurisdiction over such cases.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 187
statutes.title: The New Constitution of Kentucky
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 187
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky Constitution outlines provisions related to slavery, including the emancipation of slaves, restrictions on their presence in the state after emancipation, and the prevention of slave importation. It also grants power to the legislature to ensure the humane treatment of slaves by their owners.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 242
statutes.title: Liability for Conveying Slaves Out of State
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 242
statutes.summary: This statute establishes liability for steamboats and other vessels that transport slaves out of the state or from one part of the state to another without the owner's written consent, or without the owner or rightful controller of the slave being a passenger. It also makes the captain and owner personally liable. The statute explicitly mentions 'slaves,' indicating its context within the antebellum and immediate post-bellum period concerning enslaved people.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 243
statutes.title: An Act to Prevent the Removal of Slaves Out of This State
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 243
statutes.summary: This statute makes it illegal to transport a slave out of the state of Kentucky or from one point within the state to another on a boat. Violators face fines and/or imprisonment. The statute also outlines procedures for enforcing liens and liabilities related to such actions, including the use of attachments and bonds. Case law clarifies that the statute applies to slaves subject to Kentucky laws and not those escaping from other states.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 293
statutes.title: CONSTABLES.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 293
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the duties and responsibilities of constables in Kentucky, including their oath of office, the process for vacating their office, and the types of legal processes they are authorized to execute. Notably, it includes a provision stating that constables 'Shall whip slaves under the orders of justices of the peace.'

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 414
statutes.title: CRIMES AND PUNISHMENTS
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 414
statutes.summary: This section of the Revised Statutes of Kentucky (1867) outlines fees for commonwealth's attorneys based on fines assessed for various offenses, including gaming, operating a tippling house, and standing horses without a license. It also specifies how fines and forfeitures can be recovered. Crucially, Section XXVI states that the provisions of this chapter shall not apply to slaves, except where specifically named, nor to free negroes when punishment for the same offense is provided elsewhere in the Revised Statutes. This creates a differential application of criminal law based on race.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 415
statutes.title: Conspiracy of white person with negro.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 415
statutes.summary: This statute criminalizes a free white person who advises, counsels, or conspires with a negro (bond or free) to rebel or make insurrection against their master or the laws. The punishment is death or confinement in the penitentiary for six to ten years.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 419
statutes.title: Carnally knowing white girl under ten years, or an idiot. Abducting unmarried white girl under fourteen years. Taking or detaining white woman against her will, with intent to marry or carnally know.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 419
statutes.summary: This statute outlines criminal offenses related to sexual assault and abduction, specifically mentioning 'white girls' and 'white women'. It prescribes penalties for carnally knowing a white girl under ten or an idiot, abducting an unmarried white girl under fourteen, and taking or detaining a white woman against her will with intent to marry or have carnal knowledge. The explicit mention of 'white' in relation to victims suggests a racial distinction in the application of these laws, which is characteristic of Jim Crow era legislation that often codified racial hierarchies.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 441
statutes.title: Selling, purchasing, or removing from state negro entitled to freedom in future, without consent of court.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 441
statutes.summary: This statute prohibits the sale, purchase, or removal from Kentucky of any negro who is entitled to future freedom, without the consent of the county or circuit court. It specifies penalties including fines and imprisonment, and outlines the requirements for court authorization.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 450
statutes.title: Crimes and Punishments - Differential Penalties for Free Negroes and Slaves
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 450
statutes.summary: This section of the Revised Statutes of Kentucky (1867) outlines penalties for various offenses. Notably, it specifies differential punishments for 'free negroes' and 'slaves' compared to other persons for certain crimes, including the use of sickening or intoxicating substances and the killing, disfiguring, or maiming of animals. Free negroes and slaves could receive corporal punishment (stripes) where others would receive fines or imprisonment.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 454
statutes.title: An Act to amend the law in relation to Crimes and Punishments.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 454
statutes.summary: This act amends the Revised Statutes concerning arson and burning of buildings. It specifically addresses the willful and unlawful burning of vehicles by any person, whether white, free negro, slave, or other. It states that such an offender shall be punished in the same manner as prescribed for other arson offenses, with a specific provision that a slave offender shall be punished by any number of stripes not exceeding one hundred.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 581
statutes.title: Liability of owners, etc., for transporting slaves.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 581
statutes.summary: This statute imposes a significant financial penalty on ferry owners and keepers if they transport a slave across the Ohio River without the slave owner's explicit consent or accompaniment. The penalty is $200, and if the transport is done with the knowledge or assent of the ferry owner/keeper, the penalty increases to $1000, recoverable by any prosecutor. This indicates a legal framework that treated enslaved people as property and regulated their movement, reflecting the racial hierarchy of the time.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 597
statutes.title: FUGITIVES FROM JUSTICE. ARTICLE II. ARREST OF PERSONS FOR OFFENSES COMMITTED IN ANOTHER STATE OR TERRITORY.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 597
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for arresting and detaining individuals accused of felonies committed in other states or territories, and for dealing with persons accused of abducting people of color from Kentucky. Specifically, it requires judges to inquire into the ownership or agency of the accused in cases involving the abduction of a person of color, and to discharge the accused if they acted with the owner's sanction. Otherwise, they are to be dealt with according to the chapter's provisions. For felonies committed elsewhere, individuals found in Kentucky can be arrested and confined, then delivered to the proper authorities upon demand from the executive of the state or territory where the offense occurred.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 607
statutes.title: GAMING. - SEC. XXV. Fine for a white person gaming with a free negro or slave.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 607
statutes.summary: This section of the statutes imposes a fine of not more than fifty dollars on any white person who plays cards, dice, or any other game for money or other valuable thing with a free negro or slave. The fine is to be paid by the white person.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 611
statutes.title: An Act to amend the forty-second chapter of the Revised Statutes.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 611
statutes.summary: This act imposes penalties on free Black individuals for gaming with slaves or white persons, and on white persons for gaming with Black individuals or mulattoes. It also disqualifies white persons convicted of playing cards with Black individuals or mulattoes from holding office and serving on juries. Penalties include fines and imprisonment.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 612
statutes.title: GAMING. SEC. III. - SEC. V.
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, p. 612
statutes.summary: This statute criminalizes any free negro playing games with any white person, free negro, or slave. It also establishes a presumption of being a free man for those accused under this section, requiring rebuttal. An amendment clarifies that billiard tables for private family amusement are exempt.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 10, pp. 99–102
statutes.title: SEC. 10. And be it further enacted, That when any person held to service or labor in any state or territory, or in the district of Columbia, shall escape therefrom, the party to whom such service or labor shall be due, his, her, or their agent or attorney may apply to any court of record therein, or…
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 10, pp. 99–102
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for apprehending and returning fugitives from labor (enslaved people) to their state of origin. It details the evidence required for arrest, the authority of officers to use force to prevent rescue, and the compensation for officers and their assistants. The statute also specifies that a transcript of a court record, authenticated by the clerk and seal, serves as conclusive evidence of escape and the debt of service or labor in any other state.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 1, p. 140
statutes.title: SEC. 1. The general assembly shall have no power to pass laws for the emancipation of slaves, without the consent of their owners, or without paying their owners, previous to such emancipation, a full equivalent in money, for the slaves so emancipated. They shall have no power to prevent emigrants…
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 1, p. 140
The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 1, pp. 108–109
The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1887, § 1, pp. 107–108
The Kentucky Statutes, Third Edition, 1903, § 1, p. 78
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky Constitution outlines the powers of the General Assembly regarding slaves. It prohibits laws for emancipation without owner consent or compensation, allows emigrants to bring slaves, permits owners to emancipate slaves under certain conditions, and grants the assembly power to restrict slave importation. It also mandates laws for the humane treatment of slaves and allows for their sale if owners neglect this. Crucially, it states that grand juries are not necessary for prosecuting slaves for felony, though they retain the right to an impartial trial by a petit jury.

citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 1, pp. 188–189

Section 3 outlines that grand juries are not necessary for prosecuting slaves for felonies, but they retain the right to an impartial trial by a petit jury.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 23, pp. 185–186
statutes.title: SEC. 23. So long as the board of internal improvement shall be continued, the president thereof shall be elected by the qualified voters of this commonwealth, and hold the office for the term of four years, and until another be duly elected and qualified. The election shall be held at the same time…
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 23, pp. 185–186
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky Constitution prohibits the General Assembly from emancipating slaves without the consent of their owners or without paying them a full equivalent in money and providing for their removal from the state. It also allows immigrants to bring their slaves into the state.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 2, pp. 140–141

The Kentucky Statutes, Fourth Edition, 1909, § 2, p. 77
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky Constitution outlines the powers of the General Assembly regarding slaves. It prohibits laws for emancipation without owner consent or compensation, allows emigrants to bring slaves, permits owners to emancipate slaves under certain conditions, and grants the assembly power to restrict slave importation. It also mandates laws for the humane treatment of slaves and allows for their sale if owners neglect this. Crucially, it states that grand juries are not necessary for prosecuting slaves for felony, though they retain the right to an impartial trial by a petit jury.
