Section 3 outlines that grand juries are not necessary for prosecuting slaves for felonies, but they retain the right to an impartial trial by a petit jury.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 3, p. 93
statutes.title: SEC. 3. *And be it also enacted*, That when a person held to labor in any of the United States, or in either of the territories on the north-west or south of the river Ohio, under the laws thereof, shall escape into any other of the said states or territories, the person to whom such labor or…
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 3, p. 93
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for apprehending and returning fugitives from labor (enslaved people) to their rightful owners. It empowers agents to transport fugitives and imposes penalties on those who rescue or harbor them. The process involves presenting proof of ownership to a judge or magistrate, who then issues a certificate for removal.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 5, pp. 95–96
statutes.title: SEC. 5. *And be it further enacted*, That it shall be the duty of all marshals and deputy marshals to obey and execute all warrants and precepts issued under the provisions of this act, when to them directed; and should any marshal or deputy marshal refuse to receive such warrant, or other process…
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 5, pp. 95–96
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for reclaiming fugitives from labor. It grants commissioners concurrent jurisdiction with federal judges to issue certificates for the removal of such fugitives. It also mandates marshals and deputy marshals to execute warrants related to these fugitives, with penalties for refusal or escape. Commissioners are authorized to appoint individuals to execute these warrants and to summon bystanders or the posse comitatus for assistance.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 6, pp. 96–97
statutes.title: SEC. 6. And be it further enacted, That when a person held to service or labor in any state or territory of the United States, has heretofore or shall hereafter escape into another state or territory of the United States, the person or persons to whom such service or labor may be due, or his, her…
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 6, pp. 96–97
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for reclaiming individuals held to service or labor who have escaped into another state or territory. It details the procedures for obtaining warrants, seizing fugitives without process, and the duties of courts, judges, or commissioners in hearing and determining such cases. Proof of service or labor owed, and the identity of the claimant and fugitive, are required for the issuance of a certificate to the claimant.

statutes.statute_citation: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 8, p. 98
statutes.title: SEC. 8. *And be it further enacted*, That the marshals, their deputies, and the clerks of the said district and territorial courts, shall be paid for their services the like fees as may be allowed to them for similar services in other cases; and where such services are rendered exclusively in the…
citations: The Revised Statutes of Kentucky, v. 1, 1867, § 8, p. 98
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the fees and procedures for the arrest, custody, and delivery of fugitives from labor. It details the payment structure for marshals, deputies, clerks, and commissioners involved in these cases, specifying fees for services rendered in apprehending and examining supposed fugitives. The claimant, their agent, or attorney is responsible for these fees, regardless of the outcome of the examination.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1868, ch. 1016, pp. 470–478
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the several acts incorporating the Town of Williamstown, in Grant County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1868, ch. 1016, pp. 470–478
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1868, ch. 1016, pp. 472–480
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the Town of Williamstown and establishes a board of trustees. Section 3 explicitly states that the chairman and trustees shall be chosen from among the "freewhite citizensof said town".

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1868, ch. 805, pp. 275–276
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the Hancock County Court to levy additional Taxes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1868, ch. 805, pp. 275–276
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the Hancock County Court to levy additional taxes. Specifically, it allows for an additional ad valorem tax of eight cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property, an additional poll tax of one dollar on each white male over twenty-one years old, and a tax of two dollars on each negro or mulatto male over eighteen years old. The revenue from the white male poll tax and the negro/mulatto male poll tax is to be applied in the same manner as other taxes raised by law. The revenue from the first two sections (ad valorem and white male poll tax) is to be applied to the discharge of present indebtedness and current expenses of the county.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1868, p. 325
statutes.title: An Act to Amend the Charter of the Town of Versailles
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1868, p. 325
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1868, p. 327
statutes.summary: This section outlines the qualifications for voting in an election in Versailles, Kentucky. It specifies that only free white male citizens, aged twenty-one, who have resided in the state for two years and the town for one year, and who have paid their poll tax for the preceding year, are eligible to vote. It also details the process for examining poll books, determining election results, and handling contested elections and vacancies.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, ch. 288, pp. 457–458
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to establish a Work -house in Christian County," approved January 28, 1870.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, ch. 288, pp. 457–458
statutes.summary: This act establishes a work-house in Christian County, Kentucky. It mandates that individuals convicted of vagrancy in Christian County shall be confined in this work-house instead of the county jail. The court can adjudge confinement for a period not exceeding six months. The county court is authorized to make confined persons labor on streets and public highways, and to appoint a person to keep the work-house and employ guards. This provision takes effect upon the erection of the work-house.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, ch. 854, pp. 143–166
statutes.title: AN ACT to revise, amend, and reduce into one the laws relating to the Common Schools of Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, ch. 854, pp. 143–166
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for the Superintendent of Public Instruction to estimate and apportion state revenue for common schools. It specifies that the apportionment is based on the number of 'white children' between the ages of six and twenty. The statute also details how funds are allocated to districts and teachers, and how uncalled-for funds are reinvested. The explicit mention of 'white children' for apportionment is a key indicator of racial segregation in education.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, ch. 957, pp. 171–172
statutes.title: AN ACT to prevent sales of liquors to Negroes or Mulattoes on the Sabbath day.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, ch. 957, pp. 171–172
statutes.summary: This act prohibits the sale of liquor to Negroes or Mulattoes on the Sabbath day, citing concerns about intoxication, riotous behavior, and danger to public peace caused by large crowds congregating around stores and groceries.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, p. 59
statutes.title: AN ACT to impose an additional tax of fifteen cents for the purpose of increasing the Common School Fund.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, p. 59
statutes.summary: This act imposes an additional tax of fifteen cents per one hundred dollars of property value for the year 1870 and each succeeding year to increase the Common School Fund. Crucially, the tax is to be levied and collected from the property of white persons only. Furthermore, the revenue generated from this and previous acts for common school purposes shall be expended and appropriated for the education of white children exclusively. Any diversion of these funds for purposes other than the exclusive education of white children will cease the levying of this tax.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, pp. 677–699
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and reduce into one the several Acts in reference to the Town of Princeton. ARTICLE 1. town. Town Bounded.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1870, pp. 677–699
statutes.summary: This act outlines the qualifications for holding office and voting in the town of Hopkinsville. Specifically, Section 10 states that only 'free male white citizens' are qualified to hold office, and Section 14 defines voters as 'every free white male citizen'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, ch. 460, pp. 59–95
statutes.title: AN ACT establishing a New Charter for the City of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, ch. 460, pp. 59–95
statutes.summary: This statute mandates the segregation of public schools in Louisville, Kentucky. It explicitly states that children of the African race shall not be pupils with white children. Furthermore, it requires that school taxes paid by persons of the African race be kept as a separate fund and used exclusively for the education of African race children residing within the city or paying school tax there. The statute also outlines provisions for borrowing money for school expenses and eligibility requirements for school trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, ch. 481, pp. 125–153
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and reduce into one the several acts concerning the Town of Hopkinsville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, ch. 481, pp. 125–153
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the qualifications for voting in city elections for Hopkinsville. It explicitly states that only 'white male citizens' are eligible to vote for councilman, city marshal, or judge of the city court. Additional requirements include residency, payment of taxes, and satisfaction of fines.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, ch. 594, pp. 222–223
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the County Court of Trigg County to dispose of the Curling Fund, and for other purposes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, ch. 594, pp. 222–223
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the town trustees of Cadiz to levy and collect an ad valorem tax of fifty cents per one hundred dollars on taxable property belonging to white citizens for the years 1870, 1871, and 1872. The collected funds, along with the common school fund, are to be used for building a suitable school-house for common school purposes. The school trustees must execute a bond for the faithful appropriation of these funds.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, ch. 932, pp. 664–669
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish and maintain a Public School in the Town of Bowling Green.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, ch. 932, pp. 664–669
statutes.summary: This act establishes a public school in Bowling Green for white children aged six to twenty. It empowers the chairman and board of trustees to levy a tax on taxable property belonging to white persons to fund the school. The act also outlines the election and terms of school trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, p. 349
statutes.title: An Act to Amend the Charter of the Town of Brandenburg
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1870, p. 349
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of the town of Brandenburg, outlining the election of trustees, their powers, the duties of the town marshal, and the imposition of taxes. Crucially, it specifies that the poll tax is levied on "all white males over twenty-one years of age, resident of said town," and explicitly states, "Colored persons are not embraced herein."

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1160, p. 228
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to School District No. 14, in Simpson County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1160, p. 228
statutes.summary: This act designates School District No. 14 in Simpson County to encompass the entire town of Franklin. It specifies that only schools taught by regularly qualified white persons will be considered common schools. The trustees are required to report the number of white pupils of common school age attending these schools and to pro rata the school fund among these schools based on the number of white pupils attending each.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1170, pp. 231–233
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the erection of School Buildings in the Town of Cloverport.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1170, pp. 231–233
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the board of trustees of a town to issue bonds for the purpose of acquiring real estate and erecting school buildings. It also empowers them to levy taxes to pay for the interest and redemption of these bonds. Crucially, it explicitly states that only the property of white persons shall be taxed for these purposes, and that an increase in per capita tax shall apply to white persons only.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1233, p. 47
statutes.title: AN ACT to repeal an act, entitled " An act for the benefit of the Negroes and Mulattoes of this Commonwealth," approved March 9, 1867.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1233, p. 47
statutes.summary: This act repeals a previous act that provided benefits to Negroes and Mulattoes. It then states that Negroes and Mulattoes will be taxed the same per capita and on real and personal estate as the white population, with no additional taxes. This effectively removes any special provisions or benefits previously afforded to Black individuals and places them under the same tax structure as white citizens, while explicitly mentioning racial groups.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1241, pp. 301–302
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An actto amend an act to in corpо- rate the Town of West Point, in Hardin County," approved February 15th, 1848.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1241, pp. 301–302
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of the town of West Point by authorizing the election of a police judge and empowering the trustees to build a lockup. Crucially, Section 2 states that Section 5 of a previous amendment shall apply to the colored as well as the white population, implying that previous provisions may have been race-specific. The lockup is for confining individuals convicted of violating town ordinances and failing to pay fines, with a daily confinement rate.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1256, pp. 320–367
statutes.title: AN ACT revising the Charter of the City of Paducah.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1256, pp. 320–367
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the eligibility requirements for serving on the Common Council of the city of Paducah. Specifically, it states that a councilman must be a 'white male citizen of the United States,' among other qualifications related to age, residency, property ownership, and holding other offices. It also details conditions under which a council member's office would be vacated.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1335, pp. 433–437
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Town of Sebree City, in Webster County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1335, pp. 433–437
statutes.summary: This act amends the incorporation of the town of Madisonville. Section 7 explicitly states that all officers of the town, including the police judge, town marshal, and five trustees, "shall be white males over twenty-one years old, and residents of said town." This racial qualification for holding public office is a hallmark of Jim Crow legislation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1340, pp. 438–440
statutes.title: AN ACT to create the Office of Superintendent of the Negro Paupers of Mercer County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1340, pp. 438–440
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the county court of Mercer County to appoint a superintendent to care for, manage, and control the negro paupers within the county.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1343, pp. 444–446
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the Charter of the City of Newport.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1343, pp. 444–446
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of the City of Newport, establishing requirements for its police force. Specifically, it states that police officers must be 'white citizens of the United States' and residents of the city for one year preceding their election. The act also outlines the election process for the police force by a board of police commissioners.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1368, pp. 456–457
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the Town of Tompkinsville, in Monroe County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1368, pp. 456–457
statutes.summary: This act allows for the election of town officials in Tompkinsville, Kentucky. It specifies eligibility requirements for these offices, explicitly stating that only white persons aged twenty-one or older, who have resided in the town for twelve months, are eligible for the positions of police judge, trustee, town marshal, or town attorney. An exception is made for the town attorney, who must also be a licensed practicing lawyer in Kentucky for at least two years.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1419, pp. 498–514
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the City of Ludlow.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1419, pp. 498–514
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for tax assessment in the city of Louisville. A key provision requires the assessor to take an accurate list of all children between specified ages, distinguishing between male and female, and between white and colored children. This explicit racial distinction in the collection of data for school children indicates a segregationist intent.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1472, pp. 548–549
statutes.title: AN ACT authorizing the Trustees of School District No. 2, in Hickman County, to levy and collect a Tax for School purposes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1472, pp. 548–549
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of School District No. 2 in Hickman County to levy and collect taxes for school purposes. It specifically allows for a poll tax to be levied on every inhabitant over six years old, with an explicit exemption for 'negroes'. The remainder of the necessary funds is to be raised through taxes on personal and real estate.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1478, pp. 553–554
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a Public School for Colored Children in the City of Henderson.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1478, pp. 553–554
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the mayor and council of Henderson to levy a tax of two dollars on every male negro or mulatto over eighteen years old and a property tax on all negroes and mulattoes resident in the city. The proceeds from these taxes are to fund the education of Black children in the city.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1483, pp. 80–82
statutes.title: AN ACT to cause good School-houses to be erected in the Eighth and Ninth Congressional Districts. School -houses to be built in common school districts in the 8th and 9th Congr es-
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1483, pp. 80–82
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning common schools. Section 10 explicitly states that the provisions of this act shall not apply to negroes and mulattoes. Section 11 exempts specific counties from the act's provisions.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1926, p. 121
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to establish a State House of Reform for Juvenile Delinquents," approved February 15th, 1869.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, ch. 1926, p. 121
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law establishing a State House of Reform for juvenile delinquents. It mandates that all white male and female persons between the ages of eight and seventeen, convicted of vagrancy, petit larceny, or any crime less than murder, shall be committed to this House of Reform. It also specifies that females will not be committed until the Governor announces that provisions have been made for their care in the institution.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, pp. 469–470
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the Trustees of Common School District No. 1, in Logan County, to levy and collect a tax for the purpose of erecting Common School Buildings in said District.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1871, pp. 469–470
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of Common School District No. 1 in Logan County to hold an election for qualified white voters to decide on levying a tax on taxable property belonging to white persons. The purpose of this tax is to purchase land and erect a schoolhouse exclusively for the use and benefit of white pupils in the district. The tax is capped at one dollar per hundred dollars of taxable property and a total of four thousand dollars.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1515, pp. 60–66
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of Public Schools in the City of Owensboro for White Children in said City.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1515, pp. 60–66
statutes.summary: This act establishes a public school system specifically for white children in the city of Owensboro, Kentucky.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1637, pp. 180–183
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the City of Dayton, in Campbell County, to establish Common School System.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1637, pp. 180–183
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the city of Dayton, Kentucky, to establish a common school system. It specifies that any tax levied for this purpose shall only be applied to the property of white persons, and that only qualified white voters shall be allowed to vote on the proposition to levy such a tax.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1745, p. 334
statutes.title: AN ACT authorizing the County Court for the County of Muhlenburg to release James C. Moorman from his bond, whereby a negro girl, Caroline, was apprenticed to him.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1745, p. 334
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the Muhlenburg County Court to release James C. Moorman from a bond related to the apprenticeship of a negro girl named Caroline, if equity and justice require it for both master and apprentice.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1851, pp. 419–422
statutes.title: AN ACT for the better organization of Public Schools in Elizabethtown, and to establish the Common School District of Elizabethtown, in Hardin County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1851, pp. 419–422
statutes.summary: This act allows the town of Elizabethtown to levy a tax on the property of 'whites' in a specific district to fund a board of education for that district. It also outlines the election and powers of this board.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1945, pp. 525–530
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act to amend and reduce into one the several acts concerning the Town of Hopkinsville," approved March 5th,1870.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1871, ch. 1945, pp. 525–530
statutes.summary: This act amends several sections of a previous act concerning the city of Hopkinsville. Specifically, it modifies the qualifications for the judge of the Hopkinsville city court, requiring the individual to be a 'white male citizen of the United States, and of the State of Kentucky,' at least twenty-four years old, and a licensed practicing lawyer for two years, and a resident of the city for two years. It also outlines the duties of the chairman of the board of councilmen to preside as judge pro tempore if the judge is absent or fails to preside.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 127, pp. 246–248
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the town of Carlisle, in Nicholas county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 127, pp. 246–248
statutes.summary: This act allows the town of Carlisle to vote on a school tax, but explicitly exempts the property of negroes from being taxed for this purpose. It also outlines procedures for submitting such propositions to qualified white voters and for collecting the tax.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 191, pp. 301–306
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of public schools in the town of Madisonville, county of Hopkins.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 191, pp. 301–306
statutes.summary: This act outlines the establishment and management of public schools in Madisonville. Section 11 explicitly states that 'All white children between the age of six and twenty years, within each district, shall have equal rights of admission to the schools of said district.' This explicit racial classification for school admission is a hallmark of Jim Crow segregation in education.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 314, pp. 416–426
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and reduce into one all the acts in regard to the town of Columbia.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 314, pp. 416–426
statutes.summary: This act amends and consolidates previous laws concerning the town of Columbia. It establishes the town's boundaries, vests its governance in seven annually elected trustees, and outlines their qualifications and duties. Crucially, it specifies that only 'white citizens' who are qualified electors and have resided in the town for at least twelve months are eligible to be trustees. The act also details the election process for trustees, requiring them to be legally qualified male inhabitants over twenty-one years of age who have been bona fide residents for six months.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 318, pp. 427–428
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act for the benefit of common school districts in Clinton county."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 318, pp. 427–428
statutes.summary: This act amends existing laws regarding common schools. Specifically, it outlines the process for condemning land for school sites and explicitly states that the provisions of this act and its amendment shall apply only to white persons, excluding negroes and mulattoes from its benefits.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 361, pp. 462–463
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the trustees of the Washington Scientific School, in Mason county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 361, pp. 462–463
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the trustees of the Washington Scientific School in Mason County, Kentucky. Section 2 explicitly states that the object of the corporation shall be the building and sustaining of an educational institution of a high grade, exclusively for the white race.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 380, p. 472
statutes.title: AN ACT authorizing the trustees of Bardstown to levy a tax for the purpose of purchasing a school-house.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 380, p. 472
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of Bardstown to purchase grounds and erect buildings for school purposes, not exceeding five thousand dollars. To fund this, they can issue bonds and levy a tax not exceeding twenty-five cents per one hundred dollars valuation of real and personal property owned by white citizens. The question of levying this tax must be submitted to the qualified white voters of the town. The purchased or erected school property is to be used for the education of white children exclusively.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 389, p. 489
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Maysville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 389, p. 489
statutes.summary: This act requires the collector of taxes for Maysville to return an annual list of delinquent taxpayers to the city council. Individuals who have not paid their taxes by the first Thursday in December are ineligible to vote in the next city election. The city clerk must provide election officials with a copy of this delinquent list, and they are prohibited from allowing anyone on the list to vote. Penalties are established for officials who fraudulently alter tax receipts or delinquent lists to enable unqualified individuals to vote.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 392, pp. 493–494
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Paducab.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 392, pp. 493–494
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of the city of Paducah, allowing the common council to levy a city tax for the support and maintenance of common schools. The tax rate is specified for different years. Crucially, it includes a proviso stating that taxes levied for common schools shall not be levied upon the property of colored citizens of said city.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 412, pp. 509–511
statutes.title: AN ACT authorizing the trustees of common school district No. 4, in Mc- Crack en county, to levy and collect a tax for the erection of school buildings.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 412, pp. 509–511
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the qualified white voters of a specified district to vote on levying a tax on taxable property belonging to white persons to purchase land and build a schoolhouse exclusively for white pupils. The tax amount and duration are to be determined by trustees, with limitations on the total cost and tax rate. The act also details the election process, tax collection, and the appointment of commissioners for the purchase and construction.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 414, pp. 511–514
statutes.title: AN ACT to charter the Eddyville Male and Female Academy, in Lyon county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 414, pp. 511–514
statutes.summary: This act amends existing common school laws. Section 14 explicitly states that 'None but white children shall be permitted to attend the school provided for in this act.' This indicates a racially segregated educational system.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 520, pp. 637–641
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of public schools in the city of Hopkinsville for white children in said city.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 520, pp. 637–641
statutes.summary: This act establishes a public school district for the city of Hopkinsville, to be managed by a board of trustees. Crucially, the title explicitly states that this system is for 'white children in said city,' indicating a racially segregated educational system.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 521, pp. 641–642
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to organize and establish a system of public schools in the city of Owensboro for white children in said city," approved March 13th,1871.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, ch. 521, pp. 641–642
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning public schools in Owensboro. It specifically changes the school age for white children to over seven years old and authorizes the mayor and common council to issue bonds for school grounds and buildings, with a limit on the additional amount. It also details the capitation tax and annual tax authorized to be levied on white male citizens.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, p. 351
statutes.title: AN ACT authorizing the sale of the Henry county poor-house farm, and the purchase of a smaller lot of ground, with suitable buildings, for the accommodation of the white paupers of said county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1872, p. 351
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the sale of the Henry County poor-house farm and the purchase of a smaller lot with suitable buildings for the accommodation of 'white paupers'. Commissioners are appointed to manage the sale, purchase, and removal of inmates and property. The proceeds from the sale are to be used for the benefit of the poorhouse inmates.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 593, pp. 84–86
statutes.title: AN ACT providing for levying a tax in aid of common schools in Greenup, Boyd, and Carter counties.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 593, pp. 84–86
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning the organization of common schools in Greenup, Boyd, and Carter counties. Specifically, it exempts 'Negroes and mulattoes' from assessments and levies for school construction under this act, stating they are exempt from its operation and benefits. The act also limits the maximum levy for schoolhouse erection to six hundred dollars per district and specifies that assessments shall be made upon the property of white persons only. It applies only to the counties of Greenup, Boyd, and Carter.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 594, pp. 86–91
statutes.title: AN ACT for the better organization of the public schools in the town of Carrollton, and to establish the common school district of Carrollton, in Carroll county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 594, pp. 86–91
statutes.summary: This act establishes a board of trustees for the Carrollton public schools, granting them control over management, property, and funds. It specifies that only white children between the ages of six and twenty, who are bona fide residents of the district, are eligible for admission and that no tuition fees will be charged for required common school studies. The act explicitly states that only white children are to be admitted to these schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 597, pp. 92–94
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish an institution of learning in the town of Hardinsville, in Shelby county, to be known as the Lee Academy.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 597, pp. 92–94
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the establishment and operation of academies, including provisions for capital stock, curriculum, principal qualifications, and the levying of taxes. Crucially, it explicitly states that only white persons shall vote in tax elections and that the property of negroes shall be exempt from such taxation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 758, pp. 244–250
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a system of common schools in the town of Corydon, Henderson county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 758, pp. 244–250
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for levying and collecting taxes to pay for school bonds and expenses. It specifies that the tax will be levied on property within the school district that is also taxed by the state for common school purposes. A crucial provision states that 'only the property belonging to white persons shall be taxed.' The statute also details the roles of the assessor, collector, and the board of trustees, including penalties for delinquency.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 835, pp. 316–317
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of Elizabethtown.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 835, pp. 316–317
statutes.summary: This act allows for a vote on a town tax for common school purposes. If approved by a majority of white voters, a tax will be levied on the taxable estate of white persons and a poll tax on white males over twenty-one. The funds are to be used for school buildings and teachers' salaries for common schools taught under state law.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 898, pp. 417–418
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of school district No. 60, in Scott county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 898, pp. 417–418
statutes.summary: This act allows for the taxation of property to fund schoolhouses in districts where voters approve it. Crucially, it explicitly states that the property of colored people shall not be taxed for these purposes, nor shall they be allowed to vote on the proposition to levy such a tax.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 901, pp. 419–421
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of school district No. 1, of Ohio county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 901, pp. 419–421
statutes.summary: This act places school district No. 1 of Ohio County under the control of the trustees of the town of Hartford. These trustees are empowered to levy and collect an annual tax not exceeding fifty cents per one hundred dollars of property and not exceeding two dollars per capita. Crucially, these taxes are to be levied and collected of white citizens only. The collected funds are to be appropriated for teachers' wages and school buildings.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 965, pp. 500–501
statutes.title: AN ACT empowering the trustees of common schools in Campbell county to levy taxes for the purpose of buying lands, building, repairing, and furnishing school-houses.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1872, ch. 965, pp. 500–501
statutes.summary: This act allows for local taxation to fund schoolhouses in specific districts. It explicitly states that only legally qualified white voters can vote in elections for this tax, and only the property of white persons will be taxed for school purposes under this act.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 1055, pp. 587–588
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the education of colored children in Garrard county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 1055, pp. 587–588
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 1055, pp. 587–588
statutes.summary: This act directs the county commissioner of common schools in Garrard county to lay off the county into suitable school districts for colored children. It specifies the number of children per district, mandates the election of colored trustees by qualified colored voters, and empowers these trustees to provide school-houses and employ teachers for colored children. Parents are to be notified of their privilege to send their children to these schools free of charge.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 1072, pp. 596–597
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of common school district No. 1, in Pendleton county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 1072, pp. 596–597
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 1072, pp. 596–597
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of common school district No. 1 in Pendleton County to levy and collect a tax to pay off a debt for their schoolhouse. It also specifies that the act shall not be construed to allow any person or persons of color to vote.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 478, pp. 72–75
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act to create the Hartford Seminary, of Ohio county."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 478, pp. 72–75
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 478, pp. 72–75
statutes.summary: This act outlines the establishment and governance of graded school districts in Kentucky. It details the powers and duties of trustees, including levying taxes on "white persons" and property belonging to "white persons" to fund school expenses. The act also specifies that funds raised from taxation and private donations are to be kept separate from state school funds until seminary buildings are procured. It mandates that the tax shall not be assessed unless ratified by a majority of votes cast in an election.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 565, pp. 151–152
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Cold Spring school district, in Campbell county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 565, pp. 151–152
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 565, pp. 151–152
statutes.summary: This act allows the trustees of Cold Spring schooldistrict in Campbell County to submit to qualified white voters the question of levying a per capita tax of $1.50 on each white male citizen over 21 and an ad valorem tax of $0.50 per $100 of taxable property belonging to white persons. The funds raised are for purchasing land and erecting or purchasing a schoolhouse. The election is to be held after public notice, and if a majority of votes favor the tax, it will be levied.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 591, pp. 176–177
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of school district No. 34, in Garrard county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 591, pp. 176–177
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 591, pp. 176–177
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of common school district No. 34 in Garrard County to hold an election to determine if a tax should be levied on taxable property owned by white persons to fund the construction or repair of a schoolhouse. The tax would not exceed fifty cents on the hundred dollars of taxable property for any one year, until a sufficient amount is collected, not to exceed four hundred dollars.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 607, p. 186
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Peter Perry, committee of John Perry (of color), a pauper idiot of Hart county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 607, p. 186
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the Auditor of Public Accounts to draw a warrant for Peter Perry, committee of John Perry, a pauper idiot of Hart county. The amount due is for the period of November 1st, 1871, to January 10th, 1873. The Auditor had previously refused to pay this amount because John Perry was identified as a negro.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 616, pp. 189–195
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize Urania school district, in Barren county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 616, pp. 189–195
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 616, pp. 189–195
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning common schools in Barren County. It mandates that if a district votes for taxation, the trustees must designate the duration of the tax. Crucially, it requires that a vote be held on a two-dollar capitation tax for each white male citizen over twenty-one years old, to be collected and added to the school fund. The funds are to be used for teaching common schools, with provisions for separate male and female schools if funds allow, and for tuition at Urania College and Allen Lodge Female College.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 649, pp. 219–221
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the erection of school buildings in common school district No. 1, in the town of Hawesville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 649, pp. 219–221
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 649, pp. 219–221
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the board of trustees of Hawesville's District No. 1 to levy taxes for educational purposes. Crucially, it explicitly states that 'only the property and poll of white persons shall be taxed for the purposes of this act.' This indicates a racially segregated funding mechanism for education, where only white residents contribute to and benefit from the tax-funded schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 653, pp. 226–227
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a common school for the benefit of the colored people of Catlettsburg and vicinity.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 653, pp. 226–227
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 653, pp. 226–227
statutes.summary: This act establishes a common school for the benefit of the 'colored people' of Catlettsburg and its vicinity, to be known as the Catlettsburg common school. It defines the district boundaries and outlines the election of five trustees by qualified colored voters and widows with children of school age. These trustees have exclusive control of the school, can sue and be sued, and are empowered to assess a poll tax of up to two dollars on each colored male over eighteen and widows with children of school age within the district to fund the school.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 662, pp. 233–240
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize the Morganfield Public School.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 662, pp. 233–240
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 662, pp. 233–240
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law concerning public schools in Union County. Specifically, it states that only property belonging to white persons shall be taxed for common school purposes within the school district. It also outlines the collection and use of these funds, as well as penalties for misuse.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 678, pp. 257–261
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for organizing and establishing a system of public schools in Winchester.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 678, pp. 257–261
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 678, pp. 257–261
statutes.summary: This act establishes a system of common schools in Winchester, Kentucky. It mandates separate schools for white and colored children and requires separate voting places and separate tax levies based on the votes of each racial group for school funding. The act explicitly mentions 'white children' and 'children of color' and 'negro voters'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 697, p. 272
statutes.title: AN ACT to facilitate the collection of delinquent taxes in Owen county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 697, p. 272
statutes.summary: This act allows the city of Bowling Green to levy taxes for specific purposes, with a provision that any previously imposed taxes on persons of African descent (negroes and mulattoes) for this city are repealed. It also requires a vote of approval from the colored voters of Bowling Green before any new tax can be assessed under this act.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 711, pp. 282–283
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Mildred Broadus, a pauper idiot, of Lincoln county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 711, pp. 282–283
statutes.summary: This act appropriates fifty dollars to W. H. Miller for the support of a negro pauper idiot, Mildred Broadus, for one year.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 793, pp. 344–345
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and reduce into one the several acts relating to Stanford Female College.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 793, pp. 344–345
statutes.summary: This act allows the town of Stanford to make additional subscriptions to the capital stock of the Stanford Female College. In return, the college may issue free scholarships to meritorious indigent white girls in the town. The act also grants the trustees the power to confer degrees and fix tuition fees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 829, pp. 373–374
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of school district No. 30 (thirty), in Butlercounty.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 829, pp. 373–374
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 829, pp. 373–374
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law regarding a school tax in Butler County. It specifies that the tax will only be levied upon the property of white citizens or residents of the district and that only white persons qualified to vote are entitled to vote on the adoption or rejection of this act. The tax collection process is also detailed.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 847, pp. 388–393
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act giving the trustees of the common school district in Catlettsburg the right to levy a tax for two years to build a school-house in said district," approved March 5th, 1872, and to establish and maintain a public school in the town of Catlettsburg.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 847, pp. 388–393
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 847, pp. 388–393
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law to allow the town of Catlettsburg to levy a tax for establishing and maintaining a public school. Crucially, it specifies that the tax is to be levied on taxable property belonging to white persons only, explicitly stating that 'negroes or their property are not subject to taxation for the purposes of this act.' The funds collected, along with other sources, will form a school fund for white children.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 873, pp. 414–415
statutes.title: AN ACT to impose additional tax on dogs in Bracken county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 873, pp. 414–415
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 873, pp. 414–415
statutes.summary: This act imposes a tax on dogs in Bracken county, with different rates for housekeepers and non-housekeepers, and for female dogs. Crucially, it requires the assessor to keep separate lists of dogs owned by white persons and colored persons, and the sheriff to report the tax collected from each group separately. The collected taxes are to be distributed equally among school districts to aid schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 910, pp. 444–446
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Maysville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 910, pp. 444–446
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 910, pp. 444–446
statutes.summary: This act grants the city council of Louisville the power to purchase real estate and establish a union public graded school. It also explicitly authorizes the council to establish and govern public schools for colored children, including levying taxes upon the persons and property of colored people at the same rate as for white people, and prescribing the number of colored trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 916, pp. 456–457
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of common school district No. 1, in Lawrence county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 916, pp. 456–457
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 916, pp. 456–457
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of a specific school district in Lawrence County to levy taxes for school purposes. It explicitly states that the property of negroes shall not be taxed and that no poll or capitation tax shall be assessed upon persons of African descent. Funds collected from poll taxes (from those not of African descent) are to be used for erecting or purchasing a schoolhouse.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 997, pp. 538–542
statutes.title: AN ACT for the organization of the public schools in the town of Clayville, in Webster county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 997, pp. 538–542

statutes.summary: This statute outlines the organization and operation of common schools in Kentucky. Section 10 explicitly states that only white children are eligible for admission to these schools. Section 14, regarding taxation for school purposes, exempts property owned by colored persons from taxation for school levies.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 998, pp. 542–543
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish schools for the education of children of citizens of African descent in McCracken county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, ch. 998, pp. 542–543
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 998, pp. 542–543
statutes.summary: This act establishes a fund for the education of Black children in McCracken County by levying an annual tax. The tax includes twenty cents on each one hundred dollars' worth of property owned by persons of color in McCracken County subject to state revenue, and a poll tax of one dollar on each Black male resident over eighteen years of age.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, p. 271
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a colored free school at Bowling Green.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, p. 271
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the city of Bowling Green to levy a special tax on males of African descent over 21 years old and on property owned by persons of African descent to fund a free school for colored children between the ages of six and twenty years. It also establishes a board of trustees to manage these funds and oversee the school's establishment and support. Additionally, it directs the Warren county judge to appoint a commissioner to determine the city's share of a previously collected 'negro fund'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, pp. 557–559
statutes.title: AN ACT to charter the public schools of Falmouth and district No. 1, in Pendleton county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1873, pp. 557–559
statutes.summary: This act charters the public schools of Falmouth and an adjacent district, authorizing the establishment, support, and maintenance of a system of public schools adequate for all children applying for instruction. It specifies that the schools shall be under the control of a board of three trustees, elected annually by qualified white voters. The trustees are empowered to provide schoolhouses and schools for white children, and the board is created as a corporate body with exclusive control over school property and funds, which are dedicated to the purposes of these schools and are exempt from debt and taxes. The board is also responsible for fixing school terms, appointing examiners for teachers, and overseeing school operations.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 885, pp. 421–426
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish and incorporate the town of Stroud City, in Muhlenburg county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 885, pp. 421–426
statutes.summary: This act establishes and incorporates the town of Stroud City in Muhlenburg County. It outlines the town's boundaries, the election of five trustees annually, and their powers and duties. Crucially, it specifies that only a 'free white male person over the age of twenty-one years' is eligible to be a trustee.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 986, p. 529
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of school district No. 17, in Garrard county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1873, ch. 986, p. 529
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of school district No. 17 in Garrard County to levy a tax on taxable property listed by white persons to fund the construction of a schoolhouse. The tax is not to exceed fifty cents on the hundred dollars annually, and the total collected should not exceed seven hundred dollars. All property listed for state revenue within the district is subject to distraint for this tax. The sheriff is to collect the tax and pay it to the trustees, retaining a commission. The trustees must execute a bond for their duties.

It also establishes a board of trustees to manage these funds and oversee the school's establishment and support. statutes.summary: This statute outlines the qualifications and procedures for grand and petit juries in Kentucky. Specifically, it states that only white male citizens who are housekeepers over the age of twenty-one are qualified to serve as grand jurors. It also lists several disqualifications, including civil officers, surveyors, mill owners, tavern keepers, and those who have recently stood a horse, jack, or bull for reward. The statute details the number of grand jurors to be summoned, the process for summoning them, and penalties for non-attendance. It also covers the appointment of a foreman and the oath administered to grand jurors.

The form of this book is to be the same as the general tax book, with the only change being the substitution of the word 'white' with terms appropriate to the case, implying a distinct and separate classification for taxation purposes based on race. This establishes a racial distinction in the tax assessment process.

citations: The General Statutes of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1873, § 1, p. 92
statutes.summary: This section of the First Constitution of Kentucky outlines the powers of the Legislature regarding emancipation of slaves. It states that the Legislature cannot emancipate slaves without the consent of their owners or without paying them a full equivalent in money. It also addresses the right of emigrants to bring slaves into the state, the power to prevent slaves from being brought in as merchandise or from foreign countries, and the power to pass laws requiring owners to treat slaves humanely, provide for them, and abstain from injury. It also allows for the sale of slaves if owners neglect these duties.

statutes.summary: This act reorganizes and re-establishes various charitable institutions in Kentucky, including lunatic asylums. It renames the Eastern Lunatic Asylum to the First Kentucky Lunatic Asylum and the Western Lunatic Asylum to the Second Kentucky Lunatic Asylum. Section 23 of the original statute, which is included in the provided text, explicitly segregates white lunatics based on their county of residence, directing them to either the Western or Eastern Lunatic Asylum. This segregation based on geographic location, while not explicitly naming Black individuals, implies a racial separation in the allocation of care for white individuals, which is a hallmark of Jim Crow-era policies that often created separate and unequal systems.

The Superintendent of Public Instruction is tasked with estimating the net revenue and calculating the pro rata share for each white child, county, and district based on the number of white children between the ages of six and twenty.

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 154, pp. 224–228
statutes.summary: This act amends the law regarding graded common schools. Section 17 specifically states that only property belonging to white persons shall be taxed for the purpose of levying and collecting taxes for these schools. This explicitly creates a racially discriminatory tax system for school funding.

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 205, pp. 285–288
statutes.summary: This act incorporates a specific territory as a school district in Owingsville, Bath County, to be managed by a board of five trustees. Crucially, it specifies that trustees are to be elected annually by 'legally qualified white voters' and any 'white widow' entitled to vote. This explicit racial qualification for voting in school board elections is a hallmark of Jim Crow era segregation in education.

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 287, p. 68
statutes.summary: This act converts the State House of Reform for Juvenile Delinquents into the Central Kentucky Lunatic Asylum. It appropriates $100,000 for the construction of separate facilities for colored lunatics and additional accommodations for white individuals. The act mandates that colored lunatics be kept separate and apart from white lunatics.

It explicitly states that the public schools are to be maintained for 'all white children residing in said city, between the ages of six and twenty years'. This segregation of educational facilities based on race is a hallmark of Jim Crow laws.

The act is effective upon passage.

The tax collection is also explicitly limited to property belonging to white persons.

The tax rates are specified, and the collection and disbursement of funds are outlined, including the appointment and duties of a board of trustees for the colored school.

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 494, pp. 100–101
statutes.summary: This act amends several sections of Kentucky law, primarily related to the timing of elections, appointments, and financial distributions within educational contexts. Notably, it explicitly amends Article Seven, Section One to refer to 'the qualified white voters of the district' instead of 'county,' and Article Seven, Section Eight to specify 'a majority of the white qualified voters of such district.' These changes indicate a racial qualification for participation in district matters, likely related to school governance or funding.

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 495, pp. 590–592

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 521, pp. 102–105
statutes.summary: This act establishes a separate and distinct system of common schools for the education of colored children in Kentucky. It outlines the funding sources for this 'colored school fund,' which include specific taxes on colored persons, capitation taxes on colored males, taxes on dogs owned by colored persons, state taxes collected from colored persons, and fines/penalties collected from colored persons.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 533, pp. 633–634

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 533, pp. 633–634
statutes.summary: This act allows common school trustees in a district where Eminence College is located to subscribe to its capital stock. If they do, the county judge is authorized to levy a tax on the property of *white* tax-payers of the district to pay for this subscription. The college, in turn, must agree to teach common schools for *white* children in that district and receive public money for it. The act also specifies that the sense of *white* qualified voters must be taken before any subscription is made.

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 58, p. 168

Violators are subject to penalties prescribed in a previous act.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 592, pp. 698–701

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 592, pp. 698–701
statutes.summary: This act amends the establishment and regulation of public schools in Ashland. It grants the board of education the power to levy taxes for school purposes, including purchasing property, erecting buildings, and paying teachers. Notably, Section 16 explicitly states that only property belonging to white persons shall be taxed. Section 12 also mentions a poll-tax not to exceed one dollar on each white tithin in the district. Section 19 allows the admission of white children who are non-residents under certain conditions. Section 20 states the tax will not be levied until submitted to legally qualified white voters.

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, p. 121
statutes.summary: This resolution directs the Governor to manage the overflow of pauper lunatics in Kentucky's asylums. It explicitly states that the asylum for colored lunatics is full, and the asylums for white lunatics are nearly full. The resolution mandates that colored and white lunatics shall not be kept in the same buildings, indicating a policy of racial segregation in the care of the mentally ill.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 212, pp. 382–388

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 212, pp. 382–388

The control and management of this new district will be by a board of five trustees. Crucially, these trustees are to be elected annually by qualified white voters and any white widow entitled to a vote. This explicitly limits voting rights for school board elections to white individuals.
