citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 338, pp. 544–545
statutes.summary: This act addresses a specific financial shortfall for colored common schools in Trimble County. It details how a colored schoolteacher, Maria F. Carter, was not paid for her services due to a failure in the reporting process by school officials. The act aims to rectify this by ensuring funds are allocated for her unpaid services.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 381, p. 577
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Thomas Shanks, sheriff of the county of Jefferson.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 381, p. 577
statutes.summary: This act allows Thomas Shanks, sheriff of Jefferson County, an extension to submit his delinquent list of 'negro tax' for the year 1874. If approved by the county court of claims and certified to the Auditor, the Auditor is authorized to allow Shanks credit for this amount on his 'negro tax' list for either 1875.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 390, pp. 586–628
statutes.title: AN ACT to reduce into one all the acts relating to the city of Owensboro. ARTICLE 1.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 390, pp. 586–628
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the taxing authority of the City of Owensboro for municipal purposes, including specific taxes for railroad bonds and public schools. Crucially, it explicitly states that taxes for school purposes can only be levied on white persons and corporations, while exempting the property of negroes from all taxes connected with public schools. It also specifies a separate capitation tax for white males for school expenses.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 76, pp. 269–270
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the public schools of the city of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 76, pp. 269–270
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the city of Louisville to levy an annual tax for five years to fund public schools for white children. The tax is to be levied on real estate, improvements, mixed property, and personal property exceeding the owner's debts. The funds are to be credited to the school fund and paid to the board of trustees of the Male High School, Female High School, and public schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 900, pp. 136–149
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and reduce into one the several acts organizing and regulating the lunatic asylums of this State.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 900, pp. 136–149
statutes.summary: This act establishes separate admission districts for white and colored lunatics and idiots to the Eastern, Central, and Western Kentucky Lunatic Asylums. It specifies which counties' residents of each race are to be sent to which asylum, with provisions for overflow.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 514, pp. 199–202
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act to amend and reduce into one the several acts in relation to the town of Danville," approved March 10th, 1873.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 514, pp. 199–202
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the board of trustees to purchase land for a cemetery and issue bonds for its payment. It explicitly states that a tax will be levied on property owned by white persons to pay the interest on these bonds. Furthermore, it mandates that lots in the cemetery be sold to and used by white persons only.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 524, pp. 209–215
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Cemetery Company of Browinski Lodge, No. 64, I.O. O. F., in Carrollcounty.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 524, pp. 209–215
statutes.summary: This act incorporates Browinski Lodge, No. 64, I. O. O. F., and establishes rules for its cemetery. Section 16 explicitly prohibits the sale or ownership of cemetery lots to 'any person of color' and forbids lot holders from allowing persons of color to be buried in their lots, under penalty of forfeiture.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 744, pp. 547–550
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the District of Cold Spring, in Campbell county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 744, pp. 547–550
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the governance of public schools in a specific district. It details the appointment and dismissal of teachers, curriculum, qualifications for teachers and pupils, and provisions for free tuition for white children between the ages of six and twenty. It also allows for the establishment of tax levies for school property and maintenance, specifically mentioning property belonging to white persons.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 745, pp. 551–556
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish and maintain a graded free school in the town of Harrodsburg, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 745, pp. 551–556
statutes.summary: This act establishes a graded free school in Harrodsburg, Kentucky, and constitutes the town as a common school district. It specifies that the school district shall be under the exclusive control of six trustees who must be white men and resident voters. The election of trustees is to be conducted by qualified white voters. The act details the election process, terms of office, and the filling of vacancies for these trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 798, pp. 610–611
statutes.title: AN ACT in aid of colored common schools in Hart county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 798, pp. 610–611
statutes.summary: This act addresses an error in reporting for colored common schools in Hart County for the school year ending June 30th, 1875. Specifically, two districts numbered 'No. 4' were reported to the commissioner, but one was mistakenly omitted by the Superintendent of Public Instruction, preventing an apportionment. The act aims to rectify this oversight and ensure proper funding for these schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 880, pp. 674–675
statutes.title: AN ACT to make additional provision for the education of the colored children in the city of Covington.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 880, pp. 674–675
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the board of school trustees of Covington to establish and maintain schools for colored children using funds derived from city taxation. The number and location of these schools are to be determined by the board to ensure sufficient educational facilities for the colored children.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 905, pp. 691–692
statutes.title: AN ACT in aid of R. H. Caldwell, common school commissioner of Boyle county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 905, pp. 691–692
statutes.summary: This act directs the Superintendent of Public Instruction to withhold funds from the apportionment of colored school money for the year ending June 30th, 1877, and pay $30 to R. H. Caldwell. This payment is to compensate Caldwell for an amount he was required to advance in the current year, due to his omission to report one hundred pupil children of colored school district No. 5, Boyle county, to the Superintendent of Public Instruction.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, p. 749
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Cynthiana.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, p. 749
statutes.summary: This act mandates that offenders fined in the mayor's court of Cynthiana for violating city ordinances or state laws, who fail to pay or replevy their fines and costs, shall be compelled to labor on public works in the city with a ball and chain until the fines and costs are discharged, at a rate of one dollar per day.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, pp. 759–760
statutes.title: AN ACT for the protection of sheep in the counties of Henderson, Breckinridge, Caldwell, Hancock, McLean, and Christian.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, pp. 759–760
statutes.summary: This act imposes a tax on dogs and bitches over six months of age in several Kentucky counties. Crucially, it mandates that funds from taxes on dogs owned by white persons go to the common school fund for white children, while funds from taxes on dogs owned by colored persons go to the common school fund for colored children. This establishes a racially segregated system for the allocation of tax revenue for education.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 1089, pp. 704–705
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act to establish and maintain a graded free school in Harrodsburg, Kentucky."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 1089, pp. 704–705
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law establishing a graded free school in Harrodsburg, Kentucky. It allows for a vote by qualified white voters to determine if the school should be funded by taxation. The tax would be levied on property owned by white persons in the town, not exceeding thirty cents per one hundred dollars, to be used for common school education, excluding building erection. The act specifies that printed notices of the vote must be posted and published in a local paper.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 572, p. 54
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act to incorporate the Smithfield Cemetery Company."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 572, p. 54
statutes.summary: This act amends an earlier act to grant the Smithfield Cemetery Company the authority to condemn land for a passway. This passway is specifically designated to provide access from the Smithfield and New Castle Turnpike to the part of the cemetery used as a burial ground for persons of color. The passway is to be no more than twenty feet wide and is intended for the convenience of the colored people.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 587, p. 452
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act for the benefit of school district No. 39, in Bath county," approved February 9th, 1876.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 587, p. 452
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning school district No. 39 in Bath County. It specifies that only qualified white male voters and white widows with children between the ages of six and twenty years residing in the district have the privilege of voting for the trustees of the Sharpsburg Male and Female College. Widows can vote in person or by proxy. It also sets residency requirements for voters and limits each voter to one vote for each of the five trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 662, pp. 222–233
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of public schools in the Elizabethtown common school district, in Hardin county, for white children in said district.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 662, pp. 222–233
statutes.summary: This act establishes a public school system within the Elizabethtown common school district in Hardin County, specifically for white children. It defines the territory covered by the district and states that the system is for white children.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 734, pp. 301–304
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the West Louisville School District, in Daviess county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 734, pp. 301–304
statutes.summary: This act establishes the West Louisville School District and its board of trustees. Crucially, it explicitly exempts the property of colored citizens residing in the district from taxation for school purposes, while levying taxes on white male residents. This creates a racially segregated and unequal system of school funding.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 775, pp. 343–344
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a public school for children of the African race in the city of Paducah.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 775, pp. 343–344
statutes.summary: This act mandates the establishment and maintenance of a public school specifically for children of the African race in Paducah, to be known as the Colored Public School of Paducah. It outlines the supervisory roles of the general public school trustees, including appointing teachers, setting rules, and adopting textbooks. It also establishes an advisory board of five qualified colored voters to assist in the school's governance.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 799, pp. 373–378
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate" The Board of Trustees for the Graded City School of Cynthiana, Kentucky."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 799, pp. 373–378
statutes.summary: This act incorporates "The Board of Trustees for the Graded City School of Cynthiana, Kentucky" as a body-corporate and politic. It vests absolute control of the graded city school in this board and empowers them to manage it effectively. Crucially, Section 2 explicitly states that only a white male, resident of Cynthiana, and over twenty-one years of age is eligible for the office of trustee.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 880, pp. 443–446
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Colored Orphans 'Aid Association of the city of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 880, pp. 443–446
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the Colored Orphans' Aid Association of Louisville, which aims to establish an asylum for colored orphan children. The association was formed by benevolent individuals who subscribed funds to aid in this endeavor, particularly for purchasing property for the institution.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 888, pp. 453–454
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Pine Grove Cemetery, in Muhlenburg county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 888, pp. 453–454
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the Pine Grove Cemetery in Muhlenburg County. It specifies that land purchased for the cemetery is to be laid off into burial lots exclusively for sale to white people. Certificates of sale are assignable and transferable, provided the sale is to a white person. The act also outlines provisions for the perpetual care of the cemetery funded by a bequest.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 919, pp. 496–497
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the trustees of common school district No. 50, in Mason county, to levy and collect a tax for the erection of school buildings.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 919, pp. 496–497
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustee of common school district No. 50 in Mason County to hold an election for qualified white voters to approve a tax on taxable property belonging to white persons. The tax revenue would be used to build a schoolhouse exclusively for white pupils. The tax rate was set at forty cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property, to be levied annually for up to five years, or until a total of two thousand dollars was collected.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 924, pp. 502–503
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the erection of a school building in colored school district No. 1, in Ohio county, and to levy a tax therefor.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 924, pp. 502–503
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustee of colored school district No. 1 in Ohio County to erect a schoolhouse, not exceeding $1000 in value, for the use of colored school children. The building is to be used solely as a schoolhouse.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 925, pp. 503–504
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Mt. Sterling Library Association."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 925, pp. 503–504
statutes.summary: This act, passed in 1878, grants the Mt. Sterling Library Association the power to levy taxes on real and personal property owned by colored citizens in a specific district, not exceeding one dollar per one hundred dollars worth. It also allows for a capitation tax on colored persons over twenty-one, not exceeding five dollars. Furthermore, it authorizes the trustee to call out male colored citizens between eighteen and fifty years of age for labor on a building, not exceeding two days per week, with penalties for failure to work similar to those for road hands. The act specifies that the taxes are to be collected like school taxes and that the act will only be in force if ratified by a majority of colored voters in the district.

citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 10, p. 747
statutes.summary: This statute, from the General Statutes of Kentucky in 1879, outlines property exemptions from taxation for the support of common schools. Notably, it explicitly exempts 'all the property of negroes, mulattoes, and Indians' from this specific tax. Other exemptions include property devoted to public schools, religious institutions, and certain public service buildings.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 10, p. 893
statutes.title: § 10.The commissioner shall layoff the county into suit- Commissioner to able districts, most convenient to the greatest number of layoff school districts. colored children in each county, so that no district shall contain more than one hundred nor less than twenty colored children of pupil age.
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 10, p. 893
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the establishment and administration of separate common schools for colored children in Kentucky. It details the sheriff's role in collecting and allocating taxes for the colored school fund, the auditor's responsibility for maintaining a separate account, and the census and distribution methods for this fund, which are to mirror those for white children. It also specifies the responsibilities and compensation of county school commissioners and the appointment of three colored school trustees for each district, who will manage the schools and employ teachers. The statute also addresses the formation of school districts based on the number of colored children and the possibility of a single school in areas with insufficient numbers.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 14, p. 259
statutes.title: § 14. It shall be the duty of the trustee of each district, Annual census to annually, during the month of April, to take an exact census be taken—report thereof made.
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 14, p. 259
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the duties of school trustees in taking an annual census of white children between the ages of six and twenty years for the purpose of distributing school revenue. It details penalties for fraudulent census reporting and failure to comply with reporting requirements. It also specifies the trustee's duty to report when a district is entitled to receive its proportion of school revenue and to make detailed statistical reports at the end of each school year.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 15, p. 688
statutes.title: § 15. That from and after the passage of this act, the two Asylums named in, and established by, the second section of this act as the Third Kentucky Lunatic Asylum and the Fourth Kentucky Lunatic Asylum, shall be, and the same are hereby, set apart and devoted to the reception, care, and treatment…
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 15, p. 688
statutes.summary: This act reorganizes the Kentucky Lunatic Asylums, designating specific institutions for different types of mental afflictions (chronic mania/epilepsy vs. acute mania). Crucially, it includes a provision stating that 'colored lunatics shall remain in the Asylum where they now are, and be provided for as heretofore.' This indicates a segregation of patients based on race within the asylum system.

statutes.summary: This statute establishes separate common schools for colored children, outlining administrative structures, funding mechanisms, and curriculum development. It mandates a separate State association for colored school officers and teachers, and allows for the State Board of Education to prescribe a course of study and adopt rules for the government of these schools. Provisions from chapter eighteen of the General Statutes are to apply to colored common schools if deemed necessary by the State Board of Education. It also details the distribution and investment of surplus school funds, with a provision to equalize per capita funding with white pupils.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 26, p. 141
statutes.title: SEC. 26. When a vacancy shall happen in the office of Vacancies in any Attorney General, Auditor of Public Accounts, Treasurer, fices, how to be Register of the Land Office, President of the Board of In—of the State of—filled. the seat of gov-
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 26, p. 141
statutes.summary: This article outlines the General Assembly's limited powers regarding the emancipation of slaves. It states that emancipation requires the consent of the owners or full monetary compensation and removal from the state. The article also addresses the rights of immigrants to bring slaves into the state and the state's power to prevent the introduction of slaves as merchandise or those imported from foreign countries after a certain date. It also allows owners to emancipate slaves, with provisions for creditors and preventing emancipated slaves from remaining in the state.

statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for revenue and taxation in Kentucky. Specifically, Section 2 mandates that the taxable property of negroes, mulattoes, and Indians shall be listed on a separate book of the same form as the general tax book, with the word 'white' being changed to suit the case. This indicates a legally mandated segregation in tax record-keeping based on race.

statutes.summary: This statute establishes a dedicated revenue stream for the education of colored children in Kentucky. It details various taxes and funds to be collected and allocated specifically for this purpose, including property taxes, capitation taxes, dog taxes, state taxes on deeds, suits, and licenses levied on colored persons, fines and penalties imposed on colored persons, and funds from federal land distribution. It also mandates separate record-keeping for colored persons' taxable property and capitation by county assessors. The revenue is to be distributed annually by the Superintendent of Public Instruction.

statutes.title: § 4. Persons indicted for vagrancy shall be tried by a jury, Convicted—how and if found guilty, the jury shall fix the time for which he shall be bound out to labor, or sold into servitude, not exceeding twelve months, ifthe convict be over twenty -one years of age; ifhe be a minor, the jury shall…
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 4, p. 865
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for apprehending, trying, and punishing vagrants in Kentucky. Convicted vagrants over 21 years of age could be bound out to labor or sold into servitude for up to twelve months. Minors were to be apprenticed to learn a trade until the age of twenty-one. Fees and expenses were paid from the proceeds of the labor or servitude, with any remainder applied to the vagrant's debts and then to their family.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 5, p. 893
statutes.title: § 5. The sheriff of each county shall be allowed five per cent.of the taxes collected and paid into the Treasury by him for the colored school fund.
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 5, p. 893
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the establishment and administration of separate common schools for colored children in Kentucky. It details the sheriff's role in collecting and allocating taxes for the colored school fund, the auditor's responsibility for maintaining a separate account, and the census and distribution methods for this fund, which are to mirror those for white children. It also specifies the responsibilities and compensation of county school commissioners and the appointment of three colored school trustees for each district, who will manage the schools and employ teachers. The statute also addresses the formation of school districts based on the number of colored children and the possibility of a single school in areas with insufficient numbers.

citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 6, p. 254
statutes.summary: This section of the 1879 Kentucky Statutes outlines the administration of common schools. It details how tuition fees are handled for pupils attending schools outside their designated district and establishes provisions for cities, towns, or villages to maintain their own school systems. Crucially, it specifies that only qualified 'white voters' and 'white widows' with children are eligible to vote in trustee elections, and that the judge of such elections must be a 'commissioner' or a resident of the district. The census of 'white children' is also to be taken.

statutes.summary: This statute outlines the procedures for jury selection and management in Kentucky courts. It details the process of delivering jury lists to the clerk, the oath administered to the clerk and deputies, the clerk's duty to open envelopes and prepare lists, and the sheriff's responsibility to summon jurors. It also specifies penalties for jurors failing to attend, the possibility of discharging and summoning new panels, and provisions for adjusting panel size based on county needs. A specific instruction is given for summoning jurors by leaving notice with a 'white member of his family over sixteen years of age' if personal notice cannot be given.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 7, p. 90
statutes.title: SEC.7. The compact with the State of Virginia, subject to such alterations as may be made therein, agreeably to the mode prescribed by the said compact, shall be considered as a part of this Constitution.
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 7, p. 90
statutes.summary: This section of the First Constitution of Kentucky outlines the powers of the Legislature regarding slavery. It states that the Legislature cannot emancipate slaves without the owners' consent or compensation. It also addresses the right of emigrants to bring slaves into the state, the prevention of slave importation as merchandise or from foreign countries, and the Legislature's power to pass laws ensuring humane treatment of slaves, with provisions for their sale if owners neglect their duties. It also mentions the compact with Virginia and the establishment of the seat of government.

statutes.summary: This statute outlines provisions for common schools in Kentucky. Section 7 prohibits sectarian, infidel, or denominational books and doctrines. Section 8 allows for the establishment of common school districts that exclusively serve white children, provided certain conditions are met, including the consent of qualified voters and free tuition for white children within the district. Fines and forfeitures are to be paid into the Treasury for the Common School Fund.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 1378, pp. 212–218
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the relief of the Penitentiary.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 1378, pp. 212–218
statutes.summary: This act amends previous legislation regarding the employment of convicts. It specifies minimum squad sizes for hired convicts, mandates an inspector for each squad to ensure contractor compliance with treatment requirements, and outlines the distribution of net proceeds from convict labor (three-fourths to the state, one-fourth to the convict). It also grants contractors, guards, and employees peace officer powers to arrest individuals interfering with convicts and details penalties for escapes and attempted escapes, including forfeiture of earnings and potential return to the penitentiary.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 161, p. 450
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act to amend and reduce into one the several acts in reference to the town of Princeton, approved February 28, 1870.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 161, p. 450
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning the town of Princeton. It modifies the eligibility requirements for the office of marshal of the town. Specifically, it states that any male white person, twenty-one years of age, who has resided in Princeton for four months prior to an election, is eligible for the office of marshal, regardless of whether they meet the residency requirements to be a legal voter.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 173, pp. 461–462
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act to maintain a graded school in Hartford."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 173, pp. 461–462
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act establishing a graded school in Eminence, Kentucky. It grants the board of trustees the power to levy and collect taxes for the school's maintenance, employ staff, and purchase supplies. Crucially, it explicitly states that the act shall not apply to colored persons or their property.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 293, pp. 582–584
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish free schools for the education of colored children of the city of Owensboro.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 293, pp. 582–584
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the mayor and council of the city of Owensboro to levy a tax of two dollars on every male citizen of African descent, over the age of 21, to establish free schools for the education of colored children in the city.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 305, p. 591
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the public school for the colored people of the town of Winchester,& c.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 305, p. 591
statutes.summary: This act extends the boundaries of the public school for the colored people of Winchester, school district No. 1, to include several named areas, creating a new school district for the colored people, number ten. Crucially, this new district will not elect its own trustees but will be under the supervision and control of the trustees of the white public school of Winchester. The old common school district No. 1 for the colored people is abolished.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 30, pp. 55–58
statutes.title: AN ACT to take the sense of the people of this Commonwealth as to the propriety of calling a Convention to revise the Constitution, and to regulate the manner of taking the list of qualified voters.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 30, pp. 55–58
statutes.summary: This act mandates that tax assessors create a separate column in their books to enroll the names of citizens entitled to vote for Representative in 1881. The enrollment is to be based on the assessor's personal knowledge, information directly from the person, or sworn testimony from others. Assessors are subject to a fine for improperly enrolling names and must follow existing laws to prevent illegal voting. They are also required to take an oath to fairly ascertain qualified voters and report the numbers. Assessors are empowered to examine potential voters under oath.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 351, pp. 633–637
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to amend and reduce into one the several acts concerning the city of Henderson," approved February 11th, 1867, and the several acts amend a tory thereto.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 351, pp. 633–637
statutes.summary: This act creates the office of Collector of Taxes for the city of Henderson and establishes eligibility requirements for this office. Specifically, Section 6 states that only a 'white male citizen' of Henderson, at least twenty-five years old, and a bona fide resident for at least two years prior to election, is eligible to hold the office of tax collector. The act also abolishes the office of judge of the Henderson city court and transfers its duties to the mayor.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 377, pp. 665–668
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a system of common schools for the town of Louisa, and so much of school district No. I as may be on'sidethe corporate limits of said town. Be il enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky:
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 377, pp. 665–668
statutes.summary: This act establishes a board of education for the town of Louisa, Kentucky, granting them control over public schools, property, and funds. The board is empowered to make by-laws, appoint teachers, and fix compensation. Crucially, Section 9 explicitly states that 'all white children over six and under twenty years of age, within said district, shall have equal right of admission to the school of said district.' This explicit racial distinction in admission criteria for public education is a hallmark of Jim Crow legislation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 441, pp. 756–758
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate Germantown Normal Academy, and to grant certain powers to the common school district in which said Academy is located, in Bracken county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 441, pp. 756–758
statutes.summary: This act grants the trustees of the Germantown public school district (24th district, Bracken county) the power to lease or rent the public school building and premises. A key provision requires that the lease or rental agreement must ensure faithful instruction is provided for the 'white pupils of the district entitled to school privileges.' The lessees can improve the property, with the right to remove additions if the lease is not renewed, provided no damage is done to the district's property.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 49, pp. 58–60
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the city of Lexington to donate lands and bonds for the benefit of the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Kentucky, and to provide for the payment of the bonds.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 49, pp. 58–60
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning the city of Lexington. It authorizes the city to levy an additional tax for the payment of bonds, with the power to enforce payment by prohibiting the keeping of offices or practicing professions until the tax is paid. Crucially, it explicitly states that the taxes authorized by the fourth section shall only be levied and collected from the whites of said city and white property owners. The second part of the provided text concerns changes to court dates in Greenup County and is unrelated to the Lexington tax act.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 523, p. 862
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act to organize and establish a system of public schools in the city of Hopkinsville for white children," approved March 13, 1872.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 523, p. 862
statutes.summary: This act legalizes and confirms the organization of trustees for public schools for white children in Hopkinsville, established in 1879, and sets the date for the next election of trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 695, p. 1018
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of M. Rice, common school commissioner of Hopkins county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1880, ch. 695, p. 1018
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the Superintendent of Public Instruction to issue a warrant for $28.32 to M. Rice, the common school commissioner of Hopkins county. This payment is to compensate for a reporting error by the trustees of a colored school district, which resulted in the commissioner receiving less school fund than due. The funds are to be paid out of the school fund for colored persons due or to the credit of Hopkins county.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 1000, pp. 495–499
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of public graded schools in Carlisle, Nicholas county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 1000, pp. 495–499
statutes.summary: This act establishes a public graded school system in Carlisle, Nicholas County. It defines the boundaries of school district No. 26 to include territory within one and a half miles of the courthouse. The district is to be managed by five trustees elected by qualified white voters and white widows entitled to vote, as prescribed by general common school law. The elected trustees will form 'The Board of Trustees of the Carlisle Public Schools' and will have corporate powers.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 1126, pp. 651–653
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the town of Stroud City, in Muhlenburg county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 1126, pp. 651–653
statutes.summary: This act amends the incorporation of Stroud City. Notably, it allows the board of trustees to levy a poll tax of not exceeding one dollar on each white male citizen for the purpose of maintaining a town free school. Crucially, it includes a proviso stating that 'The property of the blacks of said town shall not be taxed for school purposes.'

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 1394, pp. 994–1001
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the town of Cane Valley.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 1394, pp. 994–1001
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the town of Cane Valley and establishes a board of five trustees to manage its fiscal, prudential, and municipal affairs. The trustees are elected annually by qualified voters. A key provision states that only a 'free white male citizen' over twenty-one years of age, who has resided in the town for six months, is eligible to be a trustee. The trustees have powers related to town planning, streets, alleys, sidewalks, and levying taxes.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 1569, pp. 1217–1219
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act to establish and maintain a graded free school in Harrodsburg, Kentucky," approved March 15th, 1876, and the acts amend a tory thereto, approved April 10th, 1878.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 1569, pp. 1217–1219
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of Harrodsburg, Kentucky, to submit to the qualified white voters of the town the question of levying a tax on property owned by white persons. The purpose of this tax is to raise funds, not exceeding one thousand dollars, to relieve debt incurred by the school trustees for property purchases. The tax can be paid in one or two levies, as determined by a majority of the white voters. The act details the process for submitting the question, including notice requirements and election procedures, explicitly limiting voting to "qualified white voters."

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 862, pp. 279–280
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend sections 41 and 9 of the charter of the city of Owensboro.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 862, pp. 279–280
statutes.summary: This act amends the incorporation of the town of Worthville. It changes a reference from 'criminal' to 'civil' in section seven, adds 'subject to State tax' to section eight, and modifies section nine by striking out the word 'white' after 'every'. It also grants town trustees exclusive rights to license taverns, coffee-houses, and saloons, and to set fees and regulations for them.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 894, pp. 314–315
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a public school for children of the African race resid. ing in the city of Frankfort.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 894, pp. 314–315
statutes.summary: This act mandates the establishment and maintenance of a separate public school for African race children in Frankfort, Kentucky. It outlines the roles of the general public school trustees and an advisory board of colored voters, and specifies the funding sources for this segregated school.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 932, pp. 392–393
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of school district No. 1, of Cartercounty.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 932, pp. 392–393
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act to allow the board of trustees for the graded city school of Cynthiana, Kentucky, to levy and collect an additional ad valorem tax on the taxable property of white persons in the city. The tax is not to exceed thirty cents on each one hundred dollars' worth of property and is to be used for the payment of interest and redemption of bonds authorized by the act. The act also states that only the property of white persons shall be taxed for the purpose of this act.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 933, pp. 393–394
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act to incorporate the board of trustees of the city graded school of Cynthiana," approved April 5th, 1878.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 933, pp. 393–394
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act to allow the board of trustees for the graded city school of Cynthiana, Kentucky, to levy and collect an additional ad valorem tax on the taxable property of white persons in the city. The tax is not to exceed thirty cents on each one hundred dollars' worth of property and is to be used for the payment of interest and redemption of bonds authorized by the act. statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 957, pp. 428–437
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a system of common schools in Smith's Mills district, in Henderson county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 957, pp. 428–437
statutes.summary: This act outlines the organization and election of trustees for a school district in Louisville. It specifies the oath of trustees, the election of a president and other officers, and the division of trustees into classes with staggered terms. Crucially, it states that "The white voters of said school district shall, upon the first Monday in August next, and upon the first Monday of August in each succeeding year, elect, as in all other elections,". This explicitly limits voting rights for school district elections to white voters.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 983, pp. 470–473
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a graded school at Willisburg, in Washington county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, ch. 983, pp. 470–473
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the establishment and maintenance of a graded school named Brown's Institute and Graded School in Willisburg, Washington County, Kentucky. The school is specifically for the instruction of 'white children' within a defined geographical boundary. It outlines the governance structure, including a board of trustees, and provisions for funding through taxation on 'white citizens'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, p. 867
statutes.title: An Act to Amend and Re-enact Chapter 86 of the General Statutes, Relating to Public Schools in the Town of Vanceburg
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1880, p. 867
statutes.summary: This act amends the public school laws for Vanceburg, Kentucky. It explicitly states that only white children have equal rights of admission to the school and that only the property of white persons shall be taxed for school purposes. The board of education is empowered to issue bonds for school construction and to levy taxes to repay them, with the tax base restricted to white property owners.

The statute specifies district sizes and the organization of schools based on the number of colored children.

It also details procedures for avoiding or affirming marriages and managing the estates of underage females marrying without parental consent.

Each school district shall be under the control of one Election of at rus trustee, an election for whom shall be held at the school-- how conducted house of such district, or such other convenient place as who to act as the trustee may select, from nine o'clock in the morning till five o'clock…
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 1, pp. 248–249
statutes.summary: This section of the statutes outlines the administration of common schools. It details how tuition fees are handled for students attending schools outside their designated district and establishes provisions for cities, towns, or villages that maintain their own school systems. Crucially, it specifies that only 'qualified white voters' and 'white widows' with children are eligible to vote in trustee elections, and that the census of 'white children' must be taken. The commissioner has no control over schools in such districts, which are governed by local authorities.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 1, p. 926

citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 1, p. 926
statutes.summary: This act establishes a separate and uniform system of common schools specifically for the education of colored children in Kentucky. It also defines the 'colored school fund' which is to consist of a specific annual revenue tax on taxable property owned or held by colored individuals.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 21, p. 930
statutes.title: § 21.The State Board of Education shall prescribe a Course of study. course of study and adopt rules for the government of the colored common schools.
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 21, p. 930
statutes.summary: This statute outlines provisions for colored common schools in Kentucky. It details the salary for a clerk assisting the Superintendent of Public Instruction for colored schools, the organization of state associations and county institutes for colored school officers and teachers, the State Board of Education's role in prescribing a course of study and rules, and the application of general statutes to colored schools. It also addresses the distribution of surplus school funds, with a provision for investment for the benefit of colored schools if per capita funding is not equal to that of white pupils.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 25, pp. 134–135
statutes.title: SEC.25.The General Assembly shall provide, by law, for the making of the returns, by the proper officers, of the election of all officers to be elected under this Constitution; and the Governor shall issue commissions to the Auditor, Register, Treasurer, President of the Board of Internal…
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 25, pp. 134–135
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky Constitution outlines the limitations on the General Assembly's power regarding the emancipation of slaves. It states that emancipation requires the consent of the owners or full monetary compensation and removal from the state. It also addresses the rights of slave owners to bring slaves into the state and to emancipate them, with restrictions on their remaining in Kentucky. The assembly is also empowered to prevent the introduction of slaves as merchandise or those imported from foreign countries.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 25, pp. 687–688
statutes.title: § 25. I. White lunatics and idiots resident in Kentucky, White lunatics, and found in the counties of Kenton, Grant, Owen, Franklin,& c., to be sent to Eastern Asylum.
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 25, pp. 687–688
The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1887, § 25, pp. 965–966
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the segregation of lunatic patients in Kentucky's asylums based on race. It specifies that colored lunatics and idiots from certain counties must be sent to the Eastern Kentucky Lunatic Asylum, while those from the rest of the state go to the Central Kentucky Lunatic Asylum. Crucially, it mandates that white and colored patients shall not be kept in the same buildings. The statute also details procedures for transferring patients between asylums if one is full and empowers the Governor to ensure asylums are filled to capacity.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 7, pp. 230–231
statutes.title: § 7. The Superintendent of Public Instruction shall, on or before the first day of August in each year, ascertain and estimate, as near as may be, the net revenue that will accrue from all sources during the school year, the pro rata share there of each white child will be entitled to according to…
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1881, § 7, pp. 230–231
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the funding and distribution of the Common School Fund in Kentucky. It specifies that the fund's revenue, derived from various sources including an annual tax and fines, shall be used exclusively for the payment of legally qualified and employed teachers of common schools. The Auditor is tasked with managing the fund's accounts and ensuring no county exceeds its proportional share. The Superintendent of Public Instruction is responsible for estimating the net revenue and the pro rata share for each white child, county, and district. Notably, the statute explicitly mentions 'white child' when determining the distribution of funds.

statutes.summary: This statute outlines the provisions for the education of "colored" children in Kentucky. It details how taxes can be designated for their education, establishes a separate fund for colored schools, mandates the census of colored children, and outlines the responsibilities of county commissioners and appointed colored school trustees in managing and operating these segregated schools. The statute specifies district sizes and the organization of schools based on the number of colored children.
