statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a uniform system of Common Schools for the Colored Children of this Commonwealth. Approved February23,1874. Gen'l Acts 1873-4, p. 63
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 80
statutes.summary: This act establishes a uniform system of common schools for colored children in Kentucky. It mandates the census of colored children and the distribution of the colored school fund in the same manner as for white children. Crucially, it explicitly prohibits colored children from attending schools for white children and vice versa.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 81
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act entitled "An act for the benefit of the Public Schools of the City of Louisville, approved January31,1873. Approved February 1, 1876. Session Acts 1876, vol.1, p.232.
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 81
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the Board of Trustees of the public schools of Louisville to use surplus funds to erect or purchase two additional school houses for colored children, one in the eastern and one in the western part of the city.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 82
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the Public Shoo ls of the City of Louisville. Approved February 1,1876. Acts of 1876, vol.1, p.234.
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 82
statutes.summary: This act levies a tax of 8 cents per $100 of property value to fund public schools in Louisville. Crucially, it specifies that these schoolhouses are 'for the use of white children'. The tax is subject to a voter referendum for its continuation.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 39
statutes.title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 39
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the powers and responsibilities of the Board of Trustees for the Public Schools of Louisville. It details their authority to elect and remove teachers, fix salaries, prescribe curriculum, set admission qualifications and numbers, and establish school districts. Crucially, it states that 'all freewhite children over six years of age within each district shall have equal rights of admission to the schools of that district.' It also prohibits sectarian teaching and fees for tuition.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 64
statutes.title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 64
statutes.summary: This statute mandates the segregation of public schools in Louisville, prohibiting children of the African race from attending schools with white children. It also requires that school taxes paid by individuals of the African race be kept separate and used exclusively for the education of children of the African race residing within the city or paying school taxes there.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 70
statutes.title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 70
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the organization and funding of public schools in Louisville, Kentucky. It designates cities or towns that maintain adequate, free common schools as a single district, entitled to a proportion of the school fund. These districts are to report to the County Commissioner and take a census of white children. The schools are governed by local authorities, and the Commissioner has no control over them. The statute also details the process for paying teachers and penalties for non-payment.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 74
statutes.title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 74
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law concerning public schools in Louisville. It directs that a portion of school revenues, previously intended for the sinking fund, shall be used by the Louisville School Board to construct and equip three schoolhouses specifically for colored children, located in the eastern, western, and central parts of the city. These schools and their operations will be under the School Board's control. Any remaining funds after building the houses will be invested for the benefit of colored schools, with the interest exclusively applied to paying teachers and for maintenance and operation.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 75
statutes.title: Public School Law of Louisv- 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 75
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for the Superintendent of Public Instruction to estimate and apportion school funds. It specifies that the pro rata share of revenue for each child is calculated based on the number of 'white children' between the ages of six and twenty. The statute also details the use of census returns or tax books for apportionment and the reporting requirements to the Auditor of Public Accounts and County Commissioners.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 76
statutes.title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 76
statutes.summary: This statute outlines provisions for public schools in cities and towns, including the establishment of a graded system of free schools and the levying of a special school tax. It also details the appointment and duties of School Commissioners for each county and the City of Louisville, requiring them to report the census of white children between the ages of six and twenty.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 91
statutes.title: Public School Law of Louisv- 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 91
statutes.summary: This act levies an additional two-cent tax per $100 of property to equalize per capita funding for white and colored pupil children. It also repeals the capitation tax on colored people for common school purposes and explicitly prohibits white children from attending colored schools and vice versa, mandating separate schools for each race.

statutes.statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 92
statutes.title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 92
statutes.summary: This act proposes an additional tax of three cents per $100 worth of property to increase the common school fund and equalize the per capita funding for white and colored students. The act's effectiveness is contingent on ratification by a majority of qualified voters in an August 1882 election. Section 8 states the act takes effect upon passage for the purpose of submitting the vote to the people, and Note 2 confirms it was ratified.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1015, pp. 426–427
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the board of councilmen of Frankfort to issue bouds for school purposes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1015, pp. 426–427
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the board of councilmen of Frankfort to issue bonds up to $10,000 for the purpose of procuring a suitable building, furniture, fixtures, and apparatus for the "colored public school" of the city. The bonds are to be sold at face value and the funds used for this specific school.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1033, pp. 477–487
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for a registration of voters in the city of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1033, pp. 477–487
statutes.summary: This act establishes a board composed of the county judge, sheriff, and county court clerk of Jefferson County to appoint four citizens in each election precinct of Louisville to serve as judges, clerk, and sheriff of registration. Eligibility requires being a voter and a house-keeper in the precinct. The act also mentions provisions for when there are two distinct political parties.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1154, pp. 693–694
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of common school districts numbers three, eleven, twenty-eight, thirty, thirty-one, forty-five, forty-nine, fifty-two, fifty-five, fifty-nine, white, and numbers eight, twelve, fourteen, colored, in Madison county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1154, pp. 693–694
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the Superintendent of Public Instruction to issue drafts for payments to common school districts in Madison County. It specifies separate amounts for white districts ($99.40) and colored districts ($77.00), to be paid from the common school fund. The payment to white districts includes a portion for unbonded interest on surplus bonds.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1162, pp. 714–720
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for good roads in Todd county, and to regulate taxation in the same.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1162, pp. 714–720
statutes.summary: This act outlines the process for road contractors in Todd County, Kentucky. It details the execution of bonds, approval by the county judge, and payment procedures. Crucially, Section 8 mandates that the Todd County judge shall provide work on county roads or town streets for persons convicted of penal offenses who are required to work on roads or streets, or to work out fines. This provision allows for the use of convicted individuals, potentially including those from the Black community who were disproportionately convicted of offenses, for forced labor on public works, a common characteristic of Jim Crow era labor practices.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1201, pp. 797–801
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Kuttawa common school district, in Lyon county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1201, pp. 797–801
statutes.summary: This act establishes the Kuttawa common school district and outlines its management, funding, and operational requirements. Notably, it specifies that instruction shall be provided to "all white children" between the ages of six and twenty years residing in the district without charge. It also defines voter qualifications for school board elections, explicitly including "all the white qualified voters" and certain tax-paying or child-rearing widows or maids, while generally qualifying voters based on age, citizenship, and taxpaying status, with an exception for sex.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1371, pp. 1087–1088
statutes.title: AN ACT to prevent idleness and vagrancy in Fleming county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1371, pp. 1087–1088
statutes.summary: This act amends existing statutes regarding vagrancy in Fleming County. It mandates that convicted vagrants be sentenced to hard labor for 50 to 100 days. Jailers are required to ensure convicted individuals work eight hours a day, with refusal leading to a bread and water diet. A provision is made for the dependents of convicted laborers, with a daily payment of twenty-five cents to be covered by the county or the beneficiary of the labor.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1393, pp. 1123–1187
statutes.title: AN ACT to revise the charter of the city of Paducah, and reduce into one the several acts relating there to.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1393, pp. 1123–1187
statutes.summary: This statute, from the Laws of Kentucky in 1884, outlines the powers and responsibilities of public school trustees in McCracken County. Specifically, section 5 mandates that the trustees shall "provide separate buildings and schools for education of white and black pupils."

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1431, pp. 1258–1261
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of common school district number forty-three, in Graves county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1431, pp. 1258–1261
statutes.summary: This act incorporates common school district number forty-three in Graves county, specifically mentioning 'white persons living in said district' as part of the incorporated entity. It grants the trustees powers to govern the school and enforce rules.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1489, pp. 1350–1351
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the levy and collection of additional tax in aid of public schools in common school district number sixteen, Breckinridge county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1489, pp. 1350–1351
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of common school district number sixteen in Breckinridge County (Hardinsburg district) to levy an ad valorem tax of up to twenty cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property and a capitation tax of up to one dollar and fifty cents per person over twenty-one years old. Crucially, it specifies that 'only white persons and property belonging to white persons shall be taxed.' The trustees are required to declare the tax amount annually by May 1st.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1518, pp. 1392–1393
statutes.title: AN ACT creating an additional voting place in the fourth magisterial district, of Fayette county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1518, pp. 1392–1393
statutes.summary: This act establishes an additional voting place in Fayette County's fourth magisterial district, designating the Bell school-house as polling place number two. It mandates that voters residing east of the Louisville, Cincinnati, and Lexington Railroad must vote at polling place number one, and those west of the railroad must vote at polling place number two. The sheriff is required to post notices informing voters of this division.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1536, p. 1416
statutes.title: AN ACT to prohibit the sale of spirituous, vino us, and malt liquors, in common school district number thirty, in Graves county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1536, p. 1416
statutes.summary: This act prohibits the sale or gifting of spirituous, vinous, or malt liquors within common school district number thirty in Graves county. Violators face fines. Notably, Section 4 specifies that if persons of color violate the act, the fines shall be appropriated to the benefit of the colored school in said district.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1595, pp. 1477–1478
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the trustees of common school district number one, in Grayson county, to levy and collect a tax for the benefit of the common school property in said district.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1595, pp. 1477–1478
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of common school district number one in Grayson county to levy and collect an ad valorem tax for the years 1884 and 1885. The tax is to be levied on all property in the district listed by white citizens for taxation, not exceeding fifteen cents on every one hundred dollars worth of taxable property.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 822, pp. 69–72
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of common and graded schools in the town of Dover, and in common school district number two, in Mason county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 822, pp. 69–72
statutes.summary: This act establishes the Dover Graded School District and outlines the governance and operation of its schools. It specifies that the schools shall be taught for ten months each year and that every white child within the district, within the common school age, shall have free access and the right to attend free of charge.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 825, pp. 78–84
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Webster and Hopkins counties, relating to the public roads in said counties.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 825, pp. 78–84
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the use of convicted individuals and delinquent taxpayers for labor on county roads and streets. It allows county judges to assign work to those convicted of penal offenses, including working off fines, and to use restraints like ball and chains to prevent escape. It also mandates that delinquent capitation taxpayers in Webster County work off their taxes on roads, with surveyors authorized to collect taxes or oversee the work. Penalties are imposed for non-compliance.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 868, p. 142
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to provide for the payment of debts contracted in building and furnishing a school-house, and for main. tain inga school in district number one, in Pendleton county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 868, p. 142
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law concerning school funding in Pendleton County. It exempts colored persons and their property from the capitation and property taxes authorized by the original act for school purposes.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 961, pp. 352–354
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the Owenton High School, in Owen county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 961, pp. 352–354
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of the Owenton High School. It allows the school board to issue bonds for purchasing a new site, building, or repairing the school. It also states that the school shall be for whites only and that the question of a tax for the school will be submitted to voters.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 994, p. 394
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act to charter the South Carrollton Male and Female Academy."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 994, p. 394
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of the South Carrollton Male and Female Academy. It specifies that the election of trustees will be held by 'white male voters' of the common school district. The trustees will serve until their successors are elected and qualified.

statutes.statute_citation: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 51
statutes.title: Common School Laws - Article XII - Colored Schools
citations: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 51
statutes.summary: This article outlines the legal framework for the establishment and operation of separate schools for colored children in Kentucky. It details the disposition of funds for colored schools, the process of laying off school districts, the age and census requirements for colored pupils, and the election of trustees for colored schools. Crucially, it includes provisions that explicitly prohibit inter-racial attendance in common schools and prevent taxation or services from one race benefiting the other's schools, as well as restricting voting rights for trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 52
statutes.title: Common School Laws - 1885
citations: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 52
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Laws from 1885 explicitly mandates racial segregation in common schools. It prohibits white individuals from contributing to schools for colored children and vice versa, and forbids individuals of one race from voting for trustees of schools designated for the other race. Furthermore, it explicitly states that white children cannot attend schools for colored children, and colored children cannot attend schools for white children. It also outlines the organization of Teachers' Institutes and State Teachers' Associations for colored people.

statutes.statute_citation: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 55
statutes.title: Colored School Fund
citations: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 55
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Laws from 1885 discusses the constitutionality of a separate common school fund for colored children, established by an act on February 23, 1874. The text states that this act is unconstitutional, citing the case of Dawson vs. Lee.

statutes.statute_citation: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 7
statutes.title: AN ACT TO AMEND AND REFORM THE COMMON SCHOOL LAWS OF THIS COMMONWEALTH
citations: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 7
statutes.summary: This act establishes a uniform system of common schools throughout Kentucky, outlining the structure, funding, and administration of the school system. It covers various aspects including the school fund, county taxation, boards of education, superintendents, districts, trustees, teachers, institutes, libraries, and fines. Notably, it includes a section specifically titled 'COLORED SCHOOLS'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1001, pp. 541–543
statutes.title: AN ACT fixing the boundary and for the benefit of the school district No. 67, in Fleming county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1001, pp. 541–543
statutes.summary: This act establishes a new school district and outlines the process for electing trustees, listing children of school age, and voting on taxes for school construction. Notably, it specifies that lists of property owners and tithes for taxation purposes shall be made for 'all the white owners of property' and 'all the white tithes residing in said district.' Additionally, it allows for a per capita tax on 'each white male person of twenty-one years of age residing in said district.'

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1010, pp. 549–551
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to incorporate Carr Institute."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1010, pp. 549–551
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of the Carr Institute, a school, by detailing fees for tax collection and establishing liens for taxes. Crucially, it explicitly states that the provisions of this act shall only apply to the white population of the Fulton school district.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1094, pp. 661–665
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the National Sick and Accident Fund in Adairville, Logan county, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1094, pp. 661–665
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the Kentucky Mutual Aid Association, outlining its purpose to provide weekly benefits for members during sickness or disability. It details the powers of the board, membership conditions, and benefit limits. Crucially, Section 8 explicitly states that only 'free-born white men between the ages of eighteen and forty-five' are eligible for membership.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1142, p. 717
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the city of Lexington to issue bonds to the amount of thirty thousand dollars for school purposes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1142, p. 717
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the city of Lexington to issue bonds up to $30,000 for school purposes. The funds are to be used for purchasing land and erecting schoolhouses for both white and colored children, with the determination of the number of schoolhouses for colored children left to the discretion of the general council.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1173, pp. 756–757
statutes.title: AN ACT to consolidate common school districts numbered eighty—three (83), eighty-four(84) and eighty-six (86), for white children, in Barren county, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1173, pp. 756–757
statutes.summary: This act consolidates three common school districts (83, 84, and 86) specifically for white children in Barren County, Kentucky, into a single district. It outlines the process for electing trustees and states that the common school laws of the Commonwealth will apply to this consolidated district.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 685, pp. 41–47
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a system of public graded schools in district No. 47, East Point.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 685, pp. 41–47
statutes.summary: This act establishes a public graded school system for district No. 47 in East Point, Kentucky. It explicitly states that the school affairs for white children of pupil age will be under the control and management of five trustees, elected by qualified white voters. It also defines who qualifies as a voter, including white widows, aliens who are taxpayers, or those with children to be educated between the ages of six and twenty.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 725, pp. 94–111
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for there-organization, maintenance and supervising of common schools in the town of Louisa and vic in itv.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 725, pp. 94–111
statutes.summary: This act establishes a common school in a specific district in Louisa, Kentucky. It outlines the boundaries of the district, the duration of the school year (5-10 months), and specifies that 'all white children between the ages of six and twenty residing therein shall receive instruction without any charge therefor.' The management and control of the school and its funds are vested in a board of education whose members must possess the qualifications of 'white voters of said district.' Elections for the board are to be held annually, and only 'white qualified voters, and any maid or widow who is a tax payer' are eligible to vote.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 885, pp. 341–342
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of colored common schools of Floyd county, and to authorize the superintendent and board of examiners of common schools of said county " to issue special license to persons to teach colored common schools of said county."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 885, pp. 341–342
statutes.summary: This act addresses the difficulty in finding qualified teachers for colored common schools in Floyd County. It authorizes the superintendent and board of examiners to issue special licenses to individuals to teach these schools, acknowledging that there were no local colored teachers who could obtain certificates under the existing rigid examination requirements. The preamble states the importance of these schools for the cultural development and civic duties of colored citizens.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 929, pp. 405–410
statutes.title: AN ACT to consolidate common school districts Nos.1 and 26, in Carrollcounty, and to provide for a school building and the better organ i zationof the public schools in said consolidated district.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 929, pp. 405–410
statutes.summary: This act allows the board of trustees of a school district in Ballard County to issue bonds, not exceeding $8,000, to fund the purchase of grounds, erection of buildings, and furnishing of school facilities. Crucially, it specifies that these facilities must be 'amply sufficient for the proper accommodation of all the white children of pupil age within the district thereby created.'

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 931, pp. 412–415
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Little Mount Cemetery Company, in Spencer county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 931, pp. 412–415
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the Scaville and Lawrenceburg Turnpike Road Company. It also contains provisions for a cemetery board that has the power to segregate burial plots by race, confining 'colored people to one portion and white people to another'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 974, p. 495
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Hawesville in relation too schools.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 974, p. 495
statutes.summary: This act mandates that funds received by the Hawesville board of education from licenses set aside for school purposes be divided equally between white and colored schools. The treasurer is required to distribute these funds proportionally based on the school census, paying the colored school trustees their share. Failure to comply within one month allows the colored school trustees to take legal action.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 992, pp. 517–526
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for a registration of voters in the city of Paducah.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 992, pp. 517–526
statutes.summary: This statute outlines procedures for challenging voter registration. It details how to serve notice to a registered voter, form a committee to hear evidence, and strike names from the register if deemed unlawfully registered. It also describes a process for marking voters as 'doubtful' if they cannot be served notice, requiring them to be sworn in and their right to vote investigated at the election.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1887, § 10, p. 1231
statutes.title: § 10.The commissioner shall layoff the county into suitable districts, most convenient to the greatest number of colored children in each county, so that no district shall contain more than one hundred nor less than twenty colored children of pupil age. § II. In counties where there are not a…
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1887, § 10, p. 1231
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the organization and management of colored common schools in Kentucky. It details the responsibilities of county commissioners in laying out school districts for colored children, specifying pupil age ranges and district sizes. It also covers the appointment of colored school trustees, their duties in managing schools, employing teachers, and notifying parents. The statute mandates a minimum school term length, with provisions for shorter terms under certain conditions. It also outlines the process for obtaining sites and erecting schoolhouses, and sets qualifications for teachers of colored schools, which are less stringent than those for white schools.

statutes.statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1887, § 12, p. 1239
statutes.title: § 12. The Superintendent of Public Instruction shall annually appoint a committee of three, who shall, in a body or by one of their number, visit said normal school once during each term, witness the exercises, and otherwise inspect the condition of said school, and by the close of the normal school…
citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1887, § 12, p. 1239
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the establishment and maintenance of a normal school specifically for the education of 'colored residents' of Kentucky. It outlines the conditions for admission, the non-sectarian nature of the school, reporting requirements, and the granting of certificates and diplomas. The statute explicitly mentions 'colored residents' in relation to educational opportunities.

statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the organization and maintenance of a graded free school in common school district No. 3, in Johnson county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 772, pp. 664–668
statutes.summary: This act establishes a board of three trustees to manage and maintain a system of common and graded schools within a specific district. It mandates that every white child in the district, within the common school age, shall have free access and the right to attend these schools free of charge. The act details the election and qualification of trustees, their organizational duties, and the requirement to take a census of scholars within the district.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 795, pp. 710–715
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Hardinsburg Normal and Collegiate Institute.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 795, pp. 710–715
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law concerning taxes for common schools in Breckinridge County. It specifies that the tax will only take effect if approved by a majority of qualified white voters in the district. The election for this approval is to be ordered by the board of trustees, with specific notice requirements and voting procedures. The superintendent of common schools for Breckinridge county is to appoint election officers, or the board of trustees will if the superintendent fails to do so. The act also details the certification and delivery of poll books.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 837, pp. 787–788
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to establish a system of public and high schools for the town of Sebree, in the county of Webster, for white children only," approved February 18,1888.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 837, pp. 787–788
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law establishing public and high schools in Sebree, Kentucky. It allows for an election to be held to determine if the existing school law, which explicitly states it is for 'white children only,' should be put into full effect. The election process is detailed, including notice, voting procedures, and certification of results.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 839, p. 791
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled "An act to create the office of county treasurer for Campbell county."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 839, p. 791
statutes.summary: This act amends the law regarding the election of the county treasurer for Campbell County. It stipulates that only voters residing outside the corporate limits of Newport, Bellevue, and Dayton will be eligible to vote for the county treasurer. The term of office is extended to four years.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 861, pp. 822–832
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for a registration of voters of the city of Covington. Officers.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 861, pp. 822–832
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law regarding voter registration in Covington, Kentucky. It outlines procedures for appointing registration officers, preserving order at registration sites, and challenging a person's right to register. Notably, it specifies that registration books should include a column for 'color'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 869, pp. 846–847
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled "An act to consolidate common school districts Nos.1 and 26, in Carroll county, and to provide for a school building and a better organization of the public schools in said consolidated district," approved May 7,1886; and providing for the levying of an additional…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 869, pp. 846–847
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the board of trustees of common school district number one (1), white, in Carroll county, to levy an additional tax of up to twenty cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property owned by white people. This tax is intended to extend the school session from five months to eight to ten months per year, as the state common school fund only provides enough to maintain the school for five months. The act also addresses existing debt for a school building and a previously levied tax to pay it off.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 896, pp. 903–906
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Williamsburg Institute.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 896, pp. 903–906
statutes.summary: This statute incorporates an institute and grants it powers related to its operations, including the ability to make contracts, sue and be sued, hold and sell property, make investments, purchase grounds, erect buildings, establish schools, and provide terms of admission and rejection of pupils. Crucially, it explicitly states that 'none but white pupils shall ever be admitted in the school of said institute.' The statute also outlines the institute's governance structure, including a board of trustees and other officers.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 905, pp. 929–937
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the several acts incorporating the town of New Liberty, in Owen county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 905, pp. 929–937
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the eligibility requirements for holding the office of trustee in the town of Vanceburg. Specifically, it states that a candidate must be a 'white male citizen' of the United States, over twenty-one years of age, a resident of the town for at least six months prior to the election, and an owner in fee-simple of real estate within the town limits.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 928, pp. 968–1036
statutes.title: AN ACT to repeal the charter of the city of Henderson and the acts amend a tory thereto, and to re incorporate the said city of Henderson.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 928, pp. 968–1036
statutes.summary: This statute outlines procedures for voter registration and challenges in the city of Henderson. It details how names can be marked as 'doubtful' and require further investigation before voting. It also specifies penalties for false registration, including registering in multiple wards or while underage or not lawfully entitled to register. The statute mandates the delivery of registration and poll books to election officials and states that a person's vote will not be received unless their name is on the register or a certificate is produced.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 941, pp. 1072–1078
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Hanson Graded School.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 941, pp. 1072–1078
statutes.summary: This act establishes a graded school district in Hanson, Kentucky. Section 2 explicitly states that only 'white children' are eligible for admission to the common schools within this district, and other 'white persons' may be admitted by trustees under prescribed terms. This segregation of educational facilities based on race is a hallmark of Jim Crow laws.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 969, p. 1123
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the county court at its court of claims to levy an ad valorem tax and fix the county levy in Adair county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 969, p. 1123
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the Adair County Court to levy an ad valorem tax for county purposes and a per capita tax from each white voter, not exceeding one dollar and fifty cents. The sheriff is responsible for collecting these taxes.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 407
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate and establish a system of public schools in district No. 49, including the town of Adairville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 407
statutes.summary: This act incorporates common school district No. 49, including the town of Adairville, into a school district under the control and management of trustees selected by the legal white voters within its limits. It establishes a Board of Trustees with corporate powers and outlines their responsibilities, quorum, vacancy filling, and eligibility requirements for trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 408
statutes.title: An Act to Establish a Public School in Adairville
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 408
statutes.summary: This act establishes a public school in Adairville and outlines the powers and duties of its board of trustees. Crucially, it explicitly states that only white children are eligible for admission to the school.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 409
statutes.title: An Act to amend an act entitled 'An Act to provide for the establishment and regulation of public schools in Adairville'
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 409
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning public schools in Adairville. It specifies that an annual tax of not exceeding seventy-five cents per one hundred dollars of property owned by white persons, and a capitation tax of not exceeding two dollars on each white male citizen over twenty-one, can be levied and collected for the Adairville public school district, provided a majority of resident voters approve the levy. The taxes are to be levied on the first Saturday in April and due on the first day of September, collected by a board-appointed collector.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1008, pp. 56–63
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a system of public graded schools in school district No. 2, in Bracken county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1008, pp. 56–63
statutes.summary: This act establishes a system of public graded schools for white children in school district No. 2, Bracken county. It specifies that the schools will be under the control and management of sixty trustees elected by qualified white voters of the district. It also mentions that any white widow of a pupil's age residing within the district is eligible to attend.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1101, pp. 251–253
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to organize and establish a system of publicschoo'sin the city of Henderson," approved March 15, 1869.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1101, pp. 251–253
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning taxation in the city of Louisville. It specifically repeals provisions that exempted property belonging to white persons from taxation and mandates that property belonging to all persons, regardless of color, shall be taxed alike. It also adjusts tax rates for common school purposes and includes property estimated under the equalization law and real estate owned by railroad or banking corporations.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1105, pp. 257–263
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a graded school at White Post, in Pike county, and to provide for maintaining same.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1105, pp. 257–263
statutes.summary: This act establishes a graded school in White Post, Pike County, Kentucky. It defines the boundaries of common school district No. 78, which is a fractional district composed of parts of Martin and Pike counties. The act specifies that the public school affairs for white children of pupil age residing within this district will be managed by five trustees elected by qualified white voters of the district. These trustees will be styled the 'Board of Trustees of Common'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1106, pp. 263–272
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of public graded schools in Madisonville, Hopkins county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1106, pp. 263–272
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the establishment and governance of public schools in specific districts. It explicitly states that only white children are to be admitted to these schools, and that white children residing within the district have free admission. It also allows for the admission of white children from outside the district upon payment of fees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1107, pp. 272–274
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate an institution of learning in or near Cadiz, in the county of Trigg.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1107, pp. 272–274
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the Cadiz Graded Colored School in Trigg County, Kentucky, establishing its name, management structure, and trustee appointments. It also outlines procedures for filling trustee vacancies and for the principal and trustees to solicit aid for the school's support.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1162, pp. 376–377
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a Normal School at Garrett, Meade county, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1162, pp. 376–377
statutes.summary: This act establishes a Normal School and outlines its governance, curriculum, and student admission policies. Notably, Section 3 explicitly states that the Normal School shall receive 'white students of both sexes'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1165, pp. 385–391
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a system of public and high schools in and for the town of Sebree, in the county of Webster, for white children only.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1165, pp. 385–391
statutes.summary: This act establishes a public and high school system in Sebree, Webster County, specifically for white children. It outlines the district boundaries, the establishment of a board of trustees, and the election process for these trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1236, pp. 483–484
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the punishment of petit larceny in Calloway county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1236, pp. 483–484
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of Cadiz, Trigg County, to allow the town trustees to levy taxes for the purchase of land and the erection/furnishing of a schoolhouse. Crucially, these taxes are to be levied *solely* on white persons and their property, and the school is to be *solely* for their use. This explicitly creates a racially segregated educational system funded by and for white residents.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1265, pp. 530–531
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the town of Belle Point.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1265, pp. 530–531
statutes.summary: This act empowers the board of trustees of Belle Point to levy an annual tax of not more than twenty-five cents on each one hundred dollars worth of taxable property of white citizens in the town to supplement the common school fund for a public school for white children.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1273, pp. 546–553
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a system of public graded schools in the city of Somerset, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1273, pp. 546–553
statutes.summary: This act establishes a system of public graded schools in Somerset, Kentucky. It defines the boundaries of school district No. 1 and outlines the control and management of the schools for white children by five trustees elected by qualified white voters. It also specifies who qualifies as a voter, including white widows and spinsters who own land, are taxpayers, or have children to educate.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1331, p. 641
statutes.title: AN ACT, entitled" An act to amend section five of an act to organize and establish a system of public schools in the city of Owensboro for white children for said city."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1331, p. 641
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law concerning public schools in Owensboro. It specifically states that the public school system is for 'white children' and outlines procedures for the expulsion of trustees who disturb the schools or abuse teachers. The amendment focuses on the governance and conduct within the school board and its officials, but the explicit mention of 'white children' in the context of public education is a strong indicator of racial segregation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1342, pp. 648–657
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the election and in part to define the duties of a mayor, board of councilmen and school trustees of the city of Frankfort, and to provide for the establishment of a board of commissioners to control the police and fire departments thereof, and to define their duties.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1342, pp. 648–657
statutes.summary: This statute mandates the creation of registration books for voters in Frankfort. These books must include columns for the voter's name, residence, color, and the election for which they are registered. Registration is to be conducted alphabetically. The statute explicitly requires a column for 'color' and states that the list of voters shall show 'whether he be white or colored.' This explicit racial categorization in the voter registration process is a hallmark of Jim Crow laws designed to disenfranchise Black voters.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1514, p. 903
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to establish a system of public and high schools for the town of Sebree, in the county of Webster, for white children only," approved April 19,1888.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1514, p. 903
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act that established public and high schools in Sebree, Kentucky, specifically for white children. The amendment strikes out the first section and inserts a new one, but the core intent of racial segregation in education remains. The new section reiterates the establishment of the Sebree Public and High Schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1515, pp. 904–905
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of Elizabethtown.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1515, pp. 904–905
statutes.summary: This act amends the charter of Elizabethtown, authorizing the board of trustees to issue bonds for town improvements. Crucially, it includes a provision stating that 'No colored person shall pay any of the tax named in said act or in this act.' This explicitly exempts Black individuals from paying taxes related to the town's funding, likely for school-related purposes given the preceding text about common school laws.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 114, pp. 482–484
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act to establish and maintain a graded free school in the town of Harrodsburg, Kentucky, approved March fifteenth, one thousand eight hundred and seventy-six.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 114, pp. 482–484
statutes.summary: This act details the taxation and funding mechanisms for a graded school in Mercer County. It explicitly states that taxes are to be levied on taxable property belonging to 'white persons' for the purpose of furnishing the school, fencing the lot, boring a well, and purchasing additional grounds. Further taxes can be imposed for school furniture, insurance, repairs, census taking, elections, janitors, fuel, and incidental expenses, also levied on property belonging to and controlled by 'white persons'. Additionally, patrons of the school are to be taxed to cover coal and incidental expenses.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 126, pp. 496–500
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to provide for organizing and establishing a system of public schools in Winchester," approved April fifteenth, one thousand eight hundred and seventy-two.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 126, pp. 496–500
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning public schools in Winchester. It relieves the board of trustees, elected by white voters, of any connection with or control over the colored public school or schools in the city.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 190, pp. 585–586
statutes.title: AN ACT to create Persimmon Grove voting precinct, in Campbell county, a magisterial district.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 190, pp. 585–586
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of colored common school district number two in Montgomery county to levy a poll tax of two dollars on each colored male person over twenty-one years old and an ad valorem tax of up to twenty-five cents per one hundred dollars on property owned by colored persons in the district for a period not exceeding three years. This is to pay for a school-house and lot purchased by the district.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 201, pp. 612–624
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to amend and reduce into one the several acts in relation to the town of Danville," approved March tenth, one thousand eight hundred and seventy-three.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 201, pp. 612–624
statutes.summary: This act details the process for voter registration in Danville, Kentucky. It specifies the appointment of registration officers, their duties, the format of the registration book (including fields for 'color'), and the days and hours for registration. It also outlines procedures for handling challenges to a person's right to register.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 205, p. 632
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of colored common school district number sixteen, Todd county..
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 205, p. 632
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the Superintendent of Public Instruction to issue a draft for $135.42 to John A. Dorris, county superintendent of common schools for Todd County, for the benefit of colored common school district number sixteen. This payment is to rectify an oversight in the census report for the school year ending June 30, 1888, where 61 pupils were omitted.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 206, pp. 633–634
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to amend, digest and reduce into one all the acts incorporating the city of Lexington," approved April nineteenth, one thousand eight hundred and eighty-two, and all acts amend a tory thereof.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 206, pp. 633–634
statutes.summary: This act re-enacts a section of the charter of the city of Lexington, requiring all voters in municipal elections to have paid their poll tax for the preceding year four days prior to the election, in addition to existing qualifications of residence and citizenship.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 250, pp. 737–739
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to establish a system of public graded schools in the city of Somerset, Kentucky."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 250, pp. 737–739
statutes.summary: This act amends an existing law concerning the school district of Somerset, Kentucky. It authorizes the board of trustees to levy an ad valorem tax and issue bonds for school purposes. Crucially, it grants the trustees the power to adopt the assessment of the city assessor of Somerset for property belonging to "white persons" within the city limits. This implies a separate assessment or differential treatment for property not belonging to white persons, which is a strong indicator of racial segregation in the context of Jim Crow era legislation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 266, pp. 773–801
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to regulate municipal elections in the city of Louisville."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 266, pp. 773–801
statutes.summary: This statute outlines procedures for voters who are unable to read, requiring them to make an affidavit to receive assistance in marking their ballot. The affidavit process involves the voter affirming their inability to read and the election clerk then marking the ballot on their behalf. This provision, while seemingly neutral, was historically used to disenfranchise Black voters by creating a barrier to voting that disproportionately affected them due to lower literacy rates resulting from systemic discrimination.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 327, pp. 905–916
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a city government for the town of North Middletown.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 327, pp. 905–916
statutes.summary: This section of the Laws of Kentucky from 1890 outlines the election process for city officials. Specifically, Section 6 details the qualifications for voting in city elections. It states that all male citizens entitled to vote for State Representative and who have resided in the city for one year are eligible. However, it includes a crucial proviso: no person shall be entitled to vote unless all taxes, fines, or other debts due to the city have been fully paid and discharged. This requirement for tax payment as a prerequisite for voting is a common feature of Jim Crow-era disenfranchisement tactics, often disproportionately affecting Black citizens.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 372, pp. 1015–1025
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of public schools in Slaughtersville, Webster county, for white children.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 372, pp. 1015–1025
statutes.summary: This act establishes a public school system in Slaughtersville, Webster County, specifically for white children. It outlines the boundaries of the school district and the formation and powers of a five-person Board of Trustees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 495, pp. 1384–1394
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of public graded schools in Lancaster, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 495, pp. 1384–1394
statutes.summary: This act incorporates a specific territory as a school district, 'The Graded City School District of Lancaster, Kentucky'. It explicitly states that the board of trustees will be elected by 'legal white voters' within the district. Additionally, it defines qualified voters to include any 'white widow or spinster' owning land, residing therein, who is a tax-payer or has children to be educated. The act also mentions the ages for education (six and twenty years).

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 497, pp. 97–100
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend section one, article one, chapter ninety-four, General Statutes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 497, pp. 97–100
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law regarding railroad taxation for school purposes. Crucially, Section 5 explicitly states that the provisions of this act shall NOT apply to any colored school district. This creates a separate and unequal system for taxation and funding of schools based on race, a hallmark of Jim Crow legislation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 508, pp. 1416–1424
statutes.title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of public graded schools in Junction City, Boyle county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 508, pp. 1416–1424
statutes.summary: This act establishes the Junction City Public Graded School District and outlines the powers and duties of its board of trustees. Crucially, it explicitly states that only white children shall be admitted to these schools, while also granting equal rights of admission to all white children residing within the district.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 53, pp. 390–392
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled An act to amend an act, entitled 'An act to incorporate Hickman College," approved April twentieth, one thousand eight hundred and eighty-eight.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 53, pp. 390–392
statutes.summary: This act allows the trustees of Hickman College to submit a question to the legally qualified white voters of Hickman City regarding a $3,000 subscription by taxation to complete and furnish the college building and improve its grounds. The election is to be held on the first Wednesday in April, 1890.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 64, pp. 401–402
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Mrs. Daisy E. Harvey, common school teacher in colored school district number six, Fulton county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 64, pp. 401–402
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the county superintendent of Fulton County to pay Daisy E. Harvey, a teacher in colored district number six, the full apportionment for the school year ending June 30, 1890, upon completion of the school term. It also includes a separate act concerning school bonds for Knott County.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 96, pp. 455–456
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the Buffalo Spring Cemetery Com - pany, Lincoln county, Kentucky.
