statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate Clay City, in Powell county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 908, pp. 994–1032
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the qualifications for policemen in Clay City, including citizenship, residency, age, literacy, and criminal history. It restricts eligibility based on the ability to read and write English, which historically could disproportionately affect Black individuals due to systemic educational inequalities.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 927, pp. 1063–1079
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a road law for Floyd county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 927, pp. 1063–1079
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the requirements for individuals to participate in road service, including conditions for exemption based on physical ability and the provision for substitutes. It establishes a system that could disproportionately affect certain groups, particularly Black Kentuckians, by enforcing manual labor obligations.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 931, pp. 1081–1097
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide a road law for Johnson county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 931, pp. 1081–1097
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the obligations of road workers in Kentucky, including penalties for failing to work or pay for a substitute. It establishes a system of enforcement that could disproportionately affect Black workers under Jim Crow laws.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 934, pp. 1102–1107
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act to incorporate the town of Fancy Farm, in Graves county, approved April first, one thousand eight hundred and eighty.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 934, pp. 1102–1107
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the duties of the town marshal in Graves County, including the collection of taxes and fines, and the confinement of individuals convicted of misdemeanors. It allows for the confinement of individuals who fail to pay fines, which can lead to forced labor on public improvements, reflecting punitive measures that disproportionately affected marginalized groups.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 938, pp. 1122–1136
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate and define the corporate limits of the town of East Point, in Johnson county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 938, pp. 1122–1136
statutes.summary: This statute establishes the election process for trustees in the Town of East Point, requiring voters to have paid their poll tax, which historically disenfranchised Black citizens and other marginalized groups.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 962, pp. 1170–1171
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Clinton.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 962, pp. 1170–1171
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that offenders of city ordinances may be sentenced to hard labor on public works as a penalty for misdemeanors, with specific provisions for the duration of labor based on fines. It explicitly exempts females from this labor requirement.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 965, pp. 1174–1176
statutes.title: AN ACT to extend and better define the limits of the city of Frankfort.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 965, pp. 1174–1176
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the land description for the Colored Normal School, indicating a separate educational institution for Black individuals, which reflects the segregationist policies of the Jim Crow era.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 967, pp. 1178–1206
statutes.title: AN ACT to regulate municipal elections in city of Bowling Green.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 967, pp. 1178–1206
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the responsibilities of the mayor regarding the preparation and security of election materials, including ballots and stubs, with strict measures to prevent unauthorized access to these materials. It emphasizes the control of election processes, which historically has been used to disenfranchise Black voters.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 968, pp. 1206–1214
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the registration of voters in the city of Bowling Green.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 968, pp. 1206–1214
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the appointment and duties of registration officers in Bowling Green, emphasizing that only voters and housekeepers in the precinct can serve. It includes provisions for maintaining order and verifying the qualifications of individuals seeking to register, which could be used to disenfranchise certain groups.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 974, pp. 1216–1221
statutes.title: AN ACT authorizing the establishment of a graded free school in district number sixteen, Fulton county, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 974, pp. 1216–1221
statutes.summary: This statute establishes a tax levy specifically for white voters in a designated school district to fund a graded free school and pay off bonds for Hickman College, effectively excluding non-white individuals from participating in the tax and educational benefits.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 978, pp. 1228–1234
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a system of public graded schools in the city of Pineville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 978, pp. 1228–1234
statutes.summary: This statute establishes a public graded school system in Pineville, Kentucky, specifically for white children, controlled by trustees elected by qualified white voters, thereby enforcing racial segregation in education.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 984, pp. 1253–1282
statutes.title: AN ACT to regulate municipal elections in the city of Paducah.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 984, pp. 1253–1282
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the procedures for municipal elections, including the nomination of candidates, the printing of ballots, and the responsibilities of the mayor and election officers. It emphasizes the need for strict control over election materials to prevent tampering.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 996, pp. 1307–1313
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a public graded school at the mouth of Beaver, in Floyd county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 996, pp. 1307–1313
statutes.summary: This statute establishes the Mouth of Beaver Graded Free School and outlines its governance by a board of trustees elected exclusively by white qualified voters, indicating a racially discriminatory practice in educational governance.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 997, pp. 1314–1316
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the University Club of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 997, pp. 1314–1316
statutes.summary: This statute incorporates the University Club of Louisville, establishing it as a body corporate with specific membership and stock ownership rules that implicitly restrict membership to certain demographics.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1222, p. 53
statutes.title: AN ACT to allow the citizens of this Commonwealth to meet, organize, hold lodge meetings or religious services in the district school-houses of this State.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1222, p. 53
statutes.summary: This act grants citizens the right to use district schoolhouses for meetings and religious services, provided it does not conflict with school operations. Crucially, it explicitly states that white citizens cannot use schoolhouses intended for colored children, and vice versa. This provision is limited to Marshall and Lyon counties.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1268, pp. 174–175
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act to incorporate an institution of learning in or near Cadiz, in the county of Trigg," approved April sixteenth, one thousand eight hundred and eighty-eight.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1268, pp. 174–175
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning the town of Trigg. It replaces the name 'Cadiz Graded Colored School' with 'The Baptist Normal Institute' and updates the corresponding 'Trustees of the Cadiz Graded School' to 'Trustees of the Baptist Normal Institute'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1340, pp. 379–387
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for a registration of voters in the city of Owensboro.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1340, pp. 379–387
statutes.summary: This statute mandates the creation of two registration books for each precinct in Owensboro. One book is kept in the registrar's office, and the other is provided to registration and election clerks. The books are to be arranged alphabetically by voter name and include columns for 'NAME', 'Residence', 'Special Elections', 'December Election', 'August Election', 'Color', and 'Remarks'. Section 5 details the registration process, requiring officers to attend voting places on the first Monday in July and the two succeeding days, from 6 AM to 7 PM. They are to record qualified voters who apply, noting their name, residence (including street and number), and whether they are 'white or colored'. The statute also includes a provision to omit a registration day if it falls on the fourth of the month.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1427, pp. 522–524
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a graded school in common school district number one, in Leslie county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1427, pp. 522–524
statutes.summary: This act establishes a graded school in district number one of Leslie County, Kentucky. It outlines the boundaries of the district, the style and powers of the board of trustees, and specifies that the board shall be elected by white voters of the district. It also states that all white pupils between the ages of six and twenty residing in the district are eligible to attend.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1431, p. 534
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize district number eighty-three, in Barren county, to vote a tax for three years for the purpose of extending the session of said school.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1431, p. 534
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of white common school district number eighty-three in Barren county to submit a proposition to legal white voters. The proposition is to assess a tax for three years of twenty-five cents on each one hundred dollars of white taxable property and a per capita tax of one dollar on each white legal voter annually. The purpose of this tax is to extend the school session by at least three months each year.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1460, pp. 583–588
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to establish a system of common schools for the town of Beech Grove; McLean county," approved April twenty-two, one thousand eight hundred and eighty—two, and to repeal an act amend a tory there to, approved March twenty—five, one thousand eight hundred and…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1460, pp. 583–588
statutes.summary: This act amends the establishment of a board of education for the Louisville district. It outlines the election process for board members, their powers and duties, and the appointment of an assessor. Crucially, Section 4 explicitly states that the assessor's duty is to 'take a list of all property of white persons in said district subject to taxation for the State revenue.'

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1487, pp. 696–697
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of E. L. Garnett, James Carman and John W. Wrather, late trustees in and for common school district number forty-two, Graves county, Kentucky. -
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1487, pp. 696–697
statutes.summary: This act empowers the trustees of district number forty-two to levy a poll-tax on legal white voters and a property tax to pay for desks and seats purchased for the district, and to reimburse individuals for costs incurred in a legal dispute over the election and the purchase. It also orders the sheriff to refund collected tax money.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1517, pp. 791–793
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to incorporate the Williamsburg Institute," approved April sixth, one thousand eight hundred and eighty-eight.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1517, pp. 791–793
statutes.summary: This statute incorporates an institute and grants it powers related to property, contracts, and operations. Crucially, it explicitly states that 'none but white pupils shall ever be admitted in the school of said institute.'

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1528, pp. 804–805
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of common school districts numbers thirty—three and thirty-four, of Henderson county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1528, pp. 804–805
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of consolidated common school districts numbers thirty-three and thirty-four in Henderson County, Kentucky, to submit to the qualified white voters of said districts a proposition regarding the districts. The submission is to occur at a general or special election, with thirty days' notice given by publication in local newspapers or by posting written or printed notices.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1572, pp. 957–1000
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the city of Maysville, in Mason county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1572, pp. 957–1000
statutes.summary: This section of the statute outlines the duties of the city assessor in Louisville, Kentucky, for the year 1890. It mandates that the assessor maintain two separate lists or books for property assessment: one for white individuals and one for black individuals. The statute details the information to be included in these assessment lists, such as names, age, property descriptions, and values of various assets.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1606, pp. 1104–1116
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for a registration of voters in the city of Co ving- 1 ton.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1606, pp. 1104–1116
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for general voter registration in Kentucky for the year 1890. It specifies the dates and hours for registration, the information to be recorded in the registration book (including name, address, and whether the person is white or colored), and the qualifications for registration. It also details a provision for omitting a registration day if it falls on the fourth of the month.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1657, pp. 1223–1225
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of white school district number twenty-eight, of Madison county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1657, pp. 1223–1225
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of a specific white school district in Madison County to issue bonds up to $20,000 for building and furnishing schoolhouses. It also establishes a tax mechanism to redeem these bonds and pay interest. The statute explicitly mentions 'white' school district and begins to discuss the assessment of property for 'colored people' in the last sentence, indicating a racial distinction in the application of the law or its context.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1658, p. 1225
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of Bedford common school district number six(white), in Trimble county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1658, p. 1225
statutes.summary: This act empowers the trustees of Bedford common school district number six (white) in Trimble county to levy an additional annual property tax and poll tax for two years, not exceeding twenty-five cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property and one dollar per white poll, respectively. These funds are specifically for repairing and furnishing the common school-house of said district.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1760, pp. 1412–1427
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to reduce into one, amend and digest the acts and amend a tory acts incorporating the city of Mount Sterling," approved March seventh, one thousand eighth un—dred and seventy-six.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1760, pp. 1412–1427
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for voter registration in Mount Sterling, Kentucky. It mandates the use of registration books with specific columns, including 'Color'. Registration officers are required to attend voting places for two days to register qualified voters who personally appear. The statute also details procedures for swearing in and interrogating potential registrants if their identity or qualifications are questioned.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1785, pp. 1497–1500
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the "C. T. Rice Cemetery Company," near Union, in Boone county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1785, pp. 1497–1500
statutes.summary: This act incorporates the Evergreen Cemetery Company and outlines its powers and regulations. Notably, Section 13 explicitly prohibits the interment of colored persons in any lot within the cemetery, with forfeiture of the lot and improvements for any owner who attempts such an interment. The company is also empowered to prohibit such interments.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1809, pp. 1543–1547
statutes.title: AN ACT to incorporate the Ekron Male and Female College, of Meade county, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Local and Private Acts], 1890, ch. 1809, pp. 1543–1547
statutes.summary: This act details the funding and operation of a common school in the Ekron common school district. It specifies that a tax levy can be imposed, collected by the sheriff, and used exclusively for maintaining the common school. Crucially, it states that 'every white child in the Ekron common school district between the ages of six and twenty years shall have the right to attend the said common school'.

statutes.statute_citation: Kentucky Jurisprudence, 1890, p. 228
statutes.title: Devolution of Landed Estates
citations: Kentucky Jurisprudence, 1890, p. 228
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky statutes, from 1890, discusses inheritance laws. Specifically, point 6 states that the issue of a marriage between a white person and a negro or mulatto is void. This explicitly addresses and prohibits interracial marriage.

statutes.statute_citation: Kentucky Jurisprudence, 1890, p. 542
statutes.title: Marriage and Divorce
citations: Kentucky Jurisprudence, 1890, p. 542
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the requirements and conditions for marriage and divorce in Kentucky. It addresses the legalization of cohabitation for former slaves, the authority of ministers to solemnize marriages, void marriages due to incestuous relationships, idiocy, lunacy, or bigamy. Crucially, it explicitly states that a marriage is void 'between a white person and a negro or mulatto (less than one eighth of negro blood not being considered)'.

statutes.statute_citation: Kentucky Jurisprudence, 1890, p. 713
statutes.title: Tax on Negroes for Common Schools
citations: Kentucky Jurisprudence, 1890, p. 713
statutes.summary: This statute discusses a case where a tax was levied on 'negroes' to fund common schools. The court held this law unconstitutional under the Fourteenth Amendment, implying that the collection of this tax was unauthorized. The case highlights the discriminatory nature of funding public education based on race, which is a hallmark of Jim Crow era legislation.

statutes.statute_citation: Constitution of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, § 185, pp. 53–54
statutes.title: SEC. 185. The General Assembly shall make provision, by law, for the payment of the interest of said school fund, and may provide for the sale of the stock in the Bank of Kentucky; and in case of a sale of all or any part of said stock, the proceeds of sale shall be invested by the Sinking Fund…
citations: Constitution of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, § 185, pp. 53–54
statutes.summary: This section mandates that in the distribution of the school fund, no distinction shall be made on account of race or color, but explicitly states that separate schools for white and colored children shall be maintained.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 103, pp. 304–393
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to Revenue and Taxation.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 103, pp. 304–393
statutes.summary: This statute amends an existing act concerning railroad taxation. Specifically, it addresses how taxes levied in common school districts are to be distributed. Section 6 explicitly states that the provisions of the law shall not apply to any colored school district, but then outlines a method for distributing railroad taxes between white and colored common school districts located within the same boundaries. This distribution is to be based on the ratio of white to colored children of pupil age residing in the district.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 117, pp. 420–423
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a board of children'sguardians in counties in which thereis a city of the first class, defining the powers and duties of said board, and providing for a special county tax for the establishment and maintenance of homes under the care of such board.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 117, pp. 420–423
statutes.summary: This act establishes a board of children's guardians in counties with a first-class city. The board is to be composed of six persons, two of whom shall be colored. The board will be a corporate body responsible for children's welfare and will be funded by a special county tax.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 205, pp. 952–968
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to husband and wife, and entitled"Husband and Wife."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 205, pp. 952–968
statutes.summary: This act outlines prohibited marriages, including those between a white person and a negro or mulatto. It also details other grounds for void marriages, such as mental incapacity, existing marriages, and improper solemnization.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 211, pp. 990–993
statutes.title: AN ACT concerning the State Normal School for Colored Persons.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 211, pp. 990–993
statutes.summary: This act places the State Normal School for Colored Persons under the control and supervision of a board of trustees. The board will consist of the Superintendent of Public Instruction as ex officio chairman and three appointed residents of Franklin county. The board is constituted as a body corporate with the power to sue and be sued, and to hold funds and property for the school.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 222, pp. 1092–1154
statutes.title: AN ACT for the government of cities of the third class.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 222, pp. 1092–1154
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that the board of education provide separate buildings and schools for the education of white and black pupils, explicitly prohibiting white children from attending colored schools and colored children from attending white schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 239, pp. 1236–1237
statutes.title: AN ACT to empower the trustees of the State Normal School for Colored Persons at Frankfort to build a dormitory.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 239, pp. 1236–1237
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the trustees of the State Normal School for Colored Persons at Frankfort to build a dormitory for students attending the school. It also appropriates $2,000 for its construction.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 241, pp. 1238–1283
statutes.title: AN ACT for the government of cities of the fourth class.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 241, pp. 1238–1283
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that cities provide separate buildings and schools for the education of white and black pupils, explicitly prohibiting white children from attending colored schools and vice versa. It also outlines administrative duties for the board of education.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 244, pp. 1292–1370
statutes.title: AN ACT for the government of cities of the first class.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 244, pp. 1292–1370
statutes.summary: This section mandates the segregation of schools by race, stating that no white child shall attend a school for colored children, and no colored child shall attend a school for white children. Schools for both races must be kept and maintained separately.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 246, pp. 1371–1372
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the levy and collection of a tax in certain common school districts to pay off indebtedness incurred by the trustees of such school districts in erecting and furnishing school -houses.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 246, pp. 1371–1372
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous act concerning the State Penitentiary. It allows the Commissioners of the Sinking Fund to purchase materials and employ prisoners for construction and repairs at the penitentiary. It also declares an emergency due to idle prisoners, making the act effective immediately upon passage. However, a separate section from the same source document, likely a preceding or following section on the same page, states that no tax shall be levied or collected from the property of colored persons to pay any indebtedness incurred for the benefit of schools for white children.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 260, pp. 1440–1518
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for an efficient system of common schools throughout the State.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 260, pp. 1440–1518
statutes.summary: This act establishes a comprehensive system for common schools in Kentucky, divided into various articles covering the school fund, board of education, superintendents, districts, taxation, graded common schools, teachers, institutes, libraries, and specifically 'Colored Schools'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 40, pp. 90–91
statutes.title: AN ACT to regulate the travel or transportation of the white and colored passengers on the railroads of this State.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 40, pp. 90–91
statutes.summary: This act requires railroad companies operating in Kentucky to provide separate coaches or compartments for white and colored passengers. Each separate coach or compartment must be clearly marked to indicate the race for which it is designated. The law also mandates that there be no discrimination in the quality, convenience, or accommodations provided for either race.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 65, pp. 133–201
statutes.title: AN ACT to regulate elections in this Commonwealth. I. General Provisions.ARTICLE ARTICLE II. Precincts. ARTICLE III. Elections, how conducted. ARTICLE IV. Registration. ARTICLE V. Canvassing returns. ARTICLE VI. Time of holding elections. ARTICLE VII. Vacancies, how filled. ARTICLE VIII. Contested…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1891, ch. 65, pp. 133–201
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for voter registration in Kentucky cities. It specifies the dates and times for registration, the information to be recorded in the registration book, and the requirements for a person to be registered. Crucially, it mandates that the registration book must record whether an applicant is 'white or colored'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 100, pp. 253–333
statutes.title: AN ACT for the government of cities of the second class in the Commonwealth of Kentucky. ART CLE I. Municipalities.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 100, pp. 253–333
statutes.summary: This section mandates the establishment and maintenance of separate schools for white and colored children in cities of the first class. It states that colored schools shall be entitled to the same benefits, governed by the same rules, and subject to the same restrictions as white schools. The statute explicitly mentions 'colored children' and 'white children', indicating a racial segregation in education.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 48, pp. 115–136
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to the Asylums for the Insane, and the Institution for Feeble-minded Children, supported by the State.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 48, pp. 115–136
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that white and colored patients shall not be kept in the same buildings within asylums. It also outlines procedures for admitting and discharging patients, including provisions for pauper idiots and pay patients from other states.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 55, pp. 153–171
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to provide for an efficient system of common schools throughout the State," approved July sixth, one thousand eight hundred and ninety-three.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 55, pp. 153–171
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for obtaining teachers' certificates in Kentucky. It mandates separate examination schedules for white and colored teachers, with white teachers examined on the first Friday and Saturday of specified months, and colored teachers on the second Friday and Saturday of the same months. The statute also specifies that the State Board of Examiners shall prepare separate series of questions for white and colored teachers, all of the same grade.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 66, pp. 182–185
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act to regulate elections in this Commonwealth, approved June thirtieth, one thousand eight hundred and ninety—two.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 66, pp. 182–185
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous election regulation act by modifying the form of the registration book. The new form includes a field for 'Color', which was not present in the original form. This addition is significant as it introduces a racial classification into voter registration.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 91, pp. 227–228
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act for the government of cities of the fourth class," approved June twenty-eighth, one thousand eight hundred and ninety-three.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1894, ch. 91, pp. 227–228
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law concerning cities of the fourth class. It mandates that public school funding from the state common school fund be distributed separately to 'white boards of education' and 'colored boards of education' based on the per capita amount for each white child and colored child of pupil age, respectively. It also outlines the process for establishing school districts and appointing trustees in these cities.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1896, ch. 18, pp. 43–46
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend section sixty-three of an act entitled "An act to provide an efficient system of common schools throughout the State," approved July sixth, one thousand eight hundred and ninety -three.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1896, ch. 18, pp. 43–46
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law regarding teacher certification. It establishes separate examination dates for white and colored teachers, with white teachers examined on the third Friday and Saturday of May, June, July, and August, and colored teachers examined on the fourth Friday and Saturday of the same months. The State Board of Examiners is also required to prepare separate sets of questions for white and colored teachers of the same grade.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1896, ch. 33, pp. 74–83
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish houses of reform, one for boys and one for girls, and to provide for the government thereof and making an appropriation therefor.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1896, ch. 33, pp. 74–83
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law concerning the protection of food fish. However, a preceding section (§ 20) within the provided text mandates that children of white and colored races committed to the Houses of Reform shall be provided with separate departments. This indicates a segregation policy within correctional institutions.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1896, ch. 36, pp. 86–88
statutes.title: AN ACT concerning the education of children.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1896, ch. 36, pp. 86–88
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law regarding compulsory education for children. It outlines exemptions for children taught at home, those with physical or mental disabilities, or those excused by trustees. Crucially, it includes a provision that excuses attendance if there is no "white school, in the case of white children, or colored school, in the case of colored children, taught within two miles by the nearest traveled road." This explicitly mandates separate educational facilities based on race and implies unequal access or availability of schools for Black children.

statutes.title: Resolution concerning the State Normal School for colored persons
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1896, p. 19
statutes.summary: This resolution makes an additional appropriation to extend the grounds and enlarge the buildings of the State Normal School for colored persons.

statutes.statute_citation: Kentucky Common School Laws., 1896, p. 171
statutes.title: District Taxation Under Special Act of Legislature
citations: Kentucky Common School Laws., 1896, p. 171
statutes.summary: This statute addresses district taxation for school purposes in the Robards District. A special act authorized a tax of 75 cents per $100 of property value and $5 per poll to erect buildings and maintain a ten-month school. The act explicitly states it does not apply to negroes or their property, though white taxpayers could not complain on this basis. The statute also details requirements for notice posting, the object of the vote, and the need for a trustee order designating the tax amount, even if not formally recorded.

statutes.statute_citation: Kentucky Common School Laws., 1896, p. 175
statutes.title: E. TOWN SCHOOL DISTRICT vs. L. & N. R. R.
citations: Kentucky Common School Laws., 1896, p. 175
statutes.summary: This case addresses the collection of delinquent taxes owed to school districts. It states that taxes due before November 11, 1892, are to be collected by trustees, while taxes due after that date must be collected by the county superintendent. Crucially, the ruling states that a corporation cannot avoid taxation by claiming it has no color, as all property is taxed except that belonging to colored people. This explicitly indicates a racially discriminatory tax exemption.

statutes.statute_citation: Kentucky Common School Laws., 1896, p. 177
statutes.title: Abstracts of Decisions, Etc. - Taxation for Schools
citations: Kentucky Common School Laws., 1896, p. 177
statutes.summary: This section outlines the taxation policies for common schools, specifically stating that taxes for white schools are to be levied on white property owners, and taxes for colored schools are to be levied on colored property owners. It also addresses how corporation property taxes are to be distributed between white and colored schools.

statutes.title: Kentucky Common School Laws - 1896
citations: Kentucky Common School Laws., 1896, p. 184
statutes.summary: This document outlines legal forms and procedures for school officers, teachers, trustees, and county superintendents in Kentucky. It includes sections on appointing examiners, adopting textbooks, reporting census data, and handling school finances. Notably, it contains separate entries for 'White' and 'Colored' census reports and election notices, indicating a legally mandated segregation in the education system.

It also specifies that voters will elect six trustees if the tax is approved. The process involves petitions, endorsements from county superintendents and trustees, and a court order directing the sheriff to hold an election.

It includes a sample notice for a sheriff to post, detailing the requirements for voters in an election to establish such a district. Crucially, the notice explicitly states that 'Those who may vote, are all white males over twenty-one years old...' This restriction on voting eligibility based on race is a hallmark of Jim Crow era legislation.

However, it also includes a segregation clause: 'but no white child shall be permitted to attend or become a pupil in any school for colored children, and no colored child shall be'. This section directly mandates racial segregation in schools.

statutes.summary: This statute outlines the conditions for forming graded free school districts and establishing graded free schools. It details the tax limits, the voting process, the organization of school districts under a board of trustees, and the powers and duties of these trustees. Notably, it specifies free tuition for 'resident white pupil-children' and terms of admission for others, and includes a poll tax levied on 'each white male person twenty-one years of age or over'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1897, ch. 16, pp. 36–37
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and re-enact section thirty-nine of article five, of an act entitled,"An act to provide for an efficient system of common schools throughout the State," approved July sixth, eighteen—hundred and ninety -three.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1897, ch. 16, pp. 36–37
statutes.summary: This statute amends the process for electing county superintendents. It specifies that in counties with cities of the first or second class that maintain separate public school systems, the county superintendent must reside outside of these cities and be elected only by voters residing outside of these cities. This creates a separate electoral and potentially administrative sphere for education based on the presence of separate school systems, which were often racially segregated under Jim Crow.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1897, ch. 21, pp. 48–49
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Kentucky, and the State Normal School for Colored Persons, of Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1897, ch. 21, pp. 48–49
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the Commissioners of the Sinking Fund to issue a bond of $165,000 to fund the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Kentucky and the State Normal School for Colored Persons. The bond bears 6% interest, payable semi-annually. The interest payments are to be divided between the two institutions, with the State Normal School for Colored Persons receiving $627.75 and the Agricultural and Mechanical College receiving $4,322.25 each semi-annual period.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1897, ch. 25, pp. 57–59
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act entitled, "An act to provide for an efficient system of common schools throughout the State," approved July sixth, 1893.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1897, ch. 25, pp. 57–59
statutes.summary: This act amends a previous law concerning common schools. It allows for the creation of graded common school districts upon petition from legal voters who are taxpayers. The key provision is that the election to approve an annual tax for these districts is to be held for the purpose of taking the sense of the 'legal white voters' in the proposed district. This explicitly limits participation in the voting process to white individuals.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1898, ch. 39, pp. 119–120
statutes.title: AN ACT to allow the children of slave marriages to inherit the property of their fathers and mothers.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1898, ch. 39, pp. 119–120
statutes.summary: This act grants inheritance rights to children born from slave marriages in Kentucky. It specifies that if parents who cohabited as husband and wife during slavery die as property owners, their children from such unions are considered lawful heirs. However, if either parent later legally married another person and had children from that subsequent marriage, the children from the slave marriage would only inherit a proportion of the property based on the ratio of children from the slave marriage to children from the legal marriage.

statutes.summary: This statute amends Section 72 of Chapter 113 of the Acts of 1891-2, which governs the election and qualifications of school trustees. The amendment specifically addresses the qualifications for teachers, stating that for white schools, teachers must be able to read and write, and for colored schools, this is only required 'if practicable'.

statutes.summary: This statute mandates compulsory education for all children, with specific provisions for separate schools for white and colored children. It outlines penalties for parents who fail to comply and for school officials who neglect their duties. Crucially, it explicitly prohibits white children from attending colored schools and colored children from attending white schools, enforcing racial segregation in education.

It mandates the apportionment of railroad taxes between white and colored schools based on the proportion of colored pupil children to the total number of pupil children within the white district's boundaries. It also specifies that taxes on private corporations for graded schools are to be taxed only for the schools of the owner's race, and agreements for different apportionment methods are void.

statutes.summary: This section details the taxation of railroad property for school districts and mandates the apportionment of these taxes between white and colored schools based on the number of pupils in each. It explicitly states that railroad taxes cannot be levied for a school district unless taxes are also levied on the property of white persons in the same district. Furthermore, it outlines the method for apportioning funds to colored districts based on the ratio of colored children to the total pupil population within the white district's boundary. The statute also clarifies that this apportionment rule applies only to railroad taxes and not to taxes on other corporations, and that stock owned by individuals is taxed for the respective white or colored schools they belong to. Agreements for apportionment contrary to the school law are deemed nullities.
