statutes.title: § 3374. Property taxed as of date fixed by city councilor commissioners—corporate property and franchises.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 3374, pp. 854–855
The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 3374, pp. 856–857
The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 3374, pp. 864–865
statutes.summary: This statute, amended in 1918, states that any child of the 'colored' race shall have the right to attend and receive instruction in a 'colored' school. This implies a system of segregated education based on race.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 3586
statutes.title: § 3586. A graded white school district which employed a truant officer has no cause of action against a colored school district having the same boundary, because part of the services of the truant officer were rendered for the colored school dis-
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 3586, p. 903
statutes.summary: This statute addresses a legal case where a graded white school district sued a colored school district for services rendered by a truant officer. The court ruled that the white school district had no cause of action against the colored school district for these services, even though the truant officer served both districts.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 3587a-27
statutes.title: § 3587a-27. Schools for colored children.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 3587a-27, pp. 923–924
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that the board of education shall provide, maintain, and support separate schools or provide for the education of all colored children who are bona fide residents of the city.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 3588
statutes.title: § 3588. This section has no application where a city adopts section 3588a and establishes a graded common school for white pupils and also one for colored pupils, both under the control of a school board. Thornton v.White, 162 Ky. 796, 173 S. W. 167.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 3588, pp. 926–927
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 3588, pp. 2026–2027
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the system for public schools in fourth-class cities, establishing a Board of Education with trustees elected from each ward. It details their qualifications, election process, terms, and powers, including the ability to contract, sue, and manage school property and funds. A note indicates that this section does not apply if a city adopts a separate act establishing graded common schools for white and colored pupils, both under the control of a school board. It also mentions that taxes imposed on railroad companies must be apportioned between schools for white and colored children.

While the ordinance was initially sustained, it was later reversed by the U.S. Supreme Court. The text also touches upon the principle of equal, though not necessarily identical, privileges for white and colored persons.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4099
statutes.title: § 4099. This section supersedes in part section 3588a relating to the establishment of graded schools for white and colored children and taxation therefor.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4099, p. 1030
statutes.summary: This statute addresses the taxation of railroad or bridge company property within graded white common school districts. It states that taxes levied on such property must be apportioned when collected.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4399a-3
statutes.title: § 4399a-3. Election of county superintendent.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4399a-3, p. 1125
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the eligibility requirements for the office of county superintendent in counties that have a system of public schools separate and distinct from the common schools of the county, specifically in counties embracing a city of the first or second class. It mandates that such a superintendent must be a resident of the county outside of the city or town. It also lists other county officials and teachers who are ineligible to hold the office of county superintendent. The statute further details the election process, term of office, and bond requirements for county superintendents. A key provision states that in counties with separate school systems in cities of the first or second class, the county superintendent must reside outside such cities and be elected by voters residing outside those cities.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4420a-3
statutes.title: § 4420a-3. White and colored school districts.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4420a-3, p. 1137
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4420a-3, p. 2414
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for collecting and distributing school taxes levied on railroad and bridge companies. It explicitly states that the provisions of the law do not apply to colored school districts. However, it mandates that taxes collected from railroad and bridge companies in white graded or common school subdistricts shall be apportioned and distributed between the white school district and any colored common school district located over the same boundary. The distribution ratio is based on the proportion of white children of pupil age and colored children of pupil age residing in the district or subdistrict.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4426a-5
statutes.title: § 4426a-5. Consolidation of subdistricts.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4426a-5, p. 1159
The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4426a-5, p. 1161
statutes.summary: This statute grants county boards of education the power to consolidate contiguous school subdistricts for either white or colored children. It outlines provisions for building or acquiring schoolhouses in convenient locations with sufficient capacity for the consolidated student population. These schools are to be known as consolidated schools. The statute also details the election of a single trustee for each consolidated school, the employment of teachers, and prohibits financial interests of trustees, board members, or county superintendents in school contracts.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4468a-3
statutes.title: § 4468a-3. Graded schools in cities of the first, second, third and fourth classes not affected acceptance of this law—provisions.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4468a-3, pp. 1184–1185
statutes.summary: This statute, specifically § 44680-3, explicitly prohibits any "colored child" from attending any "graded common school for white children." It also outlines provisions for the establishment and governance of graded common schools in cities of various classes, including mechanisms for cities to accept the provisions of the general graded common school law. Sections § 4468a-2 and § 4468a-3 detail how cities of the fifth/sixth class and cities of the first/second/third/fourth class, respectively, can adopt these provisions, with some modifications for larger cities.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4481
statutes.title: § 4481. [Repealed March 18, 1916, с. 24, p.162, preliminary provisions.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4481, pp. 1189–1190
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4481, pp. 2458–2459
statutes.summary: This section, as interpreted by court cases, outlines the process for bond issues for school purposes in graded common school districts. Crucially, it states that in elections for white graded schools, colored voters are not entitled to vote, their property will not be taxed for such buildings or maintenance, and their children cannot attend these schools. It also addresses election procedures for trustees and bond issues.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4526b-4
statutes.title: § 4526b-4. Adjacent counties may erect and maintain joint high school—contracts for—laws governing.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4526b-4, p. 1221
Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 87, pp. 113–114
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4526b-4, p. 2478
statutes.summary: This statute allows adjacent counties to jointly erect, organize, and maintain county high schools. It specifies that contracts for these joint high schools must be in writing and detail terms for teacher employment, curriculum, and general operation. Crucially, the statute explicitly states that such a contract 'may be made for the operation of either white or colored high schools.' It also permits counties to contract with existing city or graded schools for joint use.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4526c-6

citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4526c-6, p. 1223

It mandates free tuition for colored teachers in training for colored common schools and for colored boys and girls who have reached sixteen and completed common school. The appropriation cannot be used for real estate purchase or improvement.

The appropriation cannot be used for real estate purchase or improvement.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4534c
statutes.title: § 4534c. Additional appropriation for.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4534c, pp. 1227–1228
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the tuition policies for a normal school specifically for "colored residents of Kentucky." It states that tuition will be free to these residents if they meet certain conditions. It also details how tuition rates and admission conditions for non-residents will be set by the board. The statute also includes provisions for sectarian teaching, trustee visits, reports to the legislature, and annual appropriations for the school, explicitly naming it the "Colored Normal School Fund" and later the "Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons."

statutes.title: § 4758. (7.) Person failing so to labor during period of war with Germany a vagrant—penalty—prosecutions—possession of independent means not a defense.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4758, pp. 1279–1280
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4758-7, pp. 2598–2599
statutes.summary: This statute defines vagrancy and outlines penalties, including fines and mandatory labor on public works. It specifies that the possession of sufficient money or property, or the inability to obtain work, are not valid defenses against vagrancy charges. The law also details court jurisdiction, appeals, and sentence suspension mechanisms. A key provision states that proof of habitual loitering, intoxication, drug addiction, professional gambling, or being supported by the labor of others (while able-bodied) constitutes prima facie evidence of vagrancy. The statute also mandates that half the value of labor performed by convicted vagrants be paid towards the support of their dependents, if any.

These colored schools are to be taught in a similar manner to white children and are entitled to the same benefits, rules, regulations, and restrictions. It also notes that any colored person over eighteen years of age is mentioned in relation to the statute.

It also details how to obtain a duplicate certificate if the original is lost. The statute grants registration officers the power to preserve order and requires voters to present their certificate to vote.

statutes.title: § 1489. *Registration book—duties of county clerk.* It shall be the duty of the county clerk of each county containing any city or town of either of said classes mentioned in section 1486 to prepare the proper forms, and cause to be printed two registration books for each precinct in said city or…

It specifies the format of these books, including columns for Name, Residence, Precinct Number, Ward Number, Color, November Election, Special Election, and Remarks. The law also outlines the duties of registration officers regarding attendance at voting places and the recording of voter information.

statutes.title: § 1502. *Delivery of registration and stub and ballot books to election officers.* On the day previous to the November election in each year, and on the juridical day previous to every election to be held, or vote of the people to be taken, in any county containing city or town belonging to either…

The law also mandates the delivery of registration and ballot books to election officials.

statutes.statute_citation: Kentucky election laws, primary law and Corrupt Practice Act, 1919, § 1596a, pp. 114–116
statutes.title: § 1596a. (3.) *Election officers*—*Appointment*—*Qualification*—*Term*—*Removal*—*Vacancies*.
citations: Kentucky election laws, primary law and Corrupt Practice Act, 1919, § 1596a, pp. 114–116
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for appointing election officers in Kentucky. It mandates that county executive committees of the two major political parties submit lists of potential officers for each precinct. The election commissioners are to select judges, sheriffs, and clerks from these lists, ensuring representation from different political parties. The statute also details eligibility requirements for election officers, including residency, sobriety, and the ability to read the Constitution and write legibly. It grants county boards the power to remove disqualified officers, but with specific procedural limitations.

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, ch. 90, pp. 440–470
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the requirements for chauffeur registration in Kentucky, including application procedures, fees, and exemptions for non-resident chauffeurs. It establishes a system that could disproportionately affect Black chauffeurs by imposing additional requirements and fees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, ch. 94, pp. 492–513
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various Departments, Boards, Commissions, Institutions and Agencies of the State Government, except for the Legislative and Judicial Departments and except for the common schools, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1921, and…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, ch. 94, pp. 492–513
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children and the Kentucky Home Society for Colored Children, indicating a racial distinction in funding and support for children's services.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, ch. 95, pp. 513–534
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various Departments, Boards, Commissions, Institutions and Agencies of the State Government, except for the Legislative and Judicial Departments and except for the common schools, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1922, and…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, ch. 95, pp. 513–534
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children and the Kentucky Home Society for Colored Children, with a significant disparity in funding, reflecting racial segregation in child welfare services.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, ch. 99, pp. 538–544
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an Act entitled," An Act to provide for the nominations of candidates by political parties at primary elections, and for placing the names of candidates on the ballots to be voted for at general elections and prescribing penalties for the violation thereof," which Act became a law…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, ch. 99, pp. 538–544
statutes.summary: This statute requires candidates to submit an affidavit from two reputable electors of the same political party, affirming their qualifications and support for the party. This requirement can be seen as a mechanism that may have been used to restrict voting rights, particularly for Black Kentuckians, by imposing additional barriers to candidacy.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, p. 227
statutes.title: Independent Consolidated Graded and High School District Taxation
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, p. 227
statutes.summary: This statute allows for the establishment of independent consolidated graded and high school districts funded by taxes levied specifically on white voters and corporations, thereby creating a racially segregated educational funding mechanism.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, p. 482
statutes.title: Classification and Segregation of Children
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1920, p. 482
statutes.summary: This statute mandates the classification, segregation, and separation of children received into a Home based on race, sex, and conduct, reflecting the racial segregation practices of the Jim Crow era.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 103, p. 142
statutes.title: Sec.103. Books to be audited annually - power to establish kindergarten - separate schools for and colored required. white
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 103, p. 142
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law of 1922 outlines the organization and powers of the Board of Education in first-class cities in Kentucky. It details the election and duties of board members, officers, and employees, as well as provisions for purchasing supplies, managing finances, and establishing schools. Notably, Section 103 explicitly mandates separate schools for white and colored children.

statutes.title: Section103. (§ 2978a-29 Ky.St.) Books to be Audited by Expert Accountant.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 103, pp. 156–157
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 3235a-32, p. 1901
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law from 1922 outlines the powers and duties of a city's board of education in cities of the first class. It details the establishment and maintenance of kindergartens, high schools, manual training schools, and normal schools for teacher training. Crucially, it includes a provision for separate schools for white and colored children.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 3235a-33
statutes.title: Section115. (§ 3235a-33 Ky.St.) Kindergarten- Power to Establish.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 115, pp. 190–191
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 3235a-33, p. 1899
statutes.summary: This section mandates that the board of education provide, maintain, and support separate schools for all bona fide resident colored children between the ages of six and eighteen years. These colored schools are to be taught in a similar manner to white children and are entitled to the same benefits, governed by the same rules and regulations, and subject to the same restrictions as white schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 126, p. 214
statutes.title: Sec. 126. Superintendent, principals, teachers and other employees appointed by.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 126, p. 214
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law of 1922 outlines the organization and powers of the Board of Education for cities of the fourth class in Kentucky. It details the creation of a single school district, the composition and powers of the board, appointment of staff, financial management including tax levies and bond issuance, and crucially, mandates the maintenance of separate schools. Section 127 explicitly states 'separate schools to be maintained,' and Section 128a mentions that 'White and colored schools may be maintained under separate boards.'

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 3587a-18
statutes.title: Sec.128b. (§ 3587a-18 Ky.St.) Schools for Colored Children.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 128b, pp. 224–225
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law of 1922 mandates the establishment and maintenance of separate schools for colored children in cities of the fourth class. It states that these schools should be entitled to the same benefits and governed by the same rules and regulations as schools for white children, with a proviso for existing integrated systems.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4535a-32
statutes.title: Section134a-1. ($431a-lc Ky.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 134a-1, pp. 249–251
Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4535a-32, pp. 822–823
statutes.summary: This statute creates the State Normal School Commission, authorized to establish two new Normal Schools for the training of white elementary teachers, one in the western part of the state and one in the eastern part. The commission can receive gifts of land, buildings, or money for this purpose.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 135, pp. 251–252
statutes.title: Section 135. Sec. 137.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 135, pp. 251–252
statutes.summary: This statute establishes and outlines the governance of the Kentucky State Normal School for Colored Persons. It details the composition and powers of its board of trustees, including appointment, terms, removal, and the board's authority to adopt rules and supervise the school's interests. The act also references previous legislation establishing the school.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4636a-5
statutes.title: Section141a. (§ 4636a-5 Ky. St.) Law Department- Department of Law Established.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 141a, pp. 261–263
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4636a-5, pp. 2520–2522
statutes.summary: This section of the 1922 Kentucky School Laws details the establishment and requirements of various departments within the University of Kentucky, including agricultural, mechanical arts, law, and medical departments. It also outlines the process for counties to send students to the university, specifying that one white pupil is entitled to free tuition for every three thousand inhabitants and a fraction thereof over fifteen hundred.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4636k-1
statutes.title: Section147a. (§ 4636k-1 Ky. St.) Persons Engaged in the Military or Naval Service During World War Entitled to Scholarship- Privileges Included.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 147a, pp. 282–283
statutes.summary: This statute grants free scholarships to individuals who served in the U.S. military or naval service during World War I and were residents of Kentucky at the time of enlistment. These scholarships are applicable to the State University, Eastern Kentucky Normal School, Western Kentucky Normal School, and the Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for colored persons. The scholarship covers tuition, fees, room rent, fuel, and light, but not board.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 158, p. 310
statutes.title: Sec.158. Census of children, how made and reported.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 158, p. 310
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law from 1922 outlines provisions for colored schools. It details how donations and gifts for the education of colored children are to be handled, the process for taking and reporting the census of colored children, the organization of teachers' institutes for colored schools, and penalties for the failure of trustees and teachers to perform their duties. Notably, Section 161 explicitly states that white and colored schools are not to be taught in the same college.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4370
statutes.title: Section24. (§ 4370 Ky. St.) What Constitutes- Dividend on Bank Stock - Annual Tax - Fines and Forfeitures.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 24, pp. 30–34
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the distribution of surplus funds for common schools. It explicitly states that per capita derived from interest on bonded surplus shall be apportioned to "white and colored schools of the county respectively." This indicates a legally mandated segregation in the allocation of educational funds.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4421b-27
statutes.title: Sec.26.) (§ 4421b-27 Ky.St.) Penalty for Member of Commission Accepting Bribe.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 26, pp. 308–310
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law from 1922 outlines provisions for colored schools. It details how donations and gifts for the education of colored children are to be handled, the process for taking and reporting the census of colored children, the organization of teachers' institutes for colored schools, and penalties for the failure of trustees and teachers to perform their duties. Notably, Section 161 explicitly states that white and colored schools are not to be taught in the same college.

statutes.title: Section289. (Ky.School Laws of 1918) appropriated$6,- 800 for specific purposes, the latter part of section carried an • annual appropriation as follows: Whereas, there are now valuable buildings, equipment and other property without any maintenance fund for the care, growth and development of the…
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 289, pp. 254–255
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law of 1922 details appropriations and management for state normal schools. Notably, it includes an appropriation of $17,500.00 to the "Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons" for specific purposes including settling indebtedness, and mentions appropriations for a girls' dormitory and permanent improvements at other institutions.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 28, pp. 36–37
statutes.title: Section28. (§ 4526a.Ky.St.) White and Colored not to be Taught in the Same College- Penalty.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 28, pp. 36–37
statutes.summary: This statute prohibits the operation of any college, school, or institution where persons of the white and negro races are received as pupils for instruction. It imposes fines on individuals and corporations that violate this provision. It also makes it unlawful for instructors to teach in such integrated institutions and for individuals of either race to attend schools where the other race is present. However, it allows for separate and distinct branches of private institutions in different localities, at least twenty-five miles apart, for the education of exclusively one race or color. A court ruling is noted that upholds the prohibition of simultaneous teaching of white and colored persons in the same place but voids the provision regarding separate branches being less than twenty-five miles apart.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 2, pp. 18–19
statutes.title: Section2. (§184.) Fund Set Apart for Common Schools -Taxation for A. & M.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 2, pp. 18–19
statutes.summary: This document outlines constitutional provisions for common schools in Kentucky, including the establishment of an efficient system, funding mechanisms, and the principle of separate schools. It references specific sections of the Kentucky Revised Statutes and court cases related to school funding and administration.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 50, pp. 60–62
statutes.title: Section50. (§ 4501a-4.) Elementary Certificates of the First Grade.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 50, pp. 60–62
statutes.summary: This section of the 1922 Common School Law outlines procedures for teacher certificate renewals and the administration of examinations for state certificates and diplomas. Crucially, it specifies that the State Board of Examiners shall prepare three series of questions for 'white and colored teachers,' indicating a legally mandated segregation in the examination process for educators.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 51, pp. 62–64
statutes.title: Section51. (k) The State Board of Examiners under the same rules and regulations laid down in section(g) of this Act shall prepare questions for State certificate and shall enclose each branch in separate envelopes sealed, with the name of subject written or printed thereon, and enclose all these…
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 51, pp. 62–64
statutes.summary: This section of the 1922 Common School Law mandates separate examination rooms for white and colored teachers, although they are to take the same subjects and use the same questions on the same date. It also outlines the roles of county superintendents and examiners in conducting these segregated examinations.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 68, pp. 71–74
statutes.title: Section68. (§ 4399a-8.) Tax Commissioner to Certify Property Valuations Subject to Tax- School Budget- Board (Sec. 4399-7.) The board of education shall allow the county superintendent only such necessary official expenses as are incurred in the county. Beauchamp v. Snider, 170 Ky. 220. The county…
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 68, pp. 71–74
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for levying ad valorem and capitation taxes for common schools in Kentucky. Notably, it specifies that the capitation tax is imposed on 'legal voters (now males only)' residing in the affected territory. The reference to 'Act 1922 limitsschoolpolltax to male citizens' strongly suggests a discriminatory practice, as poll taxes were historically used to disenfranchise Black men.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4434a-12
statutes.title: Section72b. (§ 4434a-12 Ky.St.)- Supervisors of Rural Schools- Appointment, Duties.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 72b, pp. 84–85
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law of 1922 outlines the powers and duties of county boards of education, including the employment of supervisors for rural schools and the management of school funds. Crucially, it mandates that a county superintendent receiving a railroad tax for a school district must pay the portion due to a colored common school to the trustees of that colored school. This explicitly segregates the distribution of funds based on race.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4420a-1
statutes.title: Section79. (§ 4420a-1 Ky. St.) Superintendent of Schools and Clerk to Furnish Boundary to Company.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 79, pp. 94–96
statutes.summary: This statute, pertaining to common school laws in 1922 Kentucky, explicitly addresses the apportionment of railroad and bridge taxes for school districts. It states that the provisions of the law shall not be construed to apply to any colored school district, but then proceeds to outline how taxes collected for white graded common school districts or common school sub-districts should be apportioned. Specifically, it mandates that railroad and bridge taxes collected for the benefit of a white graded common school district or white common school sub-district should be distributed between that white district and any colored common school district if their boundaries are the same. The text further clarifies that a colored common school, graded or ungraded, is entitled to its pro rata share of the railroad school tax, determined by the number of colored pupils compared to white pupils in the district. The statute also includes case law interpretations that reinforce the segregation and separate apportionment of these funds based on race.

statutes.statute_citation: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 7, pp. 21–22
statutes.title: Section7. (§ 189.) Appropriation for Sectarian Purposes Forbidden.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 7, pp. 21–22
statutes.summary: This section of the 1922 Common School Law mandates the equal distribution of school funds between white and colored children, while also requiring the maintenance of separate schools for each race. It also touches upon the use of funds received from the United States and prohibits appropriations for sectarian purposes.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4426a-1
statutes.title: Section 80. (§ 4426a-1 Ky. St.) County to Compose School District- Excepting.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 80, pp. 102–103
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law from 1922 outlines the structure of school districts in Kentucky. It states that each county generally forms one school district, with an exception for cities or towns that maintain their own separate public school systems. In such cases, the remainder of the county outside the city or town district constitutes a separate district. The text also references various legal cases and provisions related to school boards, high schools, and taxation for educational purposes.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4433b
statutes.title: Section84. (§ 4433b Ky. St.) Independent Consolidated Graded and High School District- Election- Tax Levy -Laws Governing Such Schools.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 84, pp. 109–111
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4433b, pp. 2434–2435
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for establishing independent consolidated graded and high school districts. It specifies that white voters or corporations can vote on an annual tax, not exceeding one hundred cents per one hundred dollars of property assessed, or a poll tax not exceeding one dollar and fifty cents per capita on each white male inhabitant over twenty-one years of age residing in the district, or both. These funds are for maintaining the school, erecting/purchasing/repairing buildings, and equipping/repairing conveyances for students. The establishment of such a district requires approval from the County Board of Education and the County Superintendent. The statute also details requirements for extending boundaries, providing conveyances, and setting exact boundaries. These schools are subject to the rules governing graded common schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4526b-2
statutes.title: Section86. (§ 4526b-2 Ky. St.) Contract- Limited- Where Established- Classes County Board- City Course of Study- Who May Attend.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 86, pp. 112–113
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law of 1922 outlines the establishment and classification of county high schools. It details requirements for course of study, contract limitations for tuition, and the location of the first county high school. Crucially, it references a court case, 'Prowse & Co. v. Board of Education, etc., 134 Ky. 365', which deals with 'County Board Establishing a High School - White and Colored Children.'

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4472
statutes.title: Section96. (§ 4472 Ky.St.) Appointment and Removal of Teachers.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 96, pp. 135–136
statutes.summary: This section of the Common School Law of 1922 outlines the administration of graded common schools. It details the grounds for dismissal of principals and teachers, the authority of boards of trustees to prescribe courses of study, and explicitly states that 'All white children of common school age residing in any graded common school district shall have the right to attend the graded common school thereof.' It also allows for the admission of non-resident children or those over school age under certain conditions. Furthermore, it addresses the establishment of consolidated schools and the transportation of pupils.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4476
statutes.title: Section96a-1. (§ 4476Ky.St.) Power to Levy Taxes -Collector and Treasurer.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 96a-1, pp. 137–138
Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4476, pp. 783–784
statutes.summary: This section of the 1922 Common School Law authorizes graded common school districts to levy taxes for establishing, maintaining, and operating schools. Crucially, it explicitly states that the property tax rate and poll tax are to be levied only on 'white persons' and 'white male inhabitants' within the district, indicating a racially discriminatory tax structure for public education.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4478
statutes.title: Section 96a-3. (§ 4478 Ky. St.) State and County Funds.
citations: Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1922, § 96a-3, pp. 139–142
statutes.summary: This statute outlines provisions for the establishment and operation of graded common school districts, specifically addressing the separation of white and colored schools. It prohibits the creation of new colored graded common school districts or changes to existing ones except as previously provided. It also explicitly states that white persons shall not vote in elections for colored school districts, and that the property of white persons shall not be taxed to support colored schools, nor shall the property of colored persons be taxed to support white schools. Furthermore, it prohibits white children from attending graded common schools for colored children.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 100, pp. 319–320
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the West Kentucky Industrial College, established at Paducah, Kentucky, making appropriations thereto.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 100, pp. 319–320
statutes.summary: This act appropriates funds to the West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons at Paducah, Kentucky. It acknowledges the institution's contribution to preparing teachers for schools across the Commonwealth, particularly in rural Western Kentucky, and emphasizes the importance of continued support to avoid negative impacts on Black teachers and the institution's progress.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 10, pp. 110–112
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the establishment of two Normal Schools for the training of white elementary teachers, and appropriating moneys for the maintenance and operation thereof.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 10, pp. 110–112
statutes.summary: This act establishes two new normal schools for the training of white elementary teachers, one in the western part of the state and one in the eastern part. The schools will be managed by the State Board of Education and funded by the state, with a condition that significant gifts of land, buildings, or money must be received before state funds become available. The act explicitly states these schools are for 'white elementary teachers'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 111, pp. 361–382
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions and agencies of the State Government, except for the legislative and judicial departments and except for the common schools, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1924…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 111, pp. 361–382
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for two separate children's home societies: one explicitly for 'White Children' and another for 'Colored Children'. This segregation of services based on race is a hallmark of Jim Crow legislation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 112, pp. 382–404
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions and agencies of the State Government, except for the legislative and judicial departments and except for the common schools, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1923…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 112, pp. 382–404
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds from the general expenditure fund for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1923. It specifically allocates funds to the 'Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children' and the 'Kentucky Home Society for Colored Children', as well as the 'Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 138, pp. 471–487
statutes.title: AN ACT providing for a system of registration of every voter in the Commonwealth of Kentucky; providing for the appointment of officers for the purpose of registering voters of the Commonwealth of Kentucky in every precinct in the State; fixing the time and manner in which the voters of the…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 138, pp. 471–487
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the requirements for voter registration in Kentucky, including age, residency, and the process of signing the registration book. It mandates the recording of personal information such as name, sex, address, age, party affiliation, occupation, color or race, apparent weight, apparent height, and other means of identification. It also includes provisions for illiterate voters and for comparing signatures.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 8, pp. 94–109
statutes.title: AN ACT to repeal Chapter 38 of the Acts of the General Assembly of 1920, relating to the election and qualification of members of boards of trustees in graded common school districts; also Chapter 46 of the Acts of the General Assembly of 1920, relating to the establishment of independent…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1922, ch. 8, pp. 94–109
statutes.summary: This act outlines the powers and responsibilities of boards of trustees for common schools, including the appointment and dismissal of principals and teachers, the prescription of studies, and the admission of students. Section 4474 specifically states that 'All white children of common school age residing in any graded common school district shall have the right to attend the graded common school thereof.'

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 157a
statutes.title: § 157a. An election by the voters of a county on the question whether the fiscal court shall issue county bonds for road and bridge purposes, may be held on a day other than the regular election CONSTITUTION OF THE STATE OF KENTUCKY LXXXIII day. Albright v. Ballard, Judge, 164 Ky. 747,
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 157a, pp. 99–101
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky Constitution, as presented in the 1922 statutes, outlines the limits on indebtedness for various municipalities, including cities and counties. Crucially, it references a specific case (Moss v. City of Mayfield) where a proposition to incur indebtedness for school buildings for 'colored schools' was rightly submitted to 'colored voters.' This implies a system of separate educational facilities based on race, a hallmark of Jim Crow legislation, even though the primary focus of the statute is on fiscal limitations.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 158
statutes.title: § 158. Construction and effect of section.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 158, pp. 101–103
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky Constitution, as interpreted in 1922, addresses the incurring of municipal indebtedness for public schools. Specifically, it details how indebtedness for school buildings for colored schools should be submitted to colored voters and how the taxable property of colored persons should be considered in determining the debt limit. It also mentions separate free graded public school districts for white and colored children occupying the same territory.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 1954c-27
statutes.title: § 1954c-27. Money received from license; how disposed of.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 1954c-27, pp. 1210–1211
statutes.summary: This statute mandates the separation of white and colored inmates within houses of reform. It repeals previous legislation and enacts a new provision requiring separate apartments for children of white and colored races committed to these institutions. The statute also outlines provisions for the employment of inmates, payment of expenses, and the bonding of officers.

statutes.statute_citation: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 1, pp. 32–33
statutes.title: § 1. Carrying weapons concealed.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 1, pp. 32–33
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky Constitution, as interpreted by court cases in 1922, addresses the constitutionality of ordinances requiring separate residential and assembly spaces for white and colored people. While an ordinance from Louisville was initially sustained, it was later reversed by the U.S. Supreme Court. The text also discusses broader constitutional principles regarding absolute power and liberty of conscience.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 2062c
statutes.title: § 2062c. Annual appropriation; bond; hereby appropriated out of any money in the treasury, not otherwise appropriated, 975 § 2062d -2HEALTH, STATE BOARD OF the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000) per annum payable annually for the benefit
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 2062c, pp. 1309–1310
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates $5,000 annually for the benefit of the Red Cross Association (colored) for the purpose of equipping a hospital to care for indigent sick of the colored race. The hospital is to be supervised and cared for by their own people, and will include a nurses' training school for girls of the colored race. It also mandates at least five beds for sick and invalid colored children and those from various colored institutions. Funds are restricted to equipment, maintenance, nurses, matron, food, medicines, and physicians' services, explicitly excluding officers' salaries. A bond of $10,000 is required, and annual verified statements of expenditures are mandated.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 2095b-19a
statutes.title: § 2095b-19a. Criminals under twenty-one to be sentenced to house of reform; parole; incorrigibles; indeterminate sentence; inmates may be hired out.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 2095b-19a, pp. 1328–1330
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the operation of Houses of Reform for minor offenders, including indeterminate sentences until age twenty-one, with provisions for early discharge or parole. Crucially, it mandates separate apartments for white and colored inmates committed to these institutions. It also details inmate labor, financial management, and employment of staff.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 2096
statutes.title: § 2096.) woman§ 2097.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 2096, p. 1333
statutes.summary: This statute outlines who may contract marriage and lists prohibited marriages. Specifically, Section 2097(2) prohibits marriage 'Between a white person and a negro or mulatto.' Section 2098 further clarifies that the issue of such a marriage 'shall not be legitimate.'

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 216b-25
statutes.title: § 216b-25. Idiots and harmless lunatics; disposition of.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 216b-25, p. 307
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that asylums should be kept filled to capacity. Crucially, it states that 'the white and colored patients shall not be kept in the same building.' This explicitly enforces racial segregation within the asylums.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 2241
statutes.title: § 2241. Error in instructing commissioners.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 2241, p. 1293
statutes.summary: This statute section details the procedures for jury selection, including the number of names to be placed in the jury drum, the process for reconvening jury commissioners, and their compensation. Crucially, it includes a specific ruling stating that a negro has no right to demand negro jurors, nor can they complain if the grand jury or jury commissioners were all white. This explicitly addresses racial composition in jury selection.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 294
statutes.title: § 294. Pupils who are able to pay in part; state to pay balance.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 294, pp. 327–328
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates $750 for colored children attending an institution, with a provision that parents able to pay for their maintenance will not have their costs covered by the state treasury. The commissioners of the institution are tasked with enforcing this rule.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 297
statutes.title: § 297. Appropriation of one thousand dollars annually.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 297, pp. 328–329
statutes.summary: These sections of the 1922 Kentucky Statutes address appropriations and per capita allowances for the Kentucky School for the Deaf. Notably, § 298d-2 and § 298d-3 explicitly state that the per capita allowance made to white deaf pupils shall also apply to colored deaf pupils. This indicates a system where separate provisions were made for different racial groups, a hallmark of Jim Crow legislation, even if the intention was to provide equal per capita amounts. The statutes also cover compulsory education for deaf children and appropriations for teachers' salaries.

statutes.statute_citation: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 2, p. 33
statutes.title: § 2. Liberty of conscience.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 2, p. 33
statutes.summary: This section of the Kentucky Constitution, as interpreted by court cases in 1922, addresses the constitutionality of ordinances requiring separate residential and assembly spaces for white and colored people. While an ordinance from Louisville was initially sustained, it was later reversed by the U.S. Supreme Court. The text also discusses broader constitutional principles regarding absolute power and liberty of conscience.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 3146
statutes.title: § 3146. Police court; judge; election; gran cy arising in said cities, respectively, qualification; salary.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 3146, pp. 1862–1863
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for handling vagrancy and petit larceny cases within municipal corporations. It allows for arrest on warrant and trial by a police judge without a grand jury presentment. Convicted individuals are to be sent to labor in the city prison or workhouse for a period of three to twelve months. Women can also be tried and convicted of vagrancy under this statute. The statute also details jurisdiction for riots, unlawful assemblies, court procedures, and the confinement of prisoners.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 331b-2
statutes.title: § 331b-2. Warrant for $5,000 in June, 1902.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 331b-2, pp. 357–358
statutes.summary: This statute regulates the importation of dependent children into Kentucky for placement in family homes. It requires individuals or institutions to provide a bond to the county judge, ensuring that imported children are not incorrigible, of unsound mind or body, or suffering from contagious/incurable diseases. The statute mandates reporting of placed children, removal of those who become public charges or are convicted of crimes, and placement under written contracts for proper care, education, and training. It also requires annual visits and reports to the Kentucky Children's Home Society. Crucially, the statute explicitly states that appropriations are for the care, support, maintenance, and supervision of 'homeless and destitute white children of this commonwealth'.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 3587a-17
statutes.title: § 3587a-17. Contracts for new buildings, improvements and repairs; purchase of supplies.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 3587a-17, pp. 2021–2022
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that the board of education shall provide, maintain, and support separate schools for colored children who are bona fide residents of the district and entitled to free tuition. It states that these colored schools and children are entitled to the same benefits, governed by the same rules and regulations, and subject to the same restrictions as schools provided for white children.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4098
statutes.title: § 4098. (3) Railroad commission to equalize.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4098, p. 2256
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the apportionment of school taxes collected from railroad and bridge companies. It mandates that taxes levied in any common school district shall be paid to the county superintendent for the benefit of that district. Crucially, it specifies that these funds, when collected, shall be apportioned and distributed between white and colored common school districts located within the same boundaries, based on the ratio of white to colored children of pupilage residing in the district. The statute explicitly states that its provisions shall not be construed to apply to any colored school district, but then proceeds to detail the racial apportionment of funds collected from railroad and bridge companies.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4434a-14
statutes.title: § 4434a-14. Method of fixing salaries.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4434a-14, p. 2438
statutes.summary: This statute, titled 'Colored visitors; election,' indicates the election of 'colored visitors' at the same time and place as other elections, conducted by the same officers. While the specific duties of these 'colored visitors' are not detailed in this excerpt, the explicit mention of 'colored' in the context of an election within a school system strongly suggests a racially segregated or distinct electoral process, a hallmark of Jim Crow legislation.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4437
statutes.title: § 4437. Action by trustees may be maintained without using names of trustees, and the fact that two members of the board desire to withdraw their names as plaintiffs does not affect the prosecution of the action. Wright v. Baker, 94 Ky. 343; 15 R. 109; 22 S. W. 335; and see Anderson
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4437, pp. 2439–2440
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for electing a visitor for colored schools within a subdistrict. It specifies that such an election shall be held, with nominations and elections conducted similarly to subdistrict trustees, but with the crucial distinctions that nominating petitions must be signed by colored voters, and only colored voters are eligible to vote for the visitor. The visitor's duties for the colored school are identical to those of subdistrict trustees, with the exception of not being a member of the division board. The statute also references a court case validating the appointment of a visitor for colored schools.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4501a-4
statutes.title: § 4501a-4. Elementary certificate of the first grade.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4501a-4, pp. 2466–2468
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the requirements and procedures for obtaining elementary teaching certificates in Kentucky. It details the revocation of certificates for incompetence, age requirements, certificate renewal processes, and the preparation and administration of examinations. Crucially, section (g) explicitly states that the state board of examiners shall prepare three series of questions for 'white and colored teachers,' indicating a segregated system for teacher certification.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4535a-25
statutes.title: § 4535a-25. Funds to be applied to use intended for them.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 4535a-25, pp. 2487–2488
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the appointment process for students to normal schools in Kentucky. It specifies that each county is entitled to appoint one white pupil for every 500 white school children (or fraction thereof over 250). The selection process involves the county superintendent examining applicants based on qualifications and character. The statute also includes a provision that pupils appointed must sign a declaration to teach in public schools for a specified period, or they will be required to pay tuition. This implies a system of racial segregation in educational appointments.

statutes.statute_citation: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 6, p. 2469
statutes.title: § 6.) § 4501a -7.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 6, p. 2469
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that in all examinations for state and elementary certificates, applicants be assigned numbers instead of using their names. The county superintendent is to keep a record of these numbers and names and forward a copy to the state superintendent. The purpose is to ensure grading and certification are based on merit alone. However, it explicitly states that the only distinction made between the manuscripts of white and colored teachers shall be the use of numerals for white teachers and letters of the alphabet for colored teachers. Violation is a misdemeanor.

statutes.statute_citation: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 8, pp. 2429–2430
statutes.title: section8.) Co.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 8, pp. 2429–2430
statutes.summary: This statute outlines various aspects of common school districts in Kentucky, including voter qualifications, election procedures, tax levies, and the discretion of school boards in fund allocation. Notably, it mandates that county superintendents of schools must pay over to the county board of education the portion of railroad taxes to which a colored common school is entitled, and such payment should be made to the trustees of such colored school. It also details the process for dividing counties into educational divisions and school subdistricts, specifying that boundaries should follow existing school districts for white children as much as practicable and that all children, white and colored, residing in a subdistrict are included.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 938b-10
statutes.title: § 938b-10. Employment, training, and education of children.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 938b-10, pp. 772–773
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 938b-10, pp. 774–775
The Kentucky Statutes, Sixth Edition, 1922, § 938b-10, pp. 776–777
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that the board of a children's home must classify and segregate children based on race, sex, and their history of delinquency or conviction. It also allows for further segregation based on age, conduct, or other matters deemed wise by the board. Special care must be taken to prevent association between children with good habits and those with bad habits or a history of offenses.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 1486b-17
statutes.title: § 1486b-17. Purging of lists; procedure; hearing; appeals.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 1486b-17, pp. 297–298
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the procedure for purging voter registration lists. It details how political party committees can request a purge, the appointment of two officers (one from each major party) to conduct the purge, the process for challenging voters, notification procedures, and appeals to the circuit court. The statute emphasizes the involvement of political parties in the purging process and the need for bipartisan oversight.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 1486b-26
statutes.title: § 1486b-26. Constitutionality; construction of act.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 1486b-26, p. 299
statutes.summary: These statutes outline penalties for fraudulent voter registration, including registering in multiple precincts, providing false residence information, or registering when not lawfully entitled. They also detail penalties for altering registration books, forcibly disrupting registration, and establish procedures for using previously printed registration books that were deemed unconstitutional. A special provision allows soldiers and sailors to register on election days if they were absent during previous registration periods. The act emphasizes liberal construction in favor of its purposes and includes a severability clause.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 1486b-5
statutes.title: § 1486b-5. Challengers.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 1486b-5, pp. 293–294
statutes.summary: This statute, applicable to cities of the fourth class with over 5,000 inhabitants, outlines the process for appointing registration officers. It allows county executive committees to appoint non-residents of a precinct if no qualified residents representing their political party are available. However, if a political party received 25% of the votes in a precinct in the preceding election, they must submit names of residents. The statute also details the information to be recorded during registration, including the applicant's color or race, and allows for challenges to registration rights.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 3587a-20
statutes.title: § 3587a-20. Improvement bonds for building sites, improvements, etc.; popular election; tax to pay bonds.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 3587a-20, pp. 627–628
statutes.summary: This statute outlines procedures for municipal corporations of the fourth class in Kentucky regarding the issuance of bonds for school districts. It details the process for adopting ordinances, preparing and executing bonds, selling them, and managing the proceeds. It also mandates the annual levy of taxes to cover bond interest and create a sinking fund. The statute references election procedures for school districts and includes case law related to bond debt and the distribution of funds between white and colored school districts. It also addresses the process of adding or excluding suburban territory from a school board's jurisdiction.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4396-6
statutes.title: § 4396-6. Organization of department of education; divisions and directors; additional personnel.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4396-6, pp. 755–756
Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4396-6, pp. 757–758
Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4396-6, pp. 759–760
statutes.summary: These statutes outline the responsibilities of the Superintendent of Public Instruction in preparing and submitting budgets, forms, blanks, and reports for the state's educational institutions. They also detail the organization of the Department of Education, including various divisions such as statistics, inspection, certification, rural and high school supervision, vocational education, and crucially, a 'Division of negro education'.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4399a-1b
statutes.title: § 4399a-1b. County boards of education to divide school districts; boundaries; еxсер- tionsto action of board.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4399a-1b, p. 760
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the establishment and operation of county boards of education in Kentucky. It mandates that county school districts be divided into five divisions of roughly equal population for the election of board members. The statute also addresses the process for appealing division decisions and the qualifications for board members. Crucially, a case cited within this section states that 'Colored voters residing in a white school district have a right to vote for members of the county board of education.' While this statement acknowledges a right, the context of Jim Crow era voting rights and the potential for discriminatory practices in election outcomes or the very division of districts suggests an implicit racial dimension.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4469
statutes.title: § 4469. Requirements for organization; management; election, part of county school system.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4469, pp. 781–782
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for abolishing graded common school districts and integrating them into the county school system. It details the transfer of property, funds, and responsibilities to the county board of education. It also describes the procedure for a graded common school district to petition to become part of the county school system, including the requirement for an election. A note following the statute discusses a specific case where a graded school district had a white school but no colored school, and a corporation paid taxes to the white school district while remaining liable to the county board for a portion of its property based on the ratio of colored children to the total school population. This implies a de facto segregation in educational funding and provision.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4474
statutes.title: § 4474. Attendance; tuition.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4474, p. 783
statutes.summary: This statute authorizes the boards of trustees of graded common school districts to levy an annual tax on taxable property owned by white persons and a poll tax on white male inhabitants over twenty-one years of age. It also mandates a sufficient amount to provide for interest payments.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4484
statutes.title: § 4484. Colored graded common school districts.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4484, p. 785
statutes.summary: This section, § 4484, refers to 'Colored graded common school districts'. While the text indicates it was repealed and re-enacted, its existence and specific mention of 'colored' districts strongly suggest a racial segregation component within the education system.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4526c-2
statutes.title: § 4526c-2. Parents and guardians to send children to school; exceptions.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4526c-2, p. 799
statutes.summary: This section establishes the West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons, outlining the appointment and terms of its board of trustees, its corporate powers, and its organizational meetings and general powers. The college is placed under the control and supervision of a board of trustees, with the superintendent of public instruction as ex-officio chairman. The board is empowered to appoint a president, teachers, and other employees, and to prescribe their duties and fix their salaries and terms. The statute explicitly names the college as being for "Colored Persons."

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4526d-5
statutes.title: § 4526d-5. Purpose; courses; diplomas.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4526d-5, p. 800
statutes.summary: This statute establishes and details the operation of a state trade and training school specifically for Negroes in 'Normal District No. 2'. It outlines the commission responsible for selecting the site based on proposals and donations, and specifies the school's purpose: to train teachers for colored schools and provide industrial collegiate training to young men and women of the negro race. The statute also details the board of trustees' powers regarding courses, diplomas, and student admissions, noting that courses are open to colored young men and women resident in the Commonwealth without tuition fees.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4526e-16
statutes.title: § 4526e-16. Availability and disbursement of appropriation.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4526e-16, p. 802
statutes.summary: This statute officially changes the name of the state normal school for colored persons to the "Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons." It outlines the powers and terms of the president, and grants authority to award teachers' certificates. The statute also details the compensation and expenses for the board of regents, their supervisory duties, the treasurer's responsibilities, the secretary's duties, and appropriates funds for the college's establishment and operation, including specific allocations for buildings, equipment, and maintenance. The appropriation is conditioned on matching funds from interested citizens.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4526e-1
statutes.title: § 4526e-1. Training school established.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4526e-1, p. 800
statutes.summary: This statute establishes and details the operation of a state trade and training school specifically for Negroes in 'Normal District No. 2'. It outlines the commission responsible for selecting the site based on proposals and donations, and specifies the school's purpose: to train teachers for colored schools and provide industrial collegiate training to young men and women of the negro race. The statute also details the board of trustees' powers regarding courses, diplomas, and student admissions, noting that courses are open to colored young men and women resident in the Commonwealth without tuition fees.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4526e-2
statutes.title: § 4526e-2. Commission to receive donations and establish site.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4526e-2, p. 800
statutes.summary: This statute establishes and details the operation of a state trade and training school specifically for Negroes in 'Normal District No. 2'. It outlines the commission responsible for selecting the site based on proposals and donations, and specifies the school's purpose: to train teachers for colored schools and provide industrial collegiate training to young men and women of the negro race. The statute also details the board of trustees' powers regarding courses, diplomas, and student admissions, noting that courses are open to colored young men and women resident in the Commonwealth without tuition fees.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4526e-3
statutes.title: § 4526e-3. Objects of the school.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4526e-3, pp. 800–801
statutes.summary: This statute establishes and outlines the governance of a State Trade and Training School specifically for Negroes. It details the curriculum, which includes elementary branches, agriculture, mechanic arts, and various trades. It also creates a board of regents with powers to contract, sue, and manage the school, including appointing teachers and granting certificates of proficiency. The statute explicitly names the school as being 'for Negroes'.

statutes.statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4535-9
statutes.title: § 4535-9. Powers of boards; discharge of teachers and employes; reports to board; treasurer; bond.
citations: Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4535-9, pp. 804–805
Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4535-9, pp. 806–807
Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4535-9, pp. 808–809
Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4535-9, pp. 810–811
Baldwin's Kentucky Statute Service, 1922, § 4535-9, pp. 816–817
statutes.summary: This statute establishes and defines the governance of the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons, granting its graduates the right to teach in colored schools without further examination. It also recognizes and establishes four state normal schools and teachers colleges in Richmond, Bowling Green, Murray, and Morehead, outlining their purpose and the creation of their respective boards of regents.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 112, pp. 390–413
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions and agencies of the State government, except for the legislative and judicial departments, and except for the common schools, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1925…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 112, pp. 390–413
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children and the Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1925. It also appropriates funds for the White Department of the Kentucky School for the Blind. The appropriations are for the purposes authorized by law or as may be hereafter provided by law, and include funds for extinguishing deficits.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 113, pp. 413–435
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions and agencies of the State government, except for the legislative and judicial departments, and except for the common schools, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1926…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 113, pp. 413–435
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for two separate children's home societies: one for White Children and one for Colored Children. It details specific amounts for general operations and for extinguishing prior deficits for each society.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 122, pp. 475–491
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for the execution and sale of Seventy -Five Million Dollars of binds of the Commonwealth, fixing the time when they shall be sold and the use of the proceeds thereof, providing for the application of public funds to the payment of the principal and interest upon said bonds and to…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 122, pp. 475–491
statutes.summary: This act appropriates funds for the improvement and expansion of state normal schools. Specifically, it allocates funds for four white normal schools (Richmond, Bowling Green, Murray, and Morehead) and for the Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons at Frankfort, as well as for a new normal school for colored people in the western part of the state. It also allocates funds for the Kentucky Geological Survey and the Kentucky School for the Blind.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 137, p. 506
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the Kentucky School for the Blind and making appropriations therefor.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 137, p. 506
statutes.summary: This act appropriates funds for the Kentucky School for the Blind to erect and equip a building for a heating plant and laundry, specifically mentioning separate facilities for 'white and colored departments'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 19, pp. 70–71
statutes.title: AN ACT for the benefit of the Kentucky School for the Blind and making appropriations therefor.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 19, pp. 70–71
statutes.summary: This act appropriates funds for the erection and equipping of a building to contain the heating plant and laundry for both white and colored departments of the Kentucky School for the Blind. It also declares an emergency to reduce fire hazards and safeguard pupils.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 53, pp. 122–126
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend an act entitled "An Act to repeal and reenact Subdivision IX of Article IV of Chapter 89 of Kentucky Statutes, Carroll's Edition, 1915, and the amendment thereto as provided in Chapter 78, at page 393 of the Acts of the General Assembly of Kentucky, passed at its regular session in…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 53, pp. 122–126
statutes.summary: This act amends Chapter 53 of the 1920 Kentucky Acts concerning boards of education in third-class cities. It details the powers and duties of these boards, including financial management, property acquisition, teacher selection, curriculum, and the establishment of high schools. Crucially, it mandates 'separate buildings and schools for the education of white and black children.' The act also revises tax levies for school purposes.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 64, pp. 175–195
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to registration for elections in cities and towns having a population of 5,000 inhabitants or more.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1924, ch. 64, pp. 175–195
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the process for voter registration, including the appointment of challengers, the powers of registration officers, and the information to be recorded in the registration book. Crucially, it mandates the recording of the applicant's 'color or race' and 'apparent weight and apparent height and other means of identification'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 11, pp. 80–107
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions and agencies of the state government, except for the legis la tive and judicial departments, and except for the common schools, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1927…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 11, pp. 80–107
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds from the general expenditure fund for the use and benefit of the Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1927. The appropriation is for salaries and all other expenses incident to the operation and maintenance of the department.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 12, pp. 107–132
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions and agencies of the state government, except for the legislative and judicial departments, and except for the common schools, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1928…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 12, pp. 107–132
