statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children, the Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children, and the Kentucky Normal and Industrial Institute for Colored Persons. The appropriations are for salaries and operational expenses for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1928.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 172, pp. 855–877
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to the fiscal administration of the common schools in each of the counties of the Commonwealth by the county board of education; providing for a uniform budget system for the administration of the fiscal affairs of the common schools in each of the counties of the Commonwealth…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 172, pp. 855–877
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that the fiscal court impose a capitation tax not exceeding one dollar on all legal male voters residing in the territory affected by an ad valorem tax for the county board of education. The sheriff is responsible for collecting this tax, along with other state and county revenues, and remitting it to the county treasurer, who serves as the ex-officio treasurer for the county board of education. The sheriff's commission for collecting this specific school tax is limited to one percent of the total school tax collected, and the commission is calculated proportionally based on the combined funds collected.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 82, pp. 329–334
statutes.title: AN ACT to repeal chapter 45, Acts of 1920, being an act to authorize consolidated school districts and county boards of education to issue bonds; and sections 4100 and 4101, and 4420a -2, and 4420a -3, which relate to the collection of graded school taxes from railroad and bridge companies; and…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 82, pp. 329–334
statutes.summary: This act repeals several previous laws related to school districts, bond issuance, tax collection for graded schools, and the establishment of school districts. Notably, it repeals section 4484 from the Acts of 1922, which specifically refers to 'colored graded school districts'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 90, pp. 351–352
statutes.title: AN ACT to repeal and re -enact chapter 33 of the Acts of the General Assembly of 1902 (page 71), which is entitled "An Act to change the name of the State Normal School for Colored Persons, and regulate the conduct of same," same being section 4527 -a Kentucky Statutes, 1915 edition, and giving the…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 90, pp. 351–352
statutes.summary: This act repeals and re-enacts a previous act from 1902 concerning the State Normal School for Colored Persons. It officially changes the name to the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons and grants it the authority to issue certificates to its graduates.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 91, pp. 353–356
statutes.title: AN ACT creating a board of trustees for the West Kentucky Industrial College, repealing chapter 18 of the Acts of the General Assembly of 1918, and chapter 100 of the Acts of the General Assembly of 1922, and sections 489, 490, and 491 of Senate Bill No. 28, in the present session of the General…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 91, pp. 353–356
statutes.summary: This statute establishes the West Kentucky Industrial College, explicitly stating its purpose is to train teachers for colored schools and provide industrial collegiate training to young men and women of the negro race. It outlines the powers of the board of trustees, including rule adoption, employee dismissal, and student discipline. The courses are to be open to colored young men and women resident in the Commonwealth without tuition fees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 92, pp. 356–362
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish a State Trade and Training School for Negroes in the section of Kentucky, known as Normal District No. 2; to create a Board of Regents for the general manage. ment thereof; which shall determine the requirements for admission and graduation and the course of study for said…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1926, ch. 92, pp. 356–362
statutes.summary: This act establishes a State Trade and Training School specifically for Negroes in Normal District No. 2 of Kentucky. It creates a Board of Regents to manage the school, determine admission and graduation requirements, and set the course of study. A commission will be appointed to decide the school's location, and funds are appropriated for its maintenance.

statutes.statute_citation: Constitution of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, p. 44
statutes.title: Constitution of Kentucky - Section 187
citations: Constitution of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, p. 44
statutes.summary: This section mandates that no distinction shall be made on account of race or color in the distribution of the school fund, but explicitly states that separate schools for white and colored children shall be maintained.

statutes.statute_citation: Constitution of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, p. 92
statutes.title: WHITE AND COLORED PUPILS
citations: Constitution of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, p. 92
statutes.summary: This statute mandates separate schools for white and colored pupils.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 11, pp. 74–102
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and agencies of the State government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, except for the legislative and judicial departments, and except for the common schools, for the fiscal…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 11, pp. 74–102
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky Children's Home Society, specifically distinguishing between services for white children and colored children, indicating a racially segregated approach to child welfare.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 125, pp. 477–480
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend chapter one hundred and thirty -eight of the Session Acts of one thousand nine hundred and twenty, entitled "An Act for the benefit of the Red Cross Association (colored) of Louisville," by increasing the appropriation therein from five to ten thousand dollars per annum and…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 125, pp. 477–480
statutes.summary: This statute amends a previous act to increase the appropriation for the Red Cross Association designated for colored individuals in Louisville, reflecting a separate funding mechanism for services aimed at Black Kentuckians.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 12, pp. 102–130
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions and agencies of the State government, except for the legislative and judicial departments, and except for the common schools, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1930…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 12, pp. 102–130
statutes.summary: This statute outlines appropriations for various health and social services, including specific allocations for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children, indicating a racial dimension in the provision of state aid.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 156, pp. 587–588
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and re -enact section two thousand and ninety—seven, Kentucky Statutes, Carroll's one thousand nine hundred and fifteen edition relating to marriages which are prohibited and declared void.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 156, pp. 587–588
statutes.summary: This statute amends the age requirements for marriage, increasing the minimum age for males from fourteen to sixteen and for females from twelve to fourteen, which reflects societal norms that may have been influenced by racial and gender considerations.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 16, pp. 134–182
statutes.title: AN ACT to repeal Sections 216a -2, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, Kentucky Statutes, being part of an act creating the State Board of Charit eis and Corrections and known as Chapter 7 of the Session Acts of 1920; Section 216a -20, being a part of Session Acts 1912, Chapter 50, page 201 and part…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 16, pp. 134–182
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the requirements for superintendents of state institutions to provide detailed information about patients, including their race, upon admission and during their stay. It establishes a framework for the management of patients categorized by mental health conditions, which historically has been used to enforce racial segregation in healthcare and institutional settings.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 48, pp. 236–241
statutes.title: AN ACT providing free textbooks for all the children of the State who attend free public schools, grades one to eight, inclusive; providing for the purchase of books by the State; providing for the distribution of the books to the pupils; and providing for a reasonable expense for those engaged in…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 48, pp. 236–241
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that textbooks issued to white school children cannot be reissued to colored school children and vice versa, establishing a racially segregated system for educational resources.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 65, pp. 276–278
statutes.title: AN ACT to appropriate the sum of one hundred eighty -four thousand, one hundred forty -five ($ 184,145.66) dollars and sixty—six cents for the use and benefit of the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons for the training of teachers and industrial leaders, to restore a dormitory that…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 65, pp. 276–278
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds specifically for the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons, indicating a separate educational institution for Black individuals, which aligns with Jim Crow laws that enforced racial segregation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 84, pp. 371–380
statutes.title: AN ACT to enable cities of the third class to adopt and operate under the city manager form of goverment, and amending section three thousand four hundred and eighty b-three of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, one thousand nine hundred and twenty-two edition.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 84, pp. 371–380
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the procedure for holding an election in a city regarding its organization and government structure, specifically under the City Manager or Commission Form of Government. It mandates the publication of notices and the conduct of the election by the county sheriff or appointed officer.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 94, pp. 410–414
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend sections ten (10) and eleven (11) of chapter sixty -four, Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky one thousand nine hundred and twenty-four, "An Act relating to registration for elections in cities and towns having a population of five thousand inhabitants or…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 94, pp. 410–414
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the procedures for voter registration in Kentucky, specifying the appointment of special officers of registration and the conditions under which registration is held in towns or cities rather than at the county seat. It reflects mechanisms that could be used to control voter registration, potentially impacting Black voters.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 97, pp. 422–423
statutes.title: AN ACT repealing sections one thousand four hundred and eighty -six to one thousand five hundred and six, inclusive, of Kentucky Statutes, Carroll's one thousand nine hundred and twenty -two edition, relating to registration in certain cities and towns, including cities of the fourth class, and…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1928, ch. 97, pp. 422–423
statutes.summary: This statute establishes a registration process for qualified voters in cities of the fourth class, which includes those with populations under five thousand, aligning their registration process with that of larger cities. This could imply a system that may have been used to disenfranchise certain groups, particularly Black voters, in the context of Jim Crow laws.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, ch. 144, pp. 486–494
statutes.title: AN ACT concerning the title records and leases of land owned or leased by the State, making the Secretary of State the custodian of all records, judgments, deeds, maps and abstracts T of title or other papers or records, and all leases of the commonwealth, prescribing his duties relating thereto for…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, ch. 144, pp. 486–494
statutes.summary: This statute lists various state institutions and lands, including the "Industrial College for Colored Persons in Franklin county." While the primary focus appears to be land management and record-keeping for state properties, the explicit mention of a college for "Colored Persons" indicates a racially segregated educational institution, a hallmark of Jim Crow era legislation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, ch. 164, pp. 597–645
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and agencies of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, except for the legislative and judicial departments, and except for the common schools, for the fiscal…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, ch. 164, pp. 597–645
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for two separate children's home societies: one explicitly for 'White Children' and another for 'Colored Children'. It also appropriates funds for the 'Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons'. The appropriations are distinct for each entity and for different fiscal years.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, pp. 732–733
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating eighteen thousand ($18,000.00) dollars to the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons, at Frankfort, Kentucky, for the purpose of paying outstanding accounts for services rendered and material bought and furnished to the officers and employees of said Institution…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, pp. 732–733
statutes.summary: This act appropriates $18,000 to the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons to cover outstanding debts incurred during the 1927-1928 school year due to insufficient budget. It also outlines procedures for the Auditor to verify claims.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, p. 180
statutes.title: CHAPTER 48 125
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, p. 180
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the qualifications and appointment process for registration officers in Kentucky for the 1930 general initial precinct registration. It specifies that officers must not have been convicted of a felony, must be sober, temperate, discreet, and of good demeanor, not be a candidate in the upcoming election, and be capable of reading the Kentucky Constitution in English and writing legibly. The statute also details the partisan appointment of deputy registrars and inspectors, requiring them to be of opposite political affiliations within each precinct. Compensation for these officers is set at five dollars per day. The Board has the power to remove disqualified officers.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, p. 186
statutes.title: CHAPTER 48 131
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, p. 186
statutes.summary: This statute outlines procedures for verifying voter identity at the polls, focusing on signature comparison between registration records and the voter's signature. It details how election officers and party challengers should handle discrepancies and situations where a voter claims inability to sign. A record must be kept of individuals sworn in due to inability to sign.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, p. 196
statutes.title: An Act relating to registration records in cities of the first class.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, p. 196
statutes.summary: This act declares existing registration records in cities of the first class null and void from August 1930, requiring new registration for the primary election. It also outlines procedures for maintaining and copying registration records.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, p. 198
statutes.title: An Act relating to the registration of voters in cities of the first class
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1930, p. 198
statutes.summary: This act outlines penalties for election officials who fail to perform their duties related to voter registration and for individuals who disrupt the registration process. It also includes a severability clause and repeals conflicting laws regarding voter registration in first-class cities.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, ch. 25, pp. 208–308
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation and maintenance of the various departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and agencies of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky for the fiscal years ending June thirty, nineteen hundred thirty -three, and June thirty, nineteen hundred…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, ch. 25, pp. 208–308
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for two separate children's home societies: one for 'White Children' and one for 'Colored Children'. The society for white children receives $100,000 for each of the fiscal years ending June 30, 1933, and June 30, 1934. The society for colored children receives $30,000 for each of those same fiscal years. The funds are to be used for salaries and expenses related to the operation and maintenance of these departments.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, ch. 343, pp. 919–920
statutes.title: AN ACT to establish as part of the State primary road system i a road to be known as project Number beginning on Federal Highway Number sixty-two, at or near the farm known as the Mollie Petit farm in Caldwell County, Kentucky, extending thence by Silver Star School House to what is known as the…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, ch. 343, pp. 919–920
statutes.summary: This act designates a specific road as part of the primary system of State highways. The route is described as beginning on Federal Highway Number sixty-two, near the Mollie Pettit farm in Caldwell County, extending by the Silver Star School House to the Emerson Place, identified as 'colored', and then intersecting the Cadiz road near Jim Tandy's place.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, ch. 94, pp. 496–500
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend chapter 146 of an Act of the General Assembly passed at its 1920 session entitled " An Act relating to free public libraries in cities and towns of the third, fourth, fifth and sixth classes of this Commonwealth ", the same being sections 2741d -1 to and including 2741d -5 of…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, ch. 94, pp. 496–500
statutes.summary: This act amends existing legislation concerning free public libraries in cities and towns of certain classes. It introduces provisions for establishing free public libraries, their support, and crucially, mandates separate funds and separate libraries for the white race and the Negro race. It also outlines the taxation of separate property of the two races and the division of funds derived from such taxation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, p. 456
statutes.title: An Act to Amend Section 148.270 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, Relating to Voter Registration
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, p. 456
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the requirements for voter registration in Kentucky, including the collection of personal information such as name, address, color or race, sex, physical characteristics, party affiliation, occupation, birthplace, age, length of residency, naturalization status, and other means of identification. It also details procedures for voters who are unable to write their names, requiring them to make a mark attested by the clerk after an investigation and oath.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 155, pp. 738–773
statutes.title: AN ACT to reorganize and simplify the executive department of the state government for the purpose of providing for better service and economy, through the enactment of an administrative code providing for the administrative departments and independent agencies therein specified; redistributing the…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 155, pp. 738–773
statutes.summary: This statute establishes the Department of Education, consolidating various educational bodies. It explicitly mentions "State institutions of higher education for negroes" and abolishes the "Board of Trustees of Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons" and "Board of Trustees of West Kentucky Industrial College." This indicates a system of segregated higher education for Black individuals.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 65, pp. 256–406
statutes.title: AN ACT providing for a more uniform and efficient system of public schools and colleges throughout the Commonwealth of Kentucky, repealing section 4363 to section 4376b -10 inclusive, and section 4378 to section 4399, inclusive, Baldwin's 1930 Revision of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes with the 1933…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 65, pp. 256–406
statutes.summary: This statute consolidates and revises various sections of Baldwin's 1930 Revision of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes concerning public education. It specifically includes provisions for the 'public education for colored children' and 'higher education for colored persons', indicating a racially segregated educational system.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 97, p. 485
statutes.title: AN ACT to authorize the State Librarian to furnish without cost to the Library of the University of Kentucky and to the libraries of the four State Teachers Colleges, certain public documents and books when authorized by the trustees to do 80.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 97, p. 485
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the State Librarian to provide public documents, books, and manuscripts from the State Library, free of charge, to the University of Kentucky Library and the libraries of the four state teachers colleges, as well as the two colored teachers colleges. The decision to furnish these materials rests with the trustees of the State Library.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 19, pp. 71–77
statutes.title: § 19. State Department of Education.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 19, pp. 71–77
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for various educational purposes, including teacher training, vocational agriculture and home economics, vocational rehabilitation, and specifically allocates funds for the maintenance and operation of the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons. It also designates fees and receipts from the boarding, rooming, and athletic departments of this college to a revolving fund.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 20, pp. 77–78
statutes.title: § 20. Kentucky Institution for the Education of the Blind.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 20, pp. 77–78
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky School for the Blind for the fiscal years ending June 30, 1935, and June 30, 1936. It explicitly allocates separate funding for the 'White Department' and the 'Colored Department' of the school.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 21, p. 78
statutes.title: § 21. Kentucky School for the Deaf.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 21, p. 78
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky School for the Deaf, specifically allocating separate amounts for a 'White Department' and a 'Department for Colored Children'. It also appropriates funds for Morehead State Teachers College.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 26, pp. 84–91
statutes.title: § 26. University of Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 26, pp. 84–91
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children and the Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children for the fiscal years ending June 30, 1935, and June 30, 1936. The society for white children receives $100,000.00 for each year, while the society for colored children receives $25,000.00 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1935, with the appropriation for the following year being cut off in the provided text.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 29, pp. 92–99
statutes.title: § 29. Department of Insurance.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 29, pp. 92–99
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Colored Red Cross Hospital in Louisville for the fiscal years ending June 30, 1935, and June 30, 1936. It also appropriates funds for the Home for Incurables and the Department of Insurance.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 42, pp. 184–187
statutes.title: AN ACT amending Section three (3) of Article five (5) of Chapter sixty -five (65) of the Acts of the General Assembly of nineteen thirty -four (1934), being Section four thousand three hundred ninety -nine -three (4399-3), Kentucky Statutes, Baldwin's Kentucky Statutes Service of nineteen thirty…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 42, pp. 184–187
statutes.summary: This statute amends existing law regarding independent school districts. It specifies that independent school districts embracing cities of the first five classes, along with their surrounding territories, and any independent graded common school districts with a census of 250 or more white children, will be designated as independent school districts. It also sets a condition for continued operation: districts (other than those in cities of the first five classes already operating as independent districts) must maintain a census of at least 250 white children, unless the State Board of Education determines that operating as an independent district allows for a more efficient school service program.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 43, pp. 187–189
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide State aid for education in certain courses of study of State students pursuing certain courses of study at educational institutions outside of the State for whom no such courses are provided in the educational institutions of the State, and prescribing the conditions under which…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 43, pp. 187–189
statutes.summary: This act provides for the payment of tuition and fees by the Commonwealth of Kentucky for residents who are qualified to study at the University of Kentucky or other state institutions but cannot due to Section 187 of the Kentucky Constitution. These individuals are permitted to pursue such courses at educational institutions outside of the state, and their expenses will be covered. The State Superintendent of Public Instruction will ascertain and pay these tuition and fees, with the State Board of Education prescribing rules and regulations. Funds are appropriated for this purpose, with a limit of $175.00 per person per school year.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 45, pp. 191–212
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to suffrage and elections and providing a method of registering voters of this Commonwealth residing outside of the corporate limits of cities of the first class, fixing penalties for violations of this Act and repealing Chapter sixty-four (64) of the Acts of the General Assembly…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 45, pp. 191–212
statutes.summary: This statute details the information required on voter registration cards, including fields for 'Color'. While not explicitly discriminatory on its face, the inclusion of a 'Color' field in voter registration forms during the Jim Crow era was a common mechanism for enforcing segregation and disenfranchisement of Black voters.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 40
statutes.title: Appropriations for Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons and West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 40
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the operation and maintenance of two institutions specifically designated for "Colored Persons": the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons and the West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons. It outlines specific amounts for salaries, expenses, materials, repairs, boarding, rooming, athletics, student activities, and instructional equipment for both colleges. It also details how fees and other operating receipts will be handled for the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 41
statutes.title: Appropriations for Institutions of Higher Learning and Schools for the Blind
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 41
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for various educational institutions. Notably, it allocates $5,000.00 to pay the college tuition of negro students required to go out of state for higher education. It also details separate appropriations for the 'White Department' and 'Colored Department' of the Kentucky School for the Blind, with significantly different funding levels ($61,500.00 for the White Department and $7,000.00 for the Colored Department).

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 42
statutes.title: Appropriations for Kentucky School for the Deaf and Department of Education
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 42
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the operation of the Kentucky School for the Deaf, specifically allocating $110,000.00 for the 'White Department' and $8,500.00 for the 'Department for Colored Children'. It also appropriates funds for the Department of Education for common schools, textbook purchases, and operational expenses.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 43
statutes.title: Appropriations for Educational Institutions
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 43
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for various educational purposes, including vocational education, vocational rehabilitation, the State Board of Education, the Division of Certification, the State Textbook Commission, the War Orphans' Fund, and specifically allocates $62,000.00 for the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons, along with an additional $3,000.00 for materials and repairs, and funds for boarding, rooming, athletics, and student activities.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 44
statutes.title: Appropriations for Educational Institutions
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 44
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons and also allocates funds to pay the college tuition of negro students required to seek higher education outside of the state. It also details the funding mechanisms for the institution through fees and operating receipts.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 45
statutes.title: Acts of the General Assembly, 1936 - Institution for the Blind and School for the Deaf Funding
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 45
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky School for the Blind, specifically allocating $61,500.00 for the 'White Department' and $7,000.00 for the 'Colored Department'. It also appropriates funds for a workshop for adult blind and the 'White Department' of the Kentucky School for the Deaf ($110,000.00).

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 46
statutes.title: Chapter 133 - Department for Colored Children and Morehead State Teachers College Appropriations
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 46
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Department for Colored Children and for the maintenance and operation of Morehead State Teachers College. Specifically, it allocates $8,500.00 for the Department for Colored Children and $180,000.00 for Morehead State Teachers College for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1937, covering various operational expenses. It also details funding for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1938, for the college.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 57
statutes.title: Appropriations for Charitable Institutions, 1936
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 57
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for various institutions and societies in Kentucky for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1938. Notably, it allocates specific sums for the 'Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children' and the 'Colored Bed Cross Hospital, at Louisville', indicating a segregated approach to the distribution of public funds for charitable purposes.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 59
statutes.title: Appropriations for State Institutions
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 59
statutes.summary: This statute details appropriations for various state institutions, including specific allocations for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children and the Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children. It also includes funds for hospitals for the insane, feeble-minded, and epileptic wards of the state, and for cooperation with the Federal Government under the Social Security Act.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 111, pp. 629–651
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to primary and general elections and providing for a State -wide purgation of the registration lists of voters in the Commonwealth of Kentucky and providing for a Statewide registration and purgation board, and creating a county registration and purgation board for each of the…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 111, pp. 629–651
statutes.summary: This statute establishes a County Board of Registration and Purgation in each county of the Commonwealth of Kentucky. The board is appointed by the State Board of Registration and Purgation and consists of three members. Two members are chosen from the two dominant political parties, and one is selected by the State Board. Members must be at least twenty-one years old, reside in the county, and possess the qualifications of a legal voter. The State Board can remove members at its discretion.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 12, pp. 1092–1093
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide approved high school service for all pupils.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 12, pp. 1092–1093
statutes.summary: This act mandates that county and independent school boards provide approved high school education for all children of high school grade residing within their districts. It allows for maintaining schools or contracting with other districts. A key provision states that if the number of pupils of either race is insufficient to maintain a high school, the board must make provisions for them.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 147, pp. 772–774
statutes.title: AN ACT amending Chapter forty -two (42) of the Acts of the General Assembly of nineteen thirty -six (1936), being Section four thousand three hundred ninety-nine -three (4399-3), Carroll's Kentucky Statute, 1936 edition relating to independent school districts.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 147, pp. 772–774
statutes.summary: This act redefines independent graded common school districts, requiring a minimum of 200 white children in the school census enumeration for a district to continue operating as independent, with exceptions for certain city classes and temporary allowances by the State Board of Education. The State Board of Education has final decision-making power regarding temporary operational status.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 15, pp. 1097–1099
statutes.title: AN ACT providing for the purchase of property in Paintsville Kentucky, known as " The Mayo College property ", and for the establishment thereon of a State Vocational School; providing for the maintenance and operation of said school, and making appropriations therefor.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 15, pp. 1097–1099
statutes.summary: This act authorizes the purchase of the "Mayo College property" in Paintsville, Kentucky, for the establishment of a State Vocational School. Section 2 explicitly states that the Mayo State Vocational School is established and maintained 'for white persons'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 1, pp. 1022–1051
statutes.title: AN ACT providing a Teachers Retirement System for the State of Kentucky; providing for retirement allowances for teachers of State supported Colleges, Public Schools, (including all elementary and secondary schools of the state); providing for disability benefits for disabled teachers of such…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 1, pp. 1022–1051
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 1, pp. 54–100
statutes.summary: This act defines terms related to the Teachers' Retirement System, including 'Present Teacher' and 'New Teacher'. It specifically mentions the 'West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons at Frankfort, Kentucky' as an institution whose teachers engaged in classroom instruction are eligible for the state retirement system. This explicit mention of a college for 'Colored Persons' within the context of a state-wide retirement system suggests a segregated educational system, a hallmark of Jim Crow era legislation.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 20, pp. 1105–1111
statutes.title: AN ACT providing for matrons for jails and station houses in cities of the first class; providing for their appointment, their duties, their removal, their compensation, and repealing Chapter 8 of the Acts of 1912 of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, now embraced in Sections…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 20, pp. 1105–1111
statutes.summary: This statute mandates that mayors of first-class cities designate specific station houses for the detention of female prisoners awaiting trial. It also requires the designation of the county jail for this purpose. Crucially, it mandates the appointment of two "respectable women" as matrons to supervise female prisoners. It then explicitly allows for the appointment of a "colored respectable woman" as an Assistant Police Matron. This provision, while seemingly about care, creates a racially segregated role within the correctional system.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 275, pp. 1007–1022
statutes.title: AN ACT repealing, amending and re -enacting Section 551, Kentucky Statutes, relating to corporations, their management and control, the election and qualifications of directors of corporations.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 275, pp. 1007–1022
statutes.summary: This proclamation from Governor A. B. Chandler, issued on March 2, 1938, convenes an extraordinary session of the Kentucky General Assembly. Among the stated purposes for the session are addressing inadequate provisions for vocational education for white people in Eastern Kentucky and for Negroes in Western Kentucky. This explicit mention of separate provisions based on race for vocational education strongly indicates a Jim Crow-era policy.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 29, pp. 1136–1144
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and re -enact Sections 4527-59 to 4527-81, inclusive, of the Kentucky Statutes, Baldwin's 1936 Revision, relating to higher education for negroes; changing the name of the Kentucky State Industrial College to "Kentucky State College for Negroes "; discontinuing the West Kentucky…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 29, pp. 1136–1144
statutes.summary: This act amends sections of the Kentucky Statutes related to higher education for negroes. It specifically changes the name of the Kentucky State Industrial College to "Kentucky State College for Negroes".

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 106, pp. 482–485
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to libraries and library service, and to the powers, duties and functions of the Library Extension Division of the Department of Library and Archives.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 106, pp. 482–485
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the administration of federal grants for library service in Kentucky. It mandates that appointments to the Library Extension Division and participating libraries be based on merit and efficiency, without political consideration. Crucially, it requires the Library Extension Division to make plans to lessen inequalities of opportunity for library service and to make equitable apportionment of funds so as to provide library facilities to both the white and colored races. It also details the process of notifying the U.S. Commissioner of Education and entering into contracts for local public library service.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 125, pp. 553–562
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend Sections 3235b-l to 3236b-18, inclusive, of Car roll's Kentucky Statutes, 1936 Edition.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 125, pp. 553–562
statutes.summary: This act amends existing statutes concerning public parks in cities of the second class. It explicitly states that public parks established for the recreation, pleasure, and welfare of the 'white population' shall be managed by a 'Board of Park Commissioners (White)'. This indicates a legally mandated segregation of public park facilities based on race.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 16, pp. 166–222
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation, maintenance, support and functionings of the State Government of the Com mon wealth of Kentucky, including each of the various offi cers, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and sub divisions of the State Government, and the purchase of…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 16, pp. 166–222
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Department of Welfare in Kentucky for the year 1940. It includes allocations for the operation of charitable and penal institutions, the Kentucky Children's Home (explicitly mentioning "White and Colored"), administration of C.C.C. camps, probation and parole, the Home for Incurables, the Colored Red Cross Hospital, Public Assistance (including Old Age Assistance, Child Welfare, and Aid to the Blind), Emergency Relief, conveyance of lunatics, and Pauper Idiots.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 196, pp. 864–866
statutes.title: AN ACT to repeal section 4 of 1924 House Bill No. 44, which amended section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, 1922 edition, relating to pensions for Confederate veterans, by amending section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, 1936 edition, to read like section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 196, pp. 864–866
statutes.summary: This act re-enacts sections of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes concerning vagrancy. It grants circuit, police, quarterly, and justice courts jurisdiction over vagrancy offenses, with police, quarterly, and justice courts deemed always open for such trials. It also mandates sheriffs, constables, marshals, and policemen to watch for vagrants, warn them to leave and find work, and disperse groups of vagrants if necessary, using reasonable force.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, p. 863
statutes.title: Vagrancy Statute Re-enactment
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, p. 863
statutes.summary: This statute re-enacts and defines vagrancy for able-bodied males and females. It outlines conditions such as habitual loitering without means of support, refusal to engage in honest labor, desertion of family without support, and habitual refusal to work while loitering in public places. Penalties include fines and imprisonment, with increased penalties for subsequent offenses.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 1, pp. 56–113
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation, maintenance, support and functioning of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, including each of the various officers, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and sub -divisions of the State Government, and the purchase of record…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 1, pp. 56–113
statutes.summary: This statute details appropriations for various aspects of public education in Kentucky for the year 1942. It includes funding for general school expenses, textbooks, scholarships, vocational education, and specifically allocates funds for the 'Kentucky State College for Negroes' and the 'West Kentucky Vocational Training School' for Negroes, as well as 'College Tuition for Negroes' to attend institutions outside the state. It also lists appropriations for the 'Kentucky School for the Blind - White' and 'Kentucky School for the Blind - Colored'.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 31, pp. 276–277
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to the transfer of prisoners confined in any of the state penal institutions or reformatories.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 31, pp. 276–277
statutes.summary: This act charges the Commissioner of Welfare with classifying and segregating prisoners in state penal institutions and reformatories based on various factors including past records, rehabilitation potential, and influence on other prisoners. The Commissioner is also given the authority to transfer prisoners between institutions. The act declares an emergency and is effective upon passage.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 53, pp. 383–384
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to public parks in cities of the second class. Be it Enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky:
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 53, pp. 383–384
statutes.summary: This act consolidates and amends sections of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes concerning public parks in second-class cities. It allows cities to appropriate funds for park purchase, care, and improvement, and to maintain them from city funds. Crucially, it mandates the annual appropriation of two separate funds for park care and maintenance, one for a 'white park board' and the other for a 'colored park board', with funds paid out only upon order from the respective boards.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 87, pp. 539–540
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend section 125b - 1 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, 1936 edition, relating to the office of Commonwealth's Attorney in counties containing a population of one hundred and fifty thousand or more.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 87, pp. 539–540
statutes.summary: This act amends a statute concerning the office of Commonwealth's Attorney in counties with a population of 150,000 or more. It acknowledges that a large portion of the population in such counties is composed of 'persons of the colored race' and states that it is essential to work in harmony with this race and employ persons of that race to work among them, without discriminating against any person because of race or previous condition of servitude. The act also addresses the increase in work and the need to increase the number of district detectives in these offices.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 131, pp. 301–309
statutes.title: AN ACT to provide for Civil Service and pensions for county employes in counties containing cities of the Second Class and having a population of more than 80,000.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 131, pp. 301–309
statutes.summary: This act outlines qualifications and examination procedures for classified county employment. It requires applicants to be registered voters, of sobriety and integrity, law-abiding, and able to read, write, and understand English. Examinations are to be conducted by a commission, with notice published in the largest circulation newspaper. Applicants who served in the US military during wartime and received an honorable discharge receive a five percent increase in their examination grade. The commission certifies ranked lists of applicants to the fiscal court.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 1, pp. 472–524
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation, maintenance, support and functioning of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, including each of the various offices, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and subdivisions of the State Government, and the purchase of record…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 1, pp. 472–524
Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 1, pp. 524–573
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for various educational institutions in Kentucky for the fiscal years 1944-1945 and 1945-1946. Specifically, it allocates funds for Vocational Education, Vocational Rehabilitation, Kentucky State College for Negroes, Lincoln Institute of Kentucky, and West Kentucky Vocational Training School for Negroes.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 52, pp. 148–150
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and re-enact Sections 97.470, 97.430, Kentucky Revised Statutes, 1942 Edition, pertaining to the Secretary and Treasurer of Boards of Park Commissioners in Cities of the Second Class.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 52, pp. 148–150
statutes.summary: This statute amends Section 97.470 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, 1942 Edition. It allows cities to appropriate funds for public parks and maintain them. Crucially, it mandates that these funds be held in separate and distinct accounts for the 'white park board' and the 'colored park board', or managed by separate secretaries and treasurers appointed by each board. This explicitly segregates park funding and management based on race.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 88, pp. 213–215
statutes.title: AN ACT pertaining to registration for elections in cities of the first class, amending KRS 117.310.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 88, pp. 213–215
statutes.summary: This act amends KRS 91.010 concerning voting procedures in cities of the first class. It outlines a process for voters who claim they cannot sign their name, requiring them to be sworn in. If their registration record shows they previously signed, they will not be permitted to vote unless their inability to sign is due to a physical disability acquired after registration. Election officers must record these cases.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 97, pp. 223–228
statutes.title: AN ACT making provision for State Tuberculosis Sanatoria. Be it Enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky:
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 97, pp. 223–228
statutes.summary: This act outlines provisions for sanatoriums, including patient admission, transfer, and the specific requirement for sanatoriums to receive and provide adequate facilities for the treatment of paying and pauper patients of the negro race who are residents of the district. It also details the costs of transporting patients.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 147, pp. 463–466
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to the registration and purgation of voters. This Act shall be known as the Trivet te - Waggoner Act.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 147, pp. 463–466
statutes.summary: This act mandates the use of rubber stamps with the words "PURGATION RECOMMENDED" and a space for "Reason" and signatures of election judges. These stamps are to be provided to each precinct, except those within a first-class city, for use during primary elections. The purpose is to facilitate the process of recommending the purgation (removal) of voters from the rolls.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 160, pp. 502–503
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend Section 26.610 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, relating to Matrons for Police Courts of Cities of the first class.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 160, pp. 502–503
statutes.summary: This act amends existing law to require two court matrons in cities of the first class: one white and one of the colored race. These matrons are responsible for investigating and reporting on women and girls awaiting trial, and supervising those under suspended sentence. Both matrons are to be paid the same salary.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 38, pp. 83–121
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation, maintenance, support and functioning of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, including each of the various offices, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and subdivisions of the State Government, and the purchase of record…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 38, pp. 83–121
statutes.summary: This section of the 1946 Acts of the General Assembly details appropriations for various state institutions and programs, including cancer control, tuberculosis sanatoria, and the Colored Red Cross Hospital. It also outlines funding for the Department of Welfare, including its various divisions.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 67, p. 174
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to higher education for Negroes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 67, p. 174
statutes.summary: This act amends Section 166.170 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes concerning the granting of aid for higher education. It outlines the process for the State Board of Education to prescribe rules for aid, for the Superintendent of Public Instruction to ascertain and pay tuition and fees, and for prorating funds if insufficient. A maximum of $350.00 is allowed per person per school year.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 112, p. 313
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to education in fields related to health, with particular reference to the education of, and the training of nurses and doctors of the Negro race.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 112, p. 313
statutes.summary: This act allows hospitals to provide instruction in nursing, medicine, surgery, or other related graduate-level courses if their governing body elects to do so. It specifically addresses the lack of accredited training facilities for Negro women in nursing and postgraduate training for Negro doctors in Kentucky, while noting that adequate provisions exist for other races. The act aims to enable such training within hospitals that accept Negro patients.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 190, pp. 462–466
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to the state tuberculosis sanatoria, including Hazelwood Sanatorium; providing for a State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission and transferring to such commission certain powers and duties now possessed by the State Board of Health, the Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission of Kentucky and…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 190, pp. 462–466
statutes.summary: This act amends existing statutes concerning state tuberculosis sanatoria. It specifies provisions for paying and pauper patients, including the allocation of accommodations and the transfer of patients. Crucially, it mandates that provisions be made at each sanatorium for the receipt and furnishing of adequate facilities for the treatment of paying and pauper patients of the Negro race who are residents of the district. It also clarifies the cost of transporting patients.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 2, pp. 16–52
statutes.title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation, maintenance, support and functioning of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, including each of the various offices, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and subdivisions of the State Government, excepting the State Road Fund…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 2, pp. 16–52
statutes.summary: This statute appropriates funds for the operation of various sanatoria and hospitals, including specific allocations for the Covington T.B. Sanatorium, Warren County T.B. Sanatorium, Kentucky Division of Women's Field Army of American Society for Control of Cancer, and the Colored Red Cross Hospital. It also allocates funds for Mental Hygiene and the Department of Welfare.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1952, ch. 134, pp. 342–378
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to qualification, registration and purgation of voters.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1952, ch. 134, pp. 342–378
statutes.summary: This statute outlines the compensation and meeting schedules for county boards of registration and purgation. It specifies daily pay rates for board members and secretaries, with different provisions for counties with and without cities of the first class. The statute also details the number of days the board must meet, particularly around election periods, and mandates that purgation be concluded at least twenty days before any primary or general election. Meetings are to be held at the courthouse unless otherwise necessary and with proper notice. It also includes a mechanism for citizens to prefer charges against a board that fails to meet or purge adequately.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1952, ch. 41, pp. 80–88
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to education.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1952, ch. 41, pp. 80–88
statutes.summary: This statute amends Section 166.040 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes to explicitly state that the purpose of the West Kentucky Vocational School is to provide vocational training facilities for colored children. It also amends Section 166.050 and 166.060 regarding the appointment and removal of the school's president and employees.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1954, ch. 2, pp. 24–25
statutes.title: AN ACT to amend and re-enact Section 145 of the Constitution of the Commonwealth of Kentucky. That upon the concurrence of three-fifths of all the members elected to each House of the General Assembly, the ayes and nays being taken thereon and entered in full in their respective journals, Section…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1954, ch. 2, pp. 24–25
statutes.summary: This act amends Section 145 of the Kentucky Constitution regarding voter qualifications and disenfranchisement. It outlines the general requirements for voting (age, residency) and then lists exceptions, including persons convicted of treason, felony, bribery in an election, or "such high misdemeanor as the general assembly may declare shall operate as an exclusion from the right of suffrage." It also notes that such excluded persons may be restored to civil rights by executive pardon.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1956, ch. 25, pp. 62–65
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to recreational facilities in cities of the second class.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1956, ch. 25, pp. 62–65
statutes.summary: This act repeals existing powers and duties granted to separate 'Board of Park Commissioners (White)' and 'Board of Park Commissioners (Colored)' in cities of the second class, vesting all such powers and duties in the city itself. This implies the consolidation of previously segregated park management structures.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Special Session, 1956, § 3, pp. 63–64
statutes.title: Section 3. Section 164.540 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes is amended to read as follows: (1) The Council on Public Higher Education in Kentucky as defined in KRS 164.010 is hereby designated as the agency of the Commonwealth of Kentucky charged with the responsibility and vested with all necessary…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Special Session, 1956, § 3, pp. 63–64
statutes.summary: This statute addresses the admission of Negroes to educational institutions in Kentucky. It states that Negroes will not be admitted on an equal basis with other races and that no Negro citizen will be forced to attend a segregated regional institution if an institution offering the same course of study to other races exists within the Commonwealth. It also outlines a program for medical research and education, allowing contracts with medical schools to admit residents of the Commonwealth, with specific provisions for payment and reporting. Several sections of the Kentucky Revised Statutes are repealed.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 145, pp. 634–646
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to education.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 145, pp. 634–646
statutes.summary: This statute amends Section 157.360 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, which deals with the allocation of classroom units for the foundation program in school districts. It outlines how classroom units are determined based on average daily attendance for elementary, secondary, vocational, and special education, as well as for administrative and support staff. A specific provision is made for Lincoln Institute, stating that one twenty-seventh of a classroom unit shall be included for each pupil in average daily attendance at Lincoln Institute if attendance is under a written contract between the institute and the district of the pupil's legal residence.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 59, pp. 224–226
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to voter registration and purgation.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 59, pp. 224–226
statutes.summary: This act outlines procedures for challenging voter registrations. It specifies that a voter's name can be challenged if they have not voted in two consecutive years. The process involves written notification to the voter, an opportunity to appear before the board to contest the challenge, and the potential for removal from registration lists if the challenge is upheld or if the voter fails to appear. Challenges must be made in writing within ten days after registration books close.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, pp. 86–87
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to marriage. Approved February 15, 1960
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, pp. 86–87
statutes.summary: This act amends Section 402.020 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes to prohibit and void marriages between a white person and a Negro or mulatto. It also outlines other prohibited marriages based on mental capacity, existing marriage, solemnization, and age.

statutes.statute_citation: Public Health Laws, 1962, p. 255
statutes.title: CHAPTER 402 MARRIAGE
citations: Public Health Laws, 1962, p. 255
statutes.summary: This chapter outlines various aspects of marriage law in Kentucky, including prohibited degrees of relationship, void marriages, marriage procedures, license requirements, and age restrictions. Specifically, section 402.020(2) explicitly prohibits marriage between a white person and a Negro or mulatto.

statutes.statute_citation: Public Health Laws, 1962, p. 260
statutes.title: MARRIAGE § 402.990 Penalties
citations: Public Health Laws, 1962, p. 260
statutes.summary: This statute outlines penalties for various marriage-related offenses. Specifically, it states that any party to a marriage prohibited by KRS 402.010 or between a white person and a Negro or mulatto shall be fined and potentially imprisoned if they continue to cohabit. It also details penalties for marrying feeble-minded individuals, idiots, or lunatics, and for unauthorized solemnization of marriages.

statutes.statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1964, ch. 173, pp. 650–656
statutes.title: AN ACT relating to a city/county children's home.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1964, ch. 173, pp. 650–656
statutes.summary: This act mandates the classification and segregation of inmates in a home for delinquent children based on race, sex, and the nature of their delinquency or conviction. It also emphasizes preventing association between 'good' and 'bad' conduct children.
